    <title>What Happens When an AI Agent Runs Out of USDC? The Hidden Problem Behind Autonomous Crypto Payments</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article style="background: rgb(255, 255, 255); color: #111111; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; line-height: 1.75; margin: 0px auto; max-width: 900px;"&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEh9IjlDz-mySm4dCPFxJDbn1Jsdwzpy1a4qx0Jj0wx2GnWbHYKVmDZZg9EytZ6MPAVGEAc-CSSShUElJNu5Pgs1ScAyVnflQw8o7-G4G2fW4nGxRinYH7H9nBUVjHBhJ_nKgWrkT12a6U3GKQxFmKafEUyHeJauiDrbFRAWMeOpeu2YEFfWspSPEkDyxZjL/s1376/ai-agent-runs-out-of-usdc-autonomous-payments.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="AI agent running out of USDC during an autonomous crypto payment" border="0" data-original-height="768" data-original-width="1376" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEh9IjlDz-mySm4dCPFxJDbn1Jsdwzpy1a4qx0Jj0wx2GnWbHYKVmDZZg9EytZ6MPAVGEAc-CSSShUElJNu5Pgs1ScAyVnflQw8o7-G4G2fW4nGxRinYH7H9nBUVjHBhJ_nKgWrkT12a6U3GKQxFmKafEUyHeJauiDrbFRAWMeOpeu2YEFfWspSPEkDyxZjL/s1600/ai-agent-runs-out-of-usdc-autonomous-payments.webp.png" title="What Happens When an AI Agent Runs Out of USDC?" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By CoinAINews Editorial Team&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI agents are becoming increasingly capable of doing more than answering questions. They can search for information, call APIs, compare services, execute workflows and, increasingly, make payments without waiting for a person to approve every step.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a practical question that is easy to overlook:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;What happens when an AI agent runs out of USDC?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The answer is more complicated than simply adding more money to a wallet. An autonomous agent needs a wallet, payment permissions, spending limits, a way to handle failed transactions and rules that determine when it can spend company or user funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The issue is becoming more relevant as new infrastructure is being built specifically for machine-to-machine payments. Circle launched its Agent Stack in May 2026, Cloudflare announced programmable wallets for the agentic Internet in August, and payment standards such as x402 allow software agents to pay for certain services directly through HTTP-based payment flows. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BlackRock has now added another layer to the discussion. In its September 2026 research paper, &lt;em&gt;The Machine-Native Economy&lt;/em&gt;, the asset manager argued that broader AI adoption could become an underappreciated source of demand for digital assets, including &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/what-are-tokenized-bank-deposits-how.html"&gt;stablecoins &lt;/a&gt;and programmable payment infrastructure. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But infrastructure existing is not the same thing as mass autonomous payment activity. That distinction is critical.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Would an AI Agent Need Its Own Crypto Wallet?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Imagine an AI research agent that has been instructed to collect information from several paid data providers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of asking its human operator to manually purchase every API request, the agent could have access to a controlled &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/what-are-tokenized-bank-deposits-how.html"&gt;wallet &lt;/a&gt;containing a small amount of USDC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It might use that balance to:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Pay for API calls.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Purchase datasets.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Access premium software tools.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Pay for computing resources.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Purchase other machine-readable digital services.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one reason stablecoins are attracting attention in the agentic-commerce discussion. They can be transferred programmatically and can operate on blockchain networks without requiring the same user-interface workflow associated with traditional online payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle's Agent Stack is explicitly designed around this idea. Circle says its Agent Wallets allow agents controlled access to USDC and ERC-20 tokens, while developers can establish permissions and spending limits. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;So What Happens When the Balance Reaches Zero?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are several possible outcomes, depending on how the wallet and application have been designed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;1. The payment simply fails&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The simplest situation is also the safest.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If an agent has $10 of authorized USDC and attempts to make an $11 payment, the transaction can fail because the wallet does not contain enough funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The agent may then stop the task, return an error, or ask its human operator for additional funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;2. The agent requests additional funds&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A more sophisticated system could allow an agent to request additional funds from a parent account.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); min-width: 650px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Payment&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Possible Rule&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Action&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); padding: 10px;"&gt;$0.02&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); padding: 10px;"&gt;Within automatic &lt;br /&gt;limit&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); padding: 10px;"&gt;Approve automatically&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); padding: 10px;"&gt;$2&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); padding: 10px;"&gt;Requires additional &lt;br /&gt;policy check&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); padding: 10px;"&gt;Approve if conditions &lt;br /&gt;are satisfied&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); padding: 10px;"&gt;$50&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); padding: 10px;"&gt;Above agent limit&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(187, 187, 187); padding: 10px;"&gt;Request human &lt;br /&gt;approval&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is fundamentally different from giving an AI unrestricted access to a large cryptocurrency balance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Real Problem Is Automatic Refilling&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Running out of USDC is not necessarily the dangerous part.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Automatically refilling the wallet can be.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Suppose an AI agent starts with $10 and is allowed to request additional funds whenever its balance falls below $1.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If that mechanism has no effective upper limit, a malfunctioning agent could potentially continue requesting funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A badly designed system could therefore transform a small experimental wallet into an uncontrolled spending mechanism.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why agent wallets increasingly include concepts such as:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Maximum transaction size.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Daily or weekly spending limits.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Approved destinations.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Contract allowlists and blocklists.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Time-based permissions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Human approval for larger transactions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Separate wallets for different agents or tasks.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cloudflare's announced Virtual Wallet model follows this principle. The company says agents can spend within permissions established by the owner, while the maximum spending amount can be capped. Cloudflare also describes manual overrides when an agent exceeds its permitted limits. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;A Wallet Balance Is Not the Same as Financial Permission&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction could become one of the most important concepts in autonomous payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI agent might technically have access to a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-cant-circle-reverse-stolen-usdc-on.html"&gt;wallet containing &lt;/a&gt;$1,000, while its software permissions allow it to spend only $20 per day.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In that situation, the wallet balance is $1,000, but the agent's effective spending authority is much smaller.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That separation allows organizations to keep funds available without giving an AI system unrestricted control over them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle's Agent Stack similarly describes controlled access to USDC through defined permissions and guardrails, including spending limits and address controls. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Where Does x402 Fit Into This?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;x402 is designed to make internet-native payments possible when a service requires payment before responding.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The basic idea uses the HTTP &lt;strong&gt;402 Payment Required&lt;/strong&gt; response.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An agent requests a service. The server responds with payment requirements. The agent then signs and sends the required payment before retrying the request.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Current 0x documentation provides a practical example: its supported x402 endpoints can charge agents $0.01 per request in USDC, with payment available through Base or Solana. The documentation also describes a &lt;code&gt;--max-payment&lt;/code&gt; cap to limit what the agent can authorize. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This matters because it changes the traditional payment sequence.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Human → Website → Login → Card → Payment → Service&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;an automated workflow can look more like:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI Agent → API → Payment Request → Wallet Authorization → USDC Payment → API Response&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The payment becomes part of the machine-readable interaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If the Agent Gets Stuck in a Payment Loop?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Consider an AI agent searching for the cheapest data source.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It calls one API for $0.02, another for $0.03 and another for $0.05. If the agent is poorly programmed, it could keep testing services long after the useful information has already been obtained.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Individually, each transaction may look harmless.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Together, hundreds or thousands of small transactions can become expensive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why a useful agent-wallet design needs more than a transaction limit.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It may also need:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A maximum number of transactions per hour.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A daily spending ceiling.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Approved merchant or API lists.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Automatic shutdown after unusual activity.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Budget controls for individual tasks.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Human escalation when behavior falls outside normal patterns.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The goal is not necessarily to prevent an agent from spending. The goal is to make the agent's spending predictable.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why a Small Wallet Can Actually Be a Safety Feature&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Giving an AI agent less money may sound restrictive, but it can reduce the potential damage from mistakes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cloudflare makes a similar point in its wallet design: an agent with a $10 budget can explore services with considerably less financial exposure than an agent controlling $1,000. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, a research agent might receive only $10 USDC for one task.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When the balance reaches zero, the task stops.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The agent cannot continue spending until another authorized process supplies additional funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This creates a financial boundary around the AI system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If the Agent Pays the Wrong Service?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is another problem that becomes important as autonomous payments scale.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A human can notice that a website looks suspicious before entering card details. An AI agent may interact with a service programmatically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If it sends a blockchain payment to the wrong address, the payment may not be reversible simply because the agent made a mistake.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means wallet infrastructure has to address not only &lt;em&gt;how much&lt;/em&gt; an agent can spend, but also &lt;em&gt;where&lt;/em&gt; it can spend.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Allowlisted addresses, approved contracts, merchant restrictions and transaction limits can therefore become as important as the underlying blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Circle Is Building the Financial Layer for Agents&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle's May 2026 Agent Stack announcement illustrates how quickly this area is developing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The initial stack included Agent Wallets, Agent Marketplace, Circle CLI, Nanopayments powered by Circle Gateway and Circle Skills.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle describes the infrastructure as a way for agents to hold funds, discover services and transact programmatically using USDC while operating within defined permissions and guardrails. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle also reported that x402 had processed $24.24 million over the preceding 30 days as of April 29, with 99.8% of transaction value settled in USDC. That figure is useful as an infrastructure signal, but it should not be interpreted as proof that autonomous AI commerce has already reached mass adoption. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Cloudflare Is Approaching the Same Problem From the Internet Layer&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cloudflare's August 2026 wallet announcement focuses on another obstacle: agents need both an identity and a payment mechanism to interact with online services.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Its proposed Account Wallets and Virtual Wallets separate human ownership from delegated agent spending.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Virtual Wallets can operate through API keys and are designed to spend according to permissions established by the account owner.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That architecture addresses a central problem in autonomous commerce: an AI system needs enough freedom to act, but not enough freedom to spend without boundaries. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;BlackRock Sees a Bigger Machine-Native Economy&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The discussion goes beyond wallets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In its September 2026 paper, &lt;em&gt;The Machine-Native Economy&lt;/em&gt;, BlackRock argued that AI agents could become an additional source of demand for digital assets as machines increasingly pay for data, services and computing resources.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The firm specifically highlighted stablecoins and programmable payment infrastructure, while also discussing the possibility of tokenized claims on computing capacity. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important point is that BlackRock presented this as a broader economic thesis, not as proof that AI agents will immediately replace traditional payment systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Current infrastructure development is moving faster than demonstrated autonomous-agent economic activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Infrastructure Exists. The Big Question Is Usage.&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Today, developers can already experiment with agent wallets, programmable payments and machine-oriented payment protocols.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But that does not mean millions of AI agents are independently spending money every day.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent coverage of BlackRock's paper has also highlighted this gap between infrastructure and actual usage. The rails are being built, while real-world autonomous payment activity remains relatively early. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the thesis to become a major economic trend, agents would need to perform meaningful amounts of commerce with real businesses and services.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could include paying for:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;AI inference.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Cloud computing.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Data feeds.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Search and research APIs.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Software tools.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Digital content.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Other machine-to-machine services.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What to Watch Next&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Real agent spending:&lt;/strong&gt; Are autonomous systems making payments for genuine commercial services?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Wallet controls:&lt;/strong&gt; Do developers adopt spending limits, allowlists and transaction caps as standard features?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Payment volume:&lt;/strong&gt; Does machine-generated payment activity become large enough to matter economically?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Stablecoin usage:&lt;/strong&gt; Do agents increasingly use stablecoins for recurring small-value payments?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Tokenized deposits:&lt;/strong&gt; Can banks offer programmable alternatives that compete with public-chain stablecoins?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Fraud prevention:&lt;/strong&gt; How will companies identify compromised or malfunctioning agents?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Identity:&lt;/strong&gt; How will a merchant know which organization is financially responsible for an autonomous agent?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Human escalation:&lt;/strong&gt; Can agents operate independently while reliably handing unusual transactions back to humans?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What happens when an AI agent runs out of USDC?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The transaction can fail, the agent can stop the task, or the system can request additional funds if its permissions allow that. A well-designed system should not automatically receive unlimited funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can an AI agent have its own crypto wallet?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Infrastructure such as Circle Agent Wallets and Cloudflare's proposed Virtual Wallets is designed to give agents controlled access to funds while keeping spending permissions under defined rules. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is x402?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;x402 is an HTTP-native payment mechanism built around the HTTP 402 Payment Required response. It can allow an agent to receive payment requirements, authorize a stablecoin payment and retry a request after payment. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Could an AI agent spend unlimited USDC?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It depends entirely on the wallet architecture and permissions. Spending limits, transaction caps, approved destinations and human approval can restrict how much an agent can move.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Will AI agents replace traditional payment systems?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is currently no basis for treating that as a certainty. BlackRock's research presents a thesis about potential future demand, while current autonomous-agent payment activity remains much earlier than the infrastructure being developed around it. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most interesting problem in autonomous crypto payments may not be whether an AI agent can send USDC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is what happens &lt;strong&gt;after the first payment works&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An agent that can spend $0.02 is useful. An agent that can automatically manage hundreds of transactions is far more powerful—and potentially far more difficult to control.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes wallet permissions, spending limits, merchant restrictions, automatic shutdown mechanisms and human escalation important parts of the emerging agentic-payment stack.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle, Cloudflare and infrastructure providers such as 0x are already building components for this environment. BlackRock's latest research suggests the economic opportunity could become much larger if AI agents begin conducting meaningful machine-to-machine commerce. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the next stage will be decided by actual usage, not just infrastructure announcements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If autonomous agents eventually become real economic actors, &lt;strong&gt;the question may shift from “Can an AI pay?” to “How much money should an AI be allowed to control?”&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>White House 'Fully Committed' to Passing CLARITY Act in September, Crypto Advisor Says</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhzHQs1Kxawl1-JjORmQSVQd4YvtUeyCccBQtMZK0C-R4EcKYpvFxwFnkpYDhdCBcG1IcxQEEiQ909iXI_vx09xXSw8KQxY1Tls_koXSSyIbtPNmVyaOoYu1ia-Wug2BRpaH7xjyADnCoG2mBLJxUYHyol5EL71ZqG2tOQHLRDULiVIGBf1qkwn2M4BvSQW/s1672/CLARITY%20Act%20and%20U.S.%20Crypto%20Regulation.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="CLARITY Act and U.S. Crypto Regulation" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhzHQs1Kxawl1-JjORmQSVQd4YvtUeyCccBQtMZK0C-R4EcKYpvFxwFnkpYDhdCBcG1IcxQEEiQ909iXI_vx09xXSw8KQxY1Tls_koXSSyIbtPNmVyaOoYu1ia-Wug2BRpaH7xjyADnCoG2mBLJxUYHyol5EL71ZqG2tOQHLRDULiVIGBf1qkwn2M4BvSQW/w320-h180/CLARITY%20Act%20and%20U.S.%20Crypto%20Regulation.png" title="U.S. Capitol surrounded by blockchain and cryptocurrency graphics representing the CLARITY Act and U.S. crypto regulation" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aug 12, 2026&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;– The Trump administration remains
"fully committed" to passing the CLARITY Act in September, according
to White House crypto advisor Patrick Witt, even as prediction markets have
slashed the bill's chances of becoming law this year to just 19%&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Witt, Executive Director of the President's Council of
Advisors for Digital Assets, confirmed the administration's stance in comments
posted on X on August 11, saying that "durable rules, the kind only
legislation can provide, are needed now more than ever"&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"Every time Democrats have delayed this bill,
America has fallen further behind in the digital asset race. This has
jeopardized our leadership role in global financial markets, weakening our
national security, and denying law enforcement the tools they need to stop
crypto crime."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;—&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Patrick Witt&lt;/b&gt;, Executive Director, President's
Council of Advisors for &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/white-house-fully-committed-to-passing.html"&gt;Digital Assets&amp;nbsp;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The September 15 Cloture Showdown&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) filed a cloture
motion on August 8, setting up a key procedural vote for&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;September 15
at 2:15 PM ET&lt;/b&gt;, one day after the Senate returns from its five-week August
recess&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What's at stake:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The cloture motion
requires&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;60 votes&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;to advance the bill and overcome a
Democratic filibuster. Republicans hold 53 Senate seats, meaning they need
support from at least seven Democrats to proceed&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The bill has already passed the House and cleared the Senate
Banking Committee 15-9 in May, but it has stalled in the full Senate over
disagreements on ethics provisions, developer liability, and stablecoin
regulations&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What's in the CLARITY Act&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The CLARITY Act would establish a comprehensive federal
framework for digital assets, ending the "regulation by enforcement"
approach that has dominated U.S. crypto policy&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Key provisions include:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Clear
     classification of digital assets as securities, commodities, or payment
     stablecoins&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Protections
     for non-custodial software developers and blockchain infrastructure
     providers&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Bankruptcy
     remoteness provisions to protect customer assets if an exchange
     fails&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Ethics
     rules for federal officials involved in crypto&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Increased
     funding for law enforcement to investigate crypto-related crime&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why Passage Remains Uncertain&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Despite the administration's push, analysts have reduced
their expectations for passage:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Polymarket&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;traders
     now price a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;19% chance&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;that the CLARITY Act becomes law
     in 2026 — down from above 50% during much of the spring&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;TD
     Cowen Washington Research Group&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;analyst Jaret Seiberg assigns
     a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;25% probability&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;of enactment this fall&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Two disputes remain unresolved ahead of the September
vote&amp;nbsp;:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol start="1" style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="1"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Ethics
     provisions:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Democratic senators have demanded stricter ethics
     rules targeting Trump-linked crypto interests&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Stablecoin
     rewards:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Banking industry groups have pushed back against
     provisions that could allow companies to pay rewards to stablecoin
     holders, arguing it could pull deposits away from community banks&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Developer liability&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;has also been a flashpoint.
A revised proposal backed by law enforcement and key Democrats would make it
easier to prosecute crypto software developers, but the White House has
dismissed the latest version as insufficient&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What Delay Means for Crypto&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The delay extends uncertainty for crypto exchanges, token
issuers, and investors who have been waiting for clearer federal rules
governing digital assets&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Grayscale Research Director Zach Pandl&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;said the
CLARITY Act now seems unlikely to pass Congress this year, noting that the
Senate's busy schedule and election-year politics make it difficult to reach a
bipartisan agreement&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;However, Pandl noted that failure of the bill "will not
directly impact the demand for Bitcoin as a store of value, the functioning of
major blockchains, or the growth in stablecoin payments in the short
term"&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Industry voices remain optimistic:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Cody Carbone,
CEO of crypto trade group &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/nvidia-helps-turn-ai-compute-into.html"&gt;Digital Chamber&lt;/a&gt;, said: "While this isn't the
result any of us hoped for when we began the week, the fight is far from over.
The next few weeks, we will continue to work to find the last pieces of common ground
needed to set up a successful vote when Congress returns in
September"&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What Happens Next&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If the cloture vote succeeds on September 15, the bill moves
toward a final passage vote. If it fails, the CLARITY Act may not get another
chance in 2026.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Federal regulators are moving on separate crypto rules in
the meantime. The SEC will hold an open meeting on&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;August 14&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;to
consider a proposal for a tailored offering regime covering certain investment
contracts involving crypto assets&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The regulatory track does not replace the CLARITY Act, which
would set broader market structure rules through legislation. But the SEC's
August meeting shows that federal agencies are preparing to act while Congress
works through the outstanding disputes&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

    <title>Poland’s Crypto Bill Veto Survives After Parliament Falls 25 Votes Short</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhUr8gqlIVbaZWQNKdnnCRnthyrNknrPYCbrTn-78IJhMubGzsMXD1THZVNzJaKu0oTf5jeIarvwKzcdTejpcCBkEUZw2j6fAXEQHYxNL-SQBUsMFQVuxTQqdrvN_86l3Hw79JTxY0n9f_YhB6ahAHhErfwGdj8W9-B0vcBdemHaEnicYo_F04oIL1DF5Y9/s1672/poland-crypto-bill-veto-karol-nawrocki-parliament.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Poland Parliament fails to override President Karol Nawrocki's crypto bill veto" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhUr8gqlIVbaZWQNKdnnCRnthyrNknrPYCbrTn-78IJhMubGzsMXD1THZVNzJaKu0oTf5jeIarvwKzcdTejpcCBkEUZw2j6fAXEQHYxNL-SQBUsMFQVuxTQqdrvN_86l3Hw79JTxY0n9f_YhB6ahAHhErfwGdj8W9-B0vcBdemHaEnicYo_F04oIL1DF5Y9/w640-h360/poland-crypto-bill-veto-karol-nawrocki-parliament.jpg.png" title="Poland Crypto Bill Veto Fails in Parliament" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;
September 7, 2026&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Poland’s parliament has failed for the third time to overturn President Karol Nawrocki’s veto of a cryptocurrency regulation bill, leaving the country’s planned domestic crypto-asset framework in limbo.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Sejm, Poland’s lower house of parliament, voted on September 4 to override the presidential veto. The motion received &lt;strong&gt;241 votes in favor, 198 against and three abstentions&lt;/strong&gt; among 442 lawmakers who voted. A three-fifths majority of &lt;strong&gt;266 votes&lt;/strong&gt; was required, leaving the override attempt &lt;strong&gt;25 votes short&lt;/strong&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Poland’s Crypto Bill Remains Blocked&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The failed vote means President Nawrocki’s veto remains in force and the latest version of the crypto regulation bill cannot move forward through a successful veto override.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The legislation was intended to establish a national regulatory framework for crypto-assets and give Poland’s Financial Supervision Authority, known as &lt;strong&gt;KNF&lt;/strong&gt;, a central role in supervising the sector.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The vote is particularly important because the European Union’s &lt;strong&gt;Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA)&lt;/strong&gt; is already in effect. Poland’s problem is not whether MiCA exists, but how the country organizes its domestic supervisory and licensing framework around the EU rules.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How the Sejm Vote Ended&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 600px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Vote&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Result&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Lawmakers voting&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;442&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;For overriding the veto&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;241&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Against&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;198&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Abstained&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;3&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Votes required&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;266&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Shortfall&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;25 votes&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because the three-fifths threshold was not reached, the president’s veto was not overturned. Polish media reported that this was the third attempt to push the legislation through after presidential opposition. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Did President Karol Nawrocki Veto the Bill?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;President Karol Nawrocki has not opposed the idea of regulating cryptocurrencies altogether. His objections have focused on the structure and scope of the proposed legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Nawrocki has argued that the government-backed framework could impose excessive regulatory and compliance burdens on the crypto industry. His position has been that Poland needs rules that protect consumers and the financial system without unnecessarily discouraging legitimate businesses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The president’s third veto came after lawmakers approved the latest version of the legislation in May. Reporting on the dispute says Nawrocki had previously raised a series of objections to the bill and maintained that many of those concerns had not been adequately addressed. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does the Failed Vote Mean for MiCA?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The failed veto override does &lt;strong&gt;not cancel MiCA&lt;/strong&gt;. MiCA is an EU regulation and continues to apply across the European Union.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The issue for Poland is its domestic supervisory framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Poland’s &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-is-my-bitcoin-transaction-still.html"&gt;financial regulator&lt;/a&gt;, KNF, said on September 4 that the country still had not designated a competent authority for supervision of the crypto-assets market. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters for crypto businesses. EU-wide rules can establish common requirements, but national authorities still have important responsibilities involving supervision and authorization of crypto-asset service providers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Poland’s transition period for certain existing crypto-asset service providers also reached its July 1, 2026 deadline under the relevant MiCA provisions, according to information published by KNF. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Crypto Companies Are Watching Poland&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The regulatory uncertainty could make it harder for businesses to determine how they should navigate licensing and supervision within Poland.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proposed legislation was designed to give KNF a clearer statutory role in overseeing crypto-asset activities. Without the bill becoming law, that domestic framework remains unresolved.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This does not mean that &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-you-recover-crypto-sent-to-the-wrong-network.html"&gt;cryptocurrency&lt;/a&gt; itself has been banned in Poland. Instead, the country remains caught between an EU-level regulatory framework and an unfinished national implementation structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Zondacrypto Investigation Adds Pressure&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest parliamentary debate also took place against the backdrop of an investigation involving the failed Polish crypto exchange Zondacrypto.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Prime Minister Donald Tusk cited the case while urging lawmakers to support the veto override. However, the investigation and the crypto regulation bill are separate matters, and allegations connected to the investigation should not be treated as established facts unless confirmed through the legal process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The political dispute nevertheless added urgency to the broader discussion about consumer protection, supervision and enforcement in Poland’s crypto market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next for Poland’s Crypto Regulation?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The failed override means the current legislation remains blocked by the presidential veto.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The political focus may now shift toward whether lawmakers can produce a revised framework that addresses the president’s objections while still giving Poland a functioning domestic structure for supervising crypto-asset activities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the industry, the key issue is whether Warsaw can resolve the regulatory gap without creating rules that businesses consider excessively burdensome.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For investors, the latest vote is mainly a regulatory development rather than a direct change to the operation of Bitcoin, &lt;a href="09/can-bitcoin-transaction-be-reversed.html"&gt;Ethereum &lt;/a&gt;or other cryptocurrencies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the Poland Crypto Vote Means in Simple Terms&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;President Karol Nawrocki vetoed Poland’s crypto regulation bill.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The Sejm tried to overturn the veto on September 4.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;241 lawmakers voted in favor of the override.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;198 voted against it and three abstained.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;266 votes were required.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The override therefore failed by 25 votes.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;This was the third failed attempt to overcome the presidential veto.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The bill would have established a stronger domestic framework for crypto-asset supervision, including a central role for KNF.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;MiCA remains applicable as EU law; the unresolved issue is Poland’s domestic supervisory framework.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Did Poland overturn President Karol Nawrocki’s crypto bill veto?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. The Sejm failed to obtain the three-fifths majority required to override the veto.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How many votes were needed to override the Poland crypto bill veto?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The Sejm needed 266 votes. The motion received 241 votes, leaving it 25 votes short. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What was the result of the Poland crypto bill vote?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;There were 241 votes in favor of overriding the veto, 198 against and three abstentions among 442 lawmakers who voted. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Was this the first time Poland tried to overturn the crypto bill veto?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. The September vote was the third attempt to overcome presidential opposition to the crypto legislation. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does the failed vote mean MiCA does not apply in Poland?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. MiCA remains an EU regulation. The unresolved issue is Poland’s domestic framework for supervising and authorizing crypto-asset activities. KNF said on September 4 that Poland had still not designated a competent authority for supervision of the crypto-assets market. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What regulator would oversee crypto under the proposed Polish framework?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The legislation was designed to give Poland’s Financial Supervision Authority, or KNF, a central supervisory role in the crypto-asset market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What happens after the failed veto override?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The current bill remains blocked. Further legislative action or a revised proposal would be needed to move Poland toward a new domestic crypto regulatory framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Sources&lt;/h2&gt;

    <content type='html'>&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgmGQSGkRinHh6BSu0InR3MqwbR8Q-OEf8psaBFWf2T-qIlBiubCt3mycpU-ht9eMJEuiHItI9bspbDwBoJCMiOPpKcOzeOO-mgVr66xUFxvxNx99HztRo5546e_MwRKk9qK-l3CWuTnJyMemyjWBYO0JkgIcbr1ab2tSMw6rl4P2HG5FGvSulpo_DHHNgF/s1672/sec-token-buybacks-altcoin-meta-crypto.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="SEC's New Stance on Token Buybacks Could Spark the Next Altcoin Meta" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgmGQSGkRinHh6BSu0InR3MqwbR8Q-OEf8psaBFWf2T-qIlBiubCt3mycpU-ht9eMJEuiHItI9bspbDwBoJCMiOPpKcOzeOO-mgVr66xUFxvxNx99HztRo5546e_MwRKk9qK-l3CWuTnJyMemyjWBYO0JkgIcbr1ab2tSMw6rl4P2HG5FGvSulpo_DHHNgF/s1600/sec-token-buybacks-altcoin-meta-crypto.jpg.png" title="SEC's new FAQ on token buybacks could spark the next altcoin meta, but only for projects with real revenue." /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Key Takeaways:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px; padding-left: 18px;"&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;SEC's new FAQ clarifies that token buybacks on functional networks are not automatically securities offerings.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Crypto projects spent $638 million on buybacks in 2026, up from $545 million in 2025.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;90% of that spending came from just two projects: Hyperliquid and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;a href="https://pump.fun/" rel="noreferrer" style="border-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0); border-image: none; border-style: solid; border-width: 2px 3px; color: #3964fe; margin-left: -3px; margin-right: -3px; position: relative; text-decoration: none; transition: box-shadow 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);" target="_blank"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Pump.fun&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Buyback-and-burn tokens have averaged -35% returns, excluding Hyperliquid.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The real question isn't whether buybacks are legal — it's whether they're funded by actual revenue.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;hr style="background: none 0% 0% / auto repeat scroll padding-box border-box rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1); border-color: currentcolor; border-image: none; border-style: none; border-width: medium; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; height: 1px; margin: 32px 0px;" /&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Crypto Rover posted a simple observation this week: "THIS COULD BE THE NEXT BIG META IN ALTCOINS!" He pointed out that money has been rotating from one narrative to another — RWA tokens, then AI, then DeFi. Now, he says, token buybacks could be next.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;He's not wrong about the pattern. But the data tells a more complicated story.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What the SEC Actually Said&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;On September 25, the SEC's Division of Corporation Finance published an updated FAQ on token buybacks. The key points:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;For functional networks:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; If a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/tether-freezes-nearly-550-million-in.html"&gt;crypto network&lt;/a&gt; is already functional, announcing a buyback doesn't, by itself, make the token a security. The "managerial efforts" prong of the Howey test isn't triggered.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;For non-functional networks:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; If the network isn't functional yet, and the issuer presents the buyback as a "source of returns," securities laws may apply.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Marketing rules:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Promoting existing uses of a network is generally fine. Promising future profits is not.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Gabriel Shapiro, a corporate securities attorney at MetaLeX Labs, wrote on X that the buyback section "goes further than I expected" and that regulators have "opened a loophole in a regulatory regime whose whole point was supposed to be that you couldn't draft your way around economic reality."&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;The Buyback Boom&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Here's where the numbers get interesting.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Crypto projects spent **$638 million** on buybacks in 2026, according to data cited by Cointelegraph. That's up from $545 million in the same period in 2025. In 2024, the figure was just $366,000.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;But the spending is heavily concentrated. Hyperliquid accounted for &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;$370 million**. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;a href="https://pump.fun/" rel="noreferrer" style="border-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0); border-image: none; border-style: solid; border-width: 2px 3px; color: #3964fe; margin-left: -3px; margin-right: -3px; position: relative; text-decoration: none; transition: box-shadow 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);" target="_blank"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Pump.fun&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; accounted for **$200 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;. Together, that's &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;90% of all buyback spending&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;. The remaining projects split just $68 million.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The performance gap is striking:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="ds-scroll-area ds-scroll-area--show-on-focus-within ds-scroll-area--enabled _1210dd7 c03cafe9" style="--container-height: 277px; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Source: TradingView data cited by Cointelegraph.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;But there's a catch. An analysis by Novora Research found that buyback-and-burn tokens delivered an average return of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;-35%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; — excluding Hyperliquid, that number drops to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;-56%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;. Of the 10 largest buyback tokens, only 3 outperformed &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/zuckerberg-says-superintelligence-will.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Messari analyst Sunny Shi put it bluntly: "Our analysis finds no clear evidence that the market rewards these initiatives. Token performance remains driven by metrics growth and narrative formation."&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Who's Buying Back — And How&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Hyperliquid (HYPE):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Uses 99% of its revenue for buybacks. Generated $169 million in revenue in Q2 2026, spent $141 million on buybacks.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://pump.fun/" rel="noreferrer" style="border-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0); border-image: none; border-style: solid; border-width: 2px 3px; color: #3964fe; margin-left: -3px; margin-right: -3px; position: relative; text-decoration: none; transition: box-shadow 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);" target="_blank"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Pump.fun&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; (PUMP):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Uses 50% of net revenue for buybacks. Annualized revenue of $420 million.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Travala (AVA):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Doubled its monthly buyback. First cycle bought 739,762 AVA. Tokens are locked in a reserve wallet — permanently removed from circulation.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Ethena (ENA):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; A fee-switch proposal would allocate 95% of net revenue to ENA buybacks. The token rose 10.7% after the proposal.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Spark (SPK):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Bought back 143 million SPK. But it didn't burn them — the tokens are held in treasury to reward long-term participants.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Lido (LDO):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Plans regular buybacks once it achieves $40 million in annualized revenue.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Why Buybacks Are Attractive&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Orest Gavryliak, Chief Legal Officer at 1inch, explained the appeal: "When projects implement revenue-funded buybacks and burns, they typically have one of two objectives in mind: either to decrease the token supply in circulation or to demonstrate the rationale for investing in protocol revenues."&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;He added: "Telling users a project has 'bought and burned tokens' is much more straightforward than explaining how governance rights work, how fees are set, or how the protocol is used."&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Max Shannon, Senior Research Associate at Bitwise Europe, said: "Buybacks and burns remain an effective way to accrue value to &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitmine-buys-another-17362-eth-total.html"&gt;tokenholders&lt;/a&gt;: they create a continuous bid in the open market for the token, directly tethering token success to the platform's adoption."&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;The Reality Check&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Three problems remain.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;1. Where does the money come from?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Every dollar spent on buybacks is a dollar not spent on developer hiring, product development, or business expansion.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;2. Only two projects dominate.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; 90% of buyback spending comes from Hyperliquid and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;a href="https://pump.fun/" rel="noreferrer" style="border-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0); border-image: none; border-style: solid; border-width: 2px 3px; color: #3964fe; margin-left: -3px; margin-right: -3px; position: relative; text-decoration: none; transition: box-shadow 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);" target="_blank"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Pump.fun&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; The mechanism works when there's revenue to fund it. Without revenue, it's just tokenomics theater.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;3. Regulatory risk isn't gone.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; The FAQ is staff guidance — not legally binding. The SEC Commission hasn't approved or disapproved it. As Shapiro warned: "A private plaintiff or a future SEC could have other ideas."&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What did the SEC say about token buybacks?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The SEC's FAQ says buybacks on functional networks don't automatically make a token a security. But buybacks on non-functional networks, presented as a source of returns, may trigger securities laws.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;How much have crypto projects spent on buybacks in 2026?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;$638 million, up from $545 million in 2025. But 90% of that came from just two projects: Hyperliquid and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;a href="https://pump.fun/" rel="noreferrer" style="border-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0); border-image: none; border-style: solid; border-width: 2px 3px; color: #3964fe; margin-left: -3px; margin-right: -3px; position: relative; text-decoration: none; transition: box-shadow 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);" target="_blank"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Pump.fun&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Do buybacks actually improve token performance?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The data is mixed. HYPE and PUMP have outperformed, but the average buyback-and-burn token has returned -35% this year.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Is the SEC's guidance legally binding?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;No. It's staff guidance. The SEC Commission hasn't voted on it, and future enforcement could take a different view.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Bottom line:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; The SEC's new FAQ gives token buybacks legal cover. But legal cover isn't the same as a working strategy. The projects that are winning with buybacks — Hyperliquid, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;a href="https://pump.fun/" rel="noreferrer" style="border-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0); border-image: none; border-style: solid; border-width: 2px 3px; color: #3964fe; margin-left: -3px; margin-right: -3px; position: relative; text-decoration: none; transition: box-shadow 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);" target="_blank"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Pump.fun&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; — have real revenue to fund them. The rest are copying the mechanism without the engine. If buybacks become the next meta, the winners will be the ones who can actually afford it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>
