    <title>Citi's Custody+ Launches: Bitcoin Custody Coming to Wall Street</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgFaSFo2lyMSO3lOqNRZcCqSYv-SFtoIwS0fCP28DgLNqCQWdAFsXgfv1wz7CQqJ1dbNwip7FEWOThKEofOV9NZFQmkbQmaYbJjG44-CG_skzx8bnof_-lFB0sFSDClYOTiBCCjQKOitDoPjdxQQBg5ufAhEuIseBIreCd2Ecn3K3j-o1SjivUNebtV3GHL/s1672/citi-custody-plus-bitcoin-wall-street.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Citi Bank building exterior representing traditional finance entering cryptocurrency custody with Bitcoin" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgFaSFo2lyMSO3lOqNRZcCqSYv-SFtoIwS0fCP28DgLNqCQWdAFsXgfv1wz7CQqJ1dbNwip7FEWOThKEofOV9NZFQmkbQmaYbJjG44-CG_skzx8bnof_-lFB0sFSDClYOTiBCCjQKOitDoPjdxQQBg5ufAhEuIseBIreCd2Ecn3K3j-o1SjivUNebtV3GHL/w320-h180/citi-custody-plus-bitcoin-wall-street.jpg.png" title="Citi Custody+ integrating Bitcoin into institutional banking and digital asset custody infrastructure" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/i&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For years, the crypto industry has waited for traditional
finance to build infrastructure capable of handling digital assets at
institutional scale. Citi has now taken another major step in that direction.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The bank has launched&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Custody+&lt;/b&gt;, a suite of near-
and real-time custody solutions, and expects to go live with digital asset
custody later this year, starting with&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/b&gt;. The move would
bring Bitcoin custody closer to the same institutional infrastructure used for
traditional assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Custody+ Actually Does&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Custody+ represents what Citi calls a "strategic shift
from a standardized and traditional custody model to a modular ecosystem of
solutions." In plain English: the bank is rebuilding its operational
backbone for a world that never sleeps.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The U.S. rollout of Citi's Single Event Processing
technology is complete, with more than 80% of total events now processed in
real time. Voluntary corporate actions now process up to 92% faster, with 96%
of U.S. voluntary events completed in under two hours.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Chris Cox, Head of Investor Services at Citi, put it this
way:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"Citi's Services business invests over US$2 billion
annually in its platform strategy with a focus on speed, scale and
availability. Custody+ is a clear example of this investment as we build
infrastructure to eliminate latency and drag for institutional investor
clients."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bitcoin Piece&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The key development for the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/crypto-regulation-could-reverse-without.html"&gt;crypto market&lt;/a&gt; is
straightforward:&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Citi expects to go live with digital asset custody
later this year, starting with Bitcoin&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Citi says the Bitcoin custody service is being built on its
common digital asset architecture, allowing traditional and digital assets to
be accessed within the same broader custody framework. The bank plans to offer
a "one-stop custody experience" where clients access traditional and
crypto custody capabilities within the same framework.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Nisha Surendran, who heads Citi's digital asset custody
buildout, described the initiative as an effort to&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;"make Bitcoin
bankable."&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;At the World Strategy Forum earlier this year, she
laid out the vision:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"Later this year, Citi will be launching our
infrastructure that integrates Bitcoin into traditional finance."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Client Problem&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Institutional investors have increasingly sought exposure to
digital assets through familiar banking and custody infrastructure rather than
managing crypto wallets and private keys directly.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Surendran explained that when Citi surveyed its clients, the
response was consistent: they want exposure to Bitcoin, but they want it within
familiar banking systems.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The bank is responding by offering a "single service
model across crypto, securities and money." From a client perspective, all
they need to do is give instructions—via SWIFT, APIs, or user interfaces.
Citi's proposed model is designed to handle the operational complexity around
custody, settlement and reporting, allowing clients to interact through
familiar banking channels.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The broader appeal is operational simplicity. Instead of
maintaining separate custody relationships and workflows for traditional
securities and digital assets, institutions could increasingly manage both
through a familiar banking infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Cross-Margining: The Real Big Picture&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;One of the more significant aspects of Citi's approach is
the potential interaction between traditional and digital assets within a
common custody structure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Surendran described a future account structure where
multiple asset types sit under a single master custody account: U.S.
Treasuries, foreign bonds, tokenized money market funds,&amp;nbsp;&lt;i&gt;and Bitcoin&lt;/i&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"The fact that all of these assets are accessible
within the same account structure makes it easier to use them for
cross-margining," she said.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A unified custody structure could eventually make it easier
for institutions to manage collateral across traditional and digital assets,
although the exact scope of any Bitcoin cross-margining capability has not been
fully detailed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Building for a 24/7 World&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Citi, which connects to more than 220 payment and settlement
networks globally, has already been adapting its systems for round-the-clock
support.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Citi already operates&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Citi Token Services&lt;/b&gt;, which
enables near-instant movement of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/which-smart-contract-standards-are.html"&gt;tokenized deposits&lt;/a&gt; on a 24/7 basis across
select markets. That existing infrastructure could help Citi support the
operational demands of assets that trade continuously, including Bitcoin.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"As we move into the world of 24/7 assets like Bitcoin,
we definitely need 24/7 U.S. dollars or 24/7 digital money," Surendran
said.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The custody initiative is part of Citi's broader
digital-assets strategy, which includes tokenized money, blockchain
infrastructure, custody and collateral mobility.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Citi's Custody+ launch is significant less because it
introduces another crypto custody product and more because it brings Bitcoin
closer to the infrastructure institutional investors already understand.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The bank expects to begin digital-asset custody later this
year with Bitcoin, while its broader Custody+ platform is designed around near-
and real-time processing, liquidity, settlement and asset servicing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Citi's move is another sign that major financial
institutions are moving digital assets closer to their existing institutional
infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If Citi successfully integrates Bitcoin into its traditional
custody environment, the move could reduce one of the biggest barriers facing
institutional adoption: operational complexity.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For the crypto market, the significance lies in the
infrastructure behind the announcement. Bitcoin is being positioned within
systems designed for institutional custody, reporting and asset servicing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That does not mean institutional adoption is guaranteed. But
it does show how digital assets are increasingly being incorporated into the
same financial infrastructure used by traditional markets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;Citi has announced the planned Bitcoin custody launch;
the service is expected to go live later in 2026.&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>

    <title>Elon Musk Says AI Could Add $20 Trillion to $30 Trillion a Year to the Global Economy</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

  &lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgE9hpxNGLM4AHXvFDLpW2z9G4F8yGAEzX8BOO1NWECBSPDstOezmvCVps-AcTrEbH5WNh2sVEUsfYDISh_jkvCGr0iSMp55RhTNK0MSKG-lcW95nIpcRE_FU0oEEoelTqXgR7LXTJwlYOjHRbNWXx9yikntctXT_Vlu9PIryBp3q9oc25ZK0zLChyphenhypheni2az5/s1672/elon-musk-ai-global-economy-30-trillion.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Elon Musk AI prediction for 20 to 30 percent global economic growth" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgE9hpxNGLM4AHXvFDLpW2z9G4F8yGAEzX8BOO1NWECBSPDstOezmvCVps-AcTrEbH5WNh2sVEUsfYDISh_jkvCGr0iSMp55RhTNK0MSKG-lcW95nIpcRE_FU0oEEoelTqXgR7LXTJwlYOjHRbNWXx9yikntctXT_Vlu9PIryBp3q9oc25ZK0zLChyphenhypheni2az5/w400-h225/elon-musk-ai-global-economy-30-trillion.jpg.png" title="Elon Musk Says AI Could Add $20T to $30T a Year" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;Elon Musk believes artificial intelligence could become one of the most powerful economic forces in modern history.
    Speaking by video at a G20 meeting in North Carolina, the Tesla and SpaceX CEO said AI could
    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: large;"&gt;“probably increase the global economy by 20% to 30%”&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;, which he estimated would be roughly
    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: large;"&gt;$20 trillion to $30 trillion per year&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The figure is enormous, but it is important to understand what it represents. Musk was making a
    &lt;strong&gt;forward-looking estimate&lt;/strong&gt;, not announcing a confirmed increase in global GDP or citing an official
    economic forecast. His argument is based largely on the potential productivity gains that could come from AI,
    automation and eventually humanoid robotics.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk's comments also came with a warning. He said the AI industry could face a major electricity constraint,
    with a potential &lt;strong&gt;15-gigawatt power shortfall for AI chips in 2027&lt;/strong&gt;. At the same meeting, the
    broader G20 discussion included AI regulation, energy infrastructure and the economic opportunities created by
    emerging technologies.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Musk's $20T–$30T AI Prediction Explained&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk's basic economic argument is straightforward: if AI allows people and businesses to produce more with the
    same amount of time and resources, overall productivity can rise.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    AI is already being used for software development, research, customer service, data analysis, financial
    workflows, marketing, content production and other digital tasks. If those capabilities become significantly
    more powerful, the productivity effect could spread across multiple industries.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That is the central idea behind Musk's estimate. He is not saying that AI companies will generate $30 trillion
    in annual revenue. Instead, he is talking about the potential increase in economic output created by
    AI-driven productivity and automation.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
    &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;thead&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Musk's Claim&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;What It Means&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/thead&gt;
      &lt;tbody&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;20%–30% increase in global economy&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Musk's estimate of AI's potential &lt;br /&gt;economic impact&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;$20T–$30T per year&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Musk's rough translation of that &lt;br /&gt;estimate into annual economic output&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;15 GW potential shortfall by 2027&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Musk's warning about electricity &lt;br /&gt;availability for AI chips&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;1 billion humanoid robots&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Musk's long-term robotics prediction&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/tbody&gt;
    &lt;/table&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why the Number Is So Large&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The key word is &lt;strong&gt;productivity&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Economic growth does not depend only on having more workers. It can also come from better technology that allows
    existing workers and businesses to produce more efficiently.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Computers transformed office work. The internet dramatically reduced the cost of communication and information
    distribution. Cloud computing changed how companies access computing resources.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk's thesis is that AI could become another general-purpose productivity technology, but with a major
    difference: increasingly capable &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/what-is-gotok-truth-behind-ai-project.html"&gt;AI systems&lt;/a&gt; could perform parts of the work themselves rather than simply
    helping humans perform those tasks.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;AI Could Move Beyond Chatbots&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The economic story around AI is already much larger than consumer chatbots.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Companies are developing AI systems for coding, research, engineering, customer support, data processing,
    image and video generation, scientific discovery and enterprise automation.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk expects this progression to happen very quickly. According to reporting on his G20 remarks, he predicted
    that AI could eventually handle virtually any digital task that does not require physically reshaping matter,
    with that capability potentially arriving by the end of next year.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Musk Predicts 'Stockfish-Level' AI for Software&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    One of Musk's most aggressive predictions concerns software development.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    He said AI software could become &lt;strong&gt;“Stockfish-level”&lt;/strong&gt; at some point next year, using the powerful
    chess engine as an analogy for a system that would outperform humans in a particular intellectual task.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk also predicted that AI could become extremely capable across engineering and other digital work within
    approximately &lt;strong&gt;12 to 18 months&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    These are predictions rather than established capabilities. Today's AI systems can already assist programmers
    with coding, debugging and software architecture, but the timeline for reaching the level Musk describes
    remains uncertain.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Humanoid Robots Could Expand the Economic Impact&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk's economic vision extends beyond software.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If AI remains primarily digital, its direct economic impact would be concentrated in information-based work.
    Humanoid robots could potentially take the technology into the physical economy.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk predicted that there could be &lt;strong&gt;at least one billion humanoid robots within a decade&lt;/strong&gt;, with
    each potentially producing several times the output of a human worker.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If such a scenario became technically and economically viable, the impact could extend into manufacturing,
    logistics, construction, agriculture and other physical industries.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    However, the billion-robot forecast is an ambitious long-term prediction and should not be interpreted as an
    established industry forecast.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The $30 Trillion Figure Does Not Mean $30 Trillion in AI Revenue&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This distinction is critical.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    When Musk discusses a potential $20 trillion to $30 trillion annual economic impact, he is not saying that
    artificial intelligence companies will collectively record $30 trillion in sales.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Economic value can appear indirectly through higher productivity.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;A factory could produce more goods with the same workforce.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;A software company could develop applications with fewer engineering hours.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;A logistics company could optimize routes and reduce wasted fuel.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;A hospital could automate administrative processes.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;A research organization could process scientific information faster.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If those productivity gains spread across millions of businesses, the aggregate economic effect could become
    significant.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Power May Become AI's Biggest Physical Constraint&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    One of the most important parts of Musk's G20 remarks was not about software at all. It was about electricity.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk warned that AI development could run into a serious power constraint and said analysts were expecting at
    least a &lt;strong&gt;15-gigawatt shortfall of power for AI chips in 2027&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    He also argued that AI-chip production is growing much faster than electricity capacity in some markets.
    The 15 GW figure is &lt;strong&gt;Musk's characterization of the expected shortfall&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than an
    independently established global forecast.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The underlying issue is real: advanced AI requires large amounts of computing capacity, and data centers need
    electricity not only for chips but also for cooling, networking and supporting infrastructure.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That means the AI race is increasingly becoming an energy and infrastructure race as well.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;SpaceX Is Already Spending Billions on AI Infrastructure&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The scale of SpaceX's own AI investment provides useful context for Musk's optimism.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    SpaceX reported approximately &lt;strong&gt;$18.4 billion in total capital expenditure during the second quarter of
    2026&lt;/strong&gt;, of which roughly &lt;strong&gt;$15.8 billion supported AI compute infrastructure&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The company's AI segment generated approximately &lt;strong&gt;$2.6 billion in Q2 revenue&lt;/strong&gt;, according to
    the company's earnings disclosures, while its AI compute capacity continued to expand.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This spending shows that the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitfinex-securities-lists-five.html"&gt;AI infrastructure&lt;/a&gt; buildout is not merely a theoretical concept for Musk's
    businesses. SpaceX is committing substantial capital to data-center and computing capacity.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    At the same time, investors have to consider whether such enormous capital expenditure can generate adequate
    long-term returns. Large AI infrastructure spending can create significant revenue opportunities, but it also
    creates substantial financial and execution risks.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;SpaceX's $60 Billion Cursor Deal&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    SpaceX has also expanded its AI strategy through Cursor, an AI-native software development platform.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    According to SpaceX's SEC filings, the Cursor merger was completed on &lt;strong&gt;August 14, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, with
    Cursor valued at an implied equity value of approximately &lt;strong&gt;$60 billion&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The deal is significant because it gives SpaceX a stronger position across several parts of the AI stack:
    computing infrastructure, AI models and software-development applications.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    It also illustrates the broader strategy behind Musk's AI ambitions: rather than investing only in models,
    the company is building or acquiring infrastructure and applications that can consume and monetize AI compute.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The G20 Debate Was Also About AI Regulation&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk's economic comments came during a broader G20 discussion about the future of artificial intelligence and
    emerging technologies.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The United States promoted the &lt;strong&gt;Carolina Principles&lt;/strong&gt;, a framework calling for new AI regulation
    to focus on genuinely novel situations rather than creating broad new rules for every emerging technology.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The approach reflects Washington's preference for a relatively light-touch regulatory environment designed to
    encourage AI investment and innovation.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The meeting also exposed differences over &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/does-blockchain-ever-actually-delete.html"&gt;AI governance&lt;/a&gt;. Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis argued for safety
    testing, while other technology executives emphasized innovation and avoiding restrictions that could slow
    development.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The regulatory debate matters economically because governments are effectively deciding how quickly AI can be
    deployed while trying to balance innovation, safety, competition and public trust.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Andrew Bailey Raises a Different AI Warning&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Not every discussion around AI's economic impact is optimistic.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Financial Stability Board Chair and Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned G20 finance ministers and
    central bank governors about the potential financial-system risks associated with frontier AI.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In an August 2026 letter to G20 finance officials, the Financial Stability Board said the
    &lt;strong&gt;most immediate concern for the financial system was the potential impact of frontier AI on cyber risk&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The FSB warned that increasingly capable AI systems could alter the speed, scale and economics of cyber risks,
    potentially affecting confidence across the financial system.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This provides an important counterweight to Musk's bullish economic outlook: AI could create enormous
    productivity gains while also introducing new financial, cybersecurity and operational risks.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Could AI Really Add $30 Trillion a Year?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Nobody can know that yet.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk's estimate depends on several assumptions:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ol&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;AI capabilities continue improving rapidly.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Businesses adopt AI across a wide range of industries.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;AI systems become reliable enough for important commercial tasks.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Computing costs decline relative to productivity gains.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Electricity and data-center capacity expand fast enough.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Robotics becomes technically and economically viable at scale.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Regulation does not significantly restrict deployment.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The economic gains from AI are large enough to offset disruption and transition costs.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ol&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If many of these conditions are satisfied, AI could have a very large economic effect.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    But if AI adoption is slower than expected, infrastructure remains expensive, electricity becomes scarce or
    technical limitations persist, the eventual economic impact could be substantially smaller.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Could AI Mean for Workers?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The labor market may ultimately determine how society experiences AI-driven growth.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    AI can make individual workers more productive, which could increase output and potentially raise demand for
    workers who know how to use the technology effectively.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    At the same time, automation could reduce demand for certain tasks and occupations where AI can perform work
    at lower cost.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The effect is unlikely to be uniform. Some jobs may be heavily automated, while others could become more
    valuable because AI handles repetitive tasks and allows humans to focus on judgment, creativity,
    relationships and physical work.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This means the economic impact of AI should not be measured only by GDP. The distribution of productivity gains
    will matter just as much.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Does Musk's Prediction Mean for Investors?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk's comments are clearly bullish on the long-term economic potential of AI, but investors should avoid
    treating a macroeconomic prediction as a simple trading signal.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A larger AI economy does not automatically mean that every AI company will succeed.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The eventual winners may depend on factors including:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Computing efficiency&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Energy availability&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Semiconductor supply&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Enterprise AI adoption&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Data-center economics&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Software distribution&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Robotics capability&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Capital efficiency&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Regulation&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In other words, &lt;strong&gt;AI's economic opportunity and an individual investment opportunity are two different
    things.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Picture: AI Could Become Economic Infrastructure&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Perhaps the most important part of Musk's prediction is not the exact $20 trillion or $30 trillion figure.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The larger idea is that AI could eventually become a general-purpose economic technology.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If AI becomes deeply integrated into software, factories, transportation, healthcare, finance, research and
    robotics, its economic footprint could become difficult to separate from overall productivity growth.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That would make AI much more than another software category. It would become part of the infrastructure through
    which the global economy operates.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Elon Musk says artificial intelligence could increase the global economy by &lt;strong&gt;20% to 30%&lt;/strong&gt;,
    equivalent to roughly &lt;strong&gt;$20 trillion to $30 trillion per year&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The number is extraordinary, but it should be treated exactly for what it is:
    &lt;strong&gt;Musk's forward-looking estimate of AI's potential economic impact&lt;/strong&gt;, not an established economic
    forecast or guaranteed increase in global GDP.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    His argument is based on a combination of AI-driven productivity, increasingly capable software systems,
    large-scale computing and eventually humanoid robotics.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    At the same time, Musk's own comments highlight the industry's biggest physical challenge: electricity.
    His warning about a potential 15 GW AI power shortfall by 2027 shows that the AI boom depends on much more than
    better algorithms.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    SpaceX's roughly $15.8 billion Q2 AI infrastructure spending and its $60 billion Cursor acquisition also show
    how aggressively Musk's businesses are positioning themselves around the AI economy.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Whether AI ultimately adds $20 trillion, $30 trillion or substantially less will depend on how quickly the
    technology improves, how widely businesses adopt it, how much infrastructure can be built and how governments
    manage the risks.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    For now, Musk's $20 trillion to $30 trillion figure is best viewed as
    &lt;strong&gt;a measure of the economic potential he sees in AI—not as a number the global economy has already
    achieved.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What did Elon Musk say about AI and the global economy?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Elon Musk said AI will probably increase the global economy by 20% to 30%, which he estimated at roughly
    $20 trillion to $30 trillion per year.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is Musk's $30 trillion AI estimate guaranteed?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    No. It is Musk's personal projection about the potential economic impact of AI. It is not a guaranteed increase
    in global GDP or an official consensus forecast.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Why does Elon Musk think AI could create so much economic value?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk's argument is primarily based on productivity gains from AI automation, increasingly capable digital
    systems and the eventual use of humanoid robots in physical work.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What did Musk say about AI power demand?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk warned that AI could face a significant electricity shortage and said analysts were expecting at least
    a 15-gigawatt power shortfall for AI chips in 2027.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What is Musk's Stockfish-level AI prediction?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk predicted that AI software could become “Stockfish-level” at some point next year and said AI could become
    extremely capable in engineering and other digital work within approximately 12 to 18 months.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;How many humanoid robots does Musk predict?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Musk has predicted that there could be at least one billion humanoid robots within a decade, with each
    potentially producing several times the output of a human worker.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;How much did SpaceX spend on AI infrastructure in Q2 2026?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    SpaceX reported approximately $15.8 billion of Q2 2026 capital expenditure supporting AI compute
    infrastructure, out of approximately $18.4 billion in total quarterly capital expenditure.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Did SpaceX acquire Cursor for $60 billion?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Yes. SpaceX's SEC filing states that the Cursor merger became effective on August 14, 2026, based on an
    implied equity value of approximately $60 billion.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What are the Carolina Principles?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The Carolina Principles are a U.S.-promoted framework discussed at the G20 technology meeting that favors
    reserving new AI regulation for genuinely novel situations while encouraging innovation and foundational
    research.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Did Andrew Bailey warn about AI risks?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Yes. Financial Stability Board Chair Andrew Bailey warned G20 finance officials that frontier AI could create
    significant cyber and financial-stability risks. The FSB identified the potential impact of frontier AI on
    cyber risk as its most immediate concern for the financial system.
  &lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Can Bitcoin Be Recovered Without a Seed Phrase?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEh5xsNMvyCAv1ybkp3Z4zVMhscM_dOeqn3WZ7k5OLDwQTR_PX67x0_6_5o1pRLOXqo_9YxPApmhP6xI8LnS0yYQe1SPr7eZUG3mSUETPNFNCnHQye5oNhy5-Zc1vmtqzwcQKKsJRbfrLcySukbuSNTGeJGy5x57o4Di3qKz6ShDgbLGcrvzernj6gDYonQy/s1671/bitcoin-recovery-without-seed-phrase.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Can Bitcoin be recovered without a seed phrase using a private key or wallet backup" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1671" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEh5xsNMvyCAv1ybkp3Z4zVMhscM_dOeqn3WZ7k5OLDwQTR_PX67x0_6_5o1pRLOXqo_9YxPApmhP6xI8LnS0yYQe1SPr7eZUG3mSUETPNFNCnHQye5oNhy5-Zc1vmtqzwcQKKsJRbfrLcySukbuSNTGeJGy5x57o4Di3qKz6ShDgbLGcrvzernj6gDYonQy/w640-h360/bitcoin-recovery-without-seed-phrase.jpg.png" title="Can Bitcoin Be Recovered Without a Seed Phrase?" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Can Bitcoin be recovered without a seed phrase? &lt;strong&gt;Sometimes—but only if another valid way to access the wallet's private keys still exists.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Losing a seed phrase does not automatically mean that Bitcoin is gone. A wallet may still be accessible on an existing device, a private-key backup may exist, or the Bitcoin may actually be held by a cryptocurrency exchange rather than controlled directly by the user.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is an important limit: if Bitcoin is held in a self-custody wallet and the owner has lost the seed phrase &lt;em&gt;and&lt;/em&gt; every other form of access to the corresponding private keys, there is generally no central authority that can simply reset the wallet and return the coins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin is designed around private-key ownership. A recovery phrase is one of the most common ways wallets back up those keys, but it is not the blockchain itself. The distinction matters when trying to determine whether apparently “lost” Bitcoin can actually be recovered.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Quick Answer: Can Bitcoin Be Recovered Without a Seed Phrase?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 760px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Situation&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Can BTC Be Recovered?&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Why&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Wallet still opens &lt;br /&gt;on an old device&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Possibly&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;The device may still contain the &lt;br /&gt;wallet's keys.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Private key was &lt;br /&gt;backed up&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Yes, if valid&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;A private key can authorize &lt;br /&gt;spending without entering the &lt;br /&gt;original seed phrase.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Bitcoin Core &lt;br /&gt;wallet backup exists&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Possibly&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Depending on the wallet and &lt;br /&gt;backup, the required key material &lt;br /&gt;may still be available.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;BTC is held on an &lt;br /&gt;exchange&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Often, yes&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;The exchange controls the wallet &lt;br /&gt;infrastructure; account recovery is &lt;br /&gt;different from self-custody recovery.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Only the Bitcoin &lt;br /&gt;address is available&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;No&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;A public address does not provide &lt;br /&gt;the private key needed to spend BTC.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Seed phrase and &lt;br /&gt;private keys are completely lost&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Generally no&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;There is no Bitcoin administrator &lt;br /&gt;who can reset ownership of a self-custody wallet.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What a Seed Phrase Actually Does&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A seed phrase, also called a &lt;strong&gt;recovery phrase&lt;/strong&gt; or mnemonic, is a sequence of words used to restore a wallet's key hierarchy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Modern Bitcoin wallets commonly use hierarchical deterministic &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ledger-cto-charles-guillemet-warns-ai.html"&gt;wallet designs&lt;/a&gt;. A recovery phrase can be used to derive the wallet's private keys and, from those keys, the corresponding public keys and addresses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org describes a recovery phrase as a sequence of words from which a wallet can be fully restored. Its documentation also explains that private keys are the secret data that prove the right to spend Bitcoin. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This leads to an important point:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The Bitcoin is not physically stored inside the seed phrase.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Bitcoin exists as spendable outputs recorded on the Bitcoin blockchain. The wallet holds or derives the cryptographic keys needed to authorize transactions spending those outputs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can You Recover Bitcoin With the Private Key Instead?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Yes, if you have the correct private key and the wallet software supports the relevant type of key or import process.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A private key is fundamentally different from a public &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-someone-steal-bitcoin-with-wallet-address.html"&gt;Bitcoin address.&lt;/a&gt; The public address can be shared to receive BTC, while the private key is secret information used to authorize spending.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org explicitly states that private keys prove the right to spend Bitcoin associated with a wallet. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Therefore, someone who lost the original seed phrase but still has the necessary private-key backup may not have lost access to the Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, private-key recovery can become complicated when a wallet contains many addresses or uses a hierarchical wallet structure. A single imported key may not reproduce an entire wallet's history or all of its addresses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If the Old Phone or Computer Still Has the Wallet?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the most important situations to check before assuming that Bitcoin is permanently lost.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If an old phone, computer or hardware wallet still has access to the wallet, the user may be able to regain control without immediately knowing the original seed phrase.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is a major security warning: &lt;strong&gt;do not start experimenting with an old wallet on an internet-connected device if the device may be compromised.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;First preserve the existing wallet and look for the wallet's official backup or export options. Do not send the seed phrase, private key or wallet backup to an unknown person offering recovery assistance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org recommends keeping wallet backups secure and warns that anyone who gains access to wallet backups or private keys may be able to spend the Bitcoin. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can an Old Bitcoin Core Backup Recover the Coins?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In some cases, an old Bitcoin Core wallet backup may still contain the necessary key material.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin Core uses hierarchical deterministic wallets, and Bitcoin.org explains that a single backup can be sufficient to recover &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-someone-find-your-name-from-bitcoin-wallet.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt; controlled by the wallet. The exact recovery process can depend on the wallet version, backup date and other wallet metadata. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why an old computer should not automatically be written off as useless just because the seed phrase cannot be found.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If a wallet backup exists, preserve the original file and avoid modifying or overwriting it while investigating recovery options.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If You Only Have the Bitcoin Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where the answer becomes much more definitive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;A Bitcoin address alone cannot be used to recover or spend the Bitcoin associated with it.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You can use a blockchain explorer to see transactions and the current or historical balance associated with an address, but the blockchain does not reveal the private key needed to authorize a transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's public nature can make a wallet look surprisingly transparent. Anyone can inspect transactions associated with an address, but visibility is not the same thing as spending authority.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is central to Bitcoin security.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can a Blockchain Explorer Recover Lost Bitcoin?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blockchain explorer can help you &lt;strong&gt;locate and verify&lt;/strong&gt; Bitcoin transactions, but it cannot recreate a lost private key or authorize a transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, if you know an old Bitcoin address, a blockchain explorer may show:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Bitcoin received by the address.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Transactions sent from the address.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Unspent Bitcoin associated with the address.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Transaction dates and amounts.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;What it cannot provide is the private key required to spend those unspent outputs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If the Bitcoin Is on Coinbase or Another Exchange?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This situation is different from self-custody.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When Bitcoin is held through a centralized exchange, the customer generally does not directly control the blockchain private keys for the exchange's underlying wallets. The user instead has an account with the platform.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means losing a seed phrase may not be relevant at all if the Bitcoin was purchased and kept on a custodial exchange account.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Account recovery may involve the exchange's identity-verification and account-security procedures rather than seed-phrase restoration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org makes the same distinction: users who keep Bitcoin with an exchange or another custodian depend on that third party to safeguard the funds and process withdrawals. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What About Wallets That Do Not Use Seed Phrases?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not every modern crypto wallet uses a traditional single seed-phrase recovery model.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Some wallet systems use alternative key-management approaches, including multi-party computation (MPC), social recovery or other backup mechanisms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In an MPC design, for example, control can be distributed across multiple key shares rather than relying on one complete private key stored in a single place.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means “no seed phrase” does not automatically mean “no recovery.” It depends entirely on how the particular wallet was designed and what recovery mechanisms the user configured.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, these systems should not be confused with a magical way of recovering Bitcoin from nothing. Some valid form of authorization or recovery material must still exist somewhere in the system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can a Forgotten Wallet Password Be Recovered?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sometimes—but this is different from losing a seed phrase.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A wallet may use a password to encrypt locally stored wallet data. If the wallet remains backed up and the correct recovery material exists, there may be a route to restore access.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But Bitcoin does not provide the same kind of universal password-reset system found in ordinary online banking.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org warns that there are very limited password-recovery options for self-custodied Bitcoin and emphasizes the importance of protecting wallet backups. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why guessing passwords repeatedly or using unknown “recovery tools” can be dangerous.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can a Bitcoin Recovery Service Recover Lost BTC?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Be extremely careful with anyone who claims they can recover Bitcoin simply because you provide a wallet address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A legitimate recovery process cannot manufacture a missing private key from a public address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There may be legitimate technical recovery situations where a person still has a damaged wallet file, encrypted backup, old device or partial key material. Those are very different from recovering Bitcoin from an address alone.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Never give your seed phrase or private key to someone claiming they need it to “recover” your Bitcoin.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org states that recovery information must be kept private and that legitimate services should not require users to hand over their recovery phrase. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If You Remember Most of the Seed Phrase?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This situation requires particular caution.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you have most of the words but one or more are missing, the correct recovery procedure depends on the wallet standard and the exact information you still possess.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BIP-39 uses a checksum, meaning that not every random combination of words represents a valid mnemonic. Some wallets may also use an additional passphrase, sometimes called a “25th word,” which changes the resulting wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ledger's explanation of BIP-39 notes that a passphrase is not recoverable from the mnemonic alone and that different passphrases can produce completely different wallets. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So finding the seed words is not necessarily enough if an additional passphrase was used.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can Bitcoin Be Recovered After Losing a Hardware Wallet?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Usually, losing the physical hardware wallet does not mean losing the Bitcoin.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the correct recovery phrase or another supported backup exists, the wallet can generally be restored on a compatible device.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The hardware device is primarily a tool for securely holding and using the private keys. The Bitcoin itself remains recorded on the blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The real problem occurs when the hardware wallet is lost &lt;em&gt;and&lt;/em&gt; the recovery material is also unavailable.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In that situation, the physical device may have been the only remaining route to the keys.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If the Seed Phrase Is Completely Lost?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are two very different scenarios.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Scenario 1: You Still Have Another Form of Access&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You may still have a recovery path if you have:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;An unlocked wallet on an existing device.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A valid private-key backup.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A compatible wallet backup file.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A functioning hardware wallet containing the keys.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;An exchange account holding the Bitcoin.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A configured alternative recovery mechanism.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In these cases, losing the seed phrase does not necessarily mean the Bitcoin is permanently inaccessible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Scenario 2: You Have Lost Every Form of Key Access&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the Bitcoin is self-custodied and you have lost the seed phrase, private keys, wallet backups and every device that still provides access, the situation is fundamentally different.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no Bitcoin customer-service department that can reset ownership of a self-custodied address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org puts it plainly: developers, miners, wallet providers and exchanges cannot recover funds that a user has permanently lost from a self-custodied wallet. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is not a temporary technical limitation. It is a consequence of Bitcoin's ownership model.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why You Should Not Send Your Seed Phrase to Anyone&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A recovery phrase is effectively a master backup for the wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If another person obtains it, they may be able to restore the wallet on their own device and spend the Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means a person asking for your seed phrase while claiming to be:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;a wallet support agent,&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;a blockchain investigator,&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;a recovery expert,&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;a hardware-wallet technician, or&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;a crypto security specialist&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;should be treated with extreme suspicion unless you are dealing through a verified official process—and even then, a legitimate support team should not need your secret recovery phrase.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Never publish your seed phrase in a screenshot, email, chat, website form or social-media post.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What to Do If You Think Your Bitcoin Is Lost&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you are trying to recover your own Bitcoin, avoid rushing into a transaction or installing random recovery software.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A safer sequence is:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Identify the wallet type.&lt;/strong&gt; Determine whether it was a hardware wallet, mobile wallet, desktop wallet or exchange account.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Find the original device.&lt;/strong&gt; An old phone or computer may still contain useful wallet data.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Look for legitimate backups.&lt;/strong&gt; Check whether you created a wallet backup or private-key backup.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Determine whether a seed phrase was actually used.&lt;/strong&gt; Some wallets use different recovery mechanisms.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check the blockchain address.&lt;/strong&gt; Confirm whether the BTC is still associated with the address you remember.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Do not expose secrets.&lt;/strong&gt; Never upload seed phrases or private keys to recovery websites.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Use official wallet documentation.&lt;/strong&gt; Recovery procedures vary between wallet implementations.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Preserve original files.&lt;/strong&gt; If an old wallet file exists, make a copy before attempting recovery.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Seed Phrase vs Private Key vs Bitcoin Address&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Can be shared, though &lt;br /&gt;it reveals transaction history&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Most Important Thing to Remember&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin recovery is ultimately about recovering &lt;strong&gt;control of the cryptographic keys&lt;/strong&gt;, not recovering coins from the blockchain itself.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you still possess the keys—or a valid method of recreating them—the Bitcoin may be recoverable even without the original seed phrase.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If all key material and all valid recovery paths are gone, however, knowing the address or seeing the Bitcoin on a block explorer does not give you the ability to spend it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can Bitcoin be recovered without a seed phrase?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes, in some circumstances. If you still have the relevant private key, an accessible wallet, a valid wallet backup, a functioning hardware wallet or a custodial exchange account, you may still have a way to regain access. If every form of key access is gone from a self-custody wallet, recovery is generally not possible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can I recover Bitcoin using only my wallet address?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. A Bitcoin address can help you identify and monitor funds on the blockchain, but it does not provide the private key required to spend them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can a private key recover Bitcoin without the seed phrase?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes, where the private key controls the relevant Bitcoin and the wallet software supports the appropriate import or spending method. A private key is the cryptographic authorization needed to spend the associated funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can a Bitcoin exchange recover my lost seed phrase?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the Bitcoin was held in a self-custody wallet, an exchange generally cannot recover its private keys for you. If the Bitcoin was held in an exchange account, however, account recovery is a separate process because the exchange is the custodian.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What if I lost my Ledger or other hardware wallet?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Losing the physical device does not necessarily mean losing the Bitcoin. If the correct recovery phrase or another valid backup exists, the wallet can generally be restored using the manufacturer's supported recovery process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can a blockchain explorer recover lost Bitcoin?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. A blockchain explorer can show transaction history and unspent funds, but it cannot reconstruct a missing private key.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can someone recover my Bitcoin if I give them my seed phrase?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You should never give your seed phrase to another person. Anyone who obtains the recovery phrase may be able to restore the wallet and spend its funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Bitcoin permanently lost if the seed phrase is missing?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not necessarily. The seed phrase is one recovery method. The decisive question is whether another valid form of access to the wallet's private keys still exists.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Can Bitcoin be recovered without a seed phrase? Sometimes—but not from a public address alone.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A lost seed phrase does not automatically destroy access to Bitcoin if the owner still has a private key, wallet backup, accessible device, hardware wallet or another supported recovery method.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But self-custody comes with a hard boundary: if the private keys and every valid backup or recovery method are permanently gone, there is no central Bitcoin authority that can reset ownership and return the coins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why the safest approach is not to search for a “Bitcoin recovery trick” after losing access. The better strategy is to understand exactly which wallet was used, preserve every legitimate backup that remains and never hand a seed phrase or private key to anyone claiming they can magically recover the funds.&lt;/p&gt;
