border-color: currentcolor; border-image: none; border-style: none; border-width: medium; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; height: 1px; margin: 32px 0px;" /&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Thieves in Fremont, California, stole two Nvidia-branded trailers expecting them to be packed with high-end AI GPUs worth millions of dollars. Instead, they found 40,000 pounds of sand.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The trailers were reported stolen earlier this week from a logistics yard in Fremont, according to the San Francisco Standard. The theft was caught on CCTV footage, which showed the trailers being moved out of the yard late at night.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What actually happened&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The thieves targeted the trailers because of the Nvidia branding. Nvidia is the hottest name in tech right now, and its AI chips are worth more than gold on the black market. A trailer full of H100s or B200s could be worth tens of millions of dollars.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Nvidia recently partnered with &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitcoin-needs-95300-to-flip-meta-and-re.html"&gt;PlusAI&lt;/a&gt;, a self-driving truck company, to test autonomous freight routes in California. The Nvidia branding on the trailers may have been connected to that partnership — but the trailers themselves were not carrying GPUs.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;When the thieves opened the trailers, they found sand. 40,000 pounds of it. That's roughly 18,000 kilograms. Enough to fill a small swimming pool.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Why 40,000 pounds of sand?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;That's the part nobody has fully explained yet. Sand isn't a normal cargo for Nvidia-branded trailers. But there are a few possibilities:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;1. It was a decoy.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Companies shipping high-value electronics sometimes use decoy loads to throw off thieves. The idea is simple: if someone is watching the yard, they'll target the trailer with the fancy branding. If that trailer is full of sand, the real shipment moves safely somewhere else.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;If that's what happened here, it worked perfectly. The thieves took the bait, and the actual GPUs — if there were any — stayed safe.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;2. It was mislabeled cargo.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Logistics is messy. Trailers get mislabeled, cargo gets swapped, and mistakes happen. It's possible that the sand was supposed to go somewhere else, and the Nvidia branding was just a coincidence.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;But 40,000 pounds of sand on an Nvidia-branded trailer? That's a strange coincidence.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;3. It was a setup.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Some reports suggest the trailers were intentionally staged to catch thieves in the act. If that's the case, law enforcement might have been watching the whole time. The thieves walked into a trap, and the sand was just the punchline.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;We don't know which one it is yet. But all three are plausible, and each one tells us something different about how the AI hardware market operates.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Why this matters for the AI industry&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Nvidia's GPUs are the backbone of the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/uk-banks-complete-first-interbank.html"&gt;AI boom&lt;/a&gt;. Companies like OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Meta are buying them as fast as Nvidia can make them. Demand is so high that GPUs are being stolen, smuggled, and resold on black markets around the world.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;This isn't the first time. Earlier this year, there were reports of GPU thefts from data centers and warehouses. In one case, thieves made off with over $1 million worth of Nvidia chips. In another, a shipment of GPUs disappeared from a truck stop in California.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;We covered that truck stop theft in detail here: [link to previous article]. The pattern is clear: AI hardware is valuable, and criminals know it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;A single Nvidia H100 can sell for $25,000 to $40,000 on the open market. On the black market, the price can be even higher, especially in countries where export controls make it hard to buy directly from Nvidia.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;That's why stories like this one matter. They're funny, sure. But they also highlight a real problem: the AI supply chain is under pressure, and thieves are taking advantage of it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What happens next&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Fremont police have confirmed they are investigating the incident. The trailers have been recovered, but the sand — and the thieves — are still being traced. No arrests have been made.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Nvidia hasn't commented publicly on the incident.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;But one thing is certain: whoever stole those trailers is having a very bad day. They expected gold and got sand.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;If the trailers were a decoy, then the company that set them up is probably laughing right now. If it was a mistake, then someone in logistics has a lot of explaining to do. And if it was a setup, then the thieves walked into a trap that was designed specifically for them.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Either way, the story is a reminder that in the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitgets-3875-million-hack-on-chain.html"&gt;AI gold rush&lt;/a&gt;, not everyone who looks like they're winning is actually winning.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Why was there sand in the Nvidia trailers?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;There are three possible explanations: it was a decoy load, it was mislabeled cargo, or it was a setup to catch thieves. Investigators haven't confirmed which one yet.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Were the trailers actually carrying GPUs?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;No. The trailers were reportedly empty except for the sand. There's no evidence that they ever contained AI GPUs.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Has anyone been arrested?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Not yet. Fremont police are investigating, and no arrests have been reported.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;How much are Nvidia GPUs worth on the black market?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;A single Nvidia H100 can sell for $25,000 to $40,000 on the open market. Black market prices can be higher, especially in countries with export controls.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Bottom line:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Thieves thought they were stealing millions in AI GPUs. They got 40,000 pounds of sand instead. It's a funny story, but it shows how crazy the demand for AI hardware has become — and how far people are willing to go to get their hands on it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</content>

    <title>Saudi Arabia Withdraws From China-Led mBridge Digital Currency Platform After Completing Pilot</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjcWB3V3EulLj7tFDebR_Mq_5Hwl8elQC84qwXh43ZhWrCEKII6iClDeNJ5JC_60SzSWgf280flcjXFB50HS9D8-GVnrRzrd_Ve1SdRRDdJQeF22WZaCF6x-ZzuAR22COkuQqeuk33C215hpa6OfjE8m7cR_CEM69Kk-BMnnI4-FpIjHWHQtUpF_JzESkWn/s1734/saudi-arabia-mbridge-china-digital-currency-platform.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Saudi Arabia withdraws from China-led mBridge digital currency platform after completing its pilot" border="0" data-original-height="907" data-original-width="1734" height="334" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjcWB3V3EulLj7tFDebR_Mq_5Hwl8elQC84qwXh43ZhWrCEKII6iClDeNJ5JC_60SzSWgf280flcjXFB50HS9D8-GVnrRzrd_Ve1SdRRDdJQeF22WZaCF6x-ZzuAR22COkuQqeuk33C215hpa6OfjE8m7cR_CEM69Kk-BMnnI4-FpIjHWHQtUpF_JzESkWn/w640-h334/saudi-arabia-mbridge-china-digital-currency-platform.webp.png" title="Saudi Arabia Withdraws From China-Led mBridge Digital Currency Platform" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Saudi Arabia has withdrawn from mBridge&lt;/strong&gt;, a China-led cross-border digital currency platform designed to make international payments faster and more efficient while reducing some of the traditional reliance on correspondent banking and intermediary currencies.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) confirmed that it stopped participating in the project after successfully completing its proof-of-concept phase on &lt;strong&gt;May 13, 2025&lt;/strong&gt;. The withdrawal was not announced publicly at the time and became widely reported on &lt;strong&gt;September 20, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Importantly, SAMA said its departure was part of the original plan for its participation. That means the decision should not automatically be interpreted as evidence that Saudi Arabia abandoned digital-currency research or that the country withdrew because of pressure from the United States.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Saudi Arabia Completed Its mBridge Proof of Concept in 2025&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SAMA first joined the mBridge project as an observing member in 2023. In 2024, Saudi Arabia became a full participant as the platform moved toward its minimum viable product, or MVP, stage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to SAMA, its participation focused on research into wholesale central bank digital currencies and their potential use in improving cross-border &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/coinbase-ceo-says-sec-and-cftc-rules.html"&gt;payment &lt;/a&gt;and settlement between commercial banks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SAMA later confirmed that its mBridge proof of concept was successfully completed on &lt;strong&gt;May 13, 2025&lt;/strong&gt;. Following completion of that exercise, the Saudi central bank was no longer a participating member of the project.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Financial Times reported the development on September 20, 2026, bringing public attention to a withdrawal that had occurred more than a year earlier. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is mBridge?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;mBridge is a multi-central-bank digital currency project developed to explore how distributed ledger technology can be used for cross-border payments and settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The project was developed through cooperation involving the &lt;strong&gt;Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Innovation Hub, the Bank of Thailand, the Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates, the Digital Currency Institute of the People's Bank of China and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority&lt;/strong&gt;. Saudi Arabia joined as a full participant in 2024.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The platform reached its &lt;strong&gt;minimum viable product stage in mid-2024&lt;/strong&gt;. The BIS says mBridge was designed to explore a shared multi-central-bank digital currency infrastructure capable of supporting instant cross-border payments and settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Its underlying technology uses distributed ledger technology, with the mBridge Ledger designed to support real-time peer-to-peer &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/brazil-securities-regulator-launches-tokenization-working-group.html"&gt;cross-border payments&lt;/a&gt; and foreign-exchange transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The project's stated objectives included addressing some of the major problems associated with conventional international payments, including high costs, slow settlement and operational complexity. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why mBridge Matters for Cross-Border Payments&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional international payments can involve multiple financial institutions, correspondent banks and payment networks before money reaches its final destination. That structure can increase costs, settlement times and operational complexity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;mBridge was designed to investigate whether multiple jurisdictions could instead connect through a common digital infrastructure using central bank digital currencies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In practical terms, the technology could allow participating financial institutions to settle eligible cross-border transactions more directly using digital representations of central bank money.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS has described the project as an attempt to make cross-border payments more immediate, cheaper and more accessible while addressing inefficiencies in existing correspondent-banking arrangements. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could mBridge Reduce Reliance on the U.S. Dollar?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the reasons mBridge has attracted international attention.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The platform was not created as a replacement currency for the U.S. dollar. Instead, its technology could reduce the need for an intermediary currency in some cross-border transactions by allowing participating jurisdictions to settle directly through their own central-bank digital currencies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Financial Times reported that the system is intended to reduce the role of the dollar as an intermediary in certain foreign-exchange transactions. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important. It would be inaccurate to say that mBridge has replaced the dollar, or that Saudi Arabia's withdrawal represents the collapse of the dollar-based international financial system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, mBridge represents one of several experiments by central banks around the world to improve cross-border payment infrastructure and explore alternatives to parts of the traditional correspondent-banking model.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Saudi Arabia Says the Withdrawal Was Planned&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Saudi position is central to understanding the development.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SAMA said it initially joined mBridge under the BIS umbrella as an observing member in 2023. It subsequently participated in development of the platform's minimum viable product and its proof-of-concept work.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The central bank said it successfully completed its proof of concept on May 13, 2025, and was no longer a participating member after that stage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That explanation indicates that Saudi Arabia's formal participation was structured around a specific research and testing phase rather than an open-ended commitment to the platform.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Therefore, the Saudi withdrawal should not be presented as proof that Riyadh rejected wholesale CBDCs, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/clarity-act-stalls-in-senate-as_01396500536.html"&gt;blockchain&lt;/a&gt;-based payment infrastructure or cross-border digital currencies altogether.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Was Saudi Arabia Pressured by the United States?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There has been speculation about whether geopolitical pressure influenced Saudi Arabia's decision, particularly because mBridge has attracted attention in Washington.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, there is no verified evidence establishing that U.S. pressure was the reason for Saudi Arabia's withdrawal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Financial Times reported that a person familiar with the situation said it would be inaccurate to draw a broader inference from the Saudi decision or directly link it to U.S. pressure, given the limited nature of Saudi Arabia's involvement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Another person familiar with the matter told the newspaper that SAMA no longer wanted to remain publicly involved with the project, while suggesting that some engagement could continue more discreetly. That claim is attributed to the source and should not be treated as an official Saudi policy statement. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The safest interpretation, based on the available public evidence, is therefore that Saudi Arabia completed its planned proof-of-concept participation and subsequently ended its formal membership.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The BIS Also Left mBridge in 2024&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Saudi Arabia is not the only institution whose formal role in mBridge has changed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Bank for International Settlements announced in October 2024 that it was handing the project over to the participating central banks after the platform reached the MVP stage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS currently lists Project mBridge as &lt;strong&gt;“Concluded”&lt;/strong&gt;. Its project page says the initiative was handed over to its central-bank partners in October 2024.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Former BIS General Manager Agustín Carstens described the institution's departure as having “graduated out” of the project rather than leaving because the initiative had failed. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is another reason why the timeline matters: the BIS's formal exit and Saudi Arabia's later withdrawal were separate events.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Saudi Arabia's Digital Payments Strategy&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SAMA's participation in mBridge was part of a broader effort to examine how emerging financial technology could improve cross-border payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When Saudi Arabia joined the mBridge MVP platform in June 2024, SAMA said it was investigating wholesale CBDCs and their potential to improve the effectiveness of cross-border payment and settlement between commercial banks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SAMA also described its participation as part of its effort to build a robust and innovative cross-border payments infrastructure in cooperation with international financial institutions and central banks. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Saudi Arabia's withdrawal from one project therefore does not by itself establish a broader reversal of the country's interest in digital payment technology.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;China's Role in mBridge&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;China has been one of the major participants in mBridge through the Digital Currency Institute of the People's Bank of China.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The project grew out of international cooperation that began in 2021, involving China, Hong Kong, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates and the BIS Innovation Hub.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The platform's development has attracted geopolitical attention because a payment infrastructure that allows direct digital-currency settlement between jurisdictions could eventually change how some international transactions are conducted.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, mBridge should not be described as a Chinese replacement for the global financial system. It is more accurately described as a multi-jurisdictional payment technology project in which China is a major participant.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Saudi Arabia's Exit Does Not Mean mBridge Has Failed&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Saudi Arabia's withdrawal is significant, but it does not mean the mBridge project itself has failed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS has already handed the project to participating central banks, and the platform has continued to attract interest from other jurisdictions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to the Financial Times, the Monetary Authority of Macao joined the platform in 2026 and activated the system for participating banks in June. The development indicates that activity around the platform has continued despite changes in individual participants.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Business Standard also reported that Macao launched the system in June 2026 and that participating banks conducted cross-border transactions through the platform. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Saudi Arabia's Withdrawal Means for the Dollar&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The development is likely to receive attention because Saudi Arabia has traditionally been closely connected to the dollar-based global financial system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But one country's withdrawal from a digital payment experiment does not fundamentally change the international role of the U.S. dollar.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;What mBridge demonstrates is that central banks are actively investigating technologies that could make some international payments less dependent on traditional intermediary structures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If such systems become widely adopted, they could change the mechanics of cross-border payments over time. But that is a longer-term possibility rather than an established outcome.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The dollar remains deeply embedded in international trade, foreign-exchange markets, banking and global financial infrastructure. mBridge should therefore be viewed as part of the broader evolution of payment technology rather than as evidence that a new global currency system has already emerged.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens to mBridge Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next stage for mBridge will depend on how participating jurisdictions develop the platform and whether commercial banks use it for larger volumes of real-world transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS says the MVP platform was capable of real-value transactions, subject to jurisdictional readiness, and was designed to support additional technology solutions, new use cases and interoperability with other platforms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The future significance of mBridge will therefore depend less on the participation of any single country and more on whether the underlying infrastructure can achieve sustained adoption across multiple jurisdictions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Saudi Arabia has withdrawn from the China-led mBridge digital currency platform after completing its planned proof of concept on &lt;strong&gt;May 13, 2025&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SAMA's explanation is that the proof-of-concept phase was successfully completed and that its participation ended as planned. The withdrawal became publicly known in September 2026.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;While mBridge has geopolitical implications because its technology could allow some cross-border transactions to occur without the dollar serving as an intermediary, there is no verified basis for stating that Saudi Arabia left because of U.S. pressure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The development is best understood as another step in the rapidly evolving global experiment with central bank digital currencies, distributed-ledger payment infrastructure and faster cross-border settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, mBridge remains an important case study in how central banks are exploring new ways to move money across borders — and how technology, monetary policy and geopolitics increasingly intersect in the future of global payments.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Bitwise CIO Sees Bitcoin at $1.3M by 2035 as Institutional Demand Grows</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiI6kiX5S1YVtgN3MgnhwucSePRzm3yRmwjoIDT1JEokKu4ExR1RfgPJd7puDYkNpLqiqEdDXPQP3aBXPguJxzALkjKFl-TmmvIkWRdgRDb26baUusCugB9UPkXYUUK_6gNIZ5eyVAHnW-_Bm80Nuc0j0i2MNSSg15Z7BsOwqh0DVKllKJGG9ytHnrVsxeq/s1402/Matt%20Hougan,%20Bitwise%20Chief%20Investment%20Officer.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan Bitcoin 1.3 million by 2035 institutional demand forecast" border="0" data-original-height="1122" data-original-width="1402" height="256" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiI6kiX5S1YVtgN3MgnhwucSePRzm3yRmwjoIDT1JEokKu4ExR1RfgPJd7puDYkNpLqiqEdDXPQP3aBXPguJxzALkjKFl-TmmvIkWRdgRDb26baUusCugB9UPkXYUUK_6gNIZ5eyVAHnW-_Bm80Nuc0j0i2MNSSg15Z7BsOwqh0DVKllKJGG9ytHnrVsxeq/w320-h256/Matt%20Hougan,%20Bitwise%20Chief%20Investment%20Officer.png" title="Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan predicts Bitcoin 1.3M by 2035 institutional allocation growth" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aug 10, 2026&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;– Bitwise Chief Investment Officer
Matt Hougan has laid out a bold vision for Bitcoin's long-term
trajectory:&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$1.3 million per coin by 2035&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The forecast comes from Bitwise's 2025 Capital Market
Assumptions report, which projects a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;28.3% compound annual growth rate&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;for
Bitcoin over the next decade. The math behind the prediction starts not with
crypto but with gold. Hougan's case rests on a simple but staggering
calculation: a 1% allocation from global institutions managing between&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$100
trillion and $200 trillion&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in assets could represent $1 trillion to $2
trillion in fresh capital entering the Bitcoin market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"The first professional investors to allocate at scale
will be financial advisers and family offices," Hougan said in an email
interview with CoinDesk. "It's a process that will take 10+ years."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Gold Comparison That Drives the Math&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Hougan's $1.3 million Bitcoin price target by 2035 rests on
Bitcoin taking a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;25% share of an expanding store-of-value market&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Hougan's scenario assumes the store-of-value market
continues expanding at roughly its historical pace. If that holds for another
decade, and Bitcoin captures a quarter of the market, the math points to $1.3
million per coin.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"When people value bitcoin, they often talk about it as
competing with gold for the 'store of value' market," Hougan explained.
"They say something like: Gold is a $30 trillion asset. If bitcoin can
take 50% of the market, each bitcoin will be worth $715,000."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Institutional Math: $1 Trillion to $2 Trillion in
Fresh Capital&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Global institutions — including foundations, endowments,
pension plans, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, and central banks —
control between&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$100 trillion and $200 trillion&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A 1% allocation across that pool could represent&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$1
trillion to $2 trillion&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in capital directed toward Bitcoin. To put
that in perspective, Bitcoin's total market capitalization currently sits well
below $2 trillion.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"Retail investors have driven the cryptocurrency market
from zero to a $2 trillion market cap," Hougan said. "Over the next
decade, institutional capital will become the primary growth force."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Shift Is Already Visible&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The institutional rotation is already beginning, Hougan
said.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Early evidence:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;13F
     filings&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;for spot Bitcoin ETFs show institutional interest growing&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Financial
     advisers and family offices are the&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;first movers&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"Financial advisers and family offices are the first
professional investors to allocate at scale," Hougan said.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why Strategy's Buying Edge Is Fading&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Strategy remains the world's largest corporate Bitcoin
holder. However, Hougan believes it will no longer be the primary driver of
Bitcoin demand.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Two advantages that made Strategy's buying machine work
have weakened:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol start="1" style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="1"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Stock
     premium compressed:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Strategy's stock once traded at a premium to
     the value of its Bitcoin holdings because it was one of the few
     public-market proxies for crypto exposure. Spot ETFs now offer a direct
     alternative, making that premium harder to sustain.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Debt
     capacity constrained:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Hougan argues that Strategy's previous
     financing advantages have become harder to exploit at the same scale.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"The easy paths to accumulation have been
exhausted," Hougan said. Strategy will continue buying Bitcoin, he added,
but at a slower pace and more closely tied to the price cycle.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What This Means for Long-Term Investors&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"For long-term investors, the key question is not about
short-term price floors," Hougan said.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"The much better question is if the top is in."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Hougan's $1.3 million prediction is not a short-term call.
It's a long-term bet on:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Institutional
     adoption&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;unfolding over the next decade&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Bitcoin
     taking a meaningful share of an&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;expanding store-of-value market&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;The&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$100
     trillion to $200 trillion&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;institutional pool gradually allocating
     to digital assets&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"Institutions have most of the money in the
world," Hougan said. "Crypto grew up in retail, which took it from $0
to $2 trillion. But if it wants to get from $2 trillion to $20 trillion, it's
going to be institutional capital that leads the way."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

What THORChain Said:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span&gt;THORChain highlighted that Bitcoin's isolation forces users to rely on centralized platforms for cross-chain transactions. This undermines Bitcoin's original vision as a &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=define+peer-to-peer+currency&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=884404330691878912" target="_blank"&gt;peer-to-peer currency&lt;/a&gt; without intermediaries.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;2. The Problem:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px; padding-left: 18px;"&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important; margin: 0px;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;Bitcoin's market cap &amp;gt; $1.5T, but usability within &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=what+is+DeFi+crypto&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=884404330691878912" target="_blank"&gt;DeFi&lt;/a&gt; and other ecosystems is restricted.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important; margin: 0px;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;Any transition from $BTC requires interactions with centralized custodians (exchanges or wrapped BTC like WBTC).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important; margin: 0px;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;This creates dependency chains linked to traditional financial systems.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;3. THORChain's Solution:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span&gt;THORChain aims to enable &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;native BTC swaps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt; directly into other cryptocurrencies without central custodians. This preserves Bitcoin's core values while enhancing &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=define+interoperability+blockchain&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=884404330691878912" target="_blank"&gt;interoperability&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;4. Why It Matters:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px; padding-left: 18px;"&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important; margin: 0px;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;If successful, this could significantly influence retail investor behavior.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important; margin: 0px;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;Regulatory scrutiny around crypto intensifies—decentralized solutions reduce reliance on traditional financial networks.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important; margin: 0px;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;Other projects (like cross-chain bridges and liquidity protocols) are also working on similar interoperability solutions.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;5. Market Impact:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif;     <title>BIS Researchers Test XRP Ledger to Verify Official Statistics Onchain</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjKM_Ni8WMPhD3EZ3hcF1_Jgrgu7U8R6YP6Nzcnqa0cL7hbEqxNrLM_aeuhkmlhojqWsZyzjxO4fhLHtnlMIPnArY2E95MWmlcYRm4Hp28l4PSgRpngOgnnzP13aZrVH93Vk0c_89ZkZK3dEy3NcblnmhLEUwuCWOdlG7VwsgOZKSGPnfJDDrY17cDDe22w/s1672/bis-xrp-ledger-official-statistics-verification.jpg.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="BIS researchers test XRP Ledger to verify official statistics onchain" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjKM_Ni8WMPhD3EZ3hcF1_Jgrgu7U8R6YP6Nzcnqa0cL7hbEqxNrLM_aeuhkmlhojqWsZyzjxO4fhLHtnlMIPnArY2E95MWmlcYRm4Hp28l4PSgRpngOgnnzP13aZrVH93Vk0c_89ZkZK3dEy3NcblnmhLEUwuCWOdlG7VwsgOZKSGPnfJDDrY17cDDe22w/w640-h360/bis-xrp-ledger-official-statistics-verification.jpg.png" title="BIS Researchers Test XRP Ledger for Official Statistics" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;September 4, 2026&lt;/strong&gt; — The XRP Ledger is being tested for a use case that has little to do with cryptocurrency trading: helping users verify the origin and integrity of official statistical data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Researchers from the &lt;strong&gt;Bank for International Settlements (BIS)&lt;/strong&gt; have developed and tested a blockchain-based proof of concept that uses the &lt;strong&gt;XRP Ledger (XRPL)&lt;/strong&gt; to anchor cryptographic information associated with official statistics.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The idea is not to put entire economic datasets on a blockchain. Instead, the system creates cryptographic fingerprints of published data, combines those fingerprints using a Merkle-tree structure and records a summary value on the ledger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A consumer can then use the published file and a ledger lookup to check whether the data matches the version that was originally anchored and whether the publisher identity can be verified.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="background: rgb(245, 245, 245); border-left: 4px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); margin: 24px 0px; padding: 16px;"&gt;
&lt;p style="margin: 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: red;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Important BIS disclaimer:&lt;/strong&gt; The BIS working paper states that the views expressed are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect the views of the BIS or its member central banks.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction is important. The research represents a &lt;strong&gt;proof of concept&lt;/strong&gt;, not an announcement that the BIS has adopted XRP or XRPL as permanent production infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Did BIS Researchers Actually Test?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The researchers were looking at a problem that becomes increasingly important as official statistics move through digital systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Statistical authorities and international organizations publish economic and financial information in standardized machine-readable formats. Those files can subsequently be downloaded, redistributed, processed or consumed by third-party platforms and automated systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once data leaves the original publisher's environment, a recipient may have difficulty independently proving that the file they received is exactly the same version that the original institution published.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS project proposes adding a cryptographic verification layer to that process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Each dataset can be converted into a canonical representation and cryptographically hashed. The resulting fingerprints can then be aggregated and anchored to a public blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If someone changes the data afterward, the cryptographic result changes as well, allowing the recipient to detect a mismatch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How the XRP Ledger Is Used&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proof of concept was implemented on the &lt;strong&gt;XRP Ledger&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS paper describes the system as combining an SDMx-native canonicalisation and hashing pipeline, Merkle aggregation, publisher credentials and blockchain anchoring.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The process can be summarized in four basic steps:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The statistical data is converted into a canonical representation.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Cryptographic hashes are generated for the relevant data.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Those hashes are combined through a Merkle-tree structure into a summary root.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The root is anchored to the XRP Ledger.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The published statistical message also carries information that allows a consumer to reconstruct the verification process, including the ordered Merkle leaves and a &lt;strong&gt;W3C Verifiable Credential&lt;/strong&gt; signed by the publisher's identity key.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The publisher identity is cryptographically linked to an XRPL address through an on-chain attestation registry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The result is intended to allow a consumer to verify both the identity of the claimed publisher and the integrity of the data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Statistics Are Not Stored Onchain&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the most important facts about the project.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS prototype does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; store the complete statistical datasets on the XRP Ledger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, the underlying data remains off-chain while cryptographic information representing the data is anchored to the ledger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A useful way to understand the concept is to think of the blockchain as a &lt;strong&gt;public digital notary&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The ledger provides a timestamped, publicly verifiable reference. The actual statistical file can remain in an existing data-distribution system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This approach also helps preserve confidentiality because the underlying statistical data does not need to be published on the blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Merkle Tree Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recording a separate blockchain transaction for every dataset could create unnecessary overhead.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS architecture addresses this through &lt;strong&gt;Merkle aggregation&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Individual data fingerprints can be combined into a Merkle tree. The resulting root represents the entire batch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means a single blockchain anchoring transaction can represent a large number of datasets rather than requiring one transaction for each dataset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS paper specifically examines batching across large numbers of datasets and notes that one ledger entry can cover thousands of datasets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is important because the cost of blockchain anchoring can then be distributed across the entire batch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Much Does the XRPL Anchoring Cost?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS paper reports a &lt;strong&gt;median observed network fee of 10 drops&lt;/strong&gt; for an anchoring transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because one drop equals one-millionth of an XRP, 10 drops equals:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;0.00001 XRP&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The paper's cost comparison uses an illustrative XRP price of approximately &lt;strong&gt;$0.30 per XRP&lt;/strong&gt;. At that assumed price, 10 drops corresponds to approximately:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;$0.000003 per anchoring transaction&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That dollar figure should not be interpreted as a permanently fixed USD transaction cost. It is the conversion used in the paper's illustrative cost analysis.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The paper's cost model shows why batching matters. When many datasets share a single anchor, the blockchain cost allocated to each individual dataset can become extremely small.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Prototype Publication Took 3–5 Seconds&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The researchers also measured the performance of their prototype.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Under the controlled test conditions described in the paper, the system achieved median publication latency of approximately &lt;strong&gt;3–5 seconds&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Verification latency was approximately &lt;strong&gt;1–2 seconds&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These numbers should not be presented as a guarantee of future production performance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The prototype measurements were conducted under controlled conditions, and the research is explicitly a proof of concept rather than a production deployment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 16px; min-width: 650px; table-layout: fixed; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Did the Researchers Use XRPL?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS researchers identified several characteristics that made the XRP Ledger suitable for the proof of concept.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Low nominal transaction fees&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Fast consensus finality&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Available developer resources&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Existing technical analysis of the XRPL consensus protocol&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the research should not be interpreted as saying that XRPL is the only blockchain capable of performing this function.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The paper describes the overall approach as &lt;strong&gt;data-format-agnostic&lt;/strong&gt; and the system architecture is modular. Its blockchain component can theoretically be replaced by another suitable target blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Role Does XRP Play?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is important to distinguish the &lt;strong&gt;XRP Ledger&lt;/strong&gt; from &lt;strong&gt;XRP&lt;/strong&gt;, the network's native digital asset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The research primarily concerns XRPL as the public ledger used for cryptographic anchoring.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, XRPL transactions require network fees denominated in XRP. The BIS paper reports a median observed fee of 10 drops for its anchoring transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean that the BIS is using XRP as a central-bank settlement asset in this experiment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The research does not announce an XRP-based payment system, reserve system or cross-border settlement arrangement for central banks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;XRPL Validator Vet Suggests an NFT-Based Approach&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS research has also prompted discussion within the XRP Ledger community about how the verification record could be represented on the ledger over the long term.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Vet&lt;/strong&gt;, an XRPL validator and community figure, publicly suggested using an NFT-based ledger object rather than relying on a payment transaction memo for the verification reference.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Under the BIS proof of concept, the Merkle root is anchored through the memo field of an XRPL Payment transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Vet's suggestion is different: the hash or a reference could be placed in an NFT's URI, potentially pointing toward content-addressed or permanent storage such as IPFS or Arweave.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proposal is based on the distinction between a transaction memo and an NFT ledger object. Vet argues that an object-based approach could provide a different long-term way to locate the verification reference without depending solely on transaction-history retrieval.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, this is &lt;strong&gt;Vet's community proposal, not a BIS recommendation&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS paper does not state that the project will replace its payment-memo implementation with NFTs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;SDMx Makes the Research Potentially Broader&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The project uses &lt;strong&gt;SDMx&lt;/strong&gt;, short for Statistical Data and Metadata eXchange.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SDMx is an international standard designed to describe statistical data and metadata, normalize their exchange and improve the sharing of statistical information across organizations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The official SDMx organization lists eight international sponsors:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Bank for International Settlements (BIS)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;European Central Bank (ECB)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Eurostat&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;International Labour Organization (ILO)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;International Monetary Fund (IMF)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;United Nations Statistical Division (UNSD)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;World Bank&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This gives the research a potentially broader statistical context.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is an important distinction: &lt;strong&gt;being an SDMx sponsor does not mean an organization has adopted XRPL for its statistics.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS experiment is a BIS research project using XRPL as its proof-of-concept blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Other organizations using SDMx could potentially examine similar verification mechanisms, but any such deployment would require an independent decision by the relevant organization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could the Same Idea Work Beyond SDMx?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The researchers describe the approach as data-format-agnostic.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The paper specifically discusses extending the architecture to other structured statistical or regulatory formats, including &lt;strong&gt;XBRL&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is potentially important for financial reporting and regulatory data because many institutions already depend on machine-readable information.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Still, these are possible extensions rather than confirmed production deployments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why AI Makes Data Verification More Important&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Artificial intelligence is another reason the researchers believe data provenance deserves greater attention.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI systems increasingly process economic, financial and statistical information automatically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A human analyst may recognize the source of a dataset before using it. An automated system may simply consume whatever machine-readable information is available.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a new question:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Can an automated system verify where the data came from and whether it has changed?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BIS paper identifies &lt;strong&gt;automated verification by AI agents&lt;/strong&gt; as a possible future extension of the architecture.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The idea is not that AI would automatically determine whether a statistic is economically correct.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, an AI agent could potentially verify the cryptographic provenance and integrity of a dataset before incorporating it into an analysis or workflow.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Blockchain Cannot Prove That a Statistic Is Correct&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This limitation is essential to understanding the research.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blockchain can help establish that a dataset matches the cryptographic version that was previously anchored.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It cannot independently determine whether the original statistic was calculated correctly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, if an institution publishes an incorrect inflation figure and anchors that figure's fingerprint to a blockchain, the blockchain can later help demonstrate that the published file has not been altered.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It cannot prove that the original calculation or methodology was correct.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So the BIS project should be understood as a mechanism for &lt;strong&gt;data integrity and provenance&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than a system for determining whether a statistic is objectively true.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the BIS Experiment Does Not Mean&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;It does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean the BIS has permanently adopted XRP Ledger.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;It does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean official statistics are stored directly on XRPL.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;It does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; announce an XRP-based central-bank payment system.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;It does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean the IMF has adopted XRPL.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;It does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean the World Bank has adopted XRPL.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;It does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean the ECB, OECD or United Nations have adopted XRPL.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;It does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; provide an XRP price prediction.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;It does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; represent a production deployment of a global statistical-verification system.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;It &lt;strong&gt;does&lt;/strong&gt; demonstrate a blockchain-based proof of concept implemented on XRPL.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;It &lt;strong&gt;does&lt;/strong&gt; demonstrate how cryptographic fingerprints and Merkle aggregation can be used to anchor statistical information.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;It &lt;strong&gt;does&lt;/strong&gt; report prototype-level publication and verification times measured in seconds.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Experiment Matters for XRPL&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The significance of the research goes beyond the XRP price narrative that can easily surround news involving the XRP Ledger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The experiment demonstrates a different potential role for a public blockchain: &lt;strong&gt;serving as a verification layer for machine-readable information.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Financial infrastructure depends on reliable information as much as it depends on payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Central banks, statistical authorities, financial institutions and automated systems all need to know whether the information they are using is authentic and unchanged.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A public cryptographic anchor can provide an independently verifiable reference without requiring the complete dataset to be placed onchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is the core technological idea being tested here.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Are the Main Limitations?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The research is a prototype, so its results should not be confused with a production deployment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The researchers evaluated the system under controlled conditions and explicitly discuss the need for further work before a production environment could be considered.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A real institutional deployment would need to address areas such as operational security, identity management, key protection, monitoring, governance, infrastructure resilience and sustained-load testing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There would also need to be clear processes for handling compromised credentials, publisher-key rotation and other operational events.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proof of concept provides an engineering basis for exploring these questions, but it does not answer all of them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BIS researchers have developed and tested a proof-of-concept system that uses the &lt;strong&gt;XRP Ledger&lt;/strong&gt; to help verify the provenance and integrity of official statistical data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The actual statistics remain off-chain. The system instead uses cryptographic hashing, Merkle aggregation, publisher credentials and a public blockchain anchor.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The prototype reported median publication latency of approximately &lt;strong&gt;3–5 seconds&lt;/strong&gt; and verification latency of approximately &lt;strong&gt;1–2 seconds&lt;/strong&gt; under the controlled conditions described in the paper.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The observed network fee was &lt;strong&gt;10 drops, or 0.00001 XRP&lt;/strong&gt;. Using the paper's illustrative $0.30-per-XRP assumption, that translates to approximately &lt;strong&gt;$0.000003 per anchoring transaction&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Merkle batching is central to the economics because one root can represent a large batch of datasets, potentially thousands, rather than requiring a separate blockchain transaction for every dataset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The research also points toward possible future applications involving other structured formats such as XBRL and automated verification by AI agents.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, community discussion has already raised alternative implementation ideas, including Vet's proposal to explore an NFT-based approach for storing a long-term verification reference. That proposal is separate from the BIS research design.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The biggest takeaway is therefore not that the BIS has “adopted XRP.” It has not announced such an adoption.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The significant development is that BIS researchers have demonstrated how a public blockchain such as XRPL can be used as a cryptographic trust layer for official data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As financial information becomes increasingly machine-readable and increasingly consumed by automated systems, proving where data came from and whether it has been altered could become an important part of digital financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;1. Did BIS researchers test the XRP Ledger?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. The BIS working paper presents a proof of concept implemented on the XRP Ledger for verifying the provenance and integrity of official statistical data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;2. Did BIS put official statistics directly on XRPL?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. The underlying datasets remain off-chain. Cryptographic information representing the data is anchored to the ledger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;3. What was the XRPL transaction fee in the BIS research?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The paper reports a median observed fee of 10 drops per anchoring transaction, equal to 0.00001 XRP. Its illustrative cost comparison converts that amount to approximately $0.000003 using an XRP price of $0.30.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;4. Why is Merkle batching important?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Merkle aggregation allows many individual data fingerprints to be represented by one root. This means a single blockchain transaction can cover a large batch of datasets, reducing the effective blockchain cost per dataset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;5. How fast was the prototype?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The researchers reported median publication latency of approximately 3–5 seconds and verification latency of approximately 1–2 seconds under the controlled test conditions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;6. Does this mean the BIS adopted XRP?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. The research documents a proof of concept using XRPL. It does not announce permanent BIS adoption of XRP or XRPL.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;7. Are the IMF, World Bank and ECB adopting XRPL?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no such announcement in this research. These organizations are among the international sponsors of SDMx, the statistical standard used by the project, but that sponsorship does not constitute XRPL adoption.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;8. What did XRPL validator Vet suggest?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Vet suggested exploring an NFT-based approach for the verification reference instead of relying on a payment transaction memo. This is a community proposal and is not part of the BIS prototype.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;9. Can blockchain prove that a statistic is correct?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. Blockchain anchoring can help verify data integrity and provenance, but it cannot independently determine whether the original statistic was calculated correctly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;10. Could AI agents use this system?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Potentially. The BIS paper identifies automated verification by AI agents as a possible future extension, but it does not say that AI systems are already universally using XRPL to verify official statistics.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;11. Could the architecture work with other data formats?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. The researchers describe the approach as data-format-agnostic and specifically discuss possible extensions to structured formats such as XBRL.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;12. Is this an XRP price prediction?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. The research concerns data verification and blockchain infrastructure. It does not provide an XRP price forecast or investment recommendation.&lt;/p&gt;
