    <title>What Happens to Your Crypto When an Exchange Delists a Coin?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgZ_JHYlXS5kFnGSKw8zHFCEZ-inIoiSpBMk4qflf8SuvIOyA4qUref-AlGOxDvcxSd-I5am-G-S7YLwbmYvVoCZLZFTGSyhmc8PwIyP5Oz5mf_8GMT7I0WYekdJzZWIQmG3Yb_BD2rb8bLEapLDnWuHxoULNqhgPy7Ji6ZGwOFaGa-_k-A44_m06vvh2f6/s1536/what-happens-when-exchange-delists-crypto-coin.png.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="What happens to your crypto when an exchange delists a coin, showing withdrawal deadlines, wallet transfers, trading suspension, and steps to protect your funds." border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="213" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgZ_JHYlXS5kFnGSKw8zHFCEZ-inIoiSpBMk4qflf8SuvIOyA4qUref-AlGOxDvcxSd-I5am-G-S7YLwbmYvVoCZLZFTGSyhmc8PwIyP5Oz5mf_8GMT7I0WYekdJzZWIQmG3Yb_BD2rb8bLEapLDnWuHxoULNqhgPy7Ji6ZGwOFaGa-_k-A44_m06vvh2f6/w320-h213/what-happens-when-exchange-delists-crypto-coin.png.png" title="What happens to your crypto when an exchange delists a coin, showing withdrawal deadlines, wallet transfers, trading suspension, and steps to protect your funds." width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;You open your crypto exchange one morning and see a message
you never wanted to read:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"This asset will be delisted."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The first thought is usually pretty simple: What happens to
the coins I already own? Do they disappear? Does the exchange sell them
automatically? Can you still withdraw them? And what if you miss the deadline?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There isn't one universal answer because every exchange has
its own delisting policy. But in most cases, a delisting does not immediately
mean that your crypto has vanished.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What matters is what the exchange does after trading is
stopped — and, more importantly, whether you move your coins before the final
deadline.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Does It Mean When a Crypto Is Delisted?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;When an exchange delists a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/vitalik-buterin-eyes-bitcoins-utxo.html"&gt;cryptocurrency&lt;/a&gt;, it is removing
that asset from its supported markets. That usually means users will no longer
be able to buy or sell the token on that exchange after a specified date.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But there is an important distinction between trading being
stopped and withdrawals being stopped.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;An exchange may stop trading first while giving customers
additional time to withdraw their holdings.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For example, Kraken's 2026 delisting schedules have used
separate deadlines for trading, deposits, withdrawals and final liquidation. In
one May 2026 cycle, trading and deposits were disabled on May 29, withdrawals
remained available until August 27, and remaining balances were scheduled for
liquidation in early September .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;So when you see the word "delisted," don't assume
everything happens at once.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Do You Lose Your Crypto When a Coin Is Delisted?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Not necessarily — but it depends entirely on what you do
next.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is probably the biggest misunderstanding around crypto
delistings. If you hold a token on an exchange and that exchange announces a
delisting, your balance doesn't automatically become worthless simply because
the trading pair is being removed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Depending on the exchange, you may still be able to:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l4 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Withdraw
     the token to a compatible wallet&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l4 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Transfer
     it to another exchange&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l4 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Sell
     or convert it during a limited period&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l4 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hold
     it temporarily while withdrawals remain open&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l4 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Migrate
     it if the project is moving to a new token&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The exact options depend on the exchange, the token and the
reason for the delisting.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Coinbase, for example, explains that after a trading
deadline, some assets may still be transferable off-platform, while other
situations such as migrations can involve separate transfer or conversion
requirements .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That's why the first thing to check is the exchange's
official delisting announcement.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Usually Happens After a Delisting Announcement?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A typical delisting process looks something like this:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;1. The Exchange Announces the Delisting&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The exchange tells customers that a particular asset will no
longer be supported. The announcement should normally include important dates.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is the point where you should stop treating the
situation like normal trading and start checking your exit options.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;2. Trading Is Suspended&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;After the trading deadline, you may no longer be able to buy
or sell the token on that exchange. Your balance may still appear in your
account, but the market itself is no longer available.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This distinction matters because many users assume that
"trading stopped" means "the coins are gone." It doesn't
necessarily mean that.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;3. Deposits May Be Disabled&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The exchange may also stop accepting new deposits of the
token. At this stage, sending the asset into the exchange could become
impossible or unsupported.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;4. Withdrawals Usually Have a Separate Deadline&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is the date you need to pay the most attention to. If
withdrawals remain available, you may be able to move your coins to a
self-custody wallet or another platform that still supports the asset.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Once the withdrawal deadline passes, your options can become
much more limited.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/what-is-dolo-token-complete-guide-to.html"&gt;Kraken's &lt;/a&gt;2026 delisting notices show exactly why these dates
matter: in several cases, withdrawals stayed open for weeks or months after
trading had already been disabled .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;5. Remaining Balances May Be Liquidated&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Some exchanges don't simply leave the token sitting in your
account forever. They may automatically liquidate remaining balances after the
final deadline.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For instance, Kraken's 2026 delisting notices have
explicitly warned that remaining balances may be automatically liquidated after
the withdrawal deadline, and that the liquidation price could be significantly
lower than recent market prices due to poor liquidity .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That is a very different situation from simply moving your
coins to your own wallet.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What If You Don't Sell Before the Delisting?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;You don't necessarily have to sell. This is another point
that often gets misunderstood.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Suppose you own a token that an exchange is removing but you
still believe in the project. If withdrawals are available, you may be able to
move the tokens to a compatible self-custody wallet instead of selling them.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The blockchain itself doesn't automatically know that an
exchange has delisted the asset. The token can continue to exist on-chain even
after one exchange stops supporting it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The real question is whether there is still somewhere you
can trade, use or transfer it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What If the Coin Is Still Listed on Other Exchanges?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is where a delisting becomes much less dramatic.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A token can be removed from one exchange while continuing to
trade elsewhere. For example, an exchange may decide that an asset no longer
meets its internal liquidity, compliance, security or operational standards.
That decision doesn't automatically remove the token from every other platform.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;So if Exchange A delists the token but Exchange B still
supports it, you may be able to withdraw the asset from Exchange A and transfer
it to Exchange B.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;However, always check that the token contract, blockchain
network and deposit network match. Sending an asset using the wrong network can
create a completely different problem.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What If Every Exchange Delists the Coin?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is where things get more complicated.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If the token disappears from major exchanges and there is
little or no liquidity elsewhere, the practical value of the asset can become
extremely difficult to realize.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The blockchain may still exist. Your wallet may still show
the tokens. But that doesn't mean someone is willing to buy them.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A crypto asset can technically continue to exist while
having almost no usable market. U.S. investor guidance also warns that the
market for a crypto asset can disappear altogether or become no longer
tradable, alongside risks such as illiquidity and exchange failure .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That's why "the token still exists" and "I
can sell the token" are two completely different statements.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What If the Exchange Automatically Sells My Coins?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Sometimes this can happen. But don't assume every exchange
follows the same process.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Some platforms may provide a period during which customers
can sell or withdraw their holdings. Others may automatically convert or
liquidate remaining balances after a stated deadline.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Coinbase's documentation, for example, explains that some
delistings can leave a limited cash-out period, while certain migration
situations involve different procedures .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Kraken has also stated that remaining balances in certain
delisting processes may be automatically liquidated after the withdrawal
deadline .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;So the answer to "Will the exchange sell my crypto for
me?" is: check the specific delisting notice. Never rely on what happened
on another exchange.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What If the Token Is Being Migrated Instead of Simply
Delisted?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This situation is slightly different.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Sometimes a project launches a new token or moves from one
blockchain or contract to another. The exchange may stop supporting the old
version and require users to migrate.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In that case, selling isn't necessarily the intended
solution. You may instead need to:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l5 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Move
     the old token to a supported wallet&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l5 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Use
     the project's official migration process&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l5 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Exchange
     the old token for the new one&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l5 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Complete
     the migration before a deadline&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Coinbase currently documents several token migration
scenarios and specifically advises customers to pay attention to migration
deadlines and transfer requirements .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is why it's important to understand why an asset is
being delisted. A compliance-related delisting, a low-liquidity delisting and a
token migration can have very different outcomes.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Do Exchanges Delist Crypto?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There isn't always one reason.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;An exchange can remove an asset because of:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Very
     low trading volume&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Poor
     liquidity&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Security
     concerns&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Technical
     problems&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Project
     inactivity&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Regulatory
     or compliance concerns&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Changes
     to the project's development&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Failure
     to meet the exchange's listing standards&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Kraken, for example, describes its scheduled delistings as
part of regular reviews involving internal performance and/or compliance
standards .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A delisting therefore doesn't automatically prove that a
token is a scam. But it is still a signal worth investigating.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Is a Delisting Bad for the Price?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It can be.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;When an exchange announces a delisting, traders may rush to
sell before the trading deadline. At the same time, liquidity can fall because
fewer buyers and sellers are participating. That can make price movements more
extreme.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;And if an exchange eventually liquidates remaining balances,
the actual proceeds can depend heavily on available market liquidity. Kraken
explicitly warns that some delisted assets may have liquidation prices
significantly below recent reference prices when markets are limited or
inactive .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;So a delisting can create a negative feedback loop:
delisting → fewer traders → lower liquidity → wider spreads → greater price
impact.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But this isn't guaranteed for every token.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Should You Do If Your Coin Is Being Delisted?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Don't panic. Instead, work through the situation carefully.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Step 1: Read the Official Announcement&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Don't rely on a screenshot from Telegram, X or Reddit. Find
the exchange's official announcement and identify:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l6 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Trading
     deadline&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l6 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Deposit
     deadline&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l6 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Withdrawal
     deadline&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l6 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Liquidation
     date&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l6 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Any
     conversion or migration instructions&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Step 2: Check the Withdrawal Network&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Before transferring anything, confirm that the destination
wallet supports the same token and blockchain network. This is especially
important when a token exists on multiple networks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Step 3: Decide Where You Want to Move It&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Depending on the circumstances, that could be:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo5; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A
     self-custody wallet&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo5; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Another
     exchange&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo5; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;An
     official migration platform&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If you're using a self-custody wallet, remember that you
become responsible for protecting your private keys or recovery phrase.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission notes that
control of a blockchain wallet generally comes from control of the private key,
while assets held through an intermediary can involve different custody and
recovery risks .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Step 4: Don't Wait Until the Last Hour&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This sounds obvious, but it's one of the easiest mistakes to
make. Blockchain withdrawals can fail. Networks can become congested. Exchanges
can experience technical problems. And a withdrawal deadline is a real
deadline.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If you already know you want to keep the asset, moving it
early removes one unnecessary risk.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What If You Miss the Withdrawal Deadline?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is the situation you want to avoid.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Once withdrawals are disabled, the exchange may have limited
options available. Depending on its policy, it may:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo6; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Automatically
     liquidate the remaining balance&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo6; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Convert
     the asset into another currency&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo6; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Keep
     the balance temporarily&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo6; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Provide
     a recovery process&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo6; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Offer
     no further withdrawal option&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There is no universal rule.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Kraken's current delisting notices show that some remaining
balances are automatically liquidated after a specified deadline .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;So if you missed the deadline, contact the exchange through
its official support channel and read the exact terms of that delisting.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;And be careful with anyone who claims they can
"recover" your crypto for an upfront fee. The SEC specifically warns
that people who have already lost crypto can be targeted by recovery scams .&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Does Delisting Mean the Project Is Dead?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;No.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A token can be delisted from one exchange and continue
operating normally elsewhere. It can also be delisted because of regulatory
requirements that have nothing to do with the underlying technology.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But a delisting becomes more concerning when several warning
signs appear at the same time:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo7; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Development
     activity has stopped&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo7; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Liquidity
     is disappearing&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo7; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Major
     exchanges are removing the asset&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo7; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The
     project's website or communication channels go offline&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo7; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The
     team stops responding&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo7; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The
     blockchain itself becomes inactive&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The important thing is to look at the whole picture instead
of treating one exchange announcement as the final verdict.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Part Most People Get Wrong&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Here's the simplest way to think about it:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;An exchange delisting is not the same thing as a
blockchain deleting your coins.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If you hold a token in a self-custody wallet, an exchange
deciding not to support that token doesn't magically remove the asset from the
blockchain.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The bigger risk is what happens to your ability to trade,
withdraw or access liquidity if you leave the coins on the exchange.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That distinction is often missed when people hear the word
"delisted."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Final Takeaway&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If an exchange announces that your cryptocurrency is being
delisted, don't immediately assume you've lost your money.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;First find out when trading stops, when withdrawals stop and
what happens to balances left behind.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If withdrawals are still available and you want to keep the
asset, moving it to a compatible self-custody wallet or another supported
platform may give you more control.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But remember that self-custody comes with its own
responsibility. Losing your recovery phrase or sending assets to the wrong
address can create problems that the exchange may not be able to fix.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The most important rule is simple:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Never ignore a delisting deadline.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The token may survive. The blockchain may survive. Another
exchange may continue listing it. But once your exchange closes withdrawals,
your options can become much narrower. Act before the deadline — not after.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

    <title>What Are Tokenized Bank Deposits? How Swift's Blockchain Ledger Could Change Cross-Border Payments</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgWoaksPeOa-1VsiV0KAvZ31YtKRcE29pgg_KfefCw8uAJHpCBeMPAu_bEYNEJpEDixxAZcj895bK-9ONL1HgiYn2u6lRaEu67pT0Pl7BZcwptOPsrQa7tcGvon2CSwmsfrxE0mXffS2ee_0xZhwi-d1ZS1LRTaFHna3-TLuCCqKjQG5lHVOSaO4-882uY2/s1672/tokenized-bank-deposits-swift-blockchain-ledger.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Tokenized bank deposits and Swift blockchain ledger for cross-border payments" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgWoaksPeOa-1VsiV0KAvZ31YtKRcE29pgg_KfefCw8uAJHpCBeMPAu_bEYNEJpEDixxAZcj895bK-9ONL1HgiYn2u6lRaEu67pT0Pl7BZcwptOPsrQa7tcGvon2CSwmsfrxE0mXffS2ee_0xZhwi-d1ZS1LRTaFHna3-TLuCCqKjQG5lHVOSaO4-882uY2/s1600/tokenized-bank-deposits-swift-blockchain-ledger.webp.png" title="Tokenized Bank Deposits and Swift Blockchain Ledger" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Editorial Desk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;For years, blockchain has been discussed as a technology that could make international payments faster. The difficult part was never simply putting money on a blockchain. Banks also needed a way to connect blockchain-based assets with the payment systems, compliance processes and messaging standards they already use.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is where &lt;strong&gt;tokenized bank deposits&lt;/strong&gt; and Swift's new blockchain-based ledger come into the picture.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In July 2026, Swift said its blockchain-based ledger was ready for initial use, with 17 banks from six continents preparing to pilot live transactions using &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-cant-circle-reverse-stolen-usdc-on.html"&gt;tokenized deposits&lt;/a&gt;. The goal is to support cross-border payments around the clock rather than relying entirely on traditional banking schedules and settlement processes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Then, on September 24, IBM announced a beta integration connecting its Digital Asset Haven platform to Swift's blockchain-based shared ledger. IBM's new ISO 20022 Messaging Adapter is designed to let financial institutions instruct tokenized deposit transactions using payment messages they already understand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But what exactly is a tokenized bank deposit? Is it the same thing as a stablecoin? And does Swift's blockchain ledger actually move bank money?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The answers are important because this system is not simply replacing traditional banking with crypto. It is attempting to connect regulated bank money with blockchain infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is a Tokenized Bank Deposit?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A tokenized bank deposit is essentially a &lt;strong&gt;digital representation of a bank deposit recorded using distributed-ledger technology&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The underlying money remains a bank liability. What changes is the way the deposit can be represented, transferred and potentially programmed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes tokenized deposits different from many &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/zcash-ironwood-explained-why-80-of.html"&gt;cryptocurrencies&lt;/a&gt;. They are not designed to function as independent digital commodities whose value floats according to market demand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They are intended to represent deposits held with regulated financial institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A simple example helps.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Suppose Bank A holds $10 million for a corporate customer. Instead of representing that balance only through the bank's traditional internal ledger, a corresponding tokenized deposit can be represented within a permitted digital-asset infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The token can then potentially be transferred through a network designed for participating financial institutions, subject to the rules governing the deposit and the participating banks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important word is &lt;strong&gt;“tokenized.”&lt;/strong&gt; The bank deposit does not magically become cryptocurrency simply because distributed-ledger technology is used.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Are Tokenized Deposits Different From Stablecoins?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the most common points of confusion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px; text-align: left;"&gt;Feature&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px; text-align: left;"&gt;Tokenized Bank Deposit&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px; text-align: left;"&gt;Stablecoin&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Issuer&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Typically a regulated &lt;br /&gt;bank&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Usually a private stablecoin &lt;br /&gt;issuer&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Underlying claim&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Bank deposit&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Issuer's backing/reserve &lt;br /&gt;structure&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Blockchain/&lt;br /&gt;DLT&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Can be used to represent &lt;br /&gt;and transfer the deposit&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Commonly used for issuance &lt;br /&gt;and transfers&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Primary users&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Banks and institutional &lt;br /&gt;customers&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Broad range of users, &lt;br /&gt;depending on the stablecoin&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Purpose&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Digitizing bank money and &lt;br /&gt;improving settlement/ &lt;br /&gt;payment workflows&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 8px;"&gt;Digital money for payments, &lt;br /&gt;trading and other applications&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The distinction matters because a tokenized deposit remains closely connected to the banking system that issued it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A stablecoin, meanwhile, is generally a separate digital asset issued under the rules and legal structure of its issuer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Is Swift Building a Blockchain Ledger?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Swift already connects more than 12,500 financial institutions across more than 200 markets. Its role has historically centered on financial messaging rather than acting as a blockchain settlement network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new ledger is designed to add blockchain-based infrastructure to that existing financial ecosystem rather than asking banks to abandon everything they already use.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Swift says its blockchain-based ledger is intended to support &lt;strong&gt;24/7 cross-border payments using tokenized deposits&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is significant because traditional cross-border payments often involve multiple institutions, operating schedules, intermediary banks and settlement systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blockchain-based shared ledger can provide a common digital environment in which participating institutions can coordinate payment activity continuously.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is an important caveat:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;24/7 movement on the ledger does not automatically mean that every part of final bank settlement becomes instant.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Swift's current design allows tokenized assets to move on the ledger ahead of final settlement through existing systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;So Does Swift's Blockchain Actually Replace Banks?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is perhaps the biggest misunderstanding surrounding the project.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Swift's blockchain ledger is not designed to eliminate banks from the payment process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, it provides another infrastructure layer for participating financial institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The banks still maintain their relationships with customers, manage compliance, control their assets and participate in settlement arrangements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Swift's objective is essentially to make &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/solana-yield-optimization-in-2026.html"&gt;blockchain infrastructure &lt;/a&gt;work alongside the financial system rather than forcing banks to build a completely separate financial universe.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does IBM Have to Do With It?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;IBM's role is particularly interesting because it addresses the connection between existing bank technology and blockchain infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On September 24, IBM announced that clients using &lt;strong&gt;IBM Digital Asset Haven&lt;/strong&gt; can connect to permissioned blockchain networks including Swift's blockchain-based shared ledger through a beta offering.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The key addition is an &lt;strong&gt;ISO 20022 Messaging Adapter&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ISO 20022 is already widely used in modern financial messaging. Banks therefore do not necessarily need to create an entirely separate operational language just because the underlying transaction involves tokenized assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;IBM says institutions can use standard ISO 20022 messages to instruct tokenized deposit transactions through the shared ledger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In simple terms, the idea looks like this:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Existing bank payment system → ISO 20022 message → IBM Digital Asset Haven → Swift blockchain ledger → tokenized deposit transaction&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The architecture is designed to reduce the amount of operational change banks need to make when experimenting with blockchain-based money.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Is ISO 20022 Important?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchain developers often think in terms of wallets, smart contracts and on-chain transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional banks think in terms of payment messages, account relationships, compliance procedures and settlement instructions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ISO 20022 sits between these worlds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It provides a standardized way of representing financial information in payment messages.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;By connecting tokenized deposit transactions to ISO 20022, banks can potentially use familiar payment processes while the underlying transaction is handled through newer digital infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This may sound like a small technical detail, but it could be one of the more important pieces of institutional blockchain adoption.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Financial institutions do not necessarily need another completely separate payment system. They need blockchain technology that can fit into the systems they already operate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Would a Tokenized Cross-Border Payment Work?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Consider a simplified example involving two banks in different countries.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bank A wants to send a payment to Bank B.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Under a traditional system, the payment instruction may pass through established messaging and settlement arrangements, potentially involving correspondent relationships and different operating schedules.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With a tokenized-deposit infrastructure, the participating institutions can represent bank money digitally and coordinate the transfer through the shared ledger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A simplified process could look like this:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The customer instructs its bank to make a payment.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The bank creates the appropriate payment instruction.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The instruction is represented using an established financial messaging standard such as ISO 20022.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The tokenized deposit transaction is sent to the participating ledger infrastructure.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The shared ledger coordinates the digital transaction between participating institutions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The banks continue to handle final settlement through their existing arrangements.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The exact operational process will depend on the participating institutions and settlement arrangements. The important point is that the blockchain ledger does not have to replace every existing financial system to provide value.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why 24/7 Payments Matter&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Financial markets operate globally, but traditional payment infrastructure has historically been constrained by business hours, holidays, settlement windows and intermediary processes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A ledger capable of operating continuously can reduce some of those timing restrictions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Swift says its new ledger is designed to enable 24/7 cross-border payments using tokenized deposits.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For multinational companies, this could eventually mean better visibility over when money is moving between financial institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It could also improve liquidity management because businesses would have greater flexibility over when payments are initiated and processed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, 24/7 digital movement should not be interpreted as a guarantee that every underlying banking settlement process is already available continuously.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction will remain important as the system moves from pilot activity toward wider production use.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Who Is Testing Swift's Tokenized Deposit Ledger?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Swift announced in July that 17 banks from six continents were preparing to pilot live transactions using tokenized deposits.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The project was developed with more than 40 financial institutions, according to Swift.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The participating institutions include major banks such as HSBC, Citi, UBS, BNY and Wells Fargo, among others.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The initial focus is cross-border payment activity using bank-issued tokenized deposits.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That gives the project a different character from many crypto experiments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Rather than starting with retail users buying tokens on a public exchange, the project begins with regulated financial institutions testing digital representations of bank money.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does This Mean Banks Are Moving to Public Crypto?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not necessarily.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Swift ledger is designed as permissioned infrastructure, meaning participation is controlled rather than open in the same way as a public cryptocurrency network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important for banks because compliance, identity, transaction monitoring and operational controls remain central requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Institutional blockchain adoption therefore may not look like the permissionless crypto networks that consumers are familiar with.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, banks may use distributed-ledger technology behind controlled infrastructure while preserving regulatory and operational requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What About Blockchain Settlement?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Settlement is one of the areas where headlines can become misleading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A payment can be digitally represented or coordinated on a blockchain ledger without every component of the underlying financial settlement happening on that blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Swift's current approach explicitly allows digital assets to move on its ledger ahead of final settlement through existing systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why it is more accurate to describe the system as &lt;strong&gt;connecting blockchain-based payment infrastructure with traditional settlement rails&lt;/strong&gt; rather than saying that Swift has moved all bank settlement onto a blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could Tokenized Deposits Compete With Stablecoins?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Potentially, they could compete for some of the same payment use cases, but they are not identical products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Stablecoins have already established themselves as a major form of blockchain-based digital money, particularly for crypto trading and on-chain transfers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tokenized deposits take a more bank-centered approach.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The deposit remains tied to a regulated financial institution, while distributed-ledger technology provides additional capabilities for transfer, programmability and interoperability.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Which model becomes more important in institutional payments will depend on regulation, liquidity, interoperability, costs and the willingness of banks and businesses to adopt the infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could AI Agents Eventually Use Tokenized Bank Deposits?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Possibly, and this is one of the more interesting long-term implications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Swift itself has identified &lt;strong&gt;agentic commerce&lt;/strong&gt; as one potential future area for its ledger infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI agent that needs to purchase computing resources, access an API or pay another automated service requires a way to move value programmatically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Today, much of the discussion around autonomous payments focuses on stablecoins and public blockchains.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tokenized deposits could offer another route if banks develop infrastructure that allows programmable payment instructions within regulated environments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That future is not yet the same as saying that AI agents are already widely using tokenized bank deposits. The technology and institutional infrastructure are still developing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Are the Biggest Challenges?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tokenized deposits solve some problems, but they do not eliminate the difficult parts of global payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Interoperability&lt;/strong&gt; remains important. Different banks and networks need to communicate reliably.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Liquidity&lt;/strong&gt; is another challenge. A 24/7 ledger is useful only if participating institutions have the liquidity and settlement arrangements necessary to complete transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Regulation&lt;/strong&gt; will also determine how tokenized deposits can be issued, transferred and used across borders.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Cybersecurity and key management&lt;/strong&gt; become critical because digital assets require secure control of cryptographic credentials.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Finally, banks need to decide whether the efficiency gains justify the cost of integrating new infrastructure into existing systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why IBM's On-Premises Option Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;IBM also announced an on-premises beta for Digital Asset Haven running on IBM Z and LinuxONE.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The option allows institutions to manage digital assets such as stablecoins and tokenized deposits inside their own data centers rather than depending entirely on public-cloud infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For highly regulated institutions, control over infrastructure and cryptographic keys can be an important consideration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;IBM says the on-premises version is designed to provide the same core architecture, APIs and workflows as its existing SaaS and hybrid offerings while keeping the deployment within the client's environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This could matter for banks that want to experiment with tokenized assets without moving sensitive digital-asset operations completely into an external cloud environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does Swift's Blockchain Ledger Actually Change?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The biggest change may not be that banks are suddenly “using crypto.”&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, the more significant development is that blockchain-based value transfer is being connected to the infrastructure banks already understand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is a different adoption model.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Rather than asking a bank to replace its payment messaging system, its compliance workflows and its operational processes, the new architecture attempts to add a digital-asset layer around those existing systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If that approach works at scale, blockchain could become less visible to the end user.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A corporate customer may simply see a faster payment while the underlying infrastructure quietly combines traditional banking systems, standardized messages and distributed-ledger technology.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next important milestone is not another announcement. It is &lt;strong&gt;production-scale usage&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The current Swift ledger is moving through early adoption and pilot activity. Seventeen financial institutions are preparing to test live tokenized deposit transactions, while IBM's connection is currently described as a beta capability.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The key questions will be whether banks can move from pilot transactions to sustained commercial use, whether cross-border liquidity can be managed efficiently and whether tokenized deposits deliver measurable advantages over existing payment systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If those pieces come together, tokenized deposits could become an important bridge between traditional bank money and blockchain-based financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tokenized bank deposits are not simply another type of cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They are digital representations of bank deposits that can use distributed-ledger technology to enable new ways of moving and programming bank money.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Swift's blockchain-based ledger is attempting to bring that technology into the existing financial system rather than replacing it outright.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;IBM's September 24 integration adds another important layer: banks can use familiar &lt;strong&gt;ISO 20022 messaging&lt;/strong&gt; to instruct tokenized deposit transactions through Swift's shared ledger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The result is a model where traditional banking infrastructure and blockchain technology can operate together.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Whether this becomes a major part of global payments will depend on what happens after the pilots. But the direction is clear: the next stage of blockchain adoption may not be about replacing banks. It may be about making the existing financial system capable of moving digital value around the clock.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is a tokenized bank deposit?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;A tokenized bank deposit is a digital representation of a bank deposit that can be recorded and transferred using distributed-ledger technology. The underlying claim remains connected to the issuing bank.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Are tokenized deposits the same as stablecoins?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. Tokenized deposits represent bank deposits, while stablecoins are separately issued digital assets backed according to the structure of their respective issuers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is Swift's blockchain ledger?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It is Swift's blockchain-based shared ledger infrastructure designed to support regulated digital-asset transactions, including 24/7 cross-border payments using tokenized deposits.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What does IBM have to do with Swift's blockchain ledger?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;IBM announced a beta connection between Digital Asset Haven and Swift's blockchain-based shared ledger. Its ISO 20022 Messaging Adapter allows participating institutions to instruct tokenized deposit transactions using standard financial messages.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does Swift's blockchain ledger replace traditional banks?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. The system is designed for participating financial institutions and is intended to work alongside existing banking, compliance and settlement infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can tokenized bank deposits move 24/7?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Swift says its ledger is designed to support 24/7 cross-border payment availability using tokenized deposits. However, digital movement on the ledger should not be confused with every underlying final-settlement process becoming instant.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How many banks are participating in Swift's tokenized deposit pilot?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Swift announced in July 2026 that 17 banks from six continents were preparing to pilot live transactions using tokenized deposits.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why is ISO 20022 important for tokenized deposits?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;ISO 20022 provides standardized financial messaging. Connecting tokenized deposit transactions to that standard can allow banks to use existing payment processes rather than building completely separate blockchain-specific messaging workflows.&lt;/p&gt;
