    <title>Arthur Hayes Warns AI Bubble Could Trigger a 2008-Style Crisis — Why Bitcoin Could Benefit</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEigEOO8rQr8DcSijwO3FhQD-wLhyfnTYnP7t5UfAkm6mChj3BhSPULHwv-8DBW6TEEJTBU1YV267NTiVO8d79r-lwoteRcjiY1mOccJRhTVX48wnVlakv771YScI95sTcgqaoETj_soW2uuycTAdrw5vYQ2K59uzP_aHBsBP6XVXFzVN064Gd7XNlFYfXkV/s1672/arthur-hayes-ai-bubble-bitcoin-crisis.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Arthur Hayes AI bubble warning and Bitcoin amid financial market crisis" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEigEOO8rQr8DcSijwO3FhQD-wLhyfnTYnP7t5UfAkm6mChj3BhSPULHwv-8DBW6TEEJTBU1YV267NTiVO8d79r-lwoteRcjiY1mOccJRhTVX48wnVlakv771YScI95sTcgqaoETj_soW2uuycTAdrw5vYQ2K59uzP_aHBsBP6XVXFzVN064Gd7XNlFYfXkV/w400-h225/arthur-hayes-ai-bubble-bitcoin-crisis.jpg.png" title="Arthur Hayes AI Bubble and Bitcoin Crisis Warning" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;By CoinaiNews Staff&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes is sounding the alarm on
something much bigger than crypto. In a recent essay titled
"Situationship" and interviews with Unchained and Bankless, Hayes
dropped a prediction that's turning heads across both crypto and traditional
finance: he argues that a potential AI bubble pop could trigger a financial
crisis "larger than what happened in 2008."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;And here's the part that really matters — he argues that the
resulting liquidity response could ultimately push Bitcoin to new all-time
highs.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why This Isn't the Dot-Com Bubble 2.0&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;When people hear "tech bubble," they usually think
of the 2000 dot-com crash — overvalued companies with no profits going bust.
Hayes says that's the wrong comparison.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"The AI bubble is a 2008-style credit story, not a
2000-style earnings story," he wrote in his essay
"Situationship."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Here's the distinction:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l6 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Dot-com
     bubble:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Companies raised money based on promises, burned through
     cash, and went bankrupt when investor enthusiasm faded. The damage was
     mostly contained to equity markets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l6 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;AI
     bubble (according to Hayes):&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Companies are borrowing billions to
     build physical infrastructure — data centers, power plants, cooling
     systems. This isn't tech spending. It's real estate development disguised
     as tech innovation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hayes estimates that roughly&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$1.5 trillion in debt&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;has
been issued to finance AI-related expansion since ChatGPT's launch in late
2022. And that debt is backed by assets that are rapidly depreciating.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why that matters:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;When you build a data center,
you're not building something that appreciates like a tech patent. You're
building a physical structure that could become obsolete faster than the debt
used to finance it. But the debt stays.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The 2008 Parallel Hayes Is Drawing&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hayes draws a direct line from the subprime mortgage crisis
to today's AI infrastructure boom.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The 2008 playbook:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Banks
     lent money to build houses&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Home
     prices started to flatten, but construction kept going&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Eventually,
     borrowers couldn't repay&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The
     whole system collapsed&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The AI version, according to Hayes:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l5 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Banks
     and private credit funds are lending billions for data centers&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l5 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;AI
     capital expenditure growth will slow around mid-to-late 2027&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l5 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But
     lending will continue because banks see AI as a "strategic"
     sector with implicit government backing&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l5 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;When
     the reckoning comes, it won't be a few startups going under — it'll be a
     cascade of bad debt through the financial system&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"The banking system will take massive losses on the
credit extended to the industry."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That's the 2008 comparison in a nutshell. Not overvalued
companies — overleveraged debt.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Catalysts That Could Pop the Bubble&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hayes has highlighted several potential catalysts that could
burst the AI bubble:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;1. Rising energy costs&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
AI data centers are energy hogs. If electricity prices keep climbing, the
economics of running massive compute clusters start to break.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;2. Mega IPOs sucking up liquidity&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
Massive tech IPOs on the horizon could divert capital away from other AI
investments, creating funding gaps for less established players.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;3. Political headwinds&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
Uncertainty around government policy — including potential anti-AI rhetoric or
regulation — can freeze &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/addton-dao-inside-ton-ecosystem-with.html"&gt;capital&lt;/a&gt; deployment and spook investors.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;When these pressures hit, Hayes expects AI stocks to crater,
margin calls to cascade, and the banking system to feel the pain.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Timeline: When Hayes Thinks It Could Happen&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hayes has put a specific date on his prediction:&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;2028.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But the process has already begun. The Federal Reserve is
already trapped, according to Hayes. He argues the Fed is "fiscally
dominated" — meaning it can't hike rates meaningfully because the Treasury
is too indebted.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The sequence he envisions:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;2026-2027:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;AI
     capital expenditure growth slows. Banks keep lending because they're
     incentivized by steep yield curves and perceived government backing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;2028:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The
     bubble pops. Debt can't be repaid. Financial institutions take massive
     losses.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Immediately
     after:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Central banks panic and print money on a scale that dwarfs
     2008.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;And that's where the crypto part comes in.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Printing Money Won't Fix the Problem&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Here's the twist in Hayes' thesis: central banks can't
actually solve this crisis.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"Central banks cannot print their way out of Moore's
law."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Translation: you can't print money to make chips more
efficient. You can bail out banks, but you can't manufacture the computing
breakthroughs that the AI trade was priced on.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin's Role: The Ultimate Liquidity Barometer&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hayes views Bitcoin as highly sensitive to &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/brian-armstrong-says-clarity-act-could.html"&gt;global liquidity&lt;/a&gt;
conditions and argues that monetary expansion could support BTC.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The mechanism is straightforward:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The AI debt unwinds&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;→&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Banks face losses&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;→&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Central
banks print money&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;→&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Dollar weakens&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;→&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin
rallies&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hayes puts his long-term target at&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$1 million&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;if
this scenario plays out.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;But there's a catch.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin may need to go down before it goes up. In Hayes'
scenario, BTC could fall to&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$50,000&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in the short term as the
AI unwind causes risk assets to sell off broadly.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"Bitcoin cannot rally in the short term if the
entire world takes serious losses from the deflation of the AI bubble
globally."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;After that, the liquidity flood begins. And then the real
rally starts.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Scale of the Debt — and Why It Matters&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hayes argues that the scale of AI-related borrowing could
create significant risks for the financial system.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Tech giants like Microsoft, Meta, Oracle, Amazon, and
Alphabet are reported to have approximately&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$1.09 trillion in future
lease commitments&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;for data centers. That's nearly four times the lease
obligations already on their balance sheets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The distribution of risk is uneven:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Oracle's debt-to-EBITDA ratio is roughly&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;4.3x&lt;/b&gt;,
while competitors like Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta are under 1x. If
the bubble pops, Oracle is much more exposed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But the bigger worry is the banking system holding this
debt. When a company defaults on a data center loan, the bank holding that loan
feels the pain. And when multiple banks feel that pain simultaneously, you get
a 2008-style credit freeze.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The "Yen-Quake" Factor: Another Liquidity
Catalyst&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hayes has also discussed a separate but related scenario he
calls the "Yen-Quake."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hayes argues that Japan may need to strengthen the yen to
prevent imported inflation and capital flight. It can do this in three ways:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol start="1" style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="1"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l4 level1 lfo5; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hike
     interest rates (risks crashing its bond market)&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l4 level1 lfo5; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Force
     pension funds to sell foreign assets (risks crashing US markets)&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l4 level1 lfo5; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Borrow
     dollars from the Fed's FIMA Repo Facility and use them to buy yen (forces
     the Fed to print money)&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hayes has discussed a scenario in which the Fed's FIMA Repo
Facility could be used to support yen-related liquidity needs. If the Fed has
to expand its balance sheet to accommodate Japanese capital flows, that's more
liquidity flooding the system — and more fuel for Bitcoin.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What This Means for Investors&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Hayes' thesis isn't subtle:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo6; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;AI
     is a debt bubble, not a tech bubble&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo6; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;When
     it bursts, the financial system will take a hit&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo6; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Central
     banks will respond by printing money&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo6; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hayes
     sees Bitcoin as a potential major beneficiary&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;But it's important to understand the stages:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l7 level1 lfo7; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Phase
     1:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;AI stocks crash, credit tightens, and in Hayes' scenario,
     Bitcoin sells off to $50,000&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l7 level1 lfo7; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Phase
     2:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Central banks panic-print, liquidity floods the system&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l7 level1 lfo7; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Phase
     3:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Bitcoin rallies to new highs, potentially $1 million+&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The timeline is uncertain. Hayes points to 2028, but
acknowledges the catalyst could come sooner.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Arthur Hayes is making one of the boldest macro calls in
crypto. He estimates that AI-related borrowing has reached roughly $1.5
trillion — a debt overhang that, in Hayes' view, could contribute to a broader
financial crisis by 2028. The resulting financial crisis, he argues, could
trigger the biggest Bitcoin rally in history.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If he's right, the next few years will be volatile. But for
those who survive the turbulence, the reward could be historic.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If he's wrong — if central banks can navigate this without a
crisis, or if AI demand justifies the infrastructure spending — then the thesis
falls apart.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Either way, the debate is now firmly on the table. And for
crypto investors, that's worth paying attention to.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

    <title>Bitcoin Knocks on the 50-Week Moving Average — Could This Be the End of the Bear Market?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi9xPxToIpThl_yeeQ0mzXrseCL345so2kzl9pT_F0AYbr-f394DT3uNREn7nbuWvX64WrdrgnOCGohZvMRBMd7RKi-HnJJUVMOvH5AXAdsdZE_RFVHUg61gQQNQn394qMC4sen7a7IhJG5fAcIJYq9Ck0u6lt-f4VA9cDFxiwXgBZIT7uKPlNnzfsRfJfG/s1672/bitcoin-50-week-moving-average-bear-market-2026.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin approaching its 50-week moving average near the key bear-market resistance level" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi9xPxToIpThl_yeeQ0mzXrseCL345so2kzl9pT_F0AYbr-f394DT3uNREn7nbuWvX64WrdrgnOCGohZvMRBMd7RKi-HnJJUVMOvH5AXAdsdZE_RFVHUg61gQQNQn394qMC4sen7a7IhJG5fAcIJYq9Ck0u6lt-f4VA9cDFxiwXgBZIT7uKPlNnzfsRfJfG/w400-h225/bitcoin-50-week-moving-average-bear-market-2026.webp.png" title="Bitcoin Nears 50-Week Moving Average" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin is approaching one of the most closely watched
technical levels in the market — and a weekly close above it could change how
traders view the entire cycle.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin’s latest rebound has brought the cryptocurrency back
to a level that could prove unusually important for the broader market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy, says
Bitcoin is now “knocking on the door” of its &lt;b&gt;50-week moving average&lt;/b&gt;. The
level has historically acted as a ceiling during Bitcoin bear markets, making
the next weekly close particularly interesting for traders looking for evidence
that the market may have moved past its prolonged downturn.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The observation was highlighted by CoinMarketCap on
Saturday, citing Thorn’s analysis.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Galaxy Research’s latest study puts the current 50-week
moving average around &lt;b&gt;$81,796&lt;/b&gt;, while its estimate for the Aug. 30 weekly
close places the moving average at roughly &lt;b&gt;$81,110&lt;/b&gt;. Bitcoin had already
traded as high as about $81,265 during the week, putting the cryptocurrency
within striking distance of the indicator.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That does not mean Bitcoin’s bear market is officially over.
But if BTC manages to finish the week above the 50-week moving average, history
suggests the move could carry considerably more significance than an ordinary
short-term price rally.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why the 50-Week Moving Average Matters&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Moving averages are among the simplest tools traders use to
identify longer-term market trends. The 50-week moving average is particularly
useful for Bitcoin because it filters out much of the short-term volatility
while still responding faster than very long-term indicators such as the
200-week moving average.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;According to Galaxy’s research, the 50-week moving average
has repeatedly behaved like a &lt;b&gt;ceiling during Bitcoin bear markets&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;During the current downturn, Bitcoin lost the 50-week moving
average in November 2025. Galaxy notes that for the following 33 weeks, no
weekly close managed to reclaim the level, even though several rallies came
close before losing momentum.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That makes the current test different.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin is no longer simply bouncing from a lower support
zone. It is approaching the same trend line that has repeatedly rejected
rallies during the current bear-market structure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A decisive weekly close above it would therefore give
traders fresh evidence that the market’s longer-term trend may be changing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What History Says About a Break Above the 50-Week MA&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The most interesting part of Galaxy’s analysis is the
historical comparison.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Galaxy says that in &lt;b&gt;four of the five completed bear
markets&lt;/b&gt;, the first upside break of the 50-week moving average was followed
by confirmation that the bear market bottom had been established.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That is a notable pattern because Bitcoin’s major bear
markets have historically followed a recognizable sequence: a prolonged
decline, a period of consolidation around a major low, and eventually a
recovery above important long-term trend indicators.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The 50-week moving average has frequently been part of that
transition.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;However, there is an important exception.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The &lt;b&gt;2021–22 bear market&lt;/b&gt; produced two temporary moves
back above the 50-week moving average. Both failed, and Bitcoin eventually made
a lower low.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That history is a useful reminder that the indicator should
not be treated as a guarantee.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In other words, a weekly close above the 50-week moving
average would be &lt;b&gt;bullish evidence&lt;/b&gt;, but it would not be mathematical
proof that Bitcoin cannot fall again.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The market would still need to demonstrate that buyers can
defend the reclaimed level.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin’s Rebound Has Added Weight to the Setup&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The technical signal is arriving after an unusually strong
recovery.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Galaxy reported that Bitcoin gained more than &lt;b&gt;$14,000 in
a single week&lt;/b&gt;, its largest weekly dollar increase on record, while the
cryptocurrency moved to within roughly 2% of the 50-week moving average.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That kind of move naturally brings more attention to
technical levels that might otherwise receive less notice.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The rally has also occurred against a broader macro backdrop
that has helped risk assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin recently moved above $80,000 as a weaker U.S. dollar
and renewed demand for hard assets helped lift both Bitcoin and gold.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The macro environment matters because Bitcoin’s technical
structure does not exist in isolation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If liquidity conditions, institutional demand and broader
risk appetite continue improving at the same time that &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/ai-trading-agents-could-move-markets_0441656950.html"&gt;BTC breaks&lt;/a&gt; above its
50-week average, the technical breakout could have greater staying power.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Weekly Close Is More Important Than an Intraday Move&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For traders following this setup, there is an important
distinction between &lt;b&gt;touching or briefly crossing the 50-week moving average&lt;/b&gt;
and actually closing a weekly candle above it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin has already traded very close to the indicator.
Galaxy’s analysis focuses on the weekly close because temporary intraday moves
can produce false signals.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A sustained weekly close above the moving average would
provide stronger evidence that buyers have managed to overcome the resistance
that has capped previous rallies.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That is why the upcoming weekly candle is attracting so much
attention.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The market is effectively asking a simple question:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Can Bitcoin turn the 50-week moving average from
resistance into support?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If the answer is yes, the technical picture could change
substantially.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What a Successful Breakout Could Mean&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A confirmed move above the 50-week moving average would not
automatically guarantee a new all-time high.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It would, however, remove one of the most important
technical obstacles Bitcoin has faced during the current cycle.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Traders could begin treating the June low as a more credible
long-term bottom rather than simply another temporary rebound.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It could also encourage sidelined capital to return to the
market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Momentum traders typically pay close attention to major
trend indicators, while longer-term investors may interpret a successful
reclaim as evidence that downside risk has become more contained.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But confirmation would still be necessary.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin would need to hold above the reclaimed level rather
than immediately falling back below it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A failed breakout could produce the opposite reaction, with
traders viewing the move as another bear-market rally.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bear Market Is Not Over Until the Market Proves It&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is where the current situation becomes particularly
interesting.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The historical record gives &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/what-happens-to-dao-when-all-its.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt; bulls a reason for
optimism, but it does not eliminate risk.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The 2021–22 cycle demonstrated exactly why traders should be
careful about treating the 50-week moving average as an infallible signal.
Bitcoin reclaimed the level and subsequently lost it again before establishing
a lower low.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For that reason, the most useful way to interpret Thorn’s
observation is not that Bitcoin has already escaped its bear market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Instead, Bitcoin is &lt;b&gt;approaching a technical test that has
historically been associated with the end of major bear-market phases&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The distinction is important.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A breakout would strengthen the bullish case. A failed
attempt would suggest that sellers are still defending the longer-term trend.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Traders Will Be Watching Next&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The immediate focus is the weekly close around the 50-week
moving average.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Three scenarios stand out.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;First, Bitcoin closes clearly above the moving average.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That would represent the strongest bullish outcome and could
reinforce the argument that the June low was an important cycle bottom.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Second, Bitcoin briefly breaks above the level but closes
below it.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That would weaken the breakout thesis and raise the
possibility that the 50-week average is still acting as resistance.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Third, Bitcoin closes above the level but later loses it
again.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That would resemble the type of failed breakout seen during
the 2021–22 bear market and would make confirmation more important than the
initial move.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For investors, the third scenario is a useful reminder: &lt;b&gt;one
candle can change sentiment, but sustained price action confirms a trend.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin Has Reached a Decision Point&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin’s approach to the 50-week moving average is more
than another technical headline.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;After months of weakness and repeated failed rallies, BTC is
finally challenging the trend line that has defined much of the current
bear-market structure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Galaxy Research’s historical analysis suggests that a
successful reclaim has often occurred around the point where Bitcoin’s bear
&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/if-ai-makes-millions-in-crypto-who-owns.html"&gt;market &lt;/a&gt;was effectively finished.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But history also shows that the signal can fail.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That leaves Bitcoin at an important decision point.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A weekly close above the 50-week moving average would give
bulls a significant technical victory and strengthen the case that the market
has entered a new phase. A rejection, meanwhile, would suggest that Bitcoin
still has more work to do before the current bear-market structure can be
considered broken.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For now, the key number is not simply Bitcoin’s latest
price.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;It is the weekly close.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;And with Bitcoin now knocking directly on the door of its
50-week moving average, the next few days could provide one of the clearest
signals yet about where the 2026 market cycle is heading — &lt;b&gt;and whether the
bears are finally losing their grip.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Key Takeaways&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin
     is approaching its 50-week moving average, currently around the
     low-$81,000s.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Galaxy
     Research identifies the 50-week MA as a historically important bear-market
     ceiling.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A
     weekly close above the level would strengthen the case that Bitcoin’s June
     low was a major cycle bottom.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Historical
     evidence is supportive but not perfect; the 2021–22 cycle produced failed
     reclaim attempts.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Traders
     are likely to focus more on a sustained weekly close and subsequent hold
     than on a temporary intraday breakout.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The
     indicator is a signal, not proof that Bitcoin’s bear market is
     definitively over.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

purposes only and does not constitute investment or financial advice. Bitcoin
and other cryptocurrencies are highly volatile assets. Historical market
patterns do not guarantee future results.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Can Coinbase Pull Back a Crypto Transaction Once It Hits the Blockchain?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

  &lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgk1iSc30hOakAI33j2yLDrdwCErH_xMgeQZGB5nkTL2Yr3-uPk5IM3T5GKcbKRSLwLNMBymsDUez0Gvz0cPjkZ9_6jckoUdHVkQTuliedfLpKOXVZios6O9d-qskHzx-nwFW3FUUcB8Yqq6nc4hb5S2BmHTI-qPJqnTJJxHxYLsu72uahNiKL0K1eaLk_h/s1536/coinbase-blockchain-transaction-reversal-explained.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="266" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgk1iSc30hOakAI33j2yLDrdwCErH_xMgeQZGB5nkTL2Yr3-uPk5IM3T5GKcbKRSLwLNMBymsDUez0Gvz0cPjkZ9_6jckoUdHVkQTuliedfLpKOXVZios6O9d-qskHzx-nwFW3FUUcB8Yqq6nc4hb5S2BmHTI-qPJqnTJJxHxYLsu72uahNiKL0K1eaLk_h/w400-h266/coinbase-blockchain-transaction-reversal-explained.jpg.png" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h3 style="text-align: left;"&gt;There is a moment in crypto that can make even an experienced user nervous.&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;You press &lt;strong&gt;Send&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Then you look at the address again.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Something is wrong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Maybe you copied the wrong wallet address. Maybe you selected the wrong network. Or perhaps you simply realized a few seconds too late that you didn't want to make the transfer.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The natural question is almost immediate:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Can Coinbase stop it?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In some situations, Coinbase can stop or cancel a transaction before it has actually been broadcast to the blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But once a cryptocurrency transaction has been broadcast and ultimately confirmed or finalized by the relevant blockchain, Coinbase generally cannot simply pull it back.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That distinction is important because a transaction being visible as “pending” does not automatically mean Coinbase can reverse it.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The answer depends on &lt;strong&gt;where the transaction is in the process&lt;/strong&gt;, which blockchain is involved and whether the transaction is being handled through Coinbase's platform or a self-custody wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Coinbase Is Not the Blockchain&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The easiest way to understand the issue is to separate Coinbase from the network underneath it.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Coinbase operates a cryptocurrency exchange and related services. It can control transactions within systems that it operates.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A public blockchain, however, follows its own protocol.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;When you send Bitcoin, Ethereum or another cryptocurrency to an external blockchain address, the transaction eventually has to be processed by that network.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Once the transaction has been accepted and finalized according to the network's rules, Coinbase doesn't have a universal administrator button that says “undo.”&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Coinbase explains that cryptocurrency transactions sent to the wrong address generally cannot be canceled or reversed. The recipient would normally have to return the funds.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://help.coinbase.com/en/coinbase/trading-and-funding/sending-or-receiving-cryptocurrency/i-sent-funds-to-the-wrong-address-how-do-i-get-them-back" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;
      Coinbase: I sent funds to the wrong address
    &lt;/a&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That isn't really a limitation unique to Coinbase.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It is one of the basic characteristics of public blockchain networks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Happens Before You Hit the Final Send?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is one of the areas where the distinction matters most.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A transaction that hasn't yet been submitted to the blockchain is fundamentally different from one that has already been broadcast.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If a user notices a mistake while a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/sk-hynix-ceo-warns-memory-chip-crunch.html"&gt;transaction&lt;/a&gt; is still inside Coinbase's own transaction flow, Coinbase may be able to stop or cancel it depending on the specific product, status and circumstances.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Once the transaction has been broadcast, however, the situation changes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The blockchain network—not simply Coinbase—becomes responsible for processing the transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;So there is an important practical rule:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Stopping a transaction before broadcast is not the same thing as reversing a transaction after broadcast.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is why users should carefully review the destination address, asset, network and amount before confirming a transfer.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Does “Pending” Actually Mean?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The word “pending” causes a lot of confusion.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A pending transaction is not necessarily a completed transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Depending on the network and transaction type, it may be waiting for inclusion in a block or for enough network confirmations.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Coinbase explains that blockchain transactions require confirmations before they are considered complete.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://help.coinbase.com/en/coinbase/getting-started/crypto-education/glossary/confirmations" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;
      Coinbase: Crypto confirmations explained
    &lt;/a&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That means users shouldn't treat the word “pending” as a universal cancellation window.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A pending status can mean different things depending on the underlying network and Coinbase's transaction flow.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;How Many Confirmations Are Required?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Confirmation requirements are not identical across every cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Coinbase has published requirements that have included &lt;strong&gt;two confirmations for Bitcoin and 14 confirmations for Ethereum&lt;/strong&gt; in relevant transaction flows.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Those numbers should not be interpreted as a universal definition of blockchain finality, however.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The important distinction is between a transaction being &lt;strong&gt;broadcast&lt;/strong&gt;, &lt;strong&gt;included in a block&lt;/strong&gt;, receiving additional &lt;strong&gt;confirmations&lt;/strong&gt;, and reaching the relevant network's &lt;strong&gt;finality&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Coinbase's requirements can also vary by asset, product and transaction circumstances.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;So the safest approach is to check the confirmation status shown for the specific transaction rather than assuming that one number applies to every Coinbase transfer.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What About Ethereum?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Ethereum introduces another important distinction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;An unconfirmed Ethereum transaction can, under certain conditions, be replaced by another transaction from the same account with an appropriate nonce and higher fee.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is commonly described as &lt;strong&gt;replace-by-fee&lt;/strong&gt; or transaction replacement.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But this is a feature of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/dear-algorithm-only-show-us-1000x.html"&gt;Ethereum's&lt;/a&gt; transaction mechanics—not a Coinbase reversal button.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Coinbase does not gain unilateral control over an Ethereum transaction simply because the transaction originated through its platform.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Once again, the blockchain's rules determine what can happen.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;And after an Ethereum transaction has been finalized, submitting another transaction doesn't reverse the original transfer.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/transactions/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;
      Ethereum: Transactions documentation
    &lt;/a&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What If the Transaction Has Been Broadcast but Isn't Confirmed?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is the gray area.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A transaction can be broadcast to a blockchain network and still be waiting for confirmation.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For some networks, there are protocol-level mechanisms that can affect an unconfirmed transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Ethereum's replacement mechanism is one example.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But users should be careful about assuming that every pending transaction can be canceled.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Different blockchains have different transaction models.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Different wallets expose different controls.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;And exchanges may manage transactions differently from self-custody wallets.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;So the technically accurate answer is:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;An unconfirmed transaction may have options depending on the network, but that does not mean Coinbase can simply recall it.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Exchange Wallet vs. Self-Custody Wallet&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There is another distinction that often gets lost in this discussion.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A Coinbase exchange account is not the same thing as a self-custody wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;With an exchange account, Coinbase manages significant parts of the transaction process on the platform.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;With a self-custody wallet, the user generally controls the private keys and signs transactions directly.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That can give the user more direct control over how an unconfirmed transaction is handled.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For example, certain Ethereum wallets may allow a user to attempt transaction replacement by submitting another transaction using the same nonce with a higher fee.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But that doesn't mean a confirmed transaction can be undone.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Self-custody provides more direct control over transaction signing; it does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; create a universal blockchain “undo” function.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Happens After Confirmation?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is where the answer becomes much simpler.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Once a transaction has been confirmed and finalized according to the relevant blockchain's rules, Coinbase generally cannot reverse it.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Coinbase says crypto transactions are irreversible once completed and warns users that cryptocurrency sent to the wrong address generally cannot be retrieved by Coinbase.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://help.coinbase.com/en/coinbase/trading-and-funding/sending-or-receiving-cryptocurrency/i-sent-funds-to-the-wrong-address-how-do-i-get-them-back" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;
      Coinbase: Wrong-address crypto transfers
    &lt;/a&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The exchange cannot simply edit an old blockchain record.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Doing so would require changing the underlying network's state through mechanisms controlled by the blockchain itself.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For a public decentralized network, Coinbase does not have that unilateral authority.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Allowlisting Can Add Another Layer of Protection&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There is also a security feature that can reduce the chance of sending funds to an unfamiliar destination in the first place: &lt;strong&gt;allowlisting&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;When address allowlisting is enabled and configured, transfers can be restricted to addresses that have been approved in advance.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That doesn't make blockchain transactions reversible.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Instead, it adds another checkpoint before funds are sent.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The idea is simple: if an attacker gains access to an account, an address that has not been approved may face an additional restriction rather than immediately becoming an available withdrawal destination.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Users should still understand the exact rules of the Coinbase product they are using, because security features and waiting periods can differ.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The broader lesson is that prevention is much easier than blockchain recovery.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What If You Send Crypto to the Wrong Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is probably the most practical example.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Suppose you intend to send 1 &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/your-most-viewed-coin-this-week-heres.html"&gt;ETH&lt;/a&gt; to a friend.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;You accidentally paste another wallet address.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;You confirm the transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If the transfer has already been confirmed on Ethereum, Coinbase generally cannot simply retrieve the ETH.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The address belongs to whoever controls the corresponding private keys.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If the recipient is identifiable and cooperative, they may be able to send the funds back.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But that becomes a recovery situation rather than a blockchain reversal.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If nobody controls the destination address, recovery may be impossible.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is why crypto transfers deserve more attention before the final confirmation than many ordinary digital payments do.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What If Your Account Was Compromised?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The situation is different if someone gains unauthorized access to a Coinbase account.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Users should report suspicious or unauthorized activity to Coinbase as quickly as possible.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Coinbase provides procedures for reporting unauthorized transactions and securing compromised accounts.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://help.coinbase.com/en/coinbase/privacy-and-security/account-compromised/how-do-i-report-an-unauthorized-transaction" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;
      Coinbase: Report an unauthorized transaction
    &lt;/a&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But reporting a theft does not automatically mean a confirmed blockchain transaction can be reversed.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There are two separate questions:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Can Coinbase investigate or secure the account?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Can Coinbase reverse a transaction that the blockchain has already finalized?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The first may be possible.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The second generally is not.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why This Is Different From a Bank Transfer&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Traditional financial systems have trained consumers to expect that some payments can be stopped or reversed.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A bank transfer may sometimes be recalled.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A card transaction may be disputed.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A payment provider may intervene in certain cases.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Those systems have centralized institutions that maintain control over the payment infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Public blockchains generally work differently.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The ledger is maintained according to the network's protocol rather than by a single company handling customer complaints.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Coinbase can provide access to that system.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It does not own the underlying Bitcoin or Ethereum networks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That distinction is easy to overlook when everything happens inside a polished exchange interface.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Important Difference Between Platform Control and Network Control&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is the central idea behind the entire question.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Coinbase can control parts of its own platform.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It can implement security systems, restrict account activity, process transactions and, in appropriate circumstances, stop transactions before they are broadcast.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But Coinbase doesn't control the consensus rules of every blockchain it supports.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin has its own network.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Ethereum has its own network.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Other blockchains have their own rules.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A cryptocurrency exchange is therefore not equivalent to a central bank with the ability to rewrite the underlying payment ledger whenever it chooses.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;So, Can Coinbase Pull Back a Blockchain Transaction?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The most accurate answer is:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Generally, no—once the transaction has been broadcast and confirmed or finalized by the blockchain, Coinbase cannot simply pull it back.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Before broadcast, Coinbase may be able to cancel or stop a transaction depending on the particular transaction flow.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;After broadcast but before confirmation, the possibilities depend on the blockchain's own mechanics. Ethereum, for example, supports replacement of certain unconfirmed transactions, but that is a network-level feature rather than Coinbase exercising reversal authority.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;After confirmation and finality, the practical assumption should be that the transaction is permanent.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is the safest way for users to think about blockchain transfers.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Users Should Check Before Sending&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A few seconds of checking can prevent a potentially permanent mistake.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Before sending a significant amount of cryptocurrency:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check the destination address.&lt;/strong&gt; Make sure the first and last characters match what you intended.&lt;/li&gt;

    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check the network.&lt;/strong&gt; Sending an asset through the wrong network can create serious recovery problems.&lt;/li&gt;

    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check the asset.&lt;/strong&gt; Don't assume that similarly named tokens are interchangeable.&lt;/li&gt;

    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check the amount.&lt;/strong&gt; A decimal-point mistake can be expensive.&lt;/li&gt;

    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check whether allowlisting is enabled.&lt;/strong&gt; If you use an allowlisted-address system, make sure the intended destination has already been approved.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For a large transfer, consider sending a small test transaction first when practical.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Lesson About Blockchain&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The Coinbase question is really a question about who controls a transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;On a traditional payment network, the institution operating the network may have significant authority over transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;On a public blockchain, the rules are enforced differently.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That can give users a degree of direct control over digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But it also means mistakes can be harder to undo.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The same property that makes blockchain transactions resistant to unilateral reversal is also what makes them useful as a settlement mechanism.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There is no contradiction there.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It's a trade-off.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;More transaction finality can mean less ability to reverse mistakes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;More direct control can mean more responsibility.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Can Coinbase technically pull back a cryptocurrency transaction once it has been broadcast to the blockchain?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Not in the ordinary sense, once the transaction has been confirmed and finalized.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Coinbase may be able to cancel or stop certain transactions before broadcast, while some blockchains provide mechanisms for dealing with unconfirmed transactions. Ethereum, for example, allows certain unconfirmed transactions to be replaced under its protocol rules.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Security features such as allowlisting can also reduce the chance of an unauthorized destination being used in the first place.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But none of these mechanisms should be confused with a universal blockchain undo button.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For users, the safest rule is simple:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Treat an external crypto transfer as potentially irreversible once you confirm it.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Because once the blockchain has accepted and finalized the transaction, the question is no longer whether Coinbase can press an “undo” button.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There isn't one.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The real question is whether the person controlling the receiving address is willing—and technically able—to send the funds back.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Editorial note:&lt;/strong&gt; Blockchain transaction behavior varies by network, asset, wallet and transaction state. “Pending,” “broadcast,” “confirmed” and “finalized” are not interchangeable terms. Confirmation requirements can also vary by asset and Coinbase product. This article explains the general principles and should not be treated as a guarantee for every transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute financial, legal or investment advice.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
