&lt;header&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;time datetime="2026-09-18"&gt;September 18, 2026&lt;/time&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;By CoinAINews Editorial Team&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;h1&gt;CLARITY Act Stalls in Senate as Blackburn Blames Democrats and Bitwise CIO Calls It a "Speed Bump"&lt;/h1&gt;
&lt;/header&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Senate has stalled the CLARITY Act after a procedural vote failed to reach the 60-vote threshold needed to advance the cryptocurrency market-structure bill. Senator Marsha Blackburn said she believes Democrats opposed the legislation because they did not want to give Republicans and President Donald Trump a political win, while Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan described the setback as a "speed bump, not a roadblock" for the crypto industry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The September 15 vote was &lt;strong&gt;49-50&lt;/strong&gt;, meaning the motion to advance the bill did not receive enough support to move forward at that stage. The vote was not final passage or final rejection of the CLARITY Act itself; it was a procedural vote on whether the Senate could proceed with the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The outcome has nevertheless become an important moment for U.S. crypto regulation. Supporters had spent more than a year negotiating the legislation, while Democrats continued to seek changes involving ethics and other provisions. At the same time, some Republicans also opposed the procedural motion, making the result more complicated than a simple party-line dispute.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happened to the CLARITY Act?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On &lt;strong&gt;September 15, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, the Senate held a cloture vote on the motion to proceed with the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act, H.R. 3633.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The motion received &lt;strong&gt;49 votes in favor and 50 against&lt;/strong&gt;. Because the Senate needed 60 votes to invoke cloture and move forward, the motion failed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Four Republican senators—&lt;strong&gt;Jerry Moran, Susan Collins, Josh Hawley and Thom Tillis&lt;/strong&gt;—also voted against the motion. Senator Tillis subsequently changed his vote for procedural reasons, preserving the possibility of reconsideration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important: the September 15 result stalled the bill's advancement, but it did not represent a final Senate vote on the complete legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Senator Marsha Blackburn Said&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Senator &lt;strong&gt;Marsha Blackburn&lt;/strong&gt;, Republican of Tennessee, offered a political explanation for the Democratic opposition.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Speaking to Fox Business, Blackburn said she believed Democrats voted against the CLARITY Act because they did not want to give Republicans and the president a political win.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is &lt;strong&gt;Blackburn's characterization&lt;/strong&gt; of the vote, not an established explanation for the motives of every Democratic senator.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Democratic lawmakers had publicly raised substantive objections, particularly around ethics provisions and rules concerning digital-asset activities involving federal officials. Those concerns remained part of the negotiations even after Republicans released a revised version of the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The final procedural result also included Republican opposition, meaning the vote cannot accurately be described as Democrats alone preventing the legislation from advancing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Republicans Made Major Changes Before the Vote&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Senators &lt;strong&gt;Cynthia Lummis, John Boozman and Tim Scott&lt;/strong&gt; released a revised CLARITY Act text on September 14, one day before the Senate vote.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The senators said the new draft incorporated &lt;strong&gt;126 substantive changes&lt;/strong&gt; requested by Democrats after more than a year of bipartisan negotiations. The revised text included new ethics provisions, changes involving state attorneys general and additional provisions covering stablecoins, developers, consumer protections and CFTC jurisdiction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The ethics provisions were particularly significant because lawmakers had been negotiating restrictions involving federal officials and digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Washington Post reported that President Trump had agreed to stricter ethics provisions that would restrict federal officials from creating or backing certain digital assets while in office. The revised framework also included a role for state attorneys general in enforcing those restrictions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These provisions should be understood as part of the legislative debate over potential conflicts of interest. They do not, by themselves, establish wrongdoing by any individual.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Was the CLARITY Act Designed to Do?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CLARITY Act was designed to create a federal regulatory framework for digital assets and clarify the respective roles of the &lt;strong&gt;Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)&lt;/strong&gt; and the &lt;strong&gt;Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the central problems in U.S. crypto regulation has been determining how different digital assets and activities should be classified and which federal agency should oversee them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A statutory market-structure framework could provide clearer definitions and regulatory boundaries for exchanges, token issuers, financial institutions and other companies operating in the digital-asset sector.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Supporters of the bill have argued that clearer rules could provide greater regulatory certainty and help the United States remain competitive in digital-asset markets. Opponents and critics have focused on provisions they believe require additional changes, including ethics safeguards and consumer protections.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Matt Hougan Calls the Setback a "Speed Bump"&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitwise Chief Investment Officer &lt;strong&gt;Matt Hougan&lt;/strong&gt; offered a substantially different interpretation of the Senate setback.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In a September 16 CIO memo, Hougan described the CLARITY Act's failure as a &lt;strong&gt;"speed bump, not a roadblock."&lt;/strong&gt; His argument is that crypto-market development and institutional adoption can continue even if Congress does not immediately pass the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hougan pointed to Bitcoin's performance as one reason for his view.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to Bitwise data cited in his memo, Bitcoin reached a low of approximately &lt;strong&gt;$57,950 on July 1&lt;/strong&gt; before climbing above &lt;strong&gt;$80,000 on September 4&lt;/strong&gt;. During the same period, prediction-market odds cited by Bitwise for the CLARITY Act becoming law in 2026 declined from 39% to 18%.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hougan argues that the divergence suggests crypto-market activity does not depend entirely on the passage of the CLARITY Act.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That comparison, however, does not prove that legislation has no effect on cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin prices are influenced by multiple factors, including monetary policy, liquidity, institutional demand, leverage and broader risk sentiment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Hougan Thinks Crypto Can Keep Developing&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hougan also pointed to continued activity from major financial institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;His memo highlighted developments including Robinhood launching its own blockchain, Morgan Stanley launching a Solana exchange-traded product and DTCC settling its first batch of tokenized stock trades. Hougan used those developments to argue that financial institutions have continued building crypto-related infrastructure despite uncertainty surrounding the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;His broader argument is that the crypto market has already developed beyond the point where one congressional vote determines whether the industry continues expanding.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, Hougan acknowledged that congressional action remains important because a durable statutory framework would provide authorities that agencies cannot necessarily create on their own.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;SEC and CFTC Rulemaking Becomes More Important&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With the CLARITY Act stalled, attention is likely to remain focused on the SEC and CFTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Both agencies can continue using their existing authority to establish rules and provide regulatory guidance for parts of the digital-asset market. Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong also said after the Senate vote that the SEC and CFTC have tools available under existing authority.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But agency action is not identical to congressional legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A law passed by Congress can establish statutory authority and regulatory boundaries that remain in place beyond an individual administration. Agency rules can be changed by future regulators and can also face legal challenges.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why the failure to advance the CLARITY Act does not mean U.S. crypto regulation has stopped. Instead, it leaves part of the market-structure debate unresolved while agencies continue operating under existing law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bill Is Stalled, but Negotiations May Continue&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The September 15 vote did not necessarily end negotiations around the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent reporting indicates that &lt;strong&gt;seven Senate Democrats&lt;/strong&gt; have signaled that discussions over the CLARITY Act should continue despite the failed cloture vote. The development suggests that some lawmakers still see room for negotiations over outstanding provisions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That matters because a procedural setback and the permanent abandonment of a bill are not necessarily the same thing. Lawmakers can continue negotiating, revise legislative language or attempt to bring a measure back under Senate procedures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The remaining legislative calendar, however, could limit the time available for lawmakers to reach another agreement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Ethics Became a Major Issue&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ethics provisions became one of the most closely watched parts of the final negotiations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The revised bill included restrictions designed to address potential conflicts involving federal officials and digital assets. Republicans said the new language represented significant concessions to Democratic demands, while Democratic lawmakers continued to seek additional safeguards.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The issue became particularly sensitive because President Trump and members of his family have substantial involvement in cryptocurrency-related businesses and assets, making rules concerning officials' digital-asset interests a central part of the political debate over the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For accuracy, those concerns should not be confused with an allegation that any particular official violated an ethics or financial law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the Senate Vote Means for Crypto Companies&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For crypto exchanges, custodians, token issuers, financial institutions and blockchain companies, the biggest issue is &lt;strong&gt;regulatory certainty&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A federal market-structure law could establish clearer rules around the classification and oversight of digital assets. Without such legislation, companies may continue operating under a combination of agency rules, enforcement decisions, court rulings and state-level requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That can make long-term planning more complicated, particularly for businesses whose products involve several areas of digital finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the continued development of crypto products by major financial institutions also shows that companies are not necessarily waiting for Congress to resolve every regulatory question before building in the sector.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin's Reaction to the Senate Vote&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CLARITY Act vote also coincided with a sharp move in cryptocurrency markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Reuters reported that Bitcoin fell more than 5% as the Senate vote appeared headed for failure, while shares of Coinbase and stablecoin issuer Circle also declined. The market reaction occurred alongside other macroeconomic and financial factors, so the move cannot automatically be attributed to the CLARITY Act alone.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hougan's longer-term comparison tells a different story. His Bitwise data showed Bitcoin rising substantially from its July 1 low even as expectations for CLARITY Act passage declined.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Together, the two observations illustrate why regulatory developments and cryptocurrency prices should not be treated as having a simple one-to-one relationship.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Speed Bump or Regulatory Gap?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hougan's "speed bump" description captures one side of the debate: crypto businesses and financial institutions can continue developing products even without a comprehensive congressional market-structure law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The opposing concern is that continued agency rulemaking cannot fully replace legislation that establishes permanent statutory authority.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Both points can coexist. &lt;strong&gt;Crypto development can continue while regulatory uncertainty remains unresolved.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The September vote therefore creates two parallel stories: the immediate legislative setback and the continued expansion of crypto infrastructure outside the legislative process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next stage will likely involve a combination of congressional negotiations, agency rulemaking and continued development by crypto companies and financial institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Lawmakers could revisit provisions involving market structure, ethics, consumer protections and regulatory jurisdiction. Meanwhile, the SEC and CFTC can continue working within their existing authorities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the crypto industry, the key question is not simply whether the CLARITY Act returns for another vote. It is whether lawmakers can resolve the disagreements that prevented the bill from reaching the 60-vote threshold required to advance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CLARITY Act is currently &lt;strong&gt;stalled in the Senate after a 49-50 procedural vote&lt;/strong&gt; failed to reach the 60 votes required to advance the legislation. The vote was not final passage or final rejection of the bill, leaving open the possibility of further negotiations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Senator Marsha Blackburn has attributed Democratic opposition to political considerations, saying Democrats did not want to give Republicans and President Trump a win. Democrats, however, had raised substantive concerns about ethics provisions and other parts of the legislation, while four Republicans also voted against the procedural motion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan sees the setback differently, calling it a &lt;strong&gt;"speed bump, not a roadblock."&lt;/strong&gt; He argues that crypto adoption and financial-sector development can continue even without immediate congressional action, although he also recognizes that legislation would provide a more durable regulatory foundation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader U.S. crypto-regulation debate therefore continues on several fronts: &lt;strong&gt;Congressional negotiations, SEC and CFTC rulemaking, institutional adoption and the industry's push for clearer market rules.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the CLARITY Act has not advanced, but the regulatory debate surrounding digital assets in the United States is far from over.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;CoinAINews will update this report as lawmakers resume negotiations or new developments emerge around the CLARITY Act, SEC and CFTC crypto regulation.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Uniswap Processes $500M+ in Tokenized Stock Volume While Wall Street Was Closed</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjfLklm3y4wT1hFjqMclo7m47MPQl-UVAIvJVI0eZ39VaCL3_cB_i6PV5xn9Pj3dSuqghVee-dnTQmCtCoLtsUtmyFTjQ1DGAj0Qd1l2Ks_2zWzqCjjNPT84i36rGoR-1K9r5M9PTNIWWapJS3dR0GJgqhCGfoVMPOh5QOOAhs8bJr5BuKewmnLvBYKpqCU/s1672/uniswap-500m-tokenized-stock-volume-labor-day.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Uniswap processes more than $500 million in tokenized stock volume while Wall Street is closed" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjfLklm3y4wT1hFjqMclo7m47MPQl-UVAIvJVI0eZ39VaCL3_cB_i6PV5xn9Pj3dSuqghVee-dnTQmCtCoLtsUtmyFTjQ1DGAj0Qd1l2Ks_2zWzqCjjNPT84i36rGoR-1K9r5M9PTNIWWapJS3dR0GJgqhCGfoVMPOh5QOOAhs8bJr5BuKewmnLvBYKpqCU/w640-h360/uniswap-500m-tokenized-stock-volume-labor-day.jpg.png" title="Uniswap Processes $500M+ in Tokenized Stock Volume" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;
&lt;strong&gt;Published:&lt;/strong&gt; September 9, 2026&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap processed more than &lt;strong&gt;$500 million in stock-token volume&lt;/strong&gt; during the three-day U.S. Labor Day weekend, highlighting how tokenized markets can continue trading on blockchain infrastructure even when traditional U.S. stock markets are closed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap disclosed the figure in a post on September 8, saying that while Wall Street took a three-day weekend, its protocol processed more than $500 million in stock-token volume. The company contrasted the activity with traditional market schedules, noting that onchain markets remain available when conventional exchanges are closed. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The milestone comes as Uniswap expands beyond crypto-native assets and increasingly supports tokenized stocks, funds and other real-world assets through its decentralized trading infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Uniswap Reports More Than $500 Million in Stock-Token Volume&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The headline figure came directly from Uniswap.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In a September 8 post, the decentralized exchange said it processed &lt;strong&gt;$500 million-plus in stock-token volume&lt;/strong&gt; while Wall Street was closed for the three-day Labor Day weekend. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The statement is notable because U.S. equity markets normally operate according to set trading sessions and exchange holidays. Blockchain-based markets can operate continuously, allowing eligible tokenized assets to remain tradable outside those traditional windows.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap has been positioning its infrastructure around that difference as tokenized securities move further into decentralized finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Labor Day Weekend Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The timing is central to the story.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. stock market was closed for the Labor Day holiday, but blockchain networks do not follow the same weekday trading calendar. Onchain applications can remain operational around the clock, subject to the availability of liquidity, the specific token's trading rules and applicable restrictions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a different market structure for &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/gemini-secures-singapore-mpi-license.html"&gt;tokenized &lt;/a&gt;securities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of waiting for a traditional exchange to reopen, eligible users can potentially trade tokenized assets through blockchain-based infrastructure during periods when conventional markets are offline.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap has previously highlighted this feature as one of the advantages of bringing securities onchain. Its June announcement said tokenized securities can be traded through its Web App, Wallet and API and emphasized that onchain assets are available outside traditional market hours. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Are Tokenized Stocks?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tokenized stocks are blockchain-based representations of exposure to securities or equities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They are designed to bring some characteristics of traditional financial assets into blockchain-based markets, where tokens can potentially be transferred and traded using digital infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, &lt;strong&gt;a tokenized stock should not automatically be described as identical to directly owning the underlying shares.&lt;/strong&gt; The legal rights, issuer structure, custody arrangements, redemption mechanics and geographic eligibility can vary depending on the product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important as tokenized-equity markets grow.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Uniswap Has Been Building a Tokenized-Asset Market&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest $500 million figure did not appear in isolation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In June, Uniswap announced that tokenized securities were available through its Web App, Wallet and API. The company said users could discover and trade tokenized versions of assets including SpaceX, Apple, Tesla and NVIDIA through its products. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap also said at the time that more than &lt;strong&gt;$9.1 billion had been swapped in real-world-asset pools&lt;/strong&gt; on the protocol across more than 2.6 million transactions and more than 140,000 wallets. That figure covered the broader real-world-asset category rather than the latest $500 million stock-token figure. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The distinction matters: the $500 million reported for the Labor Day weekend is specifically described by Uniswap as &lt;strong&gt;stock-token volume&lt;/strong&gt;, while the $9.1 billion figure represents broader real-world-asset pool activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Robinhood Chain Is Part of the Tokenized-Stock Push&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap's expansion into tokenized equities has also been closely connected with Robinhood Chain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap went live on Robinhood Chain in July, with Uniswap v2, v3, v4 and UniswapX available on the network. Uniswap described itself as the primary public automated market maker on the chain. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The launch included support for Robinhood &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-bitcoin-transaction-be-reversed-if.html"&gt;Stock Tokens&lt;/a&gt; through Uniswap products and infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap said those stock tokens could be traded on Robinhood Chain around the clock, creating a direct connection between tokenized equity products and DeFi-style liquidity infrastructure. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Uniswap Had Already Seen Stock Trading Outside Market Hours&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Labor Day weekend figure also builds on earlier activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In August, Uniswap said its first correlated markets for tokenized equities were already operating on Robinhood Chain. Ten tokenized stocks were trading against SPY in Uniswap pools, and the company said those pools generated $33 million in volume during their first 12 days, with much of the activity occurring while U.S. markets were closed. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That earlier data provides useful context for the latest milestone: the idea of trading tokenized equities outside traditional market hours is becoming an increasingly important part of Uniswap's real-world-asset strategy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why 24/7 Trading Could Matter&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional financial markets have defined opening and closing times. &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-i-generate-same-bitcoin-address.html"&gt;Blockchain&lt;/a&gt;-based markets operate differently.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When tokenized securities are issued and traded through compatible blockchain infrastructure, trading can potentially continue through nights, weekends and market holidays.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not automatically mean every tokenized stock has unlimited 24/7 liquidity. Market makers, liquidity pools, issuer restrictions and regulatory requirements still matter.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the underlying infrastructure can remain available even when traditional exchanges are offline.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That difference could become increasingly relevant if tokenized securities develop into a larger part of global financial markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Uniswap Is Moving Beyond Crypto-Native Assets&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap originally became one of the best-known decentralized exchanges through crypto-native trading pairs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Its more recent strategy shows a broader ambition: become infrastructure for markets that include tokenized stocks, bonds, funds and other real-world assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In June, Uniswap said tokenized securities could use the same liquidity and routing infrastructure already used by its broader ecosystem. The company also highlighted the ability to build compliance mechanisms into liquidity pools, including allowlists and geographic restrictions. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is important because regulated securities cannot necessarily be traded under exactly the same conditions as permissionless crypto tokens.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Compliance Remains a Key Issue&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The growth of tokenized stocks does not remove financial regulation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In fact, tokenized securities often require more sophisticated compliance infrastructure because the underlying assets can be subject to securities laws, investor eligibility rules and geographic restrictions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap has been developing infrastructure designed to accommodate those requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In July, Uniswap introduced &lt;strong&gt;Permissioned Pools&lt;/strong&gt;, a framework designed for tokenized funds, equities and other regulated assets. The system allows issuers to enforce investor eligibility requirements while still using Uniswap's automated market-maker infrastructure. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The development illustrates the direction of the sector: bringing traditional assets onchain while adding the controls required for regulated markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does $500 Million Mean Investors Bought $500 Million of Stocks?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not necessarily.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The $500 million figure reported by Uniswap refers to &lt;strong&gt;stock-token trading volume&lt;/strong&gt;. Trading volume measures the value of transactions processed during a period; it is not the same thing as the total value of assets held by users or the amount of new capital invested.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It also should not be interpreted as $500 million of net buying.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A token can trade multiple times, meaning cumulative trading volume can be much larger than the amount of capital initially entering a market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For that reason, the figure is best understood as a measure of trading activity rather than a direct measure of investor inflows.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does This Prove Tokenized Stocks Are Taking Over Wall Street?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The $500 million figure is an important data point for onchain markets, but it does not establish that tokenized stocks have replaced traditional equity exchanges.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional stock markets remain vastly larger and operate under established clearing, settlement, custody and regulatory systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;What the Uniswap data does show is that there is meaningful trading activity in tokenized stock markets even during periods when conventional U.S. exchanges are closed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Whether that activity continues to grow will depend on liquidity, regulation, investor demand, product quality and the ability of tokenized securities to provide reliable economic and legal exposure to their underlying assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why This Matters for DeFi&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The development is significant for decentralized finance because tokenized stocks expand the types of assets that can potentially interact with blockchain liquidity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto-native assets have historically dominated DeFi. Tokenized equities introduce a different category of financial exposure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If regulated tokenized securities become widely available, they could potentially be used alongside stablecoins and other blockchain assets in decentralized financial applications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could expand the role of automated market makers from crypto trading venues into broader financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What to Watch Next&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next important question is whether the Labor Day weekend activity becomes a recurring pattern rather than a one-off milestone.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Investors and market participants will likely watch several metrics:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Tokenized-stock trading volume:&lt;/strong&gt; whether activity continues rising after the holiday.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Liquidity:&lt;/strong&gt; whether markets can support larger trades without excessive price impact.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Number of assets:&lt;/strong&gt; whether more stocks, ETFs and other securities move onchain.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Regulation:&lt;/strong&gt; whether regulators provide clearer frameworks for tokenized securities.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Institutional participation:&lt;/strong&gt; whether professional investors increasingly use onchain market infrastructure.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;24/7 demand:&lt;/strong&gt; whether traders consistently use tokenized markets when traditional exchanges are closed.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Picture: Markets Are Moving Onchain&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap's latest milestone reflects a broader shift in financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tokenization is no longer limited to experiments involving a small number of blockchain-native assets. Financial companies and crypto protocols are increasingly exploring ways to represent equities, funds, bonds and other instruments on distributed networks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The appeal is not simply that an asset receives a blockchain token.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The larger proposition is that trading, settlement, liquidity and financial applications could eventually operate on the same programmable infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap's $500 million-plus Labor Day weekend figure provides a real-world example of that model in action, although the long-term scale of tokenized stock markets remains uncertain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How much tokenized stock volume did Uniswap process over Labor Day weekend?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap said it processed more than &lt;strong&gt;$500 million in stock-token volume&lt;/strong&gt; while Wall Street was closed for the three-day Labor Day weekend. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why could Uniswap trade while U.S. stock markets were closed?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap operates on blockchain infrastructure rather than following the traditional trading calendar of U.S. stock exchanges. Compatible tokenized assets can therefore remain available for onchain trading outside conventional market hours, subject to their specific rules and liquidity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Are tokenized stocks the same as regular stocks?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not necessarily. A tokenized stock can represent exposure to an underlying security, but the exact legal rights, ownership structure, custody and redemption arrangements depend on the product and issuer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does $500 million in volume mean $500 million of new investment?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. Trading volume represents the cumulative value of trades and does not equal net capital inflows or the total amount of assets purchased.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does Uniswap support tokenized stocks?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Uniswap says tokenized securities are available through its Web App, Wallet and API, including tokenized versions of several well-known securities. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is Robinhood Chain's role in Uniswap's tokenized-stock strategy?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap went live on Robinhood Chain in July 2026 and supports stock tokens there. The chain provides an onchain environment where tokenized equity products can interact with decentralized liquidity infrastructure. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does the Labor Day volume prove tokenized stocks will replace Wall Street?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. The milestone demonstrates substantial onchain trading activity, but traditional equity markets remain much larger and have established clearing, settlement and regulatory infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Uniswap says it processed more than $500 million in stock-token volume during the three-day U.S. Labor Day weekend, when traditional U.S. stock markets were closed.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The milestone highlights one of the central arguments behind tokenized financial markets: blockchain infrastructure can remain operational outside traditional exchange hours.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Uniswap has been steadily expanding its role in this market, supporting tokenized securities through its products, deploying on Robinhood Chain and developing infrastructure for regulated assets. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The $500 million figure should not be mistaken for $500 million of new investment or evidence that tokenized stocks have replaced traditional markets. But it does provide another indication that trading activity around tokenized financial assets is becoming a meaningful part of the broader DeFi landscape.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Zcash Ironwood Explained: Why 80% of Shielded ZEC Is Now in the New Privacy Pool</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjkTtPukXjuXHFul6JavU-g07Itrn15yigooOMEpHoqFYBHP0RdxDO0wzZYvdIREIz4_8mN9iQyyj3QY1YUb0r88DyaIlAR1bLfjKgys2RQv-7uoauzyrxW4jP2Xeaub246u-XsCDaprCOzVCSO2YuEVmssn4S8RZEtFNFYnIC9a-n1D1qOSRklOflnfmWl/s1672/zcash-ironwood-shielded-pool-2026.webp%20(2).png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Zcash Ironwood shielded pool holding 80 percent of shielded ZEC" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjkTtPukXjuXHFul6JavU-g07Itrn15yigooOMEpHoqFYBHP0RdxDO0wzZYvdIREIz4_8mN9iQyyj3QY1YUb0r88DyaIlAR1bLfjKgys2RQv-7uoauzyrxW4jP2Xeaub246u-XsCDaprCOzVCSO2YuEVmssn4S8RZEtFNFYnIC9a-n1D1qOSRklOflnfmWl/s1600/zcash-ironwood-shielded-pool-2026.webp%20(2).png" title="Zcash Ironwood Shielded Pool Explained" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By CoinAINews Editorial Desk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Zcash's privacy architecture is going through one of its biggest changes of 2026, and a large portion of the network's shielded ZEC has already moved into a new pool called &lt;strong&gt;Ironwood&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As of September 23, about &lt;strong&gt;3.9 million ZEC&lt;/strong&gt; was held in the Ironwood pool, according to data reported by The Block. That represents roughly &lt;strong&gt;80% of Zcash's shielded supply&lt;/strong&gt;—not 80% of all ZEC in existence. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The change matters because Ironwood was introduced after a serious vulnerability was discovered in Zcash's previous Orchard shielded pool. The July 2026 network upgrade retired Orchard for new deposits and introduced a controlled mechanism for moving funds into the new pool. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So what exactly is Ironwood, why are millions of ZEC moving into it, and what does the transition mean for Zcash users?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is Zcash Ironwood?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ironwood is Zcash's newest shielded pool, introduced as part of the network's &lt;strong&gt;NU6.3&lt;/strong&gt; upgrade.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The upgrade activated on July 28, 2026. At activation, the previous Orchard pool was closed to new deposits and Ironwood started as a new shielded pool. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The technical design of Ironwood is based partly on the Orchard protocol, but it maintains a separate consensus state and a separate value pool. The official Ironwood design documentation describes it as a new shielded value pool that operates alongside Zcash's transparent, Sapling and Orchard pools. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In simple terms, Ironwood is not a new &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/solana-yield-optimization-in-2026.html"&gt;cryptocurrency&lt;/a&gt;. It is a new privacy pool within the existing Zcash network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Did Zcash Need a New Shielded Pool?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The answer goes back to a vulnerability discovered in the Orchard proving system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On May 29, 2026, researcher Taylor Hornby identified a soundness issue in the Orchard proof circuit. The issue created a theoretical possibility of creating counterfeit ZEC without leaving the normal on-chain evidence expected from legitimate issuance. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The discovery became a major security issue for Zcash because Orchard was the network's newest major shielded pool before Ironwood.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Rather than continuing to accept new deposits into Orchard, the Ironwood upgrade retired the pool and introduced a controlled migration mechanism.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This does not mean that every ZEC in Orchard was declared counterfeit. The important point is that the vulnerability created uncertainty around the integrity of the pool's accounting, which is why the network introduced safeguards around the migration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How the Ironwood Migration Works&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ironwood did not simply transfer every coin from Orchard into the new pool automatically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, users have to move their funds from the retired Orchard pool into Ironwood.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The migration uses a mechanism commonly described as a &lt;strong&gt;turnstile&lt;/strong&gt;. The basic idea is that &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/how-to-cash-out-crypto-on-etrscrypto.html"&gt;withdrawals &lt;/a&gt;from Orchard are constrained by the amount that can be verified as having entered the pool legitimately.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;CoinDesk reported that Orchard contained approximately &lt;strong&gt;3.66 million ZEC&lt;/strong&gt; when Ironwood activated. The new Ironwood pool initially contained zero ZEC, meaning the migration had to happen progressively as users moved their funds. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This design is important because it attempts to prevent the potential vulnerability in the old pool from being carried forward into the new accounting system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Is 80% of Shielded ZEC Now in Ironwood?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where the latest data becomes interesting.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Block reported on September 23 that nearly &lt;strong&gt;5 million ZEC&lt;/strong&gt; was held across Zcash's shielded pools, representing roughly 23% of the total ZEC supply. Ironwood contained about &lt;strong&gt;3.9 million ZEC&lt;/strong&gt;, giving it approximately 80% of the shielded-supply market share. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The distinction between &lt;strong&gt;shielded supply&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;total supply&lt;/strong&gt; is important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Most ZEC is still not inside shielded pools. Zcash supports both transparent and shielded transactions. Transparent addresses expose transaction information on the blockchain, while shielded transactions use zero-knowledge &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/solana-tests-alpenglow-upgrade-to-cut.html"&gt;cryptography &lt;/a&gt;to hide transaction details.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Therefore, saying "80% of ZEC is now in Ironwood" would be inaccurate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A more precise statement is:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;About 80% of Zcash's shielded ZEC is now held in the Ironwood pool.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Are Users Moving Their ZEC to Ironwood?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The primary reason is straightforward: Ironwood is now the network's main new shielded pool.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Orchard can no longer accept new deposits, while Ironwood is designed to provide the forward-looking shielded environment for Zcash.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The migration also gives users a path away from the retired pool following the Orchard vulnerability.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The transition has not been instantaneous because migration is voluntary and depends on wallets, exchanges and individual users supporting the process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;CoinDesk reported that approximately 176,000 ZEC had entered Ironwood during its first day, representing about 5% of the funds held in Orchard at activation. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;By September, the amount had grown to around 3.9 million ZEC, showing how quickly the migration accelerated after the initial launch period. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Makes Ironwood Different From Orchard?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Current role&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Retired for new deposits&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Main new shielded pool&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The official Ironwood design describes the new pool as a separate consensus-relevant value pool while retaining useful components of the Orchard architecture. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does Ironwood Make Zcash Completely Private?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the most important points for anyone researching Zcash.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Zcash privacy is &lt;strong&gt;optional&lt;/strong&gt;. The network supports transparent transactions as well as shielded transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Block reported that a large portion of ZEC remains outside shielded pools. Transparent addresses work more like Bitcoin, where transaction details can be observed on-chain. Shielded pools use zero-knowledge technology to protect transaction information. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Therefore, owning ZEC does not automatically mean that every transaction involving that ZEC is private.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The privacy feature depends on how the coins are used.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Ironwood Migration Matters for Zcash&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The migration is significant for several reasons.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;1. It Moves the Network Beyond Orchard&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Orchard was an important part of Zcash's privacy architecture, but the discovery of the proof-circuit vulnerability changed the network's security assumptions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ironwood gives Zcash a new pool designed around the post-Orchard environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;2. It Concentrates Shielded Activity in One New Pool&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With approximately 3.9 million ZEC already in Ironwood, the majority of Zcash's shielded supply is now concentrated there. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes Ironwood increasingly important to the network's future privacy activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;3. It Provides a New Security Model&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ironwood incorporates formally verified proof circuits and a controlled migration design intended to address the accounting concerns raised by the Orchard vulnerability. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;4. It Creates a New Benchmark for Privacy Adoption&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Future Zcash adoption can be measured not only by the price of ZEC, but also by how much supply enters shielded pools and how frequently shielded transactions are used.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does 3.9 Million ZEC in Ironwood Actually Tell Us?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The migration data provides evidence that users are actively moving funds into the new shielded infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, it should not automatically be interpreted as proof that Zcash adoption is permanently accelerating.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A rise in shielded balances can have several explanations. Existing ZEC holders may simply be migrating from Orchard. Some users may be moving funds because they prefer the new pool. Others may be preparing for future private transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Therefore, the migration number needs to be viewed alongside transaction activity, wallet usage, exchange support and longer-term shielded adoption.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Block's September data shows that Ironwood has become the dominant shielded pool, but the durability of that trend will depend on continued use of Zcash's privacy features. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Ironwood and the Future of Zcash Privacy&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ironwood is more than a routine network upgrade because it addresses both a technical security problem and the future structure of Zcash's privacy system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new pool gives developers and users a fresh foundation for shielded transactions while allowing the network to retire the previous Orchard environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, Zcash still faces broader challenges. Privacy-focused cryptocurrencies operate in a regulatory environment where transaction privacy can create additional compliance questions for exchanges and financial platforms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is also competition from other privacy technologies and networks, meaning technical improvements alone do not guarantee greater adoption.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Zcash, the important question now is whether Ironwood's technical improvements translate into sustained real-world use.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Should Zcash Users Watch Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Several indicators could help show how the Ironwood transition develops:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Ironwood shielded balance:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether the amount of ZEC held in the new pool continues to grow.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Shielded transaction activity:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether users are actually spending and receiving ZEC through shielded transactions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Wallet support:&lt;/strong&gt; How quickly wallets integrate and improve Ironwood functionality.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Exchange support:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether major trading platforms support the migration process smoothly.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Security:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether the new proof system and migration mechanism operate as intended.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Privacy adoption:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether the percentage of ZEC held in shielded pools remains elevated over time.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is Zcash Ironwood?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ironwood is Zcash's newest shielded pool, introduced with the NU6.3 network upgrade in July 2026. It provides the new environment for shielded ZEC after the Orchard pool was retired for new deposits. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is 80% of all ZEC in Ironwood?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. The roughly 80% figure refers to the share of &lt;strong&gt;shielded ZEC&lt;/strong&gt; held in Ironwood. The Block reported about 3.9 million ZEC in Ironwood out of the network's shielded supply. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why was Orchard retired?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Orchard was retired after a vulnerability was discovered in its proof circuit that could theoretically have allowed counterfeit ZEC to be created without normal on-chain evidence. Ironwood introduced a new shielded pool and controlled migration mechanism. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Zcash completely private?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. Zcash supports both transparent and shielded transactions. Privacy is provided when users transact through the shielded pools.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;When did Ironwood launch?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Ironwood upgrade activated on July 28, 2026, at block 3,428,143, according to CoinDesk's report on the upgrade. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why is Ironwood important now?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ironwood has become the dominant shielded pool in Zcash. About 3.9 million ZEC was reported in the pool by September 23, representing roughly 80% of Zcash's shielded supply. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Zcash's Ironwood upgrade marks a major transition in the network's privacy architecture.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important number is not that 80% of all ZEC has moved to Ironwood. Rather, approximately &lt;strong&gt;80% of Zcash's shielded supply&lt;/strong&gt; is now held in the new pool, with around &lt;strong&gt;3.9 million ZEC&lt;/strong&gt; reported there as of September 23. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The migration follows the retirement of Orchard after the discovery of a serious proof-circuit vulnerability. Ironwood provides a new shielded pool, a controlled migration path and a redesigned security framework for the next phase of Zcash's privacy system. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bigger story now is whether the technical transition turns into sustained privacy usage. If shielded balances, transactions and wallet activity continue to grow, Ironwood could become one of the most important developments in Zcash's 2026 evolution.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Term Labs Governance Exploit Drains Estimated $8.5 Million in Crypto</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEign0UQYZkune0Y6Y7vKF58NdN8vKV3M5H5PfxyJwkDa44qLvAvZMQ_RNxheS5t28Xq1EZsB1NKf3mYVxlpCh49PSgxq7Ys0WPSjX61CRnEcvaWzb-U_FjZOOo4gciiDBb47FLSvsRlNvhx4Ydpes7rwiYrjMSVnwQRZ5v_4TYUdXZbMKt4qw7Ea0NDBqD-/s1672/term-labs-governance-exploit-8-5-million-crypto.jpg.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="DeFi governance exploit involving Ethereum and DAI assets at Term Labs" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEign0UQYZkune0Y6Y7vKF58NdN8vKV3M5H5PfxyJwkDa44qLvAvZMQ_RNxheS5t28Xq1EZsB1NKf3mYVxlpCh49PSgxq7Ys0WPSjX61CRnEcvaWzb-U_FjZOOo4gciiDBb47FLSvsRlNvhx4Ydpes7rwiYrjMSVnwQRZ5v_4TYUdXZbMKt4qw7Ea0NDBqD-/w400-h225/term-labs-governance-exploit-8-5-million-crypto.jpg.png" title="Term Labs Governance Exploit Puts $8.5 Million in Crypto at Risk" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br style="mso-special-character: line-break;" /&gt;
&lt;!--[if !supportLineBreakNewLine]--&gt;&lt;br style="mso-special-character: line-break;" /&gt;
&lt;!--[endif]--&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A governance exploit at DeFi protocol &lt;b&gt;Term Labs has
drained an estimated $8.5 million in cryptocurrency&lt;/b&gt;, according to
blockchain security firms tracking the incident.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The attack affected Term Labs' vaults, with the
attacker-linked address holding approximately &lt;b&gt;2,843 ETH and 1.6 million DAI&lt;/b&gt;
after the exploit, according to security researchers.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Term Labs has confirmed that a governance exploit affected
its Term vaults and said it is investigating the incident. The protocol has not
yet publicly confirmed the $8.5 million estimate or released a complete
technical explanation of how the attacker gained control.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That distinction matters. The reported dollar figure
currently comes from security firms monitoring the blockchain, while Term Labs'
own investigation is still underway.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Happened to Term Labs?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Term Labs operates a decentralized finance system built
around lending and borrowing through its vault infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;On August 23, unusual activity involving Term vaults was
flagged by blockchain security researchers. Term Labs subsequently acknowledged
that a &lt;b&gt;governance exploit&lt;/b&gt; had affected the vaults.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;CertiK estimated the losses at approximately &lt;b&gt;$8.5 million&lt;/b&gt;.
PeckShield separately reported that roughly &lt;b&gt;2,843 ETH&lt;/b&gt;, worth around
$6.87 million at the time of its analysis, and approximately &lt;b&gt;1.68 million
USDC&lt;/b&gt; had been drained. The USDC was subsequently swapped for roughly &lt;b&gt;1.68
million DAI&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The figures may change as investigators continue tracing the
transactions and determining the full extent of the incident.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why the Word “Governance” Matters&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The word &lt;b&gt;“governance” is important here — it
distinguishes this attack from a typical smart-contract bug.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In DeFi, governance systems are used to manage important
protocol decisions. Depending on how a protocol is designed, governance can
influence vault parameters, treasury movements, upgrades and other
administrative functions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That makes governance itself a potential attack surface.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In the Term Labs incident, the protocol has specifically
described the event as a governance exploit. However, the exact mechanism used
by the attacker has not yet been fully explained by Term Labs.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Some reports suggest the attacker obtained enough voting
control to influence strategy vaults, but a complete technical postmortem from
&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/elliptic-says-irans-nobitex-was-hit-in.html"&gt;Term Labs&lt;/a&gt; is still pending.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Until that investigation is complete, it is better to
describe the attack as a &lt;b&gt;governance exploit&lt;/b&gt; rather than speculate about
a specific technical vulnerability.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Numbers Behind the Estimated $8.5 Million Loss&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The on-chain movements provide the clearest picture
currently available.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Security researchers reported that the attacker-linked
wallet contained approximately:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;2,843
     ETH&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;1.6
     million DAI&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Estimated
     total value: about $8.5 million&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The dollar value is not fixed because cryptocurrency prices
move continuously.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;PeckShield also reported that approximately &lt;b&gt;1.68 million
USDC&lt;/b&gt; was moved and subsequently exchanged for DAI.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Because Term Labs has not yet published a final accounting,
the $8.5 million figure should be described as an &lt;b&gt;estimate&lt;/b&gt;, not as a
definitive final loss figure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That distinction is particularly important in breaking
crypto-security stories, where assets can move between wallets rapidly after an
exploit.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;How the Attacker's Wallet Is Being Tracked&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;One of the unusual features of blockchain-based attacks is
that the movement of funds can be watched publicly.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Researchers can follow transactions from the affected
protocol to the attacker-linked wallet and monitor subsequent transfers.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In this case, the address associated with the exploit was
reported to hold thousands of ETH alongside millions of dollars worth of DAI.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But there is an important limitation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;A blockchain address can show where funds went — but it
does not automatically reveal who sent them.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The wallet address itself does not establish the real-world
identity of the person or group controlling it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That means on-chain tracing can provide valuable evidence
about what happened to the assets without necessarily proving who was behind
the attack.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Tornado Cash Connection&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;PeckShield reported that the attacker-linked address
initially received &lt;b&gt;2 ETH from Tornado Cash&lt;/b&gt; before the exploit
transactions began.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That detail has attracted attention because Tornado Cash is
designed to make the connection between incoming and outgoing blockchain
transactions harder to follow.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;However, the funding trail should not be confused with
attacker identification.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Receiving funds from a mixer does &lt;b&gt;not by itself prove who
controlled the wallet or who carried out the exploit&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Further investigation would be needed to establish
attribution.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For now, it is best understood as an on-chain funding
detail.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Term Labs Has Confirmed&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Term Labs has publicly acknowledged the incident and said
that a governance exploit affected its Term vaults.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The protocol said it would provide more information after
the incident had been investigated further.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Several questions therefore remain open.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It is not yet clear from Term Labs' public statement:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Which
     specific vaults were affected&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Exactly
     how governance control was obtained&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Whether
     all deposits were exposed&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Whether
     any assets can be recovered&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Whether
     withdrawals or other protocol functions have been restricted&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Whether
     users will receive compensation&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;When
     the full technical postmortem will be released&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Those details will be important for determining the ultimate
impact of the attack.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Governance Attacks Are Different From Smart-Contract
Hacks&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A conventional smart-contract exploit may involve a coding
error such as a reentrancy vulnerability, faulty accounting or an incorrectly
implemented permission check.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A governance attack can work differently.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Instead of directly breaking the underlying code, an
attacker may attempt to gain enough legitimate-looking control within the
protocol's decision-making system to authorize actions that benefit them.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Possible weaknesses can include concentrated voting power,
low participation, inadequate quorum requirements or insufficient safeguards
around sensitive governance decisions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;However, &lt;b&gt;those are general governance risks and should
not automatically be treated as the confirmed cause of the Term Labs incident&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The exact attack path remains part of the investigation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why the Incident Matters for DeFi&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Term Labs exploit highlights a broader problem for
decentralized finance.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Audited smart contracts are important, but audits do not
necessarily eliminate governance risk.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A protocol can have carefully reviewed code and still face
serious problems if its governance system can be manipulated.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That is why DeFi users increasingly need to look beyond a
simple question such as whether a protocol has been audited.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;They also need to understand:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Who controls the protocol?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;How much voting power is required to approve major
actions?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Are there delays before governance decisions take effect?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Can emergency controls stop suspicious transactions?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What happens if voting power becomes concentrated?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;These questions become especially important when governance
has authority over large pools of user funds.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The next major development will likely come from Term Labs'
investigation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The protocol will need to explain how the governance system
was compromised, which vaults were affected and whether the vulnerability has
been contained.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It will also need to clarify the final amount of assets
lost.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For now, security firms estimate the damage at roughly &lt;b&gt;$8.5
million&lt;/b&gt;, while the attacker-linked address has been reported to hold
approximately &lt;b&gt;2,843 ETH and 1.6 million DAI&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Those numbers could change as investigators trace additional
transactions or identify assets that may have been recovered.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A detailed postmortem would also help the wider DeFi
community understand whether the incident resulted from a governance design
weakness, compromised voting control or another failure in the protocol's
administrative architecture.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Term Labs has suffered a serious governance exploit that
security firms estimate resulted in approximately &lt;b&gt;$8.5 million in
&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/brian-armstrong-predicts-clarity-act.html"&gt;cryptocurrency&lt;/a&gt; losses&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The attacker-linked wallet was reported to hold around &lt;b&gt;2,843
ETH and 1.6 million DAI&lt;/b&gt;, while researchers continue tracking the movement
of the assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But the investigation is not finished.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Term Labs has confirmed that its vaults were affected by a
governance exploit, while the exact attack mechanism and final loss amount have
yet to be fully established.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For DeFi users, the incident is another reminder that
decentralization does not automatically remove every point of failure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The key question now is not simply where the stolen
cryptocurrency went.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It is &lt;b&gt;how the attacker gained the authority to move the
funds — and whether Term Labs can prevent a repeat of the same vulnerability.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;CoinAINews provides independent coverage of
cryptocurrency, blockchain, technology and financial markets. This article is
for informational purposes only and does not constitute financial advice.&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
