margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The lab is part of Morgan Stanley's broader innovation network, which runs up to 270 projects annually.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;hr style="background: none 0% 0% / auto repeat scroll padding-box border-box rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1); border-color: currentcolor; border-image: none; border-style: none; border-width: medium; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; height: 1px; margin: 32px 0px;" /&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Morgan Stanley has set up a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Digital Asset Lab&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; to test blockchain-based technologies including stablecoins, tokenization, and decentralized finance applications, according to a Bloomberg report citing an interview with Megan Brewer, who leads market innovation and labs at the firm.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The lab is part of Morgan Stanley's existing network of innovation labs, which give employees dedicated facilities to explore emerging technologies without putting the bank's core systems at risk.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What the Lab Will Test&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The digital asset lab will explore a range of blockchain-native technologies, including tokenized deposits, central bank digital currencies, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitget-attackers-move-stolen-funds-into.html"&gt;tokenized money&lt;/a&gt; market funds, and DeFi vaults.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Amy Oldenburg, head of Morgan Stanley's digital assets division, said the lab provides a "secure, compliant and segregated environment to be able to test and explore some of these new areas of digital assets."&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What Are DeFi Vaults?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;A vault is a pool of assets that uses blockchain-based software to automatically deploy capital according to a predetermined strategy. Investors deposit assets — often &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/netherlands-box-3-tax-plan-how-proposed.html"&gt;stablecoins &lt;/a&gt;or other digital tokens — into a vault, which then puts them to work across a range of decentralized markets. Investors typically receive a token representing their share in the vault.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;For asset managers, vaults resemble investment funds that automate elements of portfolio management and administration. That could allow firms to create new investment products, automate strategies, and operate them around the clock.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Oldenburg said there is "a very reasonable path to see vaults being part of the future going forward," but noted that the technology is still "nascent" and the bank cannot put its platform at risk. This makes vaults a good candidate for testing in the lab.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Morgan Stanley's Broader Crypto Push&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The lab extends a digital-asset expansion that is already moving into live products. In April, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Morgan Stanley Investment Management&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; launched the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust (MSBT)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; , a spot Bitcoin ETF that now manages over &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;$871 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; in assets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The bank's asset management arm also launched Ethereum and Solana ETFs, each charging a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;0.14% fee&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; and structured to pass staking rewards through to investors. The Ethereum Trust (MSSE) stakes between 50% and 80% of its ETH, while the Solana Trust (MSOL) plans to stake all of its SOL. Roughly 95% of staking rewards are passed through to shareholders.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;On the trading side, eligible &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;E*Trade&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; clients can now trade &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/trader-turns-105m-aster-long-into-65.html"&gt;Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana&lt;/a&gt; through infrastructure provided by zerohash.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Morgan Stanley Investment Management also launched the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Stablecoin Reserves Portfolio (MSNXX)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; , a money market fund designed for stablecoin issuers operating under the GENIUS Act.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What It Means&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The digital asset lab is a signal that Morgan Stanley is exploring how blockchain-based systems could be used across its business, from stablecoin settlement and tokenized collateral to programmable deposits that could connect with brokerage, asset-management, and wealth-management infrastructure.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;For Wall Street, the move reflects a broader trend: banks and financial firms are deepening their investments in digital assets as efforts to bring traditional assets onto blockchains gather pace.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Morgan Stanley's innovation labs run up to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;270 projects a year&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; and occupy &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;20,000 square feet&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; across cities including New York, Glasgow, and Bangalore.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What is Morgan Stanley's Digital Asset Lab?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;It's a segregated testing environment where Morgan Stanley employees can experiment with stablecoins, tokenization, and DeFi applications without risking the bank's core systems.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What DeFi applications will the lab test?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The lab will test DeFi vaults — pools of assets that use blockchain-based software to automatically deploy capital according to predetermined strategies.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Does Morgan Stanley already offer crypto products?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Yes. The bank offers crypto trading on E*Trade and its asset management arm runs spot Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana ETFs. It also launched a stablecoin reserve money market fund.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Why is this significant?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;It signals that a major Wall Street bank is actively exploring how blockchain-based infrastructure could be integrated into traditional financial operations, from settlement to collateral management.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Bottom line:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Morgan Stanley's Digital Asset Lab is a testing ground for stablecoins, tokenization, and DeFi — the building blocks of onchain finance. The bank's asset management arm already runs live crypto products, and the lab gives it a segregated environment to explore what comes next. For Wall Street, it's a sign that tokenization is moving from experiment to infrastructure.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>

    <title>POSCO International Expands Blockchain Trade Finance With Second Tokenization Pilot</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEho-lhX-HkfQP9rd1Ni__Wjk7u5EONUW12fqVlD7sQ5ncWCa1nZti0UQwtJabEvA3DqclMo3urhMXy9slgfk2NCU1sHflyETckbYAaotYDmzfgmtFETeie7swf1T8oMT6evAzb3qYY_sOhN3rvvSNhuV_YzhRXVxtzEqJIDGkE5Yb4z4lK-cSfgkPhBPkbp/s1672/posco-international-blockchain-trade-finance-tokenization-pilot.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="POSCO International blockchain trade finance tokenization pilot with digital trade receivables" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEho-lhX-HkfQP9rd1Ni__Wjk7u5EONUW12fqVlD7sQ5ncWCa1nZti0UQwtJabEvA3DqclMo3urhMXy9slgfk2NCU1sHflyETckbYAaotYDmzfgmtFETeie7swf1T8oMT6evAzb3qYY_sOhN3rvvSNhuV_YzhRXVxtzEqJIDGkE5Yb4z4lK-cSfgkPhBPkbp/w400-h225/posco-international-blockchain-trade-finance-tokenization-pilot.webp.png" title="POSCO International Tests Blockchain Tokenization for Trade Finance" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&amp;nbsp;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;POSCO International is taking another step toward bringing blockchain into global trade finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The South Korean trading company has completed a new pilot that converted real trade receivables into tokenized digital assets and recorded them on-chain. The project was carried out by &lt;strong&gt;POSCO International America&lt;/strong&gt; with trade-finance platform &lt;strong&gt;Olea&lt;/strong&gt; and blockchain infrastructure company &lt;strong&gt;Intain&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The transaction was executed on Intain's Layer-1 network, which is built using &lt;strong&gt;Avalanche&lt;/strong&gt; infrastructure. The development follows a separate trade-finance proof of concept completed by POSCO International with &lt;strong&gt;LG CNS and Injective&lt;/strong&gt; in July.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Rather than committing immediately to a single blockchain network, POSCO International appears to be testing different infrastructure approaches for a practical problem: making trade finance easier to verify, finance and manage digitally.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happened in the Latest Pilot?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest transaction focused on &lt;strong&gt;trade receivables&lt;/strong&gt; — &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/mistral-partners-with-saudi-backed.html"&gt;money&lt;/a&gt; that a company is entitled to receive after selling goods but before the buyer has actually paid.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These receivables can potentially be used as financing assets, but traditional trade-finance processes often involve large amounts of documentation and repeated checks between buyers, sellers, banks and financing providers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the POSCO pilot, Intain's platform was used to reconcile information from several types of trade documents, including:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Invoices&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Purchase orders&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Credit notes&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Shipping documents&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;After the information was verified, the receivables were converted into tokenized digital assets and registered on Intain's network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This created a digital record of the asset's ownership and transaction history while keeping the process connected to institutional trade-finance infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The transaction also involved actual trade receivables rather than being limited to a theoretical demonstration. Olea participated as the financing platform and used its own capital to acquire the tokenized receivables.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Tokenizing Trade Receivables Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trade finance is one of the less visible parts of the global economy, but it supports enormous amounts of international commerce.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A single transaction can involve buyers, sellers, subsidiaries, banks, logistics providers and financing companies. Each participant may maintain separate records, creating additional work when the parties need to confirm what was sold, who owns the receivable and whether the asset has already been financed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchain can potentially simplify part of that process by creating a shared digital record.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of every participant maintaining completely separate versions of the same information, authorized parties can work from a common record showing the status and ownership of a tokenized asset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not automatically make trade finance faster or cheaper. However, if implemented correctly, digital records could reduce some of the manual reconciliation involved in verifying commercial assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Is Also Part of the Process&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest pilot is notable because it combines &lt;strong&gt;artificial intelligence with blockchain&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI was used to reconcile and verify information contained in trade documents before the receivables were recorded on-chain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The two technologies address different parts of the workflow. AI can help process and compare large amounts of documentation, while &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/thorchain-320-brings-monero-and-zcash.html"&gt;blockchain&lt;/a&gt; can provide a shared record once the relevant information has been verified.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In this case, Intain's platform handled information from invoices, purchase orders, credit notes and shipping documentation before the asset was registered on-chain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes the project more than a simple tokenization exercise. It is an attempt to connect document verification, asset digitization and financing within a single digital workflow.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;POSCO Has Tested Two Blockchain Approaches&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest Avalanche-based project follows POSCO International's earlier collaboration with LG CNS and Injective.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That July project tested the use of blockchain for tokenized accounts receivable generated from actual international trade activity. POSCO International said the proof of concept examined areas including shared transaction records, tokenization of accounts receivable and AI-based automation of trade operations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The two projects can be summarized as follows:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 16px; margin: 20px 0px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Date&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Network&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Partners&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;What Was Tested&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px;"&gt;July 2026&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px;"&gt;Injective&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px;"&gt;LG CNS&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px;"&gt;Tokenized trade receivables, &lt;br /&gt;shared ledger and AI-based &lt;br /&gt;trade-finance processes&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px;"&gt;August 2026&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px;"&gt;Intain Layer-1 built on Avalanche infrastructure&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px;"&gt;Olea and Intain&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px;"&gt;AI-verified trade receivables, &lt;br /&gt;on-chain registration &lt;br /&gt;and institutional financing&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The significance is less about which blockchain wins and more about the fact that POSCO International is evaluating multiple approaches for institutional trade finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;POSCO Is Not Using Blockchain Just for Crypto Trading&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Perhaps the most interesting part of the development is that these experiments are focused on &lt;strong&gt;traditional financial assets&lt;/strong&gt; rather than cryptocurrency trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trade receivables already represent economic activity. Tokenization changes how those claims can potentially be represented, transferred and tracked digitally.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That places POSCO's experiments within the broader &lt;strong&gt;real-world asset (RWA)&lt;/strong&gt; trend, in which traditional financial and commercial assets are increasingly being represented on blockchain networks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The potential benefit is straightforward: if ownership and transaction information can be verified digitally, financing providers may be able to assess assets more efficiently.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For a company operating across multiple countries and business units, even relatively small improvements in reconciliation and financing could become meaningful if they work at scale.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Scale of POSCO International's Operations&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;POSCO International operates across industries including steel, energy and battery materials and has a substantial international footprint.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company reported approximately &lt;strong&gt;$22.2 billion in annual revenue&lt;/strong&gt; and operates more than 80 overseas branches, making its blockchain experiments particularly relevant to the discussion around enterprise adoption.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the technology tested in these projects eventually moves into broader production use, the potential application could extend across a large international trade network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That remains a possibility rather than an established outcome. A successful pilot does not necessarily mean a company will deploy the same system across its entire business.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Stablecoins Could Be the Next Step&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;POSCO International, Olea and Intain are also looking beyond receivables tokenization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The companies plan to explore additional applications involving &lt;strong&gt;stablecoin-based cross-border payments&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;digital treasury solutions&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could eventually create a broader blockchain-based trade-finance workflow.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, tokenized receivables could represent the financing side of a transaction, while stablecoins could potentially provide another mechanism for digital settlement across borders.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are still major questions around regulation, compliance, liquidity and institutional adoption, so it is too early to say how quickly such a system could become commercially widespread.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Still, the direction is notable. POSCO and its partners are looking beyond tokenization as an isolated blockchain experiment and exploring how different digital components could work together.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Trade-Finance Market Is Watching&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The global trade-finance system has a persistent financing gap.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Asian Development Bank has estimated the global trade-finance gap at around &lt;strong&gt;$2.5 trillion&lt;/strong&gt;, representing legitimate trade transactions that lack sufficient financing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tokenization will not eliminate that gap on its own.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, making trade assets easier to verify, transfer and finance could potentially remove some of the friction that prevents capital from reaching businesses that need it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is one reason trade receivables have become an increasingly interesting use case for blockchain technology.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Unlike speculative crypto assets, receivables are connected to existing commercial activity. The blockchain infrastructure is being tested around an established financial asset rather than creating an entirely new financial claim.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What This Means for Avalanche and Injective&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The POSCO experiments also show how competition between blockchain networks is moving beyond retail cryptocurrency applications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Avalanche&lt;/strong&gt; has increasingly positioned its infrastructure for institutional &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/monad-developers-propose-upgradeable.html"&gt;tokenization&lt;/a&gt; and financial applications, while &lt;strong&gt;Injective&lt;/strong&gt; has focused heavily on infrastructure designed for financial markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;POSCO International's decision to test both approaches shows why large enterprises may not want to commit to one blockchain immediately.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Companies can evaluate different networks based on factors such as transaction performance, privacy, compliance requirements, asset controls and integration with existing financial systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For blockchain networks, winning these enterprise experiments could eventually prove more valuable than attracting short-term speculative trading activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Biggest Challenge: Moving Beyond Pilots&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is still a significant gap between completing a pilot and deploying a system at commercial scale.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A proof of concept can demonstrate that a technology works under controlled conditions. Running the same workflow across thousands of transactions, multiple jurisdictions and numerous financial institutions is a much harder challenge.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;POSCO International and its partners will ultimately need to determine whether blockchain-based processes provide enough efficiency to justify the cost and complexity of integrating them into existing systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Regulation will also play an important role.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trade finance involves sensitive commercial information, credit risk, compliance checks and multiple legal jurisdictions. Any production system would need to address those issues before becoming part of everyday corporate operations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Comes Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next stage will be watching whether POSCO International and its partners expand these experiments into larger operational deployments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The companies have already identified areas such as stablecoin settlement and digital treasury management for further exploration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those developments could eventually turn the current experiments into a more connected digital trade-finance system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the important point is that POSCO International is continuing to test blockchain around &lt;strong&gt;real commercial trade activity&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than treating tokenization only as a theoretical exercise.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;POSCO International's latest pilot shows how blockchain experimentation is moving deeper into traditional corporate finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company has now tested trade-receivables tokenization using &lt;strong&gt;Injective&lt;/strong&gt; and, more recently, an &lt;strong&gt;Intain Layer-1 network built on Avalanche infrastructure&lt;/strong&gt;, working with different technology and financing partners.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The projects combine blockchain with AI-powered document verification and focus on a very practical problem: making trade-finance assets easier to verify, track and finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next question is whether the efficiency gains are strong enough to justify moving from controlled pilots to larger-scale production.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If they are, POSCO International's experiments could become an early example of blockchain quietly entering one of the world's oldest financial systems — not through crypto speculation, but through the invoices, receivables and payments that keep global trade moving.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment or financial advice. Blockchain projects, tokenization initiatives and regulatory frameworks can change as development continues. Readers should verify current information before making financial decisions.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
</content>

    <title>Bill Gates Seeks Xi Jinping Meeting to Discuss Global AI Risks</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiWcZ0yIddPNR7NTyH3kTzvWQM6racpoAuinnt9Ta7Tta4w2liadcq6tLmfFiTXFSGRepvS1HvKsgWHTfy8FU1OxbpaiaUlbNtUnFCSU_Q10OkrcNKsPeGRE7Yc064MjWbuO_ArpIYkY83qtmgNu1ClmGd4weyCd2hhI7vIS14DPY6aLgGqDv0VD5-iNp1o/s1672/bill-gates-xi-jinping-global-ai-risk-talks.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bill Gates seeks meeting with Xi Jinping to discuss global AI risks and international safeguards." border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiWcZ0yIddPNR7NTyH3kTzvWQM6racpoAuinnt9Ta7Tta4w2liadcq6tLmfFiTXFSGRepvS1HvKsgWHTfy8FU1OxbpaiaUlbNtUnFCSU_Q10OkrcNKsPeGRE7Yc064MjWbuO_ArpIYkY83qtmgNu1ClmGd4weyCd2hhI7vIS14DPY6aLgGqDv0VD5-iNp1o/w400-h225/bill-gates-xi-jinping-global-ai-risk-talks.jpg.png" title="Bill Gates and Xi Jinping AI Risk Talks" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;By CoinAINews Staff | &lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bill Gates wants to take his concerns about artificial
intelligence directly to Beijing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Microsoft co-founder is seeking a meeting with Chinese
President &lt;b&gt;Xi Jinping later this year&lt;/b&gt; to discuss how countries could work
together on some of the risks created by increasingly capable AI systems,
according to Reuters. Gates' staff are working to arrange the meeting during
his next China trip, which is tentatively planned for November.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Gates is not proposing a blanket crackdown on AI. Instead,
he wants countries to pay closer attention to specific capabilities that could
create serious security risks, including AI systems that can help create
molecules or contribute to biological attacks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;His broader argument is that the technology is moving
quickly enough that governments need to start coordinating before the risks
become harder to manage.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Gates Wants to Talk to Xi&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The U.S. and China are competing intensely in &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/posco-international-expands-blockchain.html"&gt;artificialintelligence&lt;/a&gt;, but Gates believes that competition does not eliminate the need
for cooperation on certain safety issues.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;He told Reuters that China could potentially support
restrictions on the release of particularly dangerous AI models if the United
States took the first step.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The idea is fairly simple: if Washington establishes a clear
framework for the highest-risk AI systems, other countries could adopt similar
measures instead of creating completely different rules.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Gates believes that could eventually lead to a broader
international approach.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Whether that is politically realistic is another matter.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The U.S. and China have major disagreements over technology,
trade and national security. Reaching even limited agreement on AI would
therefore be a significant diplomatic challenge.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The AI Risks That Concern Gates&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Gates' concerns have become sharper in recent months.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;He is worried about AI being used for cyberattacks, its
impact on employment and the possibility that increasingly sophisticated
systems could influence people in ways that are difficult to control.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;He has also focused on biological risks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;One proposal he wants to raise is international monitoring
of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/mistral-partners-with-saudi-backed.html"&gt;AI systems&lt;/a&gt; capable of creating molecules or assisting with biological
attacks. Gates believes such monitoring could focus on dangerous capabilities
without unnecessarily restricting legitimate AI research.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That distinction matters.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;AI is already being used in areas such as scientific
research, drug discovery and biology. Rules that are too broad could interfere
with useful work, while doing too little could leave potentially dangerous
capabilities largely unchecked.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The challenge is figuring out where that line should be
drawn.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Recent AI Hacking Incidents Have Added to His Concern&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Gates is also paying attention to what advanced AI systems
are already capable of doing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;According to Reuters, he pointed to recent cybersecurity
evaluations involving models from companies including &lt;b&gt;OpenAI, Anthropic and
Meta&lt;/b&gt;, where AI systems were able to hack real-world websites during
testing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For Gates, incidents like these are a sign that AI
capabilities are moving into territory that governments need to take seriously.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The concern is not simply that AI can generate code.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;More capable systems can potentially analyze a problem,
identify weaknesses and carry out multiple steps with limited human
intervention. As those capabilities improve, the consequences of misuse could
become larger as well.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Jobs Are Another Part of the Problem&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Gates' AI concerns extend beyond cybersecurity and
biological risks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;He has also warned about the effect of AI on employment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;AI is already being used for programming, research, customer
support, administration and other knowledge-based work. As models become better
at handling complex tasks, more jobs could be affected.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The difficult part is the speed of the transition.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Workers and businesses may have years to adapt to some
technological changes. AI development, however, is moving quickly, raising
questions about whether education systems, employers and governments can
respond at the same pace.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Gates has recently argued that governments should prepare
for this disruption rather than waiting until large numbers of workers have
already been affected.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Gates Wants a New International Approach&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Gates' proposal goes beyond asking individual countries to
introduce their own AI rules.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;He has called for a new international organization that
could help oversee some of the most serious risks associated with AI.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The concept draws comparisons with international systems
created around other high-risk technologies and activities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Such an organization could potentially help countries share
information, establish common safety standards and monitor particularly
sensitive AI capabilities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But creating it would be difficult.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Countries would have to agree on what should be monitored,
who would have access to information and how the rules would be enforced.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There would also be concerns about national security and
technological competition.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why China Is Important to the Conversation&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;China is now one of the world's major AI powers, which makes
its involvement important in any serious attempt at international AI
coordination.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Chinese companies are developing increasingly capable AI
models, while the government has also been building its own regulatory
framework around artificial intelligence.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That means a global AI agreement that excludes China would
have obvious limitations.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Gates appears to recognize that.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;His proposed conversation with Xi is therefore not simply
about China adopting U.S. rules. The larger idea is to see whether the two
countries can find areas where their interests overlap despite their broader
technological rivalry.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That could start with a relatively narrow set of high-risk
AI capabilities rather than a sweeping global agreement.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Timing Could Be Important&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The proposed meeting comes at a particularly interesting
moment for the AI industry.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Companies are releasing increasingly capable models, while
governments are still trying to understand how those systems should be
regulated.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;AI is no longer limited to chatbots that answer questions.
Modern systems can write software, use digital tools, analyze large amounts of
information and carry out longer sequences of tasks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That makes the policy debate more complicated.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A rule designed for traditional software may not be
sufficient for an AI system capable of performing many different types of work.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;At the same time, governments have to be careful not to slow
down useful applications in medicine, science, education and business.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Would U.S.-China Cooperation Actually Look Like?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There is no agreement yet.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Gates is seeking a conversation with Xi, and it remains
unclear whether the proposed meeting will lead to any formal policy initiative.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But there are several areas where limited cooperation could
theoretically begin.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Countries could share information about the capabilities of
advanced AI models, establish common testing standards for high-risk systems or
develop procedures for identifying models that present unusual biological or
cybersecurity risks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Those steps would not require the U.S. and China to agree on
every aspect of AI policy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;They could instead focus on areas where the consequences of
a major failure would affect both countries.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A Difficult Road Ahead&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The biggest obstacle may not be the technology itself.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It could be trust.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The United States and China are competing for leadership in
AI, computing infrastructure and advanced semiconductor technology. Both
countries also view AI as strategically important to their economies and
national security.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That makes international oversight complicated.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Any system that requires countries to share information
about powerful AI models would have to deal with concerns about intellectual
property, security and competitive advantage.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There is also the question of enforcement.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Unlike physical materials, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/thorchain-320-brings-monero-and-zcash.html"&gt;AI models&lt;/a&gt; can be copied, modified
and distributed digitally. That makes international monitoring considerably
more complicated than traditional inspections.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For now, the next step is simply whether Gates manages to
meet Xi.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Reuters reports that Gates' staff are working to finalize
the meeting for his next China trip, tentatively scheduled for November. China
has not immediately responded to Reuters' request for comment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If the meeting takes place, Gates is expected to push for
international cooperation around AI risks rather than focusing only on U.S.
domestic policy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The response from Beijing could provide an early indication
of how much room there is for cooperation between the world's two major AI
powers.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bill Gates' attempt to meet Xi Jinping shows how quickly AI
safety has moved from a technology-industry discussion into international
policy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;His concern is not that AI development should simply stop.
His argument is that some capabilities may become dangerous enough to require
countries to agree on common safeguards.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The most immediate issues include biological risks,
cybersecurity and the potential disruption of jobs.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Whether Washington and Beijing can cooperate on those
questions remains uncertain.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But as AI systems become more capable, the debate is
increasingly shifting from &lt;b&gt;what AI can do&lt;/b&gt; to a harder question: &lt;b&gt;who
decides which capabilities are too risky to leave without international
oversight?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This article is for informational purposes only. AI
capabilities, government policies and international discussions can change
rapidly. Readers should verify the latest information from authoritative
sources.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>AI Made Millions in Crypto — Who Pays the Tax?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjaO-RJRzWdvImljN-g0z8S64t2pv_y0Ny4cJbzd_Ba9iVBSsxEbOlKGSBSY2A8bcFQmnpoR5by4hbdYjz7JhrAuv_ja8Y95KX9qehHadLWmpeV4faDv1L9LQ79XOaY8l50K20yBPqH-xp0NAbRjEIJoaeG5a6pHjxyuJftSRo_9mt4aIW-mnseTKEdw2rZ/s1248/ai-crypto-trading-tax-million-profits.jpg.jpg" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="AI trading cryptocurrency and generating millions in crypto profits" border="0" data-original-height="832" data-original-width="1248" height="426" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjaO-RJRzWdvImljN-g0z8S64t2pv_y0Ny4cJbzd_Ba9iVBSsxEbOlKGSBSY2A8bcFQmnpoR5by4hbdYjz7JhrAuv_ja8Y95KX9qehHadLWmpeV4faDv1L9LQ79XOaY8l50K20yBPqH-xp0NAbRjEIJoaeG5a6pHjxyuJftSRo_9mt4aIW-mnseTKEdw2rZ/w640-h426/ai-crypto-trading-tax-million-profits.jpg.jpg" title="AI Made Millions in Crypto — Who Pays the Tax?" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;Imagine waking up to a notification that an AI trading agent has turned $100,000 of cryptocurrency into $10 million overnight.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The trades were executed automatically. The software decided when to buy and sell. No human pressed the final confirmation button.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Now comes the uncomfortable question: &lt;strong&gt;who pays the tax?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The obvious answer might be, “the AI.” But tax law does not generally treat an AI system as a taxpayer simply because software made the trades.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a much more interesting problem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As AI agents become capable of managing wallets, executing transactions and interacting with financial systems, the technology is moving faster than the legal language designed around it. India, for example, is now working on systems to identify and monitor AI agents making payments, while regulators and policymakers in other markets are also trying to understand how responsibility should work when software acts on behalf of a person or business. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So if an AI really does make millions trading crypto, the important question is not simply whether the AI owes tax.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is &lt;strong&gt;whose economic activity the AI is carrying out, who owns the assets, and who is legally responsible for the transactions.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;First, Can AI Actually Make the Trades?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That part is no longer science fiction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI systems can already be connected to financial tools, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ai-with-wallet-can-it-spend-your-crypto.html"&gt;blockchain wallets&lt;/a&gt; and trading infrastructure. An agent can analyze market information, generate a trading decision and, where it has been given the necessary authority, interact with software that executes the transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is an important distinction between &lt;strong&gt;technical capability&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;profitable investing&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A September 2026 review of research covering AI in equity and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-ai-autonomously-own-and-manage.html"&gt;crypto markets&lt;/a&gt; found meaningful progress in prediction, portfolio construction and automated execution, but said the public evidence is still much thinner when it comes to proving durable, risk-adjusted profits across changing market conditions. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In other words, an AI trading system can trade automatically without being a guaranteed money-making machine.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Our hypothetical $10 million profit is therefore a scenario — not a claim that today's AI agents can reliably produce those returns.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;So Who Actually Pays the Tax?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In most cases, the starting point is surprisingly ordinary:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Look at the person or legal entity that owns the assets and is conducting the economic activity.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The fact that software placed the order does not automatically move the income or gains onto the AI itself.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, imagine Sarah owns a crypto portfolio worth $100,000. She gives an AI agent permission to trade that portfolio. Six months later, the portfolio is worth $10 million.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI made the decisions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But Sarah still owns the wallet and the underlying assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not normally turn the AI into the taxpayer. Instead, the tax consequences would generally be analyzed under the rules that apply to Sarah and the transactions the agent carried out.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The same basic logic can apply when a company owns the wallet and deploys an AI trading system on its behalf. In that case, the company may be the relevant taxpayer, subject to the tax rules of the jurisdiction in which it operates.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The exact answer can change dramatically depending on the country, ownership structure, type of transaction and whether the activity is treated as investment, business income or something else.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The U.S. Already Treats Crypto Transactions as Taxable Events&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. provides a useful example of why “the AI did it” is not likely to be a complete tax argument.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The IRS says digital assets such as cryptocurrency and NFTs may have to be reported on a tax return and that income from digital assets is taxable. IRS guidance also generally treats digital assets as property, meaning general tax principles applicable to property transactions can apply. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means an AI executing a crypto transaction does not automatically make the transaction invisible to the tax system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is another important development: U.S. digital-asset broker reporting rules have expanded, including the introduction of Form 1099-DA reporting for certain digital-asset transactions. The IRS says the reporting regime applies to dispositions of digital assets by brokers under the applicable rules. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So an autonomous trading system may make transactions faster, but it does not necessarily make the resulting tax records disappear.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What About the U.K.?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.K. takes a similarly important approach: the tax treatment depends on what the person is doing with the crypto and the circumstances involved.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;HM Revenue &amp;amp; Customs says that selling, exchanging or giving away cryptoassets can create a Capital Gains Tax obligation. Crypto received in certain circumstances, including employment or mining, can instead raise income-tax considerations. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Now imagine an AI agent performs hundreds of crypto swaps automatically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The fact that the trades were generated by software does not by itself answer the tax question. The underlying transactions and the taxpayer's circumstances still matter.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction could become increasingly important as autonomous systems start performing large numbers of transactions on behalf of individuals and businesses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Europe Is Moving Toward More Crypto Tax Transparency&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Europe is also making crypto transactions more visible to tax authorities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The European Commission says DAC8 rules entered into force on January 1, 2026, expanding tax transparency and automatic exchange of information to crypto-asset transactions. Reporting crypto-asset service providers are therefore becoming an increasingly important part of the information chain between crypto activity and tax authorities. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This matters for AI trading because automation can dramatically increase transaction volume.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A human trader might make a handful of decisions each week. An automated system could potentially interact with markets far more frequently.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;More transactions mean more records to reconcile, more cost-basis questions and potentially more taxable events depending on the jurisdiction and activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If the AI Has Its Own Wallet?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where things become much more interesting.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI agent can technically be given access to a crypto wallet and can potentially hold or move digital assets through the credentials and infrastructure controlling that wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But &lt;strong&gt;technical control is not automatically the same thing as legal ownership.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI wallet could belong economically to a person, company, DAO, service provider or another legal structure. The agent may simply be the software authorized to operate it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is critical.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Giving an AI the ability to sign a blockchain transaction does not necessarily create a new legal person that owns the resulting profits.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If Nobody Presses “Approve”?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is the part that makes AI trading different from traditional automated finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Suppose an investor gives an agent the instruction:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;“Trade my crypto portfolio according to this strategy. You can execute transactions without asking me every time.”&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI then executes hundreds of trades.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The investor may never manually approve any individual transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Does that mean the investor has no responsibility for the result?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not necessarily.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The absence of a human click does not automatically mean the absence of human authorization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If a person deliberately gives software authority to operate their assets, that authorization can be an important part of understanding who is acting and for whose account the transactions are occurring. The precise legal consequences, however, depend on the jurisdiction, agreements and facts involved.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Problem: What If the AI Loses Money?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tax questions become even messier when the AI does not make millions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Suppose the agent turns $1 million into $200,000.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Who owns the loss?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Again, the answer does not simply become “the AI.”&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The tax treatment of losses depends on the applicable country's rules, the taxpayer's status, the nature of the transactions and how the activity is classified.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And there is a second issue that tax law cannot answer by itself:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Who is responsible if the AI made an unauthorized or erroneous trade?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is a liability question rather than simply a tax question.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Could Create a New Kind of Tax Record&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional crypto tax reporting is already complicated because investors may need to track purchases, sales, swaps, transfers, cost basis and transaction history across different platforms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Autonomous agents could make the recordkeeping problem significantly harder.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An agent might:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;swap one token for another;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;move assets between wallets;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;interact with decentralized finance protocols;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;execute trades based on predefined conditions;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;automatically rebalance a portfolio; or&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;perform multiple transactions as part of one larger strategy.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Every action may need to be reconstructed later to determine what actually happened and what the relevant tax consequences are.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one reason AI-driven finance may eventually require much better transaction-level accounting infrastructure rather than simply better trading models.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The AI May Not Be the Taxpayer — But It Could Become Part of the Evidence&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is an important distinction between &lt;strong&gt;who owes the tax&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;what evidence proves what happened&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI agent could potentially generate trading instructions, transaction logs, wallet activity, timestamps and records showing why a particular trade was executed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That information could become important when reconstructing a taxpayer's activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In a future audit, the question might not only be “What did the wallet do?”&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It could also be:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;“Who gave the agent authority, what rules was it following, what assets did it control, and who benefited from the resulting transactions?”&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;India Is Starting to Face the Same Agent-Responsibility Question&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;India's emerging agentic-payment framework shows why these questions are moving beyond cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Reuters reported on September 10, 2026 that India's National Payments Corporation of India is developing a registry to verify and monitor AI agents conducting transactions on UPI. The system is intended to authenticate agents, with potential future use cases involving more complex purchases and investment-related actions. Reuters also reported that liability for wrong or unauthorized payments remains an issue requiring further regulatory treatment. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The significance goes beyond UPI.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If regulators need to identify which AI agent initiated a transaction, they also need to know who authorized that agent and who ultimately stands behind its actions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto could face the same basic question as autonomous wallets become more common.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens When the AI Is Run by a Company?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Now consider a different scenario.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A company creates an AI trading system, funds a wallet with $5 million and allows the software to trade cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI generates $20 million in gains.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Here, the ownership structure becomes central.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the company owns the assets and the trading activity is carried out as part of its business, the tax analysis would generally start with the company rather than treating the AI as an independent taxpayer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But if the structure involves a fund, partnership, trust, DAO, investment vehicle or another legal arrangement, the answer may be different.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why there is no single global answer to the headline question.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could AI Ever Become a Taxpayer?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That would require something much bigger than giving an AI a wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It would require legal systems to recognize some form of independent legal status for an artificial system and establish rules for ownership, income, liability, enforcement and representation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Today's AI agents do not automatically acquire that status simply because they can act autonomously.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The legal debate is therefore moving in a different direction: how existing concepts such as ownership, agency, authorization and liability should apply when software can perform actions with increasingly little human intervention.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Real Problem Is Bigger Than Crypto&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto simply makes the issue easier to see.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchains allow software to directly interact with assets. There is no bank employee sitting between an autonomous agent and every transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates an unusually clean laboratory for autonomous finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the same question will eventually appear in other areas:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who pays when an AI-controlled company earns money?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who is responsible when an AI makes an investment decision?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who owns assets acquired by an autonomous agent?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who reports the income?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who answers the regulator's questions?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;And who is responsible when the agent makes a mistake?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These are not purely technical questions anymore.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;So, If AI Makes $10 Million in Crypto, Who Pays?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no universal one-line answer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is a useful starting rule:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The AI's ability to execute the trade does not, by itself, make the AI the taxpayer.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The tax analysis generally follows the person or legal entity that owns the assets, receives the economic benefit and is legally responsible for the relevant activity, subject to the rules of the applicable jurisdiction and the specific structure involved.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could mean an individual investor, a company, a fund or another legal structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The harder question will be determining exactly where the responsibility sits when an autonomous agent operates across wallets, platforms and jurisdictions with little or no human intervention.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI may eventually become one of the most powerful tools in crypto trading. It can analyze information, execute strategies and potentially manage transactions at a speed that humans cannot match.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But making money and owing tax are two different questions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If an AI makes millions trading crypto, the tax bill is unlikely to arrive addressed to “the robot.”&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, tax authorities will look toward the underlying ownership, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/pumpfun-app-temporarily-unavailable-on.html"&gt;transactions&lt;/a&gt;, economic benefit and legal structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And as autonomous agents become more capable, the most valuable financial skill may not be teaching an AI how to trade.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;It may be teaching the humans behind it how to prove exactly what the AI did.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Note: This article is for news and educational purposes only and is not tax, legal or investment advice. Crypto-tax treatment varies by jurisdiction and individual circumstances. Readers should consult a qualified tax professional for advice on their own situation.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
