    <title>CFTC Opens Three Previously Unreported Polymarket Insider-Trading Investigations Into Biden Pardons, Iran and Google</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj_nIwaIJtH7XxXZ_mtxisRQk8q_xyuE0mnYCNrInxr4bgzRGJ-8idNKz-ViMpH_rMSb80jFzdUJPUZyhSXLlBQkoBfajp0AUB-N4dd_RAzvNCc5Q80JZs7xm2jk5nUDbql5Qw55YjZO-4aOpDe1ivQRV_MN_6cn1gAfUNR7Y6l8HufbobMGgwFSLlIP_ZE/s1672/cftc-polymarket-insider-trading-investigations-biden-iran-google.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="CFTC investigations into suspected insider trading on Polymarket involving Biden pardons, Iran and Google" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj_nIwaIJtH7XxXZ_mtxisRQk8q_xyuE0mnYCNrInxr4bgzRGJ-8idNKz-ViMpH_rMSb80jFzdUJPUZyhSXLlBQkoBfajp0AUB-N4dd_RAzvNCc5Q80JZs7xm2jk5nUDbql5Qw55YjZO-4aOpDe1ivQRV_MN_6cn1gAfUNR7Y6l8HufbobMGgwFSLlIP_ZE/w640-h360/cftc-polymarket-insider-trading-investigations-biden-iran-google.webp.png" title="CFTC Polymarket Insider-Trading Investigations" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;September 12, 2026 —&lt;/strong&gt; The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) opened three previously unreported investigations into potential insider trading involving Polymarket prediction markets, according to government records obtained by &lt;em&gt;WIRED&lt;/em&gt; through a Freedom of Information Act request.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The investigations involve three sensitive areas: &lt;strong&gt;presidential pardon markets connected to former President Joe Biden, Polymarket contracts related to Iran, and Google’s 2025 Year in Search rankings.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The disclosures provide new insight into how U.S. regulators are examining trading activity on prediction markets, where users can take positions on political, geopolitical, corporate and other real-world events.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Importantly, the existence of an investigation does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; establish that a trader committed insider trading or that a particular transaction was illegal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;CFTC Investigated Polymarket Biden Pardon Markets&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to documents reviewed by &lt;em&gt;WIRED&lt;/em&gt;, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig approved an order in &lt;strong&gt;early May 2026&lt;/strong&gt; allowing the agency’s enforcement division to open a private investigation into potential insider trading involving Polymarket event contracts related to pardons issued by &lt;strong&gt;former President Joe Biden&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The investigation order did not identify the specific trades or individuals under suspicion. However, it came after reporting about a Polymarket trader who reportedly made more than &lt;strong&gt;$300,000&lt;/strong&gt; on pardon-related markets during the final days of the Biden administration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The trader correctly positioned on markets involving preemptive pardons for several prominent political figures, according to reporting cited by &lt;em&gt;WIRED&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The timing of the CFTC investigation attracted attention, although the publicly disclosed documents do not establish that the trader mentioned in earlier reporting was the specific target of the agency’s investigation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Iran-Related Polymarket Trades Also Drew CFTC Scrutiny&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the &lt;strong&gt;end of May 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, Selig approved another investigation concerning &lt;strong&gt;Iran event contracts&lt;/strong&gt; traded on Polymarket.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The investigation documents do not provide detailed information about the individual accounts or transactions under examination. According to &lt;em&gt;WIRED&lt;/em&gt;, the investigation came about two weeks after a &lt;em&gt;60 Minutes&lt;/em&gt; report highlighted a network of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/p/about-coinainews_01626707051.html"&gt;Polymarket&lt;/a&gt; accounts that had reportedly made approximately &lt;strong&gt;$2.4 million&lt;/strong&gt; from Iran-related trades while recording a roughly &lt;strong&gt;98% win rate&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The unusually high reported performance raised questions about whether some traders could have possessed information that was not publicly available. However, profitability or a high win rate by itself does not prove insider trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Third Investigation Focused on Google’s 2025 Year in Search Markets&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The third previously unreported CFTC investigation was approved in &lt;strong&gt;July 2026&lt;/strong&gt; and focused on suspected insider trading involving Google-themed Polymarket contracts.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The contracts were tied to &lt;strong&gt;Google’s 2025 Year in Search rankings&lt;/strong&gt;. Google officially published its 2025 Year in Search results on &lt;strong&gt;December 4, 2025&lt;/strong&gt;, several months before the CFTC authorized its later investigation into additional individuals.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The July investigation is separate from the CFTC’s already-public enforcement case against former Google software engineer &lt;strong&gt;Michele Spagnuolo&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happened in the Michele Spagnuolo Case?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On &lt;strong&gt;May 27, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, the CFTC announced a complaint against Spagnuolo, alleging that he used sensitive, nonpublic information about Google’s official 2025 Year in Search results to trade on Polymarket.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to the CFTC, Spagnuolo traded at least &lt;strong&gt;23 Year in Search-related contracts&lt;/strong&gt; using a Polymarket account. The regulator alleges that he generated approximately &lt;strong&gt;$1.2 million in profits&lt;/strong&gt; from those trades.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The contracts included markets concerning categories such as the most searched people, actors, passings and television shows of 2025. CFTC court documents state that Polymarket began listing some of these contracts in October 2025, before Google publicly released its Year in Search results.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC is seeking restitution, disgorgement, civil monetary penalties, trading and registration bans, and a permanent injunction, according to its complaint.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Spagnuolo Also Faces Federal Criminal Charges&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Google case also has a criminal component.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On May 27, 2026, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York announced the unsealing of a criminal complaint against Spagnuolo. Prosecutors charged him with &lt;strong&gt;one count involving the Commodity Exchange Act, one count of wire fraud, and one count of money laundering&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Spagnuolo, a 36-year-old Italian citizen residing in Switzerland, was presented that day before U.S. Magistrate Judge Sarah Netburn in the Southern District of New York, according to the Justice Department.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Prosecutors allege that he used confidential Google &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ai-insider-trading-new-market-abuse.html"&gt;business information&lt;/a&gt; to make profitable Polymarket trades and subsequently took steps to conceal the source of the proceeds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Justice Department emphasized that the allegations in the criminal complaint should be treated as allegations unless and until proven in court.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does “Material Nonpublic Information” Mean?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Material nonpublic information&lt;/strong&gt; generally refers to information that is not available to the public and that a reasonable investor or trader could consider important when making a financial decision.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In prediction markets, such information could potentially include advance knowledge of a government decision, corporate announcement, confidential ranking or another event outcome that has not yet been made public.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The distinction matters because prediction markets are built around information. A trader who independently analyzes public information is fundamentally different from someone who allegedly uses confidential information obtained through an employer or official position.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the CFTC’s Polymarket Investigations Matter&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The three investigations cover very different categories of information: &lt;strong&gt;presidential decisions, geopolitical events and corporate search data&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Together, they highlight a growing regulatory question surrounding prediction markets: &lt;strong&gt;where should regulators draw the line between legitimate information-based trading and trading based on confidential information?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The issue has become increasingly important as prediction markets have expanded beyond elections into areas such as geopolitics, corporate events, economic data and other real-world outcomes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC has already brought multiple enforcement actions involving alleged misuse of nonpublic information on prediction markets, demonstrating that the agency views market integrity as a significant regulatory issue.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Another CFTC Prediction-Market Insider-Trading Case: Gabriel Perez&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest developments also follow a separate CFTC case involving &lt;strong&gt;Gabriel Perez&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On &lt;strong&gt;August 28, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, the CFTC announced that Perez agreed to pay a total of &lt;strong&gt;$172,539.02&lt;/strong&gt; in disgorgement and civil monetary penalties after the agency found that he misappropriated material, nonpublic information obtained through his federal government employment to trade presidential mention-market contracts.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to the CFTC, Perez worked as a White House teleprompter operator and had access to presidential speeches before they were delivered. The agency said he used that information to trade prediction-market contracts concerning words or phrases the President might use during speeches.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Under the order, Perez must disgorge &lt;strong&gt;$107,539.02&lt;/strong&gt;, pay a &lt;strong&gt;$65,000 civil monetary penalty&lt;/strong&gt;, cease and desist from further violations and comply with a &lt;strong&gt;three-year trading ban&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Has Polymarket Said?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Polymarket has not commented on the specific investigations. However, according to &lt;em&gt;WIRED&lt;/em&gt;, Olivia Chalos, the company’s deputy chief legal officer, said Polymarket does not comment on specific investigations but regularly refers matters to law enforcement and supports ongoing investigations as part of its commitment to protecting market integrity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction is important because the newly disclosed CFTC investigations concern suspected trading activity. They do not, by themselves, establish that Polymarket or any individual trader violated the law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does an Investigation Mean the Traders Broke the Law?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An investigation is a regulatory process used to determine whether potential violations occurred. It is not a final finding of liability or criminal guilt.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the Biden pardon and Iran-related investigations, the publicly disclosed documents provide limited information about the specific traders or transactions being examined.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Google matter is further along because the CFTC and federal prosecutors have already brought cases against Spagnuolo. Even there, however, the criminal allegations remain subject to the judicial process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC investigations could eventually result in enforcement actions if the agency determines that specific traders violated the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-ai-own-its-own-crypto-wallet-law.html"&gt;Commodity Exchange Act&lt;/a&gt; or related regulations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Additional information could also emerge about the accounts, transactions and information allegedly available to traders before the relevant events became public.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the available records establish that the CFTC authorized investigations into Polymarket activity involving &lt;strong&gt;Biden pardons, Iran event contracts and Google’s 2025 Year in Search markets&lt;/strong&gt;. They do not establish that every trader involved in those markets engaged in illegal insider trading.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href="/2026/08/cftc-warns-prediction-markets-moneyline-odds.html"&gt;CFTC Warns Prediction Markets Against American-Style Moneyline Odds&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC has opened at least three previously undisclosed investigations into potential insider trading involving Polymarket markets, according to records obtained by &lt;em&gt;WIRED&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The investigations cover &lt;strong&gt;former President Joe Biden’s pardon markets, Iran-related event contracts and Google’s 2025 Year in Search markets&lt;/strong&gt;. The Biden investigation was authorized in May 2026, the Iran investigation followed later that month, and the Google-related investigation was approved in July 2026.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The disclosures come as U.S. regulators increasingly scrutinize prediction markets for possible fraud, manipulation and misuse of confidential information.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Polymarket and the wider prediction-market industry, these investigations could become an important test of how traditional market-integrity rules apply to event contracts tied to political, geopolitical and corporate developments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Did the CFTC investigate Polymarket for insider trading?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes. Records obtained by &lt;em&gt;WIRED&lt;/em&gt; show that the CFTC authorized at least three previously unreported investigations involving Polymarket markets tied to Biden pardons, Iran-related events and Google’s 2025 Year in Search rankings.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Was insider trading proven in all three Polymarket investigations?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. The disclosed investigations concern potential or suspected insider trading. Their existence does not establish that a specific trader violated the law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;When did the CFTC investigate the Biden pardon markets?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The CFTC authorized the Biden pardon investigation in early May 2026, according to documents obtained by &lt;em&gt;WIRED&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;When did the CFTC investigate Iran-related Polymarket trades?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The CFTC authorized an investigation into Iran event contracts at the end of May 2026, according to the documents reviewed by &lt;em&gt;WIRED&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What was the Google Polymarket investigation about?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The July 2026 investigation focused on additional individuals who may have engaged in insider trading involving Polymarket contracts tied to Google’s 2025 Year in Search rankings.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What happened to Michele Spagnuolo?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Federal prosecutors charged Spagnuolo with alleged violations involving the Commodity Exchange Act, wire fraud and money laundering. The Justice Department says he was presented before a federal magistrate judge on May 27, 2026. The allegations have not been established as criminal convictions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How much did Spagnuolo allegedly make?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The CFTC alleges that Spagnuolo generated approximately $1.2 million in profits from Polymarket trades based on confidential Google information.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What did Polymarket say?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Polymarket’s deputy chief legal officer told &lt;em&gt;WIRED&lt;/em&gt; that the company does not comment on specific investigations but regularly refers matters to law enforcement and supports ongoing investigations.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Solana Options Expiry: Why SOL Is Suddenly in Focus After Friday’s Settlement</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiXTCTKtmLfqHM4FWqQEjtESxz25KUrTlIaMEQwzLw17S_Aw1NwLiOeRU1LMBR_xTOXjEt96351-W5mAr-2jSTOODE1X0FBLEOO035bR01wXgWnRL8fGOKDNSYzoijA4fh2qe-PLpY6IaShwrungUUxakUo6KtYME5nVhp03wcpuDE7Tx3LfggropQ5LNVT/s1672/solana-options-expiry-sol-september-2026.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Solana options expiry puts SOL in focus as traders watch key $90, $105 and $125 strike levels" border="0" data-original-height="940" data-original-width="1672" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiXTCTKtmLfqHM4FWqQEjtESxz25KUrTlIaMEQwzLw17S_Aw1NwLiOeRU1LMBR_xTOXjEt96351-W5mAr-2jSTOODE1X0FBLEOO035bR01wXgWnRL8fGOKDNSYzoijA4fh2qe-PLpY6IaShwrungUUxakUo6KtYME5nVhp03wcpuDE7Tx3LfggropQ5LNVT/s1600/solana-options-expiry-sol-september-2026.webp.png" title="Solana Options Expiry and SOL Market Focus" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Solana is attracting fresh attention across crypto markets as a large portion of its options open interest reached expiry on Friday, putting SOL’s derivatives market under the spotlight alongside much larger Bitcoin and Ethereum options settlements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;About &lt;strong&gt;65% of Solana options open interest on Deribit&lt;/strong&gt; was tied to the September 25 expiry, according to market data reported ahead of the event. Key strike areas included &lt;strong&gt;$90, $105 and $125&lt;/strong&gt;, while SOL was trading around &lt;strong&gt;$116&lt;/strong&gt; during Friday’s session.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Deribit settlement took place at &lt;strong&gt;08:00 UTC&lt;/strong&gt;. The scheduled expiry has therefore already passed, and attention is now shifting toward what happens to SOL after those positions are settled or rolled into later expiries.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The options event does not automatically signal that SOL should move higher or lower. Instead, it gives traders another reason to monitor liquidity, hedging activity, futures positioning, funding rates, spot volume and volatility.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Solana Options Put SOL in Focus&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The immediate reason is the size of the expiring open interest relative to the SOL options market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Approximately 65% of Deribit’s Solana options open interest was scheduled to expire on September 25. The figure is significant because the event removes or settles a large amount of existing derivatives exposure at one time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Options can also influence short-term market conditions through dealer hedging. Market makers that provide liquidity to options traders may hedge their exposure through the underlying asset or related derivatives. As SOL moves closer to or farther from important strikes, those hedges can change.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, open interest should not be interpreted as a straightforward bullish or bearish bet. A single options position can be part of a spread, hedge or market-making strategy. The open-interest figure therefore tells traders where contracts are concentrated, not necessarily what every market participant expects SOL to do next.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction becomes particularly important with Solana because its options market remains considerably smaller and less liquid than the major &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitcoins-156-billion-options-expiry.html"&gt;Bitcoin &lt;/a&gt;and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/what-happens-when-ai-agent-runs-out-of.html"&gt;Ethereum &lt;/a&gt;options markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Three SOL Strike Levels Traders Are Watching&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most closely watched strike areas surrounding Friday’s expiry were &lt;strong&gt;$90, $105 and $125&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;$125&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Upside call area&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Above the recent $115–$118 &lt;br /&gt;trading range&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With SOL trading around $116, the $105 strike was relatively close to the underlying market, while $125 represented an upside area that was still above recent spot prices.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These levels should not be treated as guaranteed support, resistance or price targets. They are reference points showing where options positioning was concentrated around the expiry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;SOL Was Around $116 as the Expiry Arrived&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Solana entered the expiry after a strong September move.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Market data showed SOL trading around &lt;strong&gt;$116&lt;/strong&gt; on September 25, with the session reaching roughly $118.4. On September 24, SOL traded between approximately $112.7 and $117.7, according to historical market data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That recent price action is important because it puts SOL substantially above the $105 strike while still below the $125 call area that attracted attention in the options market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader trend has also been supported by increasing institutional interest in U.S. spot Solana ETFs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Solana ETF Flows Add a Separate Demand Signal&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Options positioning is only one part of the current SOL story.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;U.S. spot Solana ETFs recorded net inflows for &lt;strong&gt;12 consecutive weeks&lt;/strong&gt; through the week ending September 18, according to Solana Compass. The streak had brought cumulative net inflows to more than &lt;strong&gt;$1.4 billion&lt;/strong&gt;, while the week ending September 18 alone recorded approximately &lt;strong&gt;$60.7 million&lt;/strong&gt; of net inflows.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That data provides a different market signal from derivatives positioning. ETF flows measure capital moving into regulated spot investment products, while options open interest reflects outstanding derivatives contracts.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The two signals should therefore not be treated as interchangeable. But together they show why SOL has remained on the radar of both derivatives traders and investors seeking regulated exposure to the asset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The institutional-flow picture is particularly notable because Solana’s ETF market is much smaller than Bitcoin’s. Even relatively modest dollar flows can therefore represent meaningful changes in the size of the Solana &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/what-are-tokenized-bank-deposits-how.html"&gt;ETF asset&lt;/a&gt; base.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Friday’s Options Expiry Changes&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The main effect of the expiry is that a significant amount of existing derivatives exposure has now reached settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traders can close positions before expiry, allow contracts to settle or roll exposure into later-dated contracts. Market makers can also adjust their hedges as the contracts disappear from the active expiry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This can change liquidity and volatility around the event, but the effect is not necessarily permanent.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For SOL, the impact should also be viewed in the context of its smaller options market. Price discovery continues to occur across futures and perpetual markets on other exchanges, meaning a large move in SOL cannot automatically be attributed to the Deribit expiry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Post-expiry trading conditions may therefore be more informative than the expiry itself. If SOL moves sharply, traders will need to examine spot volume, futures open interest, funding and broader crypto-market conditions before deciding what drove the move.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin and Ethereum Expiries Make Friday More Important&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Solana’s options expiry occurred alongside much larger Bitcoin and Ethereum derivatives settlements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Market reports put the Bitcoin options expiry at roughly &lt;strong&gt;$15.9 billion&lt;/strong&gt; and Ethereum at about &lt;strong&gt;$2.1 billion&lt;/strong&gt;. Both were scheduled around the same major quarterly settlement window.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a broader market context for SOL.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin remains the largest source of liquidity and risk direction across the crypto market. A significant move in BTC following its much larger derivatives settlement can affect altcoins, including Solana.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Conversely, if Bitcoin remains relatively stable, SOL-specific factors such as ETF flows, network developments and its own derivatives positioning can become more visible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why traders are watching SOL together with BTC and ETH rather than treating Friday’s Solana expiry as an isolated event.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Alpenglow Remains a Major Upcoming Solana Catalyst&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Another reason SOL remains in focus is Solana’s planned &lt;strong&gt;Alpenglow consensus upgrade&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is an important timing clarification here. Earlier reports described &lt;strong&gt;September 28&lt;/strong&gt; as a possible Alpenglow-related date, but it should not be presented as a confirmed Alpenglow mainnet activation date. Solana Compass reported that the September 28 entry in Anza’s Agave v4.3 schedule refers to the resumption of feature activation on mainnet-beta, rather than a confirmed Alpenglow activation date.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As a result, the exact mainnet activation date should be treated as unconfirmed until Solana developers announce it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The upgrade remains an important development for the network because Alpenglow is designed to change Solana’s consensus architecture and improve finality performance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For SOL traders, the distinction matters. A protocol upgrade can become an important market narrative before activation, but the existence of a development milestone does not provide a guaranteed short-term price signal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Solana’s Network Performance Is Also Evolving&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Alpenglow is part of a broader effort to improve Solana’s consensus and network performance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Agave v4.3 release carrying Alpenglow is designed to introduce major consensus changes, including improvements to finality and fault tolerance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Solana has also been making changes to network timing and performance. Recent reporting around the network’s slot-time adjustment highlighted a move toward faster block processing, although a shorter slot does not automatically translate into a proportional increase in total network capacity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For investors, the important distinction is between technical development and immediate token-price impact. A protocol upgrade can improve the network’s capabilities without producing an immediate or predictable change in SOL’s market price.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Traders Should Watch After the Expiry&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;1. Spot Trading Volume&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A major SOL price move accompanied by stronger spot volume provides more information than a move occurring in thin trading conditions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;2. Futures Open Interest&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Futures open interest can show whether traders are adding new leveraged positions or reducing existing exposure after the options settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;3. Funding Rates&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Perpetual futures funding rates provide another indication of positioning. Extremely one-sided funding can signal crowded leverage, although funding by itself does not predict the next price move.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;4. Options Volatility&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;After the September expiry, traders can compare implied volatility across later SOL expiries. Changes in volatility pricing can show whether the market is assigning more or less risk to future price swings.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;5. ETF Flows&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Continued inflows into U.S. spot Solana ETFs would represent an additional demand signal. A reversal into sustained outflows would provide a different indication and should be assessed separately from derivatives data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;6. Bitcoin’s Post-Expiry Behavior&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because Bitcoin’s options settlement was substantially larger than Solana’s, BTC’s reaction can influence overall crypto-market liquidity and risk appetite during the next trading sessions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the SOL Options Expiry Means Now&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Friday’s expiry has removed a significant portion of the SOL options positions that had been concentrated around the $90, $105 and $125 strikes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the expiry itself does not provide a simple directional signal for Solana.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With SOL around $116, the market entered settlement between the $105 and $125 areas that drew the most attention. The more important question now is how traders reposition for later expiries and whether spot and futures markets confirm any move that follows.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, the options event is only one part of the broader SOL story. The 12-week streak of U.S. spot Solana ETF inflows provides a separate institutional-flow signal, while the continuing Alpenglow development gives the network another long-term catalyst.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That combination explains why Solana remains in focus even after the Friday settlement has passed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Solana’s September 25 options expiry was notable because roughly &lt;strong&gt;65% of Deribit’s SOL options open interest&lt;/strong&gt; was tied to the event, with key strike areas around &lt;strong&gt;$90, $105 and $125&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The scheduled &lt;strong&gt;08:00 UTC&lt;/strong&gt; settlement has now passed, shifting attention from the expiry itself to the market’s post-settlement positioning.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SOL was trading around $116 during Friday’s session, while U.S. spot Solana ETFs had recorded 12 consecutive weeks of net inflows and more than $1.4 billion in cumulative inflows through the latest reported period.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Meanwhile, Alpenglow remains an important upcoming Solana development, but its exact mainnet activation date has not been confirmed. The September 28 date should not be described as a confirmed Alpenglow activation date.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For traders and investors, the next useful signals are spot volume, futures open interest, funding rates, options volatility, ETF flows and Bitcoin’s reaction to the broader derivatives settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The options expiry is a market event, not a prediction.&lt;/strong&gt; What happens next will depend on liquidity, positioning, new demand and broader crypto-market conditions.&lt;/p&gt;

This alarming breach has sparked discussions about blockchain security, emphasizing the need for robust protective measures in decentralized finance (DeFi).&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;What Led to the Exploit?&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The NEAR Intents team attributed the loss to a bug within their Omni deposit and withdrawal infrastructure, which interacted poorly with its smart contracts. &lt;strong&gt;The vulnerability was exploited, resulting in the loss of more than $3.8 million.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Swift Action Taken&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;In light of the incident, NEAR Intents acted quickly to patch the vulnerability. They have also pledged &lt;strong&gt;full reimbursement&lt;/strong&gt; to affected users, demonstrating their commitment to user trust and security. This proactive response is crucial for maintaining confidence in their &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/morgan-stanley-launches-digital-asset.html"&gt;platform &lt;/a&gt;and the broader DeFi ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Understanding the Technical Flaw&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The bug highlights a common challenge faced by &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/10/30-crypto-ai-crypto-startups-2026.html"&gt;blockchain &lt;/a&gt;developers: ensuring the seamless interaction between various components of decentralized applications (dApps). As these systems become increasingly complex, the risk of vulnerabilities grows. This incident serves as a reminder that thorough testing and regular audits are essential for safeguarding user assets.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h3&gt;The Broader Impact on Blockchain Security&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The incident highlights the security challenges facing blockchain and DeFi infrastructure as cross-chain systems become increasingly complex.&lt;/strong&gt; As the market matures, it is imperative for developers to prioritize security measures, including:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Regular Security Audits:&lt;/strong&gt; Conducting frequent audits can help identify vulnerabilities before they are exploited.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Community Engagement:&lt;/strong&gt; Keeping the community informed about potential risks fosters transparency and trust.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;User Education:&lt;/strong&gt; Empowering users with knowledge about security best practices can mitigate risks.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Conclusion: Learning from the Incident&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p&gt;The NEAR Intents security breach underscores the critical importance of vigilance in the blockchain sector. While the team has taken commendable steps to rectify the situation, it serves as a cautionary tale for all participants in the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/treasury-just-announced-6-billion.html"&gt;DeFi &lt;/a&gt;space. Users must remain cautious and informed, while developers should continue to innovate with a strong focus on security.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;As we move forward, learning from incidents like this will be essential for building a more secure and resilient blockchain environment. By prioritizing security, the industry can protect user assets and foster greater confidence in decentralized technologies.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;hr /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Key Takeaways:&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;NEAR Intents experienced a $3.8 million exploit due to a bug in its system.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;The team has patched the vulnerability and pledged full reimbursement.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p&gt;Ongoing vigilance and security measures are essential in the evolving blockchain landscape.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;</content>

    <content type='html'>&lt;h2 style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhuuEKwq3ghCPujI_sJ-X3MG9Pljn0YaYw0X8wpAAUtrnN9zWL7lwl1z1lFDpJCEvYD9Gppfm47VL0Cu6ZF3FGGur8BtuTD-CyofqcRjNzbPUV9vxaxCSbGx1aQAifYct-e4SxzQpA7fT_krBEweucqON-JcOMMVLhE3ShISo9IsKhsiL9mmEtDbjbF9Gq8/s1536/11.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="HTX Rotates On-Chain Wallets Following UK Sanctions" border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="213" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhuuEKwq3ghCPujI_sJ-X3MG9Pljn0YaYw0X8wpAAUtrnN9zWL7lwl1z1lFDpJCEvYD9Gppfm47VL0Cu6ZF3FGGur8BtuTD-CyofqcRjNzbPUV9vxaxCSbGx1aQAifYct-e4SxzQpA7fT_krBEweucqON-JcOMMVLhE3ShISo9IsKhsiL9mmEtDbjbF9Gq8/w320-h213/11.png" title="HTX Rotates On-Chain Wallets Following UK Sanctions" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;h2 style="text-align: left;"&gt;Justin Sun's HTX Adapts with On-Chain Wallet Rotation &lt;br /&gt;Amid Sanctions&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;In a strategic move to navigate the complexities of international regulations, Justin Sun's cryptocurrency exchange, HTX, has implemented a rotation of its on-chain wallets across various blockchains. This decision comes in light of recent sanctions imposed by the UK government on the platform. According to TRM Labs, this wallet rotation is part of HTX's efforts to maintain operational integrity and continue serving its users despite regulatory challenges.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;Overview of HTX and Its Significance in Crypto Market&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;HTX, formerly known as Huobi Global, is a prominent player in the cryptocurrency exchange landscape. Founded by Justin Sun, a well-known figure in the crypto world for his role as the founder of Tron and his extensive involvement with blockchain technology, HTX has become synonymous with innovative trading solutions and user engagement strategies. As one of the largest exchanges by trading volume globally, it offers various services such as spot trading, futures contracts, and staking options that appeal to both retail and institutional investors.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;The significance of HTX extends beyond mere numbers; it represents a pivotal point for many traders who rely on its liquidity and diverse asset offerings. However, like many crypto exchanges operating at scale, it faces increasing scrutiny from regulators worldwide.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 style="text-align: left;"&gt;'Rotating' Mechanism: How Hot Wallets Work Across Blockchains&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;Hot wallets are digital wallets connected to the internet that facilitate quick transactions but are more susceptible to security breaches than cold storage alternatives. The rotating mechanism involves periodically changing these hot wallets across different blockchains to mitigate risks associated with potential hacks or regulatory actions.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;By implementing this strategy during turbulent times marked by sanctions from authorities like those in the UK, HTX seeks not only to protect user funds but also ensure compliance with evolving legal frameworks governing cryptocurrencies. This proactive approach allows them flexibility while maintaining operational continuity.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 style="text-align: left;"&gt;(TRM Labs) Analysis of the Impact of UK Sanctions on Crypto Exchanges&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;TRM Labs has conducted an analysis detailing how sanctions affect cryptocurrency exchanges like HTX. The report emphasizes that such measures can significantly hinder an exchange’s ability to process transactions smoothly due to increased scrutiny over financial flows.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;For instance,&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;when an exchange is sanctioned by major economies like the UK,&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;it may face restrictions on accessing traditional financial networks or banking services necessary for smooth operations.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;This could lead not just to liquidity issues but also affect user trust if they perceive their assets are at risk due directly or indirectly from regulatory pressures.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;The implications extend beyond immediate operational concerns; border-box; color: #f7931a; font-size: 1rem; margin: 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;"&gt;'How can other exchanges respond to similar regulatory pressures?'&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p style="background: 0px 0px; border: 0px; box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;"&gt;'Other exchanges can adopt proactive compliance strategies, enhance security measures like wallet rotation, and improve communication with regulators.'&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="background: rgb(17, 24, 39); border-radius: 8px; border: 0px; regulation?'&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;p style="background: 0px 0px; border: 0px; box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;"&gt;'The ongoing scrutiny suggests that future regulations will likely become stricter as governments seek greater oversight over cryptocurrency activities.'&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</content>

    <title>Banks Rotating Into Ethereum 3x Faster Than Bitcoin, 13F Data Shows</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgukZ-Wmb3Fna-FVQrg9TAefC_RVxHhVTK27amYhDSBIYHN1PzPKDRdH-g7WYVv4smESAGEAbcto8ak28c17IxiF9vx9C2s_MpVhEA3Ra2Zd6AKFHr-d9rKJ4EcddVc5HhpZ47qVqjuwETxivzlh9cZUWSNp6hR508fqxCH2W8EgY5Z8ftToJxZ5dYqE_Ci/s1672/banks-ethereum-exposure-3x-bitcoin-13f-data-2026.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgukZ-Wmb3Fna-FVQrg9TAefC_RVxHhVTK27amYhDSBIYHN1PzPKDRdH-g7WYVv4smESAGEAbcto8ak28c17IxiF9vx9C2s_MpVhEA3Ra2Zd6AKFHr-d9rKJ4EcddVc5HhpZ47qVqjuwETxivzlh9cZUWSNp6hR508fqxCH2W8EgY5Z8ftToJxZ5dYqE_Ci/s320/banks-ethereum-exposure-3x-bitcoin-13f-data-2026.jpg.png" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: large;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt; |&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;When Wall Street's largest banks filed their quarterly 13F forms with the SEC, a clear pattern emerged: major financial institutions appear to be building Ethereum exposure significantly faster than Bitcoin, based on their reported positions.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;According to DWF Labs' analysis of Q2 2026 13F filings, banks grew their Ethereum exposure at a rate &lt;strong&gt;3x faster&lt;/strong&gt; than Bitcoin during the second quarter.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Numbers That Tell the Story&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The data from individual bank filings is striking:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; margin: 24px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
  &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0px; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; line-height: 1.5; min-width: 650px; text-align: left; width: 100%;"&gt;

        &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(216, 216, 216); font-weight: 700; padding: 14px 16px; white-space: nowrap;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;BTC Exposure Growth&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(216, 216, 216); font-weight: 700; padding: 14px 16px; white-space: nowrap;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;ETH Exposure Growth&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/th&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Bank of America:&lt;/strong&gt; Increased its ETHA position from approximately 67,500 shares to roughly 1.98 million shares—an increase of about &lt;strong&gt;29 times&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Morgan Stanley:&lt;/strong&gt; Grew its ETHA holdings by about 202% to 4.6 million shares.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;JPMorgan:&lt;/strong&gt; Increased its ETHA position by about 338% to nearly 1.17 million shares.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;New Entrants Signal Growing Institutional Interest&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Several banks made their first-ever &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/standard-chartered-analyst-sees-100k.html"&gt;crypto ETF&lt;/a&gt; disclosures in Q2:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Spain's Banco Santander:&lt;/strong&gt; Reported new positions of 129,615 IBIT shares ($4.31 million) and 297,947 ETHA shares ($3.54 million).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Italy's Intesa Sanpaolo:&lt;/strong&gt; Tripled its staked Ethereum ETF holdings to 349,600 shares while cutting its IBIT position by nearly 94%.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What's Actually Behind the Shift?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Several factors appear to be driving the rotation:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Staking yield:&lt;/strong&gt; Some Ethereum investment products can provide exposure to staking-related yield, an additional feature that spot &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/how-to-start-with-crypto-in-2026.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt; ETFs generally do not provide.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Institutional decoupling:&lt;/strong&gt; ETF fund flows and institutional behavior are diverging—institutions appear to be buying even as retail flows head the other direction.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Q3 reversal:&lt;/strong&gt; Data from SoSoValue shows Ethereum ETFs posted net inflows of approximately $365 million in July and $243 million so far in August, suggesting the trend may be continuing.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A Word of Caution&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;13F filings only show what was held on June 30 and don't distinguish between proprietary bank positions and holdings managed on behalf of clients. The data is also already about two months old.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That means the filings should not automatically be interpreted as evidence that a bank itself is making a directional proprietary bet on Ethereum. They provide a useful snapshot of reported holdings, but the underlying reason for each position can vary.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Even with that limitation, the Q2 data highlights a notable difference in the growth of reported Ethereum and Bitcoin exposure across the institutions covered by DWF Labs' analysis.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Q2 2026 13F filings point to a notable increase in reported Ethereum exposure among several major financial institutions. DWF Labs' analysis shows Ethereum exposure growing faster than Bitcoin across the banks it examined, with some individual ETF positions recording substantial increases.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The figures do not prove that every bank is making a proprietary decision to favor Ethereum over Bitcoin. However, they do show that Ethereum-related exposure is becoming a more visible part of institutional crypto portfolios.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;With early Q3 ETF-flow data also showing renewed interest in Ethereum, the institutional side of the market will be worth watching closely through the second half of 2026.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice. Cryptocurrency markets are volatile, and past performance does not guarantee future results. Reported 13F holdings may include positions managed on behalf of clients and do not necessarily represent proprietary investment decisions.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>If an AI Makes Millions in Crypto, Who Owns the Money?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEihv19NP48aApzYWoKdM-V4ZsZaZpRZRpKuUG9djNNA0W5WOMDItpudIFbpIDrW6gX07aHh1SwbcwGLf4ii-xaCO0ma7hvj0oOC8hDdRmWzCbCW69-yw4RftGidi-6FUm-2I9MXjy3OrCmFVqDZ_zGWH75KS1U9o-ln9s6P9Se8H94HzHePWmT-2GIpoxsJ/s1672/ai-agent-crypto-wallet-ownership-millions.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="If an AI Makes Millions in Crypto, Who Owns the Money?" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEihv19NP48aApzYWoKdM-V4ZsZaZpRZRpKuUG9djNNA0W5WOMDItpudIFbpIDrW6gX07aHh1SwbcwGLf4ii-xaCO0ma7hvj0oOC8hDdRmWzCbCW69-yw4RftGidi-6FUm-2I9MXjy3OrCmFVqDZ_zGWH75KS1U9o-ln9s6P9Se8H94HzHePWmT-2GIpoxsJ/w400-h225/ai-agent-crypto-wallet-ownership-millions.jpg.png" title="AI Makes Millions in Crypto — Who Owns the Money?" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&amp;nbsp;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Imagine giving an AI agent a simple instruction: find opportunities, make money, and pay for whatever services you need. Months later, you check the wallet. It contains millions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Then comes the uncomfortable question: &lt;strong&gt;who owns the money?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI that made the decisions? The developer who built it? The company that deployed it? Or the person who originally funded the wallet?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This question is becoming less theoretical as developers experiment with AI agents that can interact directly with blockchain networks. These systems can be designed to hold digital assets, make payments, execute transactions and interact with decentralized applications with limited human intervention.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is an important distinction that should not get lost in the hype: &lt;strong&gt;an AI agent controlling or operating a crypto wallet does not automatically make the AI the legal owner of the assets.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Wallet Can Be Controlled by Software. Ownership Is Different.&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blockchain does not ask whether a human is sitting behind every transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It verifies cryptographic authorization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If an AI agent has access to a private key, delegated signing authority or a smart-contract wallet, it can potentially receive tokens, send funds and interact with decentralized applications without a person approving every transaction individually.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is a technical capability. It is not, by itself, a legal determination of ownership.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ethereum proposal &lt;strong&gt;ERC-8196&lt;/strong&gt;, for example, describes an &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/justin-sun-says-tron-targets-quantum.html"&gt;AI-agent wallet&lt;/a&gt; architecture in which an agent can execute transactions according to policies established by an asset owner. The design therefore separates the agent performing an action from the party that owns or authorizes the assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction could become increasingly important as autonomous software begins handling larger amounts of money.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Agents Are Already Moving Toward Economic Activity&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The idea of giving software access to crypto wallets is no longer purely hypothetical.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;CoinDesk reported in February 2026 that developers were experimenting with crypto wallets for AI agents, allowing autonomous software to hold assets, make payments, trade tokens and interact with other agents. Electric Capital's Avichal Garg described the development as a new legal frontier because the technology is advancing faster than the rules surrounding autonomous economic activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The reason crypto is particularly suited to this experiment is straightforward: blockchain networks allow software to interact directly with financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An agent doesn't necessarily need a bank employee, payment processor or human operator to approve every action. If it has the appropriate authorization, it can interact with smart contracts and move assets according to the rules built around its wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates enormous possibilities—but also a difficult accountability problem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If the AI Turns $10,000 Into $5 Million?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Consider a simple hypothetical.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A company gives an autonomous trading agent $10,000. The agent searches decentralized markets, identifies opportunities and executes trades. Over time, the wallet grows to $5 million.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI made every trading decision.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI executed the transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No employee manually approved every trade.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Does the AI therefore own the $5 million?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No. Not simply because the AI generated the profits.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The actual ownership question would depend on the legal and contractual structure behind the system. Relevant factors could include who supplied the original capital, who authorized the agent, who controlled the wallet or smart contract, what agreement governed the activity and which jurisdiction's laws apply.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In other words, blockchain control and legal ownership are not necessarily the same thing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Developer Doesn't Automatically Own It Either&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is another misconception worth clearing up.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The person who develops an AI agent does not automatically become the owner of every asset that the software earns.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Imagine a company builds an autonomous trading system for a client. The developer creates the software, but the client supplies the capital and authorizes the agent to trade on the client's behalf.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In that scenario, the developer's role as the software creator does not automatically transfer ownership of the client's assets to the developer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The legal and contractual arrangements would matter.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes several questions particularly important:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who funded the wallet?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who controls the underlying keys or authorization mechanism?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who instructed the AI agent to act?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;What permissions were granted?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who receives the economic benefit?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Which legal entity, if any, is responsible for the activity?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Agent Controls Need to Be Built Into the System&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As autonomous financial agents become more capable, developers are increasingly looking at ways to keep them within defined boundaries rather than simply handing an AI unrestricted access to funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; margin: 20px 0px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Control&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Purpose&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Spending limits&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;Prevent unlimited fund movement.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Policy-based authorization&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;Allow only predefined, rule-based &lt;br /&gt;transactions.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Human approval&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;Require human sign-off for high-risk&lt;br /&gt;&amp;nbsp;or large transactions.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Audit trails&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;Record agent actions and the authorization&lt;br /&gt;&amp;nbsp;behind them.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Emergency controls&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;Pause or restrict an agent when it behaves&lt;br /&gt;&amp;nbsp;unexpectedly.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ERC-8196 is one example of this approach. Its proposed architecture uses cryptographic policies to constrain what an AI agent can execute on behalf of an asset owner.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If Nobody Is Watching?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The harder scenario begins when an AI agent continues operating for a long period without meaningful human supervision.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Imagine an agent that receives revenue, pays for services and reinvests its earnings automatically. Years later, the original developer is gone, the company has changed ownership or the people who deployed the system are no longer actively involved.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The blockchain can continue processing transactions without interruption.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But determining responsibility could become much harder.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The International Monetary Fund has highlighted questions around authorization, settlement, compliance and resilience as AI agents become more involved in financial activity. It has also pointed to security concerns when autonomous systems receive access to sensitive financial information or crypto-wallet credentials.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The technical system can keep running even when the human chain of responsibility becomes difficult to identify.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Crypto Is Building Infrastructure for Autonomous Agents&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The industry is also developing standards that could make autonomous agents easier to identify, verify and control.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;ERC-8004&lt;/strong&gt; proposes an on-chain framework for &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/kalshi-sells-112b-of-equity-to-71.html"&gt;AI-agent discovery&lt;/a&gt; and interaction across organizational boundaries.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;ERC-8126&lt;/strong&gt; focuses on verification of AI agents registered through the ERC-8004 framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;ERC-8196&lt;/strong&gt; focuses on AI-agent wallet execution and policy-based authorization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These proposals do not establish that AI systems are legal persons or independent owners of assets. Instead, they show how blockchain infrastructure is being adapted for a world where software may increasingly act on behalf of people and organizations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Biggest Risk May Be an AI Making the Wrong Decision&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ownership is only one part of the problem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Giving an AI access to money also means giving software the ability to make financial mistakes at machine speed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An agent could misunderstand an instruction, rely on manipulated information, interact with a malicious smart contract or execute a transaction that technically follows its rules while producing a result the human operator never intended.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Research examining Google's Agent Payments Protocol, or AP2, has also explored security risks around agent-driven payments, including situations in which manipulated context could affect whether an authorized action actually reflects the user's original intent.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That problem becomes particularly serious in crypto because confirmed blockchain transactions can be difficult or impossible to reverse.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could an AI Ever Legally Own Crypto?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where the technology gets ahead of the law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Developers can create increasingly sophisticated agents with identities, wallets, revenue streams and the ability to transact autonomously.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But technical autonomy does not automatically create legal personhood.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is currently no general rule that says an AI becomes a legal person simply because it can make decisions or control digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The more realistic near-term model is therefore an &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/japan-eyes-blockchain-for-real-time.html"&gt;AI acting&lt;/a&gt; on behalf of a &lt;strong&gt;human, company, DAO or another legally recognized structure&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could change in the future if lawmakers create new legal frameworks for autonomous software. But that remains a future possibility, not an established rule that AI agents already possess independent property rights.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Three Possible Models for the Future&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; margin: 20px 0px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Model&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;How It Could Work&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI as a tool&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;A human or company owns the assets while&lt;br /&gt;the AI performs authorized actions.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI inside a legal structure&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;A company, foundation, trust, DAO or other&lt;br /&gt;recognized structure owns assets while AI &lt;br /&gt;manages defined activities.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI legal personhood&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;A future legal framework could theoretically&lt;br /&gt;recognize autonomous software as an &lt;br /&gt;independent legal actor, but this is not the&lt;br /&gt;current default.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Real Question Is Who Stands Behind the Wallet&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As AI agents become more capable, the question may eventually stop being whether software can make money.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That part is increasingly possible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The harder question is what happens after the money is made.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blockchain can show which wallet received the funds. It can show which address sent them and which smart contracts were involved. What it does not automatically establish is the legal relationship between that wallet, the AI agent and the people or organizations behind the system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That gap between &lt;strong&gt;on-chain control and legal ownership&lt;/strong&gt; could become one of the defining issues of the emerging agent economy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI agents are moving from systems that simply recommend actions toward software that can potentially execute transactions, make payments and interact with blockchain applications on its own.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not mean an AI automatically owns whatever it earns.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the more important questions are practical: &lt;strong&gt;who funded the wallet, who authorized the agent, who controls its permissions, who receives the economic benefit and which laws apply?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those questions will become even more important if autonomous agents start earning, spending, trading and negotiating with one another at scale.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The day an AI makes its first million may therefore not be the day machines become legal owners of wealth.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;It may be the day the legal system has to decide exactly who was standing behind the wallet — and whether the answer still includes a human.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and is not legal, financial or investment advice. Laws governing AI agents, digital assets, custody and automated transactions vary by jurisdiction and continue to evolve. This article distinguishes current technology from possible future legal structures and does not claim that AI systems currently have independent legal ownership of crypto assets.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
