    <title>The Most Underrated Crypto Projects Right Now, According to the Experts</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiI2uiLlIxL3wXvTyaGNs7vtp2oZ4SVnNEAXswK2j82lLJFlmPigpM8Eh6If12GkNS_IJBXfSeXq-zparMynwhVo9yWtWcZcKePWhogHe_tUYutyhmbKWenufeFyZdkY5zmcoFYfX25-ViouGb67jGnvIOrMW1MCZSTl5MJTCpyO0g36_x18XjS4__vJnXU/s1672/Neon%20Finance%20Network%20Hub.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Most underrated crypto projects Hyperliquid Aave Solana Chainlink Zcash expert analysis 2026" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiI2uiLlIxL3wXvTyaGNs7vtp2oZ4SVnNEAXswK2j82lLJFlmPigpM8Eh6If12GkNS_IJBXfSeXq-zparMynwhVo9yWtWcZcKePWhogHe_tUYutyhmbKWenufeFyZdkY5zmcoFYfX25-ViouGb67jGnvIOrMW1MCZSTl5MJTCpyO0g36_x18XjS4__vJnXU/w320-h180/Neon%20Finance%20Network%20Hub.png" title="Experts highlight Hyperliquid Aave Solana Chainlink and Zcash as potentially undervalued crypto projects" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aug 14, 2026&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;– The crypto market has been stuck
in a rut. Bitcoin has been range-bound, altcoins have bled, and the Fear &amp;amp;
Greed Index is hovering near "Fear" levels.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But if you look past the price charts, something interesting
is happening. Some of the smartest money in the industry – Bitwise, Grayscale,
and top executives – are quietly accumulating projects they believe are trading
at a fraction of their true value.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Here's what the experts are eyeing right now.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Hyperliquid (HYPE): The Super-App No One Sees&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan recently called &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bitcoin-shrugs-off-inflation-data-as.html"&gt;Hyperliquid&lt;/a&gt;
"one of the most undervalued assets in the crypto market today"&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The argument:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Investors are making a
"category error." They value Hyperliquid as just another perpetual
futures exchange. But Hougan argues it is actually a "global financial
super-app" that competes with Robinhood and CME – not just other DeFi
protocols.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The numbers:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Hyperliquid generates between&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$800
million and $1 billion annually&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in revenue. Its market cap sits
between $10 billion and $11 billion, giving it a price-to-revenue ratio of
10-14x. Compare that to Robinhood (37x earnings) or CME (24x) – neither grows
at Hyperliquid's pace&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Key detail:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Nearly half of Hyperliquid's volume
already comes from non-crypto assets – including S&amp;amp;P 500 futures, pre-IPO
stocks, and commodities. The platform processed $170 billion in volume last
month alone. In June 2026, Hyperliquid surpassed $1 billion in cumulative
revenue&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The protocol directs approximately 99% of eligible revenue
toward open-market HYPE purchases through its assistance fund. Since its
launch, Hyperliquid has bought and permanently removed over&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$1.3
billion worth of HYPE&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;from circulation, creating a direct link between
network activity and token-holder value&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Grayscale also named Hyperliquid as one of the most
undervalued DeFi assets, alongside Aave and Uniswap.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aave (AAVE): The Lending Giant Trading at a Discount&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Grayscale Research believes Aave is one of the strongest
value opportunities in the current market environment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The numbers:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Grayscale estimates Aave could
generate approximately **$60 million in net income in 2026**. Based on
traditional fintech valuation multiples, the firm believes AAVE's current fair
value ranges from **$80 to $100** per token – above its recent trading level
around $73. Under a more optimistic scenario driven by regulatory clarity, they
suggest AAVE could reach approximately&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$175&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;over the next
year.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why it matters:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Aave remains the largest player
in on-chain credit markets, with approximately&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$57 billion in total
value locked (TVL)** and **$23 billion in active loans&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;as of January
2026&amp;nbsp;. The protocol holds more than 80% of stablecoin deposits on
Ethereum, with roughly $20 billion in stablecoin deposits and $13 billion in
borrowed funds&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Grayscale's valuation is based on discounted cash flow
analysis and price multiples against comparable financial companies – a
framework that treats Aave's protocol revenue like earnings at a traditional
bank.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Solana (SOL): Down 75% But Still a Developer Magnet&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Solana has been highlighted as one of the most undervalued
altcoins, despite being down roughly 75% from its all-time high.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The contrarian take:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Traders are distracted by
the price drop. But behind the scenes, fundamentals are improving. U.S.-listed
Solana funds now manage about&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$1 billion&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in assets, with every
month since the spot ETF launch seeing net inflows despite the price decline.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The activity surge:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Solana's Q2 2026 Token
Holder Report from Blockworks shows tokenized asset trading volume
reached&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$5.8 billion**, a 114% increase from Q1. Tokenized stocks
accounted for **$4.8 billion&lt;/b&gt;, or approximately 97% of total tokenized
equity trading volume&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The upgrade:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Alpenglow, Solana's largest network
upgrade, is expected to reduce transaction finality from 12.8 seconds to about
150 milliseconds once fully deployed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Chainlink (LINK): The Oracle No One Is Watching&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Chainlink has been highlighted as undervalued, trading more
than 80% from its peak even as its infrastructure expands across traditional
finance.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What's happening:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The network already enables
banks and financial institutions to connect with blockchain networks. Its
partners include SWIFT (which connects about 11,000 financial institutions),
UBS, and Euroclear.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Q1 2026 milestones:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Chainlink's
     &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/cypherpunk-technologies-boosts-zcash.html"&gt;Cross-Chain&lt;/a&gt; Interoperability Protocol (CCIP) processed&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$18 billion&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in
     cross-chain transaction value – up 78% quarterly&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Over
     **$700 million** in DeFi assets migrated to CCIP after a rival bridge
     exploit, with Solv Protocol shifting $700 million in tokenized Bitcoin
     from LayerZero to Chainlink's infrastructure&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Chainlink
     secured a U.S. patent for its CCIP protocol&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The catch:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Financial institutions can use
Chainlink's infrastructure without directly purchasing LINK tokens – which
could limit direct token upside. But as tokenized real-world assets grow,
oracle demand could explode.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Zcash (ZEC): Privacy as a Political Asset&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Barry Silbert, CEO of Digital Currency Group, recently
declared the start of a "privacy era" in cryptocurrency.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The thesis:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;As governments expand financial
surveillance, asset monitoring, and restrictions on capital movement, privacy
becomes increasingly valuable. Zcash offers private digital money while
allowing users to keep transactions transparent when desired.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Institutional support:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The SEC closed its
investigation into the Zcash Foundation with no enforcement action in January
2026. Grayscale reopened its Zcash Trust and filed for a spot ETF, while
Cypherpunk Technologies accumulated&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;323,394 ZEC&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;(about 1.92%
of circulating supply) at an average price of $341.83.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Revenue Revolution: What's Really Changing&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan argues that the crypto market is
shifting from narrative-driven speculation to fundamental analysis. "The
crypto market will grow around profitable projects," he said&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Key mechanism:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Projects like Hyperliquid,
Uniswap, Aave, and Morpho are using fees collected for token buybacks or token
burning – creating a stronger link between network usage and token value.
Hyperliquid has already removed $1.3 billion worth of HYPE tokens from
circulation through its buyback mechanism&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Hougan predicts that DeFi applications and Layer-1
blockchain networks will generate more revenue in the next 12 to 24 months. If
investors recognize this shift, some of these assets could double or more in
value&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The most underrated crypto projects right now share a common
theme: they generate real revenue, have growing user bases, and are trading at
a discount because the market hasn't caught up to their true potential.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Hyperliquid is being valued as a derivatives exchange when
it's really a super-app. Aave is being priced as a speculative DeFi token when
it's a revenue-generating lending giant. Solana is being dismissed as a fallen
star when it still dominates tokenized equity trading. Chainlink is quietly
building the infrastructure for institutional tokenization.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Sometimes the best opportunities are hiding in plain sight.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Russia’s Sberbank Plans to Accept Ether and USDT as Loan Collateral</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; line-height: 1.7;"&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhVtS89UhdgCi6xOMGZtwUGHKKRpMV021XcwIZ6J0E98Um9qi5-8Srao1mheLd5iRKEdA9-S6NBPkZEwiaLJAv08XBdgblj6hC4rMHHgjtR5BlYrnny3nx4WwjxJsSCd80E8bR0ptyjaO2z_WtVgV9Bsah22POgavYPwmbOOYW24daSOFGf0NtGmiNxxOBY/s1672/russia-sberbank-bitcoin-ethereum-usdt-loan-collateral-2026.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Sberbank plans to accept Bitcoin, Ethereum and USDT as loan collateral in Russia" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhVtS89UhdgCi6xOMGZtwUGHKKRpMV021XcwIZ6J0E98Um9qi5-8Srao1mheLd5iRKEdA9-S6NBPkZEwiaLJAv08XBdgblj6hC4rMHHgjtR5BlYrnny3nx4WwjxJsSCd80E8bR0ptyjaO2z_WtVgV9Bsah22POgavYPwmbOOYW24daSOFGf0NtGmiNxxOBY/w400-h225/russia-sberbank-bitcoin-ethereum-usdt-loan-collateral-2026.jpg.png" title="Sberbank Crypto Collateral Plan: Bitcoin, Ethereum and USDT" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;Russia’s biggest bank is preparing for a significant shift in how digital assets could be used within the country’s financial system.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Sberbank plans to accept Ether (ETH) and Tether’s USDT as loan collateral alongside Bitcoin&lt;/strong&gt; once the relevant digital assets receive approval for public trading under Russia’s evolving cryptocurrency rules, according to a recent report shared by CoinMarketCap.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The announcement does not mean that Russian retail customers can immediately walk into a Sberbank branch and use any cryptocurrency as collateral. The proposed system remains dependent on regulatory approval and the rules governing which digital assets can be publicly traded and who can access them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important. Russia is moving toward a more controlled approach to cryptocurrency, with regulators seeking to define how digital assets can interact with the traditional financial system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Sberbank’s Crypto-Collateral Plan&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sberbank’s proposed approach would allow selected cryptocurrencies to play a role in lending transactions. Bitcoin would potentially be joined by &lt;strong&gt;Ether and USDT&lt;/strong&gt; if the relevant assets receive permission for public trading under Russia’s new framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For borrowers, the attraction is relatively simple: crypto could potentially be pledged as collateral while the borrower obtains financing without immediately selling the underlying digital asset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the bank, however, the process is more complicated. &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/japan-fsa-seeks-tax-filing-exemption.html"&gt;Cryptocurrency&lt;/a&gt; prices can move rapidly, meaning lenders need strict collateral requirements, reliable price feeds and procedures for handling sudden market declines.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A crypto-backed loan therefore works on the same basic principle as other secured lending, but with an additional layer of market and regulatory risk.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Ether and USDT Matter&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin is already the most established cryptocurrency in discussions about institutional digital-asset collateral. Adding Ether would expand the range of major crypto assets potentially usable in lending.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;USDT is particularly interesting because it is designed as a dollar-linked stablecoin rather than a traditional volatile cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That gives USDT a different risk profile from &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/imf-warns-stablecoins-could-cut-payment.html"&gt;Bitcoin &lt;/a&gt;and Ether. However, stablecoins are not risk-free. Their use as collateral can involve questions around liquidity, regulation, issuer exposure and the stability of their market price.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proposed combination would therefore bring three very different digital assets into the same lending conversation:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/strong&gt; — a decentralized cryptocurrency and the largest digital asset by market capitalization.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Ether&lt;/strong&gt; — the native asset of the Ethereum network.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;USDT&lt;/strong&gt; — a dollar-linked stablecoin issued by Tether.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Public Trading Approval Is the Key Condition&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most important part of the report is the regulatory condition attached to Sberbank’s proposal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bank’s potential acceptance of ETH and USDT as collateral is tied to the &lt;strong&gt;Bank of Russia allowing the relevant assets to be publicly traded under the new cryptocurrency rules&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means Sberbank is not simply deciding that every cryptocurrency can automatically become eligible collateral. The regulatory framework comes first.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is consistent with Russia’s broader approach to digital assets, where cryptocurrency activity is increasingly being placed inside a defined legal and financial framework rather than being treated as an unrestricted alternative to traditional money.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Russia’s New Crypto Framework&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Russia has been working toward a regulatory structure that distinguishes between different types of investors and different forms of digital-asset activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Qualified investors are expected to have broader access to certain cryptocurrency-related activities, while ordinary retail investors face greater restrictions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the important elements discussed in connection with the new framework is a proposed &lt;strong&gt;300,000-ruble annual limit for certain retail cryptocurrency transactions&lt;/strong&gt;, depending on the applicable rules and investor classification.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Reports have also indicated that approximately &lt;strong&gt;98% of Russian retail investors are classified as non-qualified&lt;/strong&gt; under the relevant framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes the distinction between institutional, qualified and ordinary retail participation especially important when considering Sberbank’s plans.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Digital Ruble Adds Another Layer&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sberbank’s crypto plans are also emerging as Russia continues its rollout of the &lt;strong&gt;digital ruble&lt;/strong&gt;, the country’s central bank digital currency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The digital ruble is fundamentally different from Bitcoin, Ether and USDT. It is issued by the Bank of Russia and represents a form of central-bank money, while the other assets operate within very different technological and monetary structures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The parallel development is nevertheless significant. Russia is simultaneously building infrastructure for a state-backed digital currency while creating rules for privately issued and decentralized digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Together, these developments show that digital finance is becoming a more formal part of the country's financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Sberbank’s Huge Customer Base Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sberbank is not a small financial company experimenting with cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bank reported approximately &lt;strong&gt;110.6 million retail clients in the second quarter of 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, giving it an enormous potential reach if digital-asset lending eventually expands beyond a limited institutional product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the size of Sberbank’s customer base should not be interpreted as meaning that all of those customers will immediately gain access to crypto-backed loans.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The regulatory classification of customers and the assets permitted for specific financial products will remain important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How a Crypto-Backed Loan Could Work&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The basic structure of a crypto-backed loan is relatively straightforward.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The borrower pledges an eligible cryptocurrency as collateral.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The bank determines the value of that collateral using an approved pricing mechanism.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The borrower receives a loan worth less than the full value of the collateral.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The collateral remains subject to the lending agreement while the loan is outstanding.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;If the cryptocurrency falls sharply in value, the borrower may need to provide additional collateral or repay part of the loan.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The relationship between the value of the collateral and the amount borrowed is commonly measured through a &lt;strong&gt;loan-to-value (LTV) ratio&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because cryptocurrency prices can be highly volatile, a bank may require a substantial safety buffer to protect itself against sudden market movements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin, Ether and USDT: What Could They Mean as Collateral?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Biggest Risk: Cryptocurrency Volatility&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The potential benefits of crypto-backed lending come with obvious risks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin and Ether can experience significant price movements over short periods. A borrower who pledges ETH, for example, could see the value of the collateral fall rapidly while the amount owed to the bank remains unchanged.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This can trigger a margin call, requiring the borrower to add more collateral or reduce the outstanding loan.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;USDT may behave differently because it is designed to track the U.S. dollar, but stablecoins also carry their own regulatory, issuer and liquidity risks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For a major bank, effective risk management would therefore be just as important as the underlying blockchain technology.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Sanctions Add Another Layer to Russia’s Crypto Strategy&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is also a geopolitical dimension to Russia’s growing interest in regulated cryptocurrency activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Russia’s financial sector has faced extensive Western sanctions and restrictions affecting international banking relationships and cross-border payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That environment has increased interest in alternative settlement channels.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cryptocurrencies and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/how-do-companies-use-ai-today.html"&gt;stablecoins&lt;/a&gt; can potentially transfer value across borders without depending entirely on traditional correspondent banking networks. However, this does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean that cryptocurrencies provide a simple or guaranteed way around sanctions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchain transactions can be monitored, exchanges and custodians can impose compliance controls, and governments can restrict access to regulated financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Russia’s approach therefore appears more focused on creating &lt;strong&gt;controlled and regulated digital-asset channels&lt;/strong&gt; than on allowing an unrestricted cryptocurrency economy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What This Could Mean for Russian Banks&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If Sberbank successfully introduces crypto-backed lending under the new rules, other Russian financial institutions could watch the model closely.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The biggest question will be whether banks can manage cryptocurrency volatility while maintaining acceptable levels of credit and operational risk.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the model proves practical, digital assets could gradually move from being primarily investment instruments into a broader role within regulated financial services.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That would represent an important change in how traditional banks interact with cryptocurrencies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What It Means for Bitcoin, Ethereum and USDT&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the cryptocurrency market, Sberbank’s proposal is notable because it connects major digital assets with a conventional banking use case.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin could gain another institutional collateral use case. Ether could receive additional recognition as a financial asset within a regulated banking environment. USDT, meanwhile, could demonstrate how stablecoins might be incorporated into traditional lending structures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But none of these developments automatically guarantees increased demand or higher prices for the assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The ultimate impact would depend on regulatory approval, product design, liquidity, risk controls and actual customer adoption.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The immediate question is whether the &lt;strong&gt;Bank of Russia approves the relevant framework for public cryptocurrency trading&lt;/strong&gt; and determines which assets can be used in specific financial products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the necessary approvals are granted, Sberbank could become an important test case for how a major traditional bank incorporates cryptocurrency into secured lending.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Other Russian banks could then study the results before deciding whether to introduce similar products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Picture&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Russia’s cryptocurrency policy is becoming increasingly difficult to describe simply as either “pro-crypto” or “anti-crypto.”&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The reality is more nuanced.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The country appears to be developing a framework that permits selected digital-asset activity while maintaining substantial regulatory control over who can participate, which assets can be traded and how banks can use those assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sberbank’s reported plan to accept Bitcoin, Ether and USDT as potential loan collateral fits into that broader strategy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is not necessarily a sign that cryptocurrencies are replacing the Russian banking system. Instead, it could indicate that selected digital assets are gradually being brought &lt;strong&gt;inside the regulated financial system&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sberbank’s reported plan to accept &lt;strong&gt;Ether and USDT alongside Bitcoin as potential loan collateral&lt;/strong&gt; could become an important milestone for Russia’s regulated cryptocurrency market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the proposal remains dependent on regulatory approval and the rules governing public cryptocurrency trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For borrowers, the attraction is straightforward: crypto could potentially provide access to credit without requiring an immediate sale of the underlying asset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For banks, the challenge is considerably more complicated. They would need to manage price volatility, liquidity, collateral valuation, regulatory requirements and compliance risks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Russia’s simultaneous development of regulated crypto activity and the digital ruble also demonstrates that the country is pursuing a broader digital-finance strategy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If Sberbank’s model moves forward, the more important question may not be whether banks can use cryptocurrency as collateral, but &lt;strong&gt;how deeply traditional banking can integrate digital assets while keeping their unique risks under control.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;a href="https://www.cbr.ru/eng/fintech/dr/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Bank of Russia — Digital Ruble&lt;/a&gt;

    <title>Brian Armstrong Predicts CLARITY Act Could Win Far More Than 60 Senate Votes</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi5zLZ2ZAbqfTHWCV_73-j0iT-KZKRjOwpugSIwpAfieWR8bCPk2hdEgi0EKH-HG7nImmtSHhTiQCG5CV-DpOgX46aao_14TCTV_w6nMgQLg1ABhP-yfk6yj-VUtjDkvAiMs3xKeYTDz3bMGbnWaBw4dvUPfxlU3p6NtqpfyrJp9yKvOgzqcl3mYEPwPQWq/s1672/brian-armstrong-clarity-act-senate-vote.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Brian Armstrong discusses the CLARITY Act and its upcoming Senate vote" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi5zLZ2ZAbqfTHWCV_73-j0iT-KZKRjOwpugSIwpAfieWR8bCPk2hdEgi0EKH-HG7nImmtSHhTiQCG5CV-DpOgX46aao_14TCTV_w6nMgQLg1ABhP-yfk6yj-VUtjDkvAiMs3xKeYTDz3bMGbnWaBw4dvUPfxlU3p6NtqpfyrJp9yKvOgzqcl3mYEPwPQWq/w400-h225/brian-armstrong-clarity-act-senate-vote.jpg.png" title="Brian Armstrong CLARITY Act Senate Vote" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The U.S. crypto industry may be heading toward another major
test in Washington, and Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong believes the numbers could
be much stronger than many expected.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In a fresh update circulating on social media, Armstrong
said he expects the &lt;b&gt;CLARITY Act to receive “far more than 60 votes” in the
U.S. Senate&lt;/b&gt;, describing the legislation as a strong bipartisan compromise.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The comment comes as lawmakers prepare for a crucial
September test of the bill. The Senate is scheduled to consider a procedural
vote on &lt;b&gt;September 15&lt;/b&gt;, meaning Armstrong's prediction arrives at an
important moment for the future of U.S. crypto regulation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For the crypto market, the distinction matters. The CLARITY
Act has not passed the Senate and is not yet law. The September vote is a test
of whether senators can move the legislation forward.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But Armstrong's confidence suggests that Coinbase and other
major crypto companies see a realistic path toward bipartisan support.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Armstrong's 60-Vote Prediction&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Armstrong's latest comment is essentially a political
forecast, not a vote count.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;He believes the CLARITY Act's bipartisan positioning could
allow it to clear the Senate's 60-vote threshold with room to spare.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That would be significant.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The Senate's procedural rules generally make 60 votes an
important threshold for advancing major legislation. In the case of the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bitwise-ceo-hunter-horsley-says-crypto.html"&gt;CLARITYAct&lt;/a&gt;, the upcoming September 15 cloture vote is expected to determine whether
the Senate can formally move forward with consideration of the bill.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Armstrong's argument is that the current version represents
enough of a compromise to attract support from senators on both sides of the
political aisle.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That does not guarantee passage.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Still, coming from the CEO of one of the world's largest
publicly traded crypto companies, the prediction is likely to attract attention
from investors and digital-asset businesses watching the legislation closely.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What Is the CLARITY Act?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The &lt;b&gt;Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act&lt;/b&gt; is designed to
establish clearer rules for the U.S. cryptocurrency market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;At its core, the legislation attempts to answer one of the
biggest questions facing the American crypto industry:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Which digital assets should fall under the SEC, and which
should be regulated by the CFTC?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The bill would establish a broader federal framework for
digital assets, including rules around market structure, regulatory
jurisdiction and the treatment of different types of crypto assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That could potentially reduce some of the uncertainty that
has surrounded the U.S. crypto industry for years.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The legislation is particularly important because crypto
companies have often operated in an environment where the regulatory boundaries
between securities and commodities were heavily disputed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The CLARITY Act seeks to create clearer lines.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Bill Has Already Cleared Important Hurdles&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The CLARITY Act is not starting from scratch.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The legislation has already passed the House of
Representatives, while Senate committees have also advanced the measure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The Senate Banking Committee approved the bill in May in a &lt;b&gt;15-9
vote&lt;/b&gt;, marking an important step for the legislation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But committee approval is only part of the process.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The bill still needs to navigate the Senate floor, survive
negotiations and ultimately move through the remaining stages of the
legislative process before it could become law.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That is why the September vote is attracting so much
attention.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why September 15 Matters&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;One point is particularly important for anyone following the
story.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;September 15 is not necessarily a final vote to pass the
CLARITY Act.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Instead, the Senate is expected to vote on cloture related
to moving forward with consideration of the legislation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In simple terms, senators will be deciding whether the bill
has enough support to advance through the chamber.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That makes the 60-vote threshold extremely important.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If Armstrong's prediction proves accurate and the bill
receives substantially more than 60 votes, it would send a strong political
signal that bipartisan support exists.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If the vote falls short, however, the legislation could face
another round of negotiations or delays.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Recent reporting has described the Senate's timeline as
tight, with lawmakers returning from recess and facing a limited window to
advance the bill.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why Crypto Companies Want the Bill&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For the crypto industry, regulatory clarity is more than a
political talking point.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Companies need to know which rules apply to their businesses
before making long-term decisions about products, exchanges, custody, token
issuance and investment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The absence of clear federal legislation has been a major
source of uncertainty for U.S. crypto companies.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Coinbase, for example, has spent years pushing for clearer
rules around digital assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Armstrong has previously been critical of versions of crypto
legislation that Coinbase believed did not adequately protect the industry's
interests. Earlier in 2026, he argued that the company would rather see no bill
than support legislation it considered unfavorable.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That makes his latest confidence notable.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The current version appears to have moved closer to the
compromise that Armstrong and other industry executives have been seeking.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What Could the CLARITY Act Mean for Bitcoin?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitcoin is not simply a political asset, but regulation can
influence how investors and institutions approach it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;One of the biggest potential benefits of clearer U.S. crypto
rules would be reduced uncertainty for financial institutions and market
participants.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitcoin already has a relatively established position in the
U.S. market compared with many other digital assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A clearer market-structure framework could nevertheless make
it easier for traditional financial firms to build products and services around
&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/super-micro-probe-finds-no-evidence.html?m=1"&gt;digital assets.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That could include exchanges, custody services,
institutional trading infrastructure and other financial products.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The impact would not necessarily appear overnight.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Regulation does not automatically create a Bitcoin rally.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But clearer rules could remove one of the barriers that has
historically made some institutions cautious about entering the market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Political Backdrop Is Also Changing&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Armstrong's comments come during a period of increasing
political attention on cryptocurrency in Washington.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;President Donald Trump has publicly pushed Congress to
advance crypto legislation, while the administration has also pursued changes
through federal financial regulators.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Reuters recently reported that the CLARITY Act's
congressional progress has stalled while regulators such as the SEC and CFTC
continue moving forward with their own crypto-related policy initiatives.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That creates an unusual situation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The industry is getting more regulatory activity from
Washington, but a comprehensive law from Congress would provide a more durable
framework than agency-level policy changes alone.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That is one reason the Senate process remains important.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why 60 Votes Are So Important&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The Senate is different from the House when it comes to
major legislation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A simple majority is not always enough to move a bill
through the chamber because procedural rules can require a larger coalition to
end debate and advance legislation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For the CLARITY Act, that makes the upcoming 60-vote
threshold a major checkpoint.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Armstrong is effectively saying he believes the legislation
has enough bipartisan support to clear that hurdle comfortably.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Whether that confidence translates into actual votes remains
to be seen.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That is the key distinction investors should keep in mind.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;A prediction is not a vote.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What a Strong Vote Could Signal&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If the CLARITY Act receives substantially more than 60
votes, the market could interpret the result as evidence that crypto
legislation has broader bipartisan support than previously assumed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That could be positive for companies operating in the
digital-asset sector.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It could also strengthen the argument that the United States
is moving toward a more defined regulatory framework for cryptocurrency.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But there are still several steps between a successful
procedural vote and the bill becoming law.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The Senate would need to continue working through the
legislation, differences between House and Senate versions would need to be
addressed, and the final legislation would still have to reach the president.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In other words, &lt;b&gt;a September victory would be important,
but it would not be the finish line.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What Crypto Investors Should Watch&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The biggest event on the calendar is the Senate's September
15 procedural vote.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Investors should watch three things in particular.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;First, the vote count.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A result significantly above 60 votes would support
Armstrong's argument that the legislation has strong bipartisan backing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Second, the final legislative language.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Even if the bill advances, negotiations over specific
provisions could continue.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Third, the reaction from the crypto industry.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Major exchanges, asset managers, blockchain companies and
other digital-asset businesses are likely to pay close attention to the final
framework.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For Bitcoin holders, the broader question is whether
regulatory clarity eventually encourages more institutional participation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;A Potential Turning Point for U.S. Crypto Regulation&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The CLARITY Act has already survived several difficult
stages.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It has moved through the House, cleared Senate committee
hurdles and now faces the next major test.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Armstrong's latest prediction adds another layer of interest
because he is not merely saying the bill could pass.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;He is suggesting that it could receive &lt;b&gt;far more than the
60 votes needed for the Senate's procedural hurdle&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That would represent a strong showing of bipartisan support.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Still, investors should avoid treating the prediction as a
guarantee.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The legislation remains subject to negotiations, political
disagreements and the realities of the Senate calendar.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Brian Armstrong is betting that the CLARITY Act has enough
bipartisan support to win &lt;b&gt;far more than 60 votes&lt;/b&gt; in the U.S. Senate.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;His prediction comes as the legislation approaches a crucial
September 15 procedural test.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The bill is designed to create a clearer regulatory
framework for digital assets and define the roles of the SEC and CFTC in
overseeing different parts of the crypto market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For the industry, that clarity could be significant.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For Bitcoin, the biggest potential benefit may come
indirectly through greater institutional confidence and a more predictable
regulatory environment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But there is an important caveat: &lt;b&gt;the CLARITY Act is not
law yet, and Armstrong's vote prediction is not a confirmed Senate outcome.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The real answer will come when senators cast their votes.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Until then, Armstrong's bullish assessment gives the crypto
market another reason to watch Washington closely.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>OpenAI Calls for Global AI Standards as Frontier Models Raise Recursive Self-Improvement Questions</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;
  &lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj3vg-bSC03CHBpAITFj8c3eZd_YsrfRiM3KIMt8M5uPVuLFb5Dfgl9a1ZsasWJ19hh5dzJG9FXLZ8jCCP_HxNjTzt2tcMp_zhnLH660LsFoV21-0OXW7QZvdnV-WXmKrX4VVl-Q_8eMZbI-k_HmUBQhvxYLD5Abp9pf4OflFJw8sRibhfYEyi5O3tovPfI/s1734/openai-global-ai-standards-recursive-self-improvement-2026.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="OpenAI proposes global AI standards for frontier models and recursive self-improvement" border="0" data-original-height="907" data-original-width="1734" height="334" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj3vg-bSC03CHBpAITFj8c3eZd_YsrfRiM3KIMt8M5uPVuLFb5Dfgl9a1ZsasWJ19hh5dzJG9FXLZ8jCCP_HxNjTzt2tcMp_zhnLH660LsFoV21-0OXW7QZvdnV-WXmKrX4VVl-Q_8eMZbI-k_HmUBQhvxYLD5Abp9pf4OflFJw8sRibhfYEyi5O3tovPfI/w640-h334/openai-global-ai-standards-recursive-self-improvement-2026.webp.png" title="OpenAI Global AI Standards and Recursive Self-Improvement" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Editorial Team&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;OpenAI is calling for greater international coordination on artificial intelligence safety as frontier models become more capable and AI systems take on a larger role in research and development.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In a policy proposal published on &lt;strong&gt;September 21, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, OpenAI urged the United States to help lead an international effort to develop technical standards for frontier AI, including systems that could eventually contribute to &lt;strong&gt;recursive self-improvement (RSI)&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The proposal focuses on common ways to measure AI capabilities, evaluate risks, monitor increasingly automated AI research and report serious incidents. OpenAI argues that compatible standards could help governments, companies and independent organizations evaluate increasingly capable systems across national borders.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The timing is notable. The proposal comes during the United Nations General Assembly's &lt;strong&gt;High-Level Week, scheduled for September 22–29, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, in New York. The General Assembly's general debate is scheduled for September 22–26 and September 28. &lt;a href="https://www.un.org/pga/81/meetings-and-events/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;United Nations General Assembly&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Did OpenAI Propose?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI is not proposing a single global AI regulator or a worldwide AI law.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Instead, the company is calling for countries and AI developers to work toward compatible technical standards that can be used across jurisdictions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI's September 21 proposal calls for common measurements of frontier AI progress, approaches for evaluating risks, methods for preserving human control and mechanisms for reporting significant incidents.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The company also wants standards that can help determine when advanced AI development should slow down or stop if safety requirements cannot be met.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/openai-calls-us-take-lead-global-efforts-develop-technical-standards-2026-09-21/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;Reuters reported on September 21, 2026&lt;/a&gt;, that OpenAI was calling for the United States to take a leading role in developing global technical standards for frontier AI, including recursive self-improvement.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Recursive Self-Improvement Is Getting Attention&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;One of the most important concepts in OpenAI's proposal is &lt;strong&gt;recursive self-improvement, or RSI&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In broad terms, recursive self-improvement describes a future scenario in which AI systems can contribute to improving their own capabilities or help develop increasingly capable successors, potentially reducing the amount of direct human involvement required in AI research.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That does not mean today's AI systems are independently redesigning themselves without human oversight.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI explicitly states that &lt;strong&gt;fully autonomous recursive self-improvement is not happening today&lt;/strong&gt; and says it should not be pursued unless and until it can be done safely.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;At the same time, OpenAI says AI is already accelerating parts of the research used to develop and align future models. The company has described this as evidence of the direction in which AI research could move, while distinguishing it from fully autonomous RSI.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;OpenAI Wants Common Measurements for Frontier AI&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A major challenge in international AI governance is that different organizations and governments can use different definitions and measurements when evaluating advanced systems.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI's proposal calls for more consistent technical measurements that could help policymakers understand how quickly AI capabilities are advancing.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For recursive self-improvement, the company has discussed measuring progress related to autonomous AI research and the amount of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/how-crypto-agencies-can-offer-white.html"&gt;research work&lt;/a&gt; being performed by &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bernstein-sees-prediction-markets.html"&gt;AI systems&lt;/a&gt; within AI-development organizations.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Such measurements could eventually help distinguish between an AI model that primarily assists human researchers and a system performing increasingly important portions of the research process itself.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Human Oversight Would Remain Important&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI's proposal also emphasizes human oversight of increasingly automated AI research.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;As AI systems perform longer sequences of tasks, it can become more difficult for researchers to manually inspect every experiment, decision or intermediate result.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Common technical standards could eventually help define situations in which automated AI research should trigger additional human review.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The proposal does not itself create a legally binding international review system. Instead, OpenAI is advocating technical standards that governments could consider when developing their own policies.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;AI Incident Reporting Could Become More Standardized&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Another important part of the discussion is incident reporting.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI wants common approaches for identifying and reporting significant AI safety and alignment incidents, including clearer definitions of severity and reporting thresholds.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The basic idea is that if an advanced &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/arthur-hayes-ai-safety-anthropic-ipo-2026.html"&gt;AI system&lt;/a&gt; produces a serious or unexpected behavior, researchers and policymakers should have a shared way to describe what happened and determine its significance.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI separately published a &lt;strong&gt;model misalignment reporting framework on September 16, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;. The framework describes how the company intends to track, investigate and disclose concerning model behavior, and OpenAI published six initial examples alongside it.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The company said the framework is intended to contribute to broader understanding of AI alignment and potentially help establish more consistent disclosure practices across the industry. &lt;a href="https://openai.com/index/model-misalignment-reporting-framework/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;OpenAI's September 16 framework&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Does AI Alignment Mean?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI alignment&lt;/strong&gt; generally refers to efforts to make AI systems behave consistently with intended goals, safety requirements and human-defined constraints.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The issue becomes more complicated as models become more capable and autonomous.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;An AI system that answers questions gives humans relatively direct control over its actions. An AI system capable of conducting extended research, writing and testing code, running experiments and adapting its approach could require different monitoring methods.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI's policy push is therefore connected to a broader question: how should society measure and manage AI systems when the systems themselves increasingly participate in the process of developing future AI?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Chris Lehane's September 9 Policy Push&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The September 21 proposal was not an isolated policy announcement.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;On &lt;strong&gt;September 9, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, OpenAI Chief Global Affairs Officer &lt;strong&gt;Chris Lehane&lt;/strong&gt; published a policy post outlining the company's broader approach to AI governance.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Lehane wrote that OpenAI wanted to advance industry-led frontier AI standards while also advocating compatible international approaches to measuring capabilities, managing risk, preserving human control and determining when development should slow or stop.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;He also argued that industry-led standards should complement, rather than replace, mandatory government safeguards and democratic oversight.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That September 9 position provides important context for the September 21 international standards proposal: OpenAI is pursuing several layers of AI governance rather than relying exclusively on voluntary industry commitments.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://openai.com/index/ai-policy-window/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;OpenAI — September 9, 2026&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why OpenAI Wants International Cooperation&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;AI development is now a global industry.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;AI models can be developed in one country, trained using infrastructure spanning several regions and deployed to users around the world. Researchers, computing resources and technical expertise also move across national borders.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI argues that fragmented technical standards could make advanced AI safety evaluations harder because companies and governments may use incompatible definitions, tests and reporting systems.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The company therefore wants compatible national and international approaches for measuring capabilities, managing risks, maintaining human control and determining when development should slow down.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI had already been working on shared AI standards before the September proposal. In June, the company described efforts involving the Appia Foundation and other standards organizations aimed at making AI assessment practices more interoperable across organizations and jurisdictions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://openai.com/index/helping-build-shared-standards-for-advanced-ai/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;OpenAI — Helping Build Shared Standards for Advanced AI&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why the United States Is Central to OpenAI's Proposal&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI specifically wants the United States to take a leading role in the standards effort.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The company argues that the United States has significant influence across technology, research, finance and international alliances, giving it an opportunity to shape how frontier AI standards develop.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Reuters reported on September 21 that the proposal was released as world leaders gathered at the United Nations, with AI expected to be an important subject of international discussions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Reuters also reported that OpenAI CEO &lt;strong&gt;Sam Altman was due to brief the 15-member U.N. Security Council on September 23&lt;/strong&gt; on AI and international security. The meeting was convened by France, which holds the Security Council presidency for September. &lt;a href="https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/openai-calls-us-take-lead-global-efforts-develop-technical-standards-2026-09-21/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;Reuters, September 21, 2026&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A separate &lt;strong&gt;September 22 Reuters report&lt;/strong&gt; said Sam Altman and senior representatives from Anthropic were expected to participate in the Security Council discussion, while Chinese AI companies including DeepSeek and Moonshot had been invited to contribute. &lt;a href="https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/deepseek-brief-un-security-council-ai-this-week-sources-say-2026-09-22/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;Reuters, September 22, 2026&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Standards Are Not the Same as a Global AI Law&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI's proposal should not be confused with the creation of a worldwide AI law.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Technical standards can establish common methods for testing and measuring AI systems without automatically replacing national laws.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Individual governments would continue to determine their own regulatory requirements, including rules covering AI deployment, safety, privacy, national security and liability.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The proposal is therefore better understood as an attempt to create greater technical compatibility between different AI governance systems.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;OpenAI's Recent Research Adds Context&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI's policy discussion comes alongside research showing that the company is actively exploring greater automation of AI research.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In a September 6 research update, OpenAI said it had reached its previously announced goal of having an automated research intern by September 2026. The company said its longer-term aim is to safely build an automated AI researcher that can work under human supervision to advance deep learning and alignment research.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI has described this work as AI-assisted research rather than fully autonomous recursive self-improvement.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That distinction remains central to the company's current position: AI can increasingly contribute to AI development, but OpenAI says fully autonomous RSI is not happening today.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://openai.com/index/research-acceleration-view-inside-openai/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;OpenAI — Research Acceleration: The View Inside OpenAI&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Could Change for AI Companies?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If international technical standards eventually gain broad support, AI developers could face more consistent expectations around capability evaluations, safety testing, automated research oversight and incident reporting.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That could make it easier for companies operating across multiple countries to demonstrate that their systems have undergone comparable evaluations.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There could also be additional costs. Independent evaluations, monitoring, documentation and reporting require technical infrastructure and specialized personnel.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For smaller AI companies, extensive standards could create a greater compliance burden than for large frontier laboratories.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;On the other hand, standardized testing could give customers, researchers and governments a clearer way to compare the safety characteristics of advanced AI systems.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Who Should Set Frontier AI Standards?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;One of the difficult questions raised by the proposal is who should actually create the standards.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;AI companies possess detailed technical knowledge about frontier models. Governments have regulatory authority and public-policy responsibilities. Independent researchers and standards organizations can provide additional scrutiny.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Each group brings a different perspective.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That makes international coordination complicated, particularly when companies building advanced systems are also participating in discussions about how those systems should be evaluated.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI's proposal calls for broader cooperation rather than suggesting that one company should control the standards process.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The next stage will depend on whether governments, competing AI developers, researchers and standards organizations adopt compatible approaches.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI has pointed to existing national AI safety institutions as a possible foundation for international cooperation. If those institutions begin using comparable measurements and reporting frameworks, the company's proposal could contribute to a broader technical standard-setting process.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For now, however, there is no single global standard governing recursive self-improvement.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There is also no international consensus on exactly how quickly frontier AI development should proceed or what level of capability should trigger mandatory restrictions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What did OpenAI propose about global AI standards?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI proposed greater international coordination around frontier AI standards, including common approaches to measuring capabilities, managing risks, preserving human control and reporting significant AI incidents.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What is recursive self-improvement in AI?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Recursive self-improvement refers to AI systems contributing to improvements in their own capabilities or helping develop increasingly capable successors. OpenAI has discussed RSI as a potential future development and says fully autonomous RSI is not happening today.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is OpenAI proposing a global AI law?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;No. OpenAI is proposing technical standards and international coordination. Individual governments would continue to establish their own laws and regulations.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Why does AI alignment matter?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;AI alignment focuses on making AI systems behave consistently with intended goals, safety requirements and human control. The challenge becomes more significant as systems become capable of performing longer and more autonomous tasks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Why does OpenAI want common AI incident reporting?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Common reporting standards could give governments, researchers and AI developers a consistent way to classify and respond to serious safety or alignment incidents involving advanced AI systems.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is fully autonomous recursive self-improvement already happening?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI says it is not happening today. Current AI systems can assist with AI research and development, but that is different from an AI system independently controlling a complete recursive self-improvement process.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Conclusion&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI's latest policy proposal puts a sharper focus on the technical standards that could be needed as frontier AI becomes more capable.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The company wants international coordination around capability measurement, risk assessment, human oversight and incident reporting, while asking the United States to take a leading role in developing compatible standards.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Recursive self-improvement is one reason the issue is receiving increased attention. AI has not reached the point of fully autonomous recursive self-improvement, according to OpenAI, but the possibility of AI systems performing a larger share of the work involved in developing future AI is becoming an important technical and policy question.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;With the U.N. General Assembly High-Level Week taking place in New York from September 22–29, 2026, the discussion is also moving beyond individual AI companies and into the international policy arena.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The eventual framework will depend on governments, AI developers, researchers and standards organizations. For now, OpenAI's proposal represents a push toward creating a common technical language for evaluating advanced AI before future capabilities become harder to measure and govern.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Sources:&lt;/strong&gt; OpenAI, Reuters and United Nations General Assembly materials.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/article&gt;

    <title>OpenAI Sets 2027 IPO Target, CFO Says 'We Will Be a Public Company'</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiqMcdRSuEAO5bPe1P9t7n6Du7pcbBrQQ5EjTa2JDQ4GhFAMfv74jp3-whFwjo2HlX5MI62mfcPV_atmpZnsjwnyRp0dCdv5VAwTrc4BbVSYWYl9Gv3sHXA-FbEsTZOhfD3XC6nSni8n2ydRFfaRnvYnWbU8Ly7q3Is3yV9W-aTCnczd-ihGF5XQ-VdsxRi/s1672/openai-2027-ipo-ai-market-growth.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin and U.S. Treasury bonds illustrated as Standard Chartered sees a potential $100,000 Bitcoin target" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiqMcdRSuEAO5bPe1P9t7n6Du7pcbBrQQ5EjTa2JDQ4GhFAMfv74jp3-whFwjo2HlX5MI62mfcPV_atmpZnsjwnyRp0dCdv5VAwTrc4BbVSYWYl9Gv3sHXA-FbEsTZOhfD3XC6nSni8n2ydRFfaRnvYnWbU8Ly7q3Is3yV9W-aTCnczd-ihGF5XQ-VdsxRi/w400-h225/openai-2027-ipo-ai-market-growth.jpg.png" title="Standard Chartered Bitcoin $100K Treasury Bond Buybacks" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;OpenAI appears to be getting closer to one of the biggest potential technology IPOs in years. The company has reportedly told employees that it expects to become a public company in 2027, although the timeline could move sooner if its business continues to grow rapidly.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;During an all-hands meeting on Wednesday, OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar reportedly told employees that the company &lt;strong&gt;“will be a public company in 2027.”&lt;/strong&gt; The comments offer one of the clearest indications yet that OpenAI is preparing for a future listing.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;blockquote&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;em&gt;“The IPO is not a finish line, it is a milestone, another fundraise. We raised $122 billion in March, and that gives us flexibility.”&lt;/em&gt; — Sarah Friar, OpenAI CFO&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/blockquote&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Numbers Behind OpenAI's IPO Plans&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;OpenAI has already taken an important step toward a potential public offering by confidentially filing an IPO prospectus with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in June, according to reports.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The company's rapidly expanding revenue and enormous private-market valuation could make the eventual offering one of the most closely watched technology listings in the market.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;$852 billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;About $40 billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Enterprise Revenue Growth&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(221, 221, 221); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;50% QTD&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
