    <title>White House 'Fully Committed' to Passing CLARITY Act in September, Crypto Advisor Says</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjoiQNI4FRN5YwJtbovNRGnO_LLzLQxllQUuitQJOtzkOmfDPY-Om2fdoUGVpvl4X6V2kNHay7YK1q2WASFkv8lBtcjgdjQhFgv72-xqQtkAZrwMvz1UmLmR_8CAvd-fceIqzFuC3YjlQP-5wI_BT-c1KnynEC_uSkvWR_YVKPY0ziyI_wiTZ1ZhYgt8mdy/s1672/clarity-act-us-crypto-regulation-senate.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="U.S. Capitol surrounded by blockchain and cryptocurrency graphics representing the CLARITY Act and U.S. crypto regulation" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjoiQNI4FRN5YwJtbovNRGnO_LLzLQxllQUuitQJOtzkOmfDPY-Om2fdoUGVpvl4X6V2kNHay7YK1q2WASFkv8lBtcjgdjQhFgv72-xqQtkAZrwMvz1UmLmR_8CAvd-fceIqzFuC3YjlQP-5wI_BT-c1KnynEC_uSkvWR_YVKPY0ziyI_wiTZ1ZhYgt8mdy/w320-h180/clarity-act-us-crypto-regulation-senate.png" title="CLARITY Act Crypto Regulation and U.S. Senate" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aug 11, 2026&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;– The Trump administration remains
"fully committed" to passing the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/nvidia-helps-turn-ai-compute-into.html"&gt;CLARITY Act&lt;/a&gt; in September, according
to White House crypto advisor Patrick Witt, even as the bill's chances of
becoming law this year have dropped to just 19% on prediction markets&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Witt, Executive Director of the President's Council of
Advisors for Digital Assets, confirmed the administration's stance in comments
posted on X on August 11, saying that "durable rules, the kind only
legislation can provide, are needed now more than ever"&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"Every time Democrats have delayed this bill,
America has fallen further behind in the digital asset race. This has
jeopardized our leadership role in global financial markets, weakening our
national security, and denying law enforcement the tools they need to stop
crypto crime."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;—&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Patrick Witt&lt;/b&gt;, Executive Director, President's
Council of Advisors for Digital Assets&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;September 15: The Cloture Showdown&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) filed a cloture
motion on August 8, setting up a key procedural vote for&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;September 15
at 2:15 PM ET&lt;/b&gt;, when the Senate returns from its five-week August
recess&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What's at stake:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The cloture motion
requires&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;60 votes&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;to advance the bill and overcome a
Democratic filibuster. Republicans hold 53 Senate seats, meaning they need
support from at least seven Democrats to proceed&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The bill has already passed the House and cleared the Senate
Banking Committee 15-9 in May, but it has stalled in the full Senate over
disagreements on developer liability, ethics provisions, and stablecoin
regulations&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What's in the CLARITY Act&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The CLARITY Act would establish a comprehensive federal
framework for digital assets, ending the "regulation by enforcement"
approach that has dominated U.S. crypto policy&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Key provisions include:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Clear
     classification of digital assets as securities, commodities, or payment
     stablecoins&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Protections
     for non-custodial software developers and blockchain infrastructure
     providers&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Bankruptcy
     remoteness provisions to protect customer assets if an exchange fails&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Ethics
     rules for federal officials involved in crypto&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Increased
     funding for law enforcement to investigate crypto-related crime&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why Passage Is Uncertain&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Despite the administration's push, analysts have reduced
their expectations for passage:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/cathie-wood-says-deflation-risk-is.html"&gt;Polymarket&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;traders
     now price a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;19% chance&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;that the CLARITY Act becomes law
     in 2026 — down from above 50% during much of the spring&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;TD
     Cowen Washington Research Group&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;analyst Jaret Seiberg assigns
     a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;25% probability&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;of enactment this fall&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Two disputes remain unresolved ahead of the September
vote&amp;nbsp;:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol start="1" style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="1"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Ethics
     provisions:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Democratic senators have demanded stricter ethics
     rules targeting Trump-linked crypto interests&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Stablecoin
     rewards:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Banking industry groups have pushed back against
     provisions that could allow companies to pay rewards to stablecoin
     holders, arguing it could pull deposits away from community banks&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Developer liability&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;has also been a flashpoint.
A revised proposal backed by law enforcement and key Democrats would make it
easier to prosecute crypto software developers, but the White House dismissed
the latest version as "not even close" to meeting its expectations&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What Delay Means for Crypto&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The delay extends uncertainty for crypto exchanges, token
issuers, and investors who have been waiting for clearer federal rules
governing digital assets&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Grayscale Research Director Zach Pandl&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;said the
CLARITY Act now seems unlikely to pass Congress this year, noting that the
Senate's busy schedule and election-year politics make it difficult to reach a
bipartisan agreement&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;However, Pandl noted that failure of the bill "will not
directly impact the demand for Bitcoin as a store of value, the functioning of
major blockchains, or the growth in stablecoin payments in the short
term"&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Industry voices remain optimistic:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Cody Carbone,
CEO of crypto trade group Digital Chamber, said: "While this isn't the
result any of us hoped for when we began the week, the fight is far from over.
The next few weeks, we will continue to work to find the last pieces of common ground
needed to set up a successful vote when Congress returns in
September"&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What Happens Next&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If the cloture vote succeeds on September 15, the bill moves
toward a final passage vote. If it fails, the CLARITY Act may not get another
chance in 2026.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Federal regulators are moving on separate crypto rules in
the meantime. The SEC will hold an open meeting on August 14 to consider a
proposal for a tailored offering regime covering certain investment contracts
involving crypto assets&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The regulatory track does not replace the CLARITY Act, which
would set broader market structure rules through legislation. But the SEC's
August meeting shows that federal agencies are preparing to act while Congress
works through the outstanding disputes&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

    <title>South Korea Unveils 3-Phase Plan to Tokenize Stocks, Bonds and Funds</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgphQUePbbHdGtWMEcLyfRGN3DihayR9g4lCjenlDlOyA3QzKJV3LS3Gr0Uk-wWCyMMyr6LRbTzHZ4GgA1Z_UcOuWCbpK8jx6XlfFFgL65n2qn_L49yswzmdEexg5JjuD4TE1qUHI3nLuukz1sIB0orVwbQ39hqcSz80h_vmLaanKLNR4SJ1k0iguGgO56P/s1672/south-korea-tokenized-securities-stocks-bonds-funds-2027.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="South Korea three-phase roadmap for tokenized stocks bonds and funds" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgphQUePbbHdGtWMEcLyfRGN3DihayR9g4lCjenlDlOyA3QzKJV3LS3Gr0Uk-wWCyMMyr6LRbTzHZ4GgA1Z_UcOuWCbpK8jx6XlfFFgL65n2qn_L49yswzmdEexg5JjuD4TE1qUHI3nLuukz1sIB0orVwbQ39hqcSz80h_vmLaanKLNR4SJ1k0iguGgO56P/w640-h360/south-korea-tokenized-securities-stocks-bonds-funds-2027.jpg.png" title="South Korea's 3-Phase Tokenized Securities Roadmap" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;September 4, 2026&lt;/strong&gt; — South Korea is preparing for a major shift in the way traditional securities could be issued, traded and eventually settled, with regulators laying out a three-phase roadmap for tokenized securities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Financial Services Commission (FSC) announced the roadmap on Friday, outlining a plan that could eventually bring a much wider range of financial assets onto blockchain-based infrastructure. The framework covers selected securities in its first stage, broader publicly offered securities in the second and an eventual on-chain payment and settlement system in the third.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The first phase is scheduled to begin on &lt;strong&gt;February 4, 2027&lt;/strong&gt;, when amendments to South Korea's electronic securities framework are expected to take effect.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the February 2027 date should not be misunderstood. South Korea is &lt;strong&gt;not planning to turn every stock, bond and investment fund into a blockchain token overnight&lt;/strong&gt;. The initial rollout is limited to specific categories, while broader tokenization is planned for later stages.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;South Korea's Tokenization Plan Explained&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The FSC's roadmap represents an attempt to move tokenized securities from a relatively narrow digital-asset concept into a regulated capital-market framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The regulator's broader objective is to develop a digital capital market covering more than just the token itself. The work involves the wider chain of financial-market activities, including issuance, trading, clearing, settlement, the exercise of investor rights and the connection with underlying assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes the announcement significant beyond the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/small-crypto-transactions-are-draining.html"&gt;cryptocurrency &lt;/a&gt;industry. If the roadmap progresses as planned, blockchain infrastructure could eventually become part of the country's mainstream securities-market architecture.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 16px; min-width: 760px; table-layout: fixed; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px; width: 15%;"&gt;Phase&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px; width: 48%;"&gt;What It Covers&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px; width: 37%;"&gt;Expected Timing&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Phase 1&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Institutional-only private money&lt;br /&gt;-market funds, institutional-only&lt;br /&gt;private corporate bonds, unlisted &lt;br /&gt;shares through a trust-based &lt;br /&gt;structure and public fractional-&lt;br /&gt;investment securities.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;February 4, 2027&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Phase 2&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Expansion toward publicly offered &lt;br /&gt;securities and broader tokenization &lt;br /&gt;of traditional financial products.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Timing to depend on &lt;br /&gt;Phase 1 and market &lt;br /&gt;conditions.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Phase 3&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;On-chain payment and settlement &lt;br /&gt;infrastructure using stablecoins or &lt;br /&gt;other appropriate payment methods.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;No fixed date announced.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Phase 1 Starts on February 4, 2027&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The first stage is designed as a controlled launch rather than a wholesale transformation of South Korea's securities market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Under the FSC's roadmap, Phase 1 will cover &lt;strong&gt;institutional-only private money-market funds and private corporate bonds&lt;/strong&gt;. It will also allow the tokenization of &lt;strong&gt;unlisted shares through a trust-based structure&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Public fractional-investment securities are another part of the first stage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The selection of these products gives regulators and financial institutions an opportunity to test the legal, technical and operational foundations of tokenized securities before the system is expanded to a much broader range of public securities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This staged approach is important because tokenization is not simply a matter of creating a blockchain token. Financial markets require reliable ownership records, investor protections, trading rules, custody arrangements, cybersecurity controls, settlement mechanisms and clear legal responsibilities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does Tokenizing a Stock or Bond Actually Mean?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tokenization generally means representing ownership or rights associated with a real-world financial asset through a digital token recorded on a distributed ledger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For a tokenized security, the underlying financial asset does not simply disappear into the blockchain. Instead, the digital token is designed to represent legally recognized rights connected to that security under the applicable regulatory framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is particularly important when comparing tokenized securities with cryptocurrencies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A token representing a regulated security is not automatically equivalent to a conventional cryptocurrency. The underlying asset, investor rights, transfer restrictions and regulatory obligations can remain part of the financial product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why South Korea Is Taking a Phased Approach&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Financial-market infrastructure cannot easily be replaced overnight.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Existing securities markets involve exchanges, brokers, custodians, clearing organizations, securities depositories, banks and regulators. A &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/how-is-a-token-generated-in-blockchain.html"&gt;blockchain-based system&lt;/a&gt; therefore has to work with — or carefully replace — multiple layers of established infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;South Korea's phased strategy allows regulators to evaluate the first generation of tokenized products before expanding the framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The FSC has indicated that the move toward later phases will depend on factors including the stability and efficiency of Phase 1, demand from market participants and technological developments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In other words, February 2027 is the beginning of the experiment at scale, not the end of the project.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Phase 2 Could Expand Tokenization to Public Securities&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The second phase could be much more significant for mainstream investors.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The FSC plans to expand the tokenization infrastructure toward &lt;strong&gt;publicly offered securities&lt;/strong&gt;, potentially bringing a much broader range of conventional investment products into the digital securities framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where tokenization could start affecting the structure of traditional capital markets more directly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, there is currently no fixed date for this expansion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The regulator has tied the next stage to the results of Phase 1, technological innovation and the practical demand for tokenized securities. That means the pace of implementation will be determined by how well the initial framework performs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Investors should therefore avoid interpreting the September 4 announcement as confirmation that every publicly listed Korean company will have a tokenized version of its shares available in February 2027.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Phase 3: Bringing Settlement On-Chain&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The third phase could ultimately be the most transformative.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The FSC's roadmap includes the development of &lt;strong&gt;on-chain settlement infrastructure&lt;/strong&gt;, with stablecoins or other suitable payment mechanisms potentially being used as part of the settlement process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The idea is to eventually connect the digital representation of securities with digital payment infrastructure rather than treating securities trading and payment settlement as completely separate processes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;South Korea has not yet specified one particular stablecoin that must be used for this purpose. The FSC's language leaves room for stablecoins or other appropriate payment methods, while the country's broader stablecoin regulatory framework continues to develop.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means it would be premature to say that South Korea has already chosen a specific Korean won stablecoin for securities settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The &lt;strong&gt;Korean won (KRW)&lt;/strong&gt; remains the country's national currency and the natural reference point for domestic securities markets. But the exact design of any future blockchain-based payment layer — including whether and how KRW-linked stablecoins are used — remains a matter for future regulation and infrastructure development.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could Tokenization Make Financial Markets Faster?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the main arguments behind financial-market tokenization is the potential to reduce friction between different parts of the transaction lifecycle.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional securities transactions can involve multiple systems for trading, clearing, settlement and record keeping. Blockchain-based infrastructure could potentially allow some of these functions to operate through more closely connected digital systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Potential advantages include:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Faster settlement:&lt;/strong&gt; Digital infrastructure could reduce the time required to finalize certain transactions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Greater automation:&lt;/strong&gt; Smart-contract technology can potentially automate predefined financial rules and processes.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Improved record management:&lt;/strong&gt; Distributed ledgers can maintain synchronized transaction records.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Lower operational friction:&lt;/strong&gt; Digitized workflows could reduce some reconciliation and administrative work.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Fractional investment:&lt;/strong&gt; Certain securities can be divided into smaller investment units under regulated structures.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These are potential benefits rather than guaranteed results. The final outcome will depend on system design, regulation, liquidity, interoperability and adoption by financial institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;South Korea's Political and Policy Context&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The tokenized-securities push is part of a broader policy effort to modernize South Korea's capital markets and strengthen the country's position in digital finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The current roadmap comes from the &lt;strong&gt;Financial Services Commission and its public-private consultative process&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than being a simple announcement about launching a cryptocurrency product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters because the project involves changes to regulated financial-market infrastructure and requires coordination among government agencies, exchanges, securities firms, technology providers and other market participants.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The FSC's work throughout 2026 has focused on questions around issuance, infrastructure, distribution and settlement of security tokens. The September roadmap brings those discussions into a clearer three-stage structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;South Korea vs. Japan: Two Different Paths to Tokenized Markets&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;South Korea is not the only major Asian economy exploring blockchain-based financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Japan has also been examining how blockchain technology could be used in securities markets. Recent reporting has highlighted Japanese efforts to study blockchain-based infrastructure for faster settlement of stocks and Japanese government bonds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;South Korea's current roadmap stands out because it lays out a &lt;strong&gt;three-stage sequence covering selected tokenized securities, broader public securities and eventually on-chain payment and settlement&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Japan's approach has been developing through its own regulatory and market-infrastructure process, including studies around potential blockchain-based settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So while both countries are exploring similar technological themes, they are not following identical regulatory roadmaps or timelines.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader Asian trend is nevertheless clear: traditional financial institutions and regulators are increasingly examining blockchain as potential &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/clarity-act-gains-momentum-as-sheriffs.html"&gt;market infrastructure&lt;/a&gt; rather than treating it solely as the technology behind cryptocurrencies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Global Tokenization Race Is Accelerating&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;South Korea's announcement also comes as financial institutions in other markets explore tokenized securities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Major exchanges, asset managers and financial technology companies have been experimenting with blockchain-based representations of stocks, funds and other financial assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In the United States, for example, exchanges and financial firms have been exploring ways to combine traditional securities-market protections with tokenized assets and blockchain-based settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This global activity suggests that tokenization is increasingly being considered a potential evolution of financial-market infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, regulators face difficult questions about investor rights, custody, market integrity, liquidity, cybersecurity and the relationship between tokenized assets and the underlying securities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does the Roadmap Mean for Investors?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For investors, the most important takeaway is that tokenized securities are moving closer to regulated mainstream finance in South Korea.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could eventually create new ways to issue, hold and transfer certain financial assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But tokenization does not eliminate investment risk.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blockchain-based record cannot guarantee that a company will grow, that a bond issuer will repay its debt or that an investment fund will produce positive returns.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Investors will still need to consider valuation, liquidity, credit risk, market volatility, regulatory restrictions and the underlying asset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There may also be new technology-related risks, including cybersecurity vulnerabilities and operational failures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Before February 2027?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The period between now and February 4, 2027 will be important for the development of the new framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Financial institutions and infrastructure providers will need to prepare systems capable of supporting tokenized securities within the legal framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Regulators will also have to work through technical and operational questions surrounding issuance, ownership records, trading, settlement and investor protection.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The first phase will effectively serve as a test of whether tokenized securities can operate efficiently within a regulated capital-market environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the system proves stable and useful, the results could provide the foundation for the broader second phase.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Could Change if Phase 3 Succeeds?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If South Korea eventually reaches the third stage, the country's financial infrastructure could look considerably different from today's system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A tokenized security and a blockchain-based payment instrument could potentially interact within a connected digital environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could reduce some of the separation between trading, clearing and settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the exact architecture remains uncertain. The FSC has not promised instant settlement for every asset, 24-hour trading for all securities or a single stablecoin-based system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those outcomes would require additional regulatory decisions, technical development and market adoption.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;South Korea is moving toward one of the more ambitious regulated tokenization frameworks in Asia.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Financial Services Commission's three-phase roadmap begins with selected securities on &lt;strong&gt;February 4, 2027&lt;/strong&gt;, expands toward broader publicly offered securities and ultimately aims to connect securities settlement with on-chain payment infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most important point is that this is a &lt;strong&gt;phased transformation&lt;/strong&gt;, not an overnight conversion of the country's entire stock market into cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Phase 1 will provide the first real-world test. If the infrastructure performs as expected, Phase 2 could widen the scope to more public securities. Phase 3 could then bring payment and settlement further onto blockchain-based infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the global digital-asset industry, the development is significant because it shows a major financial regulator exploring blockchain not merely as a crypto technology, but as a potential foundation for the future operation of regulated capital markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;1. When will South Korea's tokenized securities plan begin?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The first phase is scheduled to begin on &lt;strong&gt;February 4, 2027&lt;/strong&gt;, when the relevant amended electronic securities framework is scheduled to take effect.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;2. Will all South Korean stocks be tokenized on February 4, 2027?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. Phase 1 covers selected securities and investment products. Broader publicly offered securities are part of the planned second phase, whose timing has not been fixed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;3. Which securities are included in Phase 1?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Phase 1 includes institutional-only private money-market funds, institutional-only private corporate bonds, unlisted shares through a trust-based structure and public fractional-investment securities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;4. What is South Korea's Phase 2 tokenization plan?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Phase 2 is intended to expand the tokenization framework toward publicly offered securities. The timing will depend on the performance of Phase 1, technology and market demand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;5. What is planned for Phase 3?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Phase 3 aims to develop on-chain payment and settlement infrastructure using stablecoins or other appropriate payment mechanisms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;6. Will South Korea use a Korean won stablecoin?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The FSC has not specified a particular stablecoin. Its roadmap refers to stablecoins or other appropriate payment methods, meaning the precise payment architecture remains open.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;7. Are tokenized securities the same as cryptocurrencies?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. Tokenized securities are digital representations of regulated financial securities and can carry rights and restrictions connected to the underlying asset. They should not automatically be treated as ordinary cryptocurrencies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;8. Why is South Korea tokenizing securities?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader objective is to modernize capital-market infrastructure and explore whether blockchain can make issuance, trading, record keeping and settlement more digitally connected and efficient.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;9. Is South Korea the only country exploring tokenized securities?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. Financial institutions and regulators in markets including the United States and Japan are also exploring tokenized securities and blockchain-based settlement infrastructure, although their regulatory approaches and timelines differ.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Sources&lt;/h2&gt;

    <title>Crypto’s Strongest Moats: Why Bitcoin, Chainlink and Zcash Are Hard to Replace</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiAU1jtWylmR2PFmB15GmdRODTjTVP4BmrcYZzgjwlo63r40VLeZzMVFw1cPv7rWCsPru-zX1tiSe0W0BHnEqEiWMbg1uuPYtkds5YNSmeZNNEnwRKVEb6HxgxGKpPnYA3UEZoU5dh17IyxqdZh-eZHvFcL25FCAADOdaDXTEf25PP6UJRYoNM_zHuxQAjA/s1536/crypto-strongest-moats-bitcoin-chainlink-zcash.png.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin, Chainlink and Zcash compared by their competitive advantages, including network effects, blockchain infrastructure and privacy-focused user lock-in." border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="213" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiAU1jtWylmR2PFmB15GmdRODTjTVP4BmrcYZzgjwlo63r40VLeZzMVFw1cPv7rWCsPru-zX1tiSe0W0BHnEqEiWMbg1uuPYtkds5YNSmeZNNEnwRKVEb6HxgxGKpPnYA3UEZoU5dh17IyxqdZh-eZHvFcL25FCAADOdaDXTEf25PP6UJRYoNM_zHuxQAjA/w320-h213/crypto-strongest-moats-bitcoin-chainlink-zcash.png.png" title="Bitcoin, Chainlink and Zcash take different approaches to building long-term competitive advantages in crypto." width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aug 15, 2026&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;In most industries, a strong product eventually attracts
competition. If a company finds a profitable market, someone else usually shows
up with a cheaper version, a faster version, or simply a better-funded version.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Crypto makes that process even easier.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Much of the technology is open source. Users can move
between networks with relatively little friction. Developers can copy code,
launch new tokens and build competing protocols in a matter of months.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;So what happens when a crypto project becomes difficult
to replace?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The answer isn't always better &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/who-is-satoshi-nakamoto-why-bitcoins.html"&gt;technology.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Sometimes the advantage comes from network effects.
Sometimes it comes from becoming deeply embedded in financial infrastructure.
And sometimes the product offers something that is surprisingly difficult to
replicate once users, developers and liquidity have gathered around it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin, Chainlink and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/what-happens-to-bitcoin-if-satoshi.html"&gt;Zcash &lt;/a&gt;offer three very different
examples.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;None of them is literally impossible to compete with.
There are competitors in every category. But each has developed a form of
defensibility that makes displacement much harder than simply launching another
blockchain or protocol.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin: The Network Effect Is the Moat&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin is probably the clearest example of a crypto
network whose biggest advantage is not a particular feature, but everything
that has accumulated around it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The software is open source. Anyone can copy the code.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;But copying Bitcoin's code doesn't give a new project
Bitcoin's history, liquidity, brand recognition, infrastructure, holders,
miners, developers or institutional acceptance.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That's the important distinction.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin was the first successful decentralized digital
currency to solve the double-spending problem without relying on a central
authority. More than 15 years later, that first-mover advantage has turned into
something much larger: a network effect that is extremely difficult to
reproduce.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin's monetary policy is another part of the story.
The protocol is designed around a maximum supply of 21 million BTC, with new
issuance falling over time through scheduled halvings. Bitcoin nodes
independently enforce those consensus rules, including the supply limit. &lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That predictable supply has become one of Bitcoin's
defining characteristics.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;But scarcity alone isn't enough to create a moat.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The bigger advantage is that Bitcoin has become the asset
that much of the crypto industry already understands and supports. Exchanges
list it. Custodians support it. Institutional products are built around it.
Wallets support it. Developers build infrastructure for it. And millions of
people already know what Bitcoin is.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That creates a feedback loop.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;More users create more liquidity. More liquidity makes
the asset more useful to institutions. Institutional involvement increases
legitimacy and infrastructure. Better infrastructure makes Bitcoin easier for
more users to access.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;A competing cryptocurrency can copy the underlying
software.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;It can't simply copy that entire ecosystem.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That is why Bitcoin's moat is best understood as network
effect plus monetary credibility plus accumulated infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;And that's considerably harder to reproduce than a
software feature.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Chainlink: Becoming Part of the Infrastructure&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin's moat comes largely from the network itself.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Chainlink's advantage is different.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;It sits underneath a large part of the blockchain
economy, providing infrastructure that smart contracts cannot easily create on
their own.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Blockchains are powerful, but they have a fundamental
limitation: a smart contract cannot simply look outside its own blockchain and
know what is happening in the real world.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;It needs reliable external data.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That could be the price of Bitcoin, the value of a stock,
an interest rate, weather information or another piece of data required by an
application.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That's where blockchain oracles come in.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Chainlink has built one of the largest oracle
infrastructures in the industry and has expanded beyond price feeds into
cross-chain interoperability, data services and infrastructure for tokenized
assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Its own July 2026 metrics show more than $32 trillion in
cumulative Transaction Value Enabled, along with billions of verified onchain
messages. Chainlink defines TVE as the cumulative monetary value of
transactions facilitated by its oracle infrastructure; it isn't the same thing
as Chainlink owning or holding $32 trillion in assets. &lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That distinction matters.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The original article's claim that Chainlink was simply
“processing $30 trillion in tokenized real-world assets” was too broad. The
more accurate description is that Chainlink's infrastructure has facilitated
transactions representing tens of trillions of dollars in value.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The scale is still significant.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Chainlink also reports relationships with major financial
institutions and blockchain projects. Its infrastructure has been used in
experiments and applications involving Swift, J.P. Morgan and other financial
institutions, while major DeFi protocols such as Aave have used Chainlink
services. &lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That's where the moat becomes interesting.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;If Chainlink were simply another application competing
for retail users, switching costs would be relatively low.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Infrastructure is different.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;When developers depend on a particular oracle system,
changing providers can mean testing new data sources, reviewing security
assumptions, changing smart contracts and potentially taking on additional
operational risk.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The more applications depend on the same infrastructure,
the more valuable that infrastructure can become.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Chainlink has also pushed into cross-chain infrastructure
through CCIP, positioning the protocol as a connectivity layer between
different blockchain environments and traditional financial systems. &lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That doesn't mean competitors cannot challenge Chainlink.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;They can, and they do.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;But the longer a protocol remains deeply integrated into
applications and institutional experiments, the harder it becomes for a new
competitor to win simply by offering a similar product.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That's the difference between having a good product and becoming
part of the industry's infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Zcash: Privacy Creates a Different Kind of Lock-In&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Zcash represents a completely different idea.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Its moat isn't primarily about being the largest
cryptocurrency or providing infrastructure to other applications.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;It's about privacy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Most major public blockchains are transparent by design.
Transactions can be examined on-chain, and depending on the network, balances
and transaction histories can be analyzed by anyone with the right tools.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Zcash offers another model.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The network supports both transparent and shielded
transactions. With shielded transactions, cryptographic technology can hide
transaction details such as addresses and amounts from public view while still
allowing the network to verify that the transaction is valid. &lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That distinction is important because Zcash isn't simply
an entirely invisible blockchain.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Users can make transparent transactions too.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The privacy advantage exists when users actually use the
shielded system and follow practices that protect their privacy. Zcash's own
documentation also warns that metadata and other information can create privacy
leaks, meaning privacy isn't something that can be treated as a magic switch. &lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Still, the underlying idea creates an interesting
competitive advantage.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Privacy is difficult to add after the fact.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;A blockchain built around completely transparent
transactions can't necessarily become a privacy-first network simply by adding
a new feature. Privacy involves cryptography, wallet design, transaction
architecture, liquidity, user behavior and, importantly, the size of the
anonymity set.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That's why privacy can create a different kind of network
effect.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;In a January 2026 analysis, a16z crypto argued that
privacy could become one of the strongest moats in crypto because private
information is harder to move between networks than ordinary tokens. Its
argument is essentially that moving assets between chains can be relatively
straightforward, while moving an established privacy ecosystem without exposing
information is much harder. &lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That's a compelling idea.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;And it helps explain why privacy-focused networks could
become increasingly important if more financial activity moves on-chain.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The challenge for Zcash is that having strong privacy
technology isn't automatically the same thing as having mass adoption.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;It still needs users, liquidity, wallets, exchanges,
developers and applications.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;So Zcash's moat should not be described as “unbreakable.”&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;It's better described as specialized technological
differentiation combined with the possibility of privacy-driven network effects.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That is a much more defensible argument.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What Actually Makes a Crypto Moat Strong?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Looking at these three projects side by side reveals
something interesting.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Their advantages are completely different.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin: Network Effects&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin's biggest advantage is the enormous ecosystem
that has developed around it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Its code can be copied.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Its network cannot.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The combination of liquidity, recognition,
infrastructure, holders, institutional adoption and a long operating history
creates a powerful barrier for competitors.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Chainlink: Infrastructure Dependence&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Chainlink's moat comes from becoming infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;When a protocol provides critical services to
applications and institutions, replacing it isn't as simple as downloading
another piece of software.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The more integrations it accumulates, the more difficult
switching can become.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Zcash: Privacy and Specialized Technology&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Zcash takes a different route.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Its differentiation comes from privacy technology and the
ecosystem built around it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;If privacy becomes an increasingly important requirement
for on-chain finance, specialized privacy networks could benefit from strong
network effects of their own.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;No Crypto Moat Is Truly Permanent&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;There is one important caveat.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Calling any crypto project “unassailable” is probably too
strong.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Crypto moves too quickly for that.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Ethereum once looked almost impossible to challenge in
smart contracts. New layer-1 networks later attracted developers and liquidity.
DeFi protocols that dominated one cycle were replaced by new competitors in the
next.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Technology changes.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Regulation changes.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;User preferences change.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;And new business models can appear faster in crypto than
in almost any other financial technology market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;So the real question isn't whether Bitcoin, Chainlink or
Zcash can never be replaced.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;It's whether a competitor can offer enough additional
value to convince users, developers and institutions to abandon an ecosystem
that already works.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That's a much higher hurdle.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;And it is exactly where a strong moat matters.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Real Advantage Is Being Hard to Replace&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Crypto was built around open networks and permissionless
innovation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That means competition isn't going away.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Anyone can build another blockchain. Anyone can launch
another token. Developers can fork open-source code and experiment with new
designs.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;But a fork doesn't automatically inherit the things that
make an established network valuable.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin has spent years accumulating users, liquidity and
credibility.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Chainlink has spent years integrating its infrastructure
into the wider blockchain and financial ecosystem.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Zcash has spent years developing privacy technology
around a specific use case that most transparent blockchains were never
designed to solve.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Those are three different paths to defensibility.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;And that's perhaps the more useful way to think about
crypto moats.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The strongest projects aren't necessarily the ones with
the most features. They're the ones that would be the hardest for users,
developers and institutions to replace.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;In an industry where code can be copied overnight, that
may be the most valuable advantage of all.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

    <title>Gemini Secures Singapore MPI License for Crypto Services</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEg180GmYqmCPCBvy-QtXQDMR8MtsD1nB9XuN-ColgmlzXCiN1a2vV6ZqjYryNmD-1u5Dl9IxYSWxKtLWAa1nD1jWVEAY_8sSNvVpPlZzBUeJTjjI5eyOWZGG4r6GV78Vq1imxGEKyLH_cxsoXBbfFepvveUbfdydCWID-O2jri1236g8tPlDMC-RLTbTPkF/s1670/gemini-singapore-mpi-license-crypto-services.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Gemini secures Singapore MPI license for regulated crypto services" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1670" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEg180GmYqmCPCBvy-QtXQDMR8MtsD1nB9XuN-ColgmlzXCiN1a2vV6ZqjYryNmD-1u5Dl9IxYSWxKtLWAa1nD1jWVEAY_8sSNvVpPlZzBUeJTjjI5eyOWZGG4r6GV78Vq1imxGEKyLH_cxsoXBbfFepvveUbfdydCWID-O2jri1236g8tPlDMC-RLTbTPkF/w640-h360/gemini-singapore-mpi-license-crypto-services.jpg.png" title="Gemini Secures Singapore MPI License for Crypto Services" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;
&lt;strong&gt;Published:&lt;/strong&gt; September 9, 2026&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gemini has secured a &lt;strong&gt;Major Payment Institution (MPI) licence&lt;/strong&gt; from Singapore's Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), giving the cryptocurrency company full regulatory authorization for key payment and digital-asset activities in the country.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The licence was granted to &lt;strong&gt;Gemini Digital Payments Singapore, Pte. Ltd.&lt;/strong&gt; and became effective on &lt;strong&gt;September 1, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, according to Singapore's official financial institution directory. MAS lists the Gemini entity as a Major Payment Institution authorized for &lt;strong&gt;Digital Payment Token Service&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;Cross-border Money Transfer Service&lt;/strong&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The approval is an important step for Gemini because it moves the company beyond the in-principle approval it previously held and gives its Singapore operation a full local licence under the country's payments framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Gemini Moves From In-Principle Approval to Full Singapore Licence&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest development completes a licensing process that Gemini began several years ago.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In October 2024, Gemini announced that it had received &lt;strong&gt;in-principle approval&lt;/strong&gt; from MAS for a Major Payment Institution licence. That approval covered digital payment token services and cross-border money transfer services, but it was not the same as holding the final licence. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gemini subsequently transitioned its Singapore customers to Gemini Digital Payments Singapore in April 2025 while the company continued working toward full licensing. At the time, Gemini described the entity as having MAS in-principle approval. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That status has now changed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;MAS's current directory lists Gemini Digital Payments Singapore as an active Major Payment Institution, with the relevant payment services shown on the regulator's official database. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does Gemini's MPI Licence Allow?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A Major Payment Institution licence is a regulatory authorization under Singapore's payments framework. It allows a licensed institution to conduct regulated &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-bitcoin-transaction-be-reversed-if.html"&gt;payment services&lt;/a&gt; within the scope approved by MAS.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Gemini's Singapore entity, the regulator currently lists two relevant activities:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Digital Payment Token Service&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Cross-border Money Transfer Service&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;MAS explains that Major Payment Institutions are subject to more comprehensive regulatory requirements than standard payment institutions because of the larger scale and risks associated with their operations. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The licence therefore provides Gemini with a regulated foundation for its Singapore digital-asset and payment-related activities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;This Is Not a Banking Licence&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One important distinction is worth making clear: &lt;strong&gt;Gemini has not become a bank in Singapore.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An MPI licence is a payments licence, not a conventional banking licence. It authorizes specified regulated payment services and does not mean Gemini has the same regulatory status as a commercial bank.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The approval also does not guarantee the value or &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-i-generate-same-bitcoin-address.html"&gt;performance&lt;/a&gt; of any cryptocurrency offered through the platform.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, the significance of the licence is that Gemini's Singapore entity is now operating under the country's formal payments regulatory framework for the services covered by its authorization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Singapore Is Important for Gemini&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Singapore has positioned itself as a major financial and technology hub in Asia while maintaining a relatively detailed regulatory framework for digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For global crypto companies, that combination makes Singapore an important market but also one where regulatory authorization matters.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gemini's full MPI licence gives the company a clearer regulatory footing as it continues serving customers in the country.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It also comes at a time when crypto exchanges are increasingly building regulated operations in individual jurisdictions rather than relying only on licences or registrations from other markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Gemini's Singapore Entity Handles Local Operations&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gemini Digital Payments Singapore was established as the local entity responsible for the company's Singapore operations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gemini had already moved Singapore customers from Gemini Trust Company to the Singapore entity in April 2025 as part of its licensing process. The company said the transition did not change customers' crypto holdings or fiat funds. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The transition also meant that Singapore customers would be managed under the local Gemini entity rather than the U.S.-based Gemini Trust Company.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With the full MPI licence now in place, that local regulatory structure has moved into a more established phase.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the Licence Means for Gemini Customers&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Singapore customers, the most important change is the regulatory status of the entity providing the relevant services.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of operating only under an earlier exemption and in-principle approval arrangement, Gemini Digital Payments Singapore is now listed by MAS as a Major Payment Institution.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not remove the normal risks associated with &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/cronos-recovers-1112m-after-tectonic.html"&gt;crypto markets&lt;/a&gt;. Bitcoin and other digital assets can still experience significant price volatility, and users remain responsible for understanding the products they use.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Regulation should therefore not be confused with a guarantee against investment losses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Gemini's Expansion Into Regulated Crypto Markets&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Singapore approval fits into a broader trend among major cryptocurrency companies: establishing regulated entities in key financial centers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For exchanges, local licensing can provide a clearer framework for dealing with customers, financial institutions and other businesses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It can also make the regulatory status of specific services easier for customers to understand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gemini's latest Singapore approval is particularly notable because the licence covers both digital payment token services and cross-border money transfer services.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is a Digital Payment Token Service?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Singapore uses the term &lt;strong&gt;Digital Payment Token (DPT)&lt;/strong&gt; within its regulatory framework for certain crypto and digital-token activities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gemini's MPI licence specifically includes Digital Payment Token Service, according to MAS's official financial institution directory. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This does not mean every digital asset or every possible crypto product is automatically approved. Specific services and tokens remain subject to applicable regulatory requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For users, the key point is that Gemini's Singapore entity is now licensed for the regulated DPT activity identified by MAS.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Cross-Border Money Transfer Service Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The second licensed activity is &lt;strong&gt;Cross-border Money Transfer Service&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is notable because crypto markets increasingly overlap with international payments and money movement. Stablecoins, digital assets and blockchain-based payment infrastructure are being explored for faster cross-border transfers, although their regulatory treatment varies by jurisdiction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gemini's authorization gives its Singapore entity a regulated basis for the cross-border money transfer service listed by MAS. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It does not mean every cross-border crypto payment product Gemini could potentially develop is automatically approved. Any new service would still need to comply with the applicable regulatory framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Gemini Had Already Built a Singapore Presence&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new licence does not represent Gemini's first entry into Singapore.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company has been building its Singapore operation for several years, including the creation of Gemini Digital Payments Singapore and the transfer of Singapore customers to the local entity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gemini's earlier licensing announcement in 2024 described the MPI approval as part of its effort to expand its regulated presence in the region. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The full licence now gives that strategy a more definitive regulatory milestone.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Could Come Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The licence creates room for Gemini to continue developing its regulated Singapore business, but the approval itself does not announce a specific new product launch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company's next steps could involve expanding services that fit within its licensed activities, strengthening institutional relationships or developing additional payment-related infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, those possibilities should not be presented as confirmed plans unless Gemini or MAS announces them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the confirmed development is straightforward: Gemini Digital Payments Singapore has received the full MPI licence and is listed by MAS for Digital Payment Token and Cross-border Money Transfer services.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What This Means for the Wider Crypto Industry&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gemini's approval is another example of the cryptocurrency industry moving toward jurisdiction-specific regulation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Rather than treating crypto as a single global regulatory market, large exchanges increasingly need to meet different licensing requirements in different countries.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Singapore's decision is therefore relevant beyond Gemini itself. It shows how an established financial center is incorporating regulated digital-asset activities into its existing payments framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For crypto businesses, the message is clear: regulatory infrastructure is becoming an increasingly important part of international expansion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Did Gemini receive a crypto licence in Singapore?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Gemini Digital Payments Singapore, Pte. Ltd. has received a Major Payment Institution licence from Singapore's Monetary Authority of Singapore. MAS lists the entity as an MPI. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;When did Gemini's Singapore MPI licence become effective?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The licence became effective on September 1, 2026, according to the regulatory information associated with Gemini's Singapore licence. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What services are covered by Gemini's Singapore licence?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;MAS lists Digital Payment Token Service and Cross-border Money Transfer Service for Gemini Digital Payments Singapore. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Did Gemini previously have approval in Singapore?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Gemini received in-principle approval for an MPI licence in October 2024 and later transitioned Singapore customers to its local entity while working toward full licensing. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does the Singapore MPI licence make Gemini a bank?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. An MPI licence is a payments authorization and does not give Gemini the status of a conventional commercial bank.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does the licence guarantee crypto investors' funds?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. Regulatory licensing does not eliminate cryptocurrency price, technology or market risks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does Gemini's licence mean every crypto product is approved in Singapore?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. The authorization applies to the regulated services covered by the licence. Individual products and activities remain subject to applicable laws and regulatory requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Gemini has secured a full Major Payment Institution licence in Singapore, strengthening the exchange's regulated presence in one of Asia's key financial markets.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The licence was granted to Gemini Digital Payments Singapore and is effective from September 1, 2026. MAS lists the entity for Digital Payment Token Service and Cross-border Money Transfer Service. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The development is especially significant because it completes Gemini's move from the in-principle approval it received in 2024 to a full local payment licence.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Gemini, Singapore now provides a clearer regulatory foundation for its digital-asset and payment operations. For the wider crypto market, the approval highlights the growing importance of regulated local entities as exchanges expand across major financial centers.&lt;/p&gt;
