color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The exchange emphasized that the September 24 incident did not impact its reserves. PoR updates will continue monthly, as they have since December 2022.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What Happened on September 24&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Attackers moved approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;$351.6 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; in assets from Bitget's hot and warm wallets. The stolen assets included ETH, XRP, BNB, AVAX, USDT, and USDC across multiple blockchains.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Chen said the attacker compromised a critical backend system within the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/spacecoins-parent-company-signs-50m-pre.html"&gt;wallet &lt;/a&gt;infrastructure, used it to spoof transaction data, and triggered the exchange's authorization process to move funds. Importantly, she stated that &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;private keys were not compromised&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;cold wallets remained unaffected&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Bitget engaged cybersecurity firms &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Mandiant&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;SlowMist&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; to assist with the investigation, alongside law enforcement agencies.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Investigation Continues&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Chen has said the attack method is "highly consistent with known patterns of North Korean hacker organizations," citing IP behavior patterns and on-chain analysis.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Blockchain analytics firm &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Elliptic&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; assessed the incident as "highly likely" linked to North Korea, noting infrastructure overlaps with previous DPRK-attributed exploits including the 2025 Bybit hack. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;TRM Labs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; similarly pointed to on-chain links with previously identified North Korean thefts.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The Bitget incident pushed Elliptic's tracked total of DPRK-attributed crypto theft in 2026 past &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;$1 billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;However, definitive attribution has not been publicly confirmed. Bitget's initial security notice said the company would not speculate on the attack vector until the investigation was complete.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What This Means for Bitget Users&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;For users, the immediate concern — access to funds — is nearly resolved. By Friday, all withdrawal channels will be operational.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The bigger question is trust. Bitget's rapid response — replenishing the Protection Fund, resuming withdrawals in phases, and maintaining 131% PoR — has been faster than some peers in similar situations.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;But the incident also highlights a broader issue: the September 24 breach was not a private key theft. It was a backend compromise that manipulated the exchange's own authorization systems. That's a different kind of failure, and it raises questions about operational security that go beyond cold storage.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Is Bitget's Protection Fund fully replenished?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Yes. It's back above $300 million, with the official page showing $309 million and 3,705 BTC in the fund wallet.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;When will all withdrawals resume?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;P2P, all remaining assets, and fiat withdrawals open Friday, October 2, at 8:00 AM UTC.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What is Bitget's Proof of Reserves ratio?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;131% as of the September 29 snapshot, covering 19 assets. All covered assets are above 100%.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Was North Korea behind the attack?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Multiple analytics firms have assessed it as "highly likely" linked to DPRK, but definitive attribution has not been publicly confirmed.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What was the attack method?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;A backend system compromise that allowed the attacker to spoof transaction data and trigger Bitget's authorization process. Private keys were not compromised.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin-bottom: 0px !important; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 16px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Bottom line:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; Bitget is nearly back to full operations. The Protection Fund is replenished, Proof of Reserves is above 131%, and withdrawals resume fully on Friday. The exchange moved quickly to stabilize — but the North Korea investigation continues, and the backend compromise raises operational security questions that won't be resolved by a fund balance alone.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>

    <title>AI Trading Agents Are Already Here — But Not How You Think</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgv_WtSxmL9kjW3fu-W3qyr4RKGZSFYj2AuBgzNIRQ03JPM7OGyrTOp3RwUXWlkQm-oOVCnRlbeJCRrvcayyNFvnwffUfJcWwHX_WFqooRpryZt397GaGqeQP5PxM2cq00Acd0VJGAk1Wj5BFZRar3VSrw8JhpKUMykMHPtrYZK0ARI0v9ofHqjPfTnlMiR/s1672/ai-trading-agents-institutional-crypto-markets-2026.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="AI trading agent assisting a human professional with supervised cryptocurrency trading and institutional market analysis" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgv_WtSxmL9kjW3fu-W3qyr4RKGZSFYj2AuBgzNIRQ03JPM7OGyrTOp3RwUXWlkQm-oOVCnRlbeJCRrvcayyNFvnwffUfJcWwHX_WFqooRpryZt397GaGqeQP5PxM2cq00Acd0VJGAk1Wj5BFZRar3VSrw8JhpKUMykMHPtrYZK0ARI0v9ofHqjPfTnlMiR/w400-h225/ai-trading-agents-institutional-crypto-markets-2026.jpg.png" title="AI Trading Agents Enter Institutional Crypto Markets" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/i&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Ask most people about AI trading agents in crypto, and
you'll get one of two answers. Either it's all hype — a buzzword that VCs use
to pump their portfolios. Or it's a terrifying future where robots take over
Wall Street.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The truth, as usual, sits somewhere in between.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Here's what's actually happening right now:&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;AI
agents are being deployed by institutional players, but not in the "set it
and forget it" way you might imagine.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Where the Rubber Actually Meets the Road&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The clearest evidence comes from Sygnum Bank, a regulated
Swiss &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/openai-sets-2027-ipo-target-cfo-says-we.html"&gt;digital asset&lt;/a&gt; bank. In May 2026, they completed what they called the
first set of live AI-agent-driven digital asset transactions by a regulated
bank.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Here's the critical detail: it wasn't autonomous.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The pilot used a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;"human-in-the-loop"&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;model.
A client issued plain-text instructions — like "swap this stablecoin for
that token" — and the AI independently planned the steps, reviewed smart
contracts, flagged risks, and presented each transaction for client approval.
Private keys never left the client's self-custodial wallet.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The architecture used an in-house Model Context Protocol
(MCP) server with Anthropic's Claude as the underlying model. According to
Sygnum's announcement, the MCP-based architecture is described as
model-agnostic and asset-class agnostic, allowing the infrastructure to scale
as the ecosystem develops.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It can currently handle stablecoin transfers, asset swaps,
on-chain lending, token wrapping, and liquidity provisioning.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;real institutional adoption&lt;/b&gt;, but with
training wheels on. Production deployment is still subject to full regulatory,
compliance, and security reviews.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Exchange Layer Is Opening Up&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Meanwhile, regulated exchanges are building infrastructure
specifically for AI-assisted and agentic trading.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;VALR&lt;/b&gt;, Africa's largest regulated &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/banks-rotating-into-ethereum-3x-faster.html"&gt;crypto exchange&lt;/a&gt;,
launched its AI Service in April 2026 — explicitly inviting autonomous AI
agents to open accounts, authenticate, and execute trades. They published an
open-source Agent Skills repository and built infrastructure compatible with
OpenClaw, Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex, and OpenCode.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The compliance architecture treats agent identity through
a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;"Know Your Agent" (KYA)&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;framework: agent identity
(who created it), authority binding (which human authorized it), runtime
controls (position limits, asset class restrictions), and tamper-evident audit
trails.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Revolut&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;connected its Revolut X exchange to
external AI assistants including Claude, Gemini, OpenClaw, and Cursor in June.
Users can analyze markets, test strategies, set alerts, and place orders
through natural-language prompts.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Gemini&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;moved in a similar direction in April
with Agentic Trading, allowing customers to connect AI agents such as Claude
and ChatGPT through the MCP protocol. Gemini described it as "the first
agentic trading tool to be available directly through a regulated US-based
exchange."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What Actually Works — And What Doesn't&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The honest scorecard on AI agents in crypto is more nuanced
than the marketing suggests.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Narrow agents with well-defined parameters&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;are
currently showing the clearest practical use cases. That's the Sygnum model:
assisted execution within strict guardrails, with human approval at every step.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Fully autonomous agents&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;still face significant
reliability challenges, particularly on complex multi-step workflows. The
technology continues to improve, but the transition from
"experimental" to "operational" is happening gradually —
not overnight.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why This Matters for Institutional Investors&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The key takeaway: AI agent technology is moving from
experimental to operational, but with&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;guardrails&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Institutional participation is happening through:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Assisted
     execution&lt;/b&gt;, not autonomous decision-making&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Human-in-the-loop
     models&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;where the client approves every transaction&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Controlled
     environments&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;with explicit position limits and asset restrictions&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Regulated
     exchanges&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;with KYA (Know Your Agent) frameworks&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan has projected that the convergence
of tokenized markets and autonomous AI agents could boost blockchain
transaction volumes by&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;10 to 100 times&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;current levels. This is
speculative — he offered no specific timeline or platforms — but it illustrates
where institutional thinkers see the trajectory heading.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Are AI trading agents actually being used by institutional
crypto investors?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Yes — but in a controlled, supervised capacity.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The
"wild west" vision of autonomous AI trading billions of dollars
without human oversight is still a ways off. But the infrastructure is being
built, the regulatory frameworks are being established, and the transaction
volume is already material.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The technology is transitioning from "hype" to
"operational reality" — just not as dramatically as the headlines
suggest.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

    <title>Bernstein Predicts $300,000 Bitcoin by 2029 — But There's a Catch</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;div class="article"&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgSMDXuCcy4AysSmewUq-wJopqgLJY5oO700UxWpMTCeDFnc_Q5xivdCCGfjrwsMVAA-9NvwLf77vmKRnJRWxrLO8ERSLHWjwXJlaq8F2pCMeBOWAPt5J2nI3uz_GuvzCgfRN02NaKbEmvZXa7HdjgmB3SfpH31ey5MDjrltlBKkJxCLx01baXr4ocZo4H-/s1672/bernstein-bitcoin-300k-2029-price-prediction.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin price forecast showing Bernstein's $300,000 target for 2029" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgSMDXuCcy4AysSmewUq-wJopqgLJY5oO700UxWpMTCeDFnc_Q5xivdCCGfjrwsMVAA-9NvwLf77vmKRnJRWxrLO8ERSLHWjwXJlaq8F2pCMeBOWAPt5J2nI3uz_GuvzCgfRN02NaKbEmvZXa7HdjgmB3SfpH31ey5MDjrltlBKkJxCLx01baXr4ocZo4H-/w400-h225/bernstein-bitcoin-300k-2029-price-prediction.jpg.png" title="Bernstein Predicts $300,000 Bitcoin by 2029" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&amp;nbsp;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin could climb to &lt;strong&gt;$300,000 by 2029&lt;/strong&gt;, according to a new forecast from Bernstein — but the firm's base case is only part of the story.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Wall Street research firm expects Bitcoin to reach around &lt;strong&gt;$125,000 by the end of 2026&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;$150,000 by mid-2027&lt;/strong&gt;, before potentially reaching $300,000 during the next major cycle in 2029.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bernstein's more aggressive scenario is considerably higher. If institutional demand accelerates and investors increasingly turn to Bitcoin as a hedge against currency debasement, the cryptocurrency could potentially reach &lt;strong&gt;$500,000 in 2029&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The difference between those two scenarios is important. The $300,000 figure is the firm's base case, while $500,000 represents a much more bullish outcome.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Bernstein Is Bullish on Bitcoin&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bernstein's argument goes beyond Bitcoin's traditional four-year market cycle.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The firm believes the global economic backdrop could become increasingly favorable for scarce assets as governments deal with high debt levels and rising borrowing costs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The basic problem is straightforward. Higher interest rates increase the cost of servicing government debt. If fiscal deficits remain large, policymakers face difficult choices between spending cuts, higher taxes, restructuring debt or allowing inflation and currency depreciation to reduce the real burden.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bernstein's view is that policymakers may ultimately lean toward &lt;strong&gt;currency debasement rather than severe fiscal austerity&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could create a stronger investment case for assets whose supply cannot be expanded at will.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin is one of the clearest examples.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Its supply is capped by its underlying protocol, making it fundamentally different from fiat currencies that can be expanded through monetary policy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bernstein's Bitcoin Price Targets&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The firm's latest outlook gives investors several milestones to watch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); margin: 20px 0px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Timeline&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Price Target&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;End of 2026&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;~$125,000&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Mid-2027&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;~$150,000&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;2029 Base Case&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;~$300,000&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;2029 Accelerated Case&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Up to ~$500,000&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;End of 2033&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;~$1 million&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The $1 million target is Bernstein's longer-term forecast and is separate from the firm's 2029 base case.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters because headlines around Bitcoin forecasts can sometimes make an aggressive scenario sound like the firm's primary expectation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In this case, Bernstein's central 2029 target remains approximately &lt;strong&gt;$300,000&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Bet: Currency Debasement&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Perhaps the most important part of Bernstein's thesis is its belief that governments may have limited room to pursue aggressive fiscal tightening.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The firm's analysts argue that decades of declining interest rates helped governments accumulate large amounts of debt at relatively low borrowing costs. That environment has changed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With rates and debt-servicing expenses higher, the cost of maintaining those obligations becomes more significant.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bernstein believes this could eventually encourage policymakers to tolerate higher inflation or currency depreciation rather than accept the economic and political consequences of aggressive austerity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Bitcoin investors, that is potentially significant.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If investors believe their traditional currencies are gradually losing purchasing power, they may look for assets that are scarce and difficult to dilute.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's fixed issuance makes it a natural candidate for that trade.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But this is still a macroeconomic thesis, not a guaranteed outcome.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Institutional Investors Could Be the Difference&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's investor base has changed dramatically compared with previous market cycles.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Spot Bitcoin ETFs have made it easier for traditional investors to gain exposure without directly managing wallets or private keys. Corporate treasury strategies have also created another route for institutions and companies to accumulate BTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bernstein believes this institutional participation could alter the behavior of future &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bill-gates-seeks-xi-jinping-meeting-to.html?m=1"&gt;Bitcoin cycles&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Earlier Bitcoin markets were heavily influenced by retail speculation and could experience enormous drawdowns after major rallies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The growing presence of institutional capital could potentially make the market deeper and reduce the likelihood of some of the extreme boom-and-bust moves seen in previous cycles.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not mean Bitcoin will stop experiencing major corrections.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, the argument is that the market may now have a larger base of investors willing to buy during periods of weakness.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin's Recent Recovery Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bernstein's forecast also comes after a significant Bitcoin correction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The firm's analysts highlighted a roughly &lt;strong&gt;50% decline from Bitcoin's October 2025 peak&lt;/strong&gt; before the subsequent recovery.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin then posted a strong short-term rebound, gaining roughly &lt;strong&gt;28% over a 10-day period&lt;/strong&gt; in the period covered by Bernstein's analysis.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the firm, the recovery is another indication that Bitcoin's market structure may be changing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Previous cycles often featured dramatic declines after major peaks. With ETFs, corporate buyers and other institutional investors now involved, Bernstein expects future corrections could become less severe.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That remains one of the key questions for the next phase of the market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The $500,000 Scenario&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most eye-catching number in Bernstein's outlook is arguably &lt;strong&gt;$500,000&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, investors should not confuse it with the firm's base case.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bernstein sees the possibility of Bitcoin reaching roughly &lt;strong&gt;$200,000 by mid-2027&lt;/strong&gt; and potentially peaking around $500,000 in 2029 if institutional capital moves aggressively into the cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That would require a much stronger demand environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In other words, Bitcoin would need more than just a continuation of its historical cycle. It would need substantial institutional flows and a broader macroeconomic shift toward scarce assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The scenario is therefore better understood as an upside case than as Bernstein's expected outcome.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the Forecast Means for Strategy&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bernstein has also updated its outlook for &lt;strong&gt;Strategy&lt;/strong&gt;, the company known for maintaining a large Bitcoin treasury.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The firm kept its &lt;strong&gt;Outperform&lt;/strong&gt; rating but reduced its price target from &lt;strong&gt;$450 to $350&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Strategy's &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/posco-international-expands-blockchain.html"&gt;Bitcoin holdings&lt;/a&gt; make its stock particularly sensitive to movements in BTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bernstein's analysis noted that Strategy held &lt;strong&gt;840,447 BTC&lt;/strong&gt;, representing roughly 4% of Bitcoin's total supply at the time of the analysis.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The firm also estimated that the company had around &lt;strong&gt;3.9 years of cash coverage&lt;/strong&gt; for annual interest and preferred-dividend obligations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If Bitcoin continues to rise and Strategy's preferred securities recover, Bernstein believes the company could once again become more aggressive in purchasing Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could create another source of institutional demand for BTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why $300,000 Isn't Guaranteed&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is an obvious catch to any long-term Bitcoin price forecast: the market does not have to follow historical patterns.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's previous cycles produced extraordinary percentage gains, but each successive cycle has generally required more capital to generate similar increases in market value.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The cryptocurrency is also now much larger than it was during its early years.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a different challenge for future rallies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A move from $30,000 to $60,000 requires far less additional market value than a move from $150,000 to $300,000.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As Bitcoin grows, the amount of capital needed to push the price substantially higher also increases.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That doesn't make $300,000 impossible. It simply means the path is likely to become more demanding as the asset matures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Could Push Bitcoin Higher?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Several factors could support Bernstein's bullish scenario.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Institutional ETF demand&lt;/strong&gt; could provide a steady source of buying pressure if inflows remain strong.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Corporate Bitcoin accumulation&lt;/strong&gt; could add another layer of demand, particularly if more companies follow treasury strategies similar to Strategy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Monetary policy&lt;/strong&gt; could also become important. Lower real yields or renewed concerns about currency purchasing power could make scarce assets more attractive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Regulatory developments&lt;/strong&gt; are another variable. A clearer regulatory environment could make it easier for traditional financial institutions to offer Bitcoin-related products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;None of these factors operates independently, however.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A major deterioration in global liquidity or a sharp decline in investor risk appetite could overwhelm bullish fundamentals in the short term.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Investors Should Watch Next&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Rather than focusing only on the $300,000 headline, investors may want to watch the underlying signals behind Bernstein's thesis.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ETF inflows and outflows can provide clues about institutional demand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's behavior during major market corrections can show whether the market is becoming more resilient.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Interest rates, inflation expectations and government debt levels can reveal whether the broader debasement argument is gaining or losing momentum.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And perhaps most importantly, Bitcoin will need to continue attracting &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/mistral-partners-with-saudi-backed.html"&gt;capital&lt;/a&gt; as its market capitalization becomes larger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The $300,000 target is therefore less about one magic number and more about whether these trends continue moving in the same direction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bernstein expects Bitcoin to reach &lt;strong&gt;$300,000 by 2029&lt;/strong&gt; under its base case, with a potential path toward &lt;strong&gt;$150,000 by mid-2027&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;$125,000 by the end of 2026&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The firm's more aggressive scenario puts Bitcoin as high as &lt;strong&gt;$500,000 in 2029&lt;/strong&gt;, while its longer-term outlook remains around &lt;strong&gt;$1 million by 2033&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the real story behind those numbers is the firm's macroeconomic thesis.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bernstein is betting that high government debt, rising debt-servicing costs and concerns about currency purchasing power could push investors toward scarce assets such as Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That thesis could prove powerful if institutional demand continues growing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It could also weaken if governments manage to stabilize their finances without relying heavily on inflation or currency depreciation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, Bernstein's forecast is best viewed as a long-term scenario rather than a promise. The path to $300,000 will depend heavily on what happens beyond the crypto market itself — and whether policymakers choose debasement over austerity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice. Cryptocurrency markets are highly volatile, and analyst forecasts are estimates rather than guarantees of future prices.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Cronos Recovers $111.2M After Tectonic Exploit, $9.19M Remains Unrecovered</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhE7c6bINeZ_5219y9eo71JnOQCifznY2UwWaGL4qa0Kba3t5I4P3u_bLaB_I_5c5rIZvniu9AdmbidpGNncwqMrTs2394-MTZd_sc60BZteHNK7sVeYvcK4mRfzOR2kmmn9bEWv3gRy-zHGLcKbnA6FfbigeIgRfPmhePBMsVXq0QwbhpkeS5tsByNpFXD/s1672/cronos-tectonic-exploit-111-million-recovery.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Cronos Tectonic exploit and $111.2 million recovery after blockchain rollback" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhE7c6bINeZ_5219y9eo71JnOQCifznY2UwWaGL4qa0Kba3t5I4P3u_bLaB_I_5c5rIZvniu9AdmbidpGNncwqMrTs2394-MTZd_sc60BZteHNK7sVeYvcK4mRfzOR2kmmn9bEWv3gRy-zHGLcKbnA6FfbigeIgRfPmhePBMsVXq0QwbhpkeS5tsByNpFXD/w640-h360/cronos-tectonic-exploit-111-million-recovery.jpg.png" title="Cronos Recovers $111.2M After Tectonic Exploit" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;
September 8, 2026&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Cronos has released its post-mortem on the August 30 Tectonic exploit, detailing how validators rolled the blockchain back to recover most of the funds affected by the attack.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to the post-mortem, approximately &lt;strong&gt;$120.4 million was borrowed across nine Tectonic markets&lt;/strong&gt; during the exploit. Cronos says about &lt;strong&gt;$111.2 million&lt;/strong&gt; was recovered through the rollback, while approximately &lt;strong&gt;$9.19 million&lt;/strong&gt; had already left the Cronos network before block production was halted and remains unrecovered. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The distinction matters because the $120.4 million figure should not be described as the amount permanently stolen. Most of the affected value remained on Cronos and could be reversed when validators restored the chain to its pre-exploit state.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happened in the Cronos Tectonic Exploit?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The incident involved &lt;strong&gt;Tectonic&lt;/strong&gt;, a decentralized lending protocol operating on the Cronos blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The attacker manipulated the price of &lt;strong&gt;TONIC&lt;/strong&gt;, Tectonic's relatively thinly traded token. The inflated valuation was then used as collateral inside the lending protocol, increasing the amount the attacker could borrow.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to Cronos' post-mortem, the attacker ultimately borrowed approximately &lt;strong&gt;$120.4 million across nine lending markets&lt;/strong&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In simple terms, the exploit took advantage of the relationship between &lt;strong&gt;collateral value and borrowing power&lt;/strong&gt;. When the protocol accepted an artificially inflated price for the collateral, the attacker's position appeared capable of supporting much larger loans than the underlying asset would normally justify.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Much Did Cronos Recover?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cronos says validators rolled the blockchain back to &lt;strong&gt;block 90,896,188&lt;/strong&gt;, the last block before the exploit.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The rollback reversed approximately &lt;strong&gt;$111.2 million&lt;/strong&gt; that remained within the Cronos ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, approximately &lt;strong&gt;$9.19 million had already left Cronos&lt;/strong&gt; before validators halted block production. That amount could not be recovered simply by rewriting Cronos' own chain history. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;1 hour 54 minutes&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Approximate period of blockchain history reversed&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Did Cronos Roll Back the Blockchain?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The rollback was an emergency response designed to recover assets that were still recorded on the Cronos network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of allowing the compromised state to remain permanently on-chain, Cronos validators restored the chain to the last block before the exploit.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This meant that the affected borrowing activity could be reversed along with the other transactions recorded during the rollback window.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It was an unusual decision because blockchain users generally expect confirmed transactions to remain part of the chain's history.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cronos therefore faced a difficult choice: preserve transaction history and finality, or reverse a portion of the chain to recover a much larger amount of funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The validators chose the rollback option. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why $9.19M Could Not Be Recovered by the Rollback&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blockchain rollback can change the state of the blockchain being rolled back. It cannot automatically reverse assets that have already moved outside that network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is what happened to approximately &lt;strong&gt;$9.19 million&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those funds had already left Cronos before validators stopped block production. Once they were outside the chain's rollback window, restoring Cronos to an earlier block could not simply bring them back. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The remaining recovery effort therefore depends on tracing the funds and coordinating with exchanges, bridges and other services that may have interacted with them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Rollback Removed 10,961 Blocks&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The scale of Cronos' response becomes clearer when looking at the blockchain history that was reversed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Validators removed approximately &lt;strong&gt;10,961 blocks&lt;/strong&gt;, representing about &lt;strong&gt;one hour and 54 minutes&lt;/strong&gt; of Cronos history.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That history did not contain only Tectonic-related transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Other transactions made during the affected period were also reversed because the chain was restored to its pre-exploit state.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This creates an important lesson about emergency &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/senate-crypto-bill-faces-september-15.html"&gt;blockchain&lt;/a&gt; interventions: recovering stolen or exploited assets can sometimes require making decisions that affect users who were not involved in the attack.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How TONIC Price Manipulation Created Borrowing Power&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The attack demonstrates why price feeds are such an important part of DeFi lending.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A lending protocol needs to know how much a user's collateral is worth before deciding how much that user can borrow.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If an asset's price is artificially inflated, the protocol can mistakenly believe that a relatively small collateral position supports a much larger loan.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In the Cronos incident, the attacker manipulated the price of TONIC and then used the inflated valuation to borrow assets from multiple Tectonic markets. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The underlying problem was therefore not simply the market price of TONIC. It was the connection between that price, collateral valuation and the amount of capital the lending protocol allowed the attacker to borrow.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Low-Liquidity Tokens Can Create DeFi Risk&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Thinly traded tokens can be particularly sensitive to large orders or other forms of market manipulation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For a lending protocol, that creates a dangerous possibility: the token's displayed market price can rise dramatically even though there may not be enough real liquidity to sell a large position anywhere near that price.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the lending system accepts the manipulated valuation without sufficient safeguards, the attacker may gain borrowing power that is much larger than the collateral's realistic liquidation value.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ledger-cto-charles-guillemet-warns-ai.html"&gt;DeFi protocols&lt;/a&gt; commonly consider factors such as collateral ratios, borrowing caps, market liquidity, oracle design and isolated lending markets when managing risk.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Was the Entire $120.4M Stolen?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the most important details in the Cronos post-mortem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The approximately $120.4 million figure represents the value borrowed during the exploit. It does not mean that the attacker permanently removed $120.4 million from Cronos.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Most of the affected value—approximately &lt;strong&gt;$111.2 million&lt;/strong&gt;—was still within reach of the network's emergency rollback.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Approximately &lt;strong&gt;$9.19 million&lt;/strong&gt; had already left Cronos and remained outside the rollback's reach. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;When Did Cronos Halt the Network?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The response window was critical because the attacker was able to move part of the borrowed funds before validators halted block production.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cronos' timeline shows that the attack progressed rapidly from the initial manipulation of TONIC to borrowing across multiple Tectonic markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;By the time validators stopped the chain, the approximately $9.19 million that had already left Cronos could no longer be recovered simply by restoring the earlier chain state. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The network later resumed after the pre-exploit state was restored.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happened to Unrelated Cronos Transactions?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because the rollback restored the entire chain to an earlier &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-is-my-bitcoin-transaction-still_0394756778.html"&gt;block&lt;/a&gt;, it affected more than the transactions directly connected to Tectonic.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Transactions recorded during the approximately one-hour-and-54-minute rollback window were reversed as part of the restoration process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the biggest practical consequences of the incident for ordinary Cronos users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;While the rollback helped recover the majority of the affected funds, it also meant that users and applications had to reconcile transactions that had existed on the chain before the rollback.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does the Exploit Mean for Cronos Users?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The immediate emergency response has already restored the chain to its pre-exploit state, and Cronos has resumed block production.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, exchanges, bridges, indexers and other services may need to reconcile their own records after the rollback.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is particularly important for services that processed transactions during the period that was later removed from the chain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cronos says the affected ecosystem is continuing the reconciliation process. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does the Tectonic Exploit Mean for DeFi Security?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The incident highlights several layers of risk that DeFi users often overlook.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Price Oracle Risk&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If a protocol receives a manipulated price, its risk calculations can become inaccurate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Collateral Risk&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A token may appear valuable on a price feed while lacking enough real market liquidity to support that valuation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Borrowing Caps&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Limiting how much can be borrowed against a specific asset can reduce the damage from an oracle or market manipulation event.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Liquidity Risk&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A protocol needs to consider not just an asset's quoted price but whether sufficient liquidity exists to liquidate large positions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Emergency Controls&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Protocols can use circuit breakers or temporary borrowing restrictions when an asset's price behaves abnormally.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No single measure eliminates DeFi risk, but combining these controls can reduce the amount an attacker is able to extract before an abnormal event is detected.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens to the Remaining $9.19M?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The remaining $9.19 million is the unresolved portion of the incident.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because those funds had already left Cronos before the halt, the blockchain rollback cannot recover them by itself.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The remaining recovery process will therefore depend on blockchain tracing, cooperation from centralized services and other measures outside the rollback mechanism.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cronos has been working with exchanges, bridges and other ecosystem participants as part of the post-incident reconciliation process. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why This Incident Matters Beyond Cronos&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Tectonic exploit is a useful reminder that DeFi security is not determined by the underlying blockchain alone.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blockchain can continue operating according to its consensus rules while an application built on top of it suffers from a serious economic or oracle vulnerability.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For lending protocols, the most important questions often involve the entire risk chain:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Where does the asset price come from?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;How easily can that price be manipulated?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;How much can users borrow against the asset?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;How much real liquidity exists?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;How quickly can borrowing be paused?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Can the protocol isolate risky collateral from major markets?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Cronos incident shows why those questions matter before an exploit happens—not after.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How much was involved in the Cronos Tectonic exploit?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Approximately $120.4 million was borrowed across nine Tectonic markets during the exploit. Most of that value was subsequently recovered through the Cronos rollback. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How much did Cronos recover?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cronos recovered approximately $111.2 million through the rollback of the chain to its pre-exploit state.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How much was permanently lost or remains unrecovered?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Approximately $9.19 million had already left Cronos before validators halted the network and remains unrecovered according to the post-mortem reporting. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why did Cronos roll back the blockchain?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Validators rolled the chain back to a block immediately before the exploit so that affected assets still on Cronos could be restored to their earlier state.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How was TONIC involved?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The attacker manipulated the price of TONIC and used the inflated valuation as collateral, allowing substantially more assets to be borrowed from Tectonic markets. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Did Cronos reverse unrelated transactions?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Because the rollback removed a period of blockchain history rather than selectively reversing only exploit-related transactions, unrelated transactions in that window were also reversed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Cronos operating again?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Cronos resumed block production after restoring the pre-exploit chain state, with ecosystem services continuing reconciliation work.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Was this a Bitcoin or Ethereum hack?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. The incident involved the Tectonic lending protocol on Cronos. It was not an exploit of Bitcoin or Ethereum.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Cronos' Tectonic post-mortem shows that the August 30 exploit was large, but the amount permanently unrecovered was far smaller than the total value initially at risk.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Approximately &lt;strong&gt;$120.4 million was borrowed&lt;/strong&gt; through the exploit. Cronos' emergency rollback recovered about &lt;strong&gt;$111.2 million&lt;/strong&gt;, while approximately &lt;strong&gt;$9.19 million&lt;/strong&gt; had already left the network before validators halted the chain. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The response came with a significant cost: Cronos reversed approximately &lt;strong&gt;10,961 blocks covering about 1 hour and 54 minutes&lt;/strong&gt; of blockchain history, including transactions unrelated to the exploit.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the wider DeFi market, the incident reinforces a familiar but important lesson: &lt;strong&gt;an asset's quoted price is not necessarily the same as its real liquidation value.&lt;/strong&gt; Lending protocols must account for oracle manipulation, market liquidity, collateral limits and emergency controls when deciding how much users can borrow.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Sources&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href="https://coindoo.com/why-cronos-could-recover-tectonic-exploit/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;Coindoo — Cronos Rollback and Tectonic Exploit&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

    <title>Michael Saylor Calls Bitcoin’s “Most Profound Breakthrough” Its Digital Form of Economic Energy</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi0-m7ZBPYFQvVBDTZoM5kGRgvI_2zNMjH579pOshw-_14sJBcXFixLfjnPvFiuyGUakI2kK8J6PhBTzbtnM7QorG8HAT8y-OdZVW0C30EmWPrT697ypHx7mi2zae5vIfCET-zZh3f9wf9pRXAzTpicPxBRZbcn8PVD_uM1uX_iVl8SkdCOIgsV3gCLvlRd/s1672/michael-saylor-bitcoin-digital-economic-energy.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Illustration of Bitcoin representing economic energy in digital form, inspired by Michael Saylor’s Bitcoin thesis." border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi0-m7ZBPYFQvVBDTZoM5kGRgvI_2zNMjH579pOshw-_14sJBcXFixLfjnPvFiuyGUakI2kK8J6PhBTzbtnM7QorG8HAT8y-OdZVW0C30EmWPrT697ypHx7mi2zae5vIfCET-zZh3f9wf9pRXAzTpicPxBRZbcn8PVD_uM1uX_iVl8SkdCOIgsV3gCLvlRd/w400-h225/michael-saylor-bitcoin-digital-economic-energy.jpg.png" title="Michael Saylor’s Bitcoin Digital Economic Energy Concept" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;By CoinAINews Staff | &lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitcoin’s value proposition is often described in terms of
scarcity, decentralization and digital ownership. Strategy Executive Chairman
Michael Saylor has offered a different lens: &lt;b&gt;Bitcoin is digital economic
energy.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In an August 23 post on X, Saylor described &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/solanas-sgp-0002-vote-faster.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt;’s “most
profound breakthrough” as its ability to convert economic energy into digital
form and securely bind that value to a person, company, machine or nation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The statement adds another layer to Saylor’s long-running
argument that Bitcoin should be viewed as more than a payment network or
speculative asset. He has increasingly described BTC as a form of digital
monetary energy that can be stored, transferred and controlled without relying
on a central issuer.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What Saylor Means by “Economic Energy”&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The phrase “economic energy” is best understood as Saylor’s
conceptual description — &lt;b&gt;a metaphor, not a literal scientific or accounting
classification.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The idea is relatively straightforward. People and
organizations generate economic value through work, businesses, assets and
productive activity. Saylor argues that Bitcoin provides a way to represent
some of that value digitally while allowing ownership to remain under the
control of the holder.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Unlike physical assets such as property or commodities,
Bitcoin can be transferred globally through a digital network without
physically moving the underlying asset.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That portability is central to Saylor’s argument.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin as Digital Monetary Energy&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Saylor has used the “digital energy” concept repeatedly when
explaining why he believes Bitcoin is different from traditional forms of
wealth.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Gold, for example, can store value but requires physical
custody and transportation. Real estate can represent significant wealth but is
tied to a particular location. Traditional financial assets depend on legal and
institutional infrastructure to establish ownership and facilitate transfers.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitcoin approaches the problem differently.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Ownership is recorded on a decentralized blockchain, while
control of the coins depends on private cryptographic keys. This makes Bitcoin
digitally native while allowing holders to transfer value across borders
without physically transporting an asset.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Saylor’s latest statement essentially compresses that
argument into a single idea: &lt;b&gt;economic value can be represented in digital
form while remaining directly controllable by its owner.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why “Person, Company, Machine or Nation” Matters&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Saylor’s statement is also notable because he extends the
concept beyond individual Bitcoin holders.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitcoin can be held by individuals, corporations, investment
vehicles, institutions and governments. It can also be integrated into
automated systems and machines through digital &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bitcoin-in-2011-how-300k-could-move-btc.html"&gt;wallets&lt;/a&gt; and digital
infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That broadens the potential use case beyond personal
savings.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For companies, Bitcoin can function as a treasury asset. For
institutions, it can serve as an alternative form of reserve capital. For
governments, the concept raises questions about sovereign reserves and
long-term monetary strategy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The underlying Bitcoin network does not distinguish between
these categories of holders. Control ultimately comes down to the cryptographic
authorization required to move the coins.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Scarcity Is Part of the Argument&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The digital-energy thesis also depends heavily on Bitcoin’s
scarcity.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitcoin’s protocol limits the eventual supply to 21 million
coins. That fixed issuance schedule is one of the primary reasons Saylor
compares Bitcoin with scarce forms of property and monetary assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But scarcity alone does not guarantee value.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitcoin’s market price is determined by supply and demand,
while its usefulness depends on factors including network security, liquidity,
adoption, regulation and user confidence.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Saylor’s argument is therefore not simply that Bitcoin is
scarce. It is that scarcity combined with digital ownership and global
transferability creates a form of property that is difficult to replicate with
traditional assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;From Energy to Digital Value&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitcoin’s connection with energy is also literal at the
network level.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitcoin uses proof-of-work mining, in which specialized
computers perform computational work to secure the network and add new blocks.
Mining consumes electricity, making physical energy an important part of
Bitcoin’s security model.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Saylor’s “economic energy” description goes beyond that
technical relationship, however.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;He is describing the economic value represented by Bitcoin
rather than claiming that a bitcoin is literally a unit of electricity.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The distinction matters because “digital energy” is a
metaphor, not a physical claim about the nature of Bitcoin itself.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Strategy Has Put the Idea Into Practice&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Saylor’s Bitcoin thesis is closely connected to Strategy’s
corporate treasury strategy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The company has accumulated a large Bitcoin position over
several years, making its balance sheet one of the most prominent corporate
examples of a Bitcoin-focused treasury approach. Saylor remains Strategy’s
executive chairman and continues to be one of Bitcoin’s most vocal corporate
advocates.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That makes his latest comments more than an abstract
discussion.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Strategy’s own balance sheet is effectively an example of
the model Saylor describes: corporate capital has been converted into a digital
asset that can be held, transferred and independently verified on the Bitcoin
network.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;At the same time, the strategy carries market risk. Bitcoin
prices can fluctuate substantially, and a corporate treasury holding Bitcoin
remains exposed to those movements.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;A Different Way to Think About Bitcoin&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Saylor’s latest description is ultimately an attempt to
answer a bigger question: &lt;b&gt;What exactly is Bitcoin?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Depending on who is asked, Bitcoin can be described as
digital money, a decentralized settlement network, a scarce digital asset, a
store of value or a speculative investment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Saylor prefers a broader framing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In his view, Bitcoin represents a new way of storing
economic value in digital form while maintaining direct control over that
value. That makes portability, scarcity and ownership just as important to the
thesis as Bitcoin’s use as a payment mechanism.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Michael Saylor’s latest Bitcoin statement puts his
long-running thesis into a simple framework: &lt;b&gt;economic value can be converted
into digital form and securely attached to its owner.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Whether Bitcoin ultimately becomes the dominant form of
digital monetary property remains an open question. Its future will depend on
adoption, regulation, market liquidity, technological development and the
continued security of the network.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But Saylor’s “economic energy” concept highlights one of
Bitcoin’s defining characteristics: &lt;b&gt;it allows scarce digital value to exist
independently of a traditional physical location while remaining transferable
across a global network.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;For Saylor, that capability — not its price, not its
volatility — represents Bitcoin’s most profound breakthrough.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does
not constitute investment advice. Cryptocurrency markets are volatile, and
readers should conduct their own research before making investment decisions.&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>

    <title>Fasset Hits $1B Valuation After $68M SBI-Led Series C</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article style="line-height: 1.8; margin: 0px auto; max-width: 820px; padding: 20px;"&gt;

  &lt;h1 style="line-height: 1.25; margin: 0px 0px 12px;"&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhRjpb3ajVawksIT4GElfNr388PLASytC0tDcn1_5t3uU2g0UFdxDymMnQ-yrmpDoRr09kb-DDKW5AvlyxfHvMKA-uHfiaCr_WxZrT2KvC2KN_X_oOonvcezlcymk4C7dbroT5pjYVMA3_JNycWDB4bdJdb7nowLP41WpFoheaJHn6pnbEGA2fMOEHHIHYV/s1672/fasset-1-billion-valuation-sbi-68m-funding.jpg.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Fasset reaches a $1 billion valuation after a $68 million Series C funding round led by Japan's SBI Group" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhRjpb3ajVawksIT4GElfNr388PLASytC0tDcn1_5t3uU2g0UFdxDymMnQ-yrmpDoRr09kb-DDKW5AvlyxfHvMKA-uHfiaCr_WxZrT2KvC2KN_X_oOonvcezlcymk4C7dbroT5pjYVMA3_JNycWDB4bdJdb7nowLP41WpFoheaJHn6pnbEGA2fMOEHHIHYV/w400-h225/fasset-1-billion-valuation-sbi-68m-funding.jpg.png" title="Fasset Reaches $1 Billion Valuation After $68M SBI-Led Funding" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span face="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" style="color: #01ffff; font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1 style="line-height: 1.25; margin: 0px 0px 12px;"&gt;&lt;span face="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

  &lt;p style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; margin: 0px 0px 22px;"&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: 18px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;Fasset has reached a $1 billion valuation after raising $68 million in a Series C funding round led by Japan's SBI Group, pushing the stablecoin-focused neobanking platform into unicorn territory.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;
    The financing was announced on August 24, 2026, and follows Fasset's $51 million Series B round in May. The latest raise takes the company's total fundraising for 2026 to &lt;strong&gt;$119 million&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;
    Fasset says the new capital will be used to expand its regulated financial infrastructure, known as &lt;strong&gt;Own Network&lt;/strong&gt;, while increasing investment in AI-enabled systems for corridor banking, stablecoin settlement and tokenized assets.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2 style="border-left: 4px solid rgb(247, 147, 26); font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 24px; margin-top: 35px; padding-left: 12px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;
    Fasset Funding: Key Facts
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;div style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; margin: 20px 0px 28px; overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
    &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 15px; min-width: 600px; width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;thead&gt;

          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 13px 15px; text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;Details&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/thead&gt;

        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;Series C Funding&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;$68 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;

        &lt;tr style="background: rgb(245, 245, 245);"&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;Lead Investor&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;SBI Group, Japan&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;

        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;Private Valuation&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;$1 billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;

        &lt;tr style="background: rgb(245, 245, 245);"&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;2026 Funding Total&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;$119 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;

        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;Annualized Transaction Volume&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;More than $40 billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;

        &lt;tr style="background: rgb(245, 245, 245);"&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;Wallets&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;More than 3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;

        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;Enterprise Customers&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;More than 1,000&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;

        &lt;tr style="background: rgb(245, 245, 245);"&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;Countries&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;125&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;

        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;Banking Corridors&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(209, 213, 219); padding: 12px 15px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #01ffff;"&gt;More than 100&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
