    <title>Bitcoin’s 4-Year Cycle May Be Changing: Willy Woo Sees a 6–8 Year Cycle</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

  &lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgY83bjVRLG3KkRpK7rZxCAp9KQwbPHcWMWEx2TQTURBl2-X9YXOG_CmFs5Y4iLCbhvrMVRFZfHQQ3TuBG4IPdaqAh0v7iWOxP0UK0mWtsb9HDsMN5FwJRxlF5K0VvlAVppM5PmIZ5q924o7go0yjSXDE1tfTYbb-1N2vmhVzUWTPe1pwZjvU1UztahXMl8/s1672/bitcoin-4-year-cycle-6-8-year-willy-woo.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin four-year cycle potentially shifting to a six-to-eight-year cycle according to Willy Woo" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgY83bjVRLG3KkRpK7rZxCAp9KQwbPHcWMWEx2TQTURBl2-X9YXOG_CmFs5Y4iLCbhvrMVRFZfHQQ3TuBG4IPdaqAh0v7iWOxP0UK0mWtsb9HDsMN5FwJRxlF5K0VvlAVppM5PmIZ5q924o7go0yjSXDE1tfTYbb-1N2vmhVzUWTPe1pwZjvU1UztahXMl8/w400-h225/bitcoin-4-year-cycle-6-8-year-willy-woo.jpg.png" title="Willy Woo on Bitcoin’s 4-Year to 6–8 Year Cycle Shift" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For years, Bitcoin investors have had one familiar question whenever the crypto market enters a major rally or correction:
    &lt;strong&gt;Where are we in the four-year Bitcoin cycle?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The four-year cycle has become one of the most widely followed ideas in crypto. The theory connects Bitcoin’s halving schedule with major bull and bear market phases, suggesting that changes in new BTC supply help shape the timing of large market moves.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    But that framework may be evolving.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A new insight attributed to veteran Bitcoin analyst &lt;strong&gt;Willy Woo&lt;/strong&gt; suggests that Bitcoin could eventually move away from its traditional four-year rhythm and toward a much longer &lt;strong&gt;six-to-eight-year market cycle&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean Bitcoin has officially entered a six-to-eight-year cycle. It is better understood as a thesis about how the market could change as Bitcoin becomes larger, more institutionalized and increasingly connected to global financial conditions.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Willy Woo’s Bitcoin Cycle View Is Changing&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The interesting part of Woo’s latest observation is not simply the six-to-eight-year number. The bigger question is what could cause Bitcoin’s traditional cycle to become less predictable.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin's market is dramatically different from the one that existed during its early halving cycles.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Today, the asset is surrounded by institutional investors, exchange-traded products, derivatives, professional trading firms, corporate treasury strategies and global macro investors.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    As a result, Bitcoin can increasingly react to factors that have little direct connection to mining rewards.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Interest rates, global liquidity, credit conditions, institutional &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/trump-1-coin-is-here-us-mints-new.html"&gt;capital flows&lt;/a&gt; and investor risk appetite can all influence the amount of money moving into or out of BTC.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Woo’s latest six-to-eight-year idea therefore points toward a Bitcoin market that could increasingly behave like a macro asset rather than an asset governed primarily by its halving calendar.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why the Four-Year Bitcoin Cycle Became So Popular&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin’s four-year cycle is based on a real feature of the network.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Approximately every 210,000 blocks, the amount of new Bitcoin awarded to miners is cut in half. This event is known as the &lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin halving&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Historically, major Bitcoin market expansions have broadly occurred around halving periods. That created a recognizable sequence:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
    &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;thead&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Traditional Cycle&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Typical Interpretation&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/thead&gt;
      &lt;tbody&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Halving&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;New BTC issuance falls&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Supply Shock&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;New supply becomes scarcer relative to demand&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Bull Market&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Demand and speculation increase&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Market Euphoria&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Speculation reaches extreme levels&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Correction&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Prices fall and the market enters another accumulation phase&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/tbody&gt;
    &lt;/table&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The pattern has been useful, but it has never been a perfectly accurate market clock.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That distinction is becoming increasingly important as Bitcoin matures.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Halving’s Relative Supply Impact Is Getting Smaller&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    One of the central arguments behind the longer-cycle theory is that every new Bitcoin halving produces a smaller percentage change in the overall supply landscape.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In Bitcoin’s early years, newly mined BTC represented a much larger share of the existing supply.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Today, the amount of new Bitcoin entering the market is relatively small compared with the total amount already in existence and the enormous amount of capital trading the asset.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The halving still matters. It remains one of Bitcoin’s defining monetary-policy features.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    But the question is whether another reduction in issuance can continue to control the timing of major market cycles in the same way it appeared to during Bitcoin’s earlier years.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Woo’s thesis suggests that its influence could gradually become smaller.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin Is Becoming More Sensitive to Global Liquidity&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If the halving becomes less dominant, something else has to explain more of Bitcoin’s price behavior.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Increasingly, that “something” may be global liquidity.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    When financial conditions are loose and investors are willing to take more risk, capital can move toward assets such as Bitcoin.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    When interest rates rise, liquidity tightens or investors become defensive, speculative assets can face stronger selling pressure.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This creates a different way of thinking about Bitcoin.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Instead of asking only:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;blockquote&gt;
    &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;“When is the next Bitcoin halving?”&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/blockquote&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    investors may increasingly need to ask:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;blockquote&gt;
    &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;“Where are we in the global liquidity cycle?”&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/blockquote&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That could become one of the most important changes in Bitcoin market analysis.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Would a 6–8 Year Bitcoin Cycle Actually Mean?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A six-to-eight-year cycle does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean Bitcoin would rise continuously for six or eight years.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This is one of the easiest parts of the theory to misunderstand.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A longer cycle would refer to the broader market structure. Inside that larger cycle, Bitcoin could still experience multiple rallies, corrections, accumulation periods and sharp selloffs.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Think of it as a longer financial season rather than a straight upward line.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin could potentially spend several years inside a broader expansion or contraction while experiencing significant shorter-term moves along the way.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Four-Year Cycle vs. Possible 6–8 Year Cycle&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
    &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;thead&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Factor&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Traditional 4-Year Model&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Possible 6–8 Year Model&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/thead&gt;
      &lt;tbody&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;

          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Bitcoin halving&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Macro conditions, liquidity &lt;br /&gt;and Bitcoin supply&lt;/td&gt;

          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Still important but potentially &lt;br /&gt;less dominant&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;

          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Market timing&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Halving-centered&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Broader economic-cycle &lt;br /&gt;centered&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Institutional influence&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Historically limited&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Much greater&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Liquidity&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Important&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Potentially critical&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Cycle duration&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Approximately four years&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Potentially six to eight years&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/tbody&gt;
    &lt;/table&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    These two models do not necessarily have to compete with each other.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin can continue to follow its programmed supply schedule while simultaneously becoming more influenced by global financial conditions.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Four-Year Cycle Is Not Suddenly “Dead”&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This is where the current discussion needs some context.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Earlier in 2026, reporting on Woo’s analysis indicated that he still considered the traditional four-year Bitcoin cycle valid at that point, with long-term capital flows not yet showing a decisive break from historical patterns.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That means the latest six-to-eight-year observation should not be presented as:
    &lt;strong&gt;“Willy Woo says the four-year cycle is over.”&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A more accurate interpretation is that Bitcoin’s market structure may be evolving and that the influence of the halving could gradually decline relative to other market forces.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That is a much more interesting question than simply declaring the old cycle dead.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin’s Institutional Market Changes the Equation&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin’s market has become far more institutional than it was during its early cycles.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Large investors now have more ways to gain exposure to &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/andrew-cuomo-warns-us-could-lose-crypto.html"&gt;BTC&lt;/a&gt;, while derivatives markets allow sophisticated traders to hedge positions or express views without necessarily buying spot Bitcoin.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Institutional investors also tend to evaluate Bitcoin alongside stocks, bonds, commodities, currencies and other macro assets.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That means Bitcoin can increasingly become part of a broader portfolio-allocation decision.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If global investors become more willing to take risk, Bitcoin can benefit.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If those same investors reduce risk exposure, Bitcoin can suffer—even if Bitcoin’s underlying network fundamentals have not changed.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Could Institutional Money Actually Make Bitcoin More Macro-Sensitive?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    It may seem logical that institutional adoption would make Bitcoin more stable and independent from speculative trading.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    But there is another possibility.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Institutional adoption could make Bitcoin &lt;strong&gt;more connected to global markets&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Large investors often make allocation decisions based on interest rates, liquidity, economic expectations and portfolio risk.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    When those conditions change, their Bitcoin exposure can change as well.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In that environment, Bitcoin’s four-year halving rhythm could remain important while no longer being the dominant force controlling the timing of major price movements.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Could Happen to Bitcoin Bull and Bear Markets?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Under the traditional model, investors often expect a sequence resembling:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Halving → Bull Market → Euphoria → Bear Market → Accumulation → Next Halving&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A longer-cycle model could look more like:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Liquidity Expansion → Capital Inflows → Bitcoin Expansion → Risk-Off Phase → Liquidity Reset → New Expansion&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The two models can overlap.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A Bitcoin halving can reduce new supply at the same time that global liquidity becomes more supportive.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Conversely, a halving can occur while macroeconomic conditions are unfavorable.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That is why treating the halving as an automatic signal for a Bitcoin rally may become increasingly risky.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why the 2028 Bitcoin Halving Could Be Important&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The next Bitcoin halving is expected in &lt;strong&gt;2028&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That event could provide an important test for the competing cycle theories.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If Bitcoin once again produces a market structure that closely resembles previous post-halving periods, the four-year framework will continue to have strong relevance.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    But if Bitcoin’s major market phases increasingly line up with global liquidity, institutional flows and broader economic conditions, the case for longer cycles could become stronger.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In that sense, the next several years could be a natural experiment for Bitcoin-cycle theory.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;A Longer Cycle Does Not Mean Lower Volatility&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Another common misunderstanding is that a six-to-eight-year cycle would automatically make Bitcoin less volatile.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    There is no such guarantee.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin could still experience violent rallies and deep corrections inside a longer cycle.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A longer cycle simply describes the duration of the broader market phase. It does not eliminate shorter-term volatility.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Investors could therefore see several major corrections even while Bitcoin remains inside a much longer overall expansion cycle.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Investors May Need to Watch&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If Woo’s longer-cycle thesis becomes more convincing, investors may need to look beyond the Bitcoin halving calendar.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
    &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;thead&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Indicator&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Why It Matters&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/thead&gt;
      &lt;tbody&gt;

          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Can influence the amount of capital &lt;br /&gt;available for risk assets.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Interest rates&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Higher or lower borrowing costs can change &lt;br /&gt;investor risk appetite.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Institutional flows&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Large capital movements can materially affect &lt;br /&gt;Bitcoin demand.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;On-chain activity&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Provides information about Bitcoin investor &lt;br /&gt;behavior and network activity.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;

          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin issuance&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;The halving remains a fundamental part of &lt;br /&gt;Bitcoin’s monetary design.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Market sentiment&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Investor psychology can amplify both rallies &lt;br /&gt;and selloffs.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/tbody&gt;
    &lt;/table&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin May Be Moving From a Calendar Story to a Liquidity Story&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Perhaps the most important takeaway from the debate is that Bitcoin’s future cycles may become harder to explain with a single indicator.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In Bitcoin’s early years, the halving schedule provided a simple narrative.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Investors knew when the next supply reduction was coming, and the market repeatedly responded with large price movements around the broader halving periods.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    But Bitcoin is now part of a much larger financial ecosystem.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Global liquidity can change quickly. Institutional investors can move significant amounts of capital. Derivatives can alter price discovery. Macroeconomic news can immediately affect risk assets.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That makes the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/elon-musk-says-ai-could-add-20-trillion.html"&gt;market &lt;/a&gt;increasingly complex.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What This Means for Long-Term Bitcoin Investors&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The biggest lesson from Woo’s view is not that investors should abandon the four-year cycle.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Instead, it may be time to stop treating that cycle as a guaranteed market-timing mechanism.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A halving remains important because it changes Bitcoin’s issuance rate.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    But whether that supply change produces a major price move depends on demand.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    And demand can be influenced by everything from institutional allocation and investor sentiment to interest rates and global liquidity.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In other words:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;blockquote&gt;
    &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin’s supply schedule is predictable. Bitcoin’s demand cycle is not.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/blockquote&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That may be the key reason why longer-cycle theories are attracting attention.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Could Bitcoin Eventually Have No Fixed Cycle?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    It is also possible that Bitcoin’s future market structure becomes less predictable altogether.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Markets are driven by human behavior, capital flows and changing economic conditions. There is no guarantee that one historical pattern will remain dominant forever.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin could eventually experience overlapping cycles driven by:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Global liquidity&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Credit conditions&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Institutional demand&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Monetary policy&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Bitcoin issuance&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Investor sentiment&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Derivatives positioning&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;On-chain capital flows&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If that happens, investors may no longer be able to describe Bitcoin's market using one clean four-year chart.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Story: Bitcoin Is Growing Up&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin’s changing cycle debate reflects a larger transformation in the cryptocurrency market.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The Bitcoin of 2012 was not the Bitcoin of 2020.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    And the Bitcoin of 2026 is not the Bitcoin of either period.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The market is larger, more liquid, more institutional and more closely connected to traditional finance.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That does not make Bitcoin less unique.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    It means the forces affecting its price are becoming more complicated.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The halving will continue to reduce new BTC issuance. But the market surrounding that supply schedule is evolving.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Willy Woo’s latest insight raises an important possibility: &lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin’s familiar four-year market rhythm could gradually evolve into a broader six-to-eight-year cycle.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The idea is based on the changing economics of Bitcoin and the growing importance of macroeconomic factors, rather than a claim that the four-year cycle has suddenly disappeared.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That distinction matters.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Earlier in 2026, Woo was still reported as seeing evidence that Bitcoin’s traditional four-year cycle remained valid. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    So the most reasonable interpretation is not that Bitcoin has officially entered a six-to-eight-year cycle, but that &lt;strong&gt;the forces determining Bitcoin’s market rhythm may be changing.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If the traditional halving pattern continues to dominate, the four-year framework will remain useful.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If global liquidity, institutional capital and macroeconomic conditions increasingly determine Bitcoin’s major market phases, a longer cycle could become the more useful framework.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Either way, the debate highlights a much bigger shift in crypto:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin may be moving from a market governed mainly by its own supply schedule toward one increasingly influenced by the global financial system.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    And for investors, that could mean watching two clocks at the same time:
    &lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin’s supply clock and the global economy’s liquidity clock.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is Bitcoin moving to a six-to-eight-year cycle?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Willy Woo’s latest insight suggests Bitcoin &lt;strong&gt;could&lt;/strong&gt; move toward a six-to-eight-year market cycle. However, this remains an analytical thesis rather than a confirmed rule governing Bitcoin prices.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is the four-year Bitcoin cycle dead?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    No. There is not enough evidence to declare the four-year cycle permanently over. Earlier 2026 reporting on Woo’s analysis indicated that he still saw support for the traditional cycle at that time. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Why could Bitcoin cycles become longer?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    One possible explanation is that Bitcoin’s halving-driven supply shock becomes relatively smaller as the network matures, while global liquidity, institutional capital and macroeconomic conditions become increasingly important.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Does a six-to-eight-year cycle mean Bitcoin will rise for eight years?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    No. A longer cycle does not mean continuous price growth. Bitcoin could experience multiple rallies, corrections and bear-market phases inside a longer market structure.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Does the Bitcoin halving still matter?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Yes. The halving remains fundamental to Bitcoin because it reduces the rate at which new BTC are created. The debate is about how strongly the halving controls market timing compared with other factors.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What should Bitcoin investors watch?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Investors may want to monitor Bitcoin issuance alongside global liquidity, interest rates, institutional flows, on-chain activity, derivatives positioning and broader risk sentiment.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;When is the next Bitcoin halving?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The next Bitcoin halving is expected in 2028. Its market behavior could provide another useful test of how relevant the traditional four-year cycle remains.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Editorial Note&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This article presents the six-to-eight-year Bitcoin cycle as &lt;strong&gt;Willy Woo’s market thesis&lt;/strong&gt;, not as an established fact or guaranteed price forecast. Bitcoin’s historical four-year pattern is approximate, and previous market cycles do not guarantee future performance.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Disclaimer&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This article is provided for informational and educational purposes only. It does not constitute financial, investment or trading advice. Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies are highly volatile assets. Readers should conduct their own research and consider their individual risk tolerance before making financial decisions.
  &lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Privacy Coins Surge 213% as Crypto Sector Outperforms October 2025 Levels</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhv9qGHJMjdgzRUW37rALEdLrdAFifmQ6pt8iRpbcFxlAqoZuAwd7asiO3_3Uo3Fk6fI6wGTNuyFgbJbBDVTut98qlSC1izMO48S-FMxlaSoGigX6-tcuEI0EfqI9JRa8nRbHu-tFLc8HyJ3nEbG7VJwU7znUv68iZMAw4Pt3B4up1sEqa1vZqhLRnSLx7Y/s1671/privacy-coins-glassnode-213-percent-2026.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Privacy coins lead the crypto market with strong sector performance" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1671" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhv9qGHJMjdgzRUW37rALEdLrdAFifmQ6pt8iRpbcFxlAqoZuAwd7asiO3_3Uo3Fk6fI6wGTNuyFgbJbBDVTut98qlSC1izMO48S-FMxlaSoGigX6-tcuEI0EfqI9JRa8nRbHu-tFLc8HyJ3nEbG7VJwU7znUv68iZMAw4Pt3B4up1sEqa1vZqhLRnSLx7Y/w640-h360/privacy-coins-glassnode-213-percent-2026.jpg.png" title="Privacy Coins Lead Crypto Market Rally" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;
September 7, 2026&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Privacy-focused cryptocurrencies have become the standout corner of the crypto market, with the sector now &lt;strong&gt;213% above its October 6, 2025 level&lt;/strong&gt;, according to new data from Glassnode.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The performance is striking because most major crypto sectors remain below the level they reached when Bitcoin recorded its October 2025 cycle peak. Bitcoin is still about 36% below that benchmark, while the median asset among the top 200 cryptocurrencies remains roughly 58% lower.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Privacy is the only sector in the Glassnode comparison currently trading above its October 2025 level. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Privacy Crypto Is Outperforming the Broader Market&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The 213% figure does not mean that every privacy coin has gained 213%. It represents the performance of the &lt;strong&gt;privacy sector&lt;/strong&gt; relative to the October 6, 2025 benchmark.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 720px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Crypto Market Segment&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Performance vs. Oct. 6, 2025&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Privacy sector&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;+213%&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;About -36%&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;DeFi&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;About -27%&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Median top-200 crypto asset&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;About -58%&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Gaming&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;About -74%&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The gap shows how unusual the privacy-sector rally has been. While the broader market has recovered over shorter periods, most sectors have not recovered to their October 2025 levels. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Zcash Is Driving Much of the Rally&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Zcash (ZEC)&lt;/strong&gt; has been the biggest force behind the sector's performance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Glassnode data cited in recent reporting shows ZEC up approximately &lt;strong&gt;2,496% over the past year&lt;/strong&gt;. Its market-cap ranking has climbed from around No. 82 to No. 7, and the cryptocurrency now represents roughly &lt;strong&gt;62% of the privacy sector's market capitalization&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That concentration is important. A large part of the sector's headline performance is being generated by one exceptionally strong asset rather than an equal rally across every privacy cryptocurrency. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;But the Rally Is Not Only About ZEC&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is another reason the Glassnode data is attracting attention: removing Zcash does not eliminate the sector's outperformance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The privacy basket excluding ZEC is still reported to be up approximately &lt;strong&gt;85% over the past year&lt;/strong&gt; and about &lt;strong&gt;56% above its October 6, 2025 level&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That suggests the privacy narrative has spread beyond a single &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/fed-researchers-examine-whether-payment.html"&gt;token&lt;/a&gt;, although Zcash remains by far the largest contributor to the sector's overall performance. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Monero and Dash Add to the Sector Rotation&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Monero (XMR)&lt;/strong&gt; is another major beneficiary of the renewed interest in privacy-focused crypto assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Glassnode's reported data shows that XMR, along with &lt;strong&gt;Dash (DASH)&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;Horizen (ZEN)&lt;/strong&gt;, has outperformed Bitcoin over the most recent 90-day period.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The data also indicates that all eight privacy assets with at least one year of available history were positive over the one-year period examined. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This broader participation makes the move more significant than a simple Zcash price rally.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Privacy Sector Market Cap Expands Sharply&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The sector's growth is also visible in its total &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/liquid-network-paused-after-nearly-4000.html"&gt;market capitalization&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Glassnode data cited by recent reports puts the privacy sector at approximately &lt;strong&gt;$33.6 billion&lt;/strong&gt;, compared with about &lt;strong&gt;$7.1 billion a year earlier&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That represents roughly $26.5 billion in additional market value, with almost half of the expansion occurring during the latest 30-day period. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The move has happened during a wider crypto rebound. About &lt;strong&gt;91.5% of the top 200 crypto assets&lt;/strong&gt; gained over the most recent 30-day period, according to the reported Glassnode data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the longer-term picture remains much more selective. Only around 25 of the top 200 assets were positive over the one-year period in the cited comparison. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Are Privacy Coins Getting Attention Again?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Privacy has returned as a major crypto narrative at a time when &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/hanwha-builds-tokenized-securities.html"&gt;blockchain &lt;/a&gt;transactions are becoming increasingly easy to analyze.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin and Ethereum transactions are publicly recorded, allowing blockchain analytics firms and other observers to trace transaction flows. Privacy-focused networks take a different approach by using cryptographic mechanisms designed to make transaction information less transparent.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The exact technology varies between projects.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Monero uses privacy mechanisms designed to conceal transaction participants and amounts by default, while Zcash uses zero-knowledge technology that allows users to make shielded transactions. Other projects take different approaches to transaction mixing or confidential applications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This creates a distinct investment narrative around &lt;strong&gt;financial privacy, transaction confidentiality and blockchain surveillance&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Privacy Narrative Comes With Regulatory Risk&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The same characteristics that make privacy technology attractive to some users can create challenges for regulated exchanges and financial institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Privacy-focused cryptocurrencies have historically faced greater scrutiny around anti-money-laundering controls and transaction monitoring because their designs can make blockchain analysis more difficult.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means the sector's strong market performance does not remove its regulatory risk.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For investors, exchange availability, jurisdiction-specific rules and liquidity can be just as important as the underlying technology.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Only a Few Large Crypto Assets Are Above October 2025 Levels&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The strength of privacy coins becomes even clearer when looking at the largest cryptocurrencies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Among the 25 largest assets in the cited Glassnode comparison, only &lt;strong&gt;ZEC, HYPE, XMR and WBT&lt;/strong&gt; were above their October 6, 2025 levels.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Two of those four assets—ZEC and XMR—are privacy-focused cryptocurrencies. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not mean privacy is the only successful crypto narrative in 2026. It does show that privacy assets have performed unusually well compared with the broader market over the period being measured.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does the 213% Figure Actually Tell Investors?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most important point is that &lt;strong&gt;213% is a sector-level comparison, not an individual-token return&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sector performance can be heavily influenced by the largest assets. In this case, Zcash's extraordinary rise has a major effect because it represents a large portion of the privacy sector's total market capitalization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, the sector excluding ZEC remains significantly above the October benchmark, suggesting that the broader privacy category has also strengthened.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Investors should therefore look at both figures: the headline &lt;strong&gt;+213%&lt;/strong&gt; sector performance and the much lower but still substantial &lt;strong&gt;+56%&lt;/strong&gt; performance of the privacy basket excluding ZEC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Is This Proof of a New Crypto Bull Market?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The data shows strong performance from privacy assets, but it does not establish that the entire crypto market has entered a new sustained bull cycle.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The recent one-month rebound has been broad, yet longer-term performance remains uneven. Bitcoin is still below its October 2025 benchmark, while the median top-200 cryptocurrency is considerably further below it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The more accurate conclusion is that privacy has become the &lt;strong&gt;leading crypto sector in the current market rotation&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Could Determine Whether Privacy Coins Keep Leading?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Zcash performance:&lt;/strong&gt; ZEC currently has an outsized influence on the sector.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Monero and other privacy assets:&lt;/strong&gt; Continued gains outside ZEC would make the sector's rally more diversified.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Regulation:&lt;/strong&gt; Exchange listing policies and AML rules remain major risks.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Liquidity:&lt;/strong&gt; Large percentage gains need to be evaluated alongside trading depth and market participation.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Capital rotation:&lt;/strong&gt; Investors could shift toward Bitcoin, DeFi, AI, infrastructure or other narratives if market conditions change.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Are privacy coins up 213%?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The 213% figure refers to the privacy sector's performance compared with its October 6, 2025 level. It does not mean every individual privacy coin has gained 213%.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Which privacy coin is driving the rally?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Zcash is the biggest contributor. Glassnode data cited in recent reports shows ZEC up approximately 2,496% over the past year and accounting for roughly 62% of the privacy sector's market capitalization. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Monero also benefiting?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes. Monero is among the privacy assets that have outperformed Bitcoin over the recent 90-day period in the cited Glassnode data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How big is the privacy crypto sector?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The sector was reported at approximately $33.6 billion in market capitalization, compared with about $7.1 billion a year earlier. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why are privacy coins outperforming?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The current move appears to reflect a combination of strong performance from Zcash, broader interest in privacy-focused crypto assets and capital rotation within the market. The available data does not establish a single cause for the entire rally.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does the rally mean privacy coins will continue rising?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. The sector remains highly volatile and faces regulatory, liquidity and market-rotation risks. Past performance does not guarantee future returns.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Privacy-focused cryptocurrencies have become the clearest sector leader in the latest crypto market rotation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to Glassnode data cited in recent reporting, the privacy sector is &lt;strong&gt;213% above its October 6, 2025 level&lt;/strong&gt;, while Bitcoin remains about 36% below that benchmark and the median top-200 crypto asset is down roughly 58%.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Zcash has driven much of the move, but the strength does not disappear when ZEC is excluded. The privacy basket excluding Zcash is still reported to be 56% above the October benchmark.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the numbers show a powerful sector rotation—not proof that every cryptocurrency is entering a new bull market. Whether privacy can maintain its lead will depend on continued market demand, liquidity and the regulatory environment surrounding privacy-focused digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>CFTC Launches Frontier Forum for AI and Agentic Finance on October 28</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi54jUyskx4CnMOYtiFUu_Nm7quS4saU9v1UygYsJRbYNqCz-s07KDTvh6k_PM3dVE-FlXkumwB_L3mQIn_x_Nv_hNH8W5RBn4iOFJeHIYkJ-W8jySihoLxX6y-pwXsfkFxaVIdPqsD8XX3M6m5w06dDr6lqEpMUIrMxjHRQfGK9ZO4eaUcUQ-MWc6LKENj/s1734/cftc-frontier-forum-ai-agentic-finance.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="CFTC Frontier Forum on AI and agentic finance in US financial markets" border="0" data-original-height="907" data-original-width="1734" height="334" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi54jUyskx4CnMOYtiFUu_Nm7quS4saU9v1UygYsJRbYNqCz-s07KDTvh6k_PM3dVE-FlXkumwB_L3mQIn_x_Nv_hNH8W5RBn4iOFJeHIYkJ-W8jySihoLxX6y-pwXsfkFxaVIdPqsD8XX3M6m5w06dDr6lqEpMUIrMxjHRQfGK9ZO4eaUcUQ-MWc6LKENj/w640-h334/cftc-frontier-forum-ai-agentic-finance.webp.png" title="CFTC Frontier Forum AI and Agentic Finance" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is launching a new public roundtable series focused on emerging technologies reshaping financial markets, with artificial intelligence and agentic finance set to headline the first session on October 28, 2026.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The initiative, called the &lt;strong&gt;Frontier Forum Series&lt;/strong&gt;, was announced September 21 by the CFTC's Innovation Task Force. The agency said the forums will bring together builders and leaders from the public and private sectors to discuss new financial technologies and evolving market structures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The first Frontier Forum will focus specifically on &lt;strong&gt;AI and agentic finance&lt;/strong&gt;, putting autonomous and AI-driven financial technology directly into the discussion around the future of U.S. financial markets. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is the CFTC Frontier Forum?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Frontier Forum is designed as a series of public discussions about technologies that are changing how financial markets operate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to the CFTC, each forum will provide a venue for public dialogue about financial technologies and evolving market structures. The agency says the discussions are intended to help it examine how it can support responsible innovation while protecting market participants and maintaining the integrity and resilience of U.S. &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ecb-pontes-tokenized-assets-central-bank-money-2028.html"&gt;financial markets.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The initiative is being organized by the CFTC's &lt;strong&gt;Innovation Task Force&lt;/strong&gt;, which has been given a broader role in examining emerging areas of financial technology.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;First Forum Will Focus on AI and Agentic Finance&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The inaugural Frontier Forum is scheduled for &lt;strong&gt;Wednesday, October 28, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, and will focus on artificial intelligence and agentic finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The timing is notable because AI systems are increasingly being developed to perform tasks beyond generating text or analyzing information. Agentic systems can be designed to plan actions, interact with software and execute tasks with varying degrees of human oversight.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In financial markets, that raises questions about how AI systems could interact with trading, market infrastructure, risk management, compliance and other activities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC has not yet published the complete agenda or list of speakers. The agency said information about the agenda, speakers and registration will be posted later. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Agentic Finance Is Becoming a Regulatory Topic&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional financial software generally follows predefined rules and instructions. Agentic AI introduces a different model in which software can potentially interpret information, make decisions within defined parameters and take actions through connected systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates potential opportunities as well as new regulatory questions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, an AI agent could potentially monitor market information, identify conditions that meet predefined criteria and initiate an action through a connected financial system. The exact level of autonomy would depend on how the system is designed and what permissions it receives.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For regulators, the challenge is determining how existing market rules apply when technology becomes capable of performing increasingly complex activities with less direct human intervention.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;CFTC Wants Public and Private Sector Input&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC says the Frontier Forum will bring together people from both the public and private sectors.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That includes technology builders, financial-market participants, researchers and other stakeholders involved in developing or using emerging financial technologies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The agency's stated objective is to engage directly with people who are building, using and studying these technologies while considering how regulation can support responsible innovation and protect market participants. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;CFTC Chairman &lt;strong&gt;Michael S. Selig&lt;/strong&gt; said the technologies transforming financial markets are advancing rapidly and that the agency needs to engage directly with the people building, using and studying them. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Could Change More Than Trading&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The discussion around AI in financial markets extends beyond automated trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Financial institutions are exploring &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/rex-tuttle-assx-2x-etf-strive-bitcoin-treasury.html"&gt;AI for areas&lt;/a&gt; such as market analysis, fraud detection, compliance, customer service, risk monitoring and operational processes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Agentic systems could potentially combine several of these capabilities and perform multi-step tasks with less human intervention.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That also creates practical questions about accountability. If an autonomous system makes an incorrect decision, for example, firms and regulators may need to determine how responsibility is assigned between the technology provider, financial institution, human supervisor and other parties involved in the system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Market Integrity and Resilience Are Part of the Discussion&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC's announcement does not frame the Frontier Forum as a technology-only initiative.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The agency specifically says the forums will consider innovation alongside the protection of market participants and the integrity and resilience of U.S. financial markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means future discussions could involve issues such as system reliability, cybersecurity, operational controls, market manipulation risks, transparency and oversight of AI-enabled financial activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the October 28 event itself should not be described as announcing new AI trading rules. The CFTC has announced a public discussion forum, not a final regulatory framework for agentic finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;CFTC's Broader Innovation Agenda&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Frontier Forum fits into a wider innovation agenda at the CFTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The agency's Innovation Task Force identifies three core innovation themes: &lt;strong&gt;crypto assets and blockchain technologies, artificial intelligence and autonomous systems, and prediction markets and event contracts&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC says its innovation work includes public roundtables, written input, the Innovation Advisory Committee and industry engagement. The stated goal is to develop insights that can inform Commission policy, interpretations and potential rulemaking considerations. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This broader structure means the Frontier Forum is not limited to AI. Future sessions can address other technologies and market structures affecting the derivatives and financial markets overseen by the agency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Public Can Nominate Speakers&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC is also opening the process to public participation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Members of the public can submit speaker nominations to the CFTC's Innovation Task Force through the email address provided in the agency's announcement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The agency cautioned that the number of people allowed to attend in person may be limited and that visitors will be subject to security checks. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the October 28 Forum Could Cover&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC has not yet published the detailed agenda, so specific discussion topics should not be presented as confirmed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Based on the announced focus on AI and agentic &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/visa-memecoin-card-rewards-crossmint-robinhood-wallet.html"&gt;finance&lt;/a&gt;, however, areas likely to be relevant include the interaction between autonomous systems and financial markets, the use of AI in market infrastructure, oversight of AI-enabled financial activity and the balance between technological innovation and market protections.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The final agenda and speakers will determine the actual scope of the inaugural session.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frontier Forum vs. New CFTC Regulation&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why This Matters for Crypto and Blockchain&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Although the first Frontier Forum is focused on AI and agentic finance, the initiative is also relevant to the broader digital-asset industry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI and blockchain are increasingly being developed together in areas such as automated financial services, decentralized applications, trading infrastructure and autonomous software agents.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC's Innovation Task Force separately lists crypto assets and blockchain technologies among its core innovation themes. That creates a regulatory forum where developments across AI, blockchain and financial-market technology can potentially intersect. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Still, the October 28 meeting should be viewed primarily as an AI and agentic-finance discussion. Any future policy consequences will depend on what the CFTC learns from these discussions and any subsequent agency actions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The immediate next step is the October 28 inaugural Frontier Forum.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC said additional information about the agenda, speakers and registration will be posted at a later date. The agency also invited public speaker nominations, creating an opportunity for industry participants and researchers to contribute to the discussion. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As AI systems become increasingly capable of interacting with financial infrastructure, the questions raised by agentic finance are likely to extend beyond technology into market structure, oversight and operational risk.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC is launching the &lt;strong&gt;Frontier Forum Series&lt;/strong&gt; to create a public venue for discussing emerging technologies that are changing U.S. financial markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The first session on &lt;strong&gt;October 28, 2026&lt;/strong&gt; will focus on artificial intelligence and agentic finance, bringing the growing role of autonomous financial technology into a formal regulatory discussion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The initiative does not itself create new AI trading regulations. Instead, it gives regulators, technology builders, financial institutions and other stakeholders a structured forum to discuss how emerging systems can develop while financial-market integrity, resilience and participant protections remain part of the conversation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Updated September 22, 2026. The CFTC has not yet released the detailed agenda or speaker list for the October 28 forum.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Cathie Wood Says Deflation Risk Is Rising as AI Boosts Bitcoin and Stablecoins</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhu2gXi91C0G4bIj-Rly6OLiqfs_D7dTMNeNtmRWRd7NcrOZ3esjGcGDyS2__7kwxiw49giW2IU0Xuor8TqfDFx-76o3jOEp92yDIGKgy7gc6_k0wTIMM3SztxQK7r_8wC0i1iOdHF7Z_qO7weldxfMzwsJw4NPT4489OIOrPI4_-3wVL5mEHJWsECgkfMi/s1402/ARK%20Invest%20CEO%20Cathie%20Wood.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Cathie Wood deflation risk AI Bitcoin stablecoins agent commerce ARK Invest CEO" border="0" data-original-height="1122" data-original-width="1402" height="256" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhu2gXi91C0G4bIj-Rly6OLiqfs_D7dTMNeNtmRWRd7NcrOZ3esjGcGDyS2__7kwxiw49giW2IU0Xuor8TqfDFx-76o3jOEp92yDIGKgy7gc6_k0wTIMM3SztxQK7r_8wC0i1iOdHF7Z_qO7weldxfMzwsJw4NPT4489OIOrPI4_-3wVL5mEHJWsECgkfMi/w320-h256/ARK%20Invest%20CEO%20Cathie%20Wood.png" title="Cathie Wood Says Deflation Risk Is Rising as AI Boosts Bitcoin and Stablecoins | CoinaiNews" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aug 10, 2026&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;– ARK Invest CEO Cathie Wood says
the economic risk may be shifting from persistent inflation toward deflation as
artificial intelligence and automation accelerate productivity. She also argues
that Bitcoin and stablecoins could benefit from the rise of AI-driven
"agent commerce," where software agents increasingly handle payments
and other financial transactions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In comments posted on X (formerly Twitter) on August 9, Wood
said the widespread adoption of AI-powered commerce could create significant
opportunities for digital assets, particularly as they become essential tools
in what she calls "agent commerce" — where AI agents autonomously
execute financial transactions without human intervention&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why Deflation, Not Inflation, Is the Real Threat&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Wood's argument starts with the data. She pointed to recent
economic indicators showing price pressures are fading faster than markets
expect&amp;nbsp;:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;CPI
     fell 0.4% month-over-month in June&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;— the largest one-month
     decline since April 2020&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;PPI
     dropped 0.3% month-over-month&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Core
     PCE rose just 0.1% month-over-month&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"The risk going forward is going to be deflation,
not inflation — particularly for businesses that fail to adopt AI and
productivity tools."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
—&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Cathie Wood&lt;/b&gt;, ARK Invest CEO&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Her reasoning:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;As AI and automation drive
productivity gains, costs across the economy could fall. Companies that don't
adopt these tools risk being left behind&amp;nbsp;. Wood also warned that a supply
surplus is forming in oil markets, which could push energy prices lower and add
to deflationary pressure&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;She also noted the U.S. federal deficit as a percentage of
GDP is currently&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;5.6%&lt;/b&gt;, a level she compares to the early 1980s
during the dawn of Reaganomics&amp;nbsp;. Wood estimates that if productivity and
technology adoption continue accelerating as ARK anticipates, this ratio could
approach 5% by year-end&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Agent Commerce: Why Bitcoin and Stablecoins Win&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Wood's bullishness on crypto is tied directly to AI. She
sees the emergence of&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;agent commerce&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;— where AI agents
autonomously execute financial transactions on behalf of humans — as a
structural shift that will demand fast, programmable, global payment
rails&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In this world, stablecoins would serve as the medium of
exchange — digital dollars moving at the speed of code — while Bitcoin would
function as a store of value, offering a fixed maximum supply designed to
resist monetary dilution&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"Bitcoin and stablecoins are the two digital assets
that could benefit most from this new commerce model."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
—&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Cathie Wood&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Wood noted that as AI agents gain the ability to make
payments, move assets, and execute financial decisions, the demand for
blockchain-based systems alongside traditional banking infrastructure will
rise. Wood also pointed to Bitcoin's relative performance against gold as
evidence that she believes the asset is maturing as a store of value&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;AI Capex Is Not a Bubble&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Wood pushed back against concerns that AI investment is
overdone. She noted that&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;AI-related capital expenditures have already
exceeded the range of the past 30 years&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;— but that's a sign of a
technological revolution in its early stages, not a bubble about to burst&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"We are not at a peak of a bubble, but rather in the
early stages of a technological revolution."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
—&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Cathie Wood&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The productivity growth story is just beginning&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;—
and companies that delay AI adoption will face greater risks&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Macro Outlook&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Wood also shared her macro expectations&amp;nbsp;:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;DXY
     index could rise to 102.6&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;this year&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Oil
     prices face downside&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;due to supply surplus&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Fiscal
     deficit could narrow&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;to 5% of GDP by year-end&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Her bottom line: markets are pricing in a worst-case
scenario that doesn't reflect the underlying economic reality. The jobs report
that looked "scary on the surface" is actually not as bad as it
appears&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What This Means for Crypto&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Wood's comments reinforce her broader view that&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;AI
and crypto are converging&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;As AI agents gain the ability to make payments, move assets,
and execute financial decisions, the demand for blockchain-based systems
alongside traditional banking infrastructure will rise&amp;nbsp;. Stablecoins offer
the rails. Bitcoin offers the reserve.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"If productivity and technology adoption continue to
accelerate as ARK anticipates, this could shift the entire economic
landscape."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
—&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Cathie Wood&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For Bitcoin, that shift could be a tailwind.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
