    <title>Strategy CEO Phong Le Says AI Agents Could Drive Demand for Digital Assets</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgguwbjd7CPGrilB4iikN2EuriQ3fYgL6ivGqNAj32QklrpxQM4KBjmkv5RO0X2o-HUh9ylFXIjrR8o2-8D3ADS-MnFABeqBqifguASJ1smL5HKaM22whsKEu0QKW6vnMGjyeRRxY-2QaB1fAWPWT01rF1f9pXwMvz9DE_ilpJEJBSz0jdhn0VAWeYqVRXy/s1672/strategy-ceo-phong-le-ai-agents-digital-assets.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Strategy CEO Phong Le speaking at WOLF Financial about AI agents driving demand for digital assets" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgguwbjd7CPGrilB4iikN2EuriQ3fYgL6ivGqNAj32QklrpxQM4KBjmkv5RO0X2o-HUh9ylFXIjrR8o2-8D3ADS-MnFABeqBqifguASJ1smL5HKaM22whsKEu0QKW6vnMGjyeRRxY-2QaB1fAWPWT01rF1f9pXwMvz9DE_ilpJEJBSz0jdhn0VAWeYqVRXy/w640-h360/strategy-ceo-phong-le-ai-agents-digital-assets.jpg.png" title="Phong Le: AI Agents Could Drive Demand for Digital Assets" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Strategy CEO Phong Le says the rise of autonomous AI agents could create a new source of demand for digital assets as machines begin handling real-world tasks and interacting directly with financial systems.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In a recent appearance with WOLF Financial, Le discussed a future in which autonomous agents do more than generate information or assist humans. As these systems begin running errands, making decisions and interacting with financial infrastructure, he argued that they could also require digital assets to support those activities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;“They’re going to want digital assets behind it too,” Le said when describing the potential financial needs of autonomous agents.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The comment points to a broader thesis that Le has been developing for months: the growth of agentic artificial intelligence could eventually create an economy in which software systems become active participants in commerce, rather than simply tools controlled by people.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why AI Agents Could Need Digital Assets&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Today's AI assistants generally operate within systems funded and controlled by humans. A user asks an AI to perform a task, while a person or company remains responsible for the account, payment and final decision.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Autonomous agents could change that model.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An agent capable of operating independently could eventually arrange deliveries, purchase computing resources, book services, manage subscriptions, negotiate contracts or coordinate other software systems. If those activities involve payments, the agent needs a way to identify itself, authorize transactions and transfer value.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a potential connection between agentic AI and digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of relying exclusively on traditional payment networks designed primarily around human customers, autonomous software could use programmable digital payment systems that operate around the clock and across borders.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This does not mean every AI agent will necessarily use &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/cftc-opens-three-previously-unreported.html"&gt;cryptocurrency&lt;/a&gt;. Traditional payment networks, bank accounts and centralized financial platforms will likely remain important. Le’s argument is that a world containing vastly more autonomous economic actors could create demand for financial infrastructure designed specifically for machine-to-machine transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Phong Le’s 6 Trillion-Agent Vision&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest comments are not an isolated prediction from Le.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In a June 2026 interview, the Strategy CEO described a future in which the world could move from billions of humans to trillions of autonomous decision-making agents. Le used the figure of &lt;strong&gt;6 trillion agents&lt;/strong&gt; to illustrate the potential scale of an agent-driven economy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In that vision, AI agents would make decisions on behalf of individuals, companies and potentially other organizations. When those agents conduct commercial interactions and exchange value, Le has argued that traditional financial networks may not be the ideal infrastructure for the task.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, he has pointed toward decentralized &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/hunter-biden-says-i-dont-want-anybody.html"&gt;crypto rails&lt;/a&gt; and Bitcoin as potential components of a future digital financial system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The idea is ambitious, but it provides important context for his latest comments about autonomous agents wanting digital assets behind them. The central argument is that if software becomes an economic actor, it may eventually need access to assets and payment infrastructure that software can use natively.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;From AI Assistants to Autonomous Economic Actors&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important distinction is between an AI assistant and an autonomous economic agent.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An assistant can recommend a product or prepare an order. A truly autonomous agent could potentially execute the entire process: identify what is needed, compare options, select a provider, authorize payment and confirm delivery.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At larger scale, thousands or millions of specialized agents could interact with one another without requiring humans to manually approve every individual step.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, a company’s supply-chain agent could detect that inventory is running low and automatically purchase additional supplies. A software agent could rent additional computing capacity when demand increases. Another agent could negotiate pricing with service providers and settle the resulting transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Each of these activities introduces a financial component.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is where digital assets could potentially become part of the infrastructure supporting the machine economy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Crypto Rails Could Become More Important&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One reason crypto networks are relevant to this discussion is their ability to transfer digital value programmatically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchain-based transactions can be initiated by software, recorded on a shared ledger and settled without requiring the same sequence of human approvals associated with many traditional financial processes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For autonomous systems, programmability could be particularly important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An agent could theoretically be given a wallet, a spending limit and a defined set of rules. It could then make authorized payments according to those parameters while the underlying transactions remain verifiable on a blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Stablecoins could also play an important role in this model because they are designed to represent relatively stable units of value while retaining blockchain-based transfer capabilities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin, meanwhile, occupies a different position in Le’s thesis. Rather than functioning simply as a payment token for every transaction, Bitcoin could serve as a reserve or collateral asset within a broader digital financial ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Strategy’s Bitcoin Treasury Adds Context&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Le’s comments are particularly notable because of Strategy’s position in the Bitcoin market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As of &lt;strong&gt;September 7, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, Strategy held &lt;strong&gt;845,050 BTC&lt;/strong&gt;, according to the company’s latest reported holdings. The position makes Strategy one of the largest corporate Bitcoin holders in the world.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company has also demonstrated that its Bitcoin strategy can involve active capital management rather than simply buying and holding under every circumstance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Strategy sold approximately 7,000 BTC during 2026 while managing its capital requirements, but later resumed accumulation with a purchase of &lt;strong&gt;4,603 BTC at an average price of approximately $80,318 between August 24 and August 30, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That purchase reinforced the company’s broader strategy of maintaining significant Bitcoin exposure while using its capital markets to manage liquidity and funding requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The distinction matters when considering Le’s AI thesis. His argument is not simply that Bitcoin’s price could rise because of artificial intelligence. It is that the underlying financial infrastructure supporting autonomous digital entities could eventually become a much larger market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Strategy Also Expands Its STRC Buyback Program&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI discussion comes as Strategy continues to manage a complex capital structure around its Bitcoin treasury.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Between August 31 and September 7, the company repurchased approximately &lt;strong&gt;$176.3 million&lt;/strong&gt; of its STRC preferred shares. Strategy subsequently increased the authorization for its Digital Credit Securities Repurchase Program from &lt;strong&gt;$1 billion to $2 billion&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company did not purchase or sell Bitcoin during that latest reporting period, leaving its holdings unchanged at 845,050 BTC as of September 7.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The move highlights another part of Strategy’s broader financial strategy: using different forms of capital-market activity to manage its balance sheet while maintaining a large Bitcoin position.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Could an Agent Economy Mean for Crypto?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If autonomous agents become significantly more common, several new financial requirements could emerge.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Machine-to-Machine Payments&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Agents could transact directly with other agents, businesses and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ai-insider-trading-new-market-abuse.html"&gt;digital services&lt;/a&gt;. A machine purchasing computing power from another machine is a simple example of a transaction that could occur continuously without human involvement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Programmable Spending&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Organizations could give agents controlled wallets with predefined limits. Smart contracts and blockchain infrastructure could potentially enforce some of those rules automatically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Global Settlement&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Autonomous agents may operate across different countries and time zones. Digital assets could offer a common settlement layer that is not tied to a single national banking system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Digital Identity and Ownership&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As agents become more capable, questions around identity, authorization and ownership will become increasingly important. An agent may need to prove that it is authorized to act for a person, company or another software system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Risks Are Just as Important&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The machine-economy thesis also comes with significant risks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Giving autonomous software access to money creates obvious security concerns. A compromised agent could potentially send funds to the wrong destination, fall victim to malicious instructions or execute transactions at a scale that would be difficult for a human operator to monitor manually.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Regulation is another major issue.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Financial systems are built around concepts such as identity, authorization, consumer protection and accountability. If an AI agent makes an economic decision independently, regulators and financial institutions will have to determine who ultimately remains responsible for that decision.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is also a question of whether blockchain infrastructure can scale economically enough to support billions or trillions of autonomous interactions. Network capacity, transaction fees, latency, privacy and interoperability will all matter if machine-to-machine commerce becomes widespread.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Phong Le’s Comments Matter for Bitcoin&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Le’s argument connects two major technology trends that are increasingly being discussed together: artificial intelligence and digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI can provide the intelligence required for autonomous decision-making, while blockchain networks can potentially provide programmable ownership and settlement infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That combination could create new financial use cases that are difficult to build using systems designed primarily for human users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the timeline remains uncertain. The idea of trillions of autonomous agents operating economically is a long-term vision rather than a current market reality. The technology, regulation and infrastructure required to reach that scale are still developing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For investors, the important point is therefore not to treat the prediction as a guaranteed forecast. Instead, it offers a framework for understanding why some technology and crypto executives believe the intersection of AI and digital assets could become a major economic trend.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Agents and the Future of Digital Payments&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The potential shift toward autonomous agents could also change the way the market thinks about payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Human consumers generally make a relatively small number of financial decisions each day. Autonomous software could potentially make thousands of smaller decisions on behalf of users or businesses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could create demand for payment systems that are faster, programmable and capable of operating continuously.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, an AI agent managing cloud infrastructure might automatically pay for additional computing resources when demand rises. A travel agent could potentially purchase transportation and accommodation services within a predefined budget. A business agent could settle invoices after verifying that contractual conditions have been met.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These scenarios remain largely conceptual, but they illustrate why the intersection of AI and financial infrastructure has attracted increasing attention from the crypto industry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If such systems become mainstream, the financial infrastructure serving them may need to evolve alongside the underlying AI technology.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Strategy CEO Phong Le believes the rise of autonomous AI agents could eventually create a new class of economic participants that need their own financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;His latest comments to WOLF Financial suggest that once AI agents begin independently performing tasks and interacting with financial systems, digital assets could become part of the infrastructure supporting those activities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That idea fits with Le’s earlier vision of a future involving &lt;strong&gt;6 trillion autonomous agents&lt;/strong&gt; and increasingly programmable financial rails.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Strategy’s enormous Bitcoin treasury gives Le’s comments additional significance. With &lt;strong&gt;845,050 BTC&lt;/strong&gt; held as of September 7, 2026, the company is already deeply positioned around the digital-asset economy while continuing to develop its capital-market strategy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Whether the world eventually reaches the scale of autonomous economic activity Le envisions remains an open question. But the convergence of AI agents, programmable payments and digital assets is becoming an increasingly important theme for the cryptocurrency industry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What did Strategy CEO Phong Le say about AI agents?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Phong Le said that once autonomous agents begin running errands and interacting with the financial system, “they’re going to want digital assets behind it too.”&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What does Phong Le mean by autonomous agents?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;He is referring to AI systems capable of making decisions and carrying out tasks with limited human intervention, potentially including commercial and financial activities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is Phong Le’s 6 trillion agents prediction?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In a June 2026 interview, Le described a future in which the world could evolve toward approximately 6 trillion autonomous decision-making agents operating across digital and financial systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How much Bitcoin does Strategy hold?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Strategy reported holding &lt;strong&gt;845,050 BTC as of September 7, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;When did Strategy purchase 4,603 BTC?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Strategy purchased &lt;strong&gt;4,603 BTC between August 24 and August 30, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, at an average price of approximately &lt;strong&gt;$80,318 per Bitcoin&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why could AI agents use digital assets?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Digital assets and blockchain networks can provide programmable value-transfer and global-settlement capabilities that may be useful for autonomous software conducting machine-to-machine transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Disclaimer:&lt;/strong&gt; This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute financial, investment or trading advice. Cryptocurrency and digital-asset markets are highly volatile. Readers should conduct their own research before making investment decisions.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>If You Don't Move Your Crypto Before Q-Day, Here's What Actually Happens</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgEWDktSc9qrBJ9suVpJJdOab4-Lh2n2jQuTRXpeBJ6t5pWwPxWl1u03HgPDEN0j66WH7rUEDQBDbnbM7MlF6EVG6I6MUdhHHISCOBOUVfjnj2V9lW7avYytm4zEiQuCE120mPBAy98OA9HX2xMSXmYuV3tqdsBWZp4gsQQ7XHrYzJ5gjFX5HZAHbPTTe8K/s1672/crypto-q-day-quantum-security.jpg.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Quantum computer threatening cryptocurrency security and blockchain cryptography" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgEWDktSc9qrBJ9suVpJJdOab4-Lh2n2jQuTRXpeBJ6t5pWwPxWl1u03HgPDEN0j66WH7rUEDQBDbnbM7MlF6EVG6I6MUdhHHISCOBOUVfjnj2V9lW7avYytm4zEiQuCE120mPBAy98OA9HX2xMSXmYuV3tqdsBWZp4gsQQ7XHrYzJ5gjFX5HZAHbPTTe8K/w320-h180/crypto-q-day-quantum-security.jpg.png" title="Crypto Q-Day Quantum Security" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;b style="font-family: verdana; font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&amp;nbsp;|&amp;nbsp;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Here's a nightmare scenario that keeps crypto security
experts up at night: one morning, you open your wallet, and everything is
just... gone. Not because you fell for a phishing scam or an exchange
collapsed. Because a machine finally figured out the math that was supposed to
keep your coins safe.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;That's the reality of Q-Day—the moment when a
sufficiently powerful quantum computer can break the cryptography protecting
digital assets. And if you don't move your assets in time, the outcome depends
on a mix of technology and governance decisions that are still being debated.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;The Short Answer: Your Coins Could Become
Unspendable—or Worse&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;If a user doesn't migrate their c&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/chinas-data-strategy-could-give-it-edge.html"&gt;ryptocurrency&lt;/a&gt; to a
quantum-resistant address before Q-Day arrives, their assets could be at risk
in several ways. An attacker with a cryptographically relevant quantum computer
could derive the private key from an exposed public key and potentially spend
the coins themselves.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;The underlying cryptographic risk is well understood,
although the timing and feasibility of a practical quantum attack remain
uncertain. Once a public key is exposed on-chain, an attacker can record it and
potentially use it later if a cryptographically relevant quantum computer
becomes available. They don't need a quantum computer today. They just need to
wait.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Some Addresses Are Already Vulnerable&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Not all addresses face the same level of risk. For
Bitcoin, quantum exposure depends heavily on the cryptographic scheme used and
whether the relevant public key has already been revealed on-chain.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;🔴 Extremely High&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="border-bottom: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-color: currentcolor rgb(221, 221, 221) rgb(221, 221, 221) currentcolor; border-left: none; border-right: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-style: none solid solid none; border-top: none; border-width: medium 1pt 1pt medium; mso-border-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-left-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; padding: 9pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana;"&gt;Public key is written directly into the script and is
  visible from the moment coins are received.&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
 &lt;tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 2;"&gt;
  &lt;td style="border-top: none; border: 1pt solid rgb(221, 221, 221); mso-border-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; padding: 9pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;P2PKH (most modern addresses)&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="border-bottom: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-color: currentcolor rgb(221, 221, 221) rgb(221, 221, 221) currentcolor; border-left: none; border-right: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-style: none solid solid none; border-top: none; border-width: medium 1pt 1pt medium; mso-border-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-left-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; padding: 9pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;🟡 Conditional&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="border-bottom: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-color: currentcolor rgb(221, 221, 221) rgb(221, 221, 221) currentcolor; border-left: none; border-right: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-style: none solid solid none; border-top: none; border-width: medium 1pt 1pt medium; mso-border-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-left-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; padding: 9pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana;"&gt;Public key is hidden behind a hash until you spend.
  Once spent, the key becomes visible on-chain; reusing the address keeps the
  key exposed.&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
 &lt;tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 3; mso-yfti-lastrow: yes;"&gt;
  &lt;td style="border-top: none; border: 1pt solid rgb(221, 221, 221); mso-border-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; padding: 9pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;Taproot&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="border-bottom: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-color: currentcolor rgb(221, 221, 221) rgb(221, 221, 221) currentcolor; border-left: none; border-right: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-style: none solid solid none; border-top: none; border-width: medium 1pt 1pt medium; mso-border-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-left-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; padding: 9pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;🟡 Conditional&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="border-bottom: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-color: currentcolor rgb(221, 221, 221) rgb(221, 221, 221) currentcolor; border-left: none; border-right: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-style: none solid solid none; border-top: none; border-width: medium 1pt 1pt medium; mso-border-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-left-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; padding: 9pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana;"&gt;Uses Schnorr signatures and improves efficiency and
  privacy, but remains vulnerable to a sufficiently powerful quantum computer.&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Research cited in discussions around Bitcoin's quantum
risk estimates that more than 34% of bitcoin had revealed a public key on-chain
as of March 1, 2026. Coinbase's Quantum Advisory Council estimates that
roughly&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;1.7 million BTC&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;sit in P2PK addresses with exposed
public keys. When address reuse and other vulnerable output types are
considered, approximately&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;7 million BTC&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;could currently be
vulnerable to future quantum attacks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;What Happens After a Post-Quantum Upgrade?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Here's where it gets tricky. A blockchain can add
post-quantum cryptography to protect new addresses and future transactions. But
that&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;does not retroactively secure funds&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;that remain locked to
an old, quantum-vulnerable public key.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Think of it like upgrading the locks on a building. The
new locks protect new tenants, but if you don't change your own lock, the old
one is still vulnerable.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Once funds are successfully migrated under a
quantum-resistant authentication scheme, an attacker who later derives the old
private key would no longer control those migrated funds. But if your funds
stay at the old address when a quantum computer arrives, an attacker could
potentially derive your private key and spend your coins.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;The Governance Dilemma: What Happens to Unmoved Coins?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Once the technical migration is complete, the real fight
begins—and it's not technical at all. It's governance.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;The debate over what should happen to dormant or
quantum-vulnerable Bitcoin is already underway, with proposals ranging from
migration deadlines and freezes to &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/gen-z-on-binance-is-quietly-rewriting.html"&gt;mechanisms&lt;/a&gt; that would allow legitimate
holders to prove control.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;BIP-361&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;i&gt;, a draft proposal authored by
Bitcoin researchers including Jameson Lopp, outlines a phased transition that
would eventually render certain legacy outputs unspendable unless users migrate
to quantum-resistant alternatives. The proposal is currently a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;draft
informational BIP&lt;/b&gt;—it has not been activated and does not currently require
Bitcoin holders to move their funds.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;But the pushback is fierce. Critics argue that making
dormant coins unspendable undermines Bitcoin's core principles of immutability
and user autonomy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Which Blockchains Are Preparing?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Several major networks are already exploring migration
paths. The plans vary significantly in timeline and approach:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Under discussion&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="border-bottom: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-color: currentcolor rgb(221, 221, 221) rgb(221, 221, 221) currentcolor; border-left: none; border-right: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-style: none solid solid none; border-top: none; border-width: medium 1pt 1pt medium; mso-border-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-left-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; padding: 9pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana;"&gt;EIP-8141 (Frame Transactions) is being&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;explored as a
  precondition for&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana;"&gt;post-quantum migration and&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana;"&gt;remains under consideration.&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
 &lt;tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 6; mso-yfti-lastrow: yes;"&gt;
  &lt;td style="border-top: none; border: 1pt solid rgb(221, 221, 221); mso-border-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; padding: 9pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="border-bottom: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-color: currentcolor rgb(221, 221, 221) rgb(221, 221, 221) currentcolor; border-left: none; border-right: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-style: none solid solid none; border-top: none; border-width: medium 1pt 1pt medium; mso-border-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-left-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; padding: 9pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;No official timeline&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="border-bottom: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-color: currentcolor rgb(221, 221, 221) rgb(221, 221, 221) currentcolor; border-left: none; border-right: solid #DDDDDD 1.0pt; border-style: none solid solid none; border-top: none; border-width: medium 1pt 1pt medium; mso-border-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-left-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; mso-border-top-alt: solid #DDDDDD .75pt; padding: 9pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana;"&gt;BIP-361 is a draft proposal; there is&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana;"&gt;currently no
  consensus or migration&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana;"&gt;deadline.&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;XRPL: Ripple's Four-Phase Roadmap to 2028&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Ripple has laid out a detailed four-phase plan to make
the XRP Ledger quantum-resistant by 2028.&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Phase 1&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;(Q-Day
readiness) is an emergency measure that would force a migration to quantum-safe
accounts if quantum threats arrive sooner than expected.&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Phase 2&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;(H1
2026) involves Ripple's cryptography team conducting a full assessment of
quantum vulnerability and testing NIST-recommended algorithms.&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Phase 3&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;(H2
2026) involves integrating quantum-resistant signatures alongside existing ones
on the developer test network.&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Phase 4&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;targets a full mainnet
upgrade by 2028.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Stellar: Quantum Preparedness Plan&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Stellar's Quantum Preparedness Plan aims to enable every
Stellar account to add a quantum-safe signer through a native protocol upgrade
by the&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;end of 2027&lt;/b&gt;, keeping the same address and history. The
network's structural advantage lies in separating account identity from signing
keys—accounts can rotate keys through the existing&amp;nbsp;set_options&amp;nbsp;operation
without changing their address.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Sui: Native Post-Quantum Signatures&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Sui is adding two NIST-approved post-quantum signature
schemes:&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;ML-DSA-65&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;for everyday accounts and&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;for
high-value Move vaults. Quantum-safe vaults are targeted for Mainnet in 2026,
with native ML-DSA-65 accounts reaching Testnet by&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;end of 2026&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;and
native account authentication on Mainnet targeted for&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Q1 2027&lt;/b&gt;. All
timelines remain subject to audits and Testnet feedback.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Zcash: Ironwood Upgrade&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Zcash's Ironwood upgrade is designed to introduce
quantum-recoverable notes through ZIP 2005. This is designed as groundwork for
a smoother future transition—it does not by itself make the protocol fully
secure against quantum adversaries, but allows funds in the Ironwood pool to be
retrieved through a future Recovery Protocol if needed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Ethereum: EIP-8141 Under Consideration&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Ethereum's&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;EIP-8141&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;(Frame
Transactions), proposed by Vitalik Buterin, aims to decouple accounts from
fixed signature schemes and provide a native migration path for post-quantum
signature schemes. The proposal is currently under consideration for inclusion
in future upgrades but has not yet been finalized.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin: BIP-361 Remains a Draft&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;BIP-361&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;i&gt;, titled "Post Quantum
Migration and Legacy Signature Sunset," was first assigned on February 11,
2026, and remains a draft informational proposal. It has not been activated and
does not currently require Bitcoin holders to move their funds. The proposal
would gradually restrict legacy transactions through a multi-phase transition,
but a separate post-quantum signature standard would need to be agreed upon
first.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;The quantum threat is real enough that major blockchains
are building migration paths—but no existing quantum computer is currently
capable of breaking the cryptography used by major blockchains, and the
timeline for a cryptographically relevant quantum computer remains uncertain.
Google Quantum AI research has provided estimates under specific assumptions,
but there is still no reliable date for Q-Day.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;If you don't migrate in time, your options could be
limited:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Your
     coins could be stolen by someone with a quantum computer.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Your
     coins could be frozen by the network if it chooses a "burn"
     approach.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Your
     coins could become trapped in an address that no one can spend from or
     protect.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;Most blockchains are building migration paths, and users
may have a migration window once individual networks activate their
post-quantum transition. The timing and duration will depend on each
blockchain's governance and upgrade process.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;If a blockchain establishes a migration deadline, that
window may not remain open indefinitely. And for a generation of holders
accustomed to the idea that crypto is "unstoppable," the quantum
threat raises an uncomfortable question: what happens to an unstoppable asset
when the math that protects it stops working?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;The answer depends largely on governance decisions made
by each blockchain community—and on whether you move in time.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: verdana; font-size: medium;"&gt;

not constitute investment advice. The quantum threat timeline remains
uncertain, and users should follow official guidance from their blockchain
networks regarding post-quantum migration.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>U.S. Bank Launches USBDC Stablecoin Pilot on Stellar for Cross-Border Payments</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgKAI2M2bb3TwOdGh5kcHAnsG4bKuo6-XIWVbB5r9bV4kUntqnTzbWYSUNioJp2WrnRgYlEghQNor1PkYRmHg-izAXLTf5yN3Cn1ZYqgjkCMWVeaJfa9wOP_CoAHn0hHD2JtscVvJvnm87WPhYNxdV3P2ig-W5y4yXo56KABVbpTqo83erEP7wnNBqLnUaa/s1672/us-bank-usbdc-stablecoin-stellar-cross-border-payments.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="U.S. Bank launches USBDC stablecoin pilot on Stellar for cross-border payments" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgKAI2M2bb3TwOdGh5kcHAnsG4bKuo6-XIWVbB5r9bV4kUntqnTzbWYSUNioJp2WrnRgYlEghQNor1PkYRmHg-izAXLTf5yN3Cn1ZYqgjkCMWVeaJfa9wOP_CoAHn0hHD2JtscVvJvnm87WPhYNxdV3P2ig-W5y4yXo56KABVbpTqo83erEP7wnNBqLnUaa/w640-h360/us-bank-usbdc-stablecoin-stellar-cross-border-payments.jpg.png" title="U.S. Bank Launches USBDC Stablecoin on Stellar" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;U.S. Bank has taken a major step into bank-issued stablecoins, completing a live pilot transaction using its proprietary &lt;strong&gt;USBDC&lt;/strong&gt; dollar-backed stablecoin on the &lt;strong&gt;Stellar blockchain&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The transaction moved value between U.S. Bank entities in North America and Europe, marking a shift from the bank's earlier stablecoin experimentation toward a live operational test of blockchain-based money movement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank said the pilot was designed to demonstrate that it can move funds on a public blockchain while maintaining its existing finance, risk, compliance and operational controls.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The development is significant for the stablecoin industry because the experiment involves a major U.S. bank using its own dollar-backed &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/hunter-biden-laptop-memecoin-crash-86-5-percent.html"&gt;digital asset&lt;/a&gt; on a public blockchain rather than relying solely on an existing third-party stablecoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;U.S. Bank's USBDC Goes From Testing to a Live Payment&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank announced that it successfully executed a live pilot transaction using USBDC for a cross-border payment between its North American and European entities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The transaction was completed on Stellar, a blockchain that has developed a strong focus on payments, tokenized assets and financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to U.S. Bank, the pilot tested several important functions of the stablecoin, including &lt;strong&gt;minting, payment execution, redemption, freezing and clawback capabilities&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those features are particularly important for a regulated financial institution. A traditional bank needs more than the ability to send a token from one blockchain address to another. It also needs controls that allow the institution to manage transactions, meet compliance requirements and respond to operational or regulatory events.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank said the pilot demonstrated how its &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/blog-post.html"&gt;blockchain infrastructure&lt;/a&gt; can work alongside the bank's existing financial, risk, compliance and operations systems. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is USBDC?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;USBDC is U.S. Bank's proprietary U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Unlike Bitcoin or other volatile crypto assets, a dollar-backed stablecoin is designed to maintain a stable value relative to the U.S. dollar and can be used for digital payments and settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In U.S. Bank's case, USBDC is being developed as part of the bank's broader digital-assets and money-movement strategy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bank created its dedicated &lt;strong&gt;Digital Assets and Money Movement&lt;/strong&gt; organization in 2025 to work on areas including stablecoin issuance, cryptocurrency custody, asset tokenization and digital money movement. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank has also been involved in the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/defi-development-corp-raises-11m-with.html"&gt;stablecoin&lt;/a&gt; ecosystem as a reserve custodian. In 2025, it announced that it would provide custody services for reserves backing payment stablecoins issued by Anchorage Digital Bank. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Stellar Matters to the U.S. Bank Stablecoin&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The choice of Stellar is one of the most important parts of the USBDC development.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Stellar was designed with payments and asset issuance in mind, and the network has increasingly attracted financial institutions exploring tokenized assets and stablecoin-based settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Stellar says its infrastructure supports global payments, asset tokenization and on-chain financial applications. The network also hosts established dollar-backed assets such as Circle's USDC. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For U.S. Bank, using a public blockchain allows the bank to test whether blockchain settlement can improve the movement of money while still retaining the controls expected from a regulated financial institution.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That combination—&lt;strong&gt;public blockchain infrastructure plus traditional banking controls&lt;/strong&gt;—is central to the USBDC experiment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;USBDC Could Target 24/7 Money Movement&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the biggest potential advantages of a bank-issued stablecoin is that blockchain networks do not operate according to the traditional banking calendar.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank said USBDC could eventually support applications involving &lt;strong&gt;24/7 transaction capabilities&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could be particularly relevant for cross-border treasury operations, where traditional payment systems can involve multiple intermediaries, operating hours and settlement processes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, U.S. Bank has not announced that USBDC is already available as a general-purpose customer payment product. The current development is a live pilot and part of the bank's continuing digital-asset strategy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What U.S. Bank Tested With USBDC&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Creates the digital representation of &lt;br /&gt;dollars for the stablecoin system.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Payment&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Allows USBDC to be transferred &lt;br /&gt;between participating entities.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Redemption&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Tests converting the digital asset back &lt;br /&gt;through the bank's stablecoin infrastructure.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Freezing&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Provides an administrative control for &lt;br /&gt;the tokenized asset.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Clawback&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Tests whether the system can recover &lt;br /&gt;or reverse eligible funds under defined controls.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The inclusion of freezing and clawback functions is especially notable because it shows how a regulated bank is approaching blockchain differently from a purely decentralized cryptocurrency system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;U.S. Bank Is Building Its Own Digital Asset Platform&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The USBDC pilot also tested U.S. Bank's internally developed &lt;strong&gt;Digital Asset Platform&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bank describes the platform as infrastructure for issuing, managing and moving tokenized assets while connecting blockchain networks with its traditional financial systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That infrastructure could eventually allow U.S. Bank to use blockchain technology without requiring every part of its existing banking operation to be rebuilt around a public network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is an important distinction. The bank is not simply experimenting with a cryptocurrency wallet. It is testing an infrastructure layer designed to connect blockchain-based assets with conventional banking operations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;USBDC Could Go Beyond Cross-Border Payments&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank said it is exploring several potential applications for its stablecoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These include:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Cross-border treasury operations&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Liquidity management&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Collateral mobility&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;24/7 money movement&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Other institutional settlement applications&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These use cases point toward a broader transformation in how financial institutions could move money between their own entities and counterparties.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of using blockchain primarily as a speculative asset market, banks are increasingly examining whether tokenized dollars can function as programmable settlement instruments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;This Is Not Yet a Retail Stablecoin Launch&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is an important distinction between saying &lt;strong&gt;“U.S. Bank launched USBDC”&lt;/strong&gt; and saying that USBDC is now available to everyone.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bank has completed a live pilot, but it has not announced a broad commercial rollout of USBDC for retail customers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank also has not provided a specific date for when the stablecoin could become generally available to clients. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For that reason, the most accurate description is that &lt;strong&gt;U.S. Bank has launched and executed a live USBDC pilot on Stellar&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than claiming that the stablecoin is already a widely available payment product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;USBDC Comes as Banks Race Into Stablecoins&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank's move comes as traditional financial institutions increasingly explore stablecoins as a new payment and settlement technology.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Reuters reported that several major banks—including Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, Citigroup and Wells Fargo—are planning a company aimed at issuing a dollar-pegged cryptocurrency, with a targeted launch in the first half of 2027. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The growing interest is also being supported by the development of a clearer U.S. regulatory framework for payment stablecoins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The GENIUS Act established a federal framework for payment stablecoins, while regulators have continued to clarify how qualifying stablecoins should be treated under securities rules. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That regulatory progress could make it easier for banks and other regulated financial institutions to develop blockchain-based payment products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why This Matters for Stellar and XLM&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;USBDC's use of Stellar is also significant for the broader Stellar ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A live transaction involving a major U.S. bank provides another real-world example of Stellar being used for institutional financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the USBDC announcement should &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; be interpreted as a guarantee that XLM will rise in price.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The pilot demonstrates use of the Stellar blockchain, but that is different from announcing a direct investment in XLM or a specific future price impact for the token.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For investors, the more meaningful development is the potential validation of Stellar as infrastructure for regulated financial applications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next for USBDC?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next stage will be determining whether the pilot can move beyond controlled transactions and into broader institutional use.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank is already evaluating additional applications involving liquidity, collateral and treasury operations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If those experiments prove commercially useful, USBDC could eventually become part of a wider digital money infrastructure connecting traditional banking systems with public blockchains.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But that transition will depend on regulatory requirements, operational controls, client demand and the economics of blockchain settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Shift: Banks Are Bringing Dollars On-Chain&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most important part of the USBDC announcement may not be the name of the stablecoin or even the size of the pilot.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is the direction of the financial industry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For years, public blockchains were primarily associated with cryptocurrencies and decentralized finance. Banks are now increasingly testing whether the same infrastructure can support regulated money movement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank's live USBDC transaction on Stellar is another example of that shift.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If bank-issued stablecoins become widely adopted, blockchain networks could increasingly operate as settlement infrastructure for traditional financial institutions rather than simply as markets for digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is USBDC?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;USBDC is U.S. Bank's proprietary U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin being developed for digital money movement and institutional use cases.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Which blockchain is USBDC using?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank completed its live USBDC pilot transaction on the &lt;strong&gt;Stellar blockchain&lt;/strong&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Did U.S. Bank launch USBDC?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank announced the successful execution of a live USBDC pilot. The bank has not announced broad commercial availability of the stablecoin to all customers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What did U.S. Bank test with USBDC?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The pilot tested minting, payment, redemption, freezing and clawback capabilities through the bank's digital asset infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can customers buy USBDC now?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;U.S. Bank has not announced general public availability or a commercial launch date for USBDC. The current announcement concerns a live pilot transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Will USBDC increase the price of XLM?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;There is no basis for predicting a specific XLM price impact from the announcement. The confirmed development is that U.S. Bank used Stellar for its USBDC pilot.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why is U.S. Bank testing a stablecoin?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The bank is exploring whether blockchain-based dollars can improve cross-border payments, liquidity management, collateral mobility and treasury operations while maintaining traditional banking controls.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;U.S. Bank has moved its stablecoin strategy another step forward with a live USBDC transaction on Stellar.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The pilot transferred value between U.S. Bank entities in North America and Europe and tested core stablecoin functions including minting, redemption, freezing and clawback.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The announcement does not mean USBDC is already a mass-market stablecoin. Instead, it shows that one of the largest U.S. banking institutions is testing whether a proprietary dollar-backed digital asset can operate on public blockchain infrastructure while remaining connected to traditional banking controls.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the stablecoin sector, that may be the bigger story: &lt;strong&gt;banks are no longer just watching blockchain payments—they are beginning to test their own digital dollars in live environments.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Disclaimer:&lt;/strong&gt; This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute financial or investment advice. Readers should conduct their own research before making decisions involving cryptocurrencies, stablecoins or digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Solmate Adds 1,000 SOL, Confirms AI Push Won't Change Solana Commitment</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article class="news-article"&gt;

  &lt;figure&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgjpxAalrO0kg9U_Z-1cxVRoze9H6dR6p9uyMdOAinoj-x0wHv1YSv0FkupH8uc7y-Y9CHV5qustzs_a2AjQh79Hfi43-K4TPYI9uDXGKtN0K1kt07JK34rLBwfCBO8ML2TqFGMltRm33qtW5qeZSK_E-QuoKVWQsjgixarqvlMwXp3kFVj6XRDpUn5KdJ5/s1672/solmate-adds-1000-sol-ai-infrastructure-solana-2026.jpg.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Solmate adds Solana to its crypto treasury while expanding into AI infrastructure" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgjpxAalrO0kg9U_Z-1cxVRoze9H6dR6p9uyMdOAinoj-x0wHv1YSv0FkupH8uc7y-Y9CHV5qustzs_a2AjQh79Hfi43-K4TPYI9uDXGKtN0K1kt07JK34rLBwfCBO8ML2TqFGMltRm33qtW5qeZSK_E-QuoKVWQsjgixarqvlMwXp3kFVj6XRDpUn5KdJ5/w400-h225/solmate-adds-1000-sol-ai-infrastructure-solana-2026.jpg.png" title="Solmate Adds 1,000 SOL as AI Expansion Continues" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;figure&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Solmate Infrastructure&lt;/strong&gt;, a Nasdaq-listed company focused on
    building a Solana treasury, has added another &lt;strong&gt;1,000 SOL&lt;/strong&gt;
    to its holdings. The purchase takes the company's total SOL position to
    &lt;strong&gt;1.25 million SOL&lt;/strong&gt;, valued at roughly
    &lt;strong&gt;$102.2 million&lt;/strong&gt; based on the reference price cited by the company.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
    The purchase comes as Solmate expands into AI infrastructure. Rather than
    presenting the two strategies as alternatives, the company says its AI
    plans are intended to complement its existing focus on Solana.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Numbers Behind the Purchase&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;div style="background: rgb(17, 17, 17); border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid rgb(51, 51, 51); color: white; min-width: 500px; overflow: hidden;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
    According to the company's announcement, the acquisition was completed on
    &lt;strong&gt;August 20&lt;/strong&gt;. With the additional purchase, Solmate's SOL
    treasury now stands at more than one million tokens and has a reported
    value above $100 million based on the company's cited reference price.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The CEO's Message: AI and Solana Are Complementary&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
    Solmate CEO &lt;strong&gt;Ron Sade&lt;/strong&gt; said the company's move into &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/openai-sets-2027-ipo-target-cfo-says-we.html"&gt;AI    infrastructure&lt;/a&gt; does not represent a change in its view of Solana.
    Instead, management sees the two areas as complementary parts of its
    broader growth strategy.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;blockquote style="background: rgba(128, 128, 128, 0.08); border-left: 4px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); margin: 24px 0px; padding: 18px 20px;"&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 0px 0px 8px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
      "We see these strategies as complementary, not competing. Our expansion
      into AI infrastructure is about creating additional opportunities for
      growth while our conviction in Solana remains unchanged."
    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
    &lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;cite&gt;— Ron Sade, Solmate CEO&lt;/cite&gt;
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/blockquote&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
    The company believes that combining continued SOL accumulation,
    transparent reporting and AI infrastructure expansion gives it exposure
    to two major areas of the technology market: decentralized digital
    infrastructure and artificial intelligence.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why the Treasury Dashboard Matters&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
    The latest purchase also follows Solmate's launch of a
    &lt;strong&gt;public treasury dashboard&lt;/strong&gt;. The dashboard is updated once
    each trading day and is designed to give shareholders a clearer view of
    the company's SOL holdings and staking activity.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
    For investors following digital-asset treasury companies, more frequent
    reporting can make it easier to track changes in holdings between regular
    corporate disclosures. It also gives the market a more current view of
    how the company's &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/banks-rotating-into-ethereum-3x-faster.html"&gt;crypto treasury&lt;/a&gt; is changing.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;blockquote style="background: rgba(128, 128, 128, 0.08); border-left: 4px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); margin: 24px 0px; padding: 18px 20px;"&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 0px 0px 8px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
      "We have continued to build our SOL position in a disciplined way, and
      we believe shareholders should be able to see the results of that work
      on a regular basis."
    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
    &lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;cite&gt;— Ron Sade, Solmate CEO&lt;/cite&gt;
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/blockquote&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;AI Expansion Adds a New Layer to the Strategy&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
    Solmate's move into AI infrastructure adds another layer to what has
    primarily been a Solana-focused treasury strategy. The company is not
    describing the expansion as a replacement for its SOL holdings.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
    Instead, AI infrastructure is being positioned as another potential
    growth opportunity while Solmate continues to build its digital-asset
    treasury. That makes the latest SOL purchase notable because it came
    alongside, rather than instead of, the company's technology expansion.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Investors Should Watch Next&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
    The next question is whether Solmate continues adding SOL at a similar
    pace while developing its AI infrastructure business. Future treasury
    purchases, changes in staking activity and additional details about its
    AI operations should provide a clearer picture of how the strategy develops.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
    The dollar value of Solmate's SOL holdings will also continue to move with
    the market price of Solana. The reported valuation should therefore be
    viewed as a reference figure rather than a fixed value.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
    Solmate has added another &lt;strong&gt;1,000 SOL&lt;/strong&gt; to an already
    substantial treasury while continuing its expansion into AI infrastructure.
    For now, the company is making it clear that the two strategies are meant
    to work alongside each other rather than compete.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
    Whether that combination ultimately creates value for shareholders will
    depend on SOL's performance, the execution of Solmate's AI strategy and
    the company's ability to manage both areas effectively. For now, the latest
    purchase shows that its commitment to building a Solana treasury remains
    firmly in place.
  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Bernstein Sees Prediction Markets Reaching $10 Trillion by 2035 as Crypto and Stocks Gain Ground</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;
  &lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjXhu1rX1hp3mgkwm_qwZvhKNtr5Oxz6-__vXSGbq7hhog4hX3hMeZR5K7UgTuV2FZ4x0YR-TS0Jkss0wsCLQrgtrOa99L6GjcuHBKpc-f9jxaChD80BcXdWZ7LT2Vdz-czfqmDOB7wJ4ku4Lwsiz3m636FYvSvwvDemJGWnch8DwygWVUzTSEvhMOX3RDe/s1734/bernstein-10-trillion-prediction-markets-2035.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bernstein forecasts $10 trillion prediction market volume by 2035 as crypto stocks and commodities grow" border="0" data-original-height="907" data-original-width="1734" height="334" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjXhu1rX1hp3mgkwm_qwZvhKNtr5Oxz6-__vXSGbq7hhog4hX3hMeZR5K7UgTuV2FZ4x0YR-TS0Jkss0wsCLQrgtrOa99L6GjcuHBKpc-f9jxaChD80BcXdWZ7LT2Vdz-czfqmDOB7wJ4ku4Lwsiz3m636FYvSvwvDemJGWnch8DwygWVUzTSEvhMOX3RDe/w640-h334/bernstein-10-trillion-prediction-markets-2035.webp.png" title="Bernstein $10 Trillion Prediction Market Forecast" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By CoinAINews Editorial Team&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;Prediction markets may be moving toward a much bigger role in global trading than their current sports-heavy image suggests.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bernstein now forecasts that annual prediction-market trading volume could reach &lt;strong&gt;$10 trillion by 2035&lt;/strong&gt;, a dramatic increase from the roughly $410 billion the firm expects for 2026. The research firm also sees financial contracts tied to cryptocurrencies, equities and commodities eventually overtaking sports as the largest category of prediction-market activity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The forecast marks a major change from Bernstein's earlier outlook. In April, the firm had projected that prediction markets could reach approximately $1 trillion in annual volume by 2030. Its new $10 trillion 2035 estimate is therefore substantially more ambitious. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bernstein's $10 Trillion Prediction-Market Forecast&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;According to Bernstein analysts led by Gautam Chhugani, prediction-market volume could rise from approximately &lt;strong&gt;$50 billion in 2025&lt;/strong&gt; to about &lt;strong&gt;$410 billion in 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, before expanding toward $10 trillion annually by 2035.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The forecast implies extremely rapid growth over the period. Bernstein expects the industry to expand at roughly a 70% compound annual growth rate from its relatively small 2025 base. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That number needs some context. A prediction-market volume figure represents the value of contracts traded, not the amount of money operators would necessarily earn as revenue. Trading volume and revenue are very different measurements.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The $10 trillion figure is therefore best understood as Bernstein's estimate for annual trading activity if prediction markets successfully expand into a much wider range of financial and real-world contracts.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Crypto, Stocks and Commodities Could Overtake Sports&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The most interesting part of the forecast may not be the $10 trillion headline itself.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It is the expected change in what people trade.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bernstein estimates that financial-asset contracts—including crypto, equities and commodities—represented around &lt;strong&gt;12% of prediction-market volume in 2025&lt;/strong&gt;. By 2035, the firm expects that category to reach approximately &lt;strong&gt;49%&lt;/strong&gt; of total volume.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Sports, meanwhile, accounted for roughly 61% of volume in 2025. Bernstein expects sports' share to decline to about 38% by 2035 as financial contracts expand more rapidly. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That does not necessarily mean sports prediction markets would become smaller in absolute terms. Instead, the forecast assumes financial markets grow much faster and take a larger percentage of the overall market.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
    &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); width: 100%;"&gt;
