  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Crypto Is Becoming Important to Prediction Markets&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Crypto is one of the areas where the shift is already becoming visible.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Short-duration contracts can give traders considerably more opportunities to trade than traditional event markets. Instead of waiting weeks for an election or months for a major sporting event, participants can trade contracts tied to short-term movements in assets such as &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/arthur-hayes-ai-safety-anthropic-ipo-2026.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bernstein points to this development as part of the reason financial contracts could become a much larger portion of prediction-market activity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Data cited in recent reporting shows that crypto's share of Kalshi volume increased from less than 5% in January to roughly 20% in August 2026. Commodity activity has also expanded, although from a much smaller base. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The significance is not simply that crypto contracts are popular. It is that crypto markets operate continuously, giving prediction-market platforms a potentially large supply of events and price-related questions that can settle quickly.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Prediction Markets Could Move Beyond Simple Yes-or-No Bets&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The traditional image of a prediction market is a simple question: Will an event happen or not?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That model is changing.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bernstein expects prediction platforms to introduce contracts linked to corporate performance indicators, production numbers, deliveries, subscriber growth and other measurable outcomes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Such products could allow traders to take positions on specific business metrics without necessarily buying or shorting the company's stock itself.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The firm also highlighted the expansion of perpetual futures from crypto into commodities and individual stocks. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If these products become widely adopted, prediction markets could begin to look less like specialized event-betting websites and more like another layer of financial-market infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The $4.7 Trillion Financial-Contract Opportunity&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bernstein's long-term projection is based partly on the enormous size of the underlying financial markets.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The firm's analysis estimates the addressable market for financial assets such as crypto, equities and commodities at roughly $700 trillion in 2025, potentially reaching about $900 trillion by 2035.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bernstein's model assumes prediction markets capture only around 0.5% of that broader market by 2035. Even that relatively small penetration rate would translate into approximately &lt;strong&gt;$4.7 trillion of annual financial-asset prediction-market volume&lt;/strong&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That assumption is important because it shows where the $10 trillion forecast comes from. Bernstein is not simply assuming sports prediction markets become 20 times larger. The thesis depends on prediction markets expanding into financial assets and other measurable outcomes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Kalshi and Polymarket Show Different Market Mixes&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The current prediction-market landscape also illustrates why the industry may be difficult to define as a single category.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Kalshi has seen a substantial increase in financial-contract activity, including crypto and commodities. Recent reporting based on Bernstein's analysis put Kalshi's share of overall industry volume at approximately 60% through August 2026. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Polymarket has a different mix. Sports remained its largest category in 2026 through August, while political and crypto markets also represented significant portions of activity. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Those differences matter because prediction markets are not all following exactly the same business model or attracting exactly the same users.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Regulation Remains a Major Variable&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The industry's growth is also facing regulatory uncertainty, particularly in the United States.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Prediction-market operators have increasingly offered contracts tied to sports and financial events, raising questions about where certain products fall between financial derivatives regulation and state gambling laws.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Reuters reported recently that legal disputes over sports contracts remain unresolved, with federal courts divided over aspects of federal versus state oversight. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bernstein reportedly does not expect full regulatory clarity for U.S. sports prediction markets until at least 2027 or 2028. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For the $10 trillion forecast to materialize, regulatory access will be an important factor. A prediction-market industry expanding into financial contracts at global scale would require reliable market infrastructure, clear rules and participation from institutions as well as retail traders.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Prediction Markets Could Attract Institutional Traders&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Institutional participation is another part of the long-term thesis.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Financial institutions are already exploring ways to integrate prediction-market data into existing trading infrastructure. Reuters has reported that established financial-market companies are becoming involved as the sector develops. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The attraction is partly about information.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A prediction-market price can provide a continuously updated market-based estimate of the probability of a defined event. A contract trading at 70 cents, for example, can be interpreted as a market-implied probability of roughly 70%, although that interpretation comes with important assumptions and is not the same as a guaranteed forecast.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;As more traders participate, the resulting prices could become another data point for analysts, businesses and financial institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What the $10 Trillion Forecast Does Not Mean&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bernstein's projection should not be interpreted as a guarantee that prediction markets will reach $10 trillion.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The forecast depends on several assumptions: continued user growth, new financial products, regulatory developments, institutional participation and the ability of platforms to create sufficient liquidity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Competition could also change the market. Traditional exchanges, brokers, sportsbooks and technology companies could enter areas currently dominated by specialist prediction-market platforms.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There is also a difference between trading volume and economic value. A contract can be traded multiple times before it expires, meaning a large volume number does not represent an equivalent amount of unique capital entering the market.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why the Forecast Matters for Crypto&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For the crypto industry, Bernstein's projection is notable because it places digital assets inside a broader transformation of prediction-market trading.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin and other &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/how-crypto-agencies-can-offer-white.html"&gt;cryptocurrencies&lt;/a&gt; can generate thousands of objectively measurable price and market events every day. That gives prediction platforms a potentially continuous source of short-duration contracts.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If crypto contracts continue gaining share while prediction markets expand into stocks and commodities, digital assets could become one component of a much larger financial-contract ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That does not mean prediction markets will replace traditional exchanges or derivatives markets. Rather, the forecast suggests that a new category could develop alongside them.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The next few years will provide a better test of Bernstein's thesis.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Trading volume, new contract types, regulatory decisions and institutional adoption will show whether prediction markets can maintain their current growth rates after the industry's rapid expansion in 2026.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The most important question may be whether financial contracts can continue &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/crypto-pr-distribution-in-2026-why.html"&gt;growing faster&lt;/a&gt; than sports markets.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If that happens, the industry could gradually shift from being primarily associated with sports and political events toward a broader market for continuously traded contracts on financial and real-world outcomes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What does Bernstein forecast for prediction markets in 2035?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Bernstein forecasts approximately &lt;strong&gt;$10 trillion in annual prediction-market trading volume by 2035&lt;/strong&gt;, compared with an estimated $410 billion for 2026. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Will crypto overtake sports in prediction markets?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Bernstein's forecast groups crypto, equities and commodities together as financial assets. That combined category is projected to reach about 49% of volume by 2035, compared with approximately 38% for sports. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Why are crypto prediction markets growing?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Short-duration crypto contracts, including contracts linked to Bitcoin price movements, can generate frequent trading opportunities because crypto markets operate continuously. Bernstein identified this type of activity as one contributor to the industry's expansion in 2026.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is the $10 trillion prediction-market forecast guaranteed?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;No. It is Bernstein's long-term forecast and depends on assumptions involving regulation, product development, liquidity, user adoption and institutional participation.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What is the difference between prediction-market volume and revenue?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Trading volume measures the value of contracts traded, while revenue represents what an operator earns from fees and other sources. A $10 trillion volume forecast should therefore not be interpreted as $10 trillion of revenue for prediction-market companies.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Conclusion&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bernstein's new &lt;strong&gt;$10 trillion prediction-market forecast for 2035&lt;/strong&gt; represents a much broader vision of the industry than today's sports-heavy market.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The central idea is that prediction markets could evolve into continuously traded financial platforms where crypto, stocks, commodities and corporate metrics sit alongside sports and other event contracts.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Whether the industry reaches $10 trillion will depend on how quickly those products develop, how regulators treat them and whether traders continue moving beyond traditional event markets.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For crypto, the forecast is significant because digital assets are already becoming an important part of the short-duration contract market. If Bernstein's broader thesis proves correct, crypto could be one of the building blocks of a much larger prediction-market economy by 2035.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Sources:&lt;/strong&gt; Bernstein research as reported by The Block, Reuters and Decrypt.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>X Trade Buttons Are Coming Soon, Says Nikita Bier — But the Launch Date Is Still Unknown</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiJo9ruhmMB_zLJzOvxFZwGuUFJ4eiKIPR2U24_gmdJx7TpYPXol8K9tt5t7CnCaTgXOuBWbNAIUF_RV8PsICNt5vOL1nLWu2m4V3lZjTXDKcgwpdO7iLUlY6NeZ9lOHhWO8PE-ZFYiruedCxhkKHFIqUS-ji7HqLW8SyH9AZ9wTqihYaw-f7QhU8FZfMhE/s1672/x-crypto-trade-buttons-cashtags-bitcoin-ethereum-trading.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="X crypto trade buttons with Cashtags and cryptocurrency trading interface" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiJo9ruhmMB_zLJzOvxFZwGuUFJ4eiKIPR2U24_gmdJx7TpYPXol8K9tt5t7CnCaTgXOuBWbNAIUF_RV8PsICNt5vOL1nLWu2m4V3lZjTXDKcgwpdO7iLUlY6NeZ9lOHhWO8PE-ZFYiruedCxhkKHFIqUS-ji7HqLW8SyH9AZ9wTqihYaw-f7QhU8FZfMhE/w400-h225/x-crypto-trade-buttons-cashtags-bitcoin-ethereum-trading.jpg.png" title="X Crypto Trade Buttons and Cashtags" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;By CoinAINews Staff | &lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;X appears to be getting closer to turning crypto posts into
actual trading opportunities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Nikita Bier, who recently stepped down as X's head of
product, said Tuesday that &lt;b&gt;crypto trade buttons are coming soon&lt;/b&gt; to the
platform. Bier made the comment while responding to a post about Crypto
Twitter, pointing to the crypto features he helped build during his time at X.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The comment is notable because X has already spent months
building the pieces that could eventually lead to in-app crypto trading. Its &lt;b&gt;Smart
Cashtags&lt;/b&gt; can display crypto market information, while users can also enter
token contract addresses to identify specific assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What X has not revealed is the part traders are probably
most interested in: &lt;b&gt;when the trade button will actually launch, which assets
will be supported and how the trades will be executed.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;X's Crypto Trading Push Is Taking Shape&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;X's move into crypto trading has not happened all at once.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Instead, the platform has gradually added financial features
that make crypto information more useful inside the timeline.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Smart Cashtags were introduced in 2026 with real-time stock
and cryptocurrency information. In supported markets, users can tap financial
symbols to access market data, while the crypto side also supports identifying
assets through contract addresses.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bier's latest comment suggests that trading functionality
could be the next step.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The idea is fairly straightforward.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A user sees a cryptocurrency mentioned in a post, checks its
price and market information through the Cashtag, and then — instead of leaving
X to find an exchange or brokerage — could eventually use a trade button to
start a transaction.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That would turn X from a place where people &lt;b&gt;talk about
markets&lt;/b&gt; into a platform where market information could potentially lead
directly to an action.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Nikita Bier Actually Said&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bier's comment came in response to a post accusing him of
previously limiting the visibility of crypto-related accounts.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Rather than ignoring the criticism, Bier pointed to the
features he helped introduce at X.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;He said he had built Cashtags to let users add &lt;b&gt;Solana and
Ethereum charts directly to posts&lt;/b&gt;, and added that &lt;b&gt;trade buttons were
coming soon&lt;/b&gt;. He also highlighted the ability to paste contract addresses
for newly minted tokens.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That wording is important.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bier did &lt;b&gt;not&lt;/b&gt; announce a specific launch date.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;He also did not publicly detail the exchange, brokerage or
wallet infrastructure that would handle the trades.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;So while the statement is a clear indication that trading
functionality is being worked on, it should not be interpreted as confirmation
that users can trade directly through X today.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Cashtags Foundation&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The trade-button idea makes more sense when viewed alongside
what X has already built.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Smart Cashtags were rolled out to iPhone users in the United
States and Canada as part of X's broader push into &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/mysterious-ox-alpha-ai-model-sparks.html"&gt;financial information&lt;/a&gt;. The
feature brought real-time market data into the platform and was also connected
to a trading pilot involving Canadian brokerage Wealthsimple.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Wealthsimple integration is an important distinction,
though.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Users are &lt;b&gt;not simply executing trades inside X's own
trading system&lt;/b&gt;. Wealthsimple's documentation says supported Cashtags can
route Canadian users to Wealthsimple, where they can trade through the
brokerage.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That means X has already demonstrated one version of the
journey:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;social post → market information → trading platform&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A native or more deeply integrated trade button could
potentially shorten that journey even further.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The $1 Billion Early Signal&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;X has already claimed that its Cashtags pilot generated
roughly &lt;b&gt;$1 billion in global trading volume within 48 hours&lt;/b&gt; of launch.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That figure is an important signal for X because it suggests
there is meaningful demand for combining social content with financial
activity.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It also helps explain why the company may want to push
&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/alibabas-wan-30-turns-pdfs-and-ppts.html"&gt;Cashtags&lt;/a&gt; beyond charts and market information.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Crypto traders already spend significant amounts of time on
X discussing new tokens, market movements and trading ideas. If X can turn that
attention into transactions, the platform could potentially capture more value
from financial activity happening around its content.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The challenge is making that experience work without
creating unnecessary friction or introducing additional security and regulatory
complications.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Timing Is Still Unclear&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is probably the biggest unanswered question.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bier said the buttons are &lt;b&gt;“coming soon,”&lt;/b&gt; but neither
he nor X has publicly provided a firm launch date in the material currently
available.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There is also no confirmed public list of supported
cryptocurrencies, execution partners or exact trading mechanics.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Those details matter.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A trade button could send users to an external exchange or
brokerage. It could eventually connect to a wallet. Or X could develop a more
integrated trading experience of its own.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Each approach would have different implications for custody,
compliance, user experience and transaction execution.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Until X provides those details, it is too early to know
exactly what the finished product will look like.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bier Is No Longer Running X Product&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There is another reason to be cautious about the timeline.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bier is no longer X's head of product.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;He stepped down from the role in August after a little more
than a year and said he would continue working with the company as an adviser.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That does not mean the trade-button project has been
cancelled.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But it does mean the person publicly talking about the
feature is no longer the executive directly responsible for running X's product
organization.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The rollout will therefore depend on the current product
leadership and whatever roadmap X has adopted for the next phase of its
financial features.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In other words, &lt;b&gt;Bier's statement is meaningful, but it
isn't the same thing as an official launch announcement from X.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why the Trade Button Could Matter&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The difference between seeing a price and being able to
trade from the same screen may sound small.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For active traders, it isn't.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Today, someone can discover a token through an &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/thailand-moves-closer-to-spot-bitcoin.html"&gt;X post&lt;/a&gt;,
research it, check its price and then move to another application to execute a
trade.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Every extra step creates friction.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A trade button could potentially reduce that process to a
much simpler flow.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That could be particularly interesting for fast-moving
crypto markets, where traders often react to information in real time.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It could also make X's financial content more commercially
valuable. If users can move from conversation to market data to execution
without leaving the ecosystem, X would have a stronger argument for becoming
more than a social network.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But There Are Still Big Questions&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The feature also raises practical questions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Who executes the trade?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Who holds the assets?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Which countries will have access?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Which cryptocurrencies will be supported?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Will users need an external exchange or wallet?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What fees will apply?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;And perhaps most importantly, &lt;b&gt;how will X handle the
regulatory requirements that come with facilitating financial transactions?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;None of those questions has been fully answered by Bier's
latest comment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That is why the upcoming launch will matter more than the
announcement itself.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;X's Bigger Financial Ambition&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The crypto trade-button project fits into X's much broader
attempt to become a financial platform.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The company has been building tools around payments,
financial information and market data while positioning the platform as a
destination where users can do more than simply post and read content.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Crypto is a natural part of that strategy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The platform already has one of the largest online
communities focused on digital assets. Traders, founders, analysts and crypto
projects use X heavily to share information and react to market moves.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Adding trading functionality could therefore connect two
activities that already happen side by side: &lt;b&gt;discovering financial
information and acting on it.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Traders Should Watch Next&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For now, traders should focus less on the phrase &lt;b&gt;“coming
soon”&lt;/b&gt; and more on the details of the eventual rollout.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The most important announcements will likely involve:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Supported
     cryptocurrencies&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Launch
     countries&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Exchange
     or brokerage partners&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Wallet
     connectivity&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Trading
     and withdrawal mechanics&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Fees&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Custody
     arrangements&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list .5in;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Regulatory
     requirements&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Those details will determine whether X is simply adding
another link to existing trading platforms or genuinely building a new layer
between social media and crypto markets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;X appears to be moving closer to adding &lt;b&gt;crypto trade
buttons&lt;/b&gt; to its platform.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Nikita Bier, X's former head of product, said the buttons
are coming soon and pointed to the existing Cashtags infrastructure that
already supports Solana and Ethereum charts and token contract-address lookups.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;X has already experimented with connecting financial
information on its platform to external trading through its Wealthsimple
integration in Canada, while its Cashtags pilot generated an estimated $1
billion in trading volume during its first 48 hours.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But the biggest piece is still missing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;There is no confirmed launch date yet, and X has not
disclosed the full trading infrastructure behind the planned buttons.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If the feature arrives as described, it could make X's
crypto timeline considerably more actionable — turning a post about a token
into the starting point for a trade.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For now, though, the buttons are still on the roadmap, not
in traders' hands.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>

    <title>ARK Invest Researcher Questions Whether Robinhood Chain Is Really Bringing New Crypto Users</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiEiwFZf5Y8fKQfo7liUT70PA3Y3WlG4UR0JYdai3xyRdqt1rBLnEE4SgznmrRh9D5akduWpTXJMjgHlbAUHXfJd6VHa-7i7vmHXtcwnteupTYem8jqswzuMDc5_B58nC1imW5d0xQ57jV0fOcLxFQhUKY5imt8wIlJUD2U0nmk-Hm9_R5Asn-2TGLMR1Je/s1600/robinhood-chain-new-users-crypto-traders-lorenzo-valente.jpg.jpeg" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Robinhood Chain transaction activity raises questions about new crypto user adoption" border="0" data-original-height="900" data-original-width="1600" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiEiwFZf5Y8fKQfo7liUT70PA3Y3WlG4UR0JYdai3xyRdqt1rBLnEE4SgznmrRh9D5akduWpTXJMjgHlbAUHXfJd6VHa-7i7vmHXtcwnteupTYem8jqswzuMDc5_B58nC1imW5d0xQ57jV0fOcLxFQhUKY5imt8wIlJUD2U0nmk-Hm9_R5Asn-2TGLMR1Je/w640-h360/robinhood-chain-new-users-crypto-traders-lorenzo-valente.jpg.jpeg" title="Robinhood Chain Faces Questions Over New User Adoption" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;
September 5, 2026&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Robinhood Chain has generated significant on-chain activity since launching its public mainnet, but new analysis from ARK Invest researcher Lorenzo Valente is raising an important question: how much of that activity actually comes from new Robinhood users entering crypto?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to Valente's contract-level analysis, the share of transactions that can be clearly identified as coming through Robinhood Wallet is less than 1%. He argues that much of the remaining activity appears to come from existing crypto traders using platforms and trading terminals such as GMGN, Axiom and OKX.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The finding does not mean that fewer than 1% of Robinhood Chain users are Robinhood customers. Instead, it refers specifically to transaction activity that Valente says can be directly attributed to Robinhood Wallet through an identifiable on-chain route.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Lorenzo Valente: “Same Degens, New Chain”&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Valente, ARK Invest's digital-asset research director, shared his analysis after examining contract-level activity on Robinhood Chain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;His central question was whether the network was onboarding a new population of cryptocurrency users or whether experienced on-chain traders were simply moving some of their existing activity to another blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;His conclusion was that the latter appears to be happening to a significant extent.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Valente identified Robinhood Wallet's swap activity through the &lt;strong&gt;0x Settler&lt;/strong&gt; contract as the clearest on-chain signal that a transaction originated from Robinhood's wallet ecosystem. That identifiable activity represented less than 1% of the transactions included in his analysis.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;He also noted that some transactions could not be confidently attributed to a particular platform. If a portion of that unidentified long-tail activity were assumed to come from Robinhood users, Valente estimated that the Robinhood-linked share could reach roughly 5%.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important because blockchain transaction data does not directly reveal the identity of every person behind an address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Less-Than-1% Figure Needs Context&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The headline figure could easily be misunderstood.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean that Robinhood has converted less than 1% of its customers into crypto users. It also does not prove that 99% of Robinhood Chain activity comes from unrelated users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Rather, Valente is measuring what can be confidently identified from public smart-contract data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A transaction can pass through aggregators, trading terminals, smart contracts or other infrastructure before reaching its final destination. That makes attribution difficult, particularly on an open, EVM-compatible blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For that reason, the analysis is best understood as a measurement of &lt;strong&gt;identifiable transaction flows&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than a census of Robinhood Chain's user base.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;GMGN, Axiom and OKX Appear Prominent in the Activity&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Valente's analysis suggests that a substantial amount of the identifiable activity is connected to existing crypto-native trading infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Platforms such as GMGN and OKX allow active traders to interact with blockchain-based markets without necessarily using Robinhood Wallet as their primary interface.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This creates an important distinction between &lt;strong&gt;using Robinhood Chain&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;being a Robinhood customer&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A trader can access the network through an external wallet or trading terminal, execute transactions on Robinhood Chain and never interact directly with Robinhood's &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/zcash-surges-above-1000-as-etf-demand.html"&gt;wallet&lt;/a&gt; product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As a result, a rapidly rising transaction count can demonstrate strong blockchain activity without necessarily proving that Robinhood is bringing an equivalent number of new people into cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Robinhood Chain Has Still Seen Rapid Growth&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The debate over user composition should not obscure the network's rapid growth.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Robinhood Chain went live on public mainnet on July 1, 2026 as a dedicated Arbitrum-based chain settling to Ethereum. The network was designed to support Robinhood's broader push into on-chain finance, including tokenized stocks and decentralized financial applications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Early network data showed a rapid increase in transaction activity. CoinMetrics previously reported that more than $200 million worth of ETH had been bridged to Robinhood Chain within the first few weeks following the mainnet launch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Other data has also shown substantial transaction volumes and growing liquidity across the network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, transaction counts alone cannot tell investors how many unique people are using the blockchain or how many of those users were newly introduced to crypto through Robinhood.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Robinhood's Bigger Bet Is Tokenized Finance&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The user-acquisition question matters because Robinhood's blockchain strategy extends beyond memecoin trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company launched Robinhood Chain as part of a broader push into tokenized assets, decentralized finance and global access to financial products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Robinhood announced the mainnet launch alongside plans involving tokenized stocks, agentic trading and additional DeFi products. The company has positioned blockchain infrastructure as part of its long-term effort to expand access to financial markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If Robinhood can successfully move its existing brokerage customers onto blockchain-based products, the chain could potentially gain a large distribution advantage over competing networks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But if most early activity comes from traders who already participate in crypto markets, the network's transaction numbers may tell a different story from the company's broader user-onboarding thesis.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Transaction Volume Is Not the Same as User Growth&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the most important takeaways from the debate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; margin: 20px 0px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Metric&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;What It Can Show&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;What It Cannot Prove Alone&lt;/th&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;

&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One person can control multiple wallets, while a single smart contract or service can represent activity from many different users. Automated trading can also generate a large number of transactions without representing an equivalent number of individuals.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes user attribution one of the more difficult questions in analyzing young &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/sam-altman-says-ai-industry-did.html"&gt;blockchain &lt;/a&gt;networks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The “New Users” Question Could Become More Important&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Robinhood's strongest potential advantage is not necessarily the blockchain itself. It is the company's existing distribution.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Robinhood already operates a large consumer financial platform. If those customers begin using on-chain products through Robinhood Wallet, tokenized stocks or other blockchain services, the company could create a significant pipeline of new blockchain users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But public blockchain data needs to show that this conversion is actually happening.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For analysts, the key metrics will therefore go beyond raw transaction counts. They will include identifiable Robinhood Wallet activity, recurring users, capital flows, tokenized-asset adoption and the proportion of activity generated by users who were not previously active on other chains.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Robinhood Chain Needs to Prove Next&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Robinhood Chain has already demonstrated that traders are willing to use the network. The next question is whether that activity translates into durable user growth for Robinhood's broader financial ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Several indicators could help answer that question:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Growth in Robinhood Wallet activity:&lt;/strong&gt; Increasing identifiable wallet transactions would provide stronger evidence of direct customer adoption.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Repeat users:&lt;/strong&gt; Sustainable activity from recurring users would be more meaningful than short-term speculative bursts.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Tokenized-stock adoption:&lt;/strong&gt; Greater use of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/poland-crypto-bill-veto-parliament.html"&gt;tokenized&lt;/a&gt; equities could demonstrate whether Robinhood is attracting users beyond crypto-native traders.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;New capital entering the ecosystem:&lt;/strong&gt; Fresh liquidity from users previously inactive on-chain would strengthen the new-user thesis.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Reduced dependence on speculative trading terminals:&lt;/strong&gt; A broader application mix could indicate that the network is evolving beyond early degen-driven activity.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Debate Matters for Robinhood&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Robinhood Chain is part of a much larger competition to bring traditional financial assets onto blockchain infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If Robinhood can combine its established consumer brand with tokenized securities, wallets and DeFi applications, it could potentially use its existing customer base to accelerate blockchain adoption.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But a chain dominated by existing crypto traders would tell a different story. It would suggest that Robinhood has built an attractive venue for on-chain speculation and trading, while the harder task of bringing genuinely new users into crypto remains unfinished.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not make the network unsuccessful. Existing crypto traders can generate substantial liquidity, fees and application demand. It simply means that transaction growth and customer acquisition should be evaluated as separate metrics.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ARK Invest's Lorenzo Valente has challenged the assumption that Robinhood Chain's rapidly growing transaction activity automatically represents a large influx of new cryptocurrency users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;His contract-level analysis found that less than 1% of the transactions he examined could be clearly confirmed as Robinhood Wallet activity through the 0x Settler route. Even under a broader assumption that some unidentified transactions came from Robinhood users, he estimated the share at roughly 5%.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The remaining activity appears heavily influenced by existing crypto traders and platforms such as GMGN, Axiom and OKX.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The finding should not be interpreted as an official Robinhood user statistic. Instead, it highlights a broader analytical challenge: &lt;strong&gt;a blockchain can generate millions of transactions without necessarily onboarding millions of new people.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Robinhood, the more important test may now be whether its existing customer base increasingly moves onto the chain—and whether that activity eventually becomes visible in on-chain data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What did Lorenzo Valente say about Robinhood Chain?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;ARK Invest researcher Lorenzo Valente said his contract-level analysis suggests that most Robinhood Chain activity comes from existing crypto traders rather than a large influx of new users brought onto crypto by Robinhood.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What does the less-than-1% Robinhood figure mean?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It refers to transaction activity that Valente could clearly identify as coming through Robinhood Wallet's swap route using the 0x Settler contract. It is not an official statistic for Robinhood's total customer base.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Could Robinhood-related activity be higher than 1%?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes. Valente said that including some unidentified long-tail activity could raise the estimated Robinhood-linked share to roughly 5%.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Which platforms are driving Robinhood Chain activity?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Valente's analysis points to crypto-native trading platforms and terminals including GMGN, Axiom and OKX as important sources of activity outside the clearly identifiable Robinhood Wallet route.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;When did Robinhood Chain launch?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Robinhood Chain launched on public mainnet on July 1, 2026 as a dedicated Arbitrum-based blockchain settling to Ethereum.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does high transaction activity mean Robinhood Chain has many new users?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Not necessarily. Transaction counts measure on-chain activity, but they do not directly identify unique individuals or prove that users are new to cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire Says Crypto Adoption Will Reshape Finance With or Without CLARITY Act</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiDqt55iuhrzH9Uzr2PQmu2DZswrU3uDcpphi6DbvbEqH3HoePTn4lqkA2Z_O3ZpwalBiX5JA0-xbUdEJJwhoSCWA4jkTPhwNyaoR81dWK94rdzGinKDLtLR6uta-h6p5G0OP9FeZmbjS1zFhi4eHtdkpLIgX6__JO70DHjWErOExLcptSnKL5AI_ofZ3Cr/s1733/jeremy-allaire-crypto-adoption-financial-system.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire says crypto adoption will reshape the global financial system" border="0" data-original-height="907" data-original-width="1733" height="334" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiDqt55iuhrzH9Uzr2PQmu2DZswrU3uDcpphi6DbvbEqH3HoePTn4lqkA2Z_O3ZpwalBiX5JA0-xbUdEJJwhoSCWA4jkTPhwNyaoR81dWK94rdzGinKDLtLR6uta-h6p5G0OP9FeZmbjS1zFhi4eHtdkpLIgX6__JO70DHjWErOExLcptSnKL5AI_ofZ3Cr/w640-h334/jeremy-allaire-crypto-adoption-financial-system.jpg.png" title="Jeremy Allaire Says Crypto Will Reshape the Financial System" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire says the growth of crypto and blockchain-based finance will continue regardless of whether the U.S. Congress passes the CLARITY Act, arguing that the technology has already become an “irreversible megatrend” that will reshape the global financial system.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Allaire made the comments in a Bloomberg interview as the U.S. crypto industry deals with a major setback in Washington. On September 15, the U.S. Senate voted 49–50 on a procedural motion to advance the CLARITY Act, falling short of the 60 votes required to move the legislation forward.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The failed vote has created fresh uncertainty around U.S. crypto market-structure legislation. But Allaire argued that the setback does not change the underlying direction of financial technology, particularly the adoption of stablecoins, blockchain settlement and tokenized financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Jeremy Allaire: Crypto Adoption Is an “Irreversible Megatrend”&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;During the Bloomberg discussion, Allaire was asked about his earlier view that the CLARITY Act remained resolvable despite disagreements in Congress.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;He argued that the failed procedural vote should not automatically be interpreted as the end of the legislation. Allaire pointed to the earlier GENIUS Act process as an example of legislation that encountered procedural obstacles before ultimately moving forward.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;More broadly, however, Allaire said Circle does not need the CLARITY Act for the underlying adoption of digital dollars and blockchain-based financial infrastructure to continue.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;“This is an irreversible trend. It’s accelerating,” Allaire said, describing blockchain technology as a major technology for the future of the financial system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;He added that whether broader market-structure legislation is resolved in the next few months or takes considerably longer, he expects the transformation of financial markets to continue.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the CLARITY Act Still Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Allaire’s comments do not mean the CLARITY Act has become irrelevant.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The legislation is intended to establish a broader federal framework for digital assets and clarify how responsibilities are divided between agencies including the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Senate's 49–50 vote on September 15 prevented the bill from advancing at that stage. Bloomberg Law reported that the setback came as &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-calls-ai.html"&gt;crypto markets&lt;/a&gt; reacted sharply, with Coinbase closing about 10% lower, Circle falling more than 11%, and Bitcoin declining as much as 5.3% to below $75,000 following the vote. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important: &lt;strong&gt;stablecoin adoption and blockchain development can continue without CLARITY, while the absence of market-structure legislation can still leave important questions around trading platforms, token classification and regulatory jurisdiction unresolved.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Circle Says USDC Does Not Depend on CLARITY&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the most important parts of Allaire's argument concerns Circle's existing business.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle issues USDC, a dollar-denominated stablecoin designed to function as digital money on blockchain networks. The company has increasingly positioned itself not simply as a stablecoin issuer, but as financial infrastructure connecting digital dollars, payments, capital markets and blockchain networks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Allaire said Circle does not need the CLARITY Act to continue scaling USDC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is partly because the regulatory foundation for payment &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/balancer-could-shut-down-9m-treasury.html"&gt;stablecoins &lt;/a&gt;has already changed. Allaire pointed to the GENIUS Act and described the legislation as establishing federal recognition for digital dollars such as USDC, with its framework scheduled to take effect in January.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Circle, the implication is significant: the company's core stablecoin business can continue expanding even while lawmakers debate the separate and broader question of crypto market structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Circle Sees a $60 Trillion Market Opportunity&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Allaire also highlighted the size of the traditional financial market that stablecoins could potentially address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;He estimated that the existing market for non-interest-bearing cash and demand deposits is approximately &lt;strong&gt;$60 trillion&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The figure should not be interpreted as a forecast that $60 trillion will immediately move into stablecoins. Instead, Allaire was describing the enormous pool of money and financial activity that could potentially be affected as programmable digital dollars become more widely integrated into payments and financial markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The opportunity extends beyond cryptocurrency trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Stablecoins can potentially be used for cross-border payments, treasury management, settlement, trading collateral, financial applications and other transactions where programmable digital money can reduce friction or settlement time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;From Stablecoins to a Broader Internet Financial System&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle's strategy increasingly reflects that broader vision.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company has described its long-term direction as building an internet-native financial infrastructure around regulated stablecoins, blockchain networks and financial applications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle's own 2026 product strategy identifies USDC and other digital assets alongside Arc, its blockchain infrastructure, and payment and interoperability services as components of that broader financial platform. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This means the company's ambitions extend beyond making USDC a cryptocurrency trading instrument.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The objective is to make blockchain-based money and settlement infrastructure useful to banks, fintech companies, payment providers, corporations and capital-market participants.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is Arc and Why Does It Matter to Circle?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Another part of Allaire's Bloomberg discussion focused on Arc, Circle's blockchain infrastructure initiative.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle describes Arc as an open Layer-1 blockchain designed to provide infrastructure for an internet-native financial system. The company has positioned the network as a foundation for applications involving payments, capital markets and digital assets. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Allaire said hundreds of companies were already deploying or integrating with Arc, reflecting Circle's effort to build infrastructure around its stablecoin business rather than relying exclusively on USDC issuance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The strategy effectively gives Circle several potential routes into financial markets: digital dollars, blockchain settlement, developer infrastructure and institutional financial applications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;GENIUS Act vs. CLARITY Act: What Is the Difference?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Regulatory question&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;How payment stablecoins &lt;br /&gt;are regulated&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;How different crypto assets &lt;br /&gt;and market activities fit within &lt;br /&gt;federal regulation&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Current status&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Federal stablecoin legislation &lt;br /&gt;cited by Allaire as part of &lt;br /&gt;Circle's regulatory foundation&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Failed to advance in the &lt;br /&gt;September 15, 2026 Senate &lt;br /&gt;procedural vote&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The distinction explains why Allaire can argue that Circle's stablecoin business can continue while still supporting further market-structure legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Crypto Industry Still Wants Broader Market Rules&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle's position is only one part of the wider crypto regulatory debate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CLARITY Act was designed to address questions extending beyond stablecoins, including the regulatory treatment of digital assets and the respective roles of the SEC and CFTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;After the Senate vote, attention shifted toward what federal regulators can do under existing law. Axios reported that SEC Chairman Paul Atkins said the agency would continue working on crypto regulation regardless of the legislation's outcome, while also arguing that legislation would provide more durable rules. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;JPMorgan analysts similarly said the CLARITY Act was not necessarily permanently dead, although they described the remaining legislative window as extremely narrow. They also expected greater attention to SEC and CFTC action if Congress does not advance the bill. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That leaves the U.S. crypto market facing two different questions: whether blockchain-based financial products will continue gaining adoption, and whether Congress can establish a comprehensive statutory framework for the wider digital-asset market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Allaire's Statement Matters for USDC&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Circle, the distinction has direct commercial importance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If stablecoin adoption depends entirely on one piece of legislation, a congressional delay could create a significant obstacle for the company's expansion plans. Allaire's argument is essentially that this dependency no longer exists in the same way.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;USDC can continue operating within the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitcoin-apocalypse-15-years-ago-btc.html"&gt;stablecoin framework&lt;/a&gt; while Circle builds additional infrastructure around it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could allow the company to pursue applications across payments, financial settlement, tokenized assets and institutional markets even while policymakers continue debating broader crypto rules.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle's own 2026 strategy describes USDC as part of a wider infrastructure stack alongside Arc and other financial services rather than as an isolated cryptocurrency product. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Could Change if CLARITY Eventually Passes?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A future version of the CLARITY Act could still materially affect the market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Clearer statutory definitions and agency responsibilities could reduce uncertainty for exchanges, token issuers, developers, market makers and institutional investors. It could also establish rules that are more durable than agency policies that can change with future administrations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why the failed Senate vote should not be interpreted as meaning that crypto regulation has stopped.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, the immediate regulatory path may involve a combination of existing federal law, agency rulemaking and continued congressional negotiations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Crypto Adoption Is Moving Beyond the CLARITY Debate&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Allaire's central argument is broader than the fate of one U.S. bill.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;He believes blockchain technology is becoming embedded in financial infrastructure regardless of the speed of congressional action. Stablecoins are already being used across crypto markets, payment systems and financial applications, while companies such as Circle are developing blockchain infrastructure aimed at institutional use.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle has also publicly described its broader goal as building an internet financial system based on public blockchains, regulated digital assets and programmable money. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company's vision therefore extends beyond the traditional crypto market. It targets the infrastructure underneath payments and financial settlement itself.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next for Circle and the CLARITY Act?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Circle, the immediate focus is likely to remain on expanding USDC usage, financial infrastructure and Arc while the U.S. regulatory debate continues.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the CLARITY Act, the September 15 procedural defeat creates uncertainty over when lawmakers could revisit the legislation. The bill was not enacted, but the failed vote does not by itself establish that Congress will never reconsider it. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bigger question for the crypto industry is whether regulatory clarity will come primarily through new legislation or through agencies applying existing federal authority while Congress continues negotiations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Jeremy Allaire's message is that the adoption of blockchain-based financial infrastructure has become larger than the fate of a single piece of legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle's CEO argues that stablecoins such as USDC can continue expanding under the emerging federal framework, while the company builds infrastructure designed to connect digital dollars with payments, capital markets and institutional finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CLARITY Act remains important because it addresses a broader set of market-structure questions. But its September 15 Senate setback does not mean the development of crypto financial infrastructure has stopped.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Circle, the strategy is increasingly clear: expand the use of regulated digital dollars while building the blockchain infrastructure around them. Whether Congress ultimately passes comprehensive market-structure legislation may influence the pace and structure of that transformation, but Allaire believes the underlying shift toward blockchain-based finance is already underway.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Editorial note:&lt;/strong&gt; Allaire's characterization of crypto adoption as an “irreversible megatrend” is his assessment of the market's direction, not an independently established fact or guarantee about future adoption. The $60 trillion figure is his estimate of the existing non-interest-bearing cash and demand-deposit market and should not be interpreted as a prediction that this entire amount will migrate to stablecoins.&lt;/p&gt;
</content>

    <title>Miden to Launch USDCx: A Privacy-First Stablecoin for Institutional Finance</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiB4NfpDKKwvcfEu5Iotzb_VZFHziFTEgQnGERwK9GxI9gOtgavOXL-ZhiZA6vPxhexvOpkl4DuJytH0CS7aDsvsf0z21o0RZsNVd8Kh-YMIOj8urdz9ji182E5GrxZfdKM0pLnzP9mxSq4kAu-ErjWQ5JpUoaohglwD-R6yQGn4UZhx-nc30OD4YyO9pmt/s1672/USDCx%20Privacy-First%20Stablecoin%20Network.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Miden USDCx privacy-focused stablecoin for institutional finance" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiB4NfpDKKwvcfEu5Iotzb_VZFHziFTEgQnGERwK9GxI9gOtgavOXL-ZhiZA6vPxhexvOpkl4DuJytH0CS7aDsvsf0z21o0RZsNVd8Kh-YMIOj8urdz9ji182E5GrxZfdKM0pLnzP9mxSq4kAu-ErjWQ5JpUoaohglwD-R6yQGn4UZhx-nc30OD4YyO9pmt/w320-h180/USDCx%20Privacy-First%20Stablecoin%20Network.png" title="Miden USDCx privacy-focused stablecoin for institutional finance" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aug 13, 2026&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;– Privacy blockchain Miden has
announced plans to launch USDCx, a privacy-focused stablecoin backed 1:1 by
Circle's USDC, designed to keep balances and transaction histories hidden by
default&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The stablecoin is expected to go live alongside Miden's
mainnet, which is targeted for launch at the end of this month&amp;nbsp;. USDCx
will be issued natively on the Miden network using Circle's xReserve
infrastructure, meaning Circle's USDC will be held in an xReserve smart
contract backing the token on a one-to-one basis&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why USDCx Is Different&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The core problem USDCx aims to solve is straightforward:
public blockchains are transparent by design. Every USDC or USDT transfer
broadcasts your balance, your counterparty, and your entire transaction history
to anyone with an internet connection and a block explorer&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For institutions, that transparency is a dealbreaker.
Trading firms don't want to reveal positions. Companies can't publish payroll
and treasury activity. Individuals don't want their financial lives visible on
block explorers&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;With USDCx:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/north-korea-stole-28b-in-crypto-and-is.html"&gt;Balances&lt;/a&gt;,
     counterparties, and transaction histories remain&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;encrypted by
     default&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Users
     and institutions can&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;selectively disclose information&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;to
     auditors, regulators, or counterparties when needed&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;The
     network verifies that transactions are valid and balances add up&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;without
     revealing who sent what to whom&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;This selective disclosure mechanism is designed to satisfy
specific regulatory requirements, including sanctions screening and the
Financial Action Task Force's Travel Rule, which mandates that certain
identifying information travel alongside cross-border transfers above a
threshold&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;How It Works: Client-Side Proving&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Miden's architecture is key to how USDCx works. The project
is a zero-knowledge blockchain that spun out of Polygon in 2025, built around
what it calls&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;client-side proving&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Instead of running computations on a shared public network
where every validator sees your data, cryptographic proofs are generated on the
user's own device. The network only needs to verify the proof itself — not the
underlying data. This approach is designed to maintain scalability without
forcing users to choose between speed and confidentiality&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The practical effect: a transaction can be verified as valid
without anyone knowing the amount, the sender, or the recipient unless the
parties involved choose to disclose that information&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Business Case: "PriFi" for Institutions&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Miden is targeting a specific set of use cases where
transparency isn't a feature but a liability&amp;nbsp;:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="MsoNormalTable" style="border-collapse: collapse; mso-yfti-tbllook: 1184; width: 752px;"&gt;
 &lt;thead&gt;
  &lt;tr style="mso-yfti-firstrow: yes; mso-yfti-irow: 0;"&gt;
   &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 0cm;"&gt;
   &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Use Case&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
   &lt;/td&gt;
   &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
   &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Why Privacy Matters&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
   &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;/tr&gt;
 &lt;/thead&gt;
 &lt;tbody&gt;&lt;tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 1;"&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 0cm;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Private Payroll&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 0cm 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Companies cannot publish employee salaries on-chain&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
 &lt;tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 2;"&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 0cm;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Cross-Border Remittances&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 0cm 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Transaction values and counterparties should remain
  private&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
 &lt;tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 3;"&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 0cm;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Neobank Infrastructure&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 0cm 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Digital banks need settlement efficiency without exposing
  customer data&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
 &lt;tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 4;"&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 0cm;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;B2B Payments&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 0cm 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Corporate treasury activity requires confidentiality&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
 &lt;tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 5; mso-yfti-lastrow: yes;"&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 0cm;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Institutional Trading&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 0cm 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Firms cannot reveal positions and trading strategies&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Miden views USDCx as the foundation of its&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;"PriFi"
(Privacy Finance)&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;direction, covering scenarios where public
blockchain transparency has historically blocked institutional adoption&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;A Key Distinction: USDCx Is Not USDC&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A critical detail:&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/white-house-fully-committed-to-passing.html"&gt;USDCx&lt;/a&gt; is a separate token&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;from
USDC. While it is backed 1:1 by USDC held in Circle's xReserve contract, it is
issued natively on Miden and operates under its own mint-and-burn mechanics. A
holder of USDCx has a claim on a process that depends on Miden's software,
Miden's operators, and Circle's attestation all working correctly. A holder of
USDC has Circle's token on chains Circle already supports&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Miden has not yet published an independent attestation of
USDC already sitting in xReserve for this token because the token is not live.
Circle's design says the reserve is created when USDC is deposited. Until
deposits happen, there is nothing to count&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Miden's Backing and Competitive Position&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Miden raised&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$25 million&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in a seed round
from a16z Crypto, Hack VC, and 1kx, coming as the project separated from
Polygon to pursue its zero-knowledge vision independently&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Previous attempts at privacy-preserving digital dollars have
often run into regulatory resistance. Projects like Tornado Cash demonstrated
demand for transaction privacy but also illustrated the legal risks: the U.S.
Treasury sanctioned the protocol in 2022, and its developer faced criminal
charges&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Miden's approach differs in a crucial way. Rather than
offering privacy as an add-on mixing service for existing tokens, it bakes
encryption into the base layer while preserving a compliance valve. The
optional disclosure mechanism is the key differentiator. Regulators get their
sanctions screening and Travel Rule compliance. Users get their privacy&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What This Means for Crypto&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The USDCx announcement arrives at a moment when stablecoin
regulation is a major focus in Washington. The product is designed to be a test
case for whether compliance and privacy can coexist: hide the transaction
details by default, show them only when a legitimate request arrives&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The involvement of Circle's xReserve infrastructure is
notable. Circle, the issuer of USDC, has been building out its enterprise
toolkit for institutional adoption. Allowing a third-party project to issue a
wrapped, privacy-enhanced version of USDC through its reserve system suggests
Circle sees demand for confidential stablecoin use cases that its base product
doesn't currently address&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If USDCx launches successfully at month-end, it could become
the first widely available privacy-preserving stablecoin designed specifically
for institutions. If it encounters regulatory or technical hurdles, it will be
a case study in how difficult it is to balance privacy and compliance on public
blockchains.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
