    <title>What If AI Steals a Stablecoin Issuer's Private Keys Before Anyone Notices? The Scenario Is Becoming Less Far-Fetched.</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEh6w-H4i89vO3ibowdr_dGLtXRDRniwChx0XTNDQLKrlAp1SCZ-SyPZV4sJ33VJaiJaD9svMj7aJPSXHp7npn67wHc6Dv73QTjidgNUB1iCHSE0_lBgmtfwmog5y0rJ81UHJztzOEqjVvLWvfonzlYAIsDthyphenhyphenvatFMNyqk0U-7uzkP-OPRjiq5q0bmIDV0F/s1672/ai-stablecoin-private-key-security.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="AI cybersecurity system protecting stablecoin wallets and private keys" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEh6w-H4i89vO3ibowdr_dGLtXRDRniwChx0XTNDQLKrlAp1SCZ-SyPZV4sJ33VJaiJaD9svMj7aJPSXHp7npn67wHc6Dv73QTjidgNUB1iCHSE0_lBgmtfwmog5y0rJ81UHJztzOEqjVvLWvfonzlYAIsDthyphenhyphenvatFMNyqk0U-7uzkP-OPRjiq5q0bmIDV0F/w400-h225/ai-stablecoin-private-key-security.jpg.png" title="AI and Stablecoin Private Key Security" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&amp;nbsp;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;What if an AI agent found a way into a stablecoin issuer's most sensitive infrastructure — and nobody realized what had happened until the first suspicious transaction appeared on-chain?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It sounds like science fiction. But AI systems are becoming increasingly capable of analyzing software, navigating digital environments and carrying out multi-step tasks. At the same time, financial infrastructure is becoming increasingly automated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That combination creates a cybersecurity question that stablecoin issuers cannot afford to ignore.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;There is no credible public evidence that an AI has secretly stolen the private keys of a major stablecoin issuer.&lt;/strong&gt; This article examines a hypothetical scenario based on real developments in AI agents, blockchain wallets and cybersecurity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Stablecoin Private Keys Matter&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A stablecoin transaction may look simple on a blockchain explorer: one address sends tokens to another.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Behind that transaction, however, is a much larger infrastructure involving smart contracts, custody systems, operational controls and cryptographic authorization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Depending on an issuer's architecture, certain private keys or signing credentials can authorize important blockchain operations. The exact permissions vary between systems, which is why it would be inaccurate to assume that compromising any single key automatically gives an attacker control over an issuer's entire operation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tether's published documentation describes private keys as an important component of its token issuance process and discusses multi-signature controls designed to reduce reliance on a single authorization point.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That leads to a basic security principle: &lt;strong&gt;one compromised credential should not be enough to compromise an entire financial system.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The AI Threat Isn't About Magic&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI system would not need to somehow guess a private key to become part of a serious cyberattack.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The more realistic concern is access.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Imagine an attacker compromises an application or internal service connected to a financial company's infrastructure. An AI system operating within that environment could potentially help analyze files, identify relationships between systems, examine permissions or search for exposed credentials.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The danger comes from combining many small capabilities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A human attacker may spend hours studying an unfamiliar technology stack. An autonomous system could potentially analyze large amounts of information continuously and react to new findings without waiting for a person to manually direct every step.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean today's AI can automatically break into a stablecoin issuer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It means cybersecurity teams have to consider a world where some attacks may involve increasingly autonomous software rather than a human manually performing every stage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Agents Are Already Moving Into Crypto&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The underlying technology is already being developed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle has built infrastructure that allows &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/justin-sun-says-tron-targets-quantum.html"&gt;AI agents&lt;/a&gt; to interact with blockchain wallets and make transactions. Its Agent Wallet documentation describes MPC-based key management designed so that key shares are not exposed directly to the AI agent.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://developers.circle.com/agent-stack/agent-wallets" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Circle's Agent Wallet documentation&lt;/a&gt; provides details about this architecture.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A properly designed AI wallet does not necessarily hand an agent unrestricted control over the underlying cryptographic key. Instead, the system can provide limited permissions while sensitive signing material remains separated from the software making the decision.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This type of separation could become increasingly important as AI agents begin handling payments, treasury operations and other financial tasks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What a Worst-Case Attack Could Look Like&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The nightmare scenario probably would not begin with an AI immediately stealing a private key.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It could start much more quietly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An attacker might compromise an application, obtain a low-level credential or gain access to an internal service. An AI system could then potentially help map the environment and identify pathways toward more privileged systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A hypothetical attack could involve stages such as:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Discovering exposed credentials or access tokens&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Identifying privileged accounts and services&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Mapping connections between internal systems&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Finding weaknesses in authorization controls&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Attempting to reach sensitive signing infrastructure&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Monitoring blockchain activity&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Taking advantage of a transaction window before defenders respond&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;None of these actions necessarily looks catastrophic on its own.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The potential danger comes from connecting them together and allowing an automated system to operate at machine speed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;A Stolen Key Would Not Automatically Mean Stolen Reserves&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction is extremely important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;A blockchain signing credential and a stablecoin issuer's reserve assets are not necessarily the same thing.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If a particular operational credential were compromised, an attacker would have whatever authority is associated with that credential and the systems connected to it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not automatically mean the attacker could access every asset backing the stablecoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle's public transparency information, for example, describes USDC reserves separately from the blockchain infrastructure used to operate the token.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.circle.com/transparency" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Circle's transparency page&lt;/a&gt; provides information about USDC's reserve structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For that reason, the simplistic claim that "AI steals one key and gets billions of dollars" would be misleading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The actual consequences would depend on the exact credential, permissions, infrastructure and security controls involved.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Security Layers That Matter&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); margin: 24px 0px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Security Layer&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Purpose&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Key isolation&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;Keeps sensitive cryptographic material away &lt;br /&gt;from ordinary application environments.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;MPC or multi-signature controls&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;Helps prevent one compromised credential &lt;br /&gt;from automatically authorizing critical&lt;br /&gt;&amp;nbsp;transactions.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Least-privilege access&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;Limits what employees, applications &lt;br /&gt;and AI agents can do.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Transaction limits&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;Adds restrictions around unusually large &lt;br /&gt;or unusual transfers.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Real-time monitoring&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;Helps identify abnormal transactions and&lt;br /&gt;&amp;nbsp;authorization behavior.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Emergency controls&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(85, 85, 85); padding: 12px;"&gt;Allows affected systems or operations to be&lt;br /&gt;restricted when suspicious activity is detected.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why AI Could Make Detection Harder&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A traditional breach can produce obvious warning signs: an unfamiliar login, a suspicious file transfer or an unauthorized transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An autonomous attack could potentially be more difficult to identify if malicious activity is spread across many small actions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI system could potentially make numerous low-value requests, interact with several services and gradually gather information before an attacker attempts a more consequential action.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a different challenge for security teams.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of looking only at individual events, defenders may increasingly need to examine patterns across systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An isolated credential lookup might appear harmless. But if it is followed by unusual permission checks, access to deployment infrastructure and blockchain-related activity, the combination could warrant investigation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Real Risk Is Too Much Authority&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most important question may not be whether an AI can steal a private key.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It may be how much authority the AI receives in the first place.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Giving an AI permission to check a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/kalshi-sells-112b-of-equity-to-71.html"&gt;wallet&lt;/a&gt; balance is one thing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Allowing it to prepare a transaction is another.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Allowing it to independently approve transactions worth millions of dollars would create a much greater risk.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A safer architecture can separate decision-making from final authorization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI agent might identify an opportunity and prepare a transaction, while another security layer checks the transaction against predefined policies before anything is signed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This approach can limit the potential damage if an AI behaves unexpectedly or the agent itself becomes compromised.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why MPC and Multi-Signature Systems Matter&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The basic idea behind multi-signature and MPC systems is straightforward: do not put all the authority in one place.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of allowing one credential to authorize a critical action, multiple approvals or cryptographic components can be required.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This creates another barrier between an AI agent and the final transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Circle's Agent Wallet architecture provides one example of this approach, using MPC-based key management in which cryptographic key shares are separated rather than exposed directly to the agent.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader lesson is important for financial infrastructure: &lt;strong&gt;an AI should ideally receive permission to perform a task without receiving unrestricted control over the money behind that task.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could an AI Secretly Control a Stablecoin?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In theory, a sufficiently capable AI operating with enough access could become part of a serious cyberattack.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But that is very different from saying such an attack is happening today.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;There is currently no credible public evidence that an AI has secretly taken control of a major stablecoin issuer's private keys.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is also no basis for assuming that an &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/japan-eyes-blockchain-for-real-time.html"&gt;AI automatically&lt;/a&gt; becomes capable of bypassing MPC, multi-signature systems, hardware security or other protections simply because it is autonomous.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those controls exist specifically to prevent one compromised component from becoming a complete failure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The more realistic concern is that increasingly capable AI could make existing vulnerabilities easier to identify and potentially exploit.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Picture&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Stablecoins have become important pieces of digital-asset infrastructure. They are used across trading, payments, settlement and decentralized applications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, AI agents are moving beyond generating information and beginning to interact with financial systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Putting those two trends together creates a new cybersecurity challenge.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The answer is not to assume that every AI agent is an attacker.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is to design financial infrastructure under the assumption that &lt;strong&gt;any individual component could eventually be compromised.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means limiting permissions, separating cryptographic authority, monitoring transactions and maintaining emergency controls.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It also means ensuring that an AI agent cannot quietly turn a small security mistake into an irreversible financial event.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The scary scenario isn't an AI magically guessing a stablecoin issuer's private key.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The real concern is an AI quietly finding its way through enough systems that, by the time anyone notices, the key is no longer the hardest thing to reach.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no credible evidence that a major stablecoin issuer has already suffered an AI-driven private-key theft. For now, this remains a hypothetical cybersecurity scenario.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the question is becoming more relevant as AI agents gain access to real wallets, payment systems and financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The industry may eventually have to answer a difficult question: &lt;strong&gt;how much financial authority should a machine receive — and how quickly can that authority be taken away when something goes wrong — and who presses the button?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;This article discusses a hypothetical cybersecurity scenario and does not allege that any specific stablecoin issuer has experienced an AI-driven private-key theft. It is for informational purposes only and does not constitute financial or investment advice.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>India Plans First Tokenized Corporate Bond Issuance in September With CBDC Settlement</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjGAbtwP6cVlMmf6UdUK6aui_40Q2nHnP8kIqLya8nBu6hBuL57-Gm7ZCloVg4l69VOemE-Euo6GBdKp6hz0grnpph2EVude9mWAmO3gGB_uVcB6RzfFMPA2REWw1UzvfxGr3oO2E-JS1o4g5b-dr1kKptNaifye48e81yNkGkI3MGvyoCMuLCHXASjKpQu/s1672/india-tokenized-corporate-bond-cbdc-settlement.jpg%20(2).png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="India plans its first tokenized corporate bond issuance using CBDC settlement" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjGAbtwP6cVlMmf6UdUK6aui_40Q2nHnP8kIqLya8nBu6hBuL57-Gm7ZCloVg4l69VOemE-Euo6GBdKp6hz0grnpph2EVude9mWAmO3gGB_uVcB6RzfFMPA2REWw1UzvfxGr3oO2E-JS1o4g5b-dr1kKptNaifye48e81yNkGkI3MGvyoCMuLCHXASjKpQu/w400-h225/india-tokenized-corporate-bond-cbdc-settlement.jpg%20(2).png" title="India's First Tokenized Corporate Bond With CBDC Settlement" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;By CoinAINews Staff | &lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;India is preparing to take another major step into
blockchain-based financial infrastructure, with the country planning to launch
its &lt;b&gt;first tokenized corporate bond issuance in September&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The pilot is expected to be led by state-owned power
financier &lt;b&gt;REC&lt;/b&gt;, with the bonds issued using distributed-ledger technology
and purchased using India's central bank digital currency (CBDC), according to
Reuters, which cited people familiar with the plans.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The planned transaction is relatively small, but its
significance could extend well beyond the size of the issuance. It would give
India an opportunity to test whether tokenized securities and digital-currency
settlement can work together inside the country's regulated financial system.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What India Is Planning&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The September offering is expected to be worth &lt;b&gt;less than
₹5 billion, or roughly $57 million&lt;/b&gt;, according to Reuters.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;REC is expected to issue the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/sam-altman-warns-ais-biggest-risks.html"&gt;tokenized&lt;/a&gt; corporate bonds as
part of the pilot.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Rather than relying entirely on conventional securities
infrastructure, the bonds will be represented digitally on distributed-ledger
technology.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The idea is to create a digital record of the securities
while allowing transactions and ownership transfers to take place through a
blockchain-based system.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The broader objective is to determine whether tokenization
can make parts of India's corporate bond market &lt;b&gt;faster, more efficient and
easier to settle&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;CBDC Will Be Used for Settlement&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;One of the most notable aspects of the project is the
planned use of India's &lt;b&gt;central bank digital currency&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Investors participating in the pilot are expected to use a
wholesale CBDC wallet provided through a bank, alongside a separate digital
securities &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/crypto-fear-greed-index-hits-74-highest.html"&gt;wallet&lt;/a&gt; for holding the tokenized bonds.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;India's securities depositories are developing the digital
securities infrastructure, reportedly referred to as &lt;b&gt;DEMAT 2.0&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This creates a system in which the payment and securities
sides of a transaction can operate digitally.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In traditional financial markets, securities transfers and
payments can involve multiple systems, intermediaries and reconciliation
processes.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A tokenized structure could potentially bring those steps
closer together.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Instant Settlement Matters&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Settlement is one of the most important parts of any
&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/hugging-face-reportedly-explores-13b.html"&gt;financial transaction&lt;/a&gt;, even though investors rarely see the process directly.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;When a corporate bond changes hands, both the security and
the corresponding payment have to move between parties.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Tokenization could allow ownership of the bond to be
recorded digitally, while the CBDC could provide the payment leg.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If the two systems can operate together effectively,
transactions could potentially settle much faster than under conventional
arrangements.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That is one of the main reasons financial institutions
around the world are experimenting with tokenized bonds and other real-world
assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Pilot Will Start With Selected Investors&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;India is not expected to open the first tokenized bond issue
to the entire investment market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Reuters reported that participation will initially be
limited to a &lt;b&gt;select group of investors&lt;/b&gt; while the infrastructure is
tested.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The bonds are also expected to have an initial &lt;b&gt;three-month
lock-in period&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A secondary market could follow later, with exchanges
reportedly looking toward December for secondary trading of the tokenized
securities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This phased approach gives regulators and market
participants an opportunity to identify technical and operational problems
before expanding the system.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;RBI and SEBI Are Involved&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The initiative is being developed with the involvement of
the &lt;b&gt;Reserve Bank of India (RBI)&lt;/b&gt; and the &lt;b&gt;Securities and Exchange Board
of India (SEBI)&lt;/b&gt;, giving it formal regulatory backing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That involvement is important because tokenized securities
sit at the intersection of traditional capital markets, digital assets and
financial technology.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;India's securities regulator has already been examining how
tokenization could be applied to the corporate bond market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The new pilot moves that discussion closer to an actual
market transaction.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Corporate Bonds?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;India's corporate bond market has significant potential for
further development.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Tokenization could eventually make it easier to issue,
transfer and settle debt securities while maintaining digital records of
ownership.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;However, blockchain technology alone will not solve every
challenge.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Liquidity, investor demand, credit quality, regulation and
the availability of an active secondary market will remain critical.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That means the September transaction should be viewed
primarily as an &lt;b&gt;infrastructure test&lt;/b&gt;, rather than an immediate
transformation of India's bond market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;India's Digital Rupee Gets Another Use Case&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The project could also give India's CBDC another important
institutional use case.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Reserve Bank of India has been experimenting with the
digital rupee since 2022, including wholesale applications involving
financial-market transactions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The wholesale CBDC was initially designed to explore areas
such as government securities settlement.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Using the digital rupee alongside tokenized corporate bonds
would extend that experimentation into another part of India's capital markets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The potential significance is that the CBDC would not simply
function as digital money.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It would become part of a broader &lt;b&gt;digital settlement
infrastructure&lt;/b&gt; connecting money and financial assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Tokenized Bonds Could Change&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If the pilot performs well, tokenized bonds could eventually
offer several potential advantages.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Faster settlement:&lt;/b&gt; Digital infrastructure could
reduce the time required to complete transactions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Digital ownership records:&lt;/b&gt; Ownership and transfers
could be recorded directly through distributed-ledger infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Greater automation:&lt;/b&gt; Certain settlement, compliance
and transaction processes could potentially be automated.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Reduced reconciliation:&lt;/b&gt; Connecting the securities and
payment sides digitally could reduce the need to reconcile separate systems.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;These benefits are still potential outcomes.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The September pilot will provide a much more meaningful test
of whether they can be achieved within India's regulated financial environment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;India Joins a Growing Global Trend&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;India is not alone in exploring tokenized financial assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Financial institutions and regulators across major markets
have been testing blockchain-based securities, including tokenized bonds.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hong Kong and European markets have already experimented
with blockchain-based bond issuance and settlement.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;India's approach stands out because it combines &lt;b&gt;tokenized
securities with a central bank digital currency&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That combination could eventually provide a blueprint for
connecting traditional financial assets with government-backed digital money.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bigger Picture&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The importance of India's planned issuance goes beyond its
relatively modest size.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;An offering of less than ₹5 billion is small compared with
the country's overall financial markets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But the infrastructure being tested could eventually be
applied to a much broader range of securities if regulators and market
participants determine that it works effectively.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The key question is whether tokenization can produce
measurable efficiency gains without introducing new technological, operational
or regulatory risks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For now, India's approach is deliberately cautious: a
limited investor group, a controlled issuance and dedicated digital
infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That allows the country's financial authorities to gather
practical experience before considering wider adoption.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;India is preparing for its &lt;b&gt;first tokenized corporate bond
issuance in September&lt;/b&gt;, with state-owned REC expected to issue less than &lt;b&gt;₹5
billion ($57 million)&lt;/b&gt; of securities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The pilot is expected to use &lt;b&gt;distributed-ledger
technology for the bonds and India's CBDC for payment and settlement&lt;/b&gt;,
creating a direct test of how tokenized securities and digital money can work
together.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The transaction may be small, but the experiment could have
much broader implications for India's financial infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If the system works as intended, tokenization could
eventually make parts of the country's debt market faster, more automated and
digitally connected.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The bigger question is no longer whether India will
experiment with tokenized finance — &lt;b&gt;it is how quickly those experiments can
move from controlled pilots into the mainstream financial system — and whether
they deliver measurable improvements when they do.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does
not constitute investment advice. Cryptocurrency, digital-asset and financial
markets involve risks. Readers should conduct their own research before making
financial decisions.&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>How to Move an Encrypted Seedless Electrum Wallet to Bitcoin Core</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiDW9Jvoj2ydiM5iS9fTfEePQ4mOW4XDo-WKU5bXPof9SGDz_lgzKzfx87RpL36lkr0xAMfsgG73Tj_JKCNWir2CkXABGMuS6IQ37F6GjLThrTalsABeTPMmLO6FwgntNA1aDkvtn0Qt0umVRzLtlmWma_-7x0t3kpQYLO-BvWtwuGO4irCcVTf8zDq8zdc/s1672/encrypted-seedless-electrum-wallet-to-bitcoin-core.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="How to move an encrypted seedless Electrum wallet to Bitcoin Core" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiDW9Jvoj2ydiM5iS9fTfEePQ4mOW4XDo-WKU5bXPof9SGDz_lgzKzfx87RpL36lkr0xAMfsgG73Tj_JKCNWir2CkXABGMuS6IQ37F6GjLThrTalsABeTPMmLO6FwgntNA1aDkvtn0Qt0umVRzLtlmWma_-7x0t3kpQYLO-BvWtwuGO4irCcVTf8zDq8zdc/w640-h360/encrypted-seedless-electrum-wallet-to-bitcoin-core.jpg.png" title="Encrypted Electrum Wallet to Bitcoin Core Migration" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;
September 6, 2026&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Moving Bitcoin from an older Electrum wallet to Bitcoin Core can be confusing, particularly when the Electrum wallet is encrypted and does not have a recovery seed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In that situation, the migration is not simply a matter of copying the Electrum wallet file into Bitcoin Core. The two applications use different wallet formats and modern Bitcoin Core uses a descriptor-based wallet architecture.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For a seedless Electrum wallet containing imported private keys, the important question is how to transfer or recreate control of those Bitcoin addresses in Bitcoin Core without exposing the private keys.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is also an important version difference. Older Bitcoin Core releases supported the legacy &lt;code&gt;importprivkey&lt;/code&gt; RPC, while current Bitcoin Core 30.x no longer supports legacy wallets and the legacy-only import commands. Modern installations therefore require a different approach.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is a Seedless Electrum Wallet?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Electrum wallets can use deterministic seeds, but an Electrum wallet can also contain imported private keys.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When a wallet consists of imported keys and has no seed that can reproduce those keys, it is commonly described as a seedless or imported-key wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction matters during migration. A seed phrase cannot recreate private keys that were independently imported into an &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ark-invest-researcher-questions-whether.html"&gt;Electrum wallet&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In that case, the relevant private keys themselves—or another compatible representation of their key and script information—are needed to reproduce control of the addresses in another wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Electrum's documentation provides command-line functionality for identifying funded addresses and obtaining their private keys. The exact commands can vary with the Electrum version being used.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Do Not Copy the Electrum Wallet File Into Bitcoin Core&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Electrum and Bitcoin Core use different wallet storage formats.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Copying an Electrum wallet file into a Bitcoin Core wallet directory does not convert the file into a Bitcoin Core wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The safer way to think about the process is as a &lt;strong&gt;wallet migration&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than a file-format conversion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You either transfer the relevant key information into a compatible Bitcoin Core wallet configuration or send the Bitcoin from the old addresses to a new address generated by Bitcoin Core.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Back Up the Electrum Wallet First&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Before exporting or changing anything, make a secure backup of the original Electrum wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Do not delete the original wallet simply because the private keys have been exported. Keep the backup until the new Bitcoin Core wallet has been independently verified.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An encrypted wallet password protects the wallet data, but it should not be confused with the Bitcoin private keys. Anyone who obtains an unencrypted private key can potentially spend the Bitcoin controlled by that key.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For that reason, never paste real private keys into websites, online converters, public forums, screenshots or other services that do not need access to them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Identify the Bitcoin Addresses You Need to Migrate&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the Electrum wallet contains multiple imported keys, first determine which addresses actually contain Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is little reason to migrate unused addresses unless you specifically want to preserve them for historical or organizational reasons.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Electrum's command-line documentation includes commands for listing funded addresses and retrieving their private keys. For example:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code&gt;electrum listaddresses --funded&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Electrum also documents workflows involving &lt;code&gt;getprivatekeys&lt;/code&gt; for obtaining the private keys associated with addresses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because command syntax can change between &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/zcash-surges-above-1000-as-etf-demand.html"&gt;Electrum releases&lt;/a&gt;, users should check the documentation corresponding to the version they have installed before running wallet commands.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Export the Private Keys Carefully&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For an imported-key wallet, the private key is the critical piece of information that gives spending authority over the associated Bitcoin address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Export only the keys you actually need and keep them protected while performing the migration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A private key should be treated like cash. If another person or an untrusted application obtains it, the associated Bitcoin can potentially be spent without your permission.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is therefore a bad idea to use an online “private key converter” or paste a real key into an online tool simply to make it compatible with another wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Check Your Bitcoin Core Version&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the most important parts of the migration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Older Bitcoin Core versions supported legacy wallets. In those versions, the &lt;code&gt;importprivkey&lt;/code&gt; RPC could be used to import a private key into a legacy wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin Core's documentation for older releases describes &lt;code&gt;importprivkey&lt;/code&gt; as a legacy-wallet RPC and directs descriptor-wallet users toward &lt;code&gt;importdescriptors&lt;/code&gt; instead.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That old workflow should not be copied blindly into a current Bitcoin Core installation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin Core 30.0 removed legacy wallet support and removed legacy-only RPCs including &lt;code&gt;importprivkey&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;importwallet&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;dumpprivkey&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;importmulti&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Modern Bitcoin Core Handles Wallet Imports&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Modern Bitcoin Core uses &lt;strong&gt;output descriptors&lt;/strong&gt; to describe the scripts and keys that belong to a wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of simply placing an isolated private key into an old-style key store, the descriptor tells Bitcoin Core how the relevant key material is used to create and recognize Bitcoin scripts.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin Core provides the &lt;code&gt;importdescriptors&lt;/code&gt; RPC for importing descriptors into descriptor wallets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, an imported-key Electrum wallet does not necessarily provide a ready-made descriptor that can simply be copied into &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/sam-altman-says-ai-industry-did.html"&gt;Bitcoin Core&lt;/a&gt;. The appropriate descriptor depends on the address type and the way the private key is used.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why users migrating an older Electrum wallet should identify the exact address and script type before constructing or importing descriptor information.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Bitcoin Address Type Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin uses several different address and script formats.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An older wallet may contain legacy P2PKH addresses that commonly begin with &lt;strong&gt;1&lt;/strong&gt;. P2SH addresses commonly begin with &lt;strong&gt;3&lt;/strong&gt;, while native SegWit addresses commonly use &lt;strong&gt;bc1q&lt;/strong&gt;. Taproot addresses use the &lt;strong&gt;bc1p&lt;/strong&gt; format.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The private key alone does not always tell Bitcoin Core which script type you want the wallet to monitor.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, using the correct key with an incorrect script or descriptor can cause Bitcoin Core to watch the wrong output type and fail to display the expected balance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Address type should therefore be verified before attempting a descriptor-based migration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happened to importprivkey?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The command still appears in many older Bitcoin wallet tutorials, which is why users can encounter conflicting instructions online.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In an older compatible Bitcoin Core release, the historical command looked like this:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code&gt;importprivkey "PRIVATE_KEY"&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That command belongs to the &lt;strong&gt;legacy wallet workflow&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is not a universal command for current Bitcoin Core. Bitcoin Core 30.0 removed legacy wallet support and the associated legacy-only RPCs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Therefore, a guide written for an older version of Bitcoin Core can be technically correct for that version while being completely unsuitable for a current installation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Modern Bitcoin Core: Descriptor-Based Migration&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For a current Bitcoin Core installation, the migration should be planned around descriptors rather than the old legacy import commands.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The general process is:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Back up the original Electrum wallet.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Identify the funded Electrum addresses.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Determine the script/address type used by each address.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Securely obtain the corresponding private-key information.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Construct the appropriate descriptor for the key and script type when a descriptor-based import is appropriate.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Create or use a descriptor wallet in Bitcoin Core.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Import the descriptor using the supported Bitcoin Core wallet tools.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Allow Bitcoin Core to scan the blockchain for relevant transactions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Verify the address, transaction history and balance.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The exact descriptor syntax depends on the address type and key structure. Users should not blindly substitute a private key into a descriptor without understanding the script being described.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;An Alternative: Send the Bitcoin to a New Bitcoin Core Address&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In many cases, the simplest migration is not to import the old private keys at all.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, create a new address in a fresh Bitcoin Core wallet and send the Bitcoin from Electrum to that address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This creates a normal Bitcoin transaction and transfers the coins to a new output controlled by Bitcoin Core.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once the transaction receives sufficient confirmation, the old Electrum keys are no longer required to control those newly transferred coins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This approach can be easier to understand because the old wallet and new wallet remain completely separate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Importing vs. Sending to a New Wallet&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 650px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Method&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;What Happens&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Main Consideration&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Descriptor import&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Bitcoin Core gains knowledge &lt;br /&gt;of the existing wallet scripts &lt;br /&gt;and keys&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Requires the correct &lt;br /&gt;descriptor and script type&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Legacy private-key import&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Older Bitcoin Core could add &lt;br /&gt;the key to a legacy wallet&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Not available in current &lt;br /&gt;Bitcoin Core 30.x&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Send to new address&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Bitcoin moves to a fresh &lt;br /&gt;Bitcoin Core address&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Requires an on-chain &lt;br /&gt;transaction and network fee&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Watch-only setup&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Bitcoin Core can monitor &lt;br /&gt;addresses without spending authority&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Private keys are still &lt;br /&gt;needed to spend&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Sending to a Fresh Address Can Be Cleaner&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the purpose of the migration is to retire an old wallet, sending the Bitcoin to a newly generated Bitcoin Core address is often easier to verify.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The old Electrum wallet controls the original output, while the new Bitcoin Core wallet controls the new output after the transaction confirms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This avoids maintaining imported legacy keys in the new wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The disadvantage is that an on-chain transaction is required and therefore a transaction fee may apply.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It also creates a new publicly visible transaction linking the old and new addresses through blockchain data. Moving the Bitcoin does not erase the historical transaction record of the old address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does Encryption Change?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An encrypted Electrum wallet can still be migrated if its owner can unlock the wallet and access the necessary key information.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The encryption password protects the wallet's stored data. It is not a replacement for the underlying Bitcoin private keys.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin Core will also have its own wallet encryption and security mechanisms. Encryption from Electrum does not automatically transfer to Bitcoin Core.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;After creating the Bitcoin Core wallet, users should configure its security separately and protect the wallet data and credentials appropriately.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Blockchain Rescanning Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When wallet information is imported, Bitcoin Core needs to identify the relevant historical transactions and unspent outputs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Older Bitcoin Core import procedures could trigger a blockchain rescan. Descriptor imports can also involve scanning for transactions matching the imported descriptors.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A wallet may therefore temporarily show an incomplete or zero balance while synchronization or scanning is still in progress.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Users should wait for the relevant process to finish before concluding that the migration failed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How to Verify the Migration&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Never delete the original Electrum wallet immediately after completing the migration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;First verify that Bitcoin Core recognizes the expected address or descriptor.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Then check:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The expected Bitcoin address.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The transaction history.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The expected unspent balance.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether the wallet has spending capability rather than being watch-only.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether Bitcoin Core is fully synchronized with the Bitcoin network.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the migration involves a transfer to a new address, verify the transaction on the Bitcoin blockchain and wait for the expected confirmations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Only after the destination wallet has been independently verified should the old wallet be considered for retirement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Common Mistakes to Avoid&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Copying the Electrum wallet file into Bitcoin Core:&lt;/strong&gt; The two wallet formats are different.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Using an old tutorial without checking the Bitcoin Core version:&lt;/strong&gt; Commands available years ago may no longer exist.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Using importprivkey on Bitcoin Core 30.x:&lt;/strong&gt; This is a legacy-wallet RPC that was removed with legacy wallet support.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Using the wrong descriptor:&lt;/strong&gt; The descriptor must match the relevant Bitcoin script and address type.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Assuming a seed can recreate imported keys:&lt;/strong&gt; A seedless imported-key wallet may require the actual private keys.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Deleting the original wallet too soon:&lt;/strong&gt; Keep a secure backup until the migration is verified.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Exposing private keys:&lt;/strong&gt; Never paste real private keys into websites, forums, screenshots or untrusted software.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can I directly import an Electrum wallet file into Bitcoin Core?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. Electrum and Bitcoin Core use different wallet formats. The migration requires transferring compatible key or descriptor information, or sending the Bitcoin to a new Bitcoin Core address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can I use importprivkey in the latest Bitcoin Core?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. The legacy &lt;code&gt;importprivkey&lt;/code&gt; RPC was removed along with legacy wallet support in Bitcoin Core 30.0. Modern Bitcoin Core uses descriptor-based wallets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can an encrypted Electrum wallet be migrated?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes. If you can unlock the wallet and access the required private keys or compatible key information, the wallet's Bitcoin can be migrated using an appropriate workflow.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What if my Electrum wallet has no seed?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;If the wallet contains independently imported private keys, the seed cannot necessarily recreate those keys. The relevant private keys or compatible wallet information must be preserved.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is sending Bitcoin to a new Bitcoin Core address easier?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;For many users, yes. It creates a clean on-chain transfer to a fresh Bitcoin Core address and avoids importing the old wallet's keys. The trade-off is the transaction fee and the public blockchain record of the transfer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does importing a private key move the Bitcoin?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. Importing key information does not move coins on the blockchain. It gives the destination wallet the ability to recognize and potentially spend the Bitcoin associated with the relevant address. An actual transaction is required to move the coins to another address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why does Bitcoin Core show no balance after an import?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The wallet may still need to scan the blockchain, or the imported descriptor may not match the actual script type. Synchronization and the exact wallet configuration should be checked before assuming the funds are missing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Moving an encrypted seedless Electrum wallet to Bitcoin Core is not a simple wallet-file conversion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The correct procedure depends heavily on the type of keys in the Electrum wallet and the version of Bitcoin Core being used.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For older Bitcoin Core releases, &lt;code&gt;importprivkey&lt;/code&gt; was part of the legacy-wallet workflow. Current Bitcoin Core 30.x has removed legacy wallets and their legacy-only RPCs, so that old method should not be followed on a modern installation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For current Bitcoin Core, descriptor-based wallet management is the relevant architecture. However, the descriptor must accurately represent the original Bitcoin script and address type.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For users who simply want to move their funds into a new Bitcoin Core wallet, creating a fresh Bitcoin Core address and sending the Bitcoin there can be a straightforward alternative.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Whatever method is chosen, the most important security rule remains the same: &lt;strong&gt;protect the original Electrum backup and never expose real private keys to untrusted websites or people.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Sources&lt;/h2&gt;

Always verify the documentation for the exact Electrum and Bitcoin Core versions being used, and never disclose a real private key or wallet password.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Crypto PR Distribution in 2026: Why Startups Are Exploring Alternatives to Traditional Newswires</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEixbmzy16WWIO4M3ohm1lQKYMPx_A5NI7_G32ulYJQA9amN7ZFalOK4CdW_hlgCPDh4Ku5edZ__4N4q3JDVgAv5dk3cn05JXuUS9Pxt__-WyTZgFiiLMFJpDEswQbDzIs-Th3qS4WzneiLN7u4A_QHBOL6CxiCFVNsWSxy0nV1VkO58E7EWhw_BPgE79fRb/s1734/crypto-pr-distribution-2026-wirero.webp.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Crypto PR distribution in 2026 through traditional newswires and multi-domain publishing networks" border="0" data-original-height="907" data-original-width="1734" height="334" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEixbmzy16WWIO4M3ohm1lQKYMPx_A5NI7_G32ulYJQA9amN7ZFalOK4CdW_hlgCPDh4Ku5edZ__4N4q3JDVgAv5dk3cn05JXuUS9Pxt__-WyTZgFiiLMFJpDEswQbDzIs-Th3qS4WzneiLN7u4A_QHBOL6CxiCFVNsWSxy0nV1VkO58E7EWhw_BPgE79fRb/w640-h334/crypto-pr-distribution-2026-wirero.webp.png" title="Crypto PR Distribution in 2026" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By CoinAINews Editorial Team&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;For a crypto startup, getting an announcement in front of the right audience can be harder than writing the announcement itself.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The industry moves quickly. A new token launch, &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=blockchain+partnership+examples+crypto&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=4324214788202780066" target="_blank"&gt;blockchain partnership&lt;/a&gt; or product update can be old news within a matter of hours. At the same time, crypto companies are competing for attention across financial websites, technology publications, blockchain media and increasingly crowded search results.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That has pushed some startups and agencies to look beyond the &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=define+traditional+press+release&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=4324214788202780066" target="_blank"&gt;traditional press release&lt;/a&gt; model.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional newswires still have an important role, particularly for companies looking for established media distribution and journalist-facing services. But another model has also been gaining attention: distributing announcements through networks of publishing domains and industry-specific websites.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://wirero.com/network/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;Wirero&lt;/a&gt; is one company operating in this space. Rather than presenting itself as a conventional newswire, it describes its service as distribution infrastructure built around publishing domains and industry networks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So what does that model actually offer, and where does it fit into a crypto company's PR strategy?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Crypto Startups Are Looking Beyond Traditional Newswires&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is a practical reason for the interest.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Many crypto businesses are not large corporations with dedicated communications departments. A startup may have a small marketing team handling product launches, social media, partnerships, community management and public relations at the same time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For those companies, the economics and workflow of PR distribution matter.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A company might have several legitimate announcements throughout the year: a &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=crypto+funding+round+explained&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=4324214788202780066" target="_blank"&gt;funding round&lt;/a&gt;, a new exchange integration, a protocol upgrade, a strategic partnership or the launch of a new product. Buying and managing a separate distribution campaign for every announcement may not always fit the way a smaller company operates.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one reason subscription-based distribution infrastructure has become an option worth examining.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What a Crypto Company Actually Gets From PR Distribution&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At its simplest, PR distribution gives a company another way to put an announcement in front of people who may not have encountered it through the company's own website or social channels.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For crypto companies, those announcements can cover a wide range of subjects:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;New blockchain or &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=Web3+products+examples&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=4324214788202780066" target="_blank"&gt;Web3 products&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Exchange listings and integrations&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Funding announcements&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Strategic partnerships&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Protocol and infrastructure launches&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Research reports&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Executive appointments&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Geographic expansion&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Major product updates&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is an important distinction here. Distribution is not the same thing as journalism.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A press release being distributed to a publication does not necessarily mean that the publication's editorial team independently investigated the company or decided that the announcement deserved a separate news report.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For companies planning a PR campaign, that difference is worth keeping in mind.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is Multi-Domain Press Release Distribution?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The idea behind &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=define+multi-domain+distribution&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=4324214788202780066" target="_blank"&gt;multi-domain distribution&lt;/a&gt; is fairly straightforward.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of relying on one traditional newswire channel, an announcement can be distributed across a broader network of publishing websites. The networks may also be divided into different industry categories.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Wirero's &lt;a href="https://wirero.com/network/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;network page&lt;/a&gt; describes this approach and lists industry-focused publishing networks, including categories relevant to technology, fintech and blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For a crypto company, that can be useful when the goal is not simply to send one release through a general newswire, but to reach different parts of the online publishing ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The model is particularly relevant to businesses that expect to distribute announcements repeatedly rather than running an occasional one-off campaign.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Traditional Newswire vs. Multi-Domain Distribution&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 8px;"&gt;Factor&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 8px;"&gt;Traditional Newswire&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 8px;"&gt;Multi-Domain Distribution&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
