    <title>IMF Warns Local Stablecoins Could Accelerate Dollarization Push</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhpFTmXPIve69nlC-QoeQ6Gs5NUioArA7XTZURVIA8FiJs1SJ_ftwkVCzv8KzgijsJ4tOm39Nv2uqxzBSOkks3CB52NkkpsLVzbgDvLj-sMuQoPGrdpEB5k_IafkSslAlA0XwekaHcAAub385k2ZtxEmmOt_szdt5gpYuMe8mNd7vgz-pat5sRRY335TGMR/s1408/doll.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="IMF warns local stablecoins could accelerate dollarization push Nigeria crypto adoption" border="0" data-original-height="768" data-original-width="1408" height="175" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhpFTmXPIve69nlC-QoeQ6Gs5NUioArA7XTZURVIA8FiJs1SJ_ftwkVCzv8KzgijsJ4tOm39Nv2uqxzBSOkks3CB52NkkpsLVzbgDvLj-sMuQoPGrdpEB5k_IafkSslAlA0XwekaHcAAub385k2ZtxEmmOt_szdt5gpYuMe8mNd7vgz-pat5sRRY335TGMR/w320-h175/doll.png" title="International Monetary Fund headquarters Washington DC stablecoin regulation warning" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aug 8, 2026&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;– The International Monetary Fund
has issued a stark warning: efforts to promote stablecoins pegged to local
currencies could inadvertently accelerate adoption of dollar-backed digital
assets, strengthening the U.S. dollar's dominance in the digital economy rather
than diminishing it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In remarks delivered at the University of Cape Town, IMF
First Deputy Managing Director Dan Katz said that if local-currency and
dollar-denominated stablecoins operate on the same blockchain infrastructure,
conversion between the two could become routine through decentralized
exchanges, liquidity pools, or peer-to-peer swaps&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"In this way, local-currency stablecoins might even
accelerate the adoption of FX stablecoins," Katz said, highlighting a key
tension in the policy debate: efforts meant to localize currency exposure could
end up making dollar stablecoins more accessible&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why Infrastructure Changes the Stablecoin Story&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Katz's core argument centers on interoperability. Once local
and dollar stablecoins share technical rails, users have multiple pathways to
convert between them, effectively reducing the practical difference between
holding a rand-linked or dollar-linked token&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;This matters because stablecoin adoption is often shaped by
more than just the peg. According to Katz, even when local-currency tokens are
available, many users may still prefer dollar tokens due to factors like
liquidity, network effects, and acceptance across platforms and borders&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;When those advantages are paired with interoperability, the
"local-currency" intention can be diluted: users may treat pegged
tokens as interchangeable shortcuts rather than separate ecosystems&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Nigerian Case: Digital Dollarization in Action&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The IMF's warning comes against the backdrop of Nigeria's
surging stablecoin adoption, which the Fund says is "testing the
limits" of existing monetary and regulatory frameworks&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The scale is striking:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Nigeria
     received approximately&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$59 billion&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in crypto-asset
     inflows between July 2023 and June 2024&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;The
     country ranks second globally on Chainalysis' 2024 Global Crypto Adoption
     Index&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Nigeria
     accounts for roughly&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;60%&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;of stablecoin inflows into
     sub-Saharan Africa since 2019&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why stablecoins have taken hold:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Nigerian households and small businesses have turned to
dollar-pegged stablecoins because they offer faster, cheaper cross-border
payments compared to traditional channels&amp;nbsp;. The average cost of sending
$200 to sub-Saharan Africa remains around 9% of transaction value, well above
the global average of 6%, according to the World Bank&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Domestic conditions amplified this shift. The sharp
depreciation of the naira, high inflation, and constrained access to foreign
exchange in 2023-2024 pushed households and businesses toward dollar-linked
assets as a hedge against currency risk and a tool for paying overseas
suppliers&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Policy Trade-offs: The Digital Dollarization Dilemma&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The rise of stablecoins brings clear benefits — faster,
cheaper cross-border payments can support trade, remittances, and financial
inclusion&amp;nbsp;. Yet the same features raise serious policy concerns:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Monetary sovereignty:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Widespread use of
dollar-denominated stablecoins resembles a digital form of dollarization. By
reducing demand for the local currency, it could weaken the transmission of
domestic monetary policy&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Financial integrity:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Activity that once flowed
through banks is moving increasingly to digital wallets and crypto exchanges.
The speed and anonymity of some platforms increase risks of money laundering
and other illicit financial flows&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Capital flow monitoring:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;When payments move
through digital wallets and offshore platforms, central bankers lose visibility
over how much money is entering or leaving the country, making it harder to
manage currencies and respond to shocks&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;A Pragmatic Policy Response&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The IMF has advised against outright bans on stablecoins,
warning that such measures would likely be only partly effective&amp;nbsp;.
Instead, the Fund outlined four priorities for managing risks while preserving
innovation:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;1. Safeguard monetary stability:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The most
effective defense against digital dollarization is a stable and credible
domestic currency. Nigeria's recent macroeconomic reforms and tighter monetary
policy have helped restore confidence in the naira, and the IMF urged
sustaining this progress&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;2. Strengthen oversight:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Countries need clearer
rules on stablecoin issuers aligned with emerging international frameworks in
jurisdictions like the EU, Singapore, Japan, and the United States&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;3. Improve data visibility:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Combining blockchain
analytics with reporting on local-currency-to-stablecoin conversions would help
regulators identify risks early and respond effectively&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;4. Upgrade payment infrastructure:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Much of the
demand for stablecoins reflects gaps in existing systems. Strengthening
domestic payment channels would reduce reliance on unregulated
alternatives&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Broader Implications&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The global stablecoin market has grown into a sector worth
more than **$300 billion**, dominated by dollar-backed tokens such as Tether's
USDT (approximately $186.5 billion) and Circle's USDC (near $75 billion)&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Katz's remarks underscore a fundamental tension:
local-currency stablecoin initiatives designed to reduce dollar dependence may
paradoxically strengthen dollar dominance if they operate on interoperable
infrastructure&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For emerging markets like Nigeria, where 95% of respondents
in a recent survey said they would prefer receiving payments in stablecoins
rather than their local currency, the challenge is acute&amp;nbsp;. As the IMF's
assessment concluded: "What began as a niche technology has become a
meaningful cross-border payments channel" that is "testing the limits
of existing monetary and regulatory frameworks"&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The question for policymakers worldwide is whether they can
build regulatory frameworks that bring onchain exchange points, onramps, and
offramps within regulatory boundaries — or risk ceding control to an
increasingly dollar-dominated digital financial system&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

    <title>Taiwan Lawmaker Pushes Bitcoin Reserve Plan Into the Near Future — But It's Not a Done Deal</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;
  &lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj4M7MyeWDKS_UkIcfrmqXWzdES4gC1bYm-_S7Ibjj2Zwb_6F9UCKGxeOm7cH0oSmfkLJ95LVcQx1cdSgECM56uEqHCMSxb-eQ_-O3siVu0RUn8RYSyRAn98FL1Eg36UnbDoO-B4BcxO_g7FLMvqx1a9-RJbL3Ab9ofDsjnh65_7WCCQoo5j0-uq66lwUuG/s1672/taiwan-bitcoin-reserve-policy-proposal.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Taiwan Bitcoin reserve proposal with Bitcoin and digital financial network" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj4M7MyeWDKS_UkIcfrmqXWzdES4gC1bYm-_S7Ibjj2Zwb_6F9UCKGxeOm7cH0oSmfkLJ95LVcQx1cdSgECM56uEqHCMSxb-eQ_-O3siVu0RUn8RYSyRAn98FL1Eg36UnbDoO-B4BcxO_g7FLMvqx1a9-RJbL3Ab9ofDsjnh65_7WCCQoo5j0-uq66lwUuG/w400-h225/taiwan-bitcoin-reserve-policy-proposal.jpg.png" title="Taiwan Bitcoin Reserve Proposal Gains Policy Attention" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&amp;nbsp;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Taiwan's Bitcoin debate is moving beyond the usual crypto conference talk — and into the realm of actual policy discussion.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;At Bitcoin Asia, Taiwanese legislator &lt;strong&gt;Ko Ju-chun&lt;/strong&gt; said a national Bitcoin reserve should be considered a plan for the near future, according to a post from Cointelegraph.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The comment adds fresh momentum to an idea Ko has been promoting for months. But there is an important distinction: &lt;strong&gt;Taiwan has not officially established a national Bitcoin reserve.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For now, the country is still debating what such a policy could look like, while Ko continues pushing policymakers to take the idea seriously.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Earlier this year, he presented a Bitcoin reserve report to Taiwan's premier and central bank governor, bringing the issue directly into the country's policy conversation.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;From Bitcoin Debate to Reserve Planning&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Ko's interest in Bitcoin as a strategic asset isn't new.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In April, he delivered research from the Bitcoin Policy Institute to Premier Cho Jung-tai and Central Bank of China Governor Yang Chin-long during a Legislative Yuan session. The report examined the case for Taiwan holding Bitcoin as part of its reserves.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That was significant because the conversation moved beyond general cryptocurrency adoption.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A government considering Bitcoin as a reserve asset would have to answer a much longer list of questions:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;How would Bitcoin be acquired?&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Who would be responsible for custody?&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Where would the private keys be stored?&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;How much Bitcoin could the government hold?&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;How would extreme price volatility be handled?&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;What legal authority would be required?&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;None of those questions is particularly simple.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;And supporting the concept politically doesn't automatically answer them.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Taiwan Is Looking at Bitcoin&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Ko's argument isn't based solely on the possibility that Bitcoin could appreciate.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A major part of the case involves &lt;strong&gt;diversification&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Taiwan maintains substantial foreign-exchange reserves, largely connected to traditional reserve assets. Ko has argued that Bitcoin could provide another form of diversification while giving Taiwan exposure to an asset that isn't issued or controlled by another government.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That argument becomes more interesting when Taiwan's broader geopolitical and financial position is considered.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The island is deeply connected to international trade and global financial markets. Any disruption to those systems could create significant economic challenges.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin operates differently from conventional reserve assets.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It doesn't require a traditional banking intermediary to transfer value across borders.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But that advantage comes with an obvious downside.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin can experience much larger price swings than conventional reserve assets.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A government therefore couldn't simply treat Bitcoin like cash or short-term government securities.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The risk-management question would be unavoidable.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Taiwan Already Holds Bitcoin From Seizures&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There's another reason the debate has attracted attention.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Taiwan's government already holds Bitcoin obtained through law-enforcement seizures.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;BitcoinTreasuries.net has reported that Taiwan has held Bitcoin connected to criminal investigations, although the exact amount of government-held BTC can change as assets from different cases are processed.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That doesn't mean Taiwan already has a strategic Bitcoin reserve.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The distinction is critical.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin obtained through asset seizures is fundamentally different from Bitcoin deliberately purchased or allocated as part of a national reserve strategy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Still, the existence of government-held BTC creates a practical policy question.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Should seized Bitcoin eventually be sold?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Should it remain under government custody?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Could lawmakers eventually create a framework allowing some government-held Bitcoin to become part of a broader strategic reserve?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Those questions are likely to remain part of the debate.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Legal Framework Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A national Bitcoin reserve can't simply be created by putting coins into a government-controlled wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A formal policy would require rules around acquisition, custody, accounting and authorization.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Who would approve a purchase?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Who would control the private keys?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;How many people or institutions would be involved in signing transactions?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;What happens if Bitcoin loses half its value?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;How would the government disclose gains or losses?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;And what happens when political leadership changes?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;These questions become even more important when an asset is intended to be held for years rather than traded for short-term returns.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Ko has also linked the Bitcoin-reserve discussion to Taiwan's developing virtual-asset regulatory framework.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The country's evolving rules for digital assets could eventually provide a broader legal environment for policymakers to examine Bitcoin's potential role in the financial system.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But regulation of virtual assets does not automatically authorize the creation of a sovereign Bitcoin reserve.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That would require a separate policy decision.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Ko Has Put a Timeline on the Idea&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Ko has previously gone beyond simply saying Taiwan should study Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In July, he reportedly estimated an &lt;strong&gt;80% chance&lt;/strong&gt; that Taiwan could establish a strategic Bitcoin reserve within five years if the necessary political conditions were met.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That's Ko's assessment — &lt;strong&gt;not an official government forecast or commitment.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The political part is especially important.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A reserve policy involving a volatile digital asset would likely require support from several parts of government, including policymakers responsible for monetary stability, fiscal policy and financial regulation.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A lawmaker can push the idea.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The institutions responsible for managing Taiwan's finances would ultimately have to decide whether the risks make sense.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;This Is Not a Done Deal&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It's easy to see headlines about a "Taiwan Bitcoin reserve" and assume the country has already made the decision.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It hasn't.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The more accurate description is that &lt;strong&gt;Taiwan is debating and studying the possibility&lt;/strong&gt;, while Ko Ju-chun is advocating for a strategic reserve framework.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That difference matters.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A proposal isn't a purchase.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A policy report isn't an allocation.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;And Bitcoin held through law-enforcement seizures isn't the same thing as a deliberately constructed sovereign reserve.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For now, the discussion is moving forward, but there is no confirmed national Bitcoin reserve policy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What a Taiwan Bitcoin Reserve Could Mean for Asia&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If Taiwan eventually established a formal Bitcoin reserve, the impact would probably extend well beyond Taiwan.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Governments across Asia are watching how &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bill-gates-warns-ai-is-advancing-faster.html"&gt;digital assets&lt;/a&gt; fit into national financial systems, and Taiwan would provide another real-world case study if it decided to hold Bitcoin strategically.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The reaction from other governments could be especially interesting.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Some policymakers might see a Taiwanese reserve as evidence that Bitcoin can function alongside traditional assets at the sovereign level.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Others could focus on the risks — particularly volatility, custody, regulation and the possibility of political pressure during major market downturns.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A Taiwanese decision could therefore become less about the amount of Bitcoin purchased and more about the precedent it creates.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If the policy worked, other governments could study Taiwan's custody and risk-management model.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If it failed, those same governments would have a very clear example of what to avoid.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Either way, a formal reserve would give Asian policymakers another data point in the growing debate over whether Bitcoin belongs in national financial strategies.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Question Is Strategic, Not Speculative&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The most interesting part of Taiwan's Bitcoin discussion may not be the potential size of the reserve.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It's the reason for holding it.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If the argument were simply that Bitcoin might rise in price, a government reserve would look more like an investment portfolio.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Ko's argument is broader.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;He has framed Bitcoin as a potential diversification and financial-resilience tool, particularly in light of Taiwan's exposure to global economic and geopolitical risks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That changes the conversation.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A strategic reserve doesn't necessarily have to outperform every other asset.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Its purpose can be to provide another option when traditional &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/justin-sun-says-tron-targets-quantum.html"&gt;financial systems&lt;/a&gt; face stress.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Whether Bitcoin can actually perform that role at the sovereign level remains an open question.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For Taiwan, the next stage is likely to be less about headlines and more about implementation details.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Policymakers would need to determine whether a reserve is legally possible, how it would be funded, who would control custody and what risk controls would be required.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The central bank's position would also matter enormously.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Central banks tend to be cautious with assets capable of extreme price movements, particularly when those assets could become part of national reserves.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That means Ko's political push is only one part of the process.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The harder part would be convincing the institutions responsible for financial stability that the potential benefits justify the risks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Taiwan isn't officially launching a national Bitcoin reserve simply because Ko Ju-chun says the idea should become a near-term plan.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But his comments show how far the discussion has moved.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A Taiwanese legislator has already brought a Bitcoin-reserve proposal into discussions with senior economic policymakers, while the government also has experience holding Bitcoin obtained through seizures.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The next step would be much more difficult: turning a political proposal into an actual framework covering funding, custody, regulation and risk management.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For now, the reserve remains a proposal rather than government policy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But Bitcoin's role in sovereign finance is becoming harder for &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/kalshi-sells-112b-of-equity-to-71.html"&gt;policymakers&lt;/a&gt; to ignore — &lt;strong&gt;even if they aren't ready to buy just yet.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;This article distinguishes between Ko Ju-chun's proposal and official Taiwanese government policy. Taiwan has not been described here as having already established a national Bitcoin reserve. This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>The Truth About AI Agents: Why They're Still Not Ready for Prime Time</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiux6sMD93nX8y7WmY90glQ3fpJa_bpu_cI2CRucjddqigjVZ5Zod_bSxBkAPVV93CGXauhCDldyjaGwa9KymmVBVWl01FvNAgPFs2tN_gdk9T9FQ-KKh2KVGKWN9kcCPuR25MPtso1ivPc4aJGaiH-AjheB6M3rOoPV7H1duxI98_Sj-VnKwO1JQm4sZWC/s1672/ai-agents-production-challenges-crypto-blockchain.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="AI agents navigating web data, cybersecurity barriers, APIs and blockchain infrastructure" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiux6sMD93nX8y7WmY90glQ3fpJa_bpu_cI2CRucjddqigjVZ5Zod_bSxBkAPVV93CGXauhCDldyjaGwa9KymmVBVWl01FvNAgPFs2tN_gdk9T9FQ-KKh2KVGKWN9kcCPuR25MPtso1ivPc4aJGaiH-AjheB6M3rOoPV7H1duxI98_Sj-VnKwO1JQm4sZWC/w400-h225/ai-agents-production-challenges-crypto-blockchain.jpg.png" title="The Truth About AI Agents and Their Production Challenges" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If you've been following the AI agent narrative, you've
probably heard the promises: autonomous systems that can handle your trading,
book your flights, monitor competitors, and manage entire workflows without you
lifting a finger.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;And yet.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A Gartner projection from June 2025 suggests that&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;over
40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled before the end of 2027&lt;/b&gt;, citing
escalating costs, unclear business value, and inadequate risk controls.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Because the infrastructure hasn't caught up. The web was
built for humans, not for bots. And the gap between what agents can do in a
demo and what they can do in production is still enormous.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Four Failures of AI Answers&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Yaniv Tal, founder of Geo and co-founder of The Graph, has
spent a lot of time thinking about this problem. His diagnosis? The
unreliability of AI responses isn't just a model problem—it's a data problem.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;He points to four core weaknesses in how information
circulates online:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;1. Lost provenance.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Content gets scraped,
republished, and re-scraped until the original source disappears. Models learn
a claim but have no clear path back to who first made it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;2. Flattened authority.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Research papers, press
releases, and anonymous forum posts all end up in the same training pipeline,
treated as equivalent evidence.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;3. Hidden disagreement.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Language models compress
competing views into a single confident-sounding answer, erasing real disputes
among experts.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;4. Repeated model-generated errors.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;When AI
outputs become training data for later models, mistakes get amplified across
generations.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"AI doesn't have a truth problem, the internet
does," Tal said.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A 2024&amp;nbsp;&lt;i&gt;Nature&lt;/i&gt;&amp;nbsp;study documented this exact
dynamic in action. Successive model generations trained on prior model output
progressively lose fidelity to the original human-produced data distribution—a
phenomenon researchers call "model collapse."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why the Web Hates Bots&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Even if the underlying models were flawless, the web itself
creates enormous friction for autonomous agents.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Consider what a capable agent actually needs: consistent
access, real-time responsiveness, and structured data it can parse without
human intervention. The web, as currently built, systematically discourages
automated access.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Oxylabs' upcoming Web Openness Index illustrates the gap:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The
     global average score for&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;practical reachability&lt;/b&gt;—how well a
     site responds to standard automated HTTP requests—stands at&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;83.4
     out of 100&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The
     score for&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;anti-automation friction&lt;/b&gt;—CAPTCHAs, rate limiting,
     fingerprinting, bot detection—is only&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;62.8&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Structured
     data interoperability&lt;/b&gt;—whether sites return data in formats machines
     can actually work with—drops to&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;60.3&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Those 20-plus-point differences reflect a structural gap.
Sites generally respond to requests for automated access, but restrictions
abound, and data is often returned in machine-unfriendly ways. Agents that
depend on reliable, timely, structured information will consistently fall into
that gap.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Inside organizations, agents face a related problem: data
that hasn't been cleaned, tagged, or structured in a way that AI can
understand. The relevant information exists—it's just not accessible.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Data Access Crisis&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Research from Cloudera and Google/MIT points to the same
bottleneck:&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;AI agents can't reliably act on data they can't access,
understand, or retrieve in real time.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Cloudera's survey of 1,500 enterprise architects and cloud
&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/you-can-now-trade-spacex-and-gold.html"&gt;infrastructure&lt;/a&gt; leads found that&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;95% had delayed or canceled AI projects&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in
the past year due to issues with data governance, compliance, or regulatory
problems. A wide majority said their current data architecture requires a
"significant overhaul" to meet AI goals.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"Even if enterprises are ready to use AI, many are
coming to the realization that the foundational infrastructure it relies on is
not," the report noted.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Similarly, more than half of 300 IT execs responding to the
Google/MIT survey said they have paused or delayed AI agent deployments to
address &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/trust-wallet-ceo-eowyn-chen-speed-isnt.html"&gt;foundational&lt;/a&gt; data issues—entrenched silos, inaccessible data,
insufficient real-time access, and lack of context.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;These are not minor complaints. They're the difference
between "we can try this" and "we can scale this."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Security Problem&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Maybe the biggest bottleneck is security. A Docker survey of
800+ developers and decision-makers found that&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;40% of respondents cite
security as their top blocker&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;when building agents.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The problem isn't confined to a single layer of the stack:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Infrastructure:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;As
     organizations scale agent deployments, teams emphasize the need for secure
     sandboxing and runtime isolation—even for internal agents.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Operations:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;More
     tools, more integrations, and more orchestration logic create blind spots.
     Over a third of respondents report challenges coordinating multiple tools,
     and a comparable share say integrations introduce security or compliance
     risk.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Governance:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;45%
     of organizations say the biggest challenge is ensuring tools are secure,
     trusted, and enterprise-ready.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is widely adopted—85% of
teams further along in their agent journey are familiar with it, and two-thirds
actively use it across projects. But most teams are operating in what could be
described as "leap-of-faith mode," adopting the protocol without the
security guarantees they would demand from mature enterprise infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For teams earlier in their agentic journey,&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;46%
identify security and compliance as the top challenge with MCP&lt;/b&gt;.
Organizations are increasingly watching for threats like prompt injection, tool
poisoning, and the more foundational issues of access control and
authentication.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"AI agent security is what sets the speed limit for
agentic AI in the enterprise," the Docker report concluded.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Execution Gap&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In crypto, the bottleneck is even more visible. An agent can
analyze market trends and generate strategies, but if it can't place orders,
manage positions, or interact on-chain, its analysis remains theoretical.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://gate.io/" target="_blank"&gt;Gate.io&lt;/a&gt;'s&amp;nbsp;analysis
identifies three major execution obstacles for AI agents in the crypto
ecosystem:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol start="1" style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="1"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Interface
     fragmentation.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The crypto ecosystem spans centralized exchanges,
     DEXs, wallets, and on-chain data, each with its own API standards and
     authentication methods. Integrating and maintaining each connection is
     time-consuming and expensive.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Permission
     and security risks.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Autonomy requires access to trading systems
     and assets. But prompt injection attacks, malicious plugins, API key
     abuse, or automated errors can turn a system failure into real financial
     losses. Industry reports reveal that&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;72% of enterprises are
     operating AI agents without adequate risk controls&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Lack
     of standardized protocols.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Most agents rely on different agent
     frameworks and orchestration systems, but communication between modules
     isn't standardized. Each integration requires custom
     adaptation—fundamentally limiting scalability.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is where crypto and AI intersect most directly: the
execution layer is the missing piece. Without it, agents remain analysis tools
rather than active entities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Needs to Change&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Tal's proposed solution—through his startup Geo—is to
rebuild how information is structured at the source. His system separates
claims, authors, and evidence, preserving relationships between them.
Communities called "Spaces" would curate knowledge, ranking arguments
by assessed strength while keeping competing perspectives visible beneath the
top results.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"Pluralism doesn't have to mean noise," Tal said.
"We think several well-structured competing perspectives is often the more
honest answer."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The approach doesn't eliminate the hard questions—how
communities select editors, how they resolve manipulation, or whether expertise
in one subject should carry weight in another—but it offers a direction.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;On the infrastructure side, the answer is less sexy but more
urgent: data needs to be accessible, structured, and secure. The web needs to
work for machines as well as humans.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

    <title>39 U.S. Banking Groups Form BankChain Alliance for 2027 Blockchain Network</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiTF4t5PmWqNN7tB8kAQJB0a_eSVg5aOD4npptYHbD8uUA14Jmn9F1Fk3HK1Yi-F5xXuUF1uX2u23QLF8-yamj-C-LnBT54lGct8d4nlHHvGhVlQSX2phN7FBBPzV-8KMWXSmg5e_LL7J3fLfptLQjmAkMy01vnAjSuqK13nFmSx-HHgPkynMiiMIKaBdl5/s1672/bankchain-alliance-us-banks-blockchain-network-2027.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="BankChain Alliance blockchain network for U.S. banks and tokenized deposits" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiTF4t5PmWqNN7tB8kAQJB0a_eSVg5aOD4npptYHbD8uUA14Jmn9F1Fk3HK1Yi-F5xXuUF1uX2u23QLF8-yamj-C-LnBT54lGct8d4nlHHvGhVlQSX2phN7FBBPzV-8KMWXSmg5e_LL7J3fLfptLQjmAkMy01vnAjSuqK13nFmSx-HHgPkynMiiMIKaBdl5/w400-h225/bankchain-alliance-us-banks-blockchain-network-2027.jpg.png" title="BankChain Alliance Plans U.S. Banking Blockchain Network" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&amp;nbsp;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Thirty-nine U.S. state banking associations are joining forces to build something the banking industry has spent years debating: a blockchain network designed and controlled by banks themselves.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new initiative, called &lt;strong&gt;BankChain Alliance&lt;/strong&gt;, is targeting a &lt;strong&gt;2027 launch&lt;/strong&gt; and plans to support tokenized deposits, stablecoins, smart payments and automated settlement. The project was announced on August 25, but there is still plenty of work to do before the network can go live. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the alliance is still looking for a technology partner. That means the 2027 date should be viewed as a target rather than a guaranteed launch schedule.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is BankChain Alliance?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BankChain Alliance is being built around a simple idea: banks should have their own shared blockchain infrastructure rather than relying entirely on networks developed by crypto companies or outside technology providers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The initiative brings together banking associations from 39 U.S. states. The groups represent thousands of financial institutions, including community and regional banks that may not have the resources to build their own blockchain infrastructure from scratch. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proposed network is expected to be &lt;strong&gt;industry-owned, industry-designed and industry-governed&lt;/strong&gt;. The alliance also wants the system to work with other blockchain networks instead of operating as an isolated platform.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That interoperability could become particularly important if tokenized deposits and stablecoins end up being used across multiple banking and payment networks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Banks Want to Put on the Network&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BankChain is not being positioned simply as another blockchain for moving cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The banking groups are looking at blockchain as infrastructure for services that already exist inside traditional finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); margin: 20px 0px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Planned Use&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Potential Role&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Tokenized Deposits&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Represent bank deposits on blockchain &lt;br /&gt;infrastructure while retaining the underlying&lt;br /&gt;&amp;nbsp;banking relationship.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Stablecoins&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Support blockchain-based digital money for&lt;br /&gt;&amp;nbsp;payments and other financial applications.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Smart Payments&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Allow payment instructions and financial &lt;br /&gt;processes to be automated through &lt;br /&gt;programmable infrastructure.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Automated Settlement&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Potentially make financial transactions settle&lt;br /&gt;&amp;nbsp;faster with fewer manual steps.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These are proposed use cases rather than services that are already live on BankChain. The underlying technology and implementation details have not yet been finalized. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Banks Are Building Their Own Blockchain&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The timing is significant.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Stablecoins have moved from being a niche crypto product to a serious part of the digital payments conversation. That has forced traditional banks to think about what happens if customers increasingly use blockchain-based dollars outside the banking system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BankChain gives the banking industry another option: build blockchain infrastructure itself and use it to offer digital financial products within the regulated banking framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For banks, that could mean keeping more of the customer relationship inside the existing financial system while still adopting the technology behind &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bernstein-predicts-300000-bitcoin-by.html"&gt;digital assets&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It also gives smaller institutions a potential way to participate without each bank having to develop an independent blockchain network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Tokenized Deposits Are a Big Part of the Plan&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the most important concepts behind BankChain is the &lt;strong&gt;tokenized deposit&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A tokenized deposit is different from a typical &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bill-gates-seeks-xi-jinping-meeting-to.html?m=1"&gt;crypto stablecoin&lt;/a&gt;. In simple terms, it represents a claim on a bank that is represented using blockchain technology.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters because banks already operate within a heavily regulated deposit system. Moving the representation of that deposit onto blockchain infrastructure could potentially add programmability and faster settlement without turning the underlying relationship into a traditional cryptocurrency holding.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BankChain is therefore looking at blockchain less as a replacement for banking and more as a new layer through which banking services could operate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Stablecoins Are Part of the Equation Too&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The alliance is also planning to support stablecoins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is notable because banks and stablecoin issuers have increasingly found themselves competing for the same digital payments market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Stablecoins can move value across blockchain networks at any time and are increasingly being explored for cross-border payments and corporate transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BankChain could give participating banks infrastructure to develop their own blockchain-based financial services while remaining connected to the traditional banking system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Exactly how bank-issued stablecoins would work on the network, however, has not yet been fully disclosed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Kathy Kraninger Is Serving as Interim Chair&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The alliance is being led on an interim basis by &lt;strong&gt;Kathy Kraninger&lt;/strong&gt;, president and CEO of the Florida Bankers Association and a former director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Her involvement gives the project an unusual connection between the traditional banking industry and U.S. financial regulation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Texas Bankers Association is also among the founding participants, while banking associations from dozens of other states have joined the initiative. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Biggest Missing Piece: Technology&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Despite the attention around BankChain, the project is still at an early stage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The alliance has &lt;strong&gt;not yet selected its technology partner&lt;/strong&gt;, according to reports. The underlying blockchain architecture and several technical details also remain undisclosed. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes the 2027 target important, but not definitive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The choice of technology partner could determine everything from transaction capacity and security to interoperability and how participating banks share control of the network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Until those decisions are made, it is difficult to know exactly what BankChain will look like once it moves from concept to production.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Interoperability Could Matter&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BankChain does not appear to be planning to operate completely on its own.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The alliance has said it wants the network to be interoperable with other blockchain networks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could become critical as financial institutions develop multiple tokenized-money systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If every bank or banking consortium creates a completely separate network, the industry could end up with the same fragmentation problem that exists across many blockchain ecosystems today.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Interoperability could allow assets and payment instructions to move between different systems without requiring banks to abandon their own infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is likely to be one of the more important technical challenges for BankChain as development progresses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;BankChain Is Not Live Yet&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is worth separating what has actually happened from what is being planned.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); margin: 20px 0px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Participating state banking associations&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction is important for anyone following the story. BankChain is currently an industry initiative with a stated development goal, not an operational nationwide blockchain network. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Could Change If It Works?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If BankChain eventually reaches production, the impact could extend well beyond cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Businesses could potentially use tokenized bank money for payments, banks could automate parts of settlement, and financial institutions could create programmable products that operate around the clock.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cross-border transactions are another potential area.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional international payments can involve several intermediaries and multiple settlement systems. Blockchain-based infrastructure could potentially reduce some of those steps, although regulatory requirements and interoperability would still remain major challenges.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important point is that BankChain is trying to bring those blockchain capabilities into the banking system rather than asking customers to leave traditional finance behind.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Picture for U.S. Banking&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BankChain arrives at a moment when the line between traditional banking and blockchain finance is becoming harder to define.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Banks are experimenting with tokenized deposits, stablecoins and blockchain-based settlement, while crypto companies are increasingly building payment and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/posco-international-expands-blockchain.html"&gt;financial infrastructure&lt;/a&gt; that competes directly with traditional institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BankChain Alliance suggests that at least part of the banking industry now wants to build its own infrastructure instead of simply adapting to networks created elsewhere.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could make 2027 an important year for the U.S. digital finance market if the alliance can turn its current plan into a working network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next major milestone is likely to be the selection of a technology partner.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;After that, the alliance will need to determine the network's architecture, governance structure, security model and interoperability standards before banks can begin using it at scale.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those decisions will tell the market much more about whether BankChain can become a meaningful piece of U.S. financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the banking industry has made its intention clear. It wants a greater say in how blockchain technology is used for money and payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The formation of BankChain Alliance is one of the clearest signs yet that U.S. banks are moving from simply watching blockchain development to building infrastructure of their own.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Thirty-nine state banking associations are behind the initiative, with plans for tokenized deposits, stablecoins, smart payments and automated settlement on an industry-owned network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the project is still in its early stages. The technology partner has not been selected, the network is not live, and &lt;strong&gt;2027 remains a target rather than a guaranteed launch date&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the alliance can solve those technical and regulatory challenges, BankChain could give U.S. banks a shared route into on-chain finance without handing the entire market to crypto-native companies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The interesting part of this story is no longer whether banks are interested in blockchain. That question appears to be largely settled. The bigger question is whether they can build an infrastructure that is fast, interoperable and useful enough for the banking system to actually adopt it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment, financial or legal advice.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Sources:&lt;/strong&gt; CoinDesk, Crypto.news and American Banker reporting on the BankChain Alliance and its announced plans. &lt;/p&gt;
