    <title>CLARITY Act Stalls in Senate as Blackburn Blames Democrats and Bitwise CIO Calls It a "Speed Bump"</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjAsm3zhqOVEPmU-EqkmRRBnt7f-33YOyFfg5HhyphenhyphenBGQXTdRupnX9gYZM4v4Q1Rz2IlR_8N5NYwn0k8lq-NBYcVSkxvnGTnP0i1W2vlOduzoqBl0nf6lxD2Zg_Lw6qymdWbT-Wy5-EcwuH0CWsMl6N3hBkqhZSlS7a2QCRSN9OMiY_a0JIU2Ab_ivkw-cnX4/s1733/clarity-act-senate-crypto-regulation-matt-hougan.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="U.S. Senate CLARITY Act vote and cryptocurrency regulation debate" border="0" data-original-height="908" data-original-width="1733" height="336" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjAsm3zhqOVEPmU-EqkmRRBnt7f-33YOyFfg5HhyphenhyphenBGQXTdRupnX9gYZM4v4Q1Rz2IlR_8N5NYwn0k8lq-NBYcVSkxvnGTnP0i1W2vlOduzoqBl0nf6lxD2Zg_Lw6qymdWbT-Wy5-EcwuH0CWsMl6N3hBkqhZSlS7a2QCRSN9OMiY_a0JIU2Ab_ivkw-cnX4/w640-h336/clarity-act-senate-crypto-regulation-matt-hougan.webp.png" title="CLARITY Act Senate Vote and U.S. Crypto Regulation" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Senate has stalled the CLARITY Act after a procedural vote failed to reach the three-fifths threshold needed to advance the cryptocurrency market-structure bill. Senator Marsha Blackburn said she believes Democrats opposed the legislation because they did not want to give Republicans and President Donald Trump a political win, while Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan described the setback as a "speed bump, not a roadblock" for the crypto industry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The September 15 vote was &lt;strong&gt;49-50&lt;/strong&gt;, with one senator not voting. The Senate record identifies the vote as cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 3633, the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act. The motion was rejected, so the bill did not advance at that stage. It was not a final Senate vote on passage or final rejection of the complete legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The outcome has nevertheless become an important moment in the debate over U.S. crypto regulation. Supporters have spent more than a year negotiating the legislation, while Democrats have sought changes involving ethics and other provisions. At the same time, several Republicans also voted against the procedural motion, making the result more complicated than a simple party-line dispute.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happened to the CLARITY Act?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On &lt;strong&gt;September 15, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, the Senate held a cloture vote on the motion to proceed to the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act, H.R. 3633.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The motion received &lt;strong&gt;49 votes in favor and 50 against&lt;/strong&gt;, with one senator not voting. Because cloture required three-fifths of the Senate, the motion was rejected.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Four Republican senators—&lt;strong&gt;Jerry Moran, Susan Collins, Josh Hawley and Thom Tillis&lt;/strong&gt;—voted against the motion. The Senate Daily Press reported that Tillis voted no in order to make a motion to reconsider the vote. The Senate floor record subsequently recorded Tillis's motion to reconsider.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important: the September 15 result stalled the bill's advancement, but it did not represent a final Senate vote on the complete legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Senator Marsha Blackburn Said&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Senator &lt;strong&gt;Marsha Blackburn&lt;/strong&gt;, Republican of Tennessee, offered a political explanation for the Democratic opposition.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Speaking to Fox Business, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/openai-makes-progress-on-another.html"&gt;Blackburn &lt;/a&gt;said she believed Democrats voted against the CLARITY Act because they did not want to give Republicans and the president a political win.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is &lt;strong&gt;Blackburn's characterization&lt;/strong&gt; of the vote, not an established explanation for the motives of every Democratic senator.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Democratic lawmakers had also raised substantive objections, particularly around ethics provisions and rules concerning digital-asset activities involving federal officials. Those concerns remained part of the negotiations surrounding the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The final procedural result also included Republican opposition, meaning the vote cannot accurately be described as Democrats alone preventing the legislation from advancing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Republicans Made Major Changes Before the Vote&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Senators &lt;strong&gt;Cynthia Lummis, John Boozman and Tim Scott&lt;/strong&gt; released a revised CLARITY Act text on September 14, one day before the Senate vote.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The senators said the new draft incorporated &lt;strong&gt;126 substantive changes&lt;/strong&gt; requested by Democrats after more than a year of bipartisan negotiations. The revised text addressed areas including ethics provisions, state attorneys general, stablecoins, developers, consumer protections and CFTC jurisdiction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The ethics provisions were particularly significant because lawmakers had been negotiating restrictions involving federal officials and digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The legislative debate included proposals concerning restrictions on certain digital-asset activities by federal officials and enforcement mechanisms involving state attorneys general.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These provisions should be understood as part of the legislative debate over potential conflicts of interest. They do not, by themselves, establish wrongdoing by any individual.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Was the CLARITY Act Designed to Do?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CLARITY Act was designed to create a federal regulatory framework for digital assets and clarify the respective roles of the &lt;strong&gt;Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)&lt;/strong&gt; and the &lt;strong&gt;Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the central issues in U.S. crypto regulation has been determining how different digital assets and activities should be classified and which federal agency should oversee them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A statutory market-structure framework could provide clearer definitions and regulatory boundaries for exchanges, token issuers, financial institutions and other companies operating in the digital-asset sector.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Supporters of the bill have argued that clearer rules could provide greater regulatory certainty and help the United States remain competitive in digital-asset markets. Critics and opponents have focused on provisions they believe require additional changes, including ethics safeguards and consumer protections.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Matt Hougan Calls the Setback a "Speed Bump"&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitwise Chief Investment Officer &lt;strong&gt;Matt Hougan&lt;/strong&gt; offered a substantially different interpretation of the Senate setback.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In a September 16 CIO memo, Hougan described the CLARITY Act's failure as a &lt;strong&gt;"speed bump, not a roadblock."&lt;/strong&gt; His argument is that &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/revolut-data-breach-hacker-launches.html"&gt;crypto-market development&lt;/a&gt; and institutional adoption can continue even if Congress does not immediately pass the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hougan's memo argues that the crypto market's development does not depend entirely on Washington's immediate approval of the bill.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;He pointed to Bitcoin's performance as one part of that argument. According to data cited in the Bitwise memo, Bitcoin reached a low of approximately &lt;strong&gt;$57,950 on July 1&lt;/strong&gt; before climbing above &lt;strong&gt;$80,000 on September 4&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hougan also cited prediction-market odds for the CLARITY Act becoming law in 2026, which he said had declined from 39% to 18% during the period discussed in his memo.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hougan argues that the divergence suggests crypto-market activity does not depend entirely on passage of the CLARITY Act.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That comparison, however, does not prove that legislation has no effect on cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin prices are influenced by multiple factors, including monetary policy, liquidity, institutional demand, leverage and broader risk sentiment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Hougan Thinks Crypto Can Keep Developing&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hougan also pointed to continued activity from major financial institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;His memo highlighted developments involving Robinhood, Morgan Stanley and DTCC as examples of continued institutional work around &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ripple-adds-xrp-and-rlusd-support-to.html"&gt;blockchain &lt;/a&gt;and digital assets. Hougan used those developments to argue that financial institutions have continued building crypto-related infrastructure despite uncertainty surrounding the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;His broader argument is that the crypto market has already developed beyond the point where one congressional vote determines whether the industry continues building and adopting blockchain-based infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, Hougan acknowledged that congressional action remains important because a durable statutory framework can provide authorities and protections that agencies cannot necessarily create on their own.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;SEC and CFTC Rulemaking Becomes More Important&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With the CLARITY Act stalled, attention is likely to remain focused on the SEC and CFTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Both agencies can continue using their existing authority to establish rules and provide regulatory guidance for parts of the digital-asset market. Industry executives have also argued that the agencies have tools available under existing law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But agency action is not identical to congressional legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A law passed by Congress can establish statutory authority and regulatory boundaries that remain in place beyond an individual administration. Agency rules can be changed by future regulators and can also face legal challenges.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why the failure to advance the CLARITY Act does not mean U.S. crypto regulation has stopped. Instead, it leaves part of the market-structure debate unresolved while agencies continue operating under existing law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bill Is Stalled, but Negotiations May Continue&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The September 15 vote did not necessarily end discussions around the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Lawmakers can continue negotiating, revise legislative language or attempt to bring a measure back under Senate procedures. The Senate's record shows that the September 15 vote concerned whether cloture could be invoked on the motion to proceed, rather than a final vote on the bill's complete text.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters because a procedural setback and permanent abandonment of a bill are not necessarily the same thing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The remaining legislative calendar, however, could limit the time available for lawmakers to reach another agreement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Ethics Became a Major Issue&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ethics provisions became one of the most closely watched parts of the negotiations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The revised bill included restrictions designed to address potential conflicts involving federal officials and digital assets. Republicans said the new language represented significant concessions to Democratic demands, while Democratic lawmakers continued to seek additional safeguards.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The issue became particularly sensitive because lawmakers were debating ethics rules concerning federal officials' digital-asset interests, including concerns raised in connection with President Trump's crypto-related activities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For accuracy, those concerns should not be confused with an allegation that any particular official violated an ethics or financial law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the Senate Vote Means for Crypto Companies&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For crypto exchanges, custodians, token issuers, financial institutions and blockchain companies, the biggest issue is &lt;strong&gt;regulatory certainty&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A federal market-structure law could establish clearer rules around the classification and oversight of digital assets. Without such legislation, companies may continue operating under a combination of agency rules, enforcement decisions, court rulings and state-level requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That can make long-term planning more complicated, particularly for businesses whose products involve several areas of digital finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the continued development of crypto products and blockchain infrastructure by major financial institutions also shows that companies are not necessarily waiting for Congress to resolve every regulatory question before building in the sector.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin's Reaction to the Senate Vote&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CLARITY Act vote also coincided with a sharp move in cryptocurrency markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Market reactions around the vote reflected both the legislative development and broader financial conditions. Bitcoin prices can move for multiple reasons, including macroeconomic data, interest-rate expectations, liquidity, institutional flows and overall risk sentiment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hougan's longer-term comparison tells a different story. His Bitwise data showed Bitcoin rising substantially from its July 1 low even as expectations for CLARITY Act passage declined.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Together, these observations illustrate why regulatory developments and cryptocurrency prices should not be treated as having a simple one-to-one relationship.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Speed Bump or Regulatory Gap?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hougan's "speed bump" description captures one side of the debate: crypto businesses and financial institutions can continue developing products even without a comprehensive congressional market-structure law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The opposing concern is that continued agency rulemaking cannot fully replace legislation that establishes permanent statutory authority.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Both points can coexist. &lt;strong&gt;Crypto development can continue while regulatory uncertainty remains unresolved.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The September vote therefore creates two parallel stories: the immediate legislative setback and the continued development of crypto infrastructure outside the legislative process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next stage could involve a combination of congressional negotiations, agency rulemaking and continued development by crypto companies and financial institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Lawmakers could revisit provisions involving market structure, ethics, consumer protections and regulatory jurisdiction. Meanwhile, the SEC and CFTC can continue working within their existing authorities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the crypto industry, the key question is not simply whether the CLARITY Act returns for another vote. It is whether lawmakers can resolve the disagreements that prevented the bill from reaching the threshold required to advance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CLARITY Act is currently &lt;strong&gt;stalled in the Senate after a 49-50 procedural vote&lt;/strong&gt; failed to reach the required threshold to advance the legislation. The vote was not final passage or final rejection of the bill, leaving open the possibility of further legislative discussions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Senator Marsha Blackburn has attributed Democratic opposition to political considerations, saying Democrats did not want to give Republicans and President Trump a win. Democrats, however, had raised substantive concerns about ethics provisions and other parts of the legislation, while four Republicans also voted against the procedural motion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan sees the setback differently, calling it a &lt;strong&gt;"speed bump, not a roadblock."&lt;/strong&gt; He argues that crypto adoption and financial-sector development can continue even without immediate congressional action, although he also recognizes that legislation would provide a more durable regulatory foundation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader U.S. crypto-regulation debate therefore continues on several fronts: &lt;strong&gt;Congressional negotiations, SEC and CFTC rulemaking, institutional adoption and the industry's push for clearer market rules.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the CLARITY Act has not advanced, but the regulatory debate surrounding digital assets in the United States is far from over.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;CoinAINews will update this report as lawmakers resume negotiations or new developments emerge around the CLARITY Act and U.S. crypto regulation.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Eric Balchunas Says Rising US Interest Costs Could Prove the Fed Rate-Hike Camp Wrong</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgPlIIIqARysSmQfUMQRlHlV7ITk10oDKhUeSy9FZI8uxmD6w3tlV858bXsm337iAYUsnMIH0bWzaLLtU09o2hHNkYXLf7jh2h83UUwPiTu3tWAptvfd3wIzbokrV58TRA4CYh_SEHz8F7_5xcJBb1cIJxis-1E1WRmUWVSdVfZktoAocZsmZZSecLZEkS0/s1672/eric-balchunas-us-interest-costs-fed-rate-hike-bitcoin.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Eric Balchunas warns rising US interest costs could challenge the Fed rate-hike outlook" border="0" data-original-height="940" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgPlIIIqARysSmQfUMQRlHlV7ITk10oDKhUeSy9FZI8uxmD6w3tlV858bXsm337iAYUsnMIH0bWzaLLtU09o2hHNkYXLf7jh2h83UUwPiTu3tWAptvfd3wIzbokrV58TRA4CYh_SEHz8F7_5xcJBb1cIJxis-1E1WRmUWVSdVfZktoAocZsmZZSecLZEkS0/w640-h360/eric-balchunas-us-interest-costs-fed-rate-hike-bitcoin.webp.png" title="Eric Balchunas Warns Rising US Interest Costs Could Challenge Fed Rate Hikes" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas&lt;/strong&gt; has pointed to a growing problem for investors betting on higher U.S. interest rates: the rising cost of servicing the government's massive debt.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In a recent post on X, Balchunas argued that &lt;strong&gt;increased U.S. government interest payments are another reason the Federal Reserve's rate-hike camp could be wrong&lt;/strong&gt;. His argument adds an important fiscal dimension to the current debate over whether the Fed needs to keep monetary policy tighter for longer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The comment comes at a particularly important moment for markets. Investors are reassessing the Federal Reserve's next move after U.S. inflation data came in stronger than many expected, while Treasury yields have also moved higher.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a difficult policy environment: inflation is still above the Fed's target, but higher interest rates also make the government's debt-servicing burden more expensive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Eric Balchunas Is Actually Arguing&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Balchunas is not saying that the Federal Reserve is legally or mechanically unable to raise interest rates.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;His point is more about the economic consequences of additional tightening.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When interest rates rise, newly issued government debt generally becomes more expensive to finance. Existing Treasury securities do not all reprice immediately, but as older debt matures and is refinanced, higher market yields can gradually feed into the government's interest bill.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With the United States carrying an enormous amount of federal debt, even relatively small changes in borrowing costs can become significant when applied across a large debt base.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why Balchunas believes rising interest &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/should-ai-learn-crypto-risk-nobodys.html"&gt;payments &lt;/a&gt;deserve to be considered when evaluating the case for another rate increase.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Fed Is Still Facing Pressure to Raise Rates&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is a strong counterargument to Balchunas' view.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Federal Reserve's primary monetary-policy considerations include inflation and employment. The central bank cannot simply ignore persistent inflation because higher interest rates make government borrowing more expensive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent economic data has actually strengthened the case for tighter policy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to Reuters, U.S. core consumer prices increased 0.3% in August, above the 0.2% economists had expected. Core CPI was up 2.4% from a year earlier, while headline inflation reached 3.4%. The data increased expectations for a possible rate hike at the Fed's upcoming meeting. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means the Fed is facing a genuine dilemma rather than a simple choice between hiking and cutting.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Fed's Inflation Problem vs. America's Interest Bill&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The central tension can be summarized in one question:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;How aggressively can the Federal Reserve fight inflation when higher rates are simultaneously increasing the cost of financing the federal government's debt?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The two issues are not directly controlled by the same institution. The Federal Reserve sets monetary policy, while the U.S. Treasury manages federal borrowing and debt issuance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But they interact through financial markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Higher Fed rates can push short-term borrowing costs higher and influence Treasury yields across the maturity curve. Higher Treasury yields can then affect &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/strategy-ceo-phong-le-says-ai-agents.html"&gt;financing conditions&lt;/a&gt; for governments, companies, households and investors.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why government interest expenses have become an increasingly important part of the broader macroeconomic discussion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Rising Interest Payments Matter for Markets&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For years, investors have focused heavily on the size of the U.S. budget deficit and the country's debt-to-GDP ratio.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The interest bill adds another layer to that problem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When the government spends more money servicing debt, those resources cannot simultaneously be used for other priorities without additional borrowing, spending reductions or changes in revenue.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The result can be greater sensitivity to interest rates.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If borrowing costs remain elevated for an extended period, investors may increasingly focus on whether the government's fiscal position can absorb those costs without putting additional pressure on Treasury markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Treasury Yields Are Becoming So Important&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The debate is not limited to the Fed funds rate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Longer-term Treasury yields matter just as much for financial markets because they influence the cost of capital throughout the economy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent market moves illustrate the problem. Treasury yields have risen as investors have reassessed inflation and the possibility of additional Fed tightening. Market reports have also highlighted the 10-year Treasury yield approaching the 5% area amid renewed inflation and oil-price concerns. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If yields remain elevated, companies may face higher financing costs, consumers may face more expensive credit and investors may demand greater returns for holding riskier assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That can create pressure across stocks, bonds and cryptocurrencies simultaneously.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What This Could Mean for Bitcoin&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where Balchunas' comment becomes particularly interesting for the crypto market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin is increasingly traded as part of the broader global macro environment. Federal Reserve policy can influence liquidity, Treasury yields, the U.S. dollar and overall investor risk appetite.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A more hawkish Fed can therefore create headwinds for Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies by making relatively safe dollar-denominated assets more attractive and by tightening financial conditions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But if markets eventually conclude that the Fed cannot keep rates high for as long as previously expected because of broader economic or fiscal pressures, expectations could change.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; automatically mean Bitcoin will rise.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto prices are influenced by many other factors, including &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/hunter-biden-says-i-dont-want-anybody.html"&gt;ETF &lt;/a&gt;flows, institutional demand, regulation, liquidity, dollar strength and market positioning.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Still, a major change in expectations for the future path of U.S. interest rates could become an important catalyst for digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Balchunas' View Does Not Mean a Rate Hike Is Impossible&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction is important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Balchunas is offering a market view, not announcing a change in Federal Reserve policy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Fed could still raise rates if policymakers conclude that inflation is not moving toward the 2% target quickly enough.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent inflation data gives policymakers a reason to remain concerned. Reuters reported that the latest CPI figures, combined with higher energy prices and other inflation pressures, increased the probability assigned by markets to a near-term Fed hike. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So there are currently two competing forces.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bigger U.S. Debt Problem&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The underlying issue extends beyond one Fed meeting.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The United States has accumulated a very large federal debt burden, meaning interest rates now have a greater potential impact on government finances than they did when debt levels were substantially lower.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not mean a debt crisis is inevitable. The United States has deep capital markets, a large economy and the world's dominant reserve currency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But it does mean that investors have more reason to monitor the relationship between Treasury yields, federal borrowing and interest expenses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If borrowing costs stay elevated for years, interest payments can consume an increasingly significant share of federal resources.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could Fiscal Pressure Eventually Change the Fed Debate?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is the central question behind Balchunas' warning.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In theory, monetary policy can remain restrictive even when government interest expenses are rising. The Fed's inflation mandate does not disappear because Treasury borrowing becomes more expensive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But markets may eventually begin to price the economic consequences of sustained high rates more aggressively.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could affect Treasury demand, bond yields, equity valuations, credit markets and investor expectations about future monetary policy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In other words, fiscal pressure does not necessarily prevent rate hikes. It can, however, make the consequences of those hikes increasingly important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Investors Should Watch Next&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next major clues will come from inflation, employment, Treasury yields and Federal Reserve communication.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Investors should also watch whether market expectations for future Fed policy continue moving toward additional hikes or begin shifting back toward a pause.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For crypto investors, ETF flows and Bitcoin's response to changes in Treasury yields could provide another useful signal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If Bitcoin begins strengthening despite elevated Treasury yields and a hawkish Fed narrative, that could suggest that other forces—such as institutional demand or ETF flows—are becoming more influential.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Eric Balchunas' Comment Really Means&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most important part of Balchunas' argument is not that the Federal Reserve will definitely avoid another rate hike.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is that &lt;strong&gt;the cost of higher rates is no longer limited to slowing private-sector borrowing and spending.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With the U.S. government carrying a huge debt load, higher rates can also increase the cost of servicing federal debt as securities mature and are refinanced.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a complicated environment for policymakers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Fed may need higher rates to control inflation, while higher rates can simultaneously increase financial pressure elsewhere in the economy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Eric Balchunas' latest warning adds a new angle to the debate over whether the Federal Reserve will continue tightening monetary policy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Inflation remains a legitimate reason for the Fed to consider higher rates, and recent data has strengthened the case for caution on the inflation front. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, rising government interest payments mean that additional rate increases could have increasingly significant fiscal consequences.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not prove the rate-hike camp is wrong.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But it does explain why investors are paying closer attention to the interaction between &lt;strong&gt;Fed policy, Treasury yields, U.S. debt and government interest costs&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Bitcoin and the broader crypto market, the next major move may depend less on the headline rate decision itself and more on what that decision signals about the future path of U.S. liquidity and interest rates.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Who is Eric Balchunas?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Eric Balchunas is a Bloomberg senior ETF analyst who regularly comments on exchange-traded funds, markets and institutional investment trends.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why does the U.S. government's interest bill matter?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;As the federal government carries a large amount of debt, higher borrowing costs can increase the amount it spends servicing that debt as existing securities mature and are refinanced.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does rising interest expense mean the Fed cannot raise rates?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. The Federal Reserve can still raise rates if policymakers believe tighter monetary policy is necessary to control inflation. Rising government interest costs are a fiscal consideration, not a direct restriction on the Fed's legal authority.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why could this matter for Bitcoin?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Fed policy influences financial conditions, Treasury yields, liquidity and investor risk appetite. Changes in expectations for future rates can therefore affect Bitcoin and other risk assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Eric Balchunas predicting that the Fed will definitely stop hiking?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. His comment is an argument against the assumption that further rate hikes are necessarily the right path. The actual policy decision remains dependent on economic data and Federal Reserve officials' assessment.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Kalshi Sells $1.12B of Equity to 71 Investors in $1.5B Offering</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEioPS5riAqtr1b1IXyAIO0upnYT3hicejJRub_5mv4Ci5FA-nDIKMb3DQbfLnJIi2lyICmA2wWv57iy-aBR_d3dcTJtYhq7DMGLJPmEJql5oeoTIp_-GorMAaPb303egrx7-WhpdPJIvuZsgEydfihKvUXmIUfVx2vWvhfuYV7AelVysejeiHMiF95KMJ84/s1672/kalshi-1-12-billion-equity-offering-71-investors-2026.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Kalshi raises $1.12 billion in equity from 71 investors" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEioPS5riAqtr1b1IXyAIO0upnYT3hicejJRub_5mv4Ci5FA-nDIKMb3DQbfLnJIi2lyICmA2wWv57iy-aBR_d3dcTJtYhq7DMGLJPmEJql5oeoTIp_-GorMAaPb303egrx7-WhpdPJIvuZsgEydfihKvUXmIUfVx2vWvhfuYV7AelVysejeiHMiF95KMJ84/w320-h180/kalshi-1-12-billion-equity-offering-71-investors-2026.jpg.png" title="Kalshi $1.12 Billion Equity Offering 2026" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1 style="color: #111111; font-size: 42px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.25; margin: 0px 0px 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: 14px;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14px;"&gt; |&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px 30px; width: 100%;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #333333; font-size: 20px;"&gt;Kalshi has sold approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;strong style="color: #333333; font-size: 20px;"&gt;$1.12 billion in equity to 71 investors&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;span style="color: #333333; font-size: 20px;"&gt; under a larger $1.5 billion offering that began in April, according to a new filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The filing shows that approximately &lt;strong&gt;$380 million remains available&lt;/strong&gt; under the offering, meaning Kalshi has already sold a substantial majority of the securities covered by the fundraising.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The disclosure provides a fresh look at the amount of private capital flowing into Kalshi as prediction markets attract increasing attention from investors, financial institutions and regulators.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The latest filing is also important because it needs to be distinguished from Kalshi's previously announced funding rounds. The SEC document describes a $1.5 billion equity offering, while Kalshi separately announced a $1 billion Series F earlier in 2026.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
Kalshi's $1.5 Billion Equity Offering
&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
According to the SEC filing, Kalshi's offering began on &lt;strong&gt;April 3, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;. Since then, the company has sold approximately $1.12 billion in equity to 71 investors.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The offering has a stated size of $1.5 billion, leaving approximately $380 million still available.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The filing identifies the securities as equity and indicates that the offering is being conducted under &lt;strong&gt;Rule 506(b) of Regulation D&lt;/strong&gt;. Private offerings using this exemption can allow eligible companies to raise capital without conducting a public registered securities offering, subject to applicable securities laws and requirements.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
For Kalshi, the size of the transaction is notable because it shows that the prediction-market company has access to significant private capital while the sector continues to develop.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
Kalshi Fundraising at a Glance

&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
Why the $1.12 Billion Figure Matters
&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The amount disclosed in the filing is notable because it shows the scale of private investment flowing into Kalshi.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Prediction markets have moved into a much larger conversation around financial markets. Platforms such as Kalshi allow users to trade contracts tied to outcomes of real-world events, turning expectations about future events into market prices.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The business model has attracted interest because &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/japan-eyes-blockchain-for-real-time.html"&gt;market participants&lt;/a&gt; can use event contracts to express views on potential outcomes. Depending on the product and applicable rules, these markets can also generate information about how participants assess the probability of future events.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The latest fundraising does not by itself guarantee future growth for Kalshi. However, the size of the offering demonstrates that substantial private capital is available to support the company's expansion.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
This Offering Is Separate From the $1 Billion Series F
&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
One point deserves particular attention when comparing Kalshi's recent fundraising announcements.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The latest SEC filing describes a &lt;strong&gt;$1.5 billion equity offering&lt;/strong&gt;. &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/39-us-banking-groups-form-bankchain.html"&gt;Kalshi&lt;/a&gt; also announced a &lt;strong&gt;$1 billion Series F funding round in May 2026&lt;/strong&gt;.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Those transactions should not automatically be treated as one single fundraising round. The SEC filing itself identifies the $1.5 billion offering, while the Series F was separately announced by the company.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
That distinction is important for anyone attempting to calculate Kalshi's total capital raised or track changes in the company's valuation.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Unless additional company disclosures or filings establish a direct connection between the transactions, they are better treated as separate financing events.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
71 Investors Have Participated
&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The SEC filing reports that &lt;strong&gt;71 investors&lt;/strong&gt; have participated in the offering.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The figure indicates that the equity sale has attracted a relatively broad group of private investors rather than relying on a single disclosed source of capital.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
However, the filing does not necessarily provide readers with a complete picture of the investment size, strategic role or ownership position associated with every participant.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
For that reason, the most useful takeaway is the scale of the offering and the number of investors participating, rather than assuming that every investor has an identical stake.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
About $380 Million Is Still Available
&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Kalshi has not yet reached the full $1.5 billion offering amount.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
With approximately $1.12 billion already sold, roughly &lt;strong&gt;$380 million remains available&lt;/strong&gt; under the offering.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
That means the company has completed roughly three-quarters of the offering based on the disclosed figures.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The remaining amount leaves room for additional equity sales if Kalshi continues the offering under its existing terms.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Whether the company ultimately sells the entire remaining amount will be something investors can watch through future filings and company disclosures.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
Prediction Markets Are Attracting More Attention
&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Kalshi's fundraising comes as prediction markets receive increasing attention from the broader financial industry.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The basic concept is straightforward: users trade contracts connected to the outcome of a real-world event. The price of a contract can provide an indication of how the market values the probability of that outcome.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
These markets can cover a wide range of subjects, including economic data, political developments, sports and other measurable events.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Supporters argue that prediction markets can aggregate information from many participants and provide a market-based signal about future events.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Critics and regulators, meanwhile, have raised questions about the structure of certain event contracts and whether some products can resemble gambling.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
That regulatory discussion is likely to remain an important factor in the development of the prediction-market industry.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
Regulation Remains a Major Issue
&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Kalshi's business is closely connected to its regulatory position in the United States.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The company operates as a designated contract market under the oversight of the &lt;strong&gt;U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission&lt;/strong&gt;.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
That framework is an important part of Kalshi's position in the market because it distinguishes the company's regulated event-contract platform from many informal prediction or betting services.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
At the same time, Kalshi has faced regulatory and legal disputes involving some of its event contracts in the United States.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
As the company grows, the outcome of those regulatory questions could influence which markets it can offer, how products are structured and how prediction markets develop more broadly.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
What Could the New Capital Be Used For?
&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The SEC filing provides information about the equity offering but does not provide a detailed public breakdown of how every dollar raised will be spent.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Additional capital could give Kalshi more flexibility to invest in technology, product development, regulatory operations, market expansion and other corporate activities.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
For a financial platform operating in a rapidly developing market, technology infrastructure is particularly important. Handling increasing numbers of users and contracts requires systems capable of processing transactions reliably while meeting regulatory and security requirements.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Capital can also help a company operate through periods in which regulatory developments or market expansion require additional resources.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Still, investors should not assume that the entire $1.12 billion will be directed toward any single business activity unless Kalshi provides additional details.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
What Investors Should Watch Next
&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The most immediate number to watch is the approximately &lt;strong&gt;$380 million remaining&lt;/strong&gt; under the current offering.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
If Kalshi sells the remaining amount, the company would complete the $1.5 billion equity offering.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Investors and industry observers will also be watching the company's trading activity, revenue performance, future fundraising announcements and regulatory developments.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The company's ability to maintain growth while managing regulatory and operational challenges could ultimately matter more than the headline size of the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bernstein-predicts-300000-bitcoin-by.html"&gt;current capital&lt;/a&gt; raise.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
Why Kalshi's Fundraising Could Matter to the Industry
&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The size of Kalshi's latest equity offering highlights how prediction markets have evolved from a relatively specialized financial product into a sector attracting significant private investment.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
As more investors become interested in event-based financial contracts, competition between platforms could increase.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Greater competition could lead to new products, broader market coverage and improvements in trading infrastructure.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
However, industry growth will also depend heavily on regulation. Prediction markets operate in an area where financial-market rules, consumer protection and gambling laws can sometimes overlap.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
That makes regulatory clarity one of the most important factors for the industry's long-term development.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
Kalshi Offering: What the Numbers Show
&lt;/h2&gt;

Metric

&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
The Bigger Picture
&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Kalshi's latest filing arrives at a time when prediction markets are becoming a more visible part of the financial technology landscape.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The company's ability to raise more than $1 billion through the disclosed offering demonstrates that private investors see significant potential in the sector.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
But capital alone will not determine whether prediction markets become a permanent part of mainstream finance. The industry still needs to demonstrate sustainable demand, reliable technology, strong risk controls and a regulatory framework that can support long-term growth.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
For Kalshi, the current fundraising provides additional financial capacity at a critical point in that development.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
The Bottom Line
&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Kalshi has sold approximately &lt;strong&gt;$1.12 billion in equity to 71 investors&lt;/strong&gt; under a &lt;strong&gt;$1.5 billion offering&lt;/strong&gt;, according to an SEC filing.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
With roughly &lt;strong&gt;$380 million still available&lt;/strong&gt;, the company has already completed a substantial portion of the offering.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The disclosure provides another indication of the growing investor interest surrounding prediction markets, but the numbers should be interpreted carefully.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The new $1.5 billion offering should not automatically be combined with Kalshi's previously announced $1 billion Series F because the two financing events are separately identified.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The next developments worth watching include whether Kalshi completes the remaining portion of the offering, how its business performs and how regulators continue to approach prediction-market contracts in the United States.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
For the broader industry, the fundraising is another sign that prediction markets are attracting serious private capital and moving further into the financial-market conversation.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h2 style="border-bottom: 2px solid rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #111111; font-size: 30px; line-height: 1.4; margin: 42px 0px 18px; padding-bottom: 10px;"&gt;
Frequently Asked Questions
&lt;/h2&gt;


&lt;h3 style="color: #222222; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 28px 0px 10px;"&gt;
How much equity has Kalshi sold?
&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
According to the latest SEC filing, Kalshi has sold approximately &lt;strong&gt;$1.12 billion&lt;/strong&gt; in equity under the $1.5 billion offering.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h3 style="color: #222222; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 28px 0px 10px;"&gt;
How many investors participated in the Kalshi offering?
&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The filing reports that &lt;strong&gt;71 investors&lt;/strong&gt; have participated in the offering.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h3 style="color: #222222; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 28px 0px 10px;"&gt;
How much of Kalshi's $1.5 billion offering remains?
&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Approximately &lt;strong&gt;$380 million&lt;/strong&gt; remains available under the disclosed $1.5 billion offering.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h3 style="color: #222222; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 28px 0px 10px;"&gt;
When did Kalshi's latest equity offering begin?
&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The SEC filing indicates that the offering began on &lt;strong&gt;April 3, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h3 style="color: #222222; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 28px 0px 10px;"&gt;
Is the $1.5 billion offering the same as Kalshi's $1 billion Series F?
&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
They should not automatically be treated as the same transaction. The SEC filing describes a $1.5 billion equity offering, while Kalshi separately announced a $1 billion Series F.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h3 style="color: #222222; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 28px 0px 10px;"&gt;
What is Kalshi?
&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Kalshi is a regulated prediction-market platform where users can trade contracts tied to the outcomes of real-world events.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h3 style="color: #222222; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 28px 0px 10px;"&gt;
Why is Kalshi raising so much capital?
&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
The SEC filing does not provide a detailed breakdown of how all proceeds will be used. Additional capital could provide resources for technology, product development, regulatory operations, expansion and other corporate activities.
&lt;/p&gt;


&lt;h3 style="color: #222222; font-size: 21px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 28px 0px 10px;"&gt;
Why are prediction markets receiving more attention?
&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
Prediction markets have attracted greater attention because they allow participants to trade contracts linked to real-world events and generate market-based signals about potential outcomes.
&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Base Co-Founder Jesse Pollak’s X Account Compromised, BASEMEME Promoted in Fraudulent Posts</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

  &lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhM3UNd2S8ww1dtLcbbz4gk_R60piWB9QgbDyNQPFHAcBqYeehlDgQu31zDM-p5HShukqdu1MfCc3VQ5YC3KYgR6EA0Dm_-lTQJjH4mQ2bhhiD6fl0T_icOQ23ibsVPCvQO8F9hGl9FqK21FNivL9LoLao3kysx_0aowItCJgGhkk_FCeEiHjkIUmjUGdCY/s1672/jesse-pollak-x-account-compromised-basememe.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Jesse Pollak’s compromised X account used to promote BASEMEME token" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhM3UNd2S8ww1dtLcbbz4gk_R60piWB9QgbDyNQPFHAcBqYeehlDgQu31zDM-p5HShukqdu1MfCc3VQ5YC3KYgR6EA0Dm_-lTQJjH4mQ2bhhiD6fl0T_icOQ23ibsVPCvQO8F9hGl9FqK21FNivL9LoLao3kysx_0aowItCJgGhkk_FCeEiHjkIUmjUGdCY/w640-h360/jesse-pollak-x-account-compromised-basememe.jpg.png" title="Jesse Pollak X Account Compromised in BASEMEME Promotion" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/strong&gt; &amp;nbsp;|&amp;nbsp; September 6, 2026&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Base co-founder Jesse Pollak’s X account was compromised on September 6, with an attacker using a connected third-party application to publish posts promoting a token called BASEMEME.&lt;/strong&gt; Pollak later confirmed that the posts had been removed, third-party application connections had been revoked and he had regained full control of the account.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The incident did not involve a confirmed compromise of the Base blockchain itself. The available reports describe the problem as an account-security incident involving Pollak’s X account.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Happened to Jesse Pollak’s X Account?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Pollak said his X account had been compromised and that the attacker used a third-party application connected to the account to publish a fraudulent token ticker.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;After discovering the unauthorized activity, Pollak said the related posts were deleted and all third-party application connections were removed. He also confirmed that he had regained full control of the account and urged users to remain vigilant about security.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Reports from &lt;a href="https://www.chaincatcher.com/article/2287820" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;ChainCatcher&lt;/a&gt;, subsequently cited by other crypto news outlets, identified the token promoted through the compromised account as &lt;strong&gt;BASEMEME&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;BASEMEME Was Promoted Through the Compromised Account&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Screenshots of the deleted posts showed BASEMEME being promoted with language describing it as a meme coin with utility. The posts also included a link to &lt;strong&gt;o1.exchange&lt;/strong&gt; and a contract address for the token.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The important distinction is that the token was promoted from a compromised personal X account. There is no verified evidence in the reports reviewed for this article that BASEMEME was an official Base token or an official Base product.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That distinction matters because a post appearing on a prominent &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/how-to-move-encrypted-seedless-electrum.html"&gt;crypto executive’&lt;/a&gt;s compromised account can create the impression of an endorsement even when no such endorsement exists.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;BASEMEME’s Reported Market Cap&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Contemporary reports cited a market capitalization of approximately &lt;strong&gt;$257,000&lt;/strong&gt; for BASEMEME at the time of reporting.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That figure should be treated as a reported market snapshot rather than a stable valuation. Small-cap tokens can experience significant changes in liquidity, trading activity and market capitalization over short periods.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;CoinAINews has not included claims that BASEMEME crashed more than 90% because that move could not be independently verified with sufficiently strong market-data evidence.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Pollak Regained Control of the Account&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;According to Pollak’s clarification, the immediate security response included three key actions:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The fraudulent posts were deleted.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Third-party application connections were removed.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Full control of the X account was restored.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Pollak also warned users to remain vigilant, highlighting the risks created when attackers gain access to connected applications associated with high-profile social-media accounts.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;This Was an X Account Compromise, Not a Confirmed Base Blockchain Hack&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The incident should not be confused with a blockchain exploit.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The reporting available at the time of publication describes unauthorized activity on Pollak’s X account through a connected third-party application. It does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; establish that Base’s underlying blockchain infrastructure was compromised.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There is also no verified evidence in the sources reviewed for this article identifying the attacker, establishing a specific amount of money stolen from users, or confirming how many people interacted with the promoted token.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why the Incident Matters for Crypto Users&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Compromised social-media accounts are particularly dangerous in &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ark-invest-researcher-questions-whether.html"&gt;cryptocurrency&lt;/a&gt; because traders often treat posts from well-known developers, founders and executives as potential signals.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A fraudulent token promotion can therefore appear credible simply because it is published through a trusted account. The presence of a trading link or contract address does not establish that a token is legitimate or officially endorsed.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Users should independently verify announcements through official project websites, verified communication channels and other trusted sources before connecting &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/zcash-surges-above-1000-as-etf-demand.html"&gt;wallets&lt;/a&gt;, signing transactions or purchasing newly promoted tokens.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Is Confirmed — and What Is Not&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto;"&gt;

          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(68, 68, 68); padding: 10px;"&gt;Any definitive conclusion about total &lt;br /&gt;financial losses.&lt;/td&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;How Crypto Users Can Protect Themselves&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The incident highlights several basic security practices that remain important for crypto users:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Do not assume every post from a familiar account is authentic.&lt;/strong&gt; Even verified or prominent accounts can be compromised.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check official channels.&lt;/strong&gt; Cross-check major token announcements against a project’s official website and other verified communication channels.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Inspect links before connecting a wallet.&lt;/strong&gt; A link appearing in a compromised account’s post should not automatically be trusted.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Verify contract addresses independently.&lt;/strong&gt; Never rely solely on an address published in a social-media post.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Review connected applications regularly.&lt;/strong&gt; Removing unused or suspicious third-party connections can reduce account-security risks.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Do not trade solely because of an influential account.&lt;/strong&gt; Social-media visibility is not proof of legitimacy.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Was Jesse Pollak’s X account hacked?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Pollak confirmed that his X account was compromised. Reports say a third-party application connected to the account was used to publish unauthorized token-related content.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What token was promoted from the compromised account?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;The token promoted in the deleted posts was called &lt;strong&gt;BASEMEME&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Was BASEMEME officially launched by Base?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;There is no verified evidence in the sources reviewed for this article that BASEMEME was an official Base token or an official Base product. It was promoted through Pollak’s compromised account.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What was BASEMEME’s reported market cap?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Contemporary reports cited a market capitalization of approximately &lt;strong&gt;$257,000&lt;/strong&gt; at the relevant snapshot.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Did Pollak regain control of his account?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Yes. Pollak said the unauthorized posts were deleted, third-party application connections were removed and he had regained full control of the account.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Was the Base blockchain itself hacked?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;No such compromise was established by the sources reviewed for this report. The incident described in the available reporting concerns Pollak’s X account and a connected third-party application.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Did BASEMEME crash more than 90%?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;CoinAINews is not presenting that claim as a confirmed fact. Some secondary reports circulated claims of a sharp decline, but a sufficiently strong independent market-data source was not found to verify an exact 90%+ fall.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Jesse Pollak’s X account was compromised on September 6, and the attacker used a connected third-party application to promote BASEMEME through unauthorized posts. Pollak subsequently removed the posts and third-party connections and said he had regained control of the account.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The incident is a reminder that a cryptocurrency promotion appearing on a trusted social-media account is not automatically legitimate. In this case, the available evidence supports an account-compromise incident, while claims about attacker identity, user losses, Base blockchain security and a 90%+ BASEMEME collapse remain unconfirmed.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Sources&lt;/h2&gt;

    <title>Visa Moves to End Card Rewards Loophole for Memecoin Purchases</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj8Xex_4Humhu1vK2mNIVIYWhZomSHf5VQfHplHwyGY6Fsk8KSGVTsPvAo2gcPESL-zPvKyQ1378_mrMtvKNzga4u9AmcYntF1ctbcx8Rw8hcEYmoxb2SxuO_x5BzHtiNltbRk7QStgWMZ_gWw0hIJKSXCj_lbNvSrxQwkAnnPfRythBtA-Oh8vF2Ww77U2/s1536/visa-memecoin-card-rewards-crossmint.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Visa moves to end credit card rewards on memecoin purchases" border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="426" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj8Xex_4Humhu1vK2mNIVIYWhZomSHf5VQfHplHwyGY6Fsk8KSGVTsPvAo2gcPESL-zPvKyQ1378_mrMtvKNzga4u9AmcYntF1ctbcx8Rw8hcEYmoxb2SxuO_x5BzHtiNltbRk7QStgWMZ_gWw0hIJKSXCj_lbNvSrxQwkAnnPfRythBtA-Oh8vF2Ww77U2/w640-h426/visa-memecoin-card-rewards-crossmint.webp.png" title="Visa Memecoin Card Rewards Change" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Visa is moving to stop certain memecoin purchases from being processed as ordinary digital-media transactions, a change that could end the ability of some users to earn standard credit card rewards when buying meme coins through Crossmint-powered checkouts.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The reported move follows an investigation into memecoin purchases made through &lt;strong&gt;Robinhood Wallet&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;Fomo&lt;/strong&gt;, where some transactions were processed under a merchant category normally associated with digital goods rather than cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Visa Moves to Change How Memecoin Purchases Are Classified&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to recent reporting, Visa has told payment processors that the digital-media merchant category should not be used for memecoin purchases. The change targets a payment-processing route that allowed certain crypto purchases to appear on card networks as digital media transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The issue centers on &lt;strong&gt;merchant category code (MCC) 5815&lt;/strong&gt;, a category generally associated with digital goods and media. Earlier testing reported by The Block found that some memecoin purchases were processed under this category instead of a cryptocurrency-related classification. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because the transactions appeared as ordinary digital-media purchases, some cardholders received normal rewards such as points or cash back. Crypto purchases generally receive different treatment under card-network and issuer rules.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Crossmint, Robinhood Wallet and Fomo Fit Into the Story&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The reported transactions were powered by &lt;strong&gt;Crossmint&lt;/strong&gt;, a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/coinbase-and-robinhood-could-benefit-as.html"&gt;crypto payments&lt;/a&gt; infrastructure company whose checkout technology enabled users to purchase certain memecoins with credit cards through platforms including Robinhood Wallet and Fomo.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Block previously reported test purchases of the WIF memecoin using Visa and Mastercard cards connected through Apple Pay or Google Pay. Those transactions were reportedly classified as digital goods media and received ordinary card rewards. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The setup attracted attention because cryptocurrency purchases are normally subject to different processing and rewards rules than conventional digital goods.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Card Rewards Matter&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The main change for users could be the loss of ordinary credit card rewards on affected transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When a purchase is processed under a digital-media category, the card issuer can treat it differently from a transaction identified as cryptocurrency. That distinction can affect whether points, miles or cash-back rewards are awarded.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If processors instead classify the purchases under the appropriate cryptocurrency categories, affected users may no longer receive the same rewards. The exact impact can also depend on the card issuer and its individual rewards policies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Chase Questioned the Classification&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The classification came under additional scrutiny after JPMorgan Chase challenged at least one Visa transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Chase told The Block that the transaction appeared to have been assigned an incorrect category and should not have qualified for the associated rewards. The bank subsequently opened a case with Visa. The New York Attorney General's Office also said it was aware of the matter and was reviewing the issue. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The dispute highlights an important distinction: how a transaction is categorized by a card network is separate from the legal question of how a particular &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/trump-announces-ai-force-and-ai-czar-as.html"&gt;memecoin &lt;/a&gt;may be treated under securities or other financial regulations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Crossmint Has Defended Its Approach&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crossmint has disputed the idea that its procedures were simply designed to bypass card-network rules. The company has pointed to its treatment of certain memecoins as digital collectibles and has argued that its digital-goods processing approach is consistent with its position.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, card-network classification rules operate independently from securities-law interpretations. A token's regulatory status does not automatically determine which merchant category should be used for a card transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent reporting also said Crossmint maintained that its procedures for processing digital goods had not changed. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens to Memecoin Purchases Now?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The reported Visa change does not mean that users will suddenly be unable to buy memecoins with cards in every situation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, the immediate issue is how qualifying transactions are classified and processed. Visa has reportedly given payment processors a transition period to stop using the digital-media category for these purchases, with the period expected to end during the week beginning September 21. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once the new classification is applied, affected purchases may lose ordinary card rewards and could also be subject to issuer-specific restrictions or fees. The exact result will depend on the payment processor, card issuer and transaction flow.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why This Matters for Crypto Payments&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The episode shows how merchant-category codes can have a significant effect on the user experience for crypto purchases.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For consumers, the difference between a transaction being recognized as digital media or cryptocurrency can affect rewards, fees and how the purchase is handled by the card issuer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For crypto payment companies, the development also illustrates the importance of aligning checkout infrastructure with established card-network requirements as crypto becomes more integrated with mainstream payment systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Mastercard Has Not Announced a Matching Move&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;While the reported Visa action is focused on its payment network and processors, there has been no equivalent public announcement from Mastercard indicating that it will take the same step.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters because earlier testing found that the Crossmint-powered checkout could also process memecoin purchases using Mastercard cards. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Whether Mastercard introduces a similar requirement remains separate from Visa's reported action.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Crypto Users Should Watch Next&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether affected memecoin checkouts continue to accept credit cards after the transition period.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether ordinary card points and cash-back rewards disappear from those transactions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether payment processors introduce different restrictions or fees.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether Mastercard or other card networks issue similar guidance.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;How Robinhood Wallet, Fomo and Crossmint adjust their payment flows.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Key Facts&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Visa is reportedly tightening the way certain memecoin purchases are classified, potentially ending a payment-processing route that allowed some buyers to receive ordinary credit card rewards on crypto purchases.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The change follows scrutiny of Crossmint-powered checkouts used through Robinhood &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/sent-btc-to-wrong-address-what-happens.html"&gt;Wallet &lt;/a&gt;and Fomo, including questions raised by Chase over the classification of at least one transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For crypto users, the immediate issue is less about whether memecoins can be purchased and more about &lt;strong&gt;how those purchases are processed, classified and rewarded&lt;/strong&gt;. As payment processors transition away from the digital-media classification, the availability of card rewards and other benefits could change.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Updated September 21, 2026, to reflect the latest reported developments. Visa's reported processor guidance and transition timeline are based on industry reporting; users should check their card issuer's terms for the treatment of cryptocurrency transactions.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
