    <title>Can AI Own Its Own Crypto Wallet? The Law Says No — For Now</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi7ySD1nMn4gw2SkaFVH-9iV7hCnN4vJ9q0aoKzIYaOe6j5Aurts5dQSfP3OGjMkYYhfe_58gt7mRfKxzbrYn6qwcYpl7-N9BFgMsBY4WPj_gDSaHGhVgEeLJEJS8abuRRpMFLgAn_68zKZ5JnAIyQZ1nPlzusiN8oOVO7CkkQZPZUsbht9i9-Wm8TsLh4Q/s1248/ai-own-crypto-wallet-legal-ownership.jpg.jpg" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="AI agent controlling a cryptocurrency wallet without independent legal ownership" border="0" data-original-height="832" data-original-width="1248" height="426" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi7ySD1nMn4gw2SkaFVH-9iV7hCnN4vJ9q0aoKzIYaOe6j5Aurts5dQSfP3OGjMkYYhfe_58gt7mRfKxzbrYn6qwcYpl7-N9BFgMsBY4WPj_gDSaHGhVgEeLJEJS8abuRRpMFLgAn_68zKZ5JnAIyQZ1nPlzusiN8oOVO7CkkQZPZUsbht9i9-Wm8TsLh4Q/w640-h426/ai-own-crypto-wallet-legal-ownership.jpg.jpg" title="Can AI Own Its Own Crypto Wallet?" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;An AI agent can generate a crypto wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It can potentially hold cryptocurrency, sign blockchain transactions, pay another wallet, interact with smart contracts and even manage money without asking a human to approve every transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So here is the question that sounds simple but is becoming surprisingly difficult:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Can the AI actually own the wallet?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The short answer is: &lt;strong&gt;technical control is possible, but legal ownership is a different matter.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is becoming one of the most interesting legal questions in crypto as AI agents move from chatbots that answer questions to software that can actually take financial actions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Research and industry discussions in 2026 increasingly describe this as a new legal frontier. Electric Capital has highlighted the emergence of crypto wallets for AI agents, while legal research on AI agents points to unresolved questions around authority, responsibility, identity and agency. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Yes, an AI Can Technically Create a Crypto Wallet&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Let's start with the part that is already possible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A crypto wallet does not need a human hand to be generated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Software can generate a blockchain address and the cryptographic credentials needed to authorize transactions. An AI agent can then be connected to infrastructure that allows it to use those credentials under whatever permissions the system provides.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means an AI system can, from a technical perspective, have a wallet address associated with it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It could potentially receive cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It could potentially send &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitcoin-faces-80k-supply-wall-as-long.html"&gt;cryptocurrency&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It could interact with decentralized applications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It could potentially pay for services automatically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And it could operate continuously without someone sitting in front of a computer clicking “send.”&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is the easy part.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The difficult part begins when we replace the word &lt;em&gt;control&lt;/em&gt; with the word &lt;em&gt;ownership&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;A Wallet Address Is Not the Same Thing as a Legal Person&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where the crypto world and the legal world start speaking different languages.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On a blockchain, an address can receive assets without anyone asking for a passport, birth certificate or company registration document.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The blockchain essentially cares whether the correct cryptographic authorization is provided.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Law cares about something else.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Law needs to know who owns property, who can enter agreements, who can owe money, who can be sued, who can pay taxes and who is responsible when something goes wrong.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI agent does not automatically acquire those rights simply because it can control a private key or execute a transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Current legal discussions generally treat AI agents as systems acting on behalf of people or organizations rather than automatically recognizing the software itself as an independent legal person. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Think of It Like a Robot Holding a Key&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Imagine you give a sophisticated robot the keys to your house.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The robot can open the door.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It can walk around the house.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It can move your furniture.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It can even order groceries using an account you gave it access to.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;None of that automatically means the robot owns the house.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The same basic distinction can apply to an AI-controlled crypto wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI may have the &lt;strong&gt;technical ability to control the wallet&lt;/strong&gt; without being the &lt;strong&gt;legal owner of the assets associated with it.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is likely to become increasingly important as autonomous financial agents become more capable.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;So Who Owns the Crypto?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are several possible structures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Scenario one: an individual owns the wallet.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A person creates a wallet and gives an AI agent permission to operate it. The AI trades Bitcoin and doubles the portfolio.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI made the decisions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But that does not automatically make the AI the owner of the Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Scenario two: a company owns the wallet.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A company creates an AI trading agent and funds its wallet with company assets. The agent then trades on behalf of the business.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Again, the software's ability to execute transactions does not by itself create a new legal owner.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Scenario three: an autonomous protocol controls the assets.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is much harder.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Imagine an AI agent is deployed through a decentralized protocol, receives revenue, pays other agents and continues operating without a traditional company sitting behind every transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Now the questions become considerably more complicated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Who owns the assets?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Who controls the agent?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Who can change its rules?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Who can shut it down?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Who is responsible if it causes damage?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And if nobody has a clear answer, who does the law hold accountable?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Blockchain Can Prove Control. It May Not Prove Legal Ownership.&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction is easy to miss.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blockchain can provide extremely strong evidence that a particular private key authorized a transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But a blockchain transaction does not necessarily answer every legal question surrounding that transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, a ledger might show that wallet A sent 10 ETH to wallet B.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It does not automatically tell a court whether &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ai-made-millions-in-crypto-who-pays-tax.html"&gt;wallet &lt;/a&gt;A belonged to an individual, a company, a trust, a DAO, an AI agent operating for someone else, or a hacked system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent research on agentic finance makes a similar distinction: blockchain can provide evidence of transactions and certain authorization parameters, but it cannot by itself establish institutional mandate, legal accountability or the underlying accounting treatment. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That may become one of the defining legal issues of the AI-wallet era.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Agents Are Already Moving Beyond Simple Automation&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The idea of an AI wallet is no longer purely theoretical.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In 2026, crypto infrastructure companies and researchers are building systems designed specifically for agents that need to transact.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Electric Capital described crypto wallets for &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ai-with-wallet-can-it-spend-your-crypto.html"&gt;AI agents&lt;/a&gt; as creating a new legal frontier because agents can use wallets to hold assets, pay for services and interact economically with other systems. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The technology therefore has a very practical reason to exist.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI agents need ways to pay for things.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A software agent that books a service, buys data, pays another agent or performs an on-chain task cannot always wait for a human to approve every tiny transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto provides programmable financial infrastructure that can make those interactions possible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the legal system still has to answer a very old-fashioned question:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Whose money is it?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The “Agent” Word Creates Another Problem&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is a subtle legal issue hiding inside the word &lt;em&gt;agent&lt;/em&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In computer science, an AI agent is software capable of observing information, making decisions and taking actions toward a goal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In law, agency has a much more specific meaning.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Legal agency involves concepts such as authority, principals, duties and the consequences of actions taken on another party's behalf.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those two meanings overlap, but they are not identical.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Research on AI agents and law has highlighted exactly this problem: technical systems can behave like agents in the computer-science sense while still raising unresolved questions about legal authority, disclosure, loyalty and responsibility. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So calling software an “agent” does not automatically give it the legal status of a human agent.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If the AI Makes a Million Dollars?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Now let's make the scenario more interesting.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Suppose an AI agent starts with $10,000 worth of cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It trades continuously.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Six months later, the wallet contains $1 million.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Who owns the million dollars?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The answer cannot be determined simply by looking at the wallet address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important questions would include:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who funded the wallet?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who created or deployed the AI?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who had authority over the wallet?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;What agreement governed the agent's activities?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who was supposed to receive the profits?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Was the agent acting for an individual or a business?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;What jurisdiction applies?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI's contribution to generating the profit does not automatically make the AI the legal beneficiary.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;And What If the AI Loses Everything?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The ownership question becomes a responsibility question when things go wrong.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Suppose the AI makes a series of disastrous trades and loses 90% of the wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Or it sends funds to the wrong address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Or it interacts with a malicious smart contract.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Or it follows a manipulated instruction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Who is responsible?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is one of the biggest unanswered questions surrounding increasingly autonomous systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent legal reporting on autonomous AI systems shows that regulators and lawyers are already debating whether responsibility should fall on developers, deployers, users or other parties when AI systems cause harm. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto adds another layer because blockchain transactions can be irreversible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once an autonomous agent sends funds, there may be no bank employee who can simply reverse the payment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;India Is Already Thinking About AI Agents Making Payments&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This issue is not limited to crypto.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;India is already moving toward infrastructure designed to identify and authorize AI agents making payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Reuters reported on September 10, 2026 that the National Payments Corporation of India is developing a registry to verify and monitor AI agents conducting transactions through UPI. The proposed system is part of India's broader work on agentic payments, with potential future applications extending to conditional purchases and investment-related activity. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is an important detail in that development.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The technology may be able to identify an AI agent.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That still does not automatically answer who is legally responsible for the agent's actions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Reuters noted that liability for unauthorized or erroneous agentic payments remains an issue requiring regulatory treatment. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is essentially the same problem crypto developers are beginning to encounter.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could an AI Become a Legal Person?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Technically, there is nothing preventing society from changing the law in the future.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Legislatures could theoretically create a new legal category for autonomous software or give certain AI systems a form of legal personality.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But that would require much more than simply declaring that an AI owns its wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A legal person has rights and obligations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There would need to be rules for ownership, contracts, taxation, liability, bankruptcy, representation and enforcement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There would also need to be an answer to a strange but important question:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;What happens when the AI's wallet runs out of money?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Could the AI go bankrupt?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Could someone sue it?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Could a court order it to pay damages?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Could it inherit assets?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Could it enter a binding contract?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Could it own intellectual property?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Giving AI legal personality would open an enormous legal door.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Future May Not Require AI to Become a Legal Person&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is another possibility.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of making AI itself a legal person, lawmakers and technology companies may build systems where every autonomous agent remains linked to an accountable human or organization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI would receive limited authority.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The authority could specify what assets it can access, what transactions it can execute and how much money it can spend.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An independent control layer could then verify whether each proposed transaction falls within that authority before the blockchain transaction is executed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is close to the architecture proposed in recent research on “authority-inference separation,” where an AI's recommendation does not automatically grant it execution authority. Instead, a separate control system checks identity, ownership, mandate, risk limits and other conditions before granting temporary authority. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That model may prove more practical than trying to turn every AI agent into a legal person.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Ownership and Crypto Ownership Are Two Different Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This may be the most important takeaway.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Can an AI control a wallet?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Increasingly, yes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Can an AI transact with cryptocurrency?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes, if the necessary infrastructure and permissions are provided.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Can an AI technically generate its own wallet address?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Does that automatically mean the AI legally owns the wallet or the cryptocurrency inside it?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No—not under the legal frameworks generally discussed today.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That final distinction is where the real story begins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If the Human Owner Dies?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Here's an even stranger scenario.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Imagine someone creates an autonomous AI trading agent, funds its wallet and gives it instructions to continue operating indefinitely.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The person later dies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI continues trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It earns money.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It pays other agents.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It accumulates more cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Who owns the new assets?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That question becomes particularly complicated if the agent's original owner cannot be reached, the private keys are unavailable or the legal structure surrounding the wallet was never clearly established.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Researchers are already exploring these kinds of “principal-less” autonomous-agent scenarios, including what happens when an agent continues operating after the human principal disappears. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, these remain emerging legal and technical questions rather than settled rules.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Wallet May Be Autonomous. The Accountability Probably Isn't.&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where the future of AI finance could settle.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI may be allowed to act independently.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It may trade while its owner sleeps.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It may pay another machine.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It may manage a portfolio.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It may even negotiate transactions with other AI agents.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the infrastructure around it may still require an identifiable party who ultimately carries legal responsibility.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is also why identity and authorization systems are becoming such an important part of agentic finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The technology is moving toward autonomous action.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The law still wants to know &lt;strong&gt;who authorized the action.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;So, Can AI Own Its Own Crypto Wallet?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not in the straightforward legal sense suggested by the headline.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI can create or control a blockchain wallet from a technical perspective. It can potentially hold and transfer cryptocurrency through that wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But a wallet address does not automatically create legal personality.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In today's emerging legal landscape, ownership and responsibility generally remain connected to the humans, companies or other recognized legal structures behind the system, although the exact answer can vary by jurisdiction and circumstances.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could change.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But changing it would require lawmakers to answer far more than one question about crypto.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They would have to decide whether an autonomous machine can possess rights, obligations, assets and liabilities independently of the humans who created or deployed it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The fascinating part about AI crypto wallets is not that an AI can generate a wallet address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Software has been able to do that for years.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The fascinating part is what happens when the software becomes capable of &lt;strong&gt;earning, spending, trading and controlling valuable assets with increasingly little human intervention.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchain technology can give an AI something close to financial hands.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It does not automatically give that AI a legal identity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the wallet may belong to the person or entity behind the agent, even when the AI is the one doing the clicking—or, more accurately, signing the transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But as AI agents become more economically independent, that distinction may become one of the biggest legal questions of the next generation of crypto.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The machine may already know how to hold the money. The law still has to decide who owns it.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Disclaimer: This article is for informational and educational purposes only and is not legal, tax or investment advice. Laws concerning AI, digital assets, ownership and liability vary by jurisdiction and continue to evolve.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Standard Chartered Launches Bitcoin and Ether Spot Trading for Institutional Clients in UAE</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEitKiu56tG_RvJT1hUTMWShrea7lzMA0YJYhEGiYB55Z6C5Z4WZcdL1Fpjm5W7v1Z_YJcesDMzJoYLMKaqXysrb-Uo2mFb6A75C4jFIQynH-eaBlTVQBBYIRJ-b4PJ3TW9YouLRJfvLqvewrdoAeieWgpONfW2vomtl0kb1aXdZ24KSweYobmHHS0IwTBvd/s1672/standard-chartered-bitcoin-ether-trading-uae.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Standard Chartered launches Bitcoin and Ether spot trading for institutional clients in UAE" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEitKiu56tG_RvJT1hUTMWShrea7lzMA0YJYhEGiYB55Z6C5Z4WZcdL1Fpjm5W7v1Z_YJcesDMzJoYLMKaqXysrb-Uo2mFb6A75C4jFIQynH-eaBlTVQBBYIRJ-b4PJ3TW9YouLRJfvLqvewrdoAeieWgpONfW2vomtl0kb1aXdZ24KSweYobmHHS0IwTBvd/w640-h360/standard-chartered-bitcoin-ether-trading-uae.jpg.png" title="Standard Chartered Bitcoin and Ether Trading in UAE" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;
September 3, 2026&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Standard Chartered has launched Bitcoin and Ether spot trading for eligible institutional clients in the United Arab Emirates, expanding the bank's regulated digital-asset services in the Gulf.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new service gives eligible institutional clients access to deliverable Bitcoin and Ether trading through Standard Chartered's electronic trading channels. The offering is being provided through the bank's regulated Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) operation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Standard Chartered's announcement makes the UAE the latest market in which the global banking group is bringing cryptocurrency trading into its existing institutional financial infrastructure. Reuters reported the development on September 3, 2026. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Standard Chartered Launches Bitcoin and Ether Trading in UAE&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new service focuses on &lt;strong&gt;spot trading in Bitcoin and Ether&lt;/strong&gt; for eligible institutional clients rather than retail cryptocurrency users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In a spot transaction, the buyer and seller trade the underlying digital asset for delivery instead of entering into a derivatives contract. Standard Chartered said eligible clients can access deliverable Bitcoin and Ether through its electronic trading channels.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The trading service is integrated into the bank's existing platforms and can be accessed through familiar foreign-exchange interfaces. This approach is designed to fit cryptocurrency transactions into workflows already used by professional financial-market participants.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Clients can also settle their trades through a custodian of their choice, including Standard Chartered's digital-asset custody service.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the UAE Crypto Trading Launch Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The announcement is significant because Standard Chartered is one of the world's major international banks, while the UAE has become an increasingly important centre for digital-asset businesses and institutional finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Standard Chartered said the UAE launch makes it the &lt;strong&gt;first Global Systemically Important Bank, or G-SIB, to offer institutional Bitcoin and Ether spot trading in the UAE&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A G-SIB is a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/kraken-parent-payward-delays-ipo-to-q2.html"&gt;financial institution&lt;/a&gt; designated as systemically important because its size, interconnectedness and global operations mean that its activities can have broader implications for the international financial system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bringing spot cryptocurrency trading into a G-SIB's banking infrastructure is therefore an important development for the institutional digital-asset market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Trading Comes Through Standard Chartered's Dubai Operation&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The UAE service is being offered through Standard Chartered's operation in the &lt;strong&gt;Dubai International Financial Centre&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bank already has a digital-asset presence in the UAE. Standard Chartered launched digital-asset custody services in the country in September 2024, creating a regulated banking infrastructure for institutional clients seeking to hold digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest development adds trading execution to that existing custody capability.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This combination can be particularly relevant for institutions because professional investors often evaluate execution, custody, settlement and risk management together when deciding how to access a new asset class.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Can Institutional Clients Trade?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At launch, the UAE service supports &lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin and Ether&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin is the largest cryptocurrency by market value and remains the primary digital asset for many institutional investors. Ether is the native cryptocurrency of Ethereum and provides exposure to one of the most widely used blockchain networks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;By initially concentrating on these two assets, Standard Chartered is focusing on cryptocurrencies that already have substantial institutional trading infrastructure and market recognition.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bank previously launched institutional deliverable spot trading in Bitcoin and Ether through its UK branch in July 2025. Standard Chartered described that earlier launch as the first deliverable spot crypto-trading service from a G-SIB for institutional clients. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Standard Chartered's Institutional Crypto Trading Works&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The service is designed to operate within the bank's existing institutional trading environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Rather than requiring clients to use a separate crypto-native trading interface, Standard Chartered allows eligible institutions to access Bitcoin and Ether through its electronic trading channels and familiar foreign-exchange interfaces.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is potentially important for asset managers, corporations and other professional investors that already have established trading and compliance procedures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Clients can choose their custodian for settlement, including Standard Chartered's own digital-asset custody platform.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The model gives institutional users more flexibility over how their digital assets are held after execution.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Standard Chartered's Digital-Asset Strategy Goes Beyond Trading&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The UAE trading launch is part of a broader &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/how-does-blockchain-really-work.html"&gt;digital-assets&lt;/a&gt; strategy at Standard Chartered.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bank has been developing services across custody, trading, tokenization and other blockchain-related financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Its existing UAE custody operation provides the foundation for institutional digital-asset safekeeping, while the new trading service adds direct execution capabilities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Standard Chartered has also been expanding its digital-asset activities internationally as institutional interest in cryptocurrency and blockchain-based financial products grows.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bank's strategy increasingly treats digital assets as part of the wider evolution of financial markets rather than as a standalone cryptocurrency business.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Spot Trading Is Important for Institutions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Institutional investors have different requirements from individual cryptocurrency traders.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Large investors typically need robust trading infrastructure, operational controls, compliance processes, custody arrangements and reliable settlement mechanisms before allocating significant capital to a new asset class.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A regulated bank offering spot crypto trading can potentially address some of those requirements within an existing financial-services relationship.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not eliminate the risks associated with cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin and Ether remain volatile assets, and institutional investors still face market, liquidity, regulatory and operational risks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the availability of regulated banking infrastructure can make it easier for professional investors to evaluate and access digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The UAE Is Becoming a Key Digital-Asset Market&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The UAE has spent recent years developing its position as a regional centre for digital assets and blockchain businesses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Dubai in particular has attracted cryptocurrency companies and financial institutions seeking to operate within a defined regulatory environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Standard Chartered's expansion adds another major traditional financial institution to that ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bank's decision also highlights the growing importance of the UAE for institutional digital-asset services in the Middle East.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In 2024, Standard Chartered said its decision to launch digital-asset custody in the UAE reflected the country's approach to digital-asset adoption and financial regulation. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;From Crypto Custody to Crypto Trading&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Standard Chartered's UAE expansion follows a clear progression.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;First, the bank established digital-asset custody capabilities in the country. It is now adding direct spot trading for Bitcoin and Ether.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That development means institutional clients can potentially access multiple parts of the digital-asset lifecycle through a traditional banking relationship.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Standard Chartered, this creates an opportunity to build a broader digital-asset business around trading, custody and other financial services.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For institutional investors, it provides another route into cryptocurrency markets without relying exclusively on specialist crypto exchanges.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Standard Chartered's Previous Bitcoin and Ether Trading Launch&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bank's move into institutional crypto trading is not entirely new.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In July 2025, Standard Chartered launched deliverable spot trading in &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/how-does-blockchain-really-work.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt; and Ether through its UK branch. The bank said the service was fully integrated into its existing platforms and allowed institutional clients to access crypto assets through familiar FX interfaces. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That launch established the framework that Standard Chartered is now extending to the UAE.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The difference is that the latest announcement gives institutional clients in the Gulf access to the same type of direct spot trading infrastructure through the bank's UAE operation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What This Means for the Crypto Industry&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The development adds to a broader trend in which traditional financial institutions are moving deeper into digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto adoption is no longer limited to specialist exchanges, blockchain companies and individual investors. Banks, asset managers and other established financial institutions are increasingly building services around trading, custody, tokenization and blockchain-based settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Standard Chartered's UAE launch is another example of that shift.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If institutional demand continues to grow, more global banks could expand regulated cryptocurrency trading services across major financial centres.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could Standard Chartered Add More Digital Assets?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin and Ether are the assets supported by the UAE spot-trading launch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Whether the bank eventually adds other cryptocurrencies or digital-asset products will depend on institutional demand, market infrastructure and regulatory requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the focus on Bitcoin and Ether allows Standard Chartered to build its UAE offering around two of the most established digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Institutional Investors Should Watch Next&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Institutional demand:&lt;/strong&gt; Adoption by asset managers, corporations and other professional investors will indicate how much demand exists for bank-based crypto execution.&lt;/li&gt;

&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Trading volumes:&lt;/strong&gt; The level of Bitcoin and Ether activity through the platform could provide an indication of institutional participation.&lt;/li&gt;

&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Product expansion:&lt;/strong&gt; Future additions to trading, custody or tokenization services could broaden Standard Chartered's digital-asset offering.&lt;/li&gt;

&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Regulation:&lt;/strong&gt; UAE and international digital-asset regulations will remain an important factor for banks and institutional investors.&lt;/li&gt;

&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Custody growth:&lt;/strong&gt; Increased demand for regulated digital-asset custody could strengthen the connection between traditional banking and cryptocurrency markets.&lt;/li&gt;

&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Tokenization:&lt;/strong&gt; Growth in tokenized securities and blockchain-based financial products could become another major area of institutional adoption.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the Launch Means for Bitcoin and Ether&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The announcement does not mean that Standard Chartered is recommending Bitcoin or Ether as investments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, it means eligible institutional clients now have another regulated channel through which they can access the two digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Bitcoin and Ether, broader access through established banks could potentially increase the number of traditional financial institutions participating in the market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the actual impact on cryptocurrency prices will depend on client demand, trading volumes and broader market conditions rather than the launch itself.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Standard Chartered's Bigger Vision for Digital Assets&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest UAE expansion suggests that Standard Chartered sees digital assets as part of a much larger transformation in financial services.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trading is only one component.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Custody, tokenization, settlement and digital payment infrastructure are also becoming increasingly important as blockchain technology moves into traditional finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Standard Chartered's existing digital-asset businesses and its continued expansion indicate that the bank is positioning itself to participate across several of these areas.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Standard Chartered has launched institutional spot trading in Bitcoin and Ether in the UAE through its Dubai International Financial Centre operation.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The service is available to eligible institutional clients and provides access to deliverable Bitcoin and Ether through the bank's electronic trading infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The launch builds on Standard Chartered's digital-asset custody business in the UAE and its earlier institutional Bitcoin and Ether spot-trading service through its UK branch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;More broadly, the move highlights the continuing integration of cryptocurrency markets with traditional financial institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the UAE, the launch further strengthens its position as an important centre for regulated digital-asset activity. For Standard Chartered, it expands a digital-assets strategy that now covers trading and custody alongside its broader work in blockchain-based financial services.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The key point for investors is that this is an institutional trading launch, not a retail crypto-trading rollout.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Did Standard Chartered launch Bitcoin trading in the UAE?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Standard Chartered launched spot Bitcoin trading for eligible institutional clients in the United Arab Emirates on September 3, 2026.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can institutional clients trade Ether through Standard Chartered in the UAE?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. The UAE service supports deliverable spot trading in both Bitcoin and Ether.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Standard Chartered's UAE crypto service available to retail investors?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. The announcement concerns eligible institutional clients. It should not be interpreted as a retail Bitcoin or Ether trading launch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Where is Standard Chartered's UAE crypto trading service operated?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The service is being provided through Standard Chartered's operation in the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC).&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Standard Chartered the first G-SIB to offer this service in the UAE?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Standard Chartered says the UAE launch makes it the first Global Systemically Important Bank (G-SIB) to offer institutional Bitcoin and Ether spot trading in the UAE. Reuters also reported the same distinction. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does Standard Chartered already offer crypto custody in the UAE?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. The bank launched digital-asset custody services in the UAE in September 2024. The custody business initially supported major digital assets including Bitcoin and Ethereum. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;When did Standard Chartered first launch institutional Bitcoin and Ether spot trading?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Standard Chartered launched institutional deliverable spot trading in Bitcoin and Ether through its UK branch in July 2025. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why is Standard Chartered's UAE crypto launch important?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The launch gives eligible institutional investors access to Bitcoin and Ether through the infrastructure of a major global bank. It also demonstrates how digital assets are becoming increasingly integrated with traditional financial services.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Will Standard Chartered add more cryptocurrencies?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The UAE service currently focuses on Bitcoin and Ether. Any expansion to additional digital assets would depend on client demand, regulatory requirements and Standard Chartered's future strategy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Sources:&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;a href="https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/standard-chartered-launches-institutional-spot-crypto-trading-uae-2026-09-03/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Reuters&lt;/a&gt; | &lt;a href="https://www.sc.com/en/investors/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Standard Chartered&lt;/a&gt; | &lt;a href="https://www.sc.com/en/press-release/standard-chartered-launches-digital-assets-trading-for-institutional-clients/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Standard Chartered Digital Assets Trading&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Editorial note:&lt;/strong&gt; This article was prepared using reporting and official information available on September 3, 2026. The service described above is for eligible institutional clients and is not a general retail cryptocurrency trading launch.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Crypto Fear &amp; Greed Index Hits 74 — Highest Reading Since October 2025</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhSZeTXo6hK78HQeK8toBkWq_Y3C-St5mME8tfgOgAB7p8axLkDptRRnJNN7ljxCaJ-U_j9CUOKFCHgdQaHa1GkhapNFujkAnPW1Pol7w7YpZcAzOX56VeY6QrBFA-HK_H0w11ibcKCqor4XmUHVNLgf8VDyPK-_-k4KG9xJJnRQf9Pq0nUeKdRqA_RlSCb/s1672/crypto-fear-greed-index-74-bitcoin-sentiment.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Crypto Fear and Greed Index rises to 74 as Bitcoin sentiment reaches highest level since October 2025" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhSZeTXo6hK78HQeK8toBkWq_Y3C-St5mME8tfgOgAB7p8axLkDptRRnJNN7ljxCaJ-U_j9CUOKFCHgdQaHa1GkhapNFujkAnPW1Pol7w7YpZcAzOX56VeY6QrBFA-HK_H0w11ibcKCqor4XmUHVNLgf8VDyPK-_-k4KG9xJJnRQf9Pq0nUeKdRqA_RlSCb/w400-h225/crypto-fear-greed-index-74-bitcoin-sentiment.jpg.png" title="Crypto Fear &amp;amp; Greed Index Hits 74" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff | &lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Crypto market sentiment has moved firmly into greed
territory, with the Fear &amp;amp; Greed Index reaching its highest level since
October 2025.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The index climbed to 74, according to the latest market
update shared by Cointelegraph, signaling a sharp improvement in investor
confidence as Bitcoin and the wider cryptocurrency market regain momentum.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A reading of 74 sits firmly in the greed zone, although
it remains below the most extreme levels of optimism typically associated with
the upper end of the indicator.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Does a 74 Reading Mean?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Crypto Fear &amp;amp; Greed Index converts several market
signals into a score between 0 and 100.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Lower readings indicate fear among investors, while
higher readings indicate growing optimism and willingness to take risk. The
methodology considers factors such as market momentum, volatility, trading
activity and social-media sentiment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A score of 74 therefore suggests that investors are
becoming considerably more confident about the crypto market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But it does not mean that Bitcoin is guaranteed to
continue rising.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The index is designed to measure market psychology, not
predict future prices.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin's Rally Is Improving Sentiment&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The improvement in sentiment comes as Bitcoin has
regained momentum and moved back above the $80,000 level.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That price recovery has helped change the tone across the
broader digital-asset market. Investors who had previously remained cautious
are becoming more willing to increase their exposure as momentum improves.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Institutional demand has also become an important part of
the story.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Recent spot Bitcoin ETF flows have shown renewed buying
interest, providing another indication that the recovery is attracting capital
beyond short-term crypto traders.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;When price momentum and capital flows move in the same
direction, sentiment can change quickly.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That appears to be what is happening in the market now.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Traders Are Watching 74 Closely&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Sentiment indicators become particularly interesting when
markets move rapidly.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A high Fear &amp;amp; Greed reading can indicate that
investors are increasingly willing to take risk — but it can also signal that
optimism is becoming crowded.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That distinction matters.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;When traders become increasingly confident, more capital
can enter the market and reinforce an existing rally. Rising prices can create
stronger expectations of further gains, encouraging even more buying.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But crowded optimism can also make &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/hugging-face-reportedly-explores-13b.html"&gt;markets&lt;/a&gt; more sensitive
to negative developments.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A sudden change in Bitcoin's price trend, ETF flows,
macroeconomic conditions or regulatory expectations could cause sentiment to
reverse quickly.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For that reason, traders generally treat the Fear &amp;amp;
Greed Index as a context indicator rather than a standalone buy or sell signal.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;74 Is Strong, But Not the Extreme&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The current reading is notable because it has reached
levels not seen since October 2025.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;However, a reading of 74 should not automatically be
interpreted as an extreme market condition.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The index ranges from extreme fear at the lower end to
extreme greed at the upper end. The current score shows strong optimism, but
the market has not necessarily reached the most euphoric stage of the scale.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That leaves an important question for investors: does
sentiment continue climbing, or does enthusiasm begin to cool?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The answer could depend heavily on &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/standard-chartered-becomes-first-bank.html"&gt;Bitcoin's&lt;/a&gt; ability to
maintain its recent gains.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Happened the Last Time Sentiment Was This High?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The comparison with October 2025 provides useful
historical context, but it should not be treated as a direct prediction.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Markets can produce similar sentiment readings under very
different conditions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin's price, liquidity, leverage, institutional
flows, monetary policy and broader risk appetite can all influence what happens
after a particular Fear &amp;amp; Greed reading is reached.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In other words, history can provide context without
guaranteeing that the same pattern will repeat.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That is why the current 74 reading is best understood as
a snapshot of investor psychology rather than a forecast.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bigger Market Picture&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The rise in crypto sentiment comes against a broader
backdrop of renewed interest in risk assets and digital currencies.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin's recent recovery has helped lift attention
across the crypto sector, while institutional products such as spot Bitcoin
ETFs have given traditional investors a more direct route into the asset.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Macroeconomic developments are also influencing the
market narrative.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Changes in interest-rate expectations, bond yields and
the U.S. dollar can affect investor demand for alternative assets such as
Bitcoin.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;As those variables shift, crypto sentiment can move just
as quickly.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The current reading of 74 therefore reflects a
combination of Bitcoin's price momentum and the broader mood surrounding
digital assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Investors Should Watch Next&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The most important question is whether the improvement in
sentiment is supported by sustained demand.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Three areas could provide clues.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin's price momentum: If Bitcoin continues holding
its recent gains, confidence could remain elevated. A sharp reversal, however,
could quickly weaken sentiment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Institutional flows: Continued demand through spot
Bitcoin &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/coinmarketcap-clarifies-dex-trading.html"&gt;ETFs would&lt;/a&gt; provide evidence that the rally is attracting longer-term
capital rather than being driven solely by short-term speculation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Fear &amp;amp; Greed readings: A move substantially higher
would indicate even stronger optimism, while a rapid decline could signal that
traders are becoming more cautious.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;None of these indicators can predict Bitcoin's next move
with certainty.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Together, however, they can help investors understand
whether the current rally is building a stronger foundation or becoming
increasingly dependent on market enthusiasm.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Crypto Fear &amp;amp; Greed Index has reached 74, its
highest reading since October 2025, highlighting just how quickly investor
sentiment has improved.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The move comes as Bitcoin regains momentum and renewed
interest returns to digital-asset markets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For investors, however, the number is more useful as a
measure of market psychology than as a prediction tool.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Crypto traders have moved from caution toward optimism in
a relatively short period. The next test will be whether that optimism is
supported by sustained buying and stronger market fundamentals — or whether
increasingly crowded sentiment eventually makes the market more vulnerable to a
pullback — or whether this rally has further room to run.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and
does not constitute investment advice. Cryptocurrency markets are highly
volatile, and investors should conduct their own research before making
financial decisions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Monad Developers Propose Upgradeable Wallets With Passkeys, Social Recovery, and Quantum Security</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj8w3FdvhxhGNGxCXlFy4DvEG_3bhx3RBId1FAPR1fxwl4hx6-0EtOemssD6WiWIP4Fe0N5j7Cc9XZW54gmjCzBKK79adU9NntzC0lUB9yCHhExFIoZUhUhlvQfoXTbdPDvw8PsbzOclfEWkm2h1ZMU_6jouHpgSfjVGbkbnSrVoJx_x-HXgoxQ6Kkf5FBj/s1672/monad-upgradeable-wallet-passkeys-social-recovery-quantum-security.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Monad's proposed upgradeable wallets with passkeys, social recovery and post-quantum security" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj8w3FdvhxhGNGxCXlFy4DvEG_3bhx3RBId1FAPR1fxwl4hx6-0EtOemssD6WiWIP4Fe0N5j7Cc9XZW54gmjCzBKK79adU9NntzC0lUB9yCHhExFIoZUhUhlvQfoXTbdPDvw8PsbzOclfEWkm2h1ZMU_6jouHpgSfjVGbkbnSrVoJx_x-HXgoxQ6Kkf5FBj/w400-h225/monad-upgradeable-wallet-passkeys-social-recovery-quantum-security.jpg.png" title="Monad Proposes Upgradeable Wallets With Advanced Security" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff | &lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Monad developers are proposing a significant change to
wallet authentication — one that could let users upgrade security without ever
changing their wallet address.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The proposal would introduce a more flexible
authentication model designed to support passkeys, social recovery, key
rotation and post-&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/india-plans-first-tokenized-corporate.html"&gt;quantum security&lt;/a&gt; while allowing users to keep the same
on-chain address.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The idea addresses a long-standing problem in crypto:
wallets have traditionally placed enormous responsibility on users to protect a
private key or recovery phrase. If that credential is lost or compromised,
recovering access to assets can be extremely difficult.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Monad's proposed approach would separate the account's
persistent blockchain address from the authentication method used to authorize
transactions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Monad Is Proposing&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Under the proposed model, the authentication mechanism
associated with an account could be upgraded over time.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That means users could potentially replace an outdated or
compromised key without creating an entirely new wallet address.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The proposal is designed around the idea that an
account's security requirements can change as technology develops.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A user might initially authenticate with a conventional
cryptographic key, later add a passkey, use social recovery if access is lost,
rotate keys after a security incident, or eventually adopt cryptography
designed to withstand potential quantum-computing threats.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The blockchain address, however, could remain the same.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Passkeys Could Simplify &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/sam-altman-warns-ais-biggest-risks.html"&gt;Wallet&lt;/a&gt; Access&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;One of the most user-friendly elements of the proposal is
support for passkeys.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Passkeys allow users to authenticate through security
mechanisms built into modern devices and operating systems rather than relying
entirely on traditional passwords or manually managing cryptographic
credentials.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For crypto wallets, this could make onboarding
considerably easier.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;New users would not necessarily have to understand every
technical detail of private-key management before interacting with blockchain
applications.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The important distinction is that passkeys would become
an authentication option while the underlying account address could remain
unchanged.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Social Recovery Could Help Users Regain Access&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The proposal also includes social recovery.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Social recovery allows designated trusted parties or
accounts to participate in restoring access when a user's primary
authentication method is lost or compromised.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That could become particularly useful when someone loses
a device, replaces a phone or discovers that an authentication key may have
been exposed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Instead of treating one private key as the only possible
route to an account, social recovery can provide a controlled mechanism for
updating the credentials authorized to access it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The goal is straightforward: reduce the possibility that
losing one credential permanently means losing access to the account.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Key Rotation Adds Another Security Option&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Another important feature is key rotation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Key rotation allows an account to move from one
authorization key to another without necessarily creating a new blockchain
address.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This could be useful when a key becomes outdated or is
suspected of being compromised.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Rather than transferring assets and applications to a
completely different wallet, the account could potentially update its
authorized authentication mechanism and continue operating from the same
address.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For users managing significant on-chain assets, that
could make security maintenance much less disruptive.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Preparing for Post-Quantum Security&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The proposal also looks beyond today's security
environment by incorporating post-quantum security.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Current blockchain networks rely on cryptographic systems
designed to protect transactions against today's computing capabilities. Future
advances in quantum computing could potentially threaten some forms of
public-key cryptography.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That does not mean existing &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/crypto-fear-greed-index-hits-74-highest.html"&gt;blockchains&lt;/a&gt; are currently
vulnerable to practical quantum attacks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The concern is preparation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If cryptographic standards eventually need to change, an
account architecture capable of upgrading its authentication system could make
that transition easier.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Users would potentially be able to adopt new
cryptographic methods without abandoning their existing addresses.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Keeping the Same Address Matters&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A blockchain address can become associated with transaction
history, decentralized applications, tokens and other on-chain activity.
Creating a new address means rebuilding those relationships.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For an individual user, that can already be inconvenient.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For businesses, developers and applications, the
consequences can be even larger. An address can become part of payment
infrastructure, smart-contract interactions, accounting systems and established
on-chain identities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Changing the address can therefore create friction far
beyond simply moving assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;An authentication system that allows the security layer
to change while the address remains constant could make account upgrades
considerably easier.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The concept effectively separates who an account is
on-chain from how that account proves control.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A Different Approach to Crypto Wallet Security&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Traditional crypto wallets generally make the private key
central to ownership.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Control the key, and you control the account.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Lose the key, and the blockchain itself cannot simply
reset the password.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That model provides strong self-custody, but it also
creates a difficult user experience.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Upgradeable authentication takes a different approach.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Instead of treating one cryptographic credential as
permanently fixed, the account can potentially have rules that allow its
authentication mechanism to evolve.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That could bring blockchain accounts closer to the
flexibility users expect from conventional digital services, where
authentication credentials can be changed without replacing the underlying
account.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Convenience Does Not Automatically Mean Better Security&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There is an important trade-off.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Every additional recovery or authentication mechanism
creates another component that must be secured properly.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Social recovery needs carefully chosen recovery
participants. Key rotation needs strict authorization rules. Account upgrades
must be protected against unauthorized changes.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If these mechanisms are poorly designed, the flexibility
intended to protect users could create new attack vectors.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That makes security reviews, testing and implementation
details just as important as the features themselves.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The challenge is to provide legitimate users with more
ways to recover and secure accounts without giving attackers additional paths
to take control.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Monad's Proposal Fits a Wider Wallet Evolution&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The proposal reflects a broader shift in blockchain
development.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Early crypto wallets were largely built around a simple
model: the person controlling the private key controls the assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;As blockchain applications have become more
sophisticated, developers have increasingly explored smart accounts,
programmable authorization, passkeys and recovery mechanisms.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;These systems aim to make wallets easier to use without
giving up the benefits of blockchain-based ownership.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Monad's proposal pushes that concept further by focusing
on the ability to upgrade authentication while preserving the underlying
account address.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That could become particularly relevant as cryptographic
standards evolve.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The proposal does not automatically mean that all Monad
wallets will immediately gain these capabilities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The technical design, review and implementation process
will determine how the system eventually works in practice.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If adopted, the architecture could give Monad users more
flexibility when managing account security.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It could also make the network better prepared for future
changes in cryptographic technology.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For users, the biggest potential benefit is simple:
security credentials would no longer necessarily have to remain frozen for the
entire life of an account.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Monad developers are proposing upgradeable wallets with
support for passkeys, social recovery, key rotation and post-quantum security,
while preserving the user's existing blockchain address.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The proposal targets one of crypto's biggest usability
challenges: what happens when an authentication credential is lost, compromised
or becomes obsolete?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Instead of forcing users to abandon an address, the
proposed architecture could allow the authentication layer to evolve.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That would represent a meaningful change in how
blockchain accounts are designed — shifting the focus from permanently
protecting a single key toward building accounts that can adapt as security
requirements change.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If Monad can make that flexibility secure and reliable,
the account's security can evolve with the technology — without losing the
address that defines it on-chain.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and
does not constitute financial or investment advice. Cryptocurrency and
blockchain technologies involve risks. Readers should conduct their own
research before making financial decisions.&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
