    <title>Sam Altman Says AI Industry Did a “Terrible Job” Explaining Its Benefits</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjPm9WSccvgTqOtJCL7wCpjrww18EjpdqPTijG1-dtmz7hDF_8IovDFpwzaqmL349fcSaJ6mpE9hphiIVkg42fmpubW8mf9mLcsTBl4-Y66OzdLTzDDRgkZd2ZQoXD5CbA8IGQKwKC4j5rcRcTuct4k0dNx0vqw06CZASh1qbTC0ciaMVySL2bUPxfRCkGp/s1672/sam-altman-ai-industry-benefits-explained.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Sam Altman says the AI industry has done a terrible job explaining AI benefits" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjPm9WSccvgTqOtJCL7wCpjrww18EjpdqPTijG1-dtmz7hDF_8IovDFpwzaqmL349fcSaJ6mpE9hphiIVkg42fmpubW8mf9mLcsTBl4-Y66OzdLTzDDRgkZd2ZQoXD5CbA8IGQKwKC4j5rcRcTuct4k0dNx0vqw06CZASh1qbTC0ciaMVySL2bUPxfRCkGp/w640-h360/sam-altman-ai-industry-benefits-explained.jpg.png" title="Sam Altman on AI Industry and Its Benefits" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;
  September 5, 2026&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the artificial int&lt;br /&gt;elligence industry has a communication problem: companies building increasingly powerful AI systems have not done enough to explain what the technology can actually do for ordinary people.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Speaking with Bloomberg Television on Thursday, Altman said the AI industry has done a “terrible job” communicating the benefits of artificial intelligence. He also included OpenAI in that criticism, acknowledging that his own company has not done enough to explain the technology's potential.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The comments come as the AI industry faces growing public scrutiny over job disruption, massive data-center investments, energy use, cybersecurity and the concentration of technological power. Bloomberg reported that local opposition has blocked or delayed dozens of US data-center projects this year, adding pressure on AI companies to make a clearer case for their investments. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For Altman, that case should not rely only on futuristic promises. He believes AI companies need to show how the technology can give individuals more power to create, build businesses and accomplish things that previously required large teams or specialized expertise.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Did Sam Altman Say About AI?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Altman's criticism was unusually direct because it was aimed at the broader AI industry as well as OpenAI itself.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;“I think the industry has done a terrible job of this on the whole,” Altman said during the Bloomberg interview. He added that &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bis-researchers-test-xrp-ledger-official-statistics.html"&gt;OpenAI&lt;/a&gt; had also done a bad job, although he suggested the company may have performed better than some competitors and worse than others. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Altman argued that the industry has not done a good enough job explaining how AI could expand creativity and entrepreneurship.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is an important shift in emphasis. Much of the public conversation around AI has focused on automation, artificial general intelligence, job losses and the possibility of machines becoming dramatically more capable.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Altman wants another part of the story to receive more attention: what happens when powerful AI tools become available to millions of individuals.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Altman Says AI Should Give People More Power&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;One of the strongest themes in Altman's comments was individual autonomy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;He said it is very important to OpenAI that the technology gives people “more power and more autonomy, not less.” &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The argument goes beyond productivity. If AI can help people write software, launch businesses, analyze information, conduct research or create products, then capabilities once restricted to large organizations could become accessible to individuals and small teams.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That could potentially change entrepreneurship in a significant way.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A person with a business idea, for example, may increasingly be able to use AI to handle tasks that previously required programmers, designers, researchers or large support teams. Whether that potential becomes a widespread reality remains an open question, but it is central to the optimistic case Altman is making for AI.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Ordinary People May Not Be Convinced Yet&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The challenge for AI companies is that technological progress does not automatically translate into public support.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;AI developers often discuss benchmarks, model capabilities, computing infrastructure and future breakthroughs. Those subjects are important inside the technology industry, but they do not necessarily answer the question most people care about: &lt;strong&gt;What does AI actually do for me?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For some workers, the first noticeable effect of AI may be automation or pressure to become more productive. For communities near proposed data centers, the discussion may be about electricity, water, infrastructure or local economic impact.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That creates a communications gap.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;AI companies can see enormous long-term possibilities while the public may be dealing with much more immediate questions about employment, privacy, misinformation and control.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;AI's Benefits Go Beyond Curing Cancer&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Altman also argued that the industry's case for AI should go beyond pointing to major scientific achievements.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Breakthroughs in medicine, including the possibility of helping treat serious diseases, would obviously be significant. But Altman's broader argument is that AI should eventually improve everyday human capability as well.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That could include helping people become more creative, allowing entrepreneurs to build companies faster and giving individuals access to expertise that was previously expensive or difficult to obtain.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In other words, the value of AI does not have to come from one spectacular scientific breakthrough.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It could also come from millions of smaller improvements happening across businesses, schools, research organizations and individual lives.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Public Backlash Is Making the Message More Important&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Altman's comments arrive at a time when the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/south-korea-tokenize-stocks-bonds-funds-2027.html"&gt;AI industry's&lt;/a&gt; infrastructure expansion is facing resistance.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bloomberg reported that at least 75 US data-center projects worth roughly $130 billion were blocked or delayed by local opposition during the first three months of 2026, according to Data Center Watch. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That opposition illustrates why communicating the benefits of AI has become more than a public-relations exercise.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;AI companies need enormous amounts of computing power to train and operate increasingly capable systems. That means their expansion increasingly intersects with local communities, electricity markets and infrastructure planning.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If communities do not see a clear connection between those investments and tangible benefits, resistance can become easier to understand.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;AI Risks Are Still Part of the Conversation&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Altman's comments should not be interpreted as saying that AI risks are unimportant.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The same technology that can increase productivity and creativity can also create new problems. Cybersecurity, privacy, misinformation, labor-market disruption and the control of increasingly autonomous systems remain major concerns.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In fact, the more capable AI becomes, the more important responsible deployment becomes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The challenge for the industry is therefore not simply to promote AI. It is to explain its benefits while acknowledging legitimate concerns and demonstrating that users will have meaningful control over how the technology affects their lives.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Altman's Message Matters for OpenAI&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For OpenAI, Altman's remarks are particularly significant because the company is one of the most visible organizations in the AI industry.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI has helped move generative AI from a specialist technology into a mainstream consumer product category. But greater visibility also means greater scrutiny.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The company's latest generation of AI systems is being developed at a time when expectations are extremely high. Users want more capable &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/small-crypto-transactions-are-draining.html"&gt;models&lt;/a&gt;, while governments, businesses and the public want stronger assurances around safety and accountability.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That makes communication increasingly important.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;OpenAI cannot simply demonstrate that a model is more capable. It also has to explain why that capability matters and how people can use it without losing control over important decisions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Creativity and Entrepreneurship Could Become AI's Strongest Selling Point&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Altman's emphasis on creativity and entrepreneurship points toward a different vision for AI.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Instead of viewing AI primarily as software that replaces existing tasks, the technology could increasingly become a tool that allows people to attempt things they previously could not afford or did not have the skills to accomplish.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A small business could use AI for research, customer support and software development. An independent creator could use it to produce content and prototypes. A researcher could use AI to process large amounts of information more quickly.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;None of those possibilities guarantees economic success. But they illustrate the broader argument Altman is making: AI could expand the number of people capable of turning ideas into reality.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Question Is Who Benefits From AI&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Perhaps the most important part of Altman's comments is the question of power.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If advanced AI is controlled by a small number of companies and governments, public concerns about concentration of power are unlikely to disappear simply because the technology becomes more capable.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Altman acknowledged that people can reasonably become concerned if they believe AI leaders want to concentrate power rather than distribute it.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That creates a fundamental test for the industry.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If AI is genuinely going to give people more autonomy, access to those capabilities will matter just as much as the capabilities themselves.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Comes Next for the AI Industry?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The next phase of the AI race may involve more than building larger or more capable models.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Companies will also have to demonstrate practical value.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That means showing real examples of AI helping people solve problems, create products, learn skills, conduct research and build businesses. It also means being honest about limitations and risks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Altman's comments suggest that the industry itself recognizes the gap between technological progress and public understanding.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The companies that successfully close that gap may have an advantage as AI becomes more deeply integrated into everyday life.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Sam Altman says the AI industry has failed to explain its benefits clearly enough, and he includes OpenAI in that criticism.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;His argument is that the public should hear more about how AI can increase individual creativity, entrepreneurship, power and autonomy—not just about futuristic breakthroughs or the risks associated with increasingly powerful systems.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The message comes at a critical time for the industry. AI companies are investing billions in infrastructure while facing growing questions about jobs, energy, safety and who ultimately controls the technology.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For Altman, convincing people that AI can improve their lives may now be almost as important as making the technology itself more capable.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What did Sam Altman say about the AI industry?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Sam Altman said the AI industry has done a “terrible job” explaining the benefits of artificial intelligence. He also acknowledged that OpenAI has not communicated those benefits well enough. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What benefits of AI did Sam Altman highlight?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Altman emphasized AI's potential to support creativity and entrepreneurship while giving people more power and autonomy. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Why is the AI industry facing public backlash?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;The industry faces concerns involving job disruption, data-center expansion, energy use, cybersecurity, privacy and the concentration of technological power.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Does Altman believe AI should only focus on scientific breakthroughs?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;No. He believes major scientific breakthroughs could be valuable, but he also wants the industry to demonstrate how AI can improve everyday creativity, entrepreneurship and individual capabilities.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Does Altman's statement mean AI has no risks?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;No. His comments focused on how the industry communicates AI's benefits. They do not remove concerns about cybersecurity, employment, privacy, safety or other potential risks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Why are Altman's comments important?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;They show that AI companies are increasingly aware that technological progress alone may not be enough to win public trust. Companies also need to demonstrate how AI benefits ordinary users while addressing legitimate concerns about its impact.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Sources&lt;/h2&gt;

    <title>Coinbase CEO Says Crypto's Financial Access Revolution Is Still Underrated</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiSoAgdzWip37NdfLLRFF-Wad3XjxYrtK9yaLmyyoGcXXO_X-GEbV66D-RChrt09jdybCOMEEEWEMv_k8mtwRHs71SxbB2TK81vL-h-sDxQwuxLNigboBongQsPuold2ZgVGWvlljjDPJdofs-r80Z4MaUhX90ryyilgDfh-IceI5c93eGXwl1D1rljffa6/s1536/Coinbase%20CEO%20Brian%20Armstrong%20says.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong crypto financial access revolution stablecoins DeFi tokenized stocks" border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="213" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiSoAgdzWip37NdfLLRFF-Wad3XjxYrtK9yaLmyyoGcXXO_X-GEbV66D-RChrt09jdybCOMEEEWEMv_k8mtwRHs71SxbB2TK81vL-h-sDxQwuxLNigboBongQsPuold2ZgVGWvlljjDPJdofs-r80Z4MaUhX90ryyilgDfh-IceI5c93eGXwl1D1rljffa6/w320-h213/Coinbase%20CEO%20Brian%20Armstrong%20says.png" title="Coinbase CEO Says Crypto's Financial Access Revolution Is Still Underrated | CoinaiNews" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aug 10, 2026&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;– Brian Armstrong has a message for
the financial world: crypto isn't getting enough credit for what it's already
achieved.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The Coinbase CEO recently outlined how stablecoins,
decentralized finance, tokenized assets, and Bitcoin have quietly built a
parallel financial system that operates around the clock, costs relatively
little, and serves anyone with a smartphone&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"Crypto does not receive enough credit for the
financial access it has already unlocked globally," Armstrong said.
"Stablecoins have brought the dollar onchain, making it possible to send
and hold a low-inflation currency at any time, for just a fraction of a
cent"&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;How Stablecoins Changed the Game&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Armstrong's core argument starts with stablecoins — digital
dollars that live on blockchain networks&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The economics are simple. Traditional cross-border transfers
can take days and carry significant fees. A stablecoin transfer can settle in
minutes, any time of day or night, at relatively low network costs&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For countries with unstable currencies or limited banking
infrastructure, that's not just convenient — it's transformative. Anyone with
internet access can hold a digital dollar, send it globally, and bypass the
delays and costs of conventional banking rails&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;DeFi, Tokenized Stocks, and Bitcoin: The Access Trifecta&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Armstrong highlighted three other areas where crypto is
expanding financial access&amp;nbsp;:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Decentralized Finance:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Many DeFi protocols let
users lend, borrow, and earn interest without traditional gatekeepers. Smart
contracts handle the trust function that banks once monopolized, though most
platforms still require crypto collateral rather than credit history&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Tokenized Stocks:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Armstrong argued that
blockchain-based equity tokens could give approximately four billion
"unbrokered" people — those without brokerage accounts — exposure to
U.S. stocks&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bitcoin:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;With its fixed supply, Bitcoin offers
an alternative store of value that can't be inflated away, giving people in
countries with weak currencies a wealth-preservation option outside the
traditional banking system&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Eight Upgrades Still Needed&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Armstrong also laid out an eight-point agenda for what comes
next, writing on X that "jobs not done until we get these working for
all"&amp;nbsp;:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;/td&gt;

  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Different datasets show the tokenized-asset market
continuing to expand, with one estimate putting the sector at approximately
$33.78 billion in May 2026&amp;nbsp;, while Bernstein reported the market had
crossed $51 billion in June&amp;nbsp;. Differences in methodology and asset
coverage can produce different market-size estimates.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Coinbase has also expanded its blockchain-based payment
infrastructure through x402, while its Agentic.market initiative enables AI
agents to discover and pay for services using USDC&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What This Means for Crypto Adoption&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Armstrong's argument is notable for its clarity — and its
limits.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;He's not saying crypto will replace the financial system.
He's saying it has already built a parallel system that addresses real
problems: slow payments, limited access, high costs, and inflation risk. That
system is live, it works, and it's growing&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The challenge, as he acknowledges, is policy and
infrastructure. Stablecoins need regulatory clarity. Tokenized assets need
legal frameworks. Self-custody needs consumer protections&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But the foundation is there — and Armstrong's argument is
that the industry should be credited for building it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Brian Armstrong Says CLARITY Act Could Protect Consumers From Government Overreach</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjkkiTNVlJHMwPOUKRmBFzhn7NiKWv6QOho5NdS7hscsjVIBRWfjk8OrPGrENsGYf6CH0Nnpef_rKcIlr0Om62TLrDjZi115TVbqx6RttHHW1ap4FTRKwpeKl7q4SCLp-5tIVJ5XwUyI0U4cBJeO5yUTfYcNG165J977tjVhvp0MXYvJj-Oen-gAVsTgEzU/s1672/Brian%20Armstrong%20Discusses%20CLARITY%20Act%20and%20Crypto%20Regulation.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Brian Armstrong discussing the CLARITY Act and U.S. crypto regulation" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjkkiTNVlJHMwPOUKRmBFzhn7NiKWv6QOho5NdS7hscsjVIBRWfjk8OrPGrENsGYf6CH0Nnpef_rKcIlr0Om62TLrDjZi115TVbqx6RttHHW1ap4FTRKwpeKl7q4SCLp-5tIVJ5XwUyI0U4cBJeO5yUTfYcNG165J977tjVhvp0MXYvJj-Oen-gAVsTgEzU/w400-h225/Brian%20Armstrong%20Discusses%20CLARITY%20Act%20and%20Crypto%20Regulation.png" title="Brian Armstrong Discusses CLARITY Act and Crypto Regulation" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/i&gt; |&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong is making his message clear:
the U.S. crypto industry needs clearer rules, and he believes the CLARITY Act
could provide a path toward them.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Armstrong argues that today's regulatory uncertainty is
hurting everyday Americans. "The current status quo today is that there
isn't much clarity about what the rules are. And so we are seeing a lot of
ordinary Americans get harmed by using some of these products," he said in
a CBS News interview. The CLARITY Act, in his view, would provide stronger
consumer protections while also shielding the industry from what he describes
as "bad government or overreach."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But it's not just about safety. Armstrong also sees the bill
as a necessary safeguard against future scandals like the FTX collapse. The
bill would establish clearer regulatory responsibilities if enacted, with the
goal of strengthening oversight and reducing regulatory gaps.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Senate is expected to take up a key procedural vote—a
cloture vote—on the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/coinmarketcap-sparks-speculation-with.html"&gt;CLARITY Act&lt;/a&gt; on September 15. This procedural step would end
debate and allow the bill to proceed, requiring 60 votes to advance. Armstrong
has expressed confidence about the bill's prospects, saying he expects it to
get more than 60 votes in the Senate—but the road hasn't been easy. Earlier
versions faced pushback over ethics provisions, concerns about privacy, and
opposition from traditional banking figures.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The ethics clause remains one of the biggest sticking
points. The White House has been involved in efforts to address the ethics
concerns that have become a major obstacle to the bill. In July, a White House
official confirmed that the administration had agreed to an ethics provision,
described as "the most comprehensive and wide-ranging ethics provision in
history." However, details remain under negotiation, and Democrats have
expressed concerns that the rules do not go far enough to address the Trump
family's crypto ventures.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Despite the hurdles, Armstrong remains optimistic. He has
said that roughly 90% of the bill has bipartisan agreement, and he believes a
compromise is within reach. "We can't let banks kill their competition at
the expense of American consumers," he said, urging all sides to come
together.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Armstrong's broader argument is that regulatory clarity is
necessary, whether it ultimately comes through legislation or agency action. In
his view, a law passed by &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/will-us-actually-buy-bitcoin-for-its.html"&gt;Congress&lt;/a&gt; would be more durable and harder to reverse
than regulations written by federal agencies.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Source:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong in a CBS
News interview, August 2026.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Can Your BTC Address Reveal Your Name? The Truth</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;
  &lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhmerpxoFjK6jaT5S-vxmfC0VLE-6TZNmuEcUO1M5kmTSNMtCtxqQz5jyNHtSjY1y1wMyzeb2aNuWz9FIb8byPB_69ft2sDrJWkvLS89i7N1ZILzFrotLe96dw_0N6e8b9lDQcKTwbr-l15EUJnSa8VZ3L0urAbhatP3NwMl5qu9sCPENeSl-CeVkFfYFeJ/s1733/can-bitcoin-address-reveal-your-name-btc-privacy-2026.webp" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Can a Bitcoin address reveal your real name? BTC privacy and identity tracking" border="0" data-original-height="908" data-original-width="1733" height="336" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhmerpxoFjK6jaT5S-vxmfC0VLE-6TZNmuEcUO1M5kmTSNMtCtxqQz5jyNHtSjY1y1wMyzeb2aNuWz9FIb8byPB_69ft2sDrJWkvLS89i7N1ZILzFrotLe96dw_0N6e8b9lDQcKTwbr-l15EUJnSa8VZ3L0urAbhatP3NwMl5qu9sCPENeSl-CeVkFfYFeJ/w640-h336/can-bitcoin-address-reveal-your-name-btc-privacy-2026.webp" title="Can Your BTC Address Reveal Your Name? Bitcoin Privacy Explained" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;Can someone find your real name from a Bitcoin address?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt; Not from the address alone. A Bitcoin address does not contain your name, phone number, home address, or other direct personal information.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But that does not mean Bitcoin transactions are completely anonymous.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin transactions are recorded on a public blockchain, where addresses, transaction amounts and transaction histories can be examined. If an address becomes connected to a real person through an exchange, website, social media account, merchant, or other information, the blockchain history associated with that address can potentially be linked back to that person.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That distinction is the key to understanding Bitcoin privacy: &lt;strong&gt;the address itself does not reveal your name, but other information can connect the address to your identity.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Does a Bitcoin Address Contain Your Name?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;No.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A normal Bitcoin address is essentially a destination for receiving bitcoin. It is not a personal identification number containing your name or government-issued identity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org notes that Bitcoin addresses are created privately by wallets and that the identity behind an address remains unknown until information connects it to a person or entity. Bitcoin transactions themselves, however, are publicly recorded and permanently stored. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For example, suppose someone gives you this fictional address:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;bc1qexampleaddress123...&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Looking at that address alone does not tell you whether it belongs to Alice, Bob, a company, an exchange, or someone else.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The situation changes when additional information connects the address to a real-world identity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin Is Pseudonymous, Not a Name-Based Payment System&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin does not require every transaction to display the user's legal identity. Instead, the blockchain records addresses and transaction data.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is why Bitcoin is commonly described as &lt;strong&gt;pseudonymous&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;You can see an address and follow its transactions without automatically knowing the person's name. But once an address is associated with a known individual or organization, its public transaction history can provide additional information about that address.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin Design similarly describes Bitcoin data as pseudonymous and points out that blockchain transactions, signatures and addresses remain publicly accessible. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Six Ways a Bitcoin Address Can Become Linked to Your Name&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The important question is therefore not simply, “Can someone look at my BTC address and see my name?”&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The more useful question is:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;What information could connect that address to me?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;1. A KYC Cryptocurrency Exchange&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is one of the clearest examples.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Suppose you purchase Bitcoin through a regulated &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-same-btc-address-appear-twice-real.html"&gt;cryptocurrency exchange &lt;/a&gt;and complete identity verification. The exchange may have information connecting your customer account with cryptocurrency addresses used for deposits or withdrawals.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The blockchain itself does not necessarily contain your name. The identity connection can come from the exchange's records.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Once an address is associated with a known customer or service through appropriate evidence, investigators or analytics providers may be able to combine that information with blockchain transaction history.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;2. You Publicly Post Your Bitcoin Address&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Sometimes people voluntarily publish their &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/forgot-your-btc-password-heres-honest.html"&gt;Bitcoin addresses.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A business may put a donation address on its website. A creator might post one on social media. A project may publish an address for community contributions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If the address is publicly displayed next to a person's name, the connection is obvious.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org specifically warns that publishing an address publicly can reduce privacy unless public transparency is the intention, such as with donations. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Once that association is public, anyone can inspect the blockchain history connected with the address.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;3. You Post the Address on Social Media&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A social-media post can create the same connection.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Imagine someone writes:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;“Send BTC donations to this address.”&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If the post is connected to a personal account, the blockchain address can now be associated with the account owner.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Even if the person later deletes the post, copies, screenshots, archived pages, or previously observed blockchain activity may preserve the connection.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;4. You Reuse the Same Bitcoin Address&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Address reuse can make transaction histories easier to correlate.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If the same receiving address is used repeatedly, anyone who knows that address can potentially observe its previous and subsequent on-chain activity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org recommends using a new address for each payment, while Bitcoin Design also notes that address reuse reduces privacy because transactions become easier to associate with the same recipient. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This does not mean address reuse automatically reveals a person's name. It means that once the address becomes associated with an identity, more of its transaction history may become relevant to that identity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;5. Blockchain Analysis Can Connect Related Addresses&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A single Bitcoin address does not necessarily represent everything a person controls.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Modern blockchain analysis can examine transaction patterns and identify addresses that may be under common control.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;One important technique on Bitcoin is &lt;strong&gt;address clustering&lt;/strong&gt;. When multiple addresses are used together as inputs in a transaction, analysts can sometimes infer that they are controlled by the same party.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Chainalysis describes clustering as the structural process of grouping addresses that are likely under common control. It also emphasizes that clustering and identifying the real-world entity behind those addresses are separate steps. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That distinction matters.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Clustering does not automatically mean “this is John Smith.”&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It can indicate that several addresses may belong to the same controlling party. Additional evidence is needed to connect that group to a named individual or organization.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;6. Merchant, Business or Legal Records Can Create the Connection&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A Bitcoin address can also become identifiable through information outside the blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For example, a company could publish its payment address on an official website. A merchant could associate a payment with a customer account. A service provider could maintain transaction records. Investigators could obtain relevant records through legal processes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;These sources can provide the missing link between a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/openai-calls-for-global-ai-standards-as.html"&gt;blockchain address&lt;/a&gt; and a real-world identity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;How Blockchain Analysts Connect an Address to an Entity&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There is an important difference between &lt;strong&gt;following blockchain activity&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;identifying the person behind it&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The first can often be done directly from public blockchain data.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The second generally requires additional evidence.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Chainalysis describes wallet attribution as combining on-chain analysis with off-chain evidence to connect cryptocurrency addresses or wallet clusters to real-world entities. Examples of off-chain evidence can include direct service interactions, KYC information obtained through appropriate legal processes, seized infrastructure, third-party confirmation and publicly available information. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In other words, blockchain data can show &lt;strong&gt;what happened&lt;/strong&gt;, while other evidence may help establish &lt;strong&gt;who was behind it&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Address Clustering Is Not the Same as Knowing Your Name&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is one of the most misunderstood parts of Bitcoin privacy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Suppose an analyst determines that addresses A, B and C are likely controlled by the same entity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is a clustering conclusion.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It does not automatically establish whether the entity is:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;an individual person&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;a company&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;a cryptocurrency exchange&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;a payment processor&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;a service provider&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;another organization&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;To attach a real-world name, additional evidence is required. Chainalysis explicitly separates the structural clustering process from attribution to a named entity. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;A Bitcoin Address Can Be Connected to a Person Without Belonging to That Person&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There is another subtle issue that is easy to miss.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A Bitcoin address can be associated with a particular user while being part of infrastructure controlled by another organization.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For example, a centralized exchange may operate wallet infrastructure and provide deposit addresses to customers. The customer may be the beneficiary of the funds, while the exchange controls the underlying wallet infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Therefore, blockchain analysis has to distinguish between the &lt;strong&gt;operator&lt;/strong&gt; of wallet infrastructure and the &lt;strong&gt;beneficiary&lt;/strong&gt; using it.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is one reason why simply placing a person's name next to a blockchain address can be an oversimplification.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Information Is Public on the Bitcoin Blockchain?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;

          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Potentially yes&lt;/td&gt;

  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Does a New Bitcoin Address Hide Your Identity?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Using a fresh address for each incoming on-chain payment can improve privacy, but it is not a guarantee of anonymity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Modern Bitcoin wallets can generate many addresses from the same wallet structure. This allows users to receive payments at different addresses without publicly exposing a single address for every transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org recommends generating a new address for each payment, and Bitcoin Design describes fresh receiving addresses as an important privacy practice. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;However, users can still create connections between addresses through their own transactions, public disclosures, exchange activity, or other information.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;So a new address should be viewed as a &lt;strong&gt;privacy improvement&lt;/strong&gt;, not a promise that nobody can ever connect your transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Happens If You Move Bitcoin Between Your Own Addresses?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Moving bitcoin between addresses you control can sometimes create additional on-chain information that analysts can examine.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org specifically warns that moving funds from a publicly disclosed address to another address can publicly connect the histories of those addresses. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin Design also notes that using separate wallets can help isolate activity, while transfers between those wallets may provide information that allows observers to connect them again. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is why simply creating dozens of addresses does not automatically make all activity unrelated.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Can Someone See How Much Bitcoin You Have?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Someone who knows a particular Bitcoin address can inspect the bitcoin associated with that address and its transaction history on the public blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But that does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; necessarily tell them how much bitcoin the person behind that address owns in total.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A user may control multiple addresses, wallets or accounts. Conversely, an address may be operated by a service rather than an individual.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Therefore, the balance of one address should not automatically be treated as the person's complete Bitcoin holdings.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Can Blockchain Analysis Find the Person Behind Every Bitcoin Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;No.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Some addresses can be strongly associated with identifiable people or organizations because of public information or other evidence. Others may remain difficult to attribute.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Blockchain analysis can reveal transaction relationships and patterns, but identity attribution depends on the quality and availability of evidence outside the blockchain as well. Chainalysis itself distinguishes on-chain clustering from the separate process of attributing a cluster to a named real-world entity. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That means it would be inaccurate to say that every Bitcoin address can automatically be traced to a person's legal name.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;How to Improve Bitcoin Transaction Privacy&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Users concerned about ordinary financial privacy can take several practical steps:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Use a new receiving address for new on-chain payments when supported by your wallet.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Avoid publicly posting addresses unless public transparency is intentional.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Be careful about linking blockchain addresses to personal social-media accounts.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Understand what information an exchange or payment service can associate with your transactions.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Keep separate financial activities separated when appropriate.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Remember that blockchain transactions are permanent and publicly observable.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;These practices can reduce unnecessary exposure, but none should be interpreted as a guarantee of complete anonymity. Bitcoin Design emphasizes that there is no perfect privacy solution and that privacy depends on how wallets and transactions are used. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can someone find my name from my Bitcoin address?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Not from the address alone. A name may become associated with the address if additional information connects it to you, such as exchange records, public posts, merchant records or other evidence.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Are Bitcoin addresses anonymous?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin addresses do not inherently contain a user's name, but Bitcoin transactions are publicly recorded. Bitcoin is therefore better understood as pseudonymous rather than a system that guarantees anonymity. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can a Bitcoin transaction be traced?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin transactions are publicly recorded and can be followed through the blockchain. Determining who controls the addresses involved is a separate attribution question.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can an exchange identify a Bitcoin address?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;An exchange may have records connecting customer activity with cryptocurrency addresses. Whether a particular address can be confidently attributed depends on the available evidence.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Does reusing a Bitcoin address reveal my name?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;No. Address reuse does not automatically reveal a person's name, but it can make transactions easier to correlate. If the address later becomes linked to an identity, its visible history can become more revealing. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can blockchain analysis connect multiple Bitcoin addresses?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Yes, analysts can use on-chain patterns such as common-input relationships to identify addresses that may be under common control. This is known as address clustering. Clustering alone does not establish the owner's legal identity. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Does a new Bitcoin address make me anonymous?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;No. Fresh addresses can improve privacy, but other information can still create connections between transactions or addresses.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can someone see my entire Bitcoin balance from one address?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;They can inspect the balance and history of that address, but they cannot automatically know how much Bitcoin you control across every other address or wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Your Bitcoin address does not automatically reveal your real name.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But the Bitcoin blockchain is public, and transaction histories remain available for analysis. If an address becomes connected to your identity through an exchange, public website, social media, merchant, address reuse, or other evidence, that connection can make the associated blockchain activity easier to investigate.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The most accurate way to think about Bitcoin privacy is simple:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Your name is not written inside your Bitcoin address, but your actions can create the connection between the address and your identity.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is why address management, careful public disclosure and an understanding of how on-chain and off-chain information interact are important parts of Bitcoin privacy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Editorial note: This article explains Bitcoin privacy concepts for educational purposes. Blockchain attribution depends on the evidence available in a particular case and should not be treated as automatic identification from an address alone.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/article&gt;
</content>

    <title>Bitcoin’s $15.6 Billion Options Expiry: What Traders Are Watching After Settlement</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;br /&gt;&lt;article&gt;&lt;header&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgKex8LvbFikzxcMYrmHezvk7gbDxELtvhQ5MQyU64Q9rywivdAuMSRke9wQjx6Pgd_q9GZtqM-80vrS7KPxLtx4r3kqqIpPx49qnkU5zuSw6W2TIEK-xkd1HXBol1XuZhbhhCiypt9bQaSPur0VX-P3-hOgZncJiqLruOWjSX2YkmeyFi5UZ3VFDzUQP2t/s1672/bitcoin-15-6-billion-options-expiry-september-2026.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin $15.6 billion options expiry and crypto derivatives market on September 25, 2026" border="0" data-original-height="940" data-original-width="1672" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgKex8LvbFikzxcMYrmHezvk7gbDxELtvhQ5MQyU64Q9rywivdAuMSRke9wQjx6Pgd_q9GZtqM-80vrS7KPxLtx4r3kqqIpPx49qnkU5zuSw6W2TIEK-xkd1HXBol1XuZhbhhCiypt9bQaSPur0VX-P3-hOgZncJiqLruOWjSX2YkmeyFi5UZ3VFDzUQP2t/s1600/bitcoin-15-6-billion-options-expiry-september-2026.webp.png" title="Bitcoin $15.6 Billion Options Expiry" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;Bitcoin traders are looking beyond one of the cryptocurrency market’s biggest derivatives events of the month after a large block of BTC options reached its scheduled Deribit expiry on Friday.&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;A Deribit market snapshot cited by Decrypt showed roughly &lt;strong&gt;182,000 BTC&lt;/strong&gt; in Bitcoin options scheduled for the September 25 expiry, representing approximately &lt;strong&gt;$15.6 billion in notional value&lt;/strong&gt;. The snapshot included about &lt;strong&gt;106,200 BTC in calls&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;75,900 BTC in puts&lt;/strong&gt;, putting the reported put-to-call ratio near &lt;strong&gt;0.71&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;It is important to put that headline number into context. The $15.6 billion figure represents the notional value of the Bitcoin underlying the contracts. It does not mean $15.6 billion in cash suddenly moved into or out of the Bitcoin spot market.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;With the Deribit contracts now reaching their scheduled expiry, attention is shifting toward what happens to liquidity, hedging flows, open interest and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/what-happens-when-ai-agent-runs-out-of.html"&gt;Bitcoin’s&lt;/a&gt; price after the expiring positions disappear or are rolled into later-dated contracts.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/header&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;Why This Bitcoin Options Expiry Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin options are derivatives that give traders the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell BTC at a predetermined strike price.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Calls generally provide exposure to higher prices, while puts provide exposure to lower prices or can be used as portfolio protection. Professional traders also use options for volatility strategies, hedging and combinations of multiple contracts.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;That is why a call-heavy options book should not automatically be interpreted as a simple bet that Bitcoin will rise.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;What made this expiry notable was the amount of open interest reaching settlement within the same window. When large positions expire, market makers and other participants may need to adjust or remove hedges associated with those contracts.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The result can be a noticeable change in market liquidity even though the options expiry itself does not determine Bitcoin’s next direction.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;About 182,000 BTC Was Represented in the Expiring Contracts&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The Deribit snapshot reported by Decrypt showed approximately &lt;strong&gt;182,000 BTC&lt;/strong&gt; in open Bitcoin options scheduled for the September 25 expiry.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;ul&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;106,200 BTC&lt;/strong&gt; in call options&lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;75,900 BTC&lt;/strong&gt; in put options&lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;About 0.71&lt;/strong&gt; put-to-call ratio&lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;About $15.6 billion&lt;/strong&gt; in notional value&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;/ul&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The structure therefore contained substantially more call exposure than put exposure in the reported snapshot.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;However, options positioning needs to be interpreted carefully. A trader may buy a call as a directional position, while another participant may sell that call as part of a market-making or hedging strategy. The same contract can therefore serve different purposes for different market participants.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The reported size also changed as the expiry approached. A later September 24 market snapshot cited by TheStreet put the expiry at approximately &lt;strong&gt;185,908 BTC and $16 billion&lt;/strong&gt;, with 110,747 calls and 75,160 puts. This difference illustrates why options-expiry figures should be treated as time-sensitive market snapshots rather than permanent numbers.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;What the $15.6 Billion Figure Actually Means&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The $15.6 billion number is a &lt;strong&gt;notional value&lt;/strong&gt;, not a cash settlement figure.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Notional value measures the amount of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/what-are-tokenized-bank-deposits-how.html"&gt;Bitcoin represented&lt;/a&gt; by the outstanding contracts. Depending on the final settlement price and individual strike prices, some options can expire with value while others can expire worthless.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Therefore, it would be incorrect to describe the expiry as $15.6 billion of capital flowing directly into or out of Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The more useful question is how traders and market makers adjust their positions once the contracts are no longer active.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;$76,000 Max Pain Was an Important Reference Level&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Another widely watched figure in the earlier Deribit snapshot was the &lt;strong&gt;$76,000 max-pain level&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;In options markets, max pain refers to the theoretical price at which the largest amount of options would expire worthless. Traders often monitor the level because it provides a snapshot of where option open interest is concentrated.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;It is important, however, not to treat max pain as a guaranteed &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-cant-circle-reverse-stolen-usdc-on.html"&gt;Bitcoin price target.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Decrypt reported the $76,000 max-pain level in its September 23 snapshot, when Bitcoin was trading substantially above it. Later market reporting cited a $75,000 maximum-pain level, showing that this figure can also change as the options book develops.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;For that reason, the max-pain figure in this article is presented as a &lt;strong&gt;reported snapshot&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than as a fixed forecast for Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;The $70,000 Strike Had the Largest Concentration&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The most heavily concentrated strike in the reported Deribit book was &lt;strong&gt;$70,000&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Deribit data cited by Decrypt showed approximately &lt;strong&gt;8,705 BTC in calls&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;7,653 BTC in puts&lt;/strong&gt; at the $70,000 strike.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Other large call concentrations included approximately &lt;strong&gt;7,222 BTC at $90,000&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;6,950 BTC at $100,000&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;On the put side, approximately &lt;strong&gt;5,571 BTC&lt;/strong&gt; was concentrated around $60,000, while another &lt;strong&gt;4,257 BTC&lt;/strong&gt; was positioned around $75,000.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;These levels are useful for understanding the structure of the options book, but they should not be interpreted as guaranteed support or resistance levels for spot Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;How Dealer Hedging Can Influence Short-Term Trading&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;One reason large options expiries can affect market conditions is dealer hedging.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Market makers that sell options can acquire exposure to Bitcoin’s price movements. To manage that exposure, they may buy or sell BTC or related derivatives as the market moves.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;For example, when a dealer is short certain call exposure and Bitcoin rises, the dealer may need to increase its hedge by buying Bitcoin. If Bitcoin falls, the required hedge can move in the opposite direction.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;These transactions can contribute to short-term market flows, particularly around heavily concentrated strikes.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Once an option expires, however, the associated hedge can disappear, be reduced or be transferred into another expiration. That is why traders often watch the market immediately after a major expiry rather than focusing only on the settlement itself.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin Entered the Expiry After an Eight-Month High&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The options event arrived after a strong move in Bitcoin’s spot market.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin reached an &lt;strong&gt;eight-month high near $87,400&lt;/strong&gt; on Monday before cooling from that level. Decrypt subsequently reported Bitcoin trading around &lt;strong&gt;$84,490&lt;/strong&gt; in its September 24 market snapshot.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The exact intraday high can vary slightly between market-data feeds, which is why the article uses “near $87,400” rather than presenting that figure as an exact universal exchange price.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The price figures are market snapshots rather than permanent levels. Bitcoin can move substantially within hours, particularly around major derivatives settlements and macroeconomic releases.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;Fed Policy Is Another Variable for Bitcoin Traders&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The options expiry is also occurring against a changing U.S. interest-rate backdrop.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The Federal Reserve raised its target federal funds range by &lt;strong&gt;25 basis points on September 16&lt;/strong&gt;, bringing the target range to &lt;strong&gt;3.75%–4.00%&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;As of the September 24 market snapshot, CME FedWatch showed traders pricing roughly &lt;strong&gt;75% odds of another rate hike in October&lt;/strong&gt; and approximately &lt;strong&gt;59% odds for a December hike&lt;/strong&gt;. These were market-implied probabilities at that specific snapshot, not guarantees of future Federal Reserve decisions.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;For Bitcoin traders, changes in interest-rate expectations can influence broader liquidity and risk appetite. A shift in Treasury yields or the U.S. dollar can also affect how investors position across risk assets.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;U.S. Economic Data Adds Another Test&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The options expiry is not happening in isolation.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;U.S. &lt;strong&gt;durable goods data&lt;/strong&gt; and the University of Michigan’s final September consumer-sentiment reading are scheduled around the same period, while CME’s September Bitcoin futures also reach their scheduled settlement later on Friday.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;That creates several potential sources of volatility within a relatively short window.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;If economic data changes expectations for Federal Reserve policy, Bitcoin could react to the macro news independently of the options expiry. That makes it difficult to attribute any single price move entirely to derivatives settlement.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;Deribit Settlement Has Already Taken Place&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Deribit’s scheduled Bitcoin options expiry occurs at approximately &lt;strong&gt;08:00 UTC&lt;/strong&gt;. Deribit states that options expiring at that time are cash-settled using the official delivery price, with no physical delivery of Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Because that settlement window has now passed on September 25, traders are shifting attention toward the positioning that remains in the market after the expiring contracts are removed.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;CME’s September Bitcoin futures settlement is scheduled later in the day at approximately &lt;strong&gt;15:00 UTC&lt;/strong&gt;, providing another derivatives event for the market to absorb.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The key question is no longer simply where Bitcoin trades relative to the September 25 options strikes. Instead, traders can watch how open interest, funding rates and volatility develop after the expiry.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;What Traders Are Watching After the Expiry&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Several indicators can provide a clearer picture of the market’s next phase:&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;ul&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin spot price:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether BTC stabilizes or continues to move sharply after settlement.&lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Trading volume:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether activity increases or declines after the large expiry passes.&lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Futures open interest:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether traders rebuild leveraged positions.&lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Funding rates:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether perpetual futures positioning becomes more expensive for longs or shorts.&lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Options open interest:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether traders move exposure into October and later expiries.&lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Implied volatility:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether traders expect larger or smaller future price swings.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;/ul&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;These measures can provide more information about the post-expiry market than the headline size of the contracts alone.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;What the Options Expiry Does Not Tell Traders&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;A large options expiry does not provide a reliable standalone signal for Bitcoin’s next move.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The call-heavy structure does not guarantee a rally. The reported max-pain level does not mean BTC must move toward that price. Likewise, the $70,000 strike concentration does not establish a future support level.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Options markets contain hedges, spreads, market-making positions and strategies involving multiple maturities. Looking at one statistic without the wider positioning can therefore produce an incomplete picture.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The actual market reaction depends on spot demand, derivatives positioning, liquidity, macroeconomic data, interest-rate expectations and broader risk sentiment.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;Key Bitcoin Options Numbers&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Picture for Bitcoin&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The September 25 options expiry was large enough to attract significant attention, but its importance goes beyond the $15.6 billion headline.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Roughly 182,000 BTC of reported options exposure reached the scheduled expiry in the earlier Deribit snapshot, with calls substantially outnumbering puts. The options book also contained major concentrations at $70,000, $90,000 and $100,000.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;As the expiry passed, the market moved into the next stage of positioning. Traders can now watch whether options exposure is rebuilt at later expiries and whether futures open interest, funding and volatility change.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin’s recent move to an &lt;strong&gt;eight-month high near $87,400&lt;/strong&gt; also placed the derivatives event within a broader market context. At the same time, changing Federal Reserve expectations and U.S. economic data remain important variables for risk assets.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;For traders and investors following Bitcoin, the next signal may therefore come less from the headline size of the expiry and more from what happens to open interest, liquidity, volatility and spot demand after the contracts have settled.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin’s September 25 Deribit options expiry involved approximately &lt;strong&gt;182,000 BTC&lt;/strong&gt; in the market snapshot that put the notional value near &lt;strong&gt;$15.6 billion&lt;/strong&gt;. Calls accounted for about 106,200 BTC versus 75,900 BTC in puts, while the earlier Deribit snapshot showed max pain at $76,000.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The $70,000 strike carried the largest reported concentration, with significant additional call exposure at $90,000 and $100,000. These figures help explain where options positioning was concentrated, but they do not provide a guaranteed forecast for Bitcoin’s next price move.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;With the Deribit expiry now behind the market, attention turns to post-expiry positioning, the CME futures settlement, U.S. economic data and the Federal Reserve rate outlook.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;The key development to watch is how Bitcoin’s derivatives market rebuilds after the large block of September contracts disappears from the books.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/section&gt;

    <title>Liquid Hack Takes a New Turn as Blockstream Rejects 10% Demand and 598 BTC Remains Missing</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgcgnr1hdPWeqh7oTPXFdnvj88cXfF_90yeIUxnXLVq7i1IibWU3fxnsPO76uhNTi3hp7kWxzcn__Er29oyFTJxEvHHrimVHpfXIrSH_IQS8KjZXbjPTt4aVCalGfrPbdQR0OIrikKaunnyvaaVYJNJb9Ax_LqtWC3rV4VaQ1ENipB8W5BGJZ5PV_y40v9h/s1672/liquid-network-hack-blockstream-598-btc-ransom.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Liquid Network hack leaves 598 BTC outstanding as Blockstream rejects ransom demand" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgcgnr1hdPWeqh7oTPXFdnvj88cXfF_90yeIUxnXLVq7i1IibWU3fxnsPO76uhNTi3hp7kWxzcn__Er29oyFTJxEvHHrimVHpfXIrSH_IQS8KjZXbjPTt4aVCalGfrPbdQR0OIrikKaunnyvaaVYJNJb9Ax_LqtWC3rV4VaQ1ENipB8W5BGJZ5PV_y40v9h/w640-h360/liquid-network-hack-blockstream-598-btc-ransom.jpg.png" title="Liquid Network Hack and Blockstream Ransom Dispute" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;The $320 million Liquid Network exploit has taken another turn after Blockstream rejected a demand for a 10% payment while roughly &lt;strong&gt;598 BTC remains outstanding&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The development comes after the actors behind the incident returned approximately &lt;strong&gt;3,400 BTC&lt;/strong&gt; to Liquid's Federation wallet. That represented about 85% of the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/okx-launches-openai-and-anthropic-pre.html"&gt;Bitcoin withdrawn&lt;/a&gt; during the attack, but hundreds of millions of dollars worth of crypto remain at the center of the dispute.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The incident began earlier this week when roughly &lt;strong&gt;4,000 BTC&lt;/strong&gt; was withdrawn from Liquid's Federation wallet. The Bitcoin was worth about $320 million at the time. Liquid subsequently paused parts of its network while Blockstream and other participants worked to identify and fix the underlying vulnerability. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Blockstream Refuses to Pay for the Remaining Bitcoin&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest dispute is no longer simply about recovering stolen Bitcoin. It is now about whether the people who exploited the vulnerability should receive a financial reward for returning most of the funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The actors involved in the incident described themselves as white-hat hackers and returned 3,400 BTC after the affected infrastructure was patched. However, approximately 598 BTC remained under their control.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockstream has rejected the idea of paying for the return of the remaining Bitcoin, taking the position that unauthorized removal of assets followed by a demand for compensation should not be treated as a conventional security bounty.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters because the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/metaplanet-shareholders-push-back-as.html"&gt;crypto industry&lt;/a&gt; has long relied on bug bounties and responsible disclosure programs to encourage researchers to report vulnerabilities without exploiting them for personal gain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;About 4,000 BTC Was Pulled From Liquid's Federation Wallet&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The scale of the original incident made it one of the most significant crypto security events of September.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Liquid reported that approximately 4,000 BTC had been withdrawn from a Federation wallet that contained roughly 4,200 BTC. Reuters reported the value of the withdrawn Bitcoin at approximately $320 million when the incident occurred. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The withdrawals were processed through SideSwap's settlement infrastructure. Liquid said the cryptographic key used in the process was not compromised, shifting attention toward the software and transaction-processing mechanisms surrounding the system rather than a straightforward private-key theft. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Liquid subsequently disabled bridge nodes and paused new transactions while the security problem was investigated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
