    <title>P2P vs. Bank Transfers: Which Crypto Deposit Method Actually Makes Sense for Regular Users?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjLGw_8s6F3h_eWlI5d1RgTZ6VoCTEmL4rT-xCj-ThjadeANP6i4LR8zIituFQWPDHkq0sbkv2astQUp3Gdvo8xnAwYAYVGzMap6D2hPCwSPSYTfHzT7OWz6wonhK4LY8AtWpT6pDO1-D4N1JqsTd7oCvYjPkgrHcicuBcmiuqwaaudMwREWVFnWvhsSTlP/s1536/p2p-vs-bank-transfers-crypto-deposit-method.png.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="P2P vs bank transfers for crypto deposits, comparing speed, fees, flexibility, and convenience" border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="213" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjLGw_8s6F3h_eWlI5d1RgTZ6VoCTEmL4rT-xCj-ThjadeANP6i4LR8zIituFQWPDHkq0sbkv2astQUp3Gdvo8xnAwYAYVGzMap6D2hPCwSPSYTfHzT7OWz6wonhK4LY8AtWpT6pDO1-D4N1JqsTd7oCvYjPkgrHcicuBcmiuqwaaudMwREWVFnWvhsSTlP/w320-h213/p2p-vs-bank-transfers-crypto-deposit-method.png.png" title="P2P vs. Bank Transfers: Crypto Deposit Comparison" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;You've got crypto sitting on an exchange. You want to cash
out, or maybe you want to load up. The question is never just "what's the
price" – it's "what's the fastest way to get my money in or out
without getting eaten alive by fees?"&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If you've been in crypto long enough, you've probably tried
both sides: the clean, one-click bank transfer that takes three days to settle,
and the P2P route where you're haggling with a stranger on the other side of
the world.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;So which one actually wins? The answer depends on what
"winning" means to you.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Speed Test: P2P vs. Traditional Banking&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bank transfers are simple, but they are not fast.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If you withdraw via ACH in the US, it can take 1–3 business
days under standard processing. Coinbase's standard ACH withdrawal takes the
same 1-3 days after processing. SEPA in Europe can clear in a day, but it's
still not instant unless you're using SEPA Instant. Standard crypto-to-bank
methods just aren't built for speed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;P2P is faster, but not always immediate.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Binance P2P can process in minutes if your seller is
responsive. The actual transaction happens the moment the seller releases the
crypto, but that release depends on the seller verifying your payment. Some
sellers take 15 minutes, others take hours.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;On Bybit, experienced sellers with a 95% rating and high
completion rates can process within 15 minutes. But the entire process –
finding a seller, matching, sending payment, waiting for release – can stretch
from 10 minutes to over an hour.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The winner:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;P2P can be faster when a suitable
seller is available and responsive, while bank transfers offer more predictable
processing times.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Fee Comparison: Where the Real Cost Hides&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bank transfers are cheap – but not always.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;ACH is practically free (0–1% in fees). The trade-off is
time. If you can wait, bank transfers are the cheapest way to move fiat.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;But credit cards change the equation.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If you're depositing via card, you're looking at 3-4% in
fees. That's the cost of "instant" processing, and it adds up fast. A
$5,000 deposit costs you $150-200 just in &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/how-ai-is-making-blockchain-fraud.html"&gt;payment &lt;/a&gt;fees.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;P2P is more complex.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Binance P2P charges 0% taker fees. Bybit often advertises
zero-fee P2P trading for eligible fiat pairs, but fees can vary by currency,
advertiser level and payment method.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But there's a catch – you're paying a spread. Sellers set
their own prices, so the effective cost can appear as a spread rather than a
separately listed trading fee. Plus, the seller sets a minimum and maximum
order size (e.g. $100 to $500 per order). If you're moving large amounts, you
may need to split into multiple orders or find a merchant with higher limits.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The winner:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Bank transfers are cheaper if you
have the time. P2P is cheaper than credit cards but comes with hidden costs in
the spread.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Convenience: The Real Decider&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bank transfers require no negotiation.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;You click "deposit," enter the amount, and wait.
No searching for a seller, no checking their rating, no waiting for someone to
confirm they received your payment. It's boring, predictable, and doesn't
require social interaction.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;P2P is a marketplace, not a button.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;You need to:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol start="1" style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="1"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Find
     a seller with a good rating (95%+ recommended)&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Check
     their payment methods (&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/can-stolen-crypto-be-recovered-yes-but.html"&gt;Binance&lt;/a&gt; supports over 1,000 local options)&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Verify
     they have a high transaction count&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Send
     the payment and wait for confirmation&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bybit supports bank transfers, cards, Google Pay, Apple Pay,
and crypto deposits. P2P adds flexibility: you can pay with local bank
transfers, digital wallets, even cash in some regions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The winner:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Bank transfers are simpler. P2P is
more flexible, but only if you're willing to manage the extra complexity.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Where Toobit Fits&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Toobit now offers P2P trading alongside other fiat on-ramp
options. Its P2P marketplace supports local payment methods and escrow
protection, while the platform says P2P trading currently carries zero fees.
Users can compare offers by price and payment method before placing an order.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bottom Line: Which One Should You Use?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;If you value simplicity above all else:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Use a
bank transfer and wait 1-3 days. It's predictable, cheap, and requires no
interaction.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;If you need speed but don't want credit card fees:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;P2P
can be a strong option. You'll get faster settlement than ACH, but you need to
factor in seller responsiveness and the spread.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;If you're moving small amounts regularly:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;P2P
can work well, especially if you find a reliable seller with good rates. The
lower fees per transaction add up.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;If you're moving large amounts:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Compare the P2P
spread with your available bank-transfer and card options before choosing. A
lower advertised fee does not always mean a lower overall cost.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There's no single winner. Bank transfers are cheap and
simple. P2P is flexible and often faster. The choice depends on what you value
more – time or convenience.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

    <title>Duelbits Crypto Hack: $7 Million Drained as Platform Goes Offline</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article style="color: #222222; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; line-height: 1.75; max-width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgpaiQPClAl-3EDAnEYGAWR6KHuqsaBw7SWwsAMS3hFd05mDIvat9Jx0m6tBWHrm7q-GAxNCJkw_Owq8KRPa8Aeotq3MiHgHWE23ivy_oeiQZ973BWhixs5SdXkpXjUut5t6w8q91kr3_86_VLVGIiVIf41hwdqe_Zmrqp7nZ1RSUDuSqpsAFTwESIWpqEJ/s1672/duelbits-crypto-hack-7-million-hot-wallet-breach.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Duelbits crypto casino goes offline after a reported $7 million hot wallet hack" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgpaiQPClAl-3EDAnEYGAWR6KHuqsaBw7SWwsAMS3hFd05mDIvat9Jx0m6tBWHrm7q-GAxNCJkw_Owq8KRPa8Aeotq3MiHgHWE23ivy_oeiQZ973BWhixs5SdXkpXjUut5t6w8q91kr3_86_VLVGIiVIf41hwdqe_Zmrqp7nZ1RSUDuSqpsAFTwESIWpqEJ/s1600/duelbits-crypto-hack-7-million-hot-wallet-breach.jpg.png" title="Duelbits Crypto Hack: $7 Million Hot Wallet Breach" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Crypto betting platform &lt;strong&gt;Duelbits&lt;/strong&gt; has taken its website offline after confirming a major security breach that drained millions of dollars from its hot wallets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Initial reports put the value of the stolen cryptocurrency at approximately &lt;strong&gt;$7 million&lt;/strong&gt;. However, blockchain-security firm SlowMist's incident database currently records about &lt;strong&gt;$4.9 million&lt;/strong&gt; transferred to newly created addresses. The difference appears to reflect changing asset valuations, additional transfers and the fact that investigators are still tracking the incident.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The attack affected Duelbits' hot-wallet infrastructure across multiple blockchain networks. Security researchers have identified suspicious transactions involving &lt;strong&gt;Ethereum, BNB Chain, Tron and Bitcoin&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Duelbits co-founder Joe confirmed the incident and said the company was investigating exactly what happened and how the attackers gained access.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The platform has remained offline while the investigation continues and the company works on replenishing its affected wallets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This makes the Duelbits incident one of several significant crypto-security events reported within a very short period, following the much larger Bitget breach disclosed on September 24.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happened to Duelbits?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The first signs of the attack came from blockchain monitoring systems that detected unusual outflows from wallets associated with Duelbits.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to reporting from CoinDesk and other security-focused publications, attackers drained assets from Duelbits' hot wallets and moved the funds to newly created addresses. CoinDesk reported the stolen value at approximately &lt;strong&gt;$7 million&lt;/strong&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SlowMist's incident database provides a more conservative on-chain figure of approximately &lt;strong&gt;$4.9 million&lt;/strong&gt; transferred from the affected wallets. It lists the suspected attack method as a &lt;strong&gt;private-key compromise&lt;/strong&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because the investigation is still developing, the dollar amount should be treated as an estimate rather than a final confirmed loss figure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Duelbits subsequently took the platform offline while its team investigated the breach.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Which Blockchains Were Affected?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The incident was not limited to a single blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Security researchers identified suspicious activity involving Duelbits wallets connected to &lt;strong&gt;Ethereum, BNB Chain, Tron and Bitcoin&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is significant because a multi-chain hot-wallet environment can increase the complexity of incident response. Investigators must monitor multiple networks, identify related addresses and determine whether the same attacker controls the receiving &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ondo-surges-nearly-30-what-is-driving.html"&gt;wallets&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SlowMist specifically lists Ethereum, BSC, Tron and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/solana-options-expiry-why-sol-is.html"&gt;Bitcoin &lt;/a&gt;in its incident record for Duelbits. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AmbCrypto also reported that suspicious transfers were initially detected on BNB Chain, Ethereum and Tron before an additional Bitcoin wallet outflow was identified. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the $7 Million Figure Is Different From SlowMist's $4.9 Million&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the most important details when reporting the Duelbits hack is the difference between the headline loss estimate and the amount currently tracked by blockchain-security researchers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Several reports describe the incident as a roughly &lt;strong&gt;$7 million hack&lt;/strong&gt;. CoinDesk, for example, reported that attackers drained approximately $7 million from Duelbits' hot wallets. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SlowMist's current hacked-project database, however, lists approximately &lt;strong&gt;$4.9 million&lt;/strong&gt; as the amount transferred to newly created addresses. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These numbers should not automatically be treated as contradictory.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto-security investigations often produce changing estimates because token prices move rapidly, some transfers may be discovered later and different researchers may calculate the value at different points in time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For that reason, this article uses &lt;strong&gt;approximately $7 million&lt;/strong&gt; when describing the broader media-reported incident while separately identifying SlowMist's currently tracked $4.9 million figure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Was a Private Key Compromised?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The leading technical theory is a private-key compromise affecting Duelbits' hot-wallet infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SlowMist currently categorizes the incident as &lt;strong&gt;Private Key Leakage&lt;/strong&gt;. Its incident record says the multi-chain hot wallets suffered a suspected private-key compromise and that approximately $4.9 million was transferred to newly created addresses, with most of the funds subsequently swapped into ETH. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not mean the final root cause has been conclusively established.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Duelbits co-founder Joe said the company was still investigating &lt;strong&gt;exactly what happened and how&lt;/strong&gt;, indicating that the technical investigation was not complete when the incident was publicly confirmed. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The distinction matters because a compromised private key, leaked credentials, malware infection or another operational-security failure can produce similar on-chain symptoms while requiring very different remediation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happened to the Stolen Crypto?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchain investigators have been tracking the funds after they left Duelbits-controlled wallets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to current reporting, a large portion of the stolen assets was consolidated and converted into Ethereum.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One report said approximately &lt;strong&gt;2,234 ETH&lt;/strong&gt;, worth close to $6 million at the time of reporting, had been consolidated into a single Ethereum address and remained there. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SlowMist similarly reported that most of the funds it tracked were swapped into ETH. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This type of consolidation can make an incident easier for &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitcoins-156-billion-options-expiry.html"&gt;blockchain analysts&lt;/a&gt; to monitor because multiple stolen assets end up in fewer addresses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, tracking cryptocurrency does not automatically mean that the funds can be recovered.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can the Stolen Funds Be Frozen?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The answer depends on the type of cryptocurrency involved.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Native assets such as &lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin and Ether&lt;/strong&gt; generally cannot be frozen at the blockchain-protocol level simply because investigators identify them as stolen.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recovery can instead depend on the attacker attempting to move the funds through centralized exchanges, custodial services or other identifiable intermediaries.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Some stablecoins work differently because their issuers can have address-freezing capabilities under specific circumstances.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means investigators may have more options for certain stablecoin assets than they do for native cryptocurrencies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The ultimate recovery prospects therefore depend heavily on where the stolen funds move next and whether investigators can connect those movements to identifiable services or individuals.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Duelbits Takes the Platform Offline&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Following the breach, Duelbits took its platform offline.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company's co-founder said the team was investigating the incident and that operations would resume after the investigation and wallet-replenishment process were completed. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The decision to shut down the platform is significant because hot wallets are normally used to process routine deposits and withdrawals.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Keeping the platform offline can limit additional exposure while the company checks wallet infrastructure and determines whether other operational systems have been affected.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the time of publication, Duelbits had not provided a final technical explanation for how the attackers gained access.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Are User Funds Safe?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Duelbits has said that user funds remain safe, according to reporting on the incident.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, users should distinguish between a company's statement about customer balances and an independently verified forensic assessment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The investigation is still underway, and the platform remains offline while the company examines the breach.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Until a full incident report is released, the precise scope of the compromise should be treated as developing information.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Hot Wallets Are a Security Risk&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Duelbits incident illustrates a basic trade-off in cryptocurrency custody.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hot wallets are connected to online systems and allow platforms to process transactions quickly. That makes them useful for exchanges, payment platforms and crypto casinos that need to handle frequent deposits and withdrawals.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The same connectivity can also increase their exposure to cybersecurity threats.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A cold wallet is generally kept offline or otherwise isolated from routine online operations. That can make direct remote attacks more difficult, although cold storage does not eliminate every form of security risk.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For platforms handling significant amounts of cryptocurrency, the challenge is therefore not simply deciding between hot and cold storage. Security also depends on key management, access controls, transaction approvals, monitoring systems and procedures for detecting unusual transfers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Duelbits Hack Comes During a Busy Day for Crypto Security&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Duelbits breach did not happen in isolation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On the same day, blockchain-security researchers also reported major incidents involving &lt;strong&gt;Bitget, Meter Passport and Payy Network&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Protos reported that three separate crypto and DeFi incidents on Thursday resulted in more than &lt;strong&gt;$11 million&lt;/strong&gt; in combined losses, including approximately $7 million at Duelbits, $2.3 million involving Meter and $1.8 million at Payy Network. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitget's separate incident was considerably larger, with the exchange reporting approximately $351.6 million in affected assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The concentration of security incidents within such a short period highlights how quickly risk can spread across different parts of the digital-asset ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Investigators Will Look For Next&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next stage of the Duelbits investigation will focus on identifying the initial point of compromise.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Investigators will likely examine how the attackers obtained access to the hot-wallet keys, whether the same credentials were used across multiple blockchain networks and whether any other wallets remain exposed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They will also continue following the stolen assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchain transactions provide a permanent public record, which allows researchers to monitor the receiving addresses even after the initial theft.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important question is what happens when the funds reach services that can identify customers or potentially intervene in transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Duelbits' eventual technical report should also clarify whether the incident resulted from a direct private-key leak, an operational-security failure or another form of compromise.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the Duelbits Hack Does Not Prove&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The current evidence does not establish every detail of the attack.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In particular, the suspected private-key compromise remains the current security-research classification rather than a final forensic conclusion from Duelbits.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The incident also does not establish that every asset held by Duelbits was exposed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Similarly, the approximately $7 million media figure should not be interpreted as a final audited loss figure while blockchain researchers continue updating their estimates.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These distinctions are important because crypto-security incidents can evolve quickly as additional addresses and transactions are identified.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Duelbits Hack: Key Facts at a Glance&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Incident&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The &lt;strong&gt;Duelbits crypto hack&lt;/strong&gt; has taken the platform offline after attackers drained millions of dollars from its hot-wallet infrastructure across multiple blockchain networks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Current media reports describe the incident as an approximately &lt;strong&gt;$7 million hack&lt;/strong&gt;, while SlowMist's incident database currently tracks approximately &lt;strong&gt;$4.9 million&lt;/strong&gt; transferred to newly created addresses. The difference reflects the developing nature of the investigation and changing crypto valuations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Security researchers currently classify the incident as a suspected &lt;strong&gt;private-key compromise&lt;/strong&gt;, but Duelbits has not yet published a complete technical explanation of the root cause.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The attackers appear to have consolidated much of the stolen cryptocurrency into Ethereum, giving blockchain investigators identifiable addresses to monitor.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Duelbits has taken the platform offline and said it is investigating the incident before replenishing its wallets and resuming operations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The biggest unanswered question is therefore not simply how much cryptocurrency was stolen, but &lt;strong&gt;how the attackers gained control of the hot-wallet infrastructure and whether the security weakness has been completely contained&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;The Duelbits investigation is ongoing, and loss estimates, wallet movements and technical findings may change as additional information becomes available.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Why Is My Bitcoin Transaction Still Pending After 2 Hours?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEim_r6QBi-4dM_51q0zA2AZCbXrgGqFdsj3XBRng5Dhm4M9vaclB3LzthGE5lFjdOpLirGCbebtUhgSbZKbHUfrDOLr_t68_UA_wz1HQgrwqP8gJPeZSzz07DJtChZ1g81SW7vJom4lDawp4ZXAoIy21H1J93FRe-FGwXNSJXNButjGOFM5D6VBY-_RZ0hQ/s1670/bitcoin-transaction-pending-after-2-hours.jpg.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin transaction still pending after two hours while waiting for confirmation" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1670" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEim_r6QBi-4dM_51q0zA2AZCbXrgGqFdsj3XBRng5Dhm4M9vaclB3LzthGE5lFjdOpLirGCbebtUhgSbZKbHUfrDOLr_t68_UA_wz1HQgrwqP8gJPeZSzz07DJtChZ1g81SW7vJom4lDawp4ZXAoIy21H1J93FRe-FGwXNSJXNButjGOFM5D6VBY-_RZ0hQ/w640-h360/bitcoin-transaction-pending-after-2-hours.jpg.png" title="Why Is My Bitcoin Transaction Still Pending After 2 Hours?" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;You sent Bitcoin two hours ago. The transaction has a transaction ID, but your wallet still says &lt;strong&gt;pending&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is an easy situation to panic over, especially if the Bitcoin was supposed to arrive quickly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The good news is that &lt;strong&gt;a Bitcoin transaction being pending for two hours does not automatically mean something is wrong&lt;/strong&gt;. In most cases, the transaction is waiting because its fee rate is not competitive enough for the current demand for block space, or because the network has not yet included it in a block.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin transactions do not have a guaranteed confirmation time. A transaction can confirm relatively quickly, while another transaction with a lower fee rate can remain unconfirmed for much longer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you want the deeper explanation of why Bitcoin transactions stay pending, see our guide: &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-is-my-bitcoin-transaction-still_0394756778.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;Why Is My Bitcoin Transaction Still Pending?&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Quick Answer: Why Is My Bitcoin Transaction Still Pending After 2 Hours?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The most common reason is a low fee rate relative to the transactions currently competing for Bitcoin block space.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When you send BTC, miners do not simply process transactions in the order they were created. Fee rate is an important factor in deciding which transactions are attractive to include in a block.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your transaction was sent with a relatively low fee, it may remain in the mempool while transactions offering higher fee rates are confirmed first.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Other possibilities include:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The Bitcoin network is experiencing higher demand for block space.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Your wallet estimated a fee that turned out to be too low for current conditions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The transaction is large and therefore requires more total fees at the same fee rate.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Your wallet or exchange has not fully broadcast the transaction yet.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The transaction is eligible for RBF and can be replaced with a higher-fee version.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The recipient may be able to use CPFP to increase the effective fee rate.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Is Two Hours Too Long for a Bitcoin Transaction?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No. Two hours is not automatically too long.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's block production is probabilistic, and confirmation depends on when miners include a transaction in a block and how competitive its fee rate is at that time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A transaction with a strong fee rate may confirm quickly. A transaction with a low fee rate can wait considerably longer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Mempool.space explains that a transaction that remains unconfirmed for a while is often using a lower fee rate relative to other transactions in the mempool. It also notes that users can sometimes accelerate transactions through RBF or CPFP. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So seeing &lt;strong&gt;"pending"&lt;/strong&gt; after two hours should not by itself be interpreted as a failed Bitcoin transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does "Pending" Mean in Bitcoin?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A pending Bitcoin transaction generally means the transaction has been created and broadcast but &lt;strong&gt;has not yet been confirmed in a Bitcoin block&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;After a wallet signs a transaction, it is propagated across the Bitcoin network. Nodes may accept it into their local mempools, where it waits for a miner to include it in a block.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Until that happens, the transaction remains unconfirmed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is an important distinction:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 680px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Status&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Meaning&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Pending / Unconfirmed&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Transaction has not yet been &lt;br /&gt;included in a block.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Confirmed&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Transaction has been included &lt;br /&gt;in a Bitcoin block.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Multiple confirmations&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Additional blocks have been &lt;br /&gt;built on top of the transaction's block.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The First Thing to Check: Your Fee Rate&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your Bitcoin transaction has been pending for two hours, the first technical detail worth checking is its &lt;strong&gt;fee rate&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin transaction fees are normally expressed in &lt;strong&gt;satoshis per virtual byte (sat/vB)&lt;/strong&gt;. The fee rate matters because block space is limited and miners have an economic incentive to select transactions that offer attractive fees for the space they consume.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why two transactions sending completely different amounts of BTC can have very different confirmation experiences.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A transaction sending $10 worth of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/what-happens-if-bitcoin-transaction.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt; can theoretically pay more than a transaction sending $10,000 if the smaller transaction has a higher data size or fee rate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The amount being transferred is not the primary measurement used to determine how much block space the transaction occupies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How to Check Your Bitcoin Transaction Fee&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You normally need your &lt;strong&gt;transaction ID, also called a TXID&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Enter the TXID into a reputable Bitcoin block explorer or mempool explorer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Look for:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Current fee rate in sat/vB&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Total transaction fee&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Transaction size or virtual size&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Number of confirmations&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether the transaction is still unconfirmed&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether an RBF replacement has occurred&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Mempool.space provides transaction lookup and current fee-rate information, although its estimates are guidance rather than guarantees of a particular confirmation time. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why a Low Fee Can Keep Bitcoin Pending&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin blocks have limited capacity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When demand for block space increases, more transactions compete for inclusion. A transaction paying a relatively low fee rate can therefore spend more time waiting in the mempool.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Think of it like a busy airport.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If there are only a limited number of seats and hundreds of people want to fly, airlines have limited capacity. In Bitcoin, block space is the limited resource and transactions compete for that space through their fee rates.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This does not mean that a low-fee transaction can never confirm. It means the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-bitcoin-transaction-get-stuck.html"&gt;transaction&lt;/a&gt; may have to wait until the fee environment becomes favorable enough or until miners choose to include it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can Bitcoin Transactions Take More Than 2 Hours?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no universal rule that says a Bitcoin transaction must confirm within 10 minutes, one hour or two hours.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The commonly quoted Bitcoin block interval is only an average. Individual blocks can arrive sooner or later, and your transaction also competes with other transactions for inclusion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means a transaction can remain pending for several hours without indicating that the Bitcoin network itself has failed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is the Mempool Doing While My Transaction Is Pending?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The mempool is where nodes keep valid unconfirmed transactions that they are willing to relay and potentially make available for mining.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is not one single global mempool containing every pending Bitcoin transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Different nodes can have somewhat different transaction sets depending on what they have received and their local policy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why a transaction can sometimes appear on one mempool service but temporarily be missing from another.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For a pending transaction, the important question is whether it is still being relayed and whether its inputs remain available for the transaction to confirm.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is RBF and Can It Speed Up a Pending Bitcoin Transaction?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;RBF stands for Replace-by-Fee.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If a transaction is eligible for replacement, the sender may be able to create a replacement transaction with a higher fee.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The idea is simple:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;You send a Bitcoin transaction with a relatively low fee.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The transaction remains unconfirmed.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Your wallet allows fee bumping through RBF.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A replacement transaction is created with a higher fee.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The replacement competes for confirmation instead of the original transaction.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Mempool.space specifically recommends RBF as one possible way to accelerate a stuck transaction when the original transaction was created with RBF enabled. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Whether you can use RBF depends on the wallet and transaction circumstances, so the safest approach is to use your wallet's built-in fee-bump function rather than manually creating another transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If My Transaction Does Not Support RBF?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not necessarily mean you are stuck forever.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Another mechanism is &lt;strong&gt;CPFP, or Child Pays for Parent&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With CPFP, a new transaction spends an output from the unconfirmed transaction and attaches a sufficiently high fee. The combined fee economics of the parent and child can make the package more attractive to miners.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;CPFP is particularly relevant when the recipient controls an output from the unconfirmed transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Again, the exact availability depends on the wallet and transaction structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;RBF vs CPFP: What's the Difference?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 720px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Feature&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;RBF&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;CPFP&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Full name&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Replace-by-Fee&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Child Pays for Parent&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Basic idea&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Replace the unconfirmed transaction with a higher-fee version.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Add a child transaction with a fee that helps the package get confirmed.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Usually controlled by&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Sender&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Sender or recipient, depending on transaction outputs&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Cancels Bitcoin?&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;No. It replaces an unconfirmed transaction under applicable rules.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;No. It helps the original transaction package confirm.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could the Bitcoin Network Simply Be Busy?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Network demand changes constantly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When many users are competing for block space, the fee rate required for a quick confirmation can rise. During quieter periods, transactions with lower fee rates may confirm without much waiting.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why the fee rate that looked reasonable when you sent the transaction may no longer be competitive two hours later.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Current mempool conditions can be checked through real-time mempool data rather than relying on an old fee estimate. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does Sending More Bitcoin Make the Transaction More Expensive?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not directly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin transaction fees are primarily related to the amount of transaction data and the fee rate, not simply the number of BTC being transferred.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, a transaction moving a large amount of BTC can sometimes be smaller than a transaction moving a tiny amount if the first transaction uses fewer or more efficient inputs and outputs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the reasons the dollar value of a transaction is not a reliable way to predict its Bitcoin network fee.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If My Exchange Says "Pending" for 2 Hours?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This situation can be different from a normal self-custody Bitcoin transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When you withdraw BTC from an exchange, the exchange may first process your withdrawal internally before broadcasting an on-chain transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In that situation, a status such as &lt;strong&gt;"pending"&lt;/strong&gt; does not necessarily mean the transaction is already sitting in the Bitcoin mempool.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you have a TXID, check it on a block explorer. If you do not have a TXID yet, the exchange may not have broadcast the transaction to the Bitcoin network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For exchange withdrawals, the exchange's own withdrawal status and support documentation are therefore important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If the Transaction Has No TXID?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your wallet or exchange says the transaction is pending but does not provide a transaction ID, you may not yet have an on-chain transaction to inspect.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is an important clue.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ask:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Has the transaction actually been broadcast?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Has the exchange created the withdrawal transaction?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Is the wallet still preparing or signing the transaction?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Is there a TXID available in the transaction details?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Without a TXID, it is much harder to independently verify the transaction's position on the Bitcoin network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Should You Cancel a Bitcoin Transaction After 2 Hours?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Normally, you should not think of a pending Bitcoin transaction as something that has a simple "cancel" button.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction is unconfirmed, the relevant options depend on how it was created.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For an RBF-enabled transaction, the sender may be able to replace it with a higher-fee transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For certain transactions, CPFP may help increase the effective fee rate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction has already been confirmed, normal Bitcoin transactions cannot simply be reversed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Should You Do Right Now?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your Bitcoin transaction has been pending for two hours, follow this checklist before doing anything drastic:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Find the TXID.&lt;/strong&gt; Make sure you have the actual Bitcoin transaction ID.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check confirmations.&lt;/strong&gt; Confirm whether it is still unconfirmed.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check the fee rate.&lt;/strong&gt; Look at the transaction's sat/vB rate.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Compare it with current mempool conditions.&lt;/strong&gt; A fee that was competitive earlier may no longer be competitive.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check whether RBF is available.&lt;/strong&gt; If your wallet supports fee bumping, follow its instructions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check CPFP possibilities.&lt;/strong&gt; This can sometimes help when the recipient controls an appropriate output.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Do not send the payment again immediately.&lt;/strong&gt; First understand what happened to the original transaction.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;If an exchange is involved, check its withdrawal status.&lt;/strong&gt; A pending exchange withdrawal may not yet have been broadcast on-chain.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;When Should You Actually Be Concerned?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Two hours alone is usually not enough to conclude that your Bitcoin is in danger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You should investigate more carefully when:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The transaction has remained unconfirmed for an unusually long period.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The fee rate is far below current market conditions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The transaction disappears from mempool tracking services.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Your wallet shows conflicting information about the transaction.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;An exchange says the withdrawal is complete but there is no visible on-chain transaction.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;You suspect the recipient address was incorrect.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Your wallet reports an error or a conflicting transaction.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In these cases, the TXID is usually the best starting point.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Long Can a Bitcoin Transaction Stay Pending?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no fixed universal maximum confirmation time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A transaction can confirm in the next block, or it can remain unconfirmed much longer if its fee rate is not competitive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In some cases, an unconfirmed transaction can eventually disappear from a node's mempool. That does not necessarily mean the funds are lost; the exact outcome depends on whether the transaction confirmed, was replaced, or was dropped and whether the underlying inputs remain unspent.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why confirmation status is more important than simply counting how many hours have passed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Bitcoin Transactions Do Not Have a Guaranteed Confirmation Time&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin is not a traditional payment processor that promises every transaction will settle within a fixed number of minutes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blocks are produced through the mining process, and block space is limited.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Users effectively compete for that scarce space by attaching fees to their transactions. Miners then decide which transactions to include according to their own transaction-selection policies and economic incentives.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As a result, Bitcoin confirmation time is probabilistic rather than guaranteed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why is my Bitcoin transaction still pending after 2 hours?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most common reason is that its fee rate is too low compared with the transactions currently competing for Bitcoin block space. Network demand, transaction size and wallet or exchange behavior can also affect confirmation time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is it normal for a Bitcoin transaction to take 2 hours?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Two hours does not automatically indicate a failed transaction. A transaction can remain pending when its fee rate is not competitive enough for current conditions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How can I make my Bitcoin transaction confirm faster?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your transaction supports RBF, your wallet may allow you to replace it with a higher-fee transaction. If you control an appropriate output, CPFP may also help increase the effective fee rate. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What fee rate should I use for Bitcoin?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no single fee rate that guarantees confirmation within a specific time. The appropriate rate depends on current mempool demand and how quickly you want the transaction confirmed. Real-time fee estimates can be used as a guide, but they are not guarantees. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can I cancel a Bitcoin transaction that is pending?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no universal cancellation mechanism for an unconfirmed Bitcoin transaction. If the transaction is eligible for RBF, the sender may be able to replace it with another transaction carrying a higher fee.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What happens if my Bitcoin transaction stays pending for a day?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Check the transaction's fee rate, mempool status and whether RBF or another fee-bumping option is available. A long pending period does not automatically mean the Bitcoin is lost.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can a Bitcoin transaction confirm after being pending for several hours?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. If the transaction remains valid and is eventually selected for inclusion in a block, it can confirm even after waiting for several hours.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What if my Bitcoin withdrawal is pending on an exchange?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;First check whether the exchange has provided a TXID. If there is no TXID, the withdrawal may not yet have been broadcast on-chain. If a TXID exists, check its blockchain status independently.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;If your Bitcoin transaction is still pending after two hours, don't panic.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Two hours is not automatically an abnormal confirmation time. The first thing to investigate is the transaction's &lt;strong&gt;fee rate compared with current mempool conditions&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the fee is too low, RBF may allow the sender to replace the transaction with a higher-fee version. In other situations, CPFP can increase the effective fee rate of a transaction package. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most important steps are simple: &lt;strong&gt;find the TXID, check confirmations, inspect the fee rate, compare it with current mempool conditions, and use your wallet's supported fee-bumping tools if necessary.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A pending Bitcoin transaction is frustrating, but in most cases it is a fee-and-block-space problem—not a sign that your Bitcoin has disappeared.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Sources&lt;/h2&gt;

    <title>How Does Blockchain Really Work? The Technology Behind Bitcoin, Ethereum and Digital Assets</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 17px; line-height: 1.75; margin: 0px auto; max-width: 900px; padding: 20px;"&gt;

  &lt;h1 style="font-size: 38px; line-height: 1.25; margin: 0px 0px 20px;"&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEijv7DKR2agl_M0R-LmsDunaDtxMmPED-SZiCrDu-asl7JxDv6xPLJ9dlitDjttKKtLkbAbNfH5h8NoV7F9FP2oXGArCv2cIE3ykUgBmpCl67znSmyZyIOFSj116wCnEkJDWoKm49OWpUj4x5_MW1W4GhIfBU5v0InpPTjuejsX6ulpowCtgQUzfDU0Jabi/s1672/how-blockchain-works-bitcoin-ethereum-explained.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="How blockchain works with Bitcoin, Ethereum, smart contracts and connected blocks" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEijv7DKR2agl_M0R-LmsDunaDtxMmPED-SZiCrDu-asl7JxDv6xPLJ9dlitDjttKKtLkbAbNfH5h8NoV7F9FP2oXGArCv2cIE3ykUgBmpCl67znSmyZyIOFSj116wCnEkJDWoKm49OWpUj4x5_MW1W4GhIfBU5v0InpPTjuejsX6ulpowCtgQUzfDU0Jabi/w400-h225/how-blockchain-works-bitcoin-ethereum-explained.jpg.png" title="How Does Blockchain Really Work? Bitcoin and Ethereum Explained" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;em style="font-size: 17px; font-weight: normal;"&gt;&lt;h1 style="font-size: 38px; line-height: 1.25; margin: 0px 0px 20px;"&gt;&lt;em style="font-size: 17px; font-weight: normal;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;Blockchain is often described as the technology behind Bitcoin. But that explanation only scratches the surface. Behind every blockchain are cryptography, distributed networks, consensus mechanisms, digital signatures, data structures and, on programmable networks, smart contracts.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    So how does blockchain actually work?
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    How can thousands of computers maintain a shared record without relying on one central database? Why is it difficult to secretly change an old transaction? What happens when someone sends Bitcoin? And how can Ethereum support tokens, NFTs and decentralized applications on the same underlying network?
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The answers become much easier to understand once blockchain is broken down into its individual components.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;!--QUICK ANSWER BOX--&gt;
  &lt;div style="background: rgb(245, 245, 245); border-left: 5px solid rgb(247, 147, 26); border-radius: 6px; margin: 28px 0px; padding: 20px;"&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 0px;"&gt;
      &lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Quick Answer:&lt;/strong&gt; A blockchain is a distributed digital ledger in which transactions are grouped into blocks, cryptographically linked, validated according to network rules and replicated across participating nodes. Consensus mechanisms help the network agree on the accepted state, while cryptographic techniques make unauthorized changes detectable and increasingly difficult as more blocks are added.
    &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;h2 style="font-size: 29px; line-height: 1.35; margin-top: 45px;"&gt;
    What Is Blockchain in Simple Terms?
  &lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Imagine a digital record book that is shared among thousands of computers.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Instead of one company keeping the only copy of a database, participating computers can maintain their own copies and independently verify transactions according to the rules of the network.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Transactions are grouped together into blocks. Each block is connected cryptographically to the previous block, creating a chronological chain of records.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That is where the word &lt;strong&gt;blockchain&lt;/strong&gt; comes from:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="margin: 30px 0px; overflow-x: auto; padding: 18px; text-align: center;"&gt;
    &lt;table style="border-collapse: separate; border-spacing: 10px; min-width: 650px; width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;tbody&gt;&lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td style="background: rgb(245, 245, 245); border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); font-weight: bold; padding: 15px; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;Block 1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 0px; font-size: 25px; padding: 5px; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;→&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="background: rgb(245, 245, 245); border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); font-weight: bold; padding: 15px; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;Block 2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 0px; font-size: 25px; padding: 5px; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;→&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="background: rgb(245, 245, 245); border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); font-weight: bold; padding: 15px; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;Block 3&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 0px; font-size: 25px; padding: 5px; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;→&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="background: rgb(245, 245, 245); border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); font-weight: bold; padding: 15px; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;Block 4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
    &lt;/tbody&gt;&lt;/table&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The important idea is not simply that information is stored in blocks. The real innovation is that blockchain combines &lt;strong&gt;shared data, cryptography, distributed computing and consensus&lt;/strong&gt; into one system.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) describes blockchain as a distributed digital ledger that is tamper-evident and tamper-resistant, with transactions grouped into blocks and blocks &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-is-bitcoin-price-rising-so-fast.html"&gt;cryptographically&lt;/a&gt; linked to one another.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2 style="font-size: 29px; line-height: 1.35; margin-top: 45px;"&gt;
    Why Is Blockchain Different From a Normal Database?
  &lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A traditional database can also store transactions, timestamps and records. So why do we need blockchain?
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The biggest difference is the way control and verification are organized.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In a conventional database, a central organization typically controls who can write data, who can change it and which version of the database is considered authoritative.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A public blockchain can distribute these responsibilities across a network of participants. Nodes follow shared rules to validate transactions and determine which blocks or states are acceptable.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This does not mean blockchain eliminates trust completely. Instead, it moves much of the trust model from a single institution toward &lt;strong&gt;protocol rules, cryptography, incentives and network consensus&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2 style="font-size: 29px; line-height: 1.35; margin-top: 45px;"&gt;
    What Exactly Is Inside a Blockchain Block?
  &lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A block is essentially a container for a set of transactions and additional information required by the particular blockchain.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Although the exact structure varies between networks, a simplified model looks like this:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="background: rgb(247, 247, 247); border-radius: 7px; border: 1px solid rgb(170, 170, 170); margin: 25px 0px; padding: 20px;"&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 0px 0px 8px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;Blockchain Block&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 5px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;• Block metadata&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 5px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;• Reference to the previous block&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 5px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;• Transaction information&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 5px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;• Cryptographic verification information&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 5px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;• Consensus-specific information&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin and Ethereum do not use identical block structures, but both use cryptographic mechanisms to connect blockchain history and validate network state.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2 style="font-size: 29px; line-height: 1.35; margin-top: 45px;"&gt;
    What Is a Cryptographic Hash?
  &lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    One of the most important ideas behind blockchain is the &lt;strong&gt;cryptographic hash&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A hash can be thought of as a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/tether-brings-offline-ai-translation-to.html"&gt;digital fingerprint&lt;/a&gt; of data.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    When information is passed through a cryptographic hash function, it produces an output. If the underlying information changes, the resulting hash changes as well.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="background: rgb(247, 247, 247); border-radius: 7px; border: 1px solid rgb(170, 170, 170); margin: 25px 0px; padding: 20px;"&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 5px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Original data&lt;/strong&gt; → Cryptographic hash&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 5px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Modified data&lt;/strong&gt; → Different cryptographic hash&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This property becomes powerful when hashes are used to connect blocks together.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If someone changes information inside an earlier block, the cryptographic information associated with that block can change. That creates an inconsistency with the blocks that follow it.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin's developer documentation explains that each block header contains the hash of the previous block header, creating a cryptographic chain.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2 style="font-size: 29px; line-height: 1.35; margin-top: 45px;"&gt;
    Tamper-Evident vs. Tamper-Resistant: What Is the Difference?
  &lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    These two terms are sometimes treated as if they mean exactly the same thing. They do not.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;!--TABLE 1--&gt;
  &lt;div style="margin: 25px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
    &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); font-size: 16px; min-width: 700px; width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;thead&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;th style="background: rgb(233, 233, 233); border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); font-weight: bold; padding: 14px; text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;
            Term
          &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="background: rgb(233, 233, 233); border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); font-weight: bold; padding: 14px; text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;
            Meaning
          &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="background: rgb(233, 233, 233); border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); font-weight: bold; padding: 14px; text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;
            Blockchain Example
          &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/thead&gt;

      &lt;tbody&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; vertical-align: top;"&gt;
            &lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Tamper-Evident&lt;/strong&gt;
          &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; vertical-align: top;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;
            A change can be detected &lt;br /&gt;if the underlying data or &lt;br /&gt;cryptographic relationships &lt;br /&gt;no longer match.
          &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; vertical-align: top;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;
            Changing an old block can&lt;br /&gt;&amp;nbsp;break the cryptographic &lt;br /&gt;links connecting it to later &lt;br /&gt;blocks.
          &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;

        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="background: rgb(247, 247, 247); border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; vertical-align: top;"&gt;
            &lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Tamper-Resistant&lt;/strong&gt;
          &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="background: rgb(247, 247, 247); border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; vertical-align: top;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;
            The system is designed to &lt;br /&gt;make unauthorized modification difficult.
          &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="background: rgb(247, 247, 247); border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; vertical-align: top;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;
            Distributed copies, &lt;br /&gt;cryptography and consensus&lt;br /&gt;can make rewriting accepted history increasingly difficult.
          &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/tbody&gt;
    &lt;/table&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This distinction matters because saying that blockchain data is simply "impossible to change" can be misleading.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A better description is that blockchain architecture can make unauthorized modification &lt;strong&gt;detectable and difficult&lt;/strong&gt;, depending on the network's design and security assumptions.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2 style="font-size: 29px; line-height: 1.35; margin-top: 45px;"&gt;
    What Is a Merkle Tree and Why Does Blockchain Use It?
  &lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Another important blockchain concept that often gets overlooked is the &lt;strong&gt;Merkle tree&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A Merkle tree is a cryptographic data structure used to summarize a group of transactions into a single value known as the &lt;strong&gt;Merkle root&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Imagine a block containing hundreds or thousands of transactions. Instead of treating all transaction data as one giant piece of information, the transactions can be hashed and then those hashes can be repeatedly combined until one final hash remains.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;!--MERKLE TABLE--&gt;
  &lt;div style="margin: 28px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
    &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); min-width: 600px; text-align: center; width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;tbody&gt;&lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td colspan="4" style="background: rgb(233, 233, 233); border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); font-weight: bold; padding: 13px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;
          Merkle Root
        &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;

      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td colspan="2" style="background: rgb(247, 247, 247); border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 13px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;
          Combined Hash
        &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td colspan="2" style="background: rgb(247, 247, 247); border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 13px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;
          Combined Hash
        &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;

      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 13px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;TX1 + TX2&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 13px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;Hash&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 13px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;TX3 + TX4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 13px;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;Hash&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
    &lt;/tbody&gt;&lt;/table&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The resulting Merkle root is included in the Bitcoin block header. Merkle proofs can allow a client to verify that a transaction was included in a block without downloading and processing every transaction in the entire block.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This makes Merkle trees an important part of efficient blockchain verification.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2 style="font-size: 29px; line-height: 1.35; margin-top: 45px;"&gt;
    How Does a Bitcoin Transaction Actually Work?
  &lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Suppose Alice wants to send Bitcoin to Bob.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    From a user's perspective, the process looks simple: Alice enters Bob's address, chooses an amount and confirms the transaction.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Behind the scenes, several things happen.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ol style="padding-left: 28px;"&gt;
    &lt;li style="margin-bottom: 10px;"&gt;A transaction is created.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li style="margin-bottom: 10px;"&gt;The transaction is authorized using cryptographic information associated with Alice's wallet.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li style="margin-bottom: 10px;"&gt;The transaction is broadcast to the Bitcoin network.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li style="margin-bottom: 10px;"&gt;Network participants verify that the transaction follows &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitcoins-4-year-cycle-may-be-changing.html"&gt;Bitcoin's&lt;/a&gt; rules.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li style="margin-bottom: 10px;"&gt;Valid transactions can be included in a block.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li style="margin-bottom: 10px;"&gt;Bitcoin's Proof-of-Work consensus process determines which valid block becomes part of the accepted chain.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li style="margin-bottom: 10px;"&gt;The block is propagated through the network and becomes part of the blockchain history.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ol&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin's official documentation explains that private keys are used to sign transactions, while mining serves as the network's distributed consensus mechanism for confirming transactions and maintaining chronological order.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2 style="font-size: 29px; line-height: 1.35; margin-top: 45px;"&gt;
    What Does a Private Key Do?
  &lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A private key is one of the most important pieces of information in a cryptocurrency wallet.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    It is not simply a password stored on the blockchain.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In Bitcoin, the private key is used to create a digital signature that provides mathematical evidence that the transaction was authorized by the holder of the corresponding key.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This is why losing control of a private key can mean losing control of the assets associated with it.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2 style="font-size: 29px; line-height: 1.35; margin-top: 45px;"&gt;
    How Does Bitcoin Reach Consensus Without a Bank?
  &lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin does not have a central bank deciding which transaction history should be accepted.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Instead, network participants follow Bitcoin's consensus rules.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin uses &lt;strong&gt;Proof of Work&lt;/strong&gt;. Miners compete to produce blocks that satisfy the network's cryptographic requirements. The network then follows its consensus rules to determine the accepted chain.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The process makes it difficult for a single participant to continuously rewrite history because changing an old block would require rebuilding the subsequent Proof-of-Work chain and competing with the rest of the network.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2 style="font-size: 29px; line-height: 1.35; margin-top: 45px;"&gt;
    How Is Ethereum Different From Bitcoin?
  &lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin and Ethereum both use blockchain technology, but their primary design goals are different.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;!--TABLE 2--&gt;
  &lt;div style="margin: 25px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
    &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); font-size: 16px; min-width: 720px; width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;thead&gt;

          &lt;th style="background: rgb(233, 233, 233); border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;Feature&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="background: rgb(233, 233, 233); border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="background: rgb(233, 233, 233); border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;span style="color: #990000;"&gt;Ethereum&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/thead&gt;
