    <title>Sent BTC to the Wrong Address? What Happens After 10 Years?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi0xthsHQJD1wa3L77d2Wf8IfBFBnJNGeSnJHRbPRbWryQo_syyepV3sUPDEkQjBymIw8b9yvObBGhiCyXtCTUROHGaAl6DeT7AiClyXhP2y1tiE8VEXSoWMvbYTkbFzS90NOOhbt4QzBTcoWAuclZnFSOEiq9QEeOukMUW9TyfePRQ_D0kZeJWh7WSZ8T-/s1734/sent-btc-to-wrong-address-bitcoin-recovery.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin sent to the wrong address and the chances of recovering BTC after 10 years" border="0" data-original-height="907" data-original-width="1734" height="334" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi0xthsHQJD1wa3L77d2Wf8IfBFBnJNGeSnJHRbPRbWryQo_syyepV3sUPDEkQjBymIw8b9yvObBGhiCyXtCTUROHGaAl6DeT7AiClyXhP2y1tiE8VEXSoWMvbYTkbFzS90NOOhbt4QzBTcoWAuclZnFSOEiq9QEeOukMUW9TyfePRQ_D0kZeJWh7WSZ8T-/w640-h334/sent-btc-to-wrong-address-bitcoin-recovery.webp.png" title="Sent BTC to the Wrong Address? Bitcoin Recovery After 10 Years" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;Sending Bitcoin is supposed to be simple: copy an address, enter the amount, check the details and press send.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is one uncomfortable difference between Bitcoin and a traditional bank transfer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;There is no universal undo button.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you send BTC to the wrong address and the transaction is confirmed, waiting a few days, a few months or even 10 years does not automatically reverse it. Bitcoin's official documentation says confirmed transactions are irreversible and can only be refunded by the person or entity controlling the receiving funds. If the address is valid but nobody controls it, the bitcoin can become permanently inaccessible. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That raises a question many Bitcoin users eventually ask:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;If I accidentally sent Bitcoin to the wrong address, could I get it back after 10 years?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The answer depends almost entirely on &lt;em&gt;what kind of wrong address&lt;/em&gt; received the BTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;First, What Does “Wrong Bitcoin Address” Actually Mean?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not every mistaken Bitcoin payment is the same.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You might have:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;sent BTC to another address that you actually control;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;sent BTC to a friend or business but used the wrong address;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;sent BTC to an exchange deposit address incorrectly;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;sent BTC to a valid address controlled by a stranger;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;sent BTC to an address whose private key is lost;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;sent BTC to an address that nobody can currently control;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;or discovered the mistake while the transaction is still unconfirmed.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These situations have very different outcomes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So the idea that “Bitcoin sent to the wrong address is always gone forever” is too broad.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the opposite idea — that waiting long enough will bring it back — is also wrong.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Once a Bitcoin Transaction Is Confirmed?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin transactions are recorded on a public &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ai-crypto-will-humans-become-obsolete.html"&gt;blockchain&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once a transaction is confirmed and becomes part of the chain, the network does not provide a customer-service mechanism that allows the sender to simply cancel it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org describes transactions as irreversible and explains that a confirmed transaction can only be refunded by the recipient. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of Bitcoin's defining characteristics.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no central Bitcoin company that can press a “reverse payment” button.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no bank administrator who can manually move the coins back.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And miners do not have a normal mechanism for cancelling a confirmed payment simply because the sender made a mistake.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If You Notice the Mistake Immediately?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where timing matters.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your Bitcoin transaction is still &lt;strong&gt;unconfirmed&lt;/strong&gt;, the situation can be different from a transaction that has already received confirmations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org explains that transactions accumulate confirmations and become increasingly difficult to reverse as more blocks are added. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, users should not assume that an unconfirmed transaction can simply be cancelled whenever they want. Whether any replacement or fee-management technique is available depends on the transaction, wallet and network conditions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The safest approach is to check the transaction status immediately and avoid sending another transaction based on a mistaken assumption about whether the first one has already been confirmed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Scenario 1: You Sent BTC to Your Own Old Address&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the easiest mistakes to misunderstand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Modern Bitcoin wallets can generate a new receiving address for different payments. That does not mean older addresses suddenly stop belonging to you.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org explains that addresses generated by a wallet remain valid and that funds sent to an older address can still belong to the wallet owner. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So if you accidentally sent Bitcoin to an older address that you still control, you may not have lost anything at all.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The key question is not:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;“Is this an old address?”&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;“Do I still have the private keys needed to spend the BTC at that address?”&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Scenario 2: You Sent BTC to the Wrong Person&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is much more serious.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the receiving address belongs to another person, the Bitcoin network does not know that you made a mistake.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;From the network's perspective, a valid transaction was authorized by the sender and sent to a valid destination.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the recipient controls the private keys, they can potentially spend the BTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Your best chance of recovery is therefore communication with the recipient or the organization controlling the address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org specifically states that a confirmed &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/rex-launches-assx-2x-leveraged-etf.html"&gt;Bitcoin transaction&lt;/a&gt; can only be refunded by the person receiving the funds. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means there is no Bitcoin protocol rule saying the recipient must return the coins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If the Wrong Address Belongs to an Exchange?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This situation can be more complicated, but it is not necessarily hopeless.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Suppose you intended to send BTC to your own exchange deposit address but copied the wrong address associated with the same exchange, another account or another asset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The blockchain itself cannot reverse the transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, if a centralized exchange controls the destination wallet, the exchange may have internal records and operational procedures that can sometimes help investigate the transfer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Whether recovery is possible depends on the exchange, the asset, the destination, the transaction status and its internal policies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why contacting the exchange's official support channel as quickly as possible is important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Never give an exchange or “recovery service” your seed phrase or private key.&lt;/strong&gt; Bitcoin.org warns that legitimate support teams do not need your recovery phrase or private key to recover funds. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Scenario 3: The Address Is Valid but Nobody Controls It&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where the 10-year question becomes particularly important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A Bitcoin address can be valid even when nobody currently has the private key required to spend the funds associated with it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If BTC is sent to such an address, the coins can remain visible on the blockchain indefinitely.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But visible does not mean spendable.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org explicitly states that if a valid receiving address is not controlled by anyone, funds sent there can become permanently inaccessible. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The blockchain can continue recording the balance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The coins can remain associated with that output.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But without the necessary spending authority, nobody can simply transfer them somewhere else.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;So What Happens After 10 Years?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Here is the part many people get wrong.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin does not have a 10-year expiration rule for incorrectly sent BTC.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Waiting 10 years does not cause a transaction to automatically reverse.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you sent BTC to an address controlled by someone else and that person never sends it back, the transaction does not become refundable simply because time passed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you sent BTC to an address for which nobody has the private key, the passage of 10 years does not create the missing key.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you sent BTC to an address you control but lost access to the wallet, the coins remain inaccessible until you recover the necessary wallet credentials or keys.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In other words:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Time changes the age of the transaction. It does not change who controls the private keys.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could the Bitcoin Come Back After 10 Years?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Yes, but only under specific circumstances.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, imagine you accidentally sent BTC to an address belonging to a person you know.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ten years later, that person could still voluntarily send the bitcoin back.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Or suppose the address belonged to a wallet you actually controlled and you eventually recovered the private keys. The BTC could then become spendable again.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But those are changes in control or access.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They are not automatic reversals caused by the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/openai-makes-progress-on-another.html"&gt;Bitcoin network.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If Someone Eventually Finds the Private Key?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is another important distinction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If nobody currently has access to the private key, that does not necessarily mean the key mathematically cannot exist somewhere.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A person might discover an old wallet backup.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A hardware wallet might be recovered.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A forgotten seed phrase might be found.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An owner might regain access to an old wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the correct private key becomes available to the legitimate holder, the bitcoin can potentially be spent according to Bitcoin's rules.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But nobody should interpret this as a practical recovery method.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no legitimate service that can simply calculate a lost Bitcoin private key from an address because someone has waited long enough.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can Bitcoin Developers Recover the Coins?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No central Bitcoin authority exists that can simply reverse an individual confirmed transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's decentralized design means transactions are validated according to network consensus rather than by a central payment administrator. Bitcoin.org explains that Bitcoin has no central authority and that users and network participants collectively maintain the system's rules. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is both a feature and a responsibility.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You get control over your bitcoin without needing a bank to approve every transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But you also take responsibility for entering the correct destination.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can Miners Return Your Bitcoin?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not through an ordinary reversal process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Miners confirm transactions and contribute to the operation of the network, but they do not have a customer-service function for recovering coins sent to the wrong address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A confirmed transaction is part of Bitcoin's shared ledger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is not a bank transfer sitting in a central database waiting for an administrator to undo it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What About a Bitcoin Address With a Typo?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is an important point because people often imagine that one wrong character will automatically send BTC somewhere random.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin addresses contain mechanisms that help detect many errors, and Bitcoin.org notes that Bitcoin can usually detect typos and prevent users from sending to an invalid address. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But that protection is not a substitute for checking the complete address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A valid address can still be the wrong address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, copying a legitimate address belonging to another person is not necessarily a typo that Bitcoin can reject.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The transaction can be perfectly valid while still being completely wrong for the sender's intention.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why You Should Check the Entire Address&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org recommends verifying the entire receiving address rather than checking only the beginning or end. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This matters because crypto users can encounter scams such as address poisoning, malicious clipboard software and fake payment instructions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A wallet showing a familiar first few characters does not prove that the entire destination is correct.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For larger transfers, a small test transaction can also reduce the risk of sending a large amount to the wrong destination.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If You Sent BTC to a Scam Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the recipient is a scammer and the transaction is confirmed, recovering the bitcoin can be extremely difficult.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The blockchain may allow anyone to see where the funds moved, but knowing where coins went is not the same as having the ability to reverse the transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchain tracing can potentially help investigators identify transaction flows, but users should be extremely careful with companies or individuals promising guaranteed recovery.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org specifically warns about fake recovery services and says legitimate support should never ask for a seed phrase or private key. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If You Lost the Wallet Instead?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sending BTC to the wrong address and losing your own wallet are two different problems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you sent coins to an address you control but later lost access to the wallet, recovery depends on whether you can restore the wallet using the correct backup or recovery information.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org states that permanently losing access to a self-custodied wallet can mean the funds are permanently lost and that developers, miners, wallet providers or exchanges cannot simply recover them for you. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why wallet backups matter just as much as checking a receiving address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does Bitcoin Ever “Forget” Old Transactions?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's blockchain is designed as a public ledger containing the transaction history used by the network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The fact that a transaction is 10 years old does not by itself make it disappear or become reversible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you can identify the transaction on the blockchain, its history can generally be examined long after it occurred.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The real issue is not whether the transaction still exists.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The real issue is whether anyone has the authority and ability to spend the coins at the destination.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Should You Do Immediately After Sending BTC to the Wrong Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you realize you made a mistake, do not panic and do not immediately trust someone claiming they can “hack the blockchain” and recover your funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check the transaction ID.&lt;/strong&gt; Determine whether the transaction is confirmed or still pending.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Verify the destination address.&lt;/strong&gt; Make sure it really is the address you intended to use.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Identify who controls the address.&lt;/strong&gt; It may belong to your own wallet, an exchange, a merchant or another person.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Contact the legitimate recipient or platform.&lt;/strong&gt; If an exchange controls the address, use its official support channel.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Keep the transaction details.&lt;/strong&gt; Save the transaction ID, destination address, amount and relevant timestamps.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Do not share your seed phrase or private key.&lt;/strong&gt; Anyone asking for them to “recover” your BTC should be treated with extreme caution. &lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can a Bitcoin Transaction Be Reversed After 10 Years?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Not simply because 10 years have passed.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no Bitcoin mechanism that automatically reverses a mistaken transaction after a particular period.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the recipient still controls the coins, they can choose to return them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you recover access to your own wallet, you may regain control of coins that were actually yours.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But if the BTC was sent to a valid address whose private key nobody possesses, the coins can remain inaccessible indefinitely.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Difference Between “Lost” and “Unspent” Bitcoin&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction is useful when discussing old Bitcoin transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Coins can remain recorded on the blockchain even when nobody can practically spend them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;From a blockchain perspective, the transaction and associated outputs can remain part of the ledger.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;From the owner's perspective, however, those coins may be effectively lost if the required private key is unavailable.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why saying “the Bitcoin disappeared” is technically misleading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Bitcoin does not necessarily disappear from the blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Access to it may disappear.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Bitcoin's Irreversibility Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The same property that makes Bitcoin useful for direct digital payments also creates responsibility for users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no central institution automatically standing between the sender and recipient to reverse every mistake.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's original design emphasized transactions that are difficult to reverse, removing the need for a trusted third party to mediate every payment. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That design can make payments efficient and resistant to chargeback-style reversals.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But it also means that users must treat a Bitcoin address almost like a bank account number combined with a cryptographic lock.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line: Will Your Bitcoin Come Back After 10 Years?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you sent Bitcoin to the wrong address, &lt;strong&gt;10 years of waiting will not automatically bring it back.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the destination belongs to someone else, recovery generally depends on that person or organization voluntarily returning the funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the address belongs to you, recovering the correct wallet keys may restore access.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the address is valid but nobody controls the corresponding funds, the BTC may remain permanently inaccessible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And if the transaction is already confirmed, Bitcoin itself does not provide a normal undo button.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is the uncomfortable reality of self-custody.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin gives users control over their money, but that control comes with responsibility.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The safest habit is simple: verify the entire receiving address, confirm the amount, use trusted payment instructions and consider a small test transaction before sending a large amount. Bitcoin.org recommends these precautions because confirmed Bitcoin transactions are not normally reversible. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can I recover Bitcoin sent to the wrong address?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sometimes, but there is no automatic recovery mechanism. If another person controls the destination, they must voluntarily return the BTC. If nobody controls the address, the funds may be permanently inaccessible. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Will Bitcoin sent to the wrong address come back after 10 years?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No automatic reversal occurs after 10 years. Time alone does not change the ownership or spending authority associated with a Bitcoin address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can an exchange recover Bitcoin sent to the wrong address?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It depends on the exchange and the specific circumstances. If the exchange controls the destination, contact its official support team immediately, but recovery is not guaranteed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can Bitcoin developers reverse a transaction?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no central Bitcoin authority that can simply reverse an individual confirmed transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can miners recover incorrectly sent Bitcoin?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No ordinary miner recovery process exists for mistaken confirmed payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What if I sent Bitcoin to an old address?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the old address is still controlled by your wallet and you have the required private keys, the BTC may still belong to you. Bitcoin.org notes that older addresses generated by modern wallets can remain valid. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Bitcoin permanently lost if nobody controls the address?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If a valid address has no one with the necessary private key, the funds can become permanently inaccessible. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Should I give my seed phrase to a Bitcoin recovery service?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. A legitimate support or recovery service should not require your seed phrase or private key. Bitcoin.org specifically warns users about fake recovery services. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Sources&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;/ul&gt;

Individual recovery outcomes depend on who controls the destination address, the wallet or exchange involved and the status of the transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>How AI Is Making Blockchain Fraud Detection Smarter — And Why Scammers Are Getting Smarter Too</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgRiwI5-PV_kXW2wncqrmjed465BzN0h16fW4ZIA9M5JIxCPxJjD4kb5tQmT-CGQLhhjN69KNwWE3U8nMnVhtJFnlifWKCsGrynEKZaOiFrXbFrlDj0RJGu695nMy5Cuip2YCtO-wBNQuwb3EDTZKBopY-4sRDKdIfTDFOJc9Vv8srx-CQ1DSihCZziBOyO/s1536/ai-blockchain-fraud-detection-security.png.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="AI-powered blockchain fraud detection infographic showing transaction monitoring, smart contract scanning, phishing detection, rug pull detection, and crypto security platforms." border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="213" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgRiwI5-PV_kXW2wncqrmjed465BzN0h16fW4ZIA9M5JIxCPxJjD4kb5tQmT-CGQLhhjN69KNwWE3U8nMnVhtJFnlifWKCsGrynEKZaOiFrXbFrlDj0RJGu695nMy5Cuip2YCtO-wBNQuwb3EDTZKBopY-4sRDKdIfTDFOJc9Vv8srx-CQ1DSihCZziBOyO/w320-h213/ai-blockchain-fraud-detection-security.png.png" title="How AI Is Making Blockchain Fraud Detection Smarter" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The cryptography behind major blockchains is designed to
resist attacks, but that doesn't make the wider crypto ecosystem secure.
Phishing links that look exactly like a legitimate dApp login page. Fake
support agents that show up in your DMs at exactly the right moment. Smart
contracts with hidden backdoors that nobody noticed during the audit. These
aren't technical flaws in blockchain — they're human errors, and scammers have
gotten extremely good at exploiting them.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Traditional security can't keep up anymore. Rule-based
monitoring systems and manual audits are too slow to catch attacks that unfold
in milliseconds. That's where AI comes in. Today, artificial intelligence is
scanning millions of blockchain transactions in near real time, flagging
suspicious patterns before they complete, and protecting crypto assets in ways
that would have been impossible just a few years ago.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;1. Real-Time Transaction Monitoring — How AI Stops Fraud
in Its Tracks&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The numbers are staggering. &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/p2p-vs-bank-transfers-which-crypto.html"&gt;Ethereum &lt;/a&gt;processes a huge volume
of transactions every day, making manual monitoring at scale impractical. AI
can process that kind of transaction volume far faster than a human monitoring
team.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Modern AI algorithms scan every transaction, looking for
behavioral anomalies that might indicate fraud. AI systems can analyze
transaction patterns in near real time and flag behavior that appears
suspicious — such as a wallet suddenly moving large amounts to a mixer or an
unknown address that doesn't match its typical behavior.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bybit has reported using AI-assisted risk controls and
behavioral analysis to identify and disrupt suspicious withdrawals, combining
automated detection with human review. The exchange's three-tier framework
combines AI-powered &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/how-ai-is-making-blockchain-fraud.html"&gt;blockchain &lt;/a&gt;monitoring with human intervention and industry
collaboration. Proprietary algorithms scan transactions across multiple
networks, including cross-chain bridges and crypto mixers, analyzing wallet
behavior and historical data to flag anomalies in real time.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If the software detects suspicious activity, alerts go to
the risk-control team. Human analysts review flagged transactions, contact
users, and pause withdrawals pending verification. If a scam is confirmed, the
exchange freezes the funds.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The approach shifts fraud prevention earlier in the
transaction flow, giving users and risk teams an opportunity to stop suspicious
withdrawals before funds leave the platform.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;2. Smart Contract Vulnerability Scanning — Catching Bugs
Before They Cost Millions&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;DeFi hacks in 2025 and 2026 have been devastating. Attackers
exploit small bugs in smart contracts to drain entire protocols. But AI is now
making that much harder.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The new generation of AI-powered auditing tools can help
identify vulnerabilities that may be difficult to detect through traditional
analysis alone. Research projects such as CyberTrust AI v2 are exploring
multi-agent approaches to smart-contract security, including specialized
analysis and adversarial testing. The framework uses four specialist agents —
focusing on reentrancy, access control, economic/tokenomics, and gas/logic — to
analyze contracts in parallel. A Lead Auditor agent then synthesizes their
findings into a unified trust score and consensus assessment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The framework also includes an Adversarial Red Team/Blue
Team simulation that produces structured attack-and-defense transcripts, and an
Automated Exploit Proof-of-Concept generator that produces complete, runnable
Foundry test files. In other words, AI doesn't just tell you there's a problem
— it shows you exactly how an attacker would exploit it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;CertiK's AI Auditor has demonstrated an 88.6%
vulnerability detection rate when tested against 35 actual Web3 security
incidents from 2026, while significantly reducing false positives.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The
tool uses a "Multi-Stage Validator" architecture that runs multiple
specialized scanners simultaneously, deduplicates alerts, and cross-validates
the semantic validity and actual exploitability of vulnerabilities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Companies like Fireblocks are also using AI to simulate
attack scenarios.&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;The company's Agentic Policy Analyzer (APA) uses two
specialized AI agents — one identifying single points of failure and another
simulating adversarial exploits — to probe transaction policies for
vulnerabilities.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;It can detect when multiple rules inadvertently
combine to create exploitable paths, such as allowing small repeated
transactions to drain funds below a configured cap.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;3. Spotting Phishing and Rug Pull Patterns — AI That
Remembers Every Scam&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Machine-learning models can learn from large datasets of
previous scams, exploits and suspicious behavior, helping them recognize
patterns that may indicate risk. They can learn from years of scam data —
including rug pulls, honeypots and phishing campaigns — and use those patterns
to identify potentially suspicious behavior.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Risk analysis tools such as Marcus Rug Intel use AI-driven
systems to analyze token addresses and assess risk levels based on deployer
history, holder concentration, liquidity locks, and freeze authority. Some
projects in this space cite scam-or-honeypot rates above 70% for new tokens.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;When a new token launches with suspicious behavior — like a
deployer who's run similar scams before, or a liquidity pool that can be
drained at any moment — AI systems can alert users immediately.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Even browser extensions have begun offering real-time token
scanning, checking smart contract behavior, holder distribution, developer
activity, token history, and AI-detected scam patterns.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;4. AI-Assisted Blockchain Security Platforms&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A number of platforms are already applying AI to blockchain
security:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;a href="https://anchain.ai/" target="_blank"&gt;Anchain.AI&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;—
A Web3 security platform using AI for threat detection, risk scoring, and
real-time monitoring across multiple blockchains.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;CertiK (Skynet)&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;— CertiK's Skynet provides
real-time security monitoring and risk scoring for blockchain projects. The
company has transitioned from static "audit-as-security" to dynamic
"security-as-a-service," incorporating on-chain audit certification,
continuous monitoring, and AI-assisted auditing. The platform's AI Auditor has
been tested against 35 actual Web3 security incidents in 2026, catching 88.6%
of vulnerabilities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Fireblocks (FSPM)&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;— Fireblocks' AI Agentic
Policy Analyzer simulates attack scenarios to proactively identify
vulnerabilities in transaction policies. The platform processes 15% of global
stablecoin volume and over 35 million monthly transactions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Blockchain forensics firms&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;— Blockchain
forensics firms such as Chainalysis, TRM Labs and Elliptic help investigators
trace illicit funds and identify criminal networks. Chainalysis says its data
and software have been involved in more than $34 billion in illicit funds seized,
frozen or recovered, while more than 45 regulators worldwide use its
technology.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Arms Race — Why AI Alone Isn't Enough&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Here's the honest truth: while defensive AI has gotten
dramatically better, the scammers have gotten better too.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;AI-powered scams are 4.5x more profitable than
traditional ones.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;With AI, scammers can manufacture fake support
agents, fake investors, or trusted insiders at scale. According to Chainalysis,
the average crypto scam payment rose from $782 in 2024 to $2,764 in 2025 — a
253% increase. Impersonation fraud — criminals posing as banks, investors, or
crypto influencers — posted 1,400% year-on-year growth.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The FBI's NexFundAI sting is a reminder of how quickly
defensive tactics can become attack templates. Federal agents created a fake
token to catch wash traders. Shortly after the arrests became public, a copycat
version of the same contract appeared, reportedly generating a significant
profit using the same mechanisms the FBI had just disclosed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Forensic tools are built for detective work, not prediction.
For an investigation to happen, a crime needs to have been committed. Even the
predictive models that claim to catch a rug pull before it happens are trained
on yesterday's scams — and tomorrow's scam is being designed by someone who
read the same training data.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;AI-powered fraud detection is already making a practical
difference in transaction monitoring, smart-contract analysis and scam
detection. AI-based security systems are already showing promising results in
specific detection and auditing tasks, although performance varies widely by
model, dataset and type of attack.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But the scammers are using the same technology. AI-powered
scams are more profitable, more scalable, and harder to detect than anything
we've seen before.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The technology is ready. The question is whether it can stay
ahead of the people who are using it for the wrong reasons.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Elliptic Says Iran's Nobitex Was Hit in $90 Million Hack — What We Know About the Attack</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgeFC9QO__P2v0pLkBKQWFs5aaxM4WZCKt6vAvJ5Nj5ypFG28BgU6tVbz7HkgcucCfzXorGo_T6_02K2zvLbnVTGa-EgN_uL3_7E6GomKLRQ0K-wPzSGAiFiYvQhanuofROWlhuVAg4JFVyjHvVNixQtmaZF3emYL3W3BUxSAcwTjlXAlQ1jfkvikyIvx91/s1672/nobitex-crypto-exchange-hack-iran-cyberattack.webp.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Nobitex cryptocurrency exchange hack and Iran geopolitical cyberattack" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgeFC9QO__P2v0pLkBKQWFs5aaxM4WZCKt6vAvJ5Nj5ypFG28BgU6tVbz7HkgcucCfzXorGo_T6_02K2zvLbnVTGa-EgN_uL3_7E6GomKLRQ0K-wPzSGAiFiYvQhanuofROWlhuVAg4JFVyjHvVNixQtmaZF3emYL3W3BUxSAcwTjlXAlQ1jfkvikyIvx91/w400-h225/nobitex-crypto-exchange-hack-iran-cyberattack.webp.png" title="Nobitex Crypto Exchange Hack and Iran Cyberwarfare" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br style="mso-special-character: line-break;" /&gt;
&lt;!--[if !supportLineBreakNewLine]--&gt;&lt;br style="mso-special-character: line-break;" /&gt;
&lt;!--[endif]--&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A major cryptocurrency hack targeting Iran's largest
exchange, Nobitex, has raised fresh questions about digital assets, sanctions,
and the murky world of geopolitical cyberwarfare.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The June 2025 attack saw more than &lt;b&gt;$90 million in
cryptocurrency moved from Nobitex-controlled wallets to addresses controlled by
the attackers&lt;/b&gt;, according to blockchain analytics firm Elliptic. The funds
were subsequently sent to addresses designed to make the assets effectively
inaccessible.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The incident quickly became politically charged because the
hacking group that claimed responsibility, known as &lt;b&gt;Predatory Sparrow&lt;/b&gt;,
or &lt;b&gt;Gonjeshke Darande&lt;/b&gt;, has been widely described by researchers and media
outlets as pro-Israel or Israel-linked.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But there is an important distinction that should not be
lost in the headlines.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The available public evidence does not establish that the
Iranian government carried out the hack — a distinction that is often lost in
sensational headlines.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Instead, the available evidence points toward an attack on
an Iranian exchange by a group that claimed it was targeting Nobitex because of
the platform's alleged connections to Iran's financial system.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That distinction matters, particularly as Nobitex has since
faced growing scrutiny from U.S. authorities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Happened to Nobitex?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The attack took place on &lt;b&gt;June 18, 2025&lt;/b&gt;, during a
period of rapidly escalating tensions between Israel and Iran.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Elliptic's analysis found that more than &lt;b&gt;$90 million
worth of cryptoassets&lt;/b&gt; moved from Nobitex wallets to addresses controlled by
the attackers.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Rather than attempting to quietly launder the funds, the
attackers sent the cryptocurrency to what are commonly known as vanity
addresses — blockchain addresses created with specific words or messages
embedded in them.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The result was unusual.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The attackers effectively destroyed access to the stolen
cryptocurrency instead of treating it like a conventional theft.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Reuters reported that roughly $90 million in crypto was
transferred to hacker-controlled wallets and rendered inaccessible.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That made the incident look less like a conventional
financial crime and more like a political statement carried out through
cryptocurrency infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Who Was Behind the Attack?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is where the story becomes more complicated.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The group that claimed responsibility was &lt;b&gt;Predatory
Sparrow&lt;/b&gt;, also known by its Persian name Gonjeshke Darande.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The group has previously claimed responsibility for
cyberattacks against Iranian infrastructure and financial institutions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In the Nobitex incident, the attackers accused the exchange
of helping the Iranian government evade sanctions and support hostile
activities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Elliptic described the attackers as a pro-Israel group,
while Reuters reported that Predatory Sparrow was reportedly linked to Israel.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;However, that does &lt;b&gt;not&lt;/b&gt; mean the Israeli government
has officially acknowledged responsibility for the attack.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That distinction is important when reporting the incident.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Attributing the hack to a specific government requires
stronger evidence than simply establishing the identity or affiliations claimed
by a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/brian-armstrong-predicts-clarity-act.html"&gt;hacking group&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;So the most defensible description is that &lt;b&gt;Predatory
Sparrow claimed responsibility and has been widely linked to Israel&lt;/b&gt;, rather
than saying that Israel officially carried out the attack.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Was Nobitex Targeted?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Nobitex sits at the center of Iran's cryptocurrency
ecosystem.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The exchange is widely described as Iran's largest
cryptocurrency platform and an important gateway between Iranian users and
global digital-asset markets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That position makes Nobitex strategically significant.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Blockchain analytics firms have previously identified
transactions involving Nobitex and wallets associated with sanctioned Iranian
entities and groups.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Elliptic has also investigated Nobitex's role in Iran's
digital-asset ecosystem and reported connections involving activity that raised
sanctions-evasion and illicit-finance concerns.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The exchange, however, has denied having direct government
connections and has argued that illicit activity could occur through its
platform without management knowledge.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That means the question is not simply whether Nobitex
processed transactions connected to sanctioned entities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The bigger question is &lt;b&gt;what those transactions say about
the role of the exchange inside Iran's wider financial system.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;U.S. Sanctions Added Another Layer to the Story&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Nobitex controversy did not end with the 2025 hack.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In &lt;b&gt;June 2026&lt;/b&gt;, the U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned
Nobitex, accusing the exchange of providing significant support to the Iranian
regime and facilitating transactions connected to sanctions evasion and the
Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Treasury said Nobitex processed more than half of
Iranian &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bitwise-ceo-hunter-horsley-says-crypto.html"&gt;digital-asset&lt;/a&gt; inflows in 2025 and described the platform as a tool that
allowed Iranian regime insiders to access international cryptocurrency markets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Treasury also sanctioned Nobitex's CEO and two individuals
it identified as controlling figures connected to the exchange.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Those sanctions are significant because they provide an
official U.S. government assessment of Nobitex's role in Iran's financial
infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But they still should not be confused with proof that Iran
was responsible for the 2025 hack.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Those are two separate claims.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The $90 Million Wasn't a Typical Crypto Heist&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;One of the strangest aspects of the Nobitex attack was what
happened to the stolen cryptocurrency.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Normally, hackers who steal digital assets attempt to move
the funds through mixers, bridges, exchanges or multiple wallets before
converting them into other assets or fiat currency.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That did not happen here.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Instead, the attackers transferred the funds to addresses
that made them effectively unspendable.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Elliptic identified more than $90 million moving from
Nobitex wallets to attacker-controlled addresses.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The apparent objective was therefore not simply to make
money.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The attackers wanted the transaction itself to become a
public message.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That is one reason the Nobitex incident has attracted so
much attention from cybersecurity and blockchain analysts.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Blockchain Data Can — and Cannot — Prove&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Blockchain investigations can provide an unusually detailed
picture of where cryptocurrency moves.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Analysts can track wallet balances, transaction times, token
movements and destination addresses.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But blockchain data generally cannot identify the real-world
person sitting behind a wallet address by itself.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That distinction is particularly important in politically
sensitive cyberattacks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Blockchain analysis can establish that funds moved from a
Nobitex wallet to a particular address.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It can establish the approximate value involved.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It can sometimes connect wallets to previously identified
entities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But determining &lt;b&gt;who physically controlled the attacker
infrastructure&lt;/b&gt; can require additional evidence from cybersecurity
investigations, intelligence agencies, seized infrastructure or other sources.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That is why claims about the identity of a state actor
should be treated carefully.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why the Nobitex Hack Matters for Crypto&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The attack highlights a growing problem for cryptocurrency
exchanges operating in politically sensitive environments.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Crypto transactions are global by design.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A user in one country can send digital assets to another
country within minutes, without using the traditional banking system.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That can make cryptocurrency valuable for legitimate users
in countries with restricted access to international financial markets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;At the same time, the same infrastructure can be used for
sanctions evasion, illicit finance and state-linked activity.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Nobitex sits directly inside that tension.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For ordinary Iranian users, the exchange can function as an
important gateway to digital assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For governments and regulators, however, the same platform
can represent a potential channel for moving money around international
restrictions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That makes a large Iranian exchange an obvious strategic
target during a geopolitical conflict.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bigger Cyberwar Behind the Hack&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Nobitex attack also fits into a much broader pattern of
cyber operations connected to the Iran-Israel conflict.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Predatory Sparrow has previously claimed responsibility for
attacks targeting Iranian infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Reuters reported that the Nobitex incident occurred shortly
after another cyberattack targeting Iran's Bank Sepah.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That timing reinforced the perception that the Nobitex hack
was part of a wider campaign rather than an isolated cryptocurrency theft.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For the crypto industry, this creates a difficult reality.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A cryptocurrency exchange can become a target not only
because of the value of the assets it controls, but also because of its role in
a country's financial infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Investors Should Take From the Incident&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Nobitex hack offers several lessons for cryptocurrency
investors and exchanges.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;First, &lt;b&gt;custody matters&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Cryptocurrency held in a centralized exchange wallet
ultimately depends on the exchange's security infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Second, &lt;b&gt;geopolitical risk can affect crypto
infrastructure&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;An exchange operating in a heavily sanctioned or politically
isolated country can face risks that have little to do with normal market
volatility.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Third, &lt;b&gt;on-chain transparency cuts both ways&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Blockchain transactions can be tracked publicly, making it
possible for researchers to reconstruct large hacks. But that transparency does
not automatically reveal who controls every wallet.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Finally, investors should be careful with headlines that
turn an attribution into a certainty.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There is a meaningful difference between:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"A pro-Israel hacking group claimed
responsibility."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;and:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"Israel hacked the exchange."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The first statement reflects the available reporting. The
second requires evidence that has not been publicly established.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;So, Was Iran Behind the Hack?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Based on the evidence publicly available, &lt;b&gt;there is no
solid basis for saying that Iran was behind the Nobitex hack.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The available evidence points in the opposite direction:
Nobitex was the target, while Predatory Sparrow claimed responsibility for the
attack. Elliptic independently traced more than $90 million in crypto from
Nobitex wallets to attacker-controlled addresses.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;At the same time, there is substantial reporting and U.S.
government action concerning Nobitex's alleged connections to Iran's financial
and sanctions-evasion infrastructure. Reuters reported in 2026 that Nobitex had
processed transactions involving sanctioned Iranian entities, while the U.S.
Treasury later sanctioned the exchange.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Those facts help explain &lt;b&gt;why Nobitex may have been
targeted&lt;/b&gt;, but they do not establish that Iran conducted the attack.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;That distinction is crucial — and it is the difference
between reporting facts and spreading speculation.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Nobitex hack was far more than a typical cryptocurrency
theft.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;More than &lt;b&gt;$90 million in digital assets&lt;/b&gt; was moved
from the Iranian exchange to attacker-controlled addresses, according to
Elliptic. The funds were then effectively destroyed rather than quietly cashed
out.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The group that claimed responsibility, Predatory Sparrow,
has been widely described as pro-Israel or Israel-linked. But public evidence
does not establish that the Israeli government officially ordered or carried
out the attack.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;At the same time, Nobitex's role in Iran's financial
ecosystem has come under increasing scrutiny. In 2026, the U.S. Treasury
sanctioned the exchange, alleging that it helped the Iranian regime and
sanctioned entities move funds and evade restrictions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The result is a story where &lt;b&gt;the target, the attackers and
the geopolitical context are all important — but they should not be conflated.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For the cryptocurrency industry, the Nobitex incident is
another reminder that digital assets are increasingly intertwined with
geopolitics.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;And when a major crypto exchange becomes part of a cyberwar,
the blockchain can become not just a financial network, but also another
battlefield in a long-running geopolitical conflict.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="2" width="100%" /&gt;
