    <title>What Is Slippage in Crypto Trading? And How to Stop It From Eating Your Profits</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiJTtGEh03Bq680wU9eCEVfocBm0eaZ3nkfCcQxL9_b5NFycwaL0gmkhgqdOUeAXMKg6beka-n9z-jhqLaTN6nQQlcV7x0WQDQ55p7rfYmPsqzaTZJ5JnXhXdgUaEj8ITjVfyIgcp9HUVZV2UgHBvmIDzF3e_CZnPE52d72yRdQy-g82ut5eUhNBexvbqiS/s1536/crypto-slippage-trading-guide.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Crypto trading slippage explained with order books, liquidity, slippage tolerance, and price impact" border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="213" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiJTtGEh03Bq680wU9eCEVfocBm0eaZ3nkfCcQxL9_b5NFycwaL0gmkhgqdOUeAXMKg6beka-n9z-jhqLaTN6nQQlcV7x0WQDQ55p7rfYmPsqzaTZJ5JnXhXdgUaEj8ITjVfyIgcp9HUVZV2UgHBvmIDzF3e_CZnPE52d72yRdQy-g82ut5eUhNBexvbqiS/w320-h213/crypto-slippage-trading-guide.jpg.png" title="Crypto trading slippage explained with order books, liquidity, slippage tolerance, and price impact" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;You see a price. You click buy. The trade executes. And
somehow, you paid more than you expected.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That's slippage. It's not a fee, not a glitch, and not the
exchange trying to cheat you. It's just the gap between the price you saw and
the price you actually got.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Here's how it works, why it happens, and most importantly —
how to avoid getting hit by it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Slippage Actually Looks Like&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Let's say you want to buy 1 ETH. The price shows $3,000. You
place the order. By the time it fills, the best available price has moved to
$3,015. You just paid $15 more than you expected. That $15 is slippage.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The formula:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For a simple buy trade:&lt;br /&gt;
Slippage % = (Executed Price − Expected Price) / Expected Price × 100&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In this case:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l7 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Expected
     = $3,000&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l7 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Executed
     = $3,015&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l7 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Slippage
     = 0.5%&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;For selling:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
If you expected to sell at $3,000 but the order fills at $2,985, that's also
slippage — just in the wrong direction. For sells, the calculation should
account for the opposite direction, so traders often compare the expected and
actual execution prices using an absolute percentage difference or a
direction-specific formula.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Slippage can go both ways:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Adverse
     slippage:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;You receive a worse execution price than expected (this
     is the one that hurts)&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Favorable
     slippage:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;You receive a better execution price than expected
     (rare, but it happens)&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But let's be honest — most of the time, you're not getting
lucky. You're getting slipped.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Slippage Happens&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There are three common factors behind worse-than-expected
execution: market movement, limited liquidity, and order size. The first two
can contribute directly to slippage, while a large order can create price
impact that also worsens the final execution price.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;1. The Market Moved Before You Could Confirm&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Crypto prices can change in seconds. If the market moves
between the moment you submit your order and the moment it gets confirmed, the
final price will be different from what you saw.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This happens more often during:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;News
     events&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;High-volume
     trading hours&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Extreme
     volatility periods&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The faster the price moves, the bigger the slippage.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;2. There Isn't Enough Liquidity&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Liquidity is just a fancy word for "how many buyers and
sellers are active." If there aren't enough orders near your target price,
your &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/are-there-legit-crypto-recovery.html"&gt;trade &lt;/a&gt;gets filled at the next available price — and the next one after
that.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Think of it like this:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;You walk into a store and see one item left at $100. You
want to buy five. The first one costs $100, the second costs $110, the third
costs $120, and so on. Your average price ends up much higher than $100. That's
what happens when liquidity is thin.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is especially common with:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Smaller
     altcoins&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Newly
     launched tokens&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Tokens
     with low trading volume&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;3. Your Order Is Too Big for the Market&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Even if the market is reasonably liquid, a very large order
can move the price against you. If you're buying a large amount relative to the
available supply, your own trade pushes the price up while it fills.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is called&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;price impact&lt;/b&gt;, and it's often
confused with slippage. The difference is:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l4 level1 lfo5; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Slippage:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The
     difference between the expected/quoted execution price and the actual
     execution price&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l4 level1 lfo5; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Price
     impact:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The effect your own order has on the market price as it
     executes&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In practice, you can experience both at the same time.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Order Books vs. AMMs: Where Slippage Happens Differently&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;On Centralized Exchanges (Order Books)&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Exchanges like Binance and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/p2p-vs-bank-transfers-which-crypto.html"&gt;Kraken &lt;/a&gt;use order books — a list
of buy and sell orders at different prices. When you place a market order, it
takes the best available orders. If there's not enough volume at your target
price, the order slips to the next level, and the next one after that.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The key factor is order book depth.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Major pairs
like BTC/USDT have deep books with thousands of orders close to the market
price. Obscure altcoins have thin books where a small order can push the price
significantly.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;On Decentralized Exchanges (AMMs)&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;DEXs like Uniswap use automated market makers (AMMs) instead
of order books. Instead of matching buyers and sellers, they use a mathematical
formula to set prices based on how much of each token is in a liquidity pool.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Slippage on DEXs is tied to pool depth:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l10 level1 lfo6; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A
     large trade in a small pool will shift the price significantly&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l10 level1 lfo6; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A
     small trade in a large pool will have minimal impact&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;DEXs also have an additional risk:&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;MEV attacks&lt;/b&gt;.
Bots monitor pending transactions and can "sandwich" your trade —
buying just before you and selling just after, profiting from the price
movement they create.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is why setting your slippage tolerance correctly
matters more on DEXs than on centralized exchanges.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Slippage Tolerance: Your First Line of Defense&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Most trading platforms let you set a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;slippage
tolerance&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;— the maximum percentage difference you're willing to
accept.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;How it works:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If you set a 1% slippage tolerance on a $100 purchase,
you're allowing the execution price to move against you by up to roughly 1%
from the quoted price before the trade is rejected or reverted, depending on
the platform.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;On DEXs and other platforms that enforce a minimum-received
or maximum-paid limit, a trade may fail or revert if execution moves beyond the
permitted tolerance. On some networks, a failed on-chain transaction can still
consume network fees.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What tolerance to use:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="MsoNormalTable" style="border-collapse: collapse; mso-yfti-tbllook: 1184; width: 744px;"&gt;
 &lt;thead&gt;
  &lt;tr style="mso-yfti-firstrow: yes; mso-yfti-irow: 0;"&gt;
   &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 0cm;"&gt;
   &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Asset Type&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
   &lt;/td&gt;
   &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
   &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Suggested Tolerance&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
   &lt;/td&gt;
   &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
   &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Risk&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
   &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;/tr&gt;
 &lt;/thead&gt;
 &lt;tbody&gt;&lt;tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 1;"&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 0cm;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Stablecoins&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;(USDT, USDC)&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;0.1% – 0.5%&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 0cm 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Spreads are generally tight&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
 &lt;tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 2;"&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 0cm;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Major coins&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;(BTC, ETH)&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;0.5% – 1%&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 0cm 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Liquid markets, but prices can move quickly&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
 &lt;tr style="mso-yfti-irow: 3; mso-yfti-lastrow: yes;"&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 0cm;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Volatile tokens&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;(memecoins, new launches)&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 12.0pt 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;2% – 5%&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
  &lt;td style="padding: 7.5pt 0cm 7.5pt 12.0pt;"&gt;
  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Higher risk and potentially larger price movements&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/td&gt;
 &lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;These are illustrative ranges, not universal
recommendations. The appropriate tolerance depends on liquidity, volatility,
trade size and the specific platform.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The balancing act:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l6 level1 lfo7; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Too
     low:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Your trade keeps failing in volatile conditions. You waste
     gas fees on failed attempts.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l6 level1 lfo7; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Too
     high:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;You're exposing yourself to a worse fill, and potentially
     MEV attacks. A 5% tolerance means you could end up paying 5% more than
     expected.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For liquid major-asset pairs, traders often use relatively
low slippage settings and increase them only when market conditions require it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The MEV Trap: Why High Tolerance Is Dangerous&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;On decentralized exchanges, setting a high slippage
tolerance is like leaving your front door open.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;On chains and trading routes where pending transactions are
publicly observable, MEV bots can monitor the transaction flow and attempt
sandwich attacks. They buy the asset just before your trade, let your order
fill at the inflated price, and then sell right after — pocketing the
difference.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is called a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;sandwich attack&lt;/b&gt;, and it's a
form of Maximal Extractable Value (MEV).&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The defense:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Keep your tolerance reasonable. A
modest tolerance is generally enough for most trades. Only increase it when
absolutely necessary — and understand the risk when you do.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;How to Reduce Slippage: Practical Steps&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;1. Use Limit Orders Instead of Market Orders&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A market order executes against the best available prices in
the market, but the final execution price can differ from the price you
expected, especially when liquidity is limited or the market is moving quickly.
A limit order lets you set the exact price you're willing to pay. If the market
doesn't reach that price, the trade doesn't execute. You might miss the trade,
but you can control the worst price you're willing to accept.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The trade-off:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l5 level1 lfo8; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Market
     orders: Fast, but you might get slipped&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l5 level1 lfo8; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Limit
     orders: Control over price, but might not fill&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;2. Trade Liquid Pairs&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Stick to major pairs like BTC/USDT or ETH/USDT where
liquidity is deep. The more buyers and sellers active in a market, the smaller
your slippage.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If you're trading obscure altcoins, check the liquidity pool
or order book depth before placing a large order.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;3. Break Up Large Orders&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Instead of placing one massive order, split it into smaller
chunks over time. This allows the market to absorb your trades without pushing
the price against you.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The strategy:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l9 level1 lfo9; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Trade
     10% at a time instead of 100% at once&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l9 level1 lfo9; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Wait
     for the order book to refill between trades&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l9 level1 lfo9; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Avoid
     sweeping the entire order book in one go&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Splitting an order can reduce price impact, but it may also
increase execution time, fees, or exposure to further market movements.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;4. Avoid Trading During Extreme Volatility&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Periods of lower liquidity can increase slippage,
particularly in thinner markets. If you can wait, trade during calmer periods.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For major coins, periods of strong trading activity and
deeper liquidity can generally provide tighter spreads and better execution.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;5. Check the Order Book Before You Trade&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;On centralized exchanges, glance at the order book before
placing a market order. Look for:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l8 level1 lfo10; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Tight
     spread between bid and ask:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Good sign&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l8 level1 lfo10; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Deep
     order book with large volumes near your price:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Even better&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l8 level1 lfo10; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Thin
     order book with big gaps:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Slippage risk is higher&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;6. Set a Realistic Slippage Tolerance&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Start with relatively low settings for liquid assets and
adjust based on market conditions. Always review the platform's quoted slippage
or minimum received amount before confirming a trade.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;7. Use Tools That Aggregate Liquidity&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Platforms like 1inch can route and split trades across
available liquidity sources to help improve execution. This reduces both price
impact and slippage by spreading your trade across deeper markets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Auto-slippage modes can also help — they dynamically adjust
tolerance based on current market conditions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What to Do When You See High Slippage&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If the quoted slippage looks too high, don't force the
trade:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l11 level1 lfo11; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Cancel
     and try again later.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The market might calm down.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l11 level1 lfo11; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Reduce
     your order size.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Smaller trades are less likely to experience
     slippage.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l11 level1 lfo11; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Switch
     to a more liquid pair.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;If you're trading an obscure token,
     consider a more established one.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l11 level1 lfo11; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Use
     a limit order.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Set your price and walk away. If it fills, great.
     If not, you avoid a bad fill.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;FAQ&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What is slippage in crypto?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Slippage is the difference between the expected price of a
trade and the price at which it actually executes. It can result from market
movement, limited liquidity, order size, price impact, and execution conditions
between the quoted and final execution price.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What is a good slippage tolerance?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There is no single setting that works for every trade.
Liquid stablecoin and major-asset pairs generally require less tolerance, while
volatile or thinly traded tokens may require more. The appropriate setting
depends on liquidity, volatility, trade size and the platform being used.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Is 1% slippage high?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For highly liquid major pairs, a 1% tolerance may be
relatively high; the appropriate setting depends on liquidity, volatility,
trade size and the platform.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why is crypto slippage so high?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Low liquidity and high volatility can increase slippage,
while large orders can create price impact that worsens the final execution
price. In many trades, both effects can occur together.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;How can I avoid slippage on a DEX?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Use limit orders where available, trade larger pools, split
orders, and set a reasonable slippage tolerance.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What's the difference between slippage and price impact?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Slippage is the difference between the expected and actual
execution price. Price impact is the effect your own order has on the market
price as it executes.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Slippage is not a fee, not a scam, and not something you can
avoid entirely. It's simply a fact of trading in fast-moving markets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But you can reduce its impact.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo12; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Use
     limit orders instead of market orders&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo12; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Trade
     liquid pairs during calmer periods&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo12; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Set
     a realistic slippage tolerance&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo12; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Break
     up large trades&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo12; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Check
     the order book before you trade&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The rule is simple:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;if the quote looks too good
to be true, it probably is. Read the details, check the tolerance, and don't be
afraid to walk away if the slippage is too high.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Slippage won't stop you from trading. But if you ignore it,
it will cost you.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

I get why people reacted. But let's actually sit with this for a second — because not everything that sounds bullish actually is.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h2 style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-feature-settings: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-language-override: normal; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-size-adjust: none; font-size: 22px; font-stretch: normal; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; line-height: 32px; margin: 32px 0px 16px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;First, What Even Is a Treasury Buyback?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Okay so here's the thing — most people see "$6 billion" and think the government is printing money again. That's not exactly what's happening.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The Treasury issues bonds to fund the government. Sometimes, it buys some of those bonds &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;back&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; before they mature. Why? A few reasons:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px; padding-left: 18px;"&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Some old bonds become hard to trade — nobody wants them&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;It helps keep the bond market smooth&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;It can save the government a bit on interest&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;It gives the Treasury more flexibility with its cash&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;That's it. It's a housekeeping move, not a stimulus check.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;But — and this is the important part — &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;the market doesn't react to what something is. It reacts to what it signals.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h2 style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-feature-settings: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-language-override: normal; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-size-adjust: none; font-size: 22px; font-stretch: normal; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; line-height: 32px; margin: 32px 0px 16px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Why Bitcoin People Are Hyped&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Here's the logic crypto folks are running with:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;More liquidity = more money sloshing around = risk assets pump.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;A Treasury buyback is primarily a debt-management and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/cz-hints-crypto-pump-is-coming-soon.html"&gt;market&lt;/a&gt;-liquidity operation. It does not mean the government is creating $6 billion in new money.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Then there's the bigger narrative. &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/morgan-stanley-launches-digital-asset.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt; was literally born out of distrust in the fiat system. Every time the U.S. does something like this, the "hard money" crowd gets louder. They'll tell you the debt is unsustainable, the dollar is weakening, and Bitcoin is the escape hatch.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Is that true? Depends who you ask. But it's a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;damn good story&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;, and crypto runs on stories.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h2 style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-feature-settings: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-language-override: normal; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-size-adjust: none; font-size: 22px; font-stretch: normal; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; line-height: 32px; margin: 32px 0px 16px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Let's Be Real Though — $6 Billion Isn't That Much&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Total U.S. debt? Over &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;$35 trillion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;$6 billion is basically a rounding error. It's like finding a $20 bill in your couch when you owe $100,000 on your mortgage.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;So the headline is loud, but the actual impact is small. What matters more is the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;direction&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; — the fact that the Treasury is doing this at all, and what it says about where we're headed.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h2 style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-feature-settings: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-language-override: normal; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-size-adjust: none; font-size: 22px; font-stretch: normal; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; line-height: 32px; margin: 32px 0px 16px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;What Actually Moves Bitcoin&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Look, I've been around crypto long enough to know one thing: &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Bitcoin doesn't pump because of one headline.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;It pumps because of a combination of things:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px; padding-left: 18px;"&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Global liquidity getting looser&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Interest rates coming down (or expected to)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Institutions buying through &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/solana-treasury-firm-skyai-faces-board.html"&gt;ETFs&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Regulation getting clearer instead of messier&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li style="margin-top: 6px;"&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="margin-bottom: 0px; margin-left: 0px; margin-right: 0px; margin-top: 0px !important;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Supply shrinking after halvings&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;A Treasury buyback is one small piece of a much bigger puzzle. On its own? It's noise. In context? It's part of a pattern — and that pattern is what matters.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;h2 style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-feature-settings: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-language-override: normal; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-size-adjust: none; font-size: 22px; font-stretch: normal; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; line-height: 32px; margin: 32px 0px 16px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;My Honest Take&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Do I think this is "bullish for Bitcoin"? Yeah, kind of. But not because of the $6 billion itself.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;I think it's bullish because it adds to the pile of evidence that the system needs &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;constant liquidity management&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; just to keep functioning. And Bitcoin's entire pitch is that it doesn't need that.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The buyback is another example of how the Treasury is using debt-management tools to support the functioning of the government bond market.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Whether the market actually prices that in tomorrow? Nobody knows. Crypto is chaotic like that.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;But the narrative? The narrative just got a little stronger.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;hr style="background: none 0% 0% / auto repeat scroll padding-box border-box rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1); border-color: currentcolor; border-image: none; border-style: none; border-width: medium; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; height: 1px; margin: 32px 0px;" /&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Not financial advice.     <title>AI Borrowing From AI: Who Writes the Contract?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhOd-PE-eqmnjZROEaK0i3U1FaDlGnCYW-_eZxHr3Sj3Qbg3gIRfOiIr3G-0hDrYha5C19vXlojmxOB-SzLIi8L-r9A3XHwiudlqusAPO7s-OvajBwadSrxsG7WM9Z59Mno1Bufrq6Xe-HykOy2bc4DgdPq2tmOVA5nc4eUuFrqnrrm7NR1V7Kl2hbZ4Gvg/s1672/ai-agents-crypto-loan-contract.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="AI agents negotiating a cryptocurrency loan and creating an automated digital contract" border="0" data-original-height="940" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhOd-PE-eqmnjZROEaK0i3U1FaDlGnCYW-_eZxHr3Sj3Qbg3gIRfOiIr3G-0hDrYha5C19vXlojmxOB-SzLIi8L-r9A3XHwiudlqusAPO7s-OvajBwadSrxsG7WM9Z59Mno1Bufrq6Xe-HykOy2bc4DgdPq2tmOVA5nc4eUuFrqnrrm7NR1V7Kl2hbZ4Gvg/w640-h360/ai-agents-crypto-loan-contract.jpg.png" title="AI Borrowing From AI: Who Writes the Contract?" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;Imagine an AI agent runs a business with its own digital wallet. It needs $10,000 to pay for computing power, data, software or another service. Another AI agent has the money and agrees to lend it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The two systems negotiate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One proposes an interest rate. The other makes a counteroffer. The terms are accepted, the payment is sent, and the repayment schedule is recorded automatically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It sounds like a simple business transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is a difficult question underneath it:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;If one AI agent borrows money from another, who actually writes the contract — and who is legally bound by it?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That question is becoming less theoretical as AI agents move from generating text to taking actions, making payments and interacting with external systems. Recent work on agentic payments and autonomous transactions shows that the technology for machine-to-machine commerce is developing quickly. The legal framework, however, still has to connect those automated actions to identifiable people or organizations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Short Answer: The AI Can Write the Contract, But It May Not Be the Legal Party&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI system can already generate contractual language, negotiate terms and send an electronic acceptance. That does not necessarily mean the AI itself becomes a legal person with the ability to own money, borrow funds, sue or be sued.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The more important legal question is therefore not simply &lt;em&gt;"Did an AI write the contract?"&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;"Whose authority was the AI exercising when the contract was created?"&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters because an &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-ai-own-its-own-crypto-wallet-law.html"&gt;AI agent&lt;/a&gt; can act autonomously while still operating on behalf of a human, company or other legally recognized entity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Indian legal analysis published in September 2026, for example, examines whether an autonomous AI agent can bind a human principal under agency and contract law. The analysis notes that Indian law recognizes electronic contracting, but an AI system does not independently acquire contractual capacity merely because it can communicate and transact electronically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.livelaw.in/lawschool/articles/lawof-agency-ai-agent-autonomous-ai-agent-bind-human-principal-547909" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;Read the legal analysis on AI agents and agency law&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If AI Agent A Wants to Borrow $10,000?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Consider a fictional example.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Agent A&lt;/strong&gt; operates a software business and needs $10,000 in stablecoins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Agent B&lt;/strong&gt; has access to capital and is willing to lend it at 8% annual interest.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The negotiation might look something like this:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Agent A requests a $10,000 loan.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Agent B proposes an 8% interest rate.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Agent A asks for a six-month repayment period.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Agent B agrees but requires collateral.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The agents agree on the collateral, repayment dates and default conditions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A digital agreement is generated.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A payment system or smart contract executes the transaction.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;From a technical perspective, almost everything can be automated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the legal identity behind each agent still matters.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If Agent A belongs to Company X and Agent B belongs to Company Y, the transaction could potentially be structured as a contract between those companies, with the AI systems acting as automated representatives or transaction tools.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The difficult situation is when the two systems are presented as if &lt;strong&gt;the AI agents themselves are the borrowers and lenders&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Can Negotiate. That Does Not Automatically Give It Legal Capacity&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the biggest misconceptions surrounding autonomous AI.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is a difference between &lt;strong&gt;technical capability&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;legal capacity&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI agent may be able to:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;generate an offer;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;evaluate another agent's proposal;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;negotiate price and payment terms;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;sign or transmit an electronic acceptance;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;move cryptocurrency from a wallet;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;interact with a smart contract; and&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;maintain transaction records.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;None of those capabilities, by themselves, necessarily make the AI a legal person.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A recent 2026 legal analysis of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ai-made-millions-in-crypto-who-pays-tax.html"&gt;AI contracting&lt;/a&gt; in India describes the problem in similar terms: traditional contract doctrines assume legally relevant parties with capacity, consent and authority, while autonomous AI systems challenge those assumptions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/Delivery.cfm/7077958.pdf?abstractid=7077958&amp;amp;mirid=1" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;Read the 2026 research on AI as a contracting agent&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;So Who Actually Writes the Contract?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are several possibilities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;1. A Human Writes It&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The simplest model is still the most familiar.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A person decides that two AI systems should enter into a loan arrangement. The person or company's lawyers create the agreement, while AI agents simply execute the instructions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is little mystery about who the parties are.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;2. The AI Drafts It, but a Company Owns the Relationship&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This model is more interesting.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI agent could generate the entire loan agreement, negotiate revisions and prepare the final version. The company behind the agent could then authorize the transaction under predefined rules.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In that scenario, the AI is doing much of the work, but the legal relationship can still be tied to the company.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;3. The AI Negotiates and Executes Automatically&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where things become complicated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An agent could be given a wallet, spending limits and permission to negotiate within defined parameters. It might accept a loan automatically if the interest rate falls below a particular threshold and collateral requirements are satisfied.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The contract could therefore be created without a human manually reviewing the final terms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not necessarily make the agreement invalid. But it raises a crucial question: &lt;strong&gt;was the AI acting within authority granted by a legally responsible principal?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If Both AI Agents Have Their Own Crypto Wallets?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto makes the scenario even more interesting because an AI agent can technically interact directly with a blockchain wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A wallet can hold digital assets and authorize transactions using cryptographic credentials. An AI system can be connected to that infrastructure and, subject to its permissions, initiate payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates the appearance of two independent digital businesses:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI Agent A → Crypto Wallet A → Loan Request&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI Agent B → Crypto Wallet B → Loan Payment&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On the blockchain, the transaction can be visible and verifiable.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But blockchain records do not automatically answer every legal question.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blockchain can show which address authorized a transaction. It does not necessarily establish who legally owns that address, who authorized the AI, what contractual authority existed or who should be responsible if something goes wrong.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could a Smart Contract Become the Loan Agreement?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Possibly, depending on the structure and applicable law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A smart contract can automatically execute predefined conditions. For example, a borrower could receive funds after depositing collateral, while repayment could be triggered according to programmed rules.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is an important distinction between &lt;strong&gt;code that executes an arrangement&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;a legally enforceable contract&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Researchers examining smart contracts under Indian law have noted that issues such as offer, acceptance, consideration, capacity, performance and remedies still matter even when contractual obligations are implemented through code.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://ijlmh.com/article/view/smart-contracts-commercial-certainty-and-indian-contract-law-enforceability-and-remedies-in-code-based-automated-transactions" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;Research on smart contracts and Indian contract law&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In other words, putting the agreement on a blockchain does not make legal questions disappear.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If the AI Makes a Bad Deal?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where accountability becomes more important than the contract's wording.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Suppose an AI agent accidentally agrees to borrow $10 million at 90% interest because it misunderstood a negotiation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Or suppose a software bug causes it to accept collateral worth far more than the loan.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Or an attacker manipulates information supplied to the agent and causes it to transfer funds under fraudulent terms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Who takes the loss?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The answer will depend on the legal structure, authorization, applicable law and facts surrounding the transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is unlikely that simply saying &lt;em&gt;"the AI made the decision"&lt;/em&gt; will settle the question.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is precisely why regulators and businesses are increasingly focused on agent identity, authorization, transaction limits, monitoring and audit trails.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;India Is Already Preparing for AI-Made Payments&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This issue is no longer limited to science-fiction scenarios.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In September 2026, Reuters reported that India's National Payments Corporation of India was developing a registry to verify and monitor AI agents conducting transactions through UPI as part of the country's work on agentic payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The planned framework is intended to help authenticate AI agents&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ai-with-wallet-can-it-spend-your-crypto.html"&gt; making payments&lt;/a&gt; on behalf of users. Reuters also reported that regulatory questions remain around liability when an AI agent makes an unauthorized or erroneous transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.reuters.com/world/india/india-plans-ai-registry-it-looks-roll-out-agentic-payments-sources-say-2026-09-10/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;Reuters: India plans AI registry for agentic payments&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That development is important because it shows where the real-world debate is heading: not necessarily toward giving AI its own legal identity, but toward creating systems that can identify an AI agent and connect its actions to an authorized user or organization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Future May Be “AI Acting for a Principal,” Not “AI Becoming the Principal”&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is a tempting idea that the solution is simply to give AI agents legal personhood.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But that would create a much larger legal problem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If an AI agent became an independent legal person, lawmakers would need rules for questions such as:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who owns the AI's assets?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who is responsible for its debts?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Can it enter binding contracts?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Can it declare bankruptcy?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who pays its taxes?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Can it sue another entity?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Can creditors seize its assets?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who is responsible if the AI causes harm?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Until those questions have workable answers, the more practical model is likely to remain one in which AI agents act on behalf of identifiable people or organizations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What an AI-to-AI Contract Could Look Like&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A future agent-to-agent agreement could contain far more than a normal loan contract.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); min-width: 760px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Contract Element&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;What the AI Could Handle&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;What Still Needs Legal Attribution&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Negotiation&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Compare offers and propose terms&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Authority of the principal&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Payment&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Send crypto or fiat automatically&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Who owns the funds&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Collateral&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Check blockchain conditions&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Legal rights over collateral&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Repayment&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Execute scheduled payments&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Enforcement against the borrower&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Dispute&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Flag the transaction and preserve records&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Who has legal responsibility&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could AI Agents Eventually Sign Contracts With Each Other?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Technically, there is little reason AI systems could not exchange machine-readable agreements, negotiate terms and execute transactions automatically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In fact, researchers and developers are already working on protocols designed around machine-to-machine transactions and payments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, a September 2026 Internet-Draft called ATXN proposes a machine-checkable structure for agent-to-agent transactions, including cryptographically signed information about the agents and their identified principals. It is an Internet-Draft, not a universal legal standard, but it illustrates how the technical infrastructure is beginning to anticipate autonomous commerce.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://nic.csc.fi/pub/files/index/internet-drafts/draft-stone-atxn-01.html" rel="noopener" target="_blank"&gt;ATXN: Agent-to-Agent Transaction Definition Protocol&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The technology could therefore move much faster than legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Biggest Problem May Not Be Writing the Contract&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The hardest part of AI-to-AI commerce may not be generating the agreement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Large language models are already capable of producing sophisticated contractual language.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The harder questions are:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who authorized the agent?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;What was the agent allowed to do?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Did it remain within those limits?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Was the other party able to verify its authority?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who controls the wallet?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who bears the loss if the agent makes an unauthorized decision?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;How can the transaction be reversed or disputed?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These are governance and accountability problems as much as they are AI problems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens When Two Autonomous Agents Disagree?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Imagine Agent A says the loan was valid.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Agent B says its model misunderstood the repayment condition.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The blockchain shows that the transaction happened.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the blockchain cannot automatically decide whether the underlying agreement was legally enforceable.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means future AI commerce may require a combination of:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;machine-readable contracts;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;cryptographic identity;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;defined spending authority;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;transaction limits;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;audit logs;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;human or corporate principals;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;dispute-resolution mechanisms; and&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;clear rules assigning liability.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The technical transaction may take seconds. The legal dispute could still take months.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Borrowing From AI Is Coming Before AI Becomes a Legal Person&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is an important distinction between &lt;strong&gt;autonomous commerce&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;AI legal personhood&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI agents do not need to become independent legal persons before they can negotiate prices, arrange services, move money or interact with other software.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Businesses can instead give agents limited authority and connect their actions to existing legal entities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That may be the more realistic path for the next stage of agentic commerce.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI → legally owns money → borrows from AI&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;the structure may look more like:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Company A → authorizes AI Agent A → negotiates with AI Agent B → Company B&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The agents perform the work, while the legal entities remain accountable.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can an AI agent write a loan contract?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. An AI agent can technically generate, negotiate and transmit contractual terms. Whether the resulting agreement is legally binding depends on applicable law, authority, consent and the legal identities behind the transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can two AI agents make a contract with each other?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They can technically negotiate and exchange machine-readable agreements. The harder legal question is whether the agents are acting with authority on behalf of legally recognized parties.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can an AI legally borrow cryptocurrency?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI can technically control or operate a crypto wallet and initiate transactions where it has been given the necessary authority. That does not automatically mean the AI itself is the legal borrower.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Who is liable if an AI agent signs a bad contract?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no single global answer. Responsibility can depend on the legal structure, the agent's authority, the applicable jurisdiction, contractual terms and the facts surrounding the transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Will AI agents eventually have their own legal contracts?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Possibly, but this would require legal systems to establish rules for identity, capacity, ownership, liability, enforcement and dispute resolution. For now, AI agents are more commonly treated as systems acting for people or organizations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI agents may soon negotiate with each other so naturally that the human involvement becomes almost invisible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One agent could request financing. Another could assess the risk. They could negotiate interest, agree on collateral, sign machine-readable terms and move cryptocurrency automatically.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The contract could be written by AI.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The transaction could be executed by AI.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The payment could be made by AI.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the biggest legal question would remain the same:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Who stands behind the AI?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is likely to become one of the defining questions of agentic commerce. The technology is moving toward a world where machines can negotiate with machines. The law still has to decide how those machine-made decisions connect to the humans and organizations responsible for them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;CoinAINews Note: This article is for informational and educational purposes only and does not constitute legal, financial or tax advice. Laws governing AI agents, electronic contracts, cryptocurrency and automated transactions vary by jurisdiction and continue to evolve.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
