    <title>Which Blockchain Certification Is Best for Developers in 2026?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhbRe8pXEnSVFs-rVwNNY1i69QfOAJwoIZJ2Dd-mJtyZoqnjcY9g9MkAFg24Emiv27n8NNn6GoJOapp6o-BVavIJCXfgFCF36NNq7jbSwamNrDMl7MkyIJT5FmmfAvtmuTIrJ8m6TFw705DAOdorpHqhdbZdHNJoKapNaGOELguAwmz3TSPrEoDDpPtDP9N/s1672/best-blockchain-certification-for-developers-2026.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Blockchain developer working on Solidity smart contracts and comparing blockchain certifications in 2026" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhbRe8pXEnSVFs-rVwNNY1i69QfOAJwoIZJ2Dd-mJtyZoqnjcY9g9MkAFg24Emiv27n8NNn6GoJOapp6o-BVavIJCXfgFCF36NNq7jbSwamNrDMl7MkyIJT5FmmfAvtmuTIrJ8m6TFw705DAOdorpHqhdbZdHNJoKapNaGOELguAwmz3TSPrEoDDpPtDP9N/w320-h180/best-blockchain-certification-for-developers-2026.jpg.png" title="Best Blockchain Certification for Developers in 2026" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;August 14, 2026&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If you're trying to get your first job in blockchain
development, sooner or later you'll run into the certification question.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Should you spend money on a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/the-most-underrated-crypto-projects_060856659.html"&gt;blockchain &lt;/a&gt;developer
certificate? Does an Ethereum certification actually help with a Solidity job?
Would an enterprise credential make a difference if you're applying to a bank
or consulting firm?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;There isn't a single answer.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In fact, for a lot of developer jobs, getting another
certificate isn't the first thing you should be thinking about. A good GitHub
profile, a few projects you can explain properly and some code that is actually
deployed can tell an employer much more about you.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That doesn't mean certifications are pointless. They can be
useful, particularly if you're changing careers, moving into enterprise
blockchain or applying for a job that specifically asks for one.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The trick is knowing when the certificate is worth paying
for.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Start With the Job, Not the Certificate&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It's easy to get lost in the number of blockchain courses
and certifications available today.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;There are programs covering Ethereum, Solidity,
smart-contract security, Hyperledger, enterprise blockchain and pretty much
every other corner of the industry. Some cost a few hundred dollars, while
others run into the thousands.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Before spending anything, look at the jobs you actually
want.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's because blockchain development is one of those areas
where employers can often see what you've built.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A Solidity developer can put a contract on a public testnet.
An open-source developer can point to GitHub contributions. A security
researcher can show audit findings. Someone working with Hyperledger can
demonstrate a working Fabric application.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Those things are difficult to fake.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A recent analysis from Web3.Career looked at 30 blockchain
developer job listings and found that only two specifically mentioned a named
certification as required or preferred. The remaining listings put more
emphasis on practical skills and experience.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It's a relatively small sample, so it shouldn't be treated
as a rule for the entire industry.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Still, it illustrates something worth remembering: &lt;b&gt;blockchain
developer hiring is usually about what you can build, not how many certificates
you have collected.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;So, Are Certifications Worth It?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Sometimes, absolutely.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Imagine you're already working in software development but
have never touched Ethereum or Solidity. A structured blockchain program can
give you a way to learn the basics without trying to piece everything together
yourself.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The same applies if you're moving from IT, cybersecurity or
finance into blockchain.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A certificate can also be useful when you're applying to
companies where formal qualifications are part of the hiring process.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Enterprise blockchain is a good example.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A developer working on a permissioned blockchain for a bank
has a very different career path from someone writing smart contracts for a
DeFi protocol. The technologies, employers and expectations can all be
different.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's why choosing a certificate based purely on popularity
can be a mistake.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Free Route Is Better Than Many People Realize&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Before paying for anything, there are some excellent free
resources available.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;And if you're serious about becoming a developer, you should
probably use them anyway.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Cyfrin Updraft&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Cyfrin Updraft is one of the more useful free options for
people learning Solidity and smart-contract security.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The courses are designed around actual development rather
than just blockchain theory, and the material progresses from Solidity
fundamentals toward more advanced development and security topics.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's important because you can take what you've learned
and turn it into something you can show another person.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Ethereum.org also points developers toward Cyfrin's
resources when discussing smart-contract security.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For someone starting out, I'd take this route before paying
for an expensive certification.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Alchemy University&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Alchemy University is another good place to start.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Its courses cover Ethereum development, Solidity and Web3
application development, with practical exercises and projects included in the
learning process.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The real benefit isn't the course completion itself.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It's what you do afterward.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If you finish a course and then build your own application,
put the code on GitHub and deploy it, you've created something useful for your
portfolio.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Chainlink Fundamentals Certification&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Developers interested in oracle infrastructure have another
option through Chainlink's developer education ecosystem.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The &lt;b&gt;Chainlink Fundamentals Certification&lt;/b&gt; is available
as a credential and is particularly relevant if you're interested in building
applications that use Chainlink technology.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It's a good example of when a specialized certification
makes more sense than a broad "blockchain expert" certificate.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If the technology appears repeatedly in the jobs you're
applying for, the credential has a clearer purpose.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Ethereum.org&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;There is also the simplest option: read the documentation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Ethereum.org has extensive developer documentation covering
smart contracts, development, security and the Ethereum ecosystem.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It isn't glamorous.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;There is no expensive certificate at the end.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But understanding the primary documentation is part of
becoming a developer. Eventually, every serious Ethereum developer has to get
comfortable reading technical documentation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Security Developers Have Another Path&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If you're interested in smart-contract auditing, your
priorities should be different.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A certificate might help you get started, but security work
is ultimately about whether you can find problems that other people missed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's why public audit contests can be useful.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Code4rena, Sherlock and Cantina provide opportunities for
researchers to examine real smart contracts and look for vulnerabilities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A documented finding from a legitimate contest can give an
employer something concrete to evaluate.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It also teaches you something that a normal course often
can't: how to read unfamiliar contracts and think like an attacker.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For someone who wants to become an auditor, that experience
can be extremely valuable.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Paid Certifications: Which Ones Make Sense?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If you've already gone through the free resources and still
want a formal credential, there are several options worth knowing about.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But don't buy one simply because the website says it will
make you "job ready."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;EC-Council Blockchain Developer Certification&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;EC-Council has a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/the-most-underrated-crypto-projects.html"&gt;Blockchain &lt;/a&gt;Developer Certification covering
areas such as blockchain fundamentals, cryptography, Ethereum and enterprise
blockchain technologies.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It's more suited to someone looking for a structured
certification program than an experienced developer who already has years of
Solidity work behind them.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The price can vary depending on the training package and
provider, so check the current official pricing before paying.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;101 Blockchains Certified Enterprise Blockchain
Professional&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;This is aimed more toward enterprise blockchain than
hands-on Solidity development.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If you're interested in blockchain consulting, business
analysis, architecture or enterprise implementation, that focus can be useful.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It isn't necessarily the best choice for someone whose goal
is to spend most of the day writing Ethereum smart contracts.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Blockchain Council Certified Blockchain Developer&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Blockchain Council offers a Certified Blockchain Developer
program aimed at developers and people moving into blockchain from other
technology backgrounds.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The main advantage is the structured learning path and
formal credential.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The limitation is the same one you'll find with most general
blockchain certifications: the certificate itself doesn't demonstrate how well
you can code.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's why it should ideally be combined with actual
projects.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Certified Blockchain Developer – Ethereum&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The Blockchain Training Alliance also offers an
Ethereum-focused developer certification.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;This is more directly aligned with people interested in
Ethereum and smart-contract development.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Again, check the jobs you're targeting before buying it. If
none of the companies you're interested in recognize or request the
certification, your money may be better spent elsewhere.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Hyperledger Is a Different Story&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If you're interested in enterprise blockchain, Hyperledger
deserves separate consideration.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The &lt;b&gt;Hyperledger Fabric Certified Practitioner (HFCP)&lt;/b&gt;
is offered through the Linux Foundation and is specifically focused on
Hyperledger Fabric.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The current Linux Foundation listing shows the exam at &lt;b&gt;$250&lt;/b&gt;,
with the certification valid for &lt;b&gt;two years&lt;/b&gt;. A course-and-exam bundle is
listed at &lt;b&gt;$299&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's a much more targeted credential.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If you're applying for a role that involves Hyperledger
Fabric, banks, supply-chain systems or other permissioned blockchain
environments, it can make sense.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If you're trying to become a DeFi developer, however, it
probably isn't the certification you need.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Don't Forget About the Total Cost&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Certification prices can be misleading if you only look at
the initial fee.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Some programs require renewal. Others charge separately for
training, exams and retakes.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;So before buying anything, check the full cost.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Ask yourself:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;How much is the initial exam?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Do I need to buy training separately?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;How long does the certification remain valid?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;What does renewal cost?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Is the credential actually recognized by the employers I'm
targeting?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A certificate that costs $300 today may cost considerably
more over several years if it requires regular renewal.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;And if employers don't care about it, even a cheap
certificate isn't necessarily good value.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What About India?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For developers in India, there are additional options worth
looking at.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;University-backed blockchain programs can be useful if
you're trying to move into traditional corporate technology roles where
institutional branding carries some weight.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;There are also programs associated with institutions such as
IITs and training organizations offering blockchain development courses.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The &lt;b&gt;Kerala Blockchain Academy&lt;/b&gt;, for example, provides
blockchain education and training and has programs connected with technologies
including Hyperledger.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But don't choose a course just because it has a famous name
attached to it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Look at the actual syllabus.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Find out how much coding is involved.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Check whether students build real applications.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;And, if possible, look at where previous students ended up
working.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's more useful than relying on a marketing page
promising that a certificate will transform your career.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What I'd Do If I Were Starting Today&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If I were starting blockchain development from scratch in
2026, I wouldn't begin by buying a certificate.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;I'd start with the fundamentals.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Learn Solidity.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Understand how Ethereum transactions and smart contracts
work.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Build a few small applications.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Deploy at least one contract to a public test network.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Put everything on GitHub.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Then write about what you built.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Explain why you made certain decisions, what went wrong and
how you fixed it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That last part matters more than people think.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Being able to explain your own code during an interview is
much more convincing than simply saying you've completed a course.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Once you've done that, look at the jobs you're interested
in.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If they consistently ask for a particular certification, get
it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If they don't, keep building.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Which Option Is Best for You?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;There really isn't one universal winner.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If you want to become a &lt;b&gt;Solidity or DeFi developer&lt;/b&gt;,
start with Ethereum's documentation, Cyfrin Updraft and hands-on projects.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If you're interested in &lt;b&gt;smart-contract security&lt;/b&gt;,
spend more time learning vulnerabilities and participating in audit contests.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If you're targeting &lt;b&gt;Hyperledger Fabric&lt;/b&gt;, the Linux
Foundation's HFCP is a much more relevant credential.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If you want to move into &lt;b&gt;enterprise blockchain consulting
or strategy&lt;/b&gt;, an enterprise-focused certification may make more sense.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;And if you're a &lt;b&gt;career switcher&lt;/b&gt;, a structured
certification can give you a useful foundation while you build practical
experience.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The important thing is not to confuse completing a course
with becoming a developer.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;They're not the same thing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Blockchain certifications aren't useless.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;They're just not magic.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For some people, a recognized credential can help
demonstrate that they've learned a particular technology. For others,
especially developers applying to Web3 startups, the better investment may be
time spent building and contributing to real projects.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's why the smartest approach in 2026 is fairly simple.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Learn the technology. Build something. Put it online.
Show your work. Then get the certification if the job actually calls for it.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A certificate can strengthen your résumé.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It can't write your code for you.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;And when you're sitting in a technical interview, that's
usually the part that matters most.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

cryptocurrency, technology and financial markets. This article is intended for
informational purposes only and does not constitute professional, financial or
career advice.&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>The CLARITY Act: A Defining Moment for U.S. Crypto Markets</title>

    <title>Cypherpunk Launches Major Zcash Mining Fleet After $33M Winklevoss Deal</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgFV14sbExI_1pLQ4JO0WBSaJgLUPM7swdl-5alQdzJxYFSNkq4cgfRd8sNK3pGtkR3WL6g7BXj6bbQywEMbkOglCzPQQ-KiaB4WWv-9WbM2-xsoH5ceo8jqIRlSkrIv8okNWJndY0DM_BLo9wWopI_9Lcr7rHafsrXLD15yjOLtXFoMWMB13_4zECLkC14/s1672/cypherpunk-zcash-mining-fleet-winklevoss-deal-2026.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Cypherpunk launches a major Zcash mining fleet with 4.2 GSol/s of Equihash hashrate after a $33.33 million Winklevoss Capital deal." border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgFV14sbExI_1pLQ4JO0WBSaJgLUPM7swdl-5alQdzJxYFSNkq4cgfRd8sNK3pGtkR3WL6g7BXj6bbQywEMbkOglCzPQQ-KiaB4WWv-9WbM2-xsoH5ceo8jqIRlSkrIv8okNWJndY0DM_BLo9wWopI_9Lcr7rHafsrXLD15yjOLtXFoMWMB13_4zECLkC14/w320-h180/cypherpunk-zcash-mining-fleet-winklevoss-deal-2026.webp.png" title="Cypherpunk Launches Major Zcash Mining Fleet After $33M Winklevoss Deal" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/i&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Cypherpunk Technologies, the Nasdaq-listed privacy
technology company, says it has launched what it describes as the world's
largest Zcash mining fleet. The operation, dubbed&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Cypherpunk Mining&lt;/b&gt;,
came online with roughly&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;4.2 GSol/s of Equihash hashrate&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;deployed
across the United States.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The 4.2 GSol/s deployment represents roughly&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;18% of
Zcash's network hashrate&lt;/b&gt;, according to Cypherpunk. The entire project was
funded through a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$33.33 million equity-based transaction with
Winklevoss Capital&lt;/b&gt;—the venture firm of Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;U.S.-based facilities&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Cypherpunk estimates the current addressable mining market
at more than&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$250 million annually&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;based on prevailing ZEC
prices. With this launch, Cypherpunk Mining immediately becomes the Zcash
network's largest active fleet.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why This Is Different From Regular Mining News&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Most mining stories are about hashrate. This one is about
something bigger.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Cypherpunk describes itself as the largest corporate holder
of ZEC, currently sitting on&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;323,394 ZEC&lt;/b&gt;—about&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;1.92% of the
circulating supply&lt;/b&gt;. The company's stated goal is to reach&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;5% of
ZEC's entire supply&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The mining operation is designed to accelerate that path.
&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/citis-custody-launches-bitcoin-custody.html"&gt;Cypherpunk&lt;/a&gt; estimates that miners collectively receive roughly&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;43,800
ZEC per month&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in block rewards, and Cypherpunk says its mining
economics allow it to produce ZEC at costs significantly below the prevailing
spot price.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Will McEvoy, Cypherpunk's Chief Investment Officer, put it
this way:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"The Zcash flow from Cypherpunk Mining provides
financial and operational flexibility to fund future growth, the acquisition of
additional ZEC, and new privacy-preserving technology investments."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Winklevoss Connection&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The involvement of the Winklevoss twins adds another layer
of intrigue. Through the transaction, Winklevoss Capital gained exposure to
Cypherpunk's Zcash mining strategy through the financing arrangement.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Their statement on the deal was characteristically direct:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"Up until now, investors have had limited options for
Zcash mining exposure. With the acquisition of this mining fleet, Cypherpunk
changes that."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The transaction was structured as a warrant deal—Winklevoss
Treasury Investments received a pre-funded warrant to purchase 43,290,042
shares of Cypherpunk at an exercise price of $0.001 per share, reflecting a
purchase price of $0.77 per share.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Network Effect&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Cypherpunk is framing this as a win for Zcash itself. The
argument is straightforward:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"The additional mining hashrate and decentralization
strengthens &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/crypto-regulation-could-reverse-without.html"&gt;Zcash&lt;/a&gt; network security, and a more secure Zcash makes Cypherpunk's
treasury more valuable."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;With approximately 18% of network hashrate attributed to its
fleet, Cypherpunk will represent a significant share of Zcash mining activity.
The company's incentives are aligned with the network's long-term health,
though the concentration also raises questions about mining centralization as
the fleet expands.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Kevin Zhang Joins the Team&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Cypherpunk also brought in&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Kevin Zhang&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;as
Head of Mining. His resume is worth paying attention to: he began mining
Bitcoin in 2014, built some of the largest Bitcoin mining facilities in North
America, led the first power plant conversion to Bitcoin mining in North
America in 2019, and at Foundry, he built the largest Bitcoin mining pool in
the world.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Zhang's take on Zcash mining is bullish:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"Approximately 1,440 ZEC is awarded to miners each day,
making Zcash mining highly profitable. Even if the Zcash network hashrate
increases significantly, Zcash mining still out-earns AI colocation and Bitcoin
mining at today's ZEC prices."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;He added that the opportunity in Zcash mining shows "a
striking similarity to Bitcoin mining in 2016."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bigger Picture&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Cypherpunk's move is part of a broader strategy. The company
already holds ZEC, has invested in ZODL, a prominent Zcash wallet, and now has
a mining arm.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"Following the expansion of our ZEC treasury and
investment in ZODL, Zcash mining is the next piece of the constellation of
privacy technologies we're assembling," McEvoy said.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The implication is clear: Cypherpunk is trying to build a
vertically integrated Zcash ecosystem—holder, miner, and wallet provider.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What This Means For Zcash&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The launch of Cypherpunk Mining is significant for a few
reasons:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol start="1" style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="1"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Concentrated
     hashrate&lt;/b&gt;: One entity now accounts for roughly 18% of the network's
     hashrate. That raises centralization concerns, but Cypherpunk argues it
     strengthens network security.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Institutional
     interest&lt;/b&gt;: A Nasdaq-listed company backed by Winklevoss Capital is
     betting big on Zcash. That's a signal.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Vertical
     integration&lt;/b&gt;: Cypherpunk is positioning itself as a one-stop shop for
     Zcash exposure—treasury, mining, and wallet.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Profitability
     signal&lt;/b&gt;: If Zhang is right about Zcash mining out-earning Bitcoin
     mining, it could attract more institutional capital to the network.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Cypherpunk Technologies has committed $33.33 million through
a financing transaction tied to its Zcash mining strategy. The fleet is live,
the hashrate is real, and the network now has one of the largest mining
operations in its history.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For Zcash holders, it's a sign of institutional commitment.
For the privacy community, it represents another sign of institutional interest
in Zcash's privacy-focused ecosystem. And for Cypherpunk, it's another step
toward its goal of holding 5% of all ZEC in existence.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The bigger question now is whether Cypherpunk's bet will
attract more institutional capital—or raise fresh concerns about mining
concentration across the Zcash network. Either way, Zcash has become a much
more interesting institutional mining story.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;The mining fleet launched August 18, 2026, with
approximately 4.2 GSol/s of Equihash hashrate deployed across U.S.-based
facilities.&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>

    <title>Kraken Parent Payward Delays IPO to Q2 2027 at Earliest as Crypto Market Tests Investor Appetite</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhoiCXWvHvABsE7bua4NT4-3Q1NIQt3AtXgg7kPmDnT8-j5L1M4t8pgsKDX7H291DdTa2EsLE-beDqCg7tmrT2ws4QsQxYvM9d3oG8gY-RGxgwyt_ayX3WuQCrXy9Ub7N-WnKnBxJ2WMDSrL2otS8ItbYAjjdSiO0kKfnZe-hvliK97ow5X7nQolfjVw_TD/s1672/kraken-payward-ipo-delayed-q2-2027.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Kraken parent Payward delays IPO to Q2 2027 amid crypto market uncertainty" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhoiCXWvHvABsE7bua4NT4-3Q1NIQt3AtXgg7kPmDnT8-j5L1M4t8pgsKDX7H291DdTa2EsLE-beDqCg7tmrT2ws4QsQxYvM9d3oG8gY-RGxgwyt_ayX3WuQCrXy9Ub7N-WnKnBxJ2WMDSrL2otS8ItbYAjjdSiO0kKfnZe-hvliK97ow5X7nQolfjVw_TD/w400-h225/kraken-payward-ipo-delayed-q2-2027.jpg.png" title="Kraken Parent Payward IPO Delayed to Q2 2027" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Payward, the parent company of cryptocurrency exchange Kraken, has reportedly pushed back its planned initial public offering to the second quarter of 2027 at the earliest.&lt;/strong&gt; The latest delay extends the company's wait for a public listing after it paused the IPO process earlier this year as difficult crypto-market conditions made the timing less attractive.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new timeline was reported by &lt;a href="https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/09/02/kraken-parent-payward-pushes-ipo-back-to-mid-2027-at-earliest" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;CoinDesk&lt;/a&gt; on September 2, citing people familiar with the matter. Payward has not announced a firm IPO date, so Q2 2027 should be viewed as the earliest reported window rather than a confirmed listing date.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Is Kraken's Parent Delaying Its IPO?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The simplest explanation is market timing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Payward confidentially filed a draft S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in November 2025 for a proposed IPO. At the time, the company was valued at $20 billion after raising $800 million in new funding, including a $200 million investment from Citadel Securities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the environment changed quickly. By March 2026, Payward had put its IPO plans on hold. &lt;a href="https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/03/17/crypto-exchange-kraken-freezes-multibillion-dollar-ipo-plan-due-to-difficult-market-conditions" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;CoinDesk reported&lt;/a&gt; at the time that people familiar with the matter said the company could revisit the listing when market conditions improved.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That caution makes sense for a business whose historical performance has been closely connected to activity in cryptocurrency markets. When Bitcoin and other &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/how-does-blockchain-really-work.html"&gt;digital assets&lt;/a&gt; fall sharply, investors often become less willing to trade, leverage and take risk. That can put pressure on exchange activity and, in turn, the valuation investors are willing to assign to an exchange.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin's Downturn Has Changed the Backdrop&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's performance is an important part of the story.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;During the first quarter of 2026, Bitcoin fell about 22%, according to CoinDesk's reporting on Payward's Q1 results. The broader cryptocurrency market capitalization declined 23%, while industry-wide spot trading volume dropped 38.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That weakness changed the backdrop for crypto companies looking toward public markets. A major exchange can continue to grow its customer base and products while still facing pressure when overall trading activity and investor risk appetite weaken.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Payward, the issue is therefore not simply the price of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/i-found-old-bitcoin-txid-can-i-recover.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt;. It is whether the broader crypto cycle provides a strong enough environment for public investors to assign an attractive valuation to an exchange and financial-services platform.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Payward's Revenue Has Held Up Better Than Trading Activity&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is another side to the story that is easy to miss.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Payward's second-quarter results did not show a collapse in revenue. The company reported &lt;strong&gt;$508 million in adjusted revenue for Q2 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, up 17% from the same quarter a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA remained positive at $23 million.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That compares with &lt;strong&gt;$507 million of adjusted revenue in Q1 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, meaning quarterly revenue was broadly flat sequentially rather than falling from $602 million to $508 million. The $602 million figure sometimes cited in discussions around Payward does not match the company's reported adjusted-revenue figure for Q1.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company's own Q2 financial release provides the relevant figures and shows that revenue remained resilient despite a more difficult trading environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, transaction activity did decline.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Payward reported &lt;strong&gt;$310 billion in total platform transaction volume in Q2&lt;/strong&gt;, down from &lt;strong&gt;$357 billion in Q1&lt;/strong&gt;. The company also said crypto spot volumes were declining across the industry while activity in futures, equities and tokenized equities was growing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important. Payward's revenue did not fall sharply between Q1 and Q2, but the lower transaction volume shows why the company is working to diversify beyond traditional spot crypto trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Numbers Show Why Payward Is Diversifying&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Payward's latest results suggest that the company is trying to make its business less dependent on one source of revenue.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In Q2, asset-based and other revenue represented 60% of total revenue, compared with 55% in the same quarter a year earlier. Funded accounts increased 42% year over year to 6.6 million, while assets on the platform stood at $40 billion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Futures activity also remained important. Payward said futures daily average revenue trades increased 8% year over year in Q2. In Q1, futures DARTs had risen 51% year over year, helped by the company's NinjaTrader business and expanded derivatives offering.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That diversification could ultimately help Payward's IPO case. A company with several sources of revenue can potentially be less exposed to the boom-and-bust cycle of spot cryptocurrency trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Q2 2027 Could Be a Better IPO Window&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Waiting until 2027 gives Payward additional time to show whether its newer businesses can become meaningful contributors to the company's financial performance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It also gives the cryptocurrency market more time to stabilize.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Public investors typically want visibility into revenue, profitability and growth before assigning a valuation to a company. For a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-is-bitcoin-price-rising-so-fast.html"&gt;crypto exchange&lt;/a&gt;, the challenge is greater because market cycles can dramatically change trading activity within a matter of months.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Payward's strategy appears to be moving beyond that cycle.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company has been expanding across trading, derivatives, equities, tokenized assets and financial infrastructure. Its second-quarter results highlighted growth across several parts of the business rather than relying exclusively on spot crypto trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Kraken Is Expanding Beyond Crypto Trading&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the most significant developments for Payward is its push into tokenized financial assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Payward's xStocks platform allows eligible users to access blockchain-based representations of equities. The company has also been expanding the distribution of xStocks to additional networks and wallets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That strategy is becoming more relevant as traditional financial institutions move deeper into blockchain infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In September, &lt;a href="https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/lseg-plans-tokenised-uk-shares-partners-with-kraken-owner-payward-2026-09-01/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Reuters reported&lt;/a&gt; that London Stock Exchange Group plans to work with Payward on tokenized UK shares. The initiative is aimed at bringing blockchain-based representations of London-listed equities to investors familiar with digital-asset markets, subject to regulatory approval.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The partnership is important because it shows where Payward may want to position itself by the time it eventually goes public: not simply as a cryptocurrency exchange, but as a broader digital financial infrastructure company.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The $20 Billion Valuation Is Still an Important Reference Point&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Payward's $20 billion valuation from November 2025 remains an important benchmark when thinking about the potential IPO.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, a private funding valuation should not automatically be treated as the price public-market investors would accept.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The crypto market was considerably stronger when Payward raised that capital. Since then, Bitcoin has suffered a major drawdown, crypto trading activity has weakened and investors have become more selective about companies whose earnings are tied to digital-asset cycles.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a difficult question for Payward: should it list quickly and risk accepting a lower valuation, or wait and try to demonstrate that its expanding product mix can support a stronger public-market case?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The reported decision to wait until Q2 2027 at the earliest suggests the company is choosing the second option.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Is the Payward IPO Cancelled?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No.&lt;/strong&gt; There is currently no indication that Payward has abandoned its IPO plans.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company previously paused the process in March, while the latest reporting says it does not plan to go public before the second quarter of 2027. Its confidential SEC filing remains an important part of the company's IPO history.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Still, investors should not treat Q2 2027 as a guaranteed date. IPO plans can change because of market conditions, regulatory review, company performance or investor demand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Investors Should Watch Before the IPO&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin and crypto prices:&lt;/strong&gt; A stronger digital-asset market could improve trading activity and investor sentiment.&lt;/li&gt;

&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Trading volumes:&lt;/strong&gt; Payward will need to demonstrate that weaker spot activity can be offset by derivatives, equities, tokenized assets and other businesses.&lt;/li&gt;

&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Revenue diversification:&lt;/strong&gt; The increasing contribution from asset-based and other revenue could make Payward's business less dependent on trading cycles.&lt;/li&gt;

&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Profitability:&lt;/strong&gt; Investors will likely focus closely on whether Payward can turn revenue growth into consistently stronger EBITDA and cash generation.&lt;/li&gt;

&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Regulatory developments:&lt;/strong&gt; The company's growing number of regulated products could become an important part of its public-market story.&lt;/li&gt;

&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Public crypto valuations:&lt;/strong&gt; The performance of other listed digital-asset companies will provide an important signal about investor appetite when Payward eventually launches its offering.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the Delay Means for Kraken&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Kraken customers, the IPO delay does not fundamentally change the exchange's operations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Payward is continuing to build products and expand internationally. Its Q2 results showed growth in funded accounts, derivatives and newer financial products even while overall platform transaction volume declined.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The delay may actually give the company more time to strengthen that broader business.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If Payward can demonstrate that revenue remains resilient through a difficult crypto cycle, while its newer businesses continue to grow, the company could eventually approach the public markets with a different story from the one it had in late 2025.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Payward's reported decision to push the Kraken IPO to &lt;strong&gt;Q2 2027 at the earliest&lt;/strong&gt; is less about abandoning the public-market ambition and more about choosing a better moment to pursue it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The market backdrop has changed significantly since Payward's $20 billion valuation in November 2025. Bitcoin suffered a major decline, industry-wide spot trading activity weakened and investors became more cautious about crypto-linked businesses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, Payward's own financial results show that the company is not simply shrinking with the crypto market. Q2 adjusted revenue reached $508 million, funded accounts climbed to 6.6 million and the company remained adjusted-EBITDA positive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bigger story, therefore, is diversification.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Payward is increasingly positioning itself around derivatives, equities, tokenized assets, payments and financial infrastructure. Its partnership with London Stock Exchange Group is another indication that the company sees blockchain as something broader than cryptocurrency trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;For now, Q2 2027 is the earliest reported IPO window—not a confirmed listing date.&lt;/strong&gt; Whether Payward ultimately goes public then will depend heavily on crypto-market conditions, the company's financial performance and how much confidence public-market investors are willing to place in the next phase of the digital-asset industry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;When will Kraken's parent company Payward IPO?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Payward is reportedly not planning to go public before the second quarter of 2027. However, the company has not publicly confirmed a specific IPO date.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why was the Kraken IPO delayed?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Payward previously paused its IPO plans in March 2026 amid difficult cryptocurrency market conditions. Lower crypto prices, weaker trading activity and investor caution created a less favorable environment for a listing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Has Payward cancelled its IPO?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. Current reporting indicates that the IPO has been delayed rather than cancelled. Payward previously filed a confidential draft S-1 with the SEC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What was Payward's Q2 2026 revenue?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Payward reported &lt;strong&gt;$508 million in adjusted revenue&lt;/strong&gt; for Q2 2026, up 17% year over year. Adjusted EBITDA was $23 million.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Did Payward's trading volume fall in Q2 2026?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes. Total platform transaction volume was &lt;strong&gt;$310 billion in Q2&lt;/strong&gt;, compared with &lt;strong&gt;$357 billion in Q1&lt;/strong&gt;. Payward said crypto spot volumes declined across the industry while equities and tokenized-equity activity grew.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What was Payward's Q1 2026 revenue?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Payward reported &lt;strong&gt;$507 million in adjusted revenue for Q1 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, up 3% year over year.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Q2 2027 a confirmed Kraken IPO date?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. Q2 2027 is the earliest reported timeframe. The actual listing date could change depending on market conditions, regulatory developments and investor demand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why is the Kraken IPO important for the crypto industry?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;A successful Payward listing would give public-market investors another major way to gain exposure to digital-asset infrastructure and could provide an important signal about institutional and retail investor appetite for crypto-related businesses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Editorial note:&lt;/strong&gt; This article was updated on September 3, 2026, using current reporting and Payward's published Q1 and Q2 2026 financial information. Q2 2027 is reported as the earliest potential IPO window and should not be interpreted as a confirmed listing date.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Can AI Autonomously Own and Manage Cryptocurrency? What's Actually Possible in 2026</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgXxnf071la6kvL4l08D5V0uogG1leIy0lIARRQzyygOvcldAIU7pP4uTiMOtvCk2tXvqwNHzVJhM9f0LeJL2D0qK0KvwUzw5OjABHysliTdJRpEI5xI4JoPafTYLzXC5v0alUnpOmrcPPeqygljX6mGnl5MGPy2D1z5ClD_sL0JiXG9raHIfyPH2PlmK6t/s1248/ai-autonomous-crypto-wallet-management-2026.jpg.jpg" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="AI agent managing a cryptocurrency wallet and executing autonomous crypto transactions" border="0" data-original-height="832" data-original-width="1248" height="426" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgXxnf071la6kvL4l08D5V0uogG1leIy0lIARRQzyygOvcldAIU7pP4uTiMOtvCk2tXvqwNHzVJhM9f0LeJL2D0qK0KvwUzw5OjABHysliTdJRpEI5xI4JoPafTYLzXC5v0alUnpOmrcPPeqygljX6mGnl5MGPy2D1z5ClD_sL0JiXG9raHIfyPH2PlmK6t/w640-h426/ai-autonomous-crypto-wallet-management-2026.jpg.jpg" title="Can AI Own and Manage Cryptocurrency in 2026?" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;Can AI autonomously own and manage cryptocurrency? The honest answer depends on what you mean by "own" and "manage."&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI agents can already interact with crypto wallets. They can authorize transactions, send payments, swap tokens, and follow rules set by their operators. Developers are building systems that allow software to perform these tasks with varying degrees of autonomy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But controlling a wallet and actually owning what's inside it are two very different things.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI does not automatically become the legal owner of Bitcoin simply because it has access to the credentials used to move it. In most practical arrangements, ownership and accountability remain connected to a person, company, or other legal structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That gap between "the AI can move the money" and "the AI owns the money" is becoming increasingly important as AI agents move from providing recommendations to taking financial actions themselves.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can an AI Agent Control a Crypto Wallet?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Yes, technically.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A crypto wallet is software or infrastructure that manages the cryptographic credentials used to authorize blockchain transactions. The &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/pumpfun-app-temporarily-unavailable-on.html"&gt;blockchain&lt;/a&gt; does not require a human to manually press a button for every transaction. If valid authorization is provided, software can interact with the network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is one reason crypto can be particularly useful for AI agents. An AI agent can be given controlled wallet access and configured to monitor balances, send tokens, swap assets, or interact with decentralized applications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/02/24/crypto-wallets-for-ai-agents-are-creating-a-new-legal-frontier-says-electric-capital" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;CoinDesk reported in February 2026&lt;/a&gt; that Electric Capital's Avichal Garg was seeing developers give AI agents crypto wallets, allowing them to hold assets, pay for services, trade tokens and even interact economically with other agents.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The technology is developing faster than the legal frameworks surrounding autonomous software.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But giving an AI control of a wallet is not the same as giving it legal ownership of the assets inside.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Technical Control Is Not Legal Ownership&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is the distinction at the center of the debate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Suppose a company sets up an AI agent and funds a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/esma-warns-crypto-and-traditional.html"&gt;wallet&lt;/a&gt; with $10,000 in USDC. The AI may be authorized to decide when to spend the funds. That does not automatically make the AI the legal owner of the $10,000.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Depending on the arrangement and jurisdiction, the assets could belong to:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The person who funded the wallet&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The company operating the AI system&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A DAO or similar structure, depending on its legal arrangement&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Another identifiable legal entity responsible for the wallet&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A &lt;a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14219" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;February 2026 paper titled "The Agent Economy: A Blockchain-Based Foundation for Autonomous AI Agents"&lt;/a&gt; examines this problem and discusses how autonomous AI agents could participate in economic activity through blockchain infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The paper explores mechanisms that could support greater economic autonomy for AI agents. But it is a research proposal, not evidence that AI agents have already received general legal personhood or independent ownership rights.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI agents do not currently have general legal personhood under the frameworks discussed in these sources.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;So What Can an Autonomous Crypto AI Actually Do?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Quite a lot, provided the system has the necessary permissions and infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Needs exchange, DEX, or execution access&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Yes&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Spending limits should be defined&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Legally own crypto&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Not automatically&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Control and ownership are separate&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How AI Crypto Wallets Actually Work&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You do not simply hand an AI system unrestricted access to a private key and hope for the best. More robust systems are built in layers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A typical setup can include:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The AI model&lt;/strong&gt; — interprets information and determines what action may be appropriate.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The wallet&lt;/strong&gt; — holds assets and provides the ability to authorize blockchain transactions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The permission layer&lt;/strong&gt; — establishes boundaries on what the AI can do.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The execution system&lt;/strong&gt; — sends an approved transaction to the blockchain or financial venue.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Risk controls&lt;/strong&gt; — limit transaction sizes, destinations, assets, or frequency.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Monitoring&lt;/strong&gt; — records activity and can stop the system when abnormal behavior is detected.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The safest designs do not treat an AI's reasoning as unlimited financial authority.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A 2026 &lt;a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.30519" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;research proposal on agentic finance&lt;/a&gt; explores separating an AI agent's ability to recommend an action from the authority required to execute it. The proposed approach places a control layer between the agent and financial execution so that identity, ownership, mandate, and risk limits can be checked before a transaction is carried out.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Crypto Is a Natural Fit for AI Agents&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional financial systems were largely designed around identifiable people and organizations. Opening a bank account normally involves identity checks, contracts, and institutions determining who is authorized to act.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchains operate differently.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A wallet address can send and receive digital assets without a conventional bank account. If a system has the required credentials and permissions, it can interact directly with a blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes crypto particularly useful for machine-to-machine payments, automated services, and AI agents that need to pay for digital resources.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/05/08/ai-agents-could-solve-crypto-s-user-problem" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;CoinDesk has also examined this trend&lt;/a&gt;, including the potential for autonomous software to use crypto wallets and stablecoins for programmable payments between machines.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader concept is often called the &lt;strong&gt;agent economy&lt;/strong&gt;: software can transact with other software without requiring a human to approve every individual payment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Agents Can Manage Crypto Without Human Approval for Every Trade&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Autonomous does not mean unlimited.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A human or organization can establish rules such as:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Maximum transaction size&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Approved wallet addresses&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Approved tokens&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Daily or weekly spending limits&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Trading strategies&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Maximum portfolio exposure&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Automatic emergency shutdown conditions&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI can then operate within those boundaries.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Think of it like giving an employee a company card with a spending limit. The employee can make purchases without asking the CEO before every transaction, but the spending authority still comes from the organization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If an AI Makes a Bad Trade?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where the legal and operational questions become much harder.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If an AI buys the wrong token, sends funds to an incorrect address, or makes a trade that causes a major loss, the blockchain does not reverse the transaction simply because an AI made the decision.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Responsibility therefore has to be traced back to the people or entities that created, funded, controlled, deployed, or authorized the system, depending on the circumstances.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.trmlabs.com/resources/blog/autonomous-ai-agents-and-financial-crime-risk-responsibility-and-accountability" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;TRM Labs explains&lt;/a&gt; that AI agents do not have legal personhood and that accountability can remain connected to developers, operators, deployers, and beneficiaries depending on control, knowledge, and economic benefit.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That raises one of the central questions surrounding autonomous finance: &lt;strong&gt;who is responsible when software acts on someone else's authority?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;India Is Already Building for AI-Agent Payments&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is not purely theoretical.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.reuters.com/world/india/india-plans-ai-registry-it-looks-roll-out-agentic-payments-sources-say-2026-09-10/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Reuters reported in September 2026&lt;/a&gt; that the National Payments Corporation of India is developing a registry intended to verify and monitor AI agents making transactions through UPI.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The framework could eventually support more complex use cases, including conditional purchases and potentially investment-related activity. Earlier &lt;a href="https://www.reuters.com/world/india/india-preparing-rollout-agentic-payments-upi-sources-say-2026-09-01/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Reuters reporting&lt;/a&gt; also described India's work on agentic payments through UPI within defined controls.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The development matters for crypto because it shows mainstream financial infrastructure beginning to address a world in which software can act on behalf of people and organizations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could an AI Actually Own Crypto One Day?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not simply by controlling a wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For an AI to be recognized as an independent owner, legal systems would need to answer several fundamental questions:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Can an AI have legal personality?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Can it enter binding contracts?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Can it be responsible for taxes?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Can it be sued?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Can it inherit assets?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who is liable for its debts?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who controls its assets if the AI system is shut down?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Who is responsible if it acts outside its instructions?&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These questions do not currently have a general, settled answer that would make an AI an ordinary legal owner of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/liquid-hack-takes-new-turn-as.html"&gt;cryptocurrency&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the more practical model is &lt;strong&gt;delegated control&lt;/strong&gt;: a person, company, or other recognized legal structure owns or controls the assets while an AI system receives limited authority to manage them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can AI Create Its Own Wallet?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Software can generate a cryptographic key pair and create a blockchain wallet address without a human manually creating the address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But creating an address is not the same as establishing legal ownership.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important questions remain: who authorized the system, who funded the wallet, what permissions were granted, and who is accountable for its actions?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This becomes even more important when AI agents interact with decentralized finance applications or with other autonomous agents.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can AI Trade Crypto Completely on Its Own?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes, technically. An AI trading system can monitor market information and execute trades without a person manually approving every transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But autonomous execution is not the same thing as profitable trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A September 2026 &lt;a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04917" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;academic review of AI in equity and crypto markets&lt;/a&gt; examined research available through August 31, 2026. The authors found progress in areas such as prediction, portfolio design, and execution, but concluded that public evidence remains insufficient to establish that a general AI architecture consistently delivers persistent, risk-adjusted net returns after real-world costs and execution constraints.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In simple terms, an AI can trade on its own without necessarily being a consistently successful trader.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Are the Biggest Risks?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;1. Unauthorized Transactions&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Giving an AI excessive wallet permissions can increase the consequences of a software bug, compromised agent, or flawed instruction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;2. Bad Decisions&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI systems can misunderstand information, rely on incorrect assumptions, or make poor decisions when market conditions change rapidly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;3. Smart-Contract Risk&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An autonomous agent interacting with DeFi protocols inherits the risks of those protocols, including bugs, exploits, and malicious contracts.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;4. Private-Key Security&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the credentials controlling a wallet are compromised, an attacker may be able to move the assets regardless of what the AI intended to do.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;5. Accountability&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The more autonomous a system becomes, the more important it is to identify the person or organization responsible for its actions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;6. Market Manipulation&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Large numbers of autonomous trading agents could interact with markets at machine speed, creating new questions around surveillance, manipulation, and responsibility.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader AI safety debate is moving in a similar direction. &lt;a href="https://openai.com/index/ai-policy-window/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;OpenAI said in a September 9, 2026 policy statement&lt;/a&gt; that it is pushing for mandatory, capability-based national AI safety requirements, including work with Congress on federal rules and support for several California AI-safety bills.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That policy debate is broader than cryptocurrency, but it illustrates why security, authorization, and accountability are becoming increasingly important as AI systems gain more ability to act independently.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Ownership vs. AI Management: The Short Version&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Can AI trade crypto autonomously?&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Yes, inside an automated system.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Does wallet control equal legal ownership?&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;No.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Is AI a legal person?&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Not generally.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Can humans delegate financial authority to AI?&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Yes, subject to applicable rules and law.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Will AI Ever Become an Independent Economic Actor?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Nobody knows yet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Technically, autonomous agents are becoming more capable. Crypto is an especially accessible environment for them because blockchain networks can execute transactions based on cryptographic authorization and programmable rules.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The harder problem is legal and institutional.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If AI agents eventually earn revenue, hold assets, hire other agents, and negotiate transactions without continuous human intervention, regulators and lawmakers may need new frameworks covering identity, ownership, taxation, authorization, and liability.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the direction is &lt;strong&gt;controlled autonomy&lt;/strong&gt;, not machine personhood. AI systems can act on behalf of humans and organizations, while accountability remains connected to an identifiable owner, operator, or legal structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can AI own cryptocurrency?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI can technically control a crypto wallet and manage digital assets, but control does not automatically establish legal ownership. Current frameworks generally connect ownership and accountability to a person or legal entity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can an AI agent have a crypto wallet?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Developers can create wallets and give AI agents permission to use them for receiving, sending, swapping, or trading digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can AI trade Bitcoin without a human?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. An automated AI system can analyze information and execute Bitcoin trades without manual approval for every transaction, provided it has the required access and permissions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Who owns crypto held by an AI wallet?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That depends on the legal and contractual structure surrounding the wallet. An AI controlling the wallet does not by itself determine who legally owns the assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can AI make crypto payments?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. AI agents can be configured to make blockchain payments. Broader financial infrastructure is also being developed to identify and authorize AI agents for digital payments. &lt;a href="https://www.reuters.com/world/india/india-plans-ai-registry-it-looks-roll-out-agentic-payments-sources-say-2026-09-10/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Reuters reported on India's planned AI-agent registry&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is autonomous AI crypto trading guaranteed to make money?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. Autonomous execution is a technical capability, not proof of profitability. The September 2026 academic review found that public evidence for persistent, risk-adjusted net AI trading returns remains limited. &lt;a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04917" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Read the research paper&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI can already manage cryptocurrency at the technical level, but that does not mean AI legally owns the cryptocurrency.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An autonomous agent can hold wallet access, monitor assets, execute transactions, make payments, and trade within rules established by its operator. That makes AI-managed crypto a real technical capability today, even though the legal framework is still catching up.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The unresolved part is ownership and accountability. For now, the realistic model is that a human, company, or other recognized legal structure owns or controls the assets and delegates limited authority to an AI system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As agentic payments and autonomous finance grow, the line between &lt;strong&gt;machine control and legal ownership&lt;/strong&gt; could become one of the defining issues in the next phase of crypto and AI.&lt;/p&gt;
