    <title>Singapore Exchange Targets U.S. Institutions With Crypto Perpetual Futures</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiniJNTAWP1kP7KFpnEYnCvCwVL27AsUf7XY6un9Z2D2D670smjoz0KhpI44f2utoQjsiW9p39gMLUGXaZaHNOvm-G90lhKwu_f0_kP_om7BQtGL05YoEgZgplC_bRCteUgq1QS0F9Tecy06SqdEA3_37Idd2whYRwjbO5LJms0UfeE-qd-Yc09bnraY0bh/s1672/singapore-exchange-sgx-bitcoin-ethereum-us-institutions.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Singapore Exchange SGX Bitcoin and Ethereum perpetual futures for U.S. institutions" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiniJNTAWP1kP7KFpnEYnCvCwVL27AsUf7XY6un9Z2D2D670smjoz0KhpI44f2utoQjsiW9p39gMLUGXaZaHNOvm-G90lhKwu_f0_kP_om7BQtGL05YoEgZgplC_bRCteUgq1QS0F9Tecy06SqdEA3_37Idd2whYRwjbO5LJms0UfeE-qd-Yc09bnraY0bh/w640-h360/singapore-exchange-sgx-bitcoin-ethereum-us-institutions.jpg.png" title="Singapore Exchange Expands Bitcoin and Ethereum Perpetual Futures Access" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Singapore Exchange (SGX) is taking another major step into institutional crypto markets by opening its Bitcoin and Ether perpetual futures to eligible U.S. institutional investors.&lt;/strong&gt; The move connects one of Asia's major regulated derivatives venues with U.S. trading firms and institutional capital, potentially giving professional investors another route into crypto derivatives outside traditional crypto-native exchanges.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The development is particularly important because perpetual futures have become one of the largest trading products in the digital-asset market. Unlike traditional futures, perpetual contracts do not have a fixed expiration date and typically use funding mechanisms to keep the contract price aligned with the underlying asset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SGX launched its &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ai-crashed-market-whos-liable.html"&gt;Bitcoin and Ethereum&lt;/a&gt; perpetual futures in November 2025. The exchange has since built meaningful activity around the products, with recent reporting putting cumulative trading volume at approximately &lt;strong&gt;$5.8 billion&lt;/strong&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is Singapore Exchange Planning?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At first glance, the announcement may look like another crypto derivatives expansion. In reality, the significance is broader.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SGX is bringing Bitcoin and Ether perpetual futures into a regulated exchange environment that is already familiar to institutional trading desks. Rather than forcing traditional investors to move into an offshore crypto exchange ecosystem, the structure gives eligible U.S. institutions access to crypto perpetuals through SGX's established derivatives infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The exchange's own rules identify its Bitcoin and Ethereum perpetual futures as products intended for &lt;strong&gt;Accredited Investors, Expert Investors and Institutional Investors&lt;/strong&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters. This is not simply a new retail crypto product. It is part of a broader effort to make crypto derivatives accessible through infrastructure designed for professional market participants.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Perpetual Futures Matter&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Perpetual futures have become a core part of crypto market structure because traders can maintain long or short positions without dealing with a conventional futures expiration date.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes them useful for several institutional strategies, including:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Hedging Bitcoin and Ether exposure&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Taking directional positions&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Managing portfolio risk&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Implementing basis and arbitrage strategies&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Providing liquidity to other market participants&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, perpetual futures also introduce significant leverage and funding-related risks. A trader can lose money rapidly if the market moves against a leveraged position.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why SGX's Move Is Significant&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most important part of the story is not simply that another exchange lists Bitcoin futures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is that a major traditional exchange is pushing a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/eric-balchunas-says-rising-us-interest.html"&gt;crypto-native&lt;/a&gt; derivatives product deeper into the institutional financial system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For years, much of the world's perpetual-futures activity has been concentrated on crypto-native exchanges. SGX represents a different model: regulated exchange infrastructure, established institutional relationships and a derivatives market that already serves global financial participants.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This could make crypto derivatives easier to evaluate for institutions that have strict compliance, custody, risk-management and operational requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin and Ether Are the Initial Focus&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SGX's initial crypto derivatives offering centers on &lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin and Ethereum&lt;/strong&gt;, the two largest crypto assets by market importance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is a logical starting point for an institutional exchange. Bitcoin and Ether have deep global markets, established derivatives ecosystems and broad recognition among professional investors.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SGX's Bitcoin and Ethereum perpetual futures were launched in November 2025, giving the exchange a track record before expanding access to U.S. institutional participants. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;SGX Is Trying to Bring Crypto Perpetuals Into Traditional Finance&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader trend is easy to see.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional exchanges, banks and financial infrastructure providers are increasingly building products around digital assets rather than treating crypto as a completely separate financial system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SGX's strategy fits directly into that transition. The exchange is not trying to turn itself into a retail crypto app. Instead, it is using its existing derivatives infrastructure to offer institutional-grade access to crypto products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction could become increasingly important as more investment firms seek exposure to Bitcoin and Ethereum while maintaining traditional compliance and risk-management frameworks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Makes SGX's Contracts Different?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why U.S. Institutions Could Be Interested&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Institutional investors often care about more than the underlying asset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They also need to consider regulation, counterparty exposure, operational controls, reporting, clearing arrangements and internal risk policies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A regulated exchange such as SGX can therefore offer a familiar environment for firms that may be uncomfortable using less traditional venues for large derivatives positions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For U.S. institutions specifically, the regulatory structure is particularly important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does CFTC Regulation 48.10 Have to Do With It?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission's &lt;strong&gt;Part 48&lt;/strong&gt; framework governs how foreign boards of trade can provide qualifying U.S. participants with direct access to their electronic trading and order-matching systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CFTC explains that foreign boards of trade seeking to provide this type of direct access must apply for and receive an Order of Registration under Part 48. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent reporting says SGX has obtained the relevant CFTC authorization under Regulation 48.10, allowing eligible U.S. institutional investors to access its Bitcoin and Ether perpetual futures. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is an important distinction. The latest development is therefore not simply an application waiting for a decision. The authorization has already been reported, while actual institutional onboarding and market participation can still take time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Is SGX Really the First Major Traditional Exchange?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The phrase "first major traditional exchange" needs some context.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SGX is clearly an important traditional exchange operator bringing crypto perpetual futures into a regulated institutional environment. But saying it is the first traditional financial venue anywhere to offer any form of crypto perpetual product would be too broad.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The crypto derivatives market already includes regulated and institutional products across multiple jurisdictions and venues.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The more meaningful point is that SGX is creating another bridge between &lt;strong&gt;traditional institutional finance and crypto-native perpetual futures&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That bridge could become increasingly important as regulators and financial institutions attempt to integrate digital assets into established market infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could This Increase Bitcoin and Ethereum Liquidity?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Potentially, yes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Opening a regulated venue to eligible U.S. institutions gives another group of professional market participants a way to trade Bitcoin and Ether derivatives.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;More institutional participants can increase &lt;strong&gt;liquidity and market depth&lt;/strong&gt;, but the relationship is not automatic. Liquidity depends on how many firms actually trade the contracts, how much volume they generate, and whether market makers provide competitive quotes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If U.S. institutional participation grows meaningfully, SGX could become a more important liquidity venue connecting Asian and American trading activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The $5.8 Billion Number Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SGX did not enter the crypto derivatives market from zero.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent reporting says the exchange's Bitcoin and Ether perpetual futures have generated approximately &lt;strong&gt;$5.8 billion in cumulative trading volume&lt;/strong&gt; since their November 2025 launch. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin has accounted for the majority of activity, with recent figures indicating roughly 83% of average daily trading volume since inception and around 66% of open interest. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those figures suggest there is already institutional demand for the products before the latest expansion of U.S. access.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Are the Risks?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The expansion also comes with important risks. Greater institutional access does not make perpetual futures inherently safer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;1. Leverage Risk&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Perpetual futures allow traders to control positions larger than the amount of capital posted as margin. A relatively small move in Bitcoin or Ether can therefore produce a disproportionately large gain or loss.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;2. Market Risk&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto markets can experience sharp price movements, particularly during periods of high volatility. A leveraged position can be liquidated quickly when the underlying market moves against it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;3. Funding Risk&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Perpetual contracts use funding mechanisms rather than conventional expiration. Funding costs can change depending on market conditions and positioning, affecting the economics of holding a position.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;4. Counterparty and Operational Risk&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Even within a regulated market structure, participants remain exposed to operational, clearing, technology and counterparty risks. Institutional traders therefore need their own risk controls rather than assuming regulation eliminates all potential losses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;5. Regulatory Risk&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto regulation continues to evolve across the United States and other major financial markets. Rules governing derivatives, market access, custody and digital assets can change over time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The immediate question is no longer whether U.S. institutions can theoretically access the products. The latest reports indicate that SGX has received the relevant CFTC authorization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next stage is &lt;strong&gt;institutional onboarding and actual trading activity&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent reporting indicates that onboarding U.S. clients could take several weeks as firms complete operational and compliance requirements. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means the real test for SGX will be how much additional volume arrives from U.S. institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If participation remains limited, the announcement may have mainly symbolic importance. If major trading firms and institutional desks begin using the contracts at scale, SGX could become a more meaningful cross-border venue for Bitcoin and Ether derivatives.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Could Happen to Crypto-Native Exchanges?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SGX's expansion does not necessarily mean traditional exchanges will replace crypto-native derivatives platforms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto-native venues still have advantages, including large global user bases, extensive token coverage and deep experience with perpetual contracts.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, the market could become more fragmented.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Professional traders may use different venues for different purposes: regulated traditional exchanges for certain institutional strategies and crypto-native platforms for broader asset coverage or specialized trading opportunities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Competition could ultimately push exchanges to improve liquidity, execution quality, risk management and product design.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;SGX Could Also Connect Asian and U.S. Liquidity&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SGX's geographic position is another important part of the story.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Singapore has developed into one of Asia's major financial centers, while the United States remains the world's largest pool of institutional capital.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A regulated derivatives venue connecting these markets could potentially make Bitcoin and Ether trading more continuous across global time zones.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For institutional traders, that can matter when managing positions around major market events, macroeconomic announcements or sudden changes in &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/eric-balchunas-says-rising-us-interest.html"&gt;crypto volatility&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does This Mean for Retail Crypto Traders?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Retail traders are unlikely to become the direct beneficiaries of SGX's institutional expansion overnight.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The products are targeted at professional participants, and access requirements are different from those on many retail-focused crypto platforms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, retail traders can still be affected indirectly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;More institutional participation can potentially improve price discovery and liquidity across the broader Bitcoin and Ether derivatives ecosystem. At the same time, larger derivatives markets can also amplify short-term volatility when heavily leveraged positions are opened or closed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Trend: Traditional Exchanges Are Entering Crypto&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SGX's move is part of a much larger transformation in financial markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional exchanges and financial institutions are increasingly exploring crypto derivatives, tokenization and digital-asset infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important change is not simply that Wall Street or traditional exchanges are "buying crypto."&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is that digital assets are gradually being incorporated into established financial-market infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That includes regulated derivatives, institutional custody, tokenized assets and new trading systems designed to connect traditional capital with blockchain-based markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Comes Next for SGX?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin and Ether perpetual futures may only be the beginning.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent reporting has pointed to further development of dated Bitcoin and Ether futures and options, which could give institutional traders additional tools for hedging and portfolio construction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If SGX can attract sufficient U.S. institutional volume, the exchange could eventually build a broader digital-asset derivatives franchise around its existing infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why This Matters for Bitcoin's Institutional Future&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The significance of the SGX development goes beyond one exchange or two crypto assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Every time a major regulated financial venue integrates a crypto product, the distance between traditional markets and digital assets becomes smaller.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin and Ether are increasingly being treated not only as speculative digital assets but also as underlying instruments for professional derivatives strategies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not eliminate volatility or investment risk. But it does show how deeply crypto markets are becoming connected to the global financial system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Singapore Exchange's expansion of Bitcoin and Ether perpetual futures to eligible U.S. institutional investors is an important development in the evolution of crypto derivatives.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The exchange launched its crypto perpetual products in November 2025 and has since generated billions of dollars in cumulative volume. The latest CFTC authorization opens another potential source of institutional liquidity and creates a stronger connection between U.S. trading desks and Singapore's regulated derivatives infrastructure. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The biggest question now is not whether the products exist. It is whether U.S. institutions will use them at sufficient scale to materially increase liquidity, open interest and trading activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If they do, SGX could become an increasingly important bridge between traditional finance and the global crypto derivatives market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is SGX?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;SGX, or Singapore Exchange, is a major Asian exchange operator offering securities, fixed-income and derivatives markets. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What crypto products does SGX offer?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;SGX offers Bitcoin and Ethereum perpetual futures. Its rules state that these products are intended for accredited, expert and institutional investors. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can U.S. institutions trade SGX Bitcoin perpetual futures?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Recent reporting says SGX has received CFTC authorization under Regulation 48.10, allowing eligible U.S. institutional investors to access its Bitcoin and Ether perpetual futures. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;When did SGX launch Bitcoin and Ethereum perpetual futures?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;SGX launched its Bitcoin and Ethereum perpetual futures in November 2025. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How much volume have SGX crypto perpetuals generated?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Recent reporting puts cumulative trading volume at approximately $5.8 billion since the November 2025 launch. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Are perpetual futures risky?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes. Perpetual futures can involve leverage, funding costs, liquidation risk and significant market volatility. Traders can lose substantial amounts of capital.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does SGX's CFTC authorization make crypto perpetual futures risk-free?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. Regulatory authorization governs market access and regulatory requirements; it does not eliminate market, leverage, liquidity, operational or counterparty risks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Will SGX's move increase Bitcoin liquidity?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;It could, particularly if U.S. institutional firms actively trade the contracts. However, additional access alone does not guarantee deeper liquidity. Actual trading volume and market-maker participation will determine the impact.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Binance Launches Physically Settled Options on U.S. Stocks and ETFs</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEizIOZu410J4pfNhGSwWSC5f7b_alGIXRLjG0Im2BazNJknhsmIyZG8vj9x05VUc8eGC9W_gH6OYzOenolgggGc65a-1qPJ-qOJ7wjQ8YS539dSsJMOtw61vZmd-bCYRUkUUS26rCBcbTuSDkyvF7OEdrWK-bnQrn9HeBQb_IOaUGHNMl8Rw6u8zX5AfyVd/s1672/binance-stock-etf-options-physical-settlement-2026.webp.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Binance launches physically settled options tied to U.S. stocks and ETFs" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEizIOZu410J4pfNhGSwWSC5f7b_alGIXRLjG0Im2BazNJknhsmIyZG8vj9x05VUc8eGC9W_gH6OYzOenolgggGc65a-1qPJ-qOJ7wjQ8YS539dSsJMOtw61vZmd-bCYRUkUUS26rCBcbTuSDkyvF7OEdrWK-bnQrn9HeBQb_IOaUGHNMl8Rw6u8zX5AfyVd/w400-h225/binance-stock-etf-options-physical-settlement-2026.webp.png" title="Binance Stock and ETF Options Launch" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;Binance is expanding deeper into traditional financial markets with the launch of stock and ETF options that use physical settlement.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The cryptocurrency exchange says eligible users can trade options linked to U.S.-listed stocks and exchange-traded funds, adding another traditional-finance product to its growing platform.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Important:&lt;/strong&gt; The new Stock Options product is &lt;strong&gt;not available to users in the United States&lt;/strong&gt;. Bloomberg reported that the product is currently available to eligible users outside the U.S., meaning U.S. residents cannot access Binance Stock Options through this offering.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/30d76b73e55e463d8b3b6898f74bf0e5" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Binance's official announcement&lt;/a&gt; says the contracts are physically settled and are designed around U.S.-listed stocks and ETFs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Binance Has Launched&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Binance's new product is called &lt;strong&gt;Stock Options&lt;/strong&gt;. According to the exchange, the offering covers more than &lt;strong&gt;1,000 U.S.-listed stocks and ETFs&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Options give buyers the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an underlying asset at a predetermined strike price on or before the applicable expiration date, depending on the contract structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Binance product includes both:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Call options&lt;/strong&gt;, which provide bullish exposure to the underlying asset.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Put options&lt;/strong&gt;, which provide bearish exposure to the underlying asset.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The contracts use &lt;strong&gt;physical settlement&lt;/strong&gt;, meaning the settlement process is based on delivery of the underlying shares rather than simply paying a cash difference.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;U.S. Users Cannot Access the Product&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This geographic restriction is one of the most important details surrounding the launch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Although the options are linked to U.S.-listed stocks and ETFs, Bloomberg reports that Binance Stock Options are currently offered to users &lt;strong&gt;outside the United States&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means the launch should not be described as Binance giving American customers direct access to its new stock-options product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, it is better understood as Binance adding U.S.-market derivatives to its international product lineup while excluding U.S. users from the offering.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;More Than 1,000 Stocks and ETFs Are Covered&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The launch is broader than a small selection of well-known technology stocks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Binance says the new product covers more than &lt;strong&gt;1,000 U.S. stocks and ETFs&lt;/strong&gt;, giving eligible traders exposure to a wide range of traditional-market assets through options.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That potentially includes different sectors, market-cap categories and ETF products, although the exact availability of individual contracts can depend on Binance's current options chain and applicable jurisdictional restrictions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traders should therefore check the live Binance options interface rather than assuming that every U.S.-listed security is available for options trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Physical Settlement Is a Major Difference&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the most notable features of the launch is its settlement structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Binance says these options are physically settled. Under the applicable contract terms, settlement involves the underlying shares rather than simply paying the difference between the strike price and market price in cash.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes the product different from a cash-settled derivative that only tracks the value of a stock or ETF.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For traders, understanding settlement is important because physical delivery can have different implications for account balances, custody and post-expiration positions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Binance and Alpaca Are Part of the Infrastructure&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new product also relies on traditional securities infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Binance says &lt;strong&gt;Alpaca Securities LLC&lt;/strong&gt; serves as the U.S. clearing broker for the stock-options arrangement, while Nest Trading Limited acts as the introducing broker.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The underlying shares used for physical settlement are held through the relevant custody structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bloomberg has also reported a broader financial relationship between Binance and Alpaca, including Binance's minority stake in Alpaca and an arrangement under which Binance receives a share of payment-for-order-flow revenue.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That relationship is relevant because it provides additional context around the infrastructure supporting Binance's expansion into U.S.-listed securities and derivatives.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, traders should distinguish the &lt;strong&gt;Binance Stock Options product&lt;/strong&gt; from Alpaca's separate brokerage business and services.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Which Currencies Can Be Used?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Binance's options offering is also designed to fit into the exchange's existing crypto-based funding environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to the product information, supported funding currencies include:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;USDC&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;USDT&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;USD1&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;U&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;BNB&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The ability to use crypto-related funding assets is one of the features that separates the product experience from a conventional stock-options brokerage account.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Nevertheless, users should check the current Binance interface and product terms because supported currencies and availability can change.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Options Suitability Quiz Is Required&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Binance is not treating the new product like ordinary spot trading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Users must complete an &lt;strong&gt;Options Suitability Quiz&lt;/strong&gt; before they can trade the Stock Options product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The requirement is significant because options involve risks that are different from simply buying or selling a stock or cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A trader needs to understand concepts such as strike &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/hyperliquid-in-advanced-talks-with.html"&gt;price&lt;/a&gt;, expiration, premium, volatility and the possibility of losing the entire premium paid for an option.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Binance's Stock Options Are Long-Only at Launch&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Another important limitation is the trading direction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The initial product is &lt;strong&gt;long-only&lt;/strong&gt;. Users can purchase Call or Put options, but &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/top-token-unlocks-this-week-hype-bitway.html"&gt;Binance &lt;/a&gt;is not initially allowing customers to write options or take short option positions through the product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For buyers, the maximum loss is generally limited to the premium paid for the contract, although that premium can still be lost completely if the option expires without value.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes the risk defined, but it does not make options low-risk.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Binance Is Adding Options&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The options launch fits into a much larger strategy at Binance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto exchanges have increasingly moved beyond Bitcoin and other digital assets to offer access to stocks, ETFs, commodities, derivatives and other traditional financial products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Binance previously expanded its stock offering to thousands of U.S.-listed securities. The new options product adds another layer on top of that exposure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of simply allowing an investor to hold a stock, Binance can now offer a derivative through which an eligible trader can express a view on the future direction of that stock or ETF.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the U.S. Restriction Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. restriction makes the launch more nuanced than the headline might suggest.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Binance is using U.S.-listed securities as the underlying assets, but U.S.-based customers are excluded from this specific Stock Options product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important for both readers and investors because “options on U.S. stocks” does not mean “options available to U.S. residents.”&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Regulatory requirements can differ substantially between jurisdictions, particularly for securities and derivatives.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Stock Options Are Not the Same as Buying Shares&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;New users should also understand that an option is not the same thing as owning the underlying stock.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;table border="1" cellpadding="8" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;

&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An option can expire worthless even when the underlying stock moves in the anticipated direction if the move is not large or fast enough relative to the contract terms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Traders Should Check Before Trading&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Before placing an options order, users should review the exact contract specifications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Underlying stock or ETF:&lt;/strong&gt; Confirm exactly which security the option tracks.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Strike price:&lt;/strong&gt; Check the exercise price.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Expiration date:&lt;/strong&gt; Know exactly when the contract ends.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Premium:&lt;/strong&gt; Understand how much is being paid for the option.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Settlement:&lt;/strong&gt; Read the physical-settlement terms.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Eligibility:&lt;/strong&gt; Confirm that the product is available in your jurisdiction.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Funding currency:&lt;/strong&gt; Check which supported assets can be used.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Liquidity:&lt;/strong&gt; Review spreads and available market depth.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Risk:&lt;/strong&gt; Understand that the entire premium can potentially be lost.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What This Launch Does Not Mean&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are several conclusions investors should avoid drawing from the announcement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;It does not mean Binance Stock Options are available to U.S. residents.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;It does not mean every U.S.-listed stock automatically has an options contract on Binance.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;It does not mean users can write or short options at launch.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And it does not mean buying an option is equivalent to buying the underlying stock.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Picture for Crypto Exchanges&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Binance's latest move illustrates how &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/strategy-is-back-saylors-company-buys.html"&gt;crypto exchanges&lt;/a&gt; are increasingly becoming multi-asset financial platforms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The traditional distinction between a cryptocurrency exchange and a brokerage is becoming less obvious as platforms add stocks, ETFs and derivatives.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For users, that could mean fewer separate accounts and a more unified trading experience.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For regulators, however, the expansion creates additional questions around securities, derivatives, custody, investor protection and jurisdictional compliance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Binance has launched &lt;strong&gt;physically settled options tied to more than 1,000 U.S. stocks and ETFs&lt;/strong&gt;, expanding its push into traditional financial products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the most important qualification is that the product is currently &lt;strong&gt;not available to users in the United States&lt;/strong&gt;, according to Bloomberg.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The launch supports Call and Put options, requires an Options Suitability Quiz and is initially structured as a long-only product. Binance also supports several funding currencies, including USDC, USDT, USD1, U and BNB, subject to the applicable product terms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The relationship with Alpaca adds another layer of securities infrastructure behind the offering, while Binance's broader expansion into stocks and ETFs shows that the exchange is attempting to build a much wider multi-asset trading ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For traders, however, the headline should not obscure the details. &lt;strong&gt;Options are derivatives, physical settlement has its own mechanics, and availability depends on jurisdiction.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The launch is therefore significant—but it should be viewed as an expansion of Binance's international product lineup, not as a new stock-options service for U.S. residents.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Core Story&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The article accurately captures:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;



&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0in;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What:&lt;/b&gt; Physically
     settled options on 1,000+ U.S. stocks/ETFs&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Who:&lt;/b&gt; Eligible
     users &lt;b&gt;outside the United States&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;How:&lt;/b&gt; Long-only
     at launch, Call/Put options, physical settlement via Alpaca&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Requirements:&lt;/b&gt; Options
     Suitability Quiz required&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Funding:&lt;/b&gt; USDC,
     USDT, USD1, U, BNB&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Context:&lt;/b&gt; Binance's
     broader push into traditional finance&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

    <title>The Most Underrated Crypto Projects Right Now, According to Experts</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhaR1Bn62EVnoeBUVrurHs5gep0PsVHM3nogW4OCJUthUHq1niNu9HnkC8TLKR_kFWBeL31wzcVQ8Qm7uMU8DhlockAfPcuFMt2Fm1th83ESYY3OOaC4fT3HF5Zcbv-VcusOohxApx7GmCG4VLDmi_LOW1w1N0Ve_Y2pBL70YA8PmInTZ4-OQxtOKX6xwfz/s1536/Most%20Underrated%20Crypto%20Projects%20Right%20Now%20HYPE,%20AAVE,%20SOL,%20LINK,%20ZEC%20%20CoinaiNews.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Most underrated crypto projects Hyperliquid Aave Solana Chainlink Zcash expert analysis 2026" border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="213" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhaR1Bn62EVnoeBUVrurHs5gep0PsVHM3nogW4OCJUthUHq1niNu9HnkC8TLKR_kFWBeL31wzcVQ8Qm7uMU8DhlockAfPcuFMt2Fm1th83ESYY3OOaC4fT3HF5Zcbv-VcusOohxApx7GmCG4VLDmi_LOW1w1N0Ve_Y2pBL70YA8PmInTZ4-OQxtOKX6xwfz/w320-h213/Most%20Underrated%20Crypto%20Projects%20Right%20Now%20HYPE,%20AAVE,%20SOL,%20LINK,%20ZEC%20%20CoinaiNews.png" title="Undervalued crypto assets HYPE AAVE SOL LINK ZEC Bitwise Grayscale Helius picks" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aug 14, 2026&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Let's be honest — crypto markets have been rough lately.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitcoin is stuck in a range. Altcoins are bleeding. The Fear
&amp;amp; Greed Index is hovering near "Fear." Most traders are either
sitting on their hands or waiting for the next macro trigger.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But here's the thing: price action doesn't tell the whole
story.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;While retail is panicking, some of the smartest people in
the industry — Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan, Grayscale Research, Helius &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/crypto-scam-alert-what-to-do-if-youve.html"&gt;CEO MertMumtaz &lt;/a&gt;— are quietly accumulating projects they believe the market is
undervaluing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Not because they're guessing. Because they're looking at
revenue, adoption, and actual usage.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Here are five projects that keep coming up in those
conversations.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Hyperliquid (HYPE): The Market Is Looking at It Wrong&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Hyperliquid is probably the most misunderstood project in
&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/the-most-underrated-crypto-projects.html"&gt;crypto&lt;/a&gt; right now.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Most people see it as just another perpetual futures
exchange. And yeah, that's technically true — but it's like calling Apple a
computer company.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan made this point recently. He said
investors are making a "category error" with Hyperliquid. They're
valuing it like a DeFi protocol when they should be looking at it like a global
financial super-app that competes with Robinhood and CME.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's not hype. That's a different market entirely.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Here's what's interesting:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Hyperliquid generated
between $800 million and $1 billion in revenue last year. Its market cap is
sitting around $10-11 billion. That gives it a price-to-revenue ratio of about
10-14x.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Compare that to Robinhood (37x earnings) or CME (24x).
Neither grows at Hyperliquid's pace.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Nearly half of Hyperliquid's volume already comes from
non-crypto assets — S&amp;amp;P 500 futures, oil, silver, commodities. The platform
processed $170 billion in volume last month alone.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Since its token launched, Hyperliquid has bought and removed
over&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$1.3 billion worth of HYPE&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;from circulation using
protocol fees.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The real question:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Can it keep expanding outside
crypto derivatives? If yes, today's valuation could look very cheap years from
now.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aave (AAVE): The Old Dog That Still Has Bite&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Aave isn't new. It's been around for years, survived
multiple cycles, and outlasted hundreds of DeFi projects that came and went.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That track record matters.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Grayscale Research&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;recently put out a note
estimating that Aave could generate around&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$60 million in earnings in
2026**. Based on traditional fintech multiples, they pegged AAVE's fair value
between **$80 and $100&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;— above its current trading level.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Under a more optimistic scenario, they see it hitting&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$175&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;over
the next year.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But here's the thing — Aave isn't just about the token
price.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The protocol holds more than&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$57 billion in total
value locked** and **$23 billion in active loans&lt;/b&gt;. It commands over 80% of
stablecoin deposits on Ethereum.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;People need to borrow and lend. Stablecoins are growing.
Institutions are exploring tokenized real-world assets. Aave sits right in the
middle of all three.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The catch?&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Revenue doesn't automatically flow to
AAVE holders. Tokenomics matter. Investors need to watch whether future growth
actually benefits the token.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But if Aave can crack that, it's a different conversation
entirely.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Solana (SOL): The Price Tanked, But the Builders Stayed&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Solana is the easiest coin to hate on right now.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Down 75% from its high. Meme coin casino reputation.
Constant criticism from maximalists.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But developers don't seem to care.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Helius CEO Mert Mumtaz called Solana "massively
underpriced" and compared its developer ecosystem to a global Silicon
Valley. That sounds bold, but the numbers back it up.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Solana captured 97% of all tokenized equity trading
volume&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in Q2 2026 — $4.8 billion worth. Total tokenized asset volume
hit $5.8 billion, up 114% from Q1.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;U.S.-listed Solana funds now manage about $1 billion in
assets. Every month since the spot ETF launch has seen net inflows despite the
price drop.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;And Alpenglow is coming.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;The network upgrade
will reduce transaction finality from 12.8 seconds to about 150 milliseconds —
a massive improvement for applications that need near-instant settlement.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The real question isn't whether SOL can return to its old
high. It's whether Solana can turn its developer activity, transaction volume,
and institutional interest into a sustainable ecosystem.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If it can, the current price won't matter much in the long
run.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Chainlink (LINK): The Quiet Infrastructure Play&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Chainlink doesn't get the same attention as Bitcoin, Solana,
or DeFi tokens.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's actually part of its appeal.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Chainlink is building infrastructure — the boring but
essential layer that makes blockchain adoption possible. Its tech allows smart
contracts to interact with real-world data and communicate across different
chains.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;This matters because:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Traditional finance is
experimenting with tokenized assets. And when banks start moving assets
onchain, they'll need reliable data feeds and cross-chain infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Chainlink already works with&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;SWIFT (11,000 financial
institutions), UBS, and Euroclear&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In Q1 2026, Chainlink's Cross-Chain Interoperability
Protocol (CCIP) processed&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$18 billion&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in transaction value —
up 78% quarterly.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Here's the problem for LINK investors:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;A bank
can use Chainlink's infrastructure without buying LINK tokens. So Chainlink
could become more successful as a business without the token necessarily rising
at the same rate.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That makes token value accrual the most important thing to
watch.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The technology story is strong. The investment story depends
on how much of that success flows back to LINK.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Zcash (ZEC): Privacy Is Coming Back&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Privacy has never been an easy narrative to sell.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For years, the market was obsessed with DeFi, NFTs, and meme
coins. Financial privacy felt like a niche concern.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That may be changing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Digital Currency Group CEO Barry Silbert recently called it
the beginning of a "privacy era" in crypto. Helius CEO Mert Mumtaz
pointed to Zcash as a high-conviction privacy asset.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why Zcash?&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Unlike some privacy coins, Zcash
doesn't make every transaction invisible. It allows users to make private
transactions while retaining transparency options when needed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That flexibility could become increasingly relevant as
blockchain analytics get more sophisticated and governments expand their
ability to monitor digital-asset activity.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;There's already been renewed institutional interest. The SEC
closed its investigation into Zcash with no enforcement action in January.
Grayscale reopened its Zcash Trust and filed for a spot ETF. Cypherpunk
Technologies accumulated 323,394 ZEC (about 1.92% of circulating supply) at an
average price of $341.83.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;But Zcash is also the riskiest project on this list.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Privacy
coins attract regulatory scrutiny. The thesis depends on how governments
ultimately balance privacy with oversight.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It's a bet on technology and on society's evolving views on
financial privacy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Bigger Story: Revenue, Not Hype&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;There's a broader shift happening.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Crypto investors are becoming more interested in revenue.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In previous cycles, a project could get a massive valuation
just by having a compelling story — a big community, an ambitious roadmap, a
popular narrative.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That era is ending.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Investors are asking simpler questions now:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;How
     much revenue does the protocol generate?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;How
     many people actually use it?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Is
     usage growing?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;Does
     that activity create value for the token?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Hyperliquid has built a real trading business. Aave is one
of the biggest lending protocols in DeFi. Chainlink is positioning itself for
institutional adoption. Solana continues to attract developers. Zcash has a
defined use case that's becoming more relevant.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;None of this guarantees outperformance.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Fundamentals
can improve while prices fall. Markets can stay disconnected from reality for
long periods.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But it gives investors more information to work with than
they had in earlier cycles.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What Could Change the Picture?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Three things need to happen for these projects to justify
higher valuations:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;1. Continued adoption.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;A protocol can generate
impressive numbers for a few months, but investors need to see users stick
around.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;2. Regulatory clarity.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Especially for DeFi,
tokenized assets, and privacy projects. Clearer rules could bring in larger
institutions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;3. Better token value capture.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;This is the most
important one. A blockchain can be extremely successful while its native token
performs poorly if there's no connection between network activity and token
demand.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's why investors are looking beyond headlines and asking
how project economics actually work.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The most underrated crypto projects aren't the ones that
have been forgotten.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;They're the ones the market is looking at through the wrong
lens.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Hyperliquid could become much more than a crypto derivatives
exchange.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Aave could benefit from stablecoin growth, on-chain lending,
and tokenized assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Solana continues to attract developers despite its price
drop.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Chainlink is building infrastructure for institutional
finance.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Zcash offers a bet on the growing importance of financial
privacy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;None of these are guaranteed. Calling something
"undervalued" doesn't mean it can't fall further.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But if the market continues moving away from pure
speculation and toward revenue, adoption, and real economic activity, these are
five projects worth paying attention to.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Sometimes the biggest opportunities aren't hidden.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;They're just being valued differently from what they could
eventually become.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

    <title>India’s Arya.ag Tests Tokenized Grain Receipts on Avalanche</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEjHx2rvvJxk0HXpPDKyeUXOW8NpUo9JC_8QifTkqNrmqBCkXFApklISa0y5I_qDn0MRii_GObKQFdk0bu1C14lgo8TVMoYwnMEk-m7pJ2Q-0_mhIEV06Utg2m0FqZLZa8uoZG4xVBbpb9tmi9gd8FL7N5rCYOL8F5T1NDrXDYz_0q9Iffi4w1TQPgJz-zvM" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Arya.ag tests tokenized grain receipts on Avalanche in India" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1671" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/a/AVvXsEjHx2rvvJxk0HXpPDKyeUXOW8NpUo9JC_8QifTkqNrmqBCkXFApklISa0y5I_qDn0MRii_GObKQFdk0bu1C14lgo8TVMoYwnMEk-m7pJ2Q-0_mhIEV06Utg2m0FqZLZa8uoZG4xVBbpb9tmi9gd8FL7N5rCYOL8F5T1NDrXDYz_0q9Iffi4w1TQPgJz-zvM=w640-h360" title="Arya.ag Tests Tokenized Grain Receipts on Avalanche" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;India's agricultural finance sector is moving deeper into blockchain technology as &lt;strong&gt;Arya.ag tests a system designed to tokenize warehouse receipts for stored grain on a dedicated Avalanche Layer-1 blockchain&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to &lt;strong&gt;Cointelegraph&lt;/strong&gt;, Arya.ag is working with &lt;strong&gt;Finternet&lt;/strong&gt; to connect grain deposits, warehouse receipts, collateral commitments and loan information through the blockchain network. The companies have not disclosed when the system will launch or how much grain or lending the initial deployment will cover. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The project is significant because it targets a practical problem in agricultural finance: giving lenders a shared digital view of physical commodities, their ownership status and whether those commodities have already been pledged as collateral.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is Arya.ag Tokenizing?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The system is designed to tokenize &lt;strong&gt;warehouse receipts linked to stored grain&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A warehouse receipt is a record representing commodities held in storage. In India's agricultural finance system, such receipts can be used to support borrowing against stored crops rather than forcing farmers or agricultural businesses to sell immediately after harvest.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Under the reported blockchain system, the digital representation would connect information about the underlying grain with records covering ownership, warehouse storage, insurance and outstanding loans.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cointelegraph reported that &lt;strong&gt;Devika Mittal, Ava Labs' head of India&lt;/strong&gt;, said testing was underway and that each tokenized receipt would represent ownership of the stored commodity. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Finternet Will Connect the Agricultural Data&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Arya.ag is working with &lt;strong&gt;Finternet&lt;/strong&gt; on the initiative.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to Cointelegraph, Finternet will combine information covering the farmer, commodity, warehouse and insurance into what Finternet Labs director &lt;strong&gt;Sanmesh Kalyanpur&lt;/strong&gt; described as a “composite token.” Banks could then use the combined information when assessing collateral risk. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The idea is broader than simply putting a grain receipt on a blockchain. The proposed system is intended to connect several pieces of information that lenders need when determining whether physical agricultural commodities can safely serve as collateral.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 760px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Information&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Role in the System&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Farmer&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Identifies the agricultural participant associated with the commodity.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Grain&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Provides information about the stored commodity represented by the digital record.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Warehouse&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Links the digital record to where the physical commodity is stored.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Insurance&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Adds insurance-related information associated with the stored commodity.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Loan status&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Helps lenders understand outstanding financing connected to the collateral.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Tokenized Grain Receipts Matter for Banks&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the biggest challenges in commodity-backed lending is determining whether collateral is already pledged elsewhere.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Arya.ag has previously used blockchain technology to address this problem. In 2023, the company described a blockchain system in which tokenized commodities could be transferred to a bank through a smart contract after being pledged. The stated goal was to improve transparency and prevent the same commodity from being pledged more than once. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new Avalanche initiative builds on that broader concept by attempting to connect warehouse receipts and additional agricultural information into a digital system that lenders can use.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For banks, the potential benefit is straightforward: &lt;strong&gt;a more unified view of the collateral behind an agricultural loan.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Arya.ag Has Already Put Agricultural Commodities on Blockchain&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest Avalanche testing is not Arya.ag's first blockchain project.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In 2023, Arya.ag said its blockchain infrastructure had already been used to tokenize commodities stored in its warehouses. At the time, the company said its ledger covered 3.2 million metric tons of commodities across 894 warehouses on the blockchain network. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Arya.ag also said blockchain could provide lenders with greater visibility into commodity collateral while helping streamline loan disbursement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That previous work provides important context for the current Avalanche testing. The company is not approaching commodity tokenization as an entirely new concept; instead, the latest project represents another development in its effort to connect physical agricultural assets with digital financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How the New Avalanche System Is Expected to Work&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Based on the details reported by Cointelegraph, the process begins with information collected about grain stored in warehouses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Arya.ag's samplers collect information about stored grain and enter that information into the company's portal. Finternet can then combine information about the farmer, commodity, warehouse and insurance into the composite digital record. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The resulting tokenized receipt is intended to represent ownership of the stored commodity and provide lenders with information relevant to collateral assessment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proposed structure can be simplified into four stages:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Physical grain is stored:&lt;/strong&gt; Agricultural commodities remain in participating warehouses.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Commodity information is recorded:&lt;/strong&gt; Relevant data about the stored grain is collected.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Information is combined:&lt;/strong&gt; Farmer, commodity, warehouse, insurance and loan-related information can be linked.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Tokenized record is used for finance:&lt;/strong&gt; Banks can use the digital information when assessing collateral risk.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The blockchain record does not physically move the grain. The underlying commodity remains in the warehouse.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Physical Verification Problem Still Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchain technology can create a transparent digital record, but it cannot independently verify that physical grain exists or that its quantity and quality match the information entered into the system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why physical verification remains critical.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cointelegraph reported that the system will still depend on accurate verification of the physical commodities represented by the digital records. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is an important limitation for all real-world asset tokenization projects. A blockchain can protect the integrity of a digital record after information is recorded, but the process still needs reliable methods for connecting that record to the real-world asset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Arya.ag's Existing Scale&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Arya.ag is already a significant participant in India's grain and agricultural-finance ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to figures cited by Cointelegraph, Arya.ag stores approximately &lt;strong&gt;$2 billion in agricultural commodities&lt;/strong&gt; across its warehouse network and supports roughly &lt;strong&gt;120 billion Indian rupees, or about $1.26 billion, in loans annually&lt;/strong&gt;. Its lending arm, Arya Dhan, issues approximately $230 million in loans each year. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These numbers describe Arya.ag's existing business. They &lt;strong&gt;do not represent the amount of grain or lending already moved onto Avalanche&lt;/strong&gt;. Cointelegraph specifically noted that the companies have not disclosed the size of the initial blockchain deployment. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important because it would be misleading to describe the entire $2 billion commodity base or the full lending figures as already tokenized on Avalanche.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Avalanche Is Being Used&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The reported system is being tested on a &lt;strong&gt;dedicated Avalanche Layer-1 blockchain&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This places the project within the broader real-world asset tokenization trend, where blockchain infrastructure is increasingly being explored for assets that exist outside the crypto ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Arya.ag, the potential use case is not primarily about speculative cryptocurrency trading. Instead, the focus is on representing agricultural commodities and related financial information in a digital format that can be shared across participants in the lending ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important: &lt;strong&gt;tokenized grain receipts are fundamentally different from a conventional cryptocurrency.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;India's Warehouse-Receipt Finance Market&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Electronic warehouse receipts already play an important role in India's agricultural finance system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They allow farmers and agricultural businesses to use stored commodities as collateral for financing rather than selling the produce immediately after harvest.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In 2024, the Indian government launched a &lt;strong&gt;10 billion-rupee credit-guarantee program&lt;/strong&gt; intended to encourage financing against electronic negotiable warehouse receipts, particularly for small and marginal farmers. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The development of blockchain-based records could potentially complement that existing financial infrastructure by creating a shared digital layer for ownership and collateral information.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is the Finternet Concept?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader Finternet concept is based on the idea of interconnected ledgers for tokenized assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cointelegraph noted that the concept was outlined in a &lt;strong&gt;2024 Bank for International Settlements paper&lt;/strong&gt; co-authored by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani and former BIS General Manager Agustín Carstens. The paper proposed interconnected unified ledgers for tokenized assets while also emphasizing the need for appropriate legal and regulatory frameworks. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In the Arya.ag project, the concept is being applied to agricultural commodities and lending information rather than simply creating a standalone digital token.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could Tokenized Grain Improve Agricultural Lending?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the system works as intended, a shared digital record could potentially make it easier for lenders to determine:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;what commodity is stored;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;who owns the commodity;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;where the commodity is stored;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;whether it has already been pledged as collateral;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;what insurance information is associated with it; and&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;what debt remains outstanding against the collateral.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Having those details connected could reduce information gaps between farmers, warehouses and financial institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It could also make collateral monitoring more efficient, although the actual benefit will depend on the quality of physical verification and the legal framework surrounding tokenized ownership.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;This Is a Test, Not a Full Commercial Launch&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the most important facts about the announcement is what has &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; been disclosed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Arya.ag and its partners have not announced a public launch date for the system. They have also not disclosed how much grain or lending will be included in the initial deployment. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Therefore, the project should currently be described as a &lt;strong&gt;testing initiative&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than a fully deployed nationwide tokenized grain market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is also no basis for saying that farmers can currently buy or sell tokenized Arya.ag grain receipts as freely traded crypto assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next stage will be determining whether the technology can move from testing into a larger operational deployment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Key questions will include the size of the first deployment, how participating banks interact with the system, how ownership transfers are legally recognized, and how physical grain verification is connected to the digital records.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If those elements work together, the project could become an important example of real-world asset tokenization applied to agricultural finance rather than financial speculation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is Arya.ag?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Arya.ag is an Indian agricultural platform focused on post-harvest services, grain commerce, storage and finance. The company operates a large warehouse network and provides financing connected to agricultural commodities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is Arya.ag testing on Avalanche?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Arya.ag is testing a system to tokenize warehouse receipts for stored grain on a dedicated Avalanche Layer-1 blockchain, according to Cointelegraph.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What does a tokenized grain receipt represent?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to the reported project design, each tokenized receipt represents ownership of the stored commodity. The digital record is connected to information about the underlying physical grain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Who is Arya.ag working with?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Arya.ag is working with Finternet on the reported system. Finternet is intended to connect information about farmers, commodities, warehouses, insurance and loan status.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Has the system launched?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No public launch date has been disclosed. The companies are currently testing the system, and the size of the initial deployment has not been announced.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is the entire Arya.ag grain portfolio being tokenized?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No such claim has been made. The approximately $2 billion in agricultural commodities and the lending figures cited in the report describe Arya.ag's existing business, not assets already moved onto Avalanche.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is this a cryptocurrency?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. The project concerns tokenized warehouse receipts representing physical agricultural commodities. It should not be confused with a conventional cryptocurrency such as Bitcoin or AVAX.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Arya.ag's testing of tokenized grain receipts on Avalanche shows how blockchain technology is moving beyond traditional crypto markets and into real-world agricultural finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important part of the project is not simply putting grain records on a blockchain. It is the attempt to connect &lt;strong&gt;physical commodities, warehouse receipts, ownership, insurance and loan information&lt;/strong&gt; into a shared digital system that lenders can use when assessing collateral.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The project is still in the testing stage, and its launch date and initial deployment size remain undisclosed. But if the system can reliably connect verified physical grain with legally recognized digital ownership records, it could offer a practical model for using real-world asset tokenization in India's agricultural lending market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Source:&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;a href="https://ct.com/news/arya-ag-tests-tokenized-grain-receipts-avalanche" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Cointelegraph — India’s Arya.ag to put grain ownership records on Avalanche&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Additional background:&lt;/strong&gt; Arya.ag's earlier blockchain initiative and commodity-tokenization work were documented by the company and industry publications. &lt;/p&gt;
