    <title>Can Cryptocurrencies Survive the Quantum Era?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article class="coinainews-article"&gt;

  &lt;header&gt;
    &lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgDx7YqQGtgG-IGSj5m6kipoxTvedsg_xza5WnzQok1xUDwVb5lnywlR4TV34J5qWx608tF8gOkbgNngYkHDZ7rSPv-ooZSEbq-e5fCbMWqpjfgAPv0nryxRW6tksHXjxvWB_X-N2A1zKNYS8MaBo9fwTNE4V_qSiD-ymC7B6xjKG-QtEz8x87cgnxUPMot/s1672/Can%20Cryptocurrencies%20Survive%20the%20Quantum%20Era.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin and cryptocurrency networks facing the future threat of quantum computing and post-quantum cryptography" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgDx7YqQGtgG-IGSj5m6kipoxTvedsg_xza5WnzQok1xUDwVb5lnywlR4TV34J5qWx608tF8gOkbgNngYkHDZ7rSPv-ooZSEbq-e5fCbMWqpjfgAPv0nryxRW6tksHXjxvWB_X-N2A1zKNYS8MaBo9fwTNE4V_qSiD-ymC7B6xjKG-QtEz8x87cgnxUPMot/w400-h225/Can%20Cryptocurrencies%20Survive%20the%20Quantum%20Era.png" title="Can Cryptocurrencies Survive the Quantum Era?" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h4 style="text-align: left;"&gt;There is a question that keeps some of the brightest minds in cryptography awake at night.&lt;/h4&gt;&lt;/header&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;What happens when quantum computers become powerful enough to break the cryptography that protects Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other major cryptocurrencies?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For years, this felt like a distant theoretical concern. A problem for the next generation to solve.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Not anymore.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In March 2026, Google's quantum research team published research that changed the conversation. Their findings suggested that future quantum computers may be able to break the cryptographic systems safeguarding cryptocurrencies with roughly &lt;strong&gt;20 times less hardware&lt;/strong&gt; than previously estimated. Google also highlighted a &lt;strong&gt;2029 migration timeline&lt;/strong&gt; as a planning horizon for moving vulnerable systems toward post-quantum cryptography.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The migration clock is already running.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Quantum Threat, Explained Simply&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;To understand the risk, you need to understand the lock.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Most cryptocurrencies today rely on cryptographic systems based on &lt;strong&gt;elliptic-curve cryptography (ECC)&lt;/strong&gt;. This mathematics is used to secure digital signatures and prove ownership of funds. Think of it as a digital lock that would be extremely difficult for today's classical computers to pick.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Quantum computers don't play by those rules.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;They use a fundamentally different approach to computation. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer running &lt;strong&gt;Shor's algorithm&lt;/strong&gt; could theoretically derive a private key from a public key much more efficiently than a classical computer.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://research.google/blog/safeguarding-cryptocurrency-by-disclosing-quantum-vulnerabilities-responsibly/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Google's research&lt;/a&gt;
    estimates that, under specific hardware and error-rate assumptions, a quantum computer with fewer than &lt;strong&gt;500,000 physical qubits&lt;/strong&gt; could execute the relevant attack in a matter of minutes.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Google's estimate is still far beyond today's hardware, but the research suggests that the long-term quantum threat may require substantially less hardware than earlier estimates assumed.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Not All Blockchains Face the Same Exposure&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The quantum threat is more complex than simply asking whether someone could steal cryptocurrency. The exposure can differ considerably depending on how a blockchain handles keys, signatures, addresses and privacy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
    

```
  &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); min-width: 760px; text-align: left; width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;thead&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Factor&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Example Blockchains&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Potential Quantum Risk&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/thead&gt;&lt;tbody&gt;
    &lt;tr&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;UTXO-based&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Bitcoin, Cardano&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Public-key exposure can &lt;br /&gt;increase through address &lt;br /&gt;reuse; staking and signing &lt;br /&gt;keys may also require &lt;br /&gt;migration.&lt;/td&gt;
    &lt;/tr&gt;

    &lt;tr&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Account-based&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Ethereum, Solana, XRP Ledger&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Depending on the protocol, &lt;br /&gt;public-key information can &lt;br /&gt;become exposed on-chain &lt;br /&gt;after transactions or other &lt;br /&gt;key-use events.&lt;/td&gt;
    &lt;/tr&gt;

    &lt;tr&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Privacy-preserving&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Zcash, Monero&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Depending on the underlying &lt;br /&gt;privacy construction, sufficiently&lt;br /&gt;&amp;nbsp;powerful quantum computers could&lt;br /&gt;&amp;nbsp;create risks to the confidentiality &lt;br /&gt;of historical transactions.&lt;/td&gt;
    &lt;/tr&gt;

    &lt;tr&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Smart-contract platforms&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Ethereum, Solana&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Compromised cryptographic keys &lt;br /&gt;controlling high-value applications, &lt;br /&gt;bridges or administrative functions &lt;br /&gt;could create systemic risks.&lt;/td&gt;
    &lt;/tr&gt;
  &lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
```

  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;One of the significant concerns is that &lt;strong&gt;privacy-preserving blockchains&lt;/strong&gt; may face not only future theft risks but also potential degradation of historical privacy. The exact impact would depend on the privacy system and what information a quantum attacker could obtain.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Solution: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC)&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Here's the good news: the core cryptographic building blocks for a post-quantum transition already exist.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Post-quantum cryptography (PQC)&lt;/strong&gt; refers to cryptographic algorithms and standards designed to resist attacks from both classical and quantum computers. These systems can run on conventional computing hardware; they do not require quantum computers themselves.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The
    &lt;a href="https://www.nist.gov/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)&lt;/a&gt;
    finalized three major post-quantum cryptographic standards in August 2024:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;FIPS 203 / ML-KEM&lt;/strong&gt; — A post-quantum key-encapsulation mechanism, formerly associated with Kyber.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;FIPS 204 / ML-DSA&lt;/strong&gt; — A post-quantum digital-signature standard, formerly associated with Dilithium.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;FIPS 205 / SLH-DSA&lt;/strong&gt; — A hash-based post-quantum digital-signature standard, formerly associated with SPHINCS+.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;These standards provide important building blocks for a post-quantum migration, although individual blockchain networks will need to determine which schemes and implementation designs best fit their architectures.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;The Size Problem&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;One of the biggest practical obstacles isn't the underlying cryptography. It's the &lt;strong&gt;size&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Post-quantum signatures can be dramatically larger than the signatures used by many blockchain systems today.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://hedera.com/blog/post-quantum-cryptography-and-blockchain/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Hedera's post-quantum research&lt;/a&gt;
    notes that post-quantum signatures can be substantially larger than current cryptographic signatures.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
    

```
  &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); min-width: 650px; text-align: left; width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;thead&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Signature Scheme&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Public Key Size&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Signature Size&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/thead&gt;&lt;tbody&gt;
    &lt;tr&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;Ed25519&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;32 bytes&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;64 bytes&lt;/td&gt;
    &lt;/tr&gt;

    &lt;tr&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;ECDSA&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;33 bytes&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;~70 bytes&lt;/td&gt;
    &lt;/tr&gt;

    &lt;tr&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;ML-DSA-87&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;2,592 bytes&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;4,627 bytes&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
    &lt;/tr&gt;

    &lt;tr&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;SLH-DSA-256s&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;64 bytes&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(217, 217, 217); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;29,792 bytes&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
    &lt;/tr&gt;
  &lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
```

  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Source: NIST FIPS 204/FIPS 205 specifications and Hedera's post-quantum cryptography analysis.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In plain English, some post-quantum signatures can be dozens or even hundreds of times larger than today's commonly used signatures. That creates a difficult engineering tradeoff for blockchains, where larger signatures can increase storage, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/can-coinbase-pull-back-crypto.html"&gt;bandwidth&lt;/a&gt; and transaction-processing requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A
    &lt;a href="https://coinmarketcap.com/community/articles/69e7dd1de0b41f5baf0e364d/#1" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Coinbase advisory board analysis&lt;/a&gt;
    has also warned that replacing vulnerable cryptographic systems across networks, wallets and exchanges could take years. Some proposed quantum-resistant approaches could significantly increase blockchain data requirements.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;How the Industry Is Preparing&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Parts of the crypto industry are already preparing for a post-quantum transition.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Google's 2029 Wake-Up Call&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Google has been involved in post-quantum cryptography research and migration planning for years. In March 2026, its cryptocurrency-focused research highlighted the need for the industry to begin preparing for quantum-resistant cryptography well before cryptographically relevant quantum computers become available.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Google's research can be read in full here:
    &lt;a href="https://research.google/blog/safeguarding-cryptocurrency-by-disclosing-quantum-vulnerabilities-responsibly/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Safeguarding cryptocurrency by disclosing quantum vulnerabilities responsibly&lt;/a&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Google has also worked with government organizations and industry researchers on post-quantum migration efforts.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Ethereum's Conservative Pivot&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The Ethereum research community has taken an interesting approach to future cryptographic infrastructure. Instead of automatically adopting every new cryptographic construction, researchers are placing greater emphasis on conservative and well-studied primitives.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In August 2026, Ethereum researcher Justin Drake discussed a research direction that moves away from relying heavily on the Poseidon hash function in certain future infrastructure designs and instead emphasizes traditional SHA and BLAKE hashes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The underlying argument is straightforward: &lt;strong&gt;security through simplicity&lt;/strong&gt; can be valuable when building infrastructure that may need to remain secure for decades.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Drake has also pointed to setbacks affecting several newer cryptographic approaches and argued for caution around assumptions that have not received sufficient long-term scrutiny.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Ethereum's preliminary research targets include &lt;strong&gt;2027 for a production-grade leanVM&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;2028 for infrastructure-layer deployment&lt;/strong&gt;. These should be treated as research targets rather than confirmed Ethereum mainnet upgrade dates.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Hedera's Phased Migration&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://hedera.com/blog/post-quantum-cryptography-and-blockchain/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Hedera&lt;/a&gt;
    has outlined a deliberate, multi-phase transition approach.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ol&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Post-quantum TLS&lt;/strong&gt; for node-to-node communication when suitable libraries become available.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Post-quantum TLS&lt;/strong&gt; for client connections.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Post-quantum event signing&lt;/strong&gt; using hybrid signatures.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Post-quantum key types for users&lt;/strong&gt; as the technology matures.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ol&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This phased approach is designed to allow the network to introduce stronger cryptography without requiring an abrupt system-wide transition.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Anchorage's "Turnstile" Solution&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Custodial bank
    &lt;a href="https://www.anchorage.com/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Anchorage Digital&lt;/a&gt;
    has proposed a potential mechanism for addressing one of the hardest problems: migrating funds controlled by legacy cryptographic keys.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The company's &lt;strong&gt;Post-Quantum Turnstile&lt;/strong&gt; concept uses STARK-based zero-knowledge proofs to transfer control toward a post-quantum key without requiring the old private key to be exposed.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Anchorage says the research could apply to an &lt;strong&gt;estimated two-thirds of Bitcoin's circulating supply&lt;/strong&gt;. The company has also estimated that roughly &lt;strong&gt;6 million BTC&lt;/strong&gt; held at addresses with disclosed public keys could potentially be exposed to future quantum attacks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;These figures represent estimates of potential vulnerability, not predictions that the affected Bitcoin will necessarily be stolen.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Challenges Ahead&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;The Governance Problem: Dormant Wallets&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;What happens to Bitcoin that hasn't moved in years?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If a network eventually upgrades to post-quantum signatures, some owners may never migrate their keys. Those funds could become difficult to spend using the upgraded system, while legacy cryptography could remain a target for a sufficiently capable &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/sk-hynix-ceo-warns-memory-chip-crunch.html"&gt;quantum attacker.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This creates a governance challenge. Decentralized networks cannot simply order every holder to upgrade. Any migration strategy must consider lost keys, inactive wallets, exchanges, custodians and users who may not understand the technical changes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;The Size-Security Tradeoff&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Post-quantum signatures can be large. Blockchains are already balancing scalability, bandwidth, storage and decentralization.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Balancing quantum resistance with throughput and decentralization&lt;/strong&gt; could become one of the most significant engineering challenges facing blockchain infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Crypto-Agility Is Essential&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The Coinbase advisory board has emphasized the importance of &lt;strong&gt;crypto-agile strategies&lt;/strong&gt; for exchanges, wallets and custodians.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Crypto-agility means designing systems so cryptographic algorithms can be replaced or upgraded without forcing a complete redesign of the surrounding infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What This Means for Crypto Users&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Don't Panic. Prepare.&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The quantum threat is real, but there is currently no public evidence that a cryptocurrency has been compromised by a cryptographically relevant quantum computer.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Google's 2029 timeline should therefore be understood as a &lt;strong&gt;migration warning and planning horizon&lt;/strong&gt;, not as a guaranteed date when Bitcoin or another cryptocurrency will be hacked.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For ordinary crypto users, there is no need for panic. But staying informed will become increasingly important.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ol&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Avoid unnecessary address reuse&lt;/strong&gt; where your &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/dear-algorithm-only-show-us-1000x.html"&gt;wallet&lt;/a&gt; and blockchain design make public-key exposure relevant.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Stay informed&lt;/strong&gt; by following migration announcements from your wallet, exchange and blockchain developers.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Use test transactions&lt;/strong&gt; when moving large amounts, particularly when migrating to new wallet infrastructure.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Watch for post-quantum support&lt;/strong&gt; and follow reputable wallet or exchange instructions when new key types become available.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ol&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Can cryptocurrencies prevent quantum computers from breaking their cryptographic defenses?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Yes — but it will require one of the most complex and coordinated upgrades in the history of digital infrastructure.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The core cryptographic alternatives already exist, and NIST has standardized important post-quantum primitives. The harder challenge is deploying those technologies across decentralized blockchain networks without creating unacceptable costs in performance, storage, bandwidth or usability.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Google's 2029 migration horizon has helped turn a distant theoretical problem into an engineering issue that blockchain developers need to plan for today.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The industry is responding in different ways. Ethereum researchers are emphasizing conservative cryptographic primitives. Hedera is developing a phased migration strategy. Anchorage Digital is researching mechanisms for moving funds away from vulnerable legacy keys.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The quantum era is coming.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;But so is the post-quantum solution.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;section class="editorial-note"&gt;
    &lt;h3&gt;Editorial Note&lt;/h3&gt;

```
&lt;p&gt;Quantum computing capabilities, cryptographic standards and blockchain migration timelines are subject to change. This article is based on information available as of August 2026 and should not be treated as financial or investment advice.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute financial, legal or investment advice.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
```

    <title>ONDO Surges Nearly 30%: What Is Driving the Sudden Move?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article style="color: #222222; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; line-height: 1.75; max-width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgRPTyZM5cE4Clre8vniuzsrlJmnUuKXK7ilvBUrm3dEs2ifqwqLgV4woXLkNkAcEsP8hjLcjVxnHmWZT3HWLpuQp_B-6xvExXqvWAph1X6c-E1iWIvXiSCKYWdM8xKO8RcuSNRaFY6QWzTUtJdy3FwJ58H0bypR2RwLoloN3CYmd6H5QMbW4hG8-kHY5P9/s1672/ondo-token-surges-nearly-30-percent-intelligent-portfolios.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="ONDO token surges nearly 30% as Ondo Finance launches Intelligent Portfolios with BlackRock-developed strategies" border="0" data-original-height="940" data-original-width="1672" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgRPTyZM5cE4Clre8vniuzsrlJmnUuKXK7ilvBUrm3dEs2ifqwqLgV4woXLkNkAcEsP8hjLcjVxnHmWZT3HWLpuQp_B-6xvExXqvWAph1X6c-E1iWIvXiSCKYWdM8xKO8RcuSNRaFY6QWzTUtJdy3FwJ58H0bypR2RwLoloN3CYmd6H5QMbW4hG8-kHY5P9/s1600/ondo-token-surges-nearly-30-percent-intelligent-portfolios.jpg.png" title="ONDO Surges Nearly 30% After Ondo Intelligent Portfolios Launch" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;Ondo Finance’s &lt;/span&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: large;"&gt;ONDO&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt; token has suddenly become one of the biggest movers in the crypto market, climbing nearly 30% over 24 hours as traders reacted to a fresh institutional-tokenization development and a sharp increase in market activity.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ONDO traded around the &lt;strong&gt;$0.55 area on the September 25, 2026 market snapshot&lt;/strong&gt;, with CoinGecko showing a roughly 26% 24-hour move and substantially higher trading activity. Other market reports put the intraday move close to 29%, making ONDO one of the notable large-cap crypto gainers of the session.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Different data providers may show slightly different 24-hour percentage changes depending on their snapshot timing.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;CoinGecko’s seven-day history also showed a sharp weekly move, with ONDO rising from roughly &lt;strong&gt;$0.48 on September 19 to around $0.61 on September 25&lt;/strong&gt; on the corresponding historical market snapshots. That represents an approximate &lt;strong&gt;27% seven-day increase&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The rally is notable because several factors have arrived at roughly the same time: Ondo Finance’s launch of &lt;strong&gt;Ondo Intelligent Portfolios&lt;/strong&gt;, the company’s announcement that its first three portfolios use strategies developed by &lt;strong&gt;BlackRock for Ondo&lt;/strong&gt;, growing connections with traditional financial infrastructure and increased derivatives activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So, what exactly is driving ONDO’s sudden move?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Ondo’s New Intelligent Portfolios Are the Main Fundamental Catalyst&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most important fresh development came on &lt;strong&gt;September 24, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, when Ondo Finance announced the launch of &lt;strong&gt;Ondo Intelligent Portfolios&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to Ondo Finance’s official announcement, the product consists of professionally designed investment portfolios, with each portfolio represented by a single onchain token.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ondo said the first three portfolios are based on &lt;strong&gt;portfolio strategies developed by BlackRock for Ondo&lt;/strong&gt;. The company described the launch as the first time exposure to those portfolio strategies has been made available to onchain investors.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This attribution is important. The BlackRock reference comes from &lt;strong&gt;Ondo Finance’s own September 24 announcement&lt;/strong&gt;. It should not be interpreted as BlackRock issuing, endorsing or directly investing in the ONDO &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/solana-options-expiry-why-sol-is.html"&gt;cryptocurrency token&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, the development concerns investment strategies used within Ondo’s new portfolio products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the BlackRock Connection Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BlackRock has become one of the most visible traditional asset managers in the digital-asset and tokenization sector. That makes the use of BlackRock-developed strategies inside an Ondo onchain product a significant development for the tokenization narrative.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ondo’s broader objective is to bring traditional financial products and investment strategies onto blockchain infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new Intelligent Portfolios take that concept one step further.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of simply putting an individual stock, bond or &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitcoins-156-billion-options-expiry.html"&gt;ETF onchain&lt;/a&gt;, Ondo is packaging an entire investment strategy into a single tokenized portfolio.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to Ondo, the portfolios can use tokenized equities and ETFs, while portfolio allocation and rebalancing can be handled through the product’s underlying infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a new potential use case for tokenization: &lt;strong&gt;representing investment strategies themselves rather than only individual financial assets.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;ONDO’s Price Move Was Also Amplified by Market Activity&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new product announcement provides the fundamental backdrop, but it does not necessarily explain the entire speed of ONDO’s rally.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto markets can move rapidly when new information meets aggressive derivatives positioning. When traders are heavily positioned for a decline and the underlying token instead moves higher, short positions can be forced to close.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That process can create additional buying pressure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Market data cited in reports on September 25 showed approximately &lt;strong&gt;$240,000 in short liquidations&lt;/strong&gt; versus around &lt;strong&gt;$10,000 in long liquidations&lt;/strong&gt; during the measured period.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;About $10,000&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The imbalance suggests that short-position closures contributed to the sharp move, although liquidation figures alone cannot establish that the entire rally was caused by a short squeeze.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Spot buying, derivatives positioning, momentum traders and the new Ondo announcement can all contribute to the same price move.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Ondo’s Tokenization Story Was Already Expanding&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The BlackRock-related portfolio announcement did not arrive in isolation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ondo has been steadily expanding its tokenization infrastructure throughout 2026, moving beyond its earlier reputation as primarily a provider of tokenized U.S. Treasury exposure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company now has products and infrastructure covering tokenized stocks and ETFs, dollar-denominated assets, derivatives and blockchain infrastructure designed for financial markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That broader expansion helps explain why traders may view the latest announcement as part of a larger strategy rather than as a standalone headline.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;DTCC Fund/SERV Adds Another Institutional Layer&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Another important development came on &lt;strong&gt;September 16, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ondo Finance announced that its subsidiary &lt;strong&gt;Oasis Pro Markets&lt;/strong&gt; had joined the Depository Trust &amp;amp; Clearing Corporation’s &lt;strong&gt;Fund/SERV&lt;/strong&gt; platform.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to Ondo, Fund/SERV currently supports more than 85% of U.S. mutual-fund transaction activity. The company described Oasis Pro Markets as the first tokenization platform to participate in the fund industry's transaction-processing and distribution network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The significance is straightforward: tokenization needs connections to traditional financial infrastructure if it is going to reach a much larger institutional audience.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchain technology can create tokenized representations of assets, but distribution, settlement, compliance and transaction processing still matter.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ondo’s Fund/SERV integration therefore fits into the same broader strategy as Intelligent Portfolios: connecting blockchain-based financial products with established financial-market infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Ondo Is Moving Beyond Tokenized Treasuries&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ondo Finance initially became closely associated with tokenized U.S. Treasury products, including its USDY ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Its strategy has since expanded toward tokenized equities, exchange-traded funds and other financial products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ondo Intelligent Portfolios represents another step in that direction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The focus is no longer simply whether an individual financial asset can be represented onchain. The bigger question is whether complete investment strategies can also be packaged and distributed through blockchain infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If that model gains adoption, it could potentially make tokenization relevant to a much broader section of the asset-management industry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Ondo Stocks Reached $1 Billion in TVL in May&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company's tokenized-equity business has also been gaining attention.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On &lt;strong&gt;May 11, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, Ondo Finance announced that &lt;strong&gt;Ondo Stocks had surpassed $1 billion in total value locked&lt;/strong&gt;, describing it as the first tokenized-stocks platform to reach that milestone.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the time, Ondo said the platform had more than &lt;strong&gt;260 tokenized U.S. stocks and ETFs&lt;/strong&gt; available across Solana, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/what-happens-when-ai-agent-runs-out-of.html"&gt;Ethereum &lt;/a&gt;and BNB Chain, with more than &lt;strong&gt;$18 billion in cumulative trading volume&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because that $1 billion figure is specifically a &lt;strong&gt;May 11 milestone&lt;/strong&gt;, it should not be presented as a September 25 current TVL figure without a newer official update.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This matters for ONDO because the token's broader market narrative is increasingly connected to &lt;strong&gt;real-world asset tokenization&lt;/strong&gt; and institutional financial infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why ONDO Moved So Quickly&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Several factors appear to have converged.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Fresh product catalyst:&lt;/strong&gt; Ondo Finance launched Intelligent Portfolios on September 24.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;BlackRock-developed strategies:&lt;/strong&gt; According to Ondo Finance, the first three portfolios use strategies developed by BlackRock for Ondo.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Institutional narrative:&lt;/strong&gt; The launch strengthens Ondo’s positioning at the intersection of traditional asset management and blockchain infrastructure.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;DTCC integration:&lt;/strong&gt; Oasis Pro Markets joined DTCC Fund/SERV on September 16.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Tokenization growth:&lt;/strong&gt; Ondo continues expanding tokenized stocks, ETFs and other financial products.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Derivatives activity:&lt;/strong&gt; Reported short liquidations were substantially larger than long liquidations during the measured period.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Momentum trading:&lt;/strong&gt; A rapid price increase can attract additional traders and amplify an existing move.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;None of these factors should be treated as the sole explanation for the rally. Instead, the price action appears to reflect a combination of fresh fundamental news and market positioning.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does the Move Mean ONDO Is in a New Long-Term Trend?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A sharp daily gain can be important, but it does not by itself establish a long-term trend.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next stage will depend on whether ONDO can maintain elevated trading activity after the initial news reaction and whether the underlying Ondo ecosystem continues to expand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traders may therefore focus on spot volume, derivatives open interest, funding rates, liquidation activity and the token's ability to hold a meaningful portion of its recent gains.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;From a fundamental perspective, future Intelligent Portfolio adoption, additional tokenized-asset products, institutional integrations and the growth of Ondo’s broader infrastructure will be important developments to monitor.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the ONDO Rally Does Not Prove&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest price move does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; prove that ONDO will continue rising.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It also does not mean that BlackRock has issued or endorsed the ONDO token. The BlackRock reference in this story comes from Ondo Finance’s announcement that its first three Intelligent Portfolios are based on portfolio strategies developed by BlackRock for Ondo.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Likewise, the presence of short liquidations does not automatically mean the entire rally was a short squeeze.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These distinctions are important because cryptocurrency markets can react rapidly to institutional headlines, particularly when leveraged derivatives positions are active.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Traders Will Watch Next&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;After a move of nearly 30% in reported 24-hour data, the market's attention is likely to shift from the initial catalyst to confirmation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;First, traders will watch whether ONDO can maintain the higher price range without a rapid reversal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Second, they will monitor whether trading volume remains elevated. A large price move accompanied by sustained spot-market activity can provide different information from a short-lived derivatives spike.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Third, derivatives metrics such as open interest, funding rates and liquidation levels can show whether leverage is building again.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Finally, investors will be watching Ondo Finance's actual product adoption. Intelligent Portfolios, tokenized equities and institutional infrastructure will need continued usage and development if the broader tokenization thesis is to translate into lasting ecosystem growth.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ONDO's nearly 30% surge on September 25 is being driven by a combination of &lt;strong&gt;fresh product news, institutional tokenization developments and derivatives activity&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The immediate fundamental catalyst is Ondo Finance's September 24 launch of &lt;strong&gt;Ondo Intelligent Portfolios&lt;/strong&gt;. According to Ondo's official announcement, the first three portfolios are based on portfolio strategies developed by BlackRock for Ondo.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That announcement comes shortly after Ondo's September 16 integration with &lt;strong&gt;DTCC Fund/SERV&lt;/strong&gt;, adding another connection between tokenized financial products and traditional market infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, reported short liquidations were significantly larger than long liquidations during the measured period, suggesting that derivatives positioning helped amplify the move.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ondo's tokenized-stock business also provides longer-term context. The company reported a $1 billion TVL milestone for Ondo Stocks on May 11, demonstrating the scale the tokenization platform had already reached before the latest ONDO price move.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The key question now is whether the market treats the rally as a short-term news reaction or whether Ondo's expanding tokenization business can support sustained interest in the ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, ONDO's move highlights a broader trend in crypto: &lt;strong&gt;institutional tokenization announcements are increasingly capable of becoming major market catalysts when they collide with active derivatives markets.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;All figures in this article are snapshots from the reported periods and may have changed since publication.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Trump $1 Coin Is Here: The U.S. Mint's New Dollar Has a Surprising Story</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEheqVr5PEDzVH1NdcPWPzH7C2JpV5X5qxMdcboVkKC3cGZNkoDvdnWxf5ESihJa0LBa36t7qJQ_G97n3AtqW4LJDvrCbWpd8vZJqBCuwe4_qFFk8nyLVKK_mZ9jDOCHSaYJGIawX_KaesMyhnRsWE5B6uKgiD3W9mK7rzFD18WWNRq-r34iQbu-coraCjjj/s1672/trump-2026-us-mint-1-dollar-coin.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="2026 U.S. Mint $1 coin featuring Donald Trump for America's 250th anniversary" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEheqVr5PEDzVH1NdcPWPzH7C2JpV5X5qxMdcboVkKC3cGZNkoDvdnWxf5ESihJa0LBa36t7qJQ_G97n3AtqW4LJDvrCbWpd8vZJqBCuwe4_qFFk8nyLVKK_mZ9jDOCHSaYJGIawX_KaesMyhnRsWE5B6uKgiD3W9mK7rzFD18WWNRq-r34iQbu-coraCjjj/w400-h225/trump-2026-us-mint-1-dollar-coin.jpg.png" title="Donald Trump 2026 U.S. Mint $1 Coin" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;Donald Trump is now on an official U.S. dollar coin — and the story behind it is more interesting than the viral headline suggests.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The United States Mint has begun selling the &lt;strong&gt;2026 Semiquincentennial President Donald J. Trump $1 Coin&lt;/strong&gt;, a new dollar created as part of America's 250th-anniversary celebration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At first glance, it sounds simple: a new $1 coin with a sitting president on it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But then the details start getting interesting.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The coin has a &lt;strong&gt;circulating finish&lt;/strong&gt; and is legal tender, yet the Mint says the coins being sold in the current release &lt;strong&gt;have never been placed into circulation&lt;/strong&gt;. They are being offered in collector-oriented rolls and bags instead.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And there is another twist: the Philadelphia Mint struck &lt;strong&gt;9 million Trump $1 coins in July&lt;/strong&gt;, while the two initial collector products can hold a maximum of 8.75 million coins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Then there is the really fun part for collectors: &lt;strong&gt;250,000 coins were struck on July 4 with a special “July 4th” privy mark&lt;/strong&gt; and randomly inserted into the rolls and bags.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So, what exactly is this coin, how much does it cost, and why are collectors suddenly paying so much attention?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;First Things First: The Trump $1 Coin Is Real&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes, this is not a cryptocurrency, political token or privately produced commemorative medallion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The &lt;strong&gt;U.S. Mint is officially producing the coin&lt;/strong&gt; as part of the country's 2026 Semiquincentennial program.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The coin carries a $1 denomination and is legal tender.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The obverse features President Donald Trump, while the reverse uses the Presidential Seal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The design also carries the dates &lt;strong&gt;1776 ~ 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, marking 250 years since the founding of the United States.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to the U.S. Mint, the Trump portrait was designed by Chief Engraver Joseph Menna and was inspired by an official White House photograph by Daniel Torok.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The “Circulating Coin” Part Is Where Things Get Interesting&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You've probably seen the viral description calling this a &lt;strong&gt;circulating U.S. coin&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is a reason for that wording, but it can easily confuse readers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Mint classifies the Trump dollar as having a &lt;strong&gt;circulating finish&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the Mint's product page explicitly says these Philadelphia-struck coins &lt;strong&gt;have never been placed into circulation&lt;/strong&gt;, even though they remain legal tender.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In other words, the coin is designed to look and function like circulating-quality U.S. coinage, but the current release is being sold through the Mint in rolls and bags rather than distributed through banks for everyday change.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="overflow-x: auto;"&gt;

&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Much Does the Trump Dollar Cost?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where the $1 face value gets a little misleading.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Mint is selling the coins in two formats:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;25-coin roll:&lt;/strong&gt; $61&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;100-coin bag:&lt;/strong&gt; $154.50&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The first 24 hours of the release also carry a &lt;strong&gt;household order limit of two per product&lt;/strong&gt;. The Mint says that limit remains in place until 2 p.m. ET on September 3.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So if you're wondering whether you can simply walk into a store and buy one Trump dollar for $1, that's not how this particular release works.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The individual coin has a $1 face value. The higher Mint prices apply to the packaged collector products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Now Comes the 9 Million Coin Mystery&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Here's one of the most interesting numbers surrounding the launch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to CoinNews' analysis of U.S. Mint monthly production figures, the &lt;strong&gt;Philadelphia Mint struck 9,000,000 Trump $1 coins in July 2026&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Denver reported zero Trump dollars.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes Philadelphia the sole reported production facility for this coin so far.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But don't make the mistake of calling 9 million the &lt;strong&gt;final mintage&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It isn't.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Mint currently lists &lt;strong&gt;no mintage limit&lt;/strong&gt; for the product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So the most accurate way to describe the number is:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;9 million Trump dollars had been struck by the Philadelphia Mint in July, based on the published production figures.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is a production figure, not necessarily the final number that will exist by the end of 2026.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;9 Million Struck, But Only 8.75 Million Fit in the First Products&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Here's where the numbers get even more interesting.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Mint lists a product limit of:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;150,000 rolls × 25 coins = &lt;strong&gt;3.75 million coins&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;50,000 bags × 100 coins = &lt;strong&gt;5 million coins&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Together, those two products can contain a maximum of &lt;strong&gt;8.75 million coins&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the July production figure is &lt;strong&gt;9 million&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That leaves a difference of &lt;strong&gt;250,000 coins&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And that number happens to match the number of special July 4th privy-mark coins struck by the Mint.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is an interesting alignment, but readers should be careful here: it does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; by itself prove exactly how every one of the 9 million coins will ultimately be distributed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Mint has not announced a final 2026 mintage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The July 4th Trump Dollar: The Collector's Treasure Hunt&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is arguably the most exciting part of the launch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Mint says &lt;strong&gt;250,000 Trump $1 coins were struck on July 4, 2026&lt;/strong&gt; at the Philadelphia Mint with a special &lt;strong&gt;“July 4th” privy mark&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those coins were randomly included in the rolls and bags being sold to collectors.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means opening one of these products becomes a small treasure hunt.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You could open a roll and find only standard Trump &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/andrew-cuomo-warns-us-could-lose-crypto.html"&gt;dollars&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Or you could discover one carrying the special July 4th marking.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Mint has not said that the privy-mark coins will be distributed at a perfectly uniform ratio, so collectors should not assume that every specific roll or bag will contain one.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But with 250,000 marked coins among the July production total of 9 million, the special version represents a relatively small portion of the reported production.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;And No, the Trump Dollar Isn't Made of Gold&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The coin certainly looks golden.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But don't let the color fool you.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Trump $1 &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/elon-musk-says-ai-could-add-20-trillion.html"&gt;coin&lt;/a&gt; is &lt;strong&gt;not a gold coin&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Mint lists its composition as:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;6% zinc&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;3.5% manganese&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;2% nickel&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Balance copper&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It weighs &lt;strong&gt;8.100 grams&lt;/strong&gt; and measures &lt;strong&gt;26.49 millimeters&lt;/strong&gt; in diameter.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So if somebody tells you that every Trump dollar contains $1 worth of gold, that's simply not what the Mint's specifications say.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is on the Front and Back?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The front, or obverse, features a portrait of President Donald J. Trump.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It includes the inscriptions:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;LIBERTY&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;IN GOD WE TRUST&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;1776 ~ 2026&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The reverse features the &lt;strong&gt;Presidential Seal&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The shield on the eagle's breast contains an additional &lt;strong&gt;250&lt;/strong&gt; marking to emphasize America's Semiquincentennial.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The reverse also carries &lt;strong&gt;UNITED STATES OF AMERICA&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;ONE DOLLAR&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Does the Coin Say 1776 ~ 2026?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It's not a reference to Trump's presidency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It represents the 250th anniversary of the United States.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776, and 2026 marks 250 years since that founding-era milestone.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Mint has created a wider Semiquincentennial coin program around the anniversary, including special circulating designs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Trump dollar is one of the most politically recognizable pieces in that program.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Is Trump Really the First Sitting President on a U.S. Coin?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is another headline that deserves a little context.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trump's appearance on the 2026 dollar is certainly unusual because the United States has traditionally avoided putting living presidents on its regular currency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But saying he is the first sitting president ever to appear on &lt;em&gt;any&lt;/em&gt; U.S. coin would be too broad.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is a historical precedent: &lt;strong&gt;Calvin Coolidge appeared on a 1926 commemorative half dollar while he was still president&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why the safest description is that the Trump dollar is an &lt;strong&gt;extraordinary modern U.S. coin featuring a sitting president&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than treating the viral “first ever” wording as an absolute historical fact.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Legal Authority Behind the Coin&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The coin is not simply something the Mint decided to create on its own.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Semiquincentennial coin program was authorized through federal legislation, including the &lt;strong&gt;Circulating Collectible Coin Redesign Act of 2020&lt;/strong&gt;, Public Law 116-330.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The legislation provides authority for special $1 coinage connected with the nation's 250th anniversary.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The law's design restrictions also help explain why the president's portrait appears on the obverse rather than the reverse.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That legal framework is an important piece of the story because it shows that the coin is part of an established federal coin program rather than a temporary political novelty.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Trump Dollar vs. $TRUMP Crypto: Don't Mix Them Up&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For crypto readers, there is another obvious source of confusion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Donald Trump is already associated with the &lt;strong&gt;$TRUMP cryptocurrency&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the two are completely different.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 15px; margin: 20px 0px; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Cryptocurrency token&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Physical asset&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Digital asset&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Owning a Trump dollar therefore does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean owning $TRUMP cryptocurrency, and buying the token does not give anyone ownership of a U.S. Mint coin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could You Actually Spend the Coin?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes, it is legal tender.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But that's different from saying you'll suddenly find Trump dollars in every cash register.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The current Mint release consists of collector rolls and bags, and the Mint explicitly says the Philadelphia coins have never been placed into circulation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So theoretically you could use one as a $1 coin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Practically speaking, finding one in everyday commerce is likely to be much less common than finding the familiar $1 bill.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could the Trump Dollar Become Valuable?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is probably the question collectors will ask next.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The answer is: &lt;strong&gt;possibly, but nobody knows yet.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A coin becoming collectible does not automatically mean it becomes a great investment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Future value can depend on:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Final mintage&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Collector demand&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Coin condition&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Special varieties&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Privy marks&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Original Mint packaging&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Long-term historical interest&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The July 4th privy-mark version may attract particular attention because only 250,000 were struck according to the Mint.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But scarcity alone does not guarantee a high resale price.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Collectors should watch actual market &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/what-is-gotok-truth-behind-ai-project.html"&gt;transactions&lt;/a&gt; rather than assuming that every unusual-looking Trump dollar will become expensive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;One Number Collectors Should Watch: 9 Million&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The 9 million production figure is important because it gives collectors the first concrete look at how many Trump dollars had actually been struck.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there are three different numbers worth keeping separate:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 15px; margin: 20px 0px; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;tr&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;Trump dollars struck at Philadelphia in July 2026, &lt;br /&gt;according to CoinNews' production analysis&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(136, 136, 136); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;8.75 million&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those numbers are related, but they should not be treated as identical concepts.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Most importantly, &lt;strong&gt;9 million is not necessarily the final 2026 mintage&lt;/strong&gt;. The Mint currently lists no mintage limit for the product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why This Coin Is Getting So Much Attention&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are plenty of U.S. coins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are plenty of presidential collectibles.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And there are plenty of Trump-themed products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But this coin combines all three worlds in one official government-issued dollar.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It also arrives during America's 250th-anniversary year, giving it a historical backdrop that ordinary political merchandise simply does not have.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For traditional coin collectors, the attraction is the unusual design and anniversary connection.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Trump supporters and political memorabilia collectors, the portrait gives it another layer of interest.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And for crypto audiences, the obvious comparison with the $TRUMP token makes the launch even more intriguing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Should Collectors Look For?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you're examining a Trump dollar, several details are worth checking.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Philadelphia origin:&lt;/strong&gt; Current Trump dollar production is Philadelphia-only.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No mint mark:&lt;/strong&gt; The coin does not carry a P mint mark.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;July 4th privy:&lt;/strong&gt; Look for the special privy mark on eligible coins.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Condition:&lt;/strong&gt; Uncirculated condition can matter for collectors.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Packaging:&lt;/strong&gt; Original Mint rolls and bags may have collector interest.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Authenticity:&lt;/strong&gt; Be cautious when buying individual coins from secondary-market sellers.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The &lt;strong&gt;2026 Donald J. Trump $1 coin is officially real&lt;/strong&gt;, and the U.S. Mint has begun its collector release.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is a $1 legal-tender coin created for America's 250th anniversary, featuring Trump on the obverse and the Presidential Seal on the reverse.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the most interesting part isn't simply that Trump's face is on a dollar.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It's the combination of details surrounding the launch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The coin has a &lt;strong&gt;circulating finish&lt;/strong&gt;, but the current Mint products have never been placed into general circulation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Philadelphia Mint struck &lt;strong&gt;9 million&lt;/strong&gt; Trump dollars in July, according to CoinNews' analysis of Mint production figures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The initial rolls and bags can contain up to &lt;strong&gt;8.75 million coins&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And hidden among them are &lt;strong&gt;250,000 July 4th privy-mark coins&lt;/strong&gt; — turning the release into something of a collector treasure hunt.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So if you see someone say, “Trump is on the new $1 coin,” they're absolutely right.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But if someone tells you every Trump dollar is already circulating through American stores, or that the coin is made of gold, or that it is the same thing as the $TRUMP cryptocurrency, that's where the story starts to go off track.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the Trump dollar is best understood as something sitting at the intersection of &lt;strong&gt;American history, politics, official currency and modern collecting culture&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is the Trump $1 coin real?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes. The U.S. Mint officially issued the 2026 Semiquincentennial President Donald J. Trump $1 Coin as part of America's 250th-anniversary program.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How many Trump $1 coins were produced?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The Philadelphia Mint struck 9 million Trump $1 coins in July 2026, according to CoinNews' analysis of U.S. Mint production figures. This is a reported production figure, not necessarily the final 2026 mintage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is the Trump $1 coin in circulation?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The coin has a circulating finish and is legal tender, but the U.S. Mint says the Philadelphia-struck coins in the current release have never been placed into circulation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How much does a Trump $1 coin roll cost?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Mint lists a 25-coin roll at $61.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How much is a 100-coin Trump dollar bag?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Mint lists the 100-coin bag at $154.50.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How many July 4th Trump coins are there?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Mint says 250,000 Trump $1 coins were struck on July 4 with a special “July 4th” privy mark and randomly included in the rolls and bags.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is the Trump dollar made of gold?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. Despite its golden color, the coin uses a copper-based alloy containing zinc, manganese and nickel.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does the Trump $1 coin have a mint mark?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. The current Trump dollars are struck at the Philadelphia Mint and do not carry a mint mark.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is the Trump dollar the same as the $TRUMP cryptocurrency?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. The official U.S. Mint coin and the $TRUMP cryptocurrency are completely separate assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Will the Trump dollar become valuable?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Its future collectible value is uncertain. Rarity, condition, special varieties, packaging and long-term collector demand will all matter.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Can a Bitcoin Transaction Be Reversed If Sent to the Wrong Address?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhnTVwmam_JxA3dPELFhYEVfxBk8X-tRqrjtjM7p5QyvqbqBnhUvT-8Lx8xG9rvh4GcLBGSF1E7GfVemj5cUC8D-AyzEv-z0VvlahBJeVCJvD33avINaRE2YmUz6ULrzRDrkPgaEsO_XCmPNwraapsD4YbhIdKU3NA-uWf4L109Qm8n21zocH2_h8MkuMyB/s1670/bitcoin-transaction-wrong-address-recovery.jpg%20(2).png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin transaction sent to the wrong address and the possibility of recovery" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1670" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhnTVwmam_JxA3dPELFhYEVfxBk8X-tRqrjtjM7p5QyvqbqBnhUvT-8Lx8xG9rvh4GcLBGSF1E7GfVemj5cUC8D-AyzEv-z0VvlahBJeVCJvD33avINaRE2YmUz6ULrzRDrkPgaEsO_XCmPNwraapsD4YbhIdKU3NA-uWf4L109Qm8n21zocH2_h8MkuMyB/w640-h360/bitcoin-transaction-wrong-address-recovery.jpg%20(2).png" title="Can a Bitcoin Transaction Be Reversed If Sent to Wrong Address?" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Sending Bitcoin to the wrong address is one of the most stressful mistakes a crypto user can make. The good news is that there are situations where funds may still be recoverable. The bad news is that a confirmed Bitcoin transaction sent to the wrong on-chain address generally cannot be cancelled or reversed.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The key distinction is &lt;strong&gt;how the Bitcoin was sent&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction was broadcast to the Bitcoin blockchain, the network does not have a central authority that can simply press a reverse button. Bitcoin.org states that Bitcoin transactions are irreversible once confirmed and can only be refunded by the person who received the funds. Coinbase similarly says that on-chain sends are irreversible and that it cannot retrieve funds sent to an incorrect address. &lt;a href="https://bitcoin.org/en/faq" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Bitcoin.org&lt;/a&gt; and &lt;a href="https://help.coinbase.com/en/coinbase/trading-and-funding/cryptocurrency-trading-pairs/steps-to-send-crypto" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Coinbase&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But an &lt;strong&gt;off-chain transfer between users of the same platform&lt;/strong&gt; can work differently. Coinbase, for example, distinguishes on-chain sends from off-chain transfers between Coinbase users using a phone number, email address or username.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 750px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Situation&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Can It Be Reversed?&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;What Usually Happens&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Confirmed Bitcoin sent to wrong on-chain address&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Generally no&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;You must contact the recipient if the address is controlled by someone identifiable.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Bitcoin sent to an address nobody controls&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Generally no&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;The funds may become permanently inaccessible.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Wrong Coinbase recipient via an off-chain transfer&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Depends on status and platform rules&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;A pending eligible payment may have cancellation options; a claimed transfer is much harder to recover.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Wrong network&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Depends on asset, network and service&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Recovery is not guaranteed and may require a supported recovery process.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens When Bitcoin Is Sent to the Wrong Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin uses cryptographic addresses to determine where a transaction's outputs can be spent. Once a valid transaction is confirmed on the blockchain, the network does not provide a normal mechanism for the sender to undo it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you accidentally send BTC to another person's valid Bitcoin address, the Bitcoin network treats the transaction according to its rules. It does not know that you made a mistake.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is also no Bitcoin customer-service department that can reverse a confirmed blockchain transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org explains the situation directly: a confirmed Bitcoin payment cannot simply be reversed and can only be refunded by the person who received the funds. &lt;a href="https://bitcoin.org/en/you-need-to-know" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Bitcoin.org — Some things you need to know&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;On-Chain vs Off-Chain: The Difference That Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is the most important concept for anyone trying to recover a mistaken crypto payment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;On-chain Bitcoin transaction&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An on-chain transaction is recorded and processed by the Bitcoin network. The transaction has blockchain data such as inputs, outputs and a transaction ID.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once it is confirmed, the transaction becomes part of Bitcoin's blockchain history. Coinbase says its on-chain sends are irreversible and that it cannot retrieve funds sent to an incorrect address. &lt;a href="https://help.coinbase.com/en/coinbase/trading-and-funding/cryptocurrency-trading-pairs/steps-to-send-crypto" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Coinbase — Steps to send crypto&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Off-chain transfer&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An off-chain transfer is different because the movement may happen inside a company's own system rather than as a new transaction on the public &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-i-generate-same-bitcoin-address.html"&gt;Bitcoin blockchain&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Coinbase currently describes off-chain sends as transfers to another Coinbase user using a phone number, email address or username. Coinbase says these transfers are instant, have no network transaction fee and do not appear on the blockchain. &lt;a href="https://help.coinbase.com/en/coinbase/trading-and-funding/cryptocurrency-trading-pairs/steps-to-send-crypto" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Coinbase Help&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because the transfer is handled differently from an on-chain transaction, the platform can have controls that do not exist at the Bitcoin blockchain level.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can a Pending Bitcoin Transaction Still Be Stopped?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A pending transaction deserves a different answer from a confirmed transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If a transaction has not yet been confirmed, its status can depend on the wallet, exchange and blockchain network. However, &lt;strong&gt;pending does not automatically mean the sender can cancel it&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin transactions are designed to be broadcast and eventually confirmed according to network rules. Some wallets and services may offer cancellation or replacement features under specific conditions, but those features should not be confused with reversing a confirmed payment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, Coinbase provides separate cancellation functionality for certain pending transfers handled through its platform. Its help documentation also distinguishes pending payments from completed crypto transfers. &lt;a href="https://help.coinbase.com/en/coinbase/getting-started/crypto-education/can-i-cancel-a-digital-currency-transaction" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Coinbase — Can I cancel a cryptocurrency transaction?&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If I Sent Bitcoin to the Wrong Person?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you sent BTC to a valid address belonging to another person, your best option is to identify the recipient and request a refund.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is not the same as reversing the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-someone-find-your-name-from-bitcoin-wallet.html"&gt;Bitcoin transaction&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The recipient would have to voluntarily send the Bitcoin back to an address you control. Coinbase's guidance for crypto sent to the wrong address similarly recommends contacting the recipient and asking for cooperation. If the owner cannot be identified, recovery may not be possible. &lt;a href="https://help.coinbase.com/en/coinbase/trading-and-funding/sending-or-receiving-cryptocurrency/i-sent-funds-to-the-wrong-address-how-do-i-get-them-back" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Coinbase — Crypto sent to the wrong address&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If the Wrong Address Belongs to an Exchange?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This situation can sometimes be more complicated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Suppose you intended to send Bitcoin to your own exchange deposit address but copied an old address, selected the wrong account or made another mistake. The blockchain transaction itself may still be irreversible, but the receiving service could potentially have internal procedures for handling certain deposits.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not mean the exchange is required to recover the funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The first step is to collect the transaction ID, the sending address, receiving address, asset, network and amount. Then contact the receiving platform through its official support channel.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Do not send your private key or recovery phrase to anyone claiming they can "recover" the transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can Bitcoin Be Recovered If the Address Is Invalid?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin addresses contain checks and formats designed to reduce certain input errors, so many obvious mistakes are rejected before a transaction can be broadcast.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But if the address is valid and the transaction has been successfully confirmed, the situation is different.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A valid address does not necessarily mean that you know who controls it. If the address belongs to another person, recovery depends on that person's cooperation. If nobody controls the relevant private key, the funds may effectively become inaccessible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org notes that if a valid address is not controlled by anyone, funds sent there can become permanently inaccessible. &lt;a href="https://bitcoin.org/en/faq" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Bitcoin.org FAQ&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If I Sent Bitcoin to the Wrong Network?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A wrong-network transfer is not exactly the same problem as sending BTC to the wrong Bitcoin address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Many crypto assets can exist on multiple blockchain networks, and exchanges may support only particular networks for a given deposit or withdrawal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Coinbase specifically warns users to select the correct network when sending crypto and states that it cannot recover funds sent using an incorrect network in the relevant on-chain send flow. &lt;a href="https://help.coinbase.com/en/coinbase/trading-and-funding/cryptocurrency-trading-pairs/steps-to-send-crypto" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Coinbase — Steps to send crypto&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recovery possibilities can depend on the asset, network, destination service and whether the receiving platform supports an asset-recovery process. In other words, &lt;strong&gt;wrong network does not have one universal recovery rule&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Should You Do Immediately After Sending BTC to the Wrong Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you realize the mistake immediately, do not panic. Follow these steps:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Find the transaction ID.&lt;/strong&gt; Open your wallet or exchange and locate the transaction hash/TXID.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check the blockchain.&lt;/strong&gt; Determine whether the transaction is pending or confirmed.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Verify the destination.&lt;/strong&gt; Compare the exact address shown in the transaction with the address you intended to use.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Identify the receiving service.&lt;/strong&gt; If the address belongs to an exchange or business, contact its official support team.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;If it belongs to a person you know, contact them.&lt;/strong&gt; Explain the mistake and ask whether they can return the funds.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Do not give anyone your seed phrase or private key.&lt;/strong&gt; Legitimate recovery does not require handing over your wallet credentials.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Information Should You Give Support?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If an exchange or wallet provider may be able to investigate the transaction, provide enough information for it to identify the transfer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 650px; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;/thead&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;
