&lt;h2&gt;Existing iOS Users Are Not Affected&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For users who already installed Pump.fun on an iPhone or iPad, the latest update does not indicate a service shutdown.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Pump.fun mobile team said existing users can continue using the app normally. It also specifically stated that users’ funds are safe. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes the current development different from a full suspension of the Pump.fun application. The immediate problem is focused on &lt;strong&gt;new iOS downloads in the United States and India&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Android Users Can Still Download Pump.fun&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Android version remains available through Google Play, according to the latest update from the Pump.fun mobile team. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This means users who are new to Pump.fun and use Android still have an official mobile download option, while new iOS users in the affected regions currently have to wait for availability to return.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Is Pump.fun Temporarily Unavailable on Apple?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The exact reason for the temporary iOS download restriction has not been publicly confirmed.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is an important distinction. There is currently no verified information establishing that Apple has permanently banned Pump.fun, that regulators ordered its removal, or that the restriction was caused by a particular compliance or policy issue.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Until Pump.fun or Apple provides a specific explanation, those claims would be speculation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Pump.fun mobile team has described the situation as temporary, but a specific restoration time was not provided in the update reviewed for this report. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Is Pump.fun Still Operating?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. The current development does not indicate that Pump.fun has shut down.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Pump.fun website remains operational, and its official platform continues to offer &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/esma-warns-crypto-and-traditional.html"&gt;token creation&lt;/a&gt;, discovery and trading functionality. The website also continues to advertise its mobile experience. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company's published terms describe Pump as a platform designed to help users create and trade digital assets. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does the App Store Issue Mean for New Users?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The immediate impact is mainly about access.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A new iPhone user in the United States or India who wants to install Pump.fun may currently be unable to obtain the application through Apple's App Store. Existing users, however, are not facing the same reported restriction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Android users remain able to access the application through Google Play, while the web version of Pump.fun remains available.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For a platform that relies heavily on fast-moving &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/liquid-hack-takes-new-turn-as.html"&gt;memecoin&lt;/a&gt; activity and mobile users, even a temporary regional download interruption can create friction for onboarding new users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Pump.fun's Mobile Push Comes Under the Spotlight&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The incident also highlights how dependent crypto applications can be on the distribution policies of major mobile platforms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Pump.fun has increasingly positioned its mobile product as an important part of its trading experience. Its website describes mobile access as a faster way to interact with the platform, while its help center includes dedicated guides covering mobile trading, deposits, withdrawals, coin creation and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/okx-launches-openai-and-anthropic-pre.html"&gt;wallet functions.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That makes App Store availability an important part of the platform's ability to reach new users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Users Should Avoid Unofficial Pump.fun Downloads&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With the app temporarily unavailable to some iOS users, unofficial download links could begin circulating online.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Users should be careful about downloading applications or wallet software claiming to be an alternative Pump.fun app. An App Store restriction does not make third-party download links trustworthy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Users should rely on Pump.fun's official website and verified channels for updates about the application's availability.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Pump.fun banned from Apple's App Store?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is currently no confirmed evidence that Pump.fun has been permanently banned. The latest information says the app is temporarily unavailable for new downloads in the U.S. and India iOS App Stores.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can existing iPhone users still use Pump.fun?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Existing users are reportedly unaffected and can continue using the application normally. The Pump.fun mobile team also said users' funds are safe. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Pump.fun available on Android?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. The latest update says new users can download the Pump.fun app through Google Play. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Pump.fun still working on the web?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Pump.fun's official website remains operational and continues to provide access to its platform. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why did Pump.fun disappear from the U.S. and India App Stores?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The specific reason has not been confirmed publicly. Pump.fun has described the availability issue as temporary, but no verified explanation for the App Store restriction was provided in the latest update.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Pump.fun's mobile app is temporarily unavailable for new downloads from Apple's U.S. and India App Stores, but the platform itself has not shut down.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Existing iOS users can continue using the app, according to Pump.fun's mobile team, while Android users can still download it through Google Play. The web platform also remains operational. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The reason behind Apple's temporary availability change remains unclear. Until an official explanation is provided, claims that Pump.fun has been banned or removed because of a specific regulatory or policy issue should be treated cautiously.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Trump Announces AI Force and AI Czar as He Says AI Could Reach 25% of US GDP</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiWqRgwBC04_nShqtLF-QEFL5PIqkrZ1HQebb3NHKrZbp-3Jj0HNJinWOIvOTLtImSRxUSMD0PpeEexoM1aLcdFQpJxgbFR6wLd5yBQvuCHI4qVUEBdtxXVQKD3mwIRAJgqw0NtAf78jn4Gc2FPOi81BJl_rpCLDElb1Y8ad9ZOc0lQm40X867sx6WgKDvb/s1536/trump-ai-force-ai-czar-us-ai-strategy.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Trump announces AI Force and AI czar as US expands artificial intelligence strategy" border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="426" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiWqRgwBC04_nShqtLF-QEFL5PIqkrZ1HQebb3NHKrZbp-3Jj0HNJinWOIvOTLtImSRxUSMD0PpeEexoM1aLcdFQpJxgbFR6wLd5yBQvuCHI4qVUEBdtxXVQKD3mwIRAJgqw0NtAf78jn4Gc2FPOi81BJl_rpCLDElb1Y8ad9ZOc0lQm40X867sx6WgKDvb/w640-h426/trump-ai-force-ai-czar-us-ai-strategy.webp.png" title="Trump AI Force and AI Czar Announcement" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;U.S. President Donald Trump has announced plans to create an &lt;strong&gt;"AI Force"&lt;/strong&gt; modeled on the Space Force and said he will soon appoint an artificial intelligence "Czar" to oversee the initiative.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trump made the announcement in a post on Truth Social on September 19, saying the United States should support the growth of artificial intelligence rather than hinder the industry. He also argued that AI could eventually account for &lt;strong&gt;possibly as much as 25% of U.S. gross domestic product&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The announcement immediately raised questions about what the proposed AI Force would actually be. Trump has not yet publicly provided a detailed organizational structure, budget, legal authority or launch timetable for the initiative.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The White House also had not publicly clarified whether the proposed force would be a military organization, a civilian government body, an interagency initiative or another type of federal structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is Trump's AI Force?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trump described the proposed AI Force as something similar to the &lt;strong&gt;U.S. Space Force&lt;/strong&gt;, which was established during his first term as a new branch of the U.S. military.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the comparison does not yet establish that the AI Force would become a military branch. Creating a new military service requires congressional authorization and funding, while the current announcement does not provide those details.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the AI Force is best understood as a proposed government initiative whose final structure and legal status remain unclear.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Reuters reported that Trump provided few details about how the initiative would be implemented. The White House had also not publicly explained the precise role or authority of the proposed AI czar.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Trump Plans to Appoint an AI Czar&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Alongside the AI Force announcement, Trump said he would soon name an &lt;strong&gt;AI "Czar"&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The position would give the administration a designated official responsible for artificial intelligence policy, although the exact responsibilities of the position have not yet been publicly defined.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trump's announcement did not identify a nominee or provide a specific date for the appointment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The administration previously had an &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/chinas-new-ai-side-hustle-people-are.html"&gt;AI-focused policy&lt;/a&gt; role associated with venture capitalist David Sacks. Reuters reported that Sacks stepped down from his government position earlier in 2026 while continuing in an outside advisory capacity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new appointment could therefore become an important part of how the Trump administration coordinates its AI strategy across government agencies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Trump Says AI Could Reach 25% of U.S. GDP&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the most striking parts of Trump's announcement was his estimate of AI's potential economic impact.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trump said artificial intelligence could eventually account for &lt;strong&gt;possibly as much as 25% of the country's GDP&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That figure should be treated as &lt;strong&gt;Trump's projection, not an established economic forecast&lt;/strong&gt;. The statement does not mean that AI currently represents 25% of U.S. economic output.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The claim reflects the administration's broader view that artificial intelligence could become a major driver of economic growth, technology investment and productivity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI's potential economic impact is difficult to measure because the technology is increasingly being integrated into existing industries rather than operating as a separate economic sector. Its contribution could include software, data centers, semiconductor manufacturing, automation, financial services, healthcare, logistics and other industries.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Trump Is Comparing AI to the Space Force&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Space Force comparison places Trump's &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/sent-btc-to-wrong-address-what-happens.html"&gt;AI announcement&lt;/a&gt; in the context of national strategy and technological competition.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Space Force became the sixth branch of the U.S. military after Congress authorized its creation during Trump's first term. Trump has now used that institution as a reference point for describing the scale of his proposed AI initiative.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the administration has not said that the AI Force would have the same military status as the Space Force.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important because the term "force" can describe an initiative or coordinated government effort without automatically creating a new military branch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Competition With China Is Part of the Strategy&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trump has repeatedly framed artificial intelligence as an area of strategic competition between the United States and China.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In his announcement, he said the United States is leading China and the rest of the world in AI and indicated that maintaining that position is a priority for his administration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The focus on China adds a national-security and economic dimension to the proposed AI Force. AI development increasingly intersects with semiconductor manufacturing, data-center infrastructure, cloud computing, cybersecurity and advanced research.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Competition between the United States and China over AI capabilities has therefore become part of a broader technology and economic policy debate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Trump Says the Government Should Not Stifle AI Growth&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trump also used the announcement to emphasize his opposition to policies that he believes could unnecessarily restrict AI development.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;He said his administration would not "hinder or stifle" the growth of the industry and instead would support its expansion while addressing harmful activity through existing criminal and civil laws.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This position places the administration's AI policy around a combination of rapid technological development and enforcement of existing laws rather than a broad new regulatory framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, lawmakers, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/grayscale-zcash-etf-files-for-3-for-1.html"&gt;technology executives&lt;/a&gt; and researchers have been debating whether additional safeguards are necessary as AI systems become more capable.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the AI Force Announcement Is Still Unclear&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The biggest unanswered question is what the proposed AI Force actually is.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As of September 21, publicly available information does not establish a finalized organizational structure, budget, staffing model or legal authority for the initiative.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is also not yet clear which federal department or agency would oversee the proposed force or how it would interact with existing government AI programs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those details will matter because the authority of a new federal initiative depends heavily on how it is created and funded.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A presidential announcement can establish policy direction, but a new military branch or permanent federal agency may require additional congressional action depending on the structure ultimately proposed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Regulation Remains a Major Part of the Debate&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The AI Force announcement comes as Washington continues debating how artificial intelligence should be governed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Supporters of faster development argue that the United States needs to maintain technological leadership and avoid falling behind China. Others have called for stronger safeguards covering issues such as cybersecurity, consumer protection, data-center impacts and the risks associated with increasingly capable AI systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The disagreement is not limited to one political party. Lawmakers from both parties have introduced or discussed proposals addressing AI safety, infrastructure and government oversight.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trump's announcement therefore adds another layer to an already active policy debate: whether the government should primarily accelerate AI development, establish additional safeguards, or pursue both objectives at the same time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the AI Czar Could Mean for the Industry&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The eventual AI czar could become an important coordinator between the White House, federal agencies and the private technology sector.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Depending on the role's final authority, the official could be involved in areas such as AI infrastructure, federal AI policy, national competitiveness, research coordination and responses to potential misuse.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But it would be premature to assign specific powers to the position before the administration announces the structure and responsibilities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The same applies to the proposed AI Force. Its significance will depend on whether it becomes a formal government body, an interagency coordination mechanism or another type of presidential initiative.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Trump's 25% GDP Claim Actually Means&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trump's statement that AI could represent up to 25% of U.S. GDP should be viewed as a long-term projection rather than a current economic statistic.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For AI to account for such a large share of economic activity, the technology would need to have a substantial impact across multiple sectors of the economy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could happen through direct AI-related businesses as well as productivity gains in industries that adopt AI tools. However, the precise economic contribution of AI will depend on adoption rates, investment, productivity improvements, labor-market changes and how economists measure AI-generated output.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As a result, the 25% figure is best reported as &lt;strong&gt;Trump's stated expectation&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than as a verified forecast.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next major development will likely be the administration's announcement of the AI czar and additional information about the proposed AI Force.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Questions surrounding its structure, authority, funding and relationship with existing federal agencies will determine how significant the initiative becomes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The administration will also continue facing the broader policy question of how to balance AI development with concerns about safety, cybersecurity, infrastructure and potential misuse.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the technology industry, the announcement signals that artificial intelligence is being treated by the Trump administration as a major economic and strategic priority.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Trump's AI Force: Key Facts&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;President Donald Trump has announced plans to create an &lt;strong&gt;"AI Force"&lt;/strong&gt; modeled on the Space Force and appoint an AI czar to help oversee the administration's artificial-intelligence strategy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trump has presented AI as a major economic and strategic opportunity and said the technology could potentially account for as much as &lt;strong&gt;25% of U.S. GDP&lt;/strong&gt;. That number is his projection and should not be interpreted as a current economic statistic or independently established forecast.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The major unanswered questions are how the AI Force will be structured, what legal authority it will have, how it will be funded and what responsibilities will be assigned to the AI czar.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Until those details are announced, the initiative remains a significant policy announcement but an incomplete government structure. The next steps from the White House should provide more clarity on what Trump's proposed AI Force will actually do.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;CoinAINews will update this report as the White House announces the AI czar, provides details about the AI Force or releases additional information about the administration's AI strategy.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Liquid Network Paused After Nearly 4,000 BTC Withdrawn in $320M Incident</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhy5eKyT67QsYHNmDJrWw92X3rlsD6ZKbu5nCsnyvsMsopVDXXmVQVY8PZpgscKSGE0iw1Atk6Wz_pX3sSpKLmTR4o7d4taJJBilMICL-9l4H6CQiRxsOB_NPoIcXotRbEyZzWWLUEfaH2ziv7XQWWo3DfdG6wRZOS9pxcnOe72Z2Zzli_iQOrq80hi6tCN/s1672/liquid-network-4000-btc-security-incident.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Liquid Network security incident involving nearly 4,000 BTC withdrawn from its federation wallet" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhy5eKyT67QsYHNmDJrWw92X3rlsD6ZKbu5nCsnyvsMsopVDXXmVQVY8PZpgscKSGE0iw1Atk6Wz_pX3sSpKLmTR4o7d4taJJBilMICL-9l4H6CQiRxsOB_NPoIcXotRbEyZzWWLUEfaH2ziv7XQWWo3DfdG6wRZOS9pxcnOe72Z2Zzli_iQOrq80hi6tCN/w640-h360/liquid-network-4000-btc-security-incident.jpg.png" title="Liquid Network Nearly 4,000 BTC Security Incident" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;
September 7, 2026&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Liquid Network has paused activity after nearly 4,000 BTC was withdrawn from its federation wallet in an incident that exposed a serious vulnerability in the Bitcoin sidechain's infrastructure.&lt;/strong&gt; The Bitcoin involved was worth roughly $320 million at the time of the incident and represented about 95% of the roughly 4,200 BTC held in the federation wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The incident initially appeared to be a major compromise of Liquid's Bitcoin reserves. However, subsequent information from SideSwap and blockchain investigators points to a different mechanism: approximately 4,000 L-BTC appears to have been created through a bug in the &lt;strong&gt;Elements&lt;/strong&gt; software underlying Liquid and then used to trigger a legitimate-looking peg-out through SideSwap.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The unidentified party controlling the withdrawn funds has described itself as a &lt;strong&gt;white-hat hacker&lt;/strong&gt;. Liquid has used the more cautious description &lt;strong&gt;“purported white-hat hackers”&lt;/strong&gt;, meaning the claim has not been independently established. The party has said it intends to return most of the Bitcoin after the vulnerability is fixed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happened to Liquid Network?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Liquid Network is a Bitcoin sidechain developed by &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/hanwha-builds-tokenized-securities.html"&gt;Blockstream&lt;/a&gt;. It is designed to allow faster and more confidential transactions while maintaining a one-to-one relationship between Liquid Bitcoin, or L-BTC, and Bitcoin held by the Liquid Federation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On September 6, roughly 4,000 L-BTC was involved in a transaction that ultimately resulted in approximately 3,996 BTC being released from the federation's Bitcoin wallet. The amount represented almost all of the Bitcoin held in that wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Reuters reported that approximately 4,000 BTC out of about 4,200 BTC in the wallet had been withdrawn. Liquid subsequently halted new transactions as a precaution. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Key Detail: No Federation Key Was Reportedly Compromised&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the most important details in the incident is that the federation's cryptographic signing key was not reported to have been compromised.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, the withdrawal appears to have passed through the normal peg-out infrastructure. SideSwap said that approximately 4,000 L-BTC was submitted to its peg-out service and that the transaction was processed using a valid peg-out authorization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to reporting based on SideSwap's explanation, the problem was that the L-BTC being redeemed had apparently been created through a vulnerability in &lt;strong&gt;Elements&lt;/strong&gt;, the open-source software used by Liquid.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction changes how the incident should be understood. This was not simply a case of someone stealing a private key and signing an unauthorized transaction. The suspected vulnerability appears to have allowed invalid or unbacked L-BTC to enter the system and subsequently be redeemed for real Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How the Elements Bug Could Have Led to the Loss&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The exact technical root cause is still being investigated, so it is important not to present every early technical theory as established fact.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;What current reporting does establish is the broad sequence:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Approximately 4,000 L-BTC was created through an Elements-related vulnerability.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The L-BTC was sent to SideSwap's peg-out service.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The peg-out process treated the transaction as valid.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;The Liquid Federation released approximately 3,996 BTC to the resulting Bitcoin address.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Liquid then disabled bridge activity while developers investigated and patched the vulnerability.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SideSwap has said its systems and peg-out authorization key were not compromised. Instead, the affected L-BTC appeared valid to the system processing the redemption. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why 4,000 BTC Is Such a Big Deal&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The size of the withdrawal is what makes the incident particularly significant.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Approximately 4,000 BTC represented around 95% of the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-coinbase-reverse-bitcoin-sent-to-another-coinbase-user.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt; held in Liquid's federation wallet. In other words, the incident affected nearly the entire reserve associated with the wallet at the center of the event.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The reported value was approximately $320 million, although the dollar value naturally changes with Bitcoin's market price. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For a Bitcoin sidechain built around a one-to-one BTC/L-BTC relationship, an event involving such a large portion of the backing is a major test of the system's security and recovery procedures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Did Liquid Pause the Network?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Liquid disabled its bridge nodes after the incident, preventing new transactions from being submitted while developers investigated the vulnerability.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Exchanges also moved to suspend or prepare to suspend L-BTC deposits and withdrawals while the situation was being assessed. SideSwap said swaps, peg-ins and peg-outs were paused until the network could safely resume operations. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Pausing the network is a precaution designed to stop the same vulnerability from being exploited again while the affected software and bridge infrastructure are secured.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Are the Attackers Really White Hats?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That remains an open question.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The party controlling the funds has identified itself as a white-hat hacker and communicated with Blockstream through on-chain messages. Liquid has described the actors as &lt;strong&gt;“purported white-hat hackers.”&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The distinction is important. Calling someone a white-hat hacker is not the same as independently confirming that the activity was an authorized security test or that the actor had permission to remove the funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The actor has reportedly said that most of the Bitcoin will be returned after the underlying vulnerability is fixed. That makes the incident unusual, but the promised recovery should not be treated as complete until the funds are actually returned. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Blockstream Says the Bridge Nodes Were Patched&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Communication between the party holding the Bitcoin and Blockstream has continued through on-chain messages.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to The Block, the attacker said the funds would be returned after the underlying bug was fixed and every relevant node was patched. Blockstream later sent a signed on-chain message stating that the bridge nodes had been patched and that the funds could be returned.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the time of that report, however, the approximately 4,000 BTC was still in the attacker's &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ripple-ceo-brad-garlinghouse-says.html"&gt;wallet&lt;/a&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This means there are two separate developments to watch: &lt;strong&gt;the technical vulnerability may have been addressed, but the Bitcoin recovery itself still needs to be completed.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Did Someone Hack Bitcoin?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The incident does not indicate that Bitcoin's base blockchain or proof-of-work consensus was compromised.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The affected system was Liquid, a separate Bitcoin sidechain with its own infrastructure, federation and L-BTC peg mechanism.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction matters because a vulnerability in a sidechain does not automatically translate into a vulnerability in Bitcoin itself.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin transactions on the main network continue to operate independently of Liquid's infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is Liquid Bitcoin (L-BTC)?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;L-BTC is Liquid Network's Bitcoin-pegged asset. It is designed to represent Bitcoin on the Liquid sidechain and maintain a one-to-one relationship with BTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Users can move Bitcoin into Liquid and receive L-BTC, while the reverse process allows L-BTC to be redeemed for Bitcoin through the network's peg mechanism.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That structure makes the security of the peg particularly important. If a software vulnerability creates L-BTC that is not backed by corresponding Bitcoin, the system can potentially face a shortfall between the amount of L-BTC circulating and the amount of BTC available to back it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Incident Matters Beyond Liquid&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Liquid incident highlights a broader issue for crypto infrastructure: &lt;strong&gt;asset backing and software integrity are two different security problems.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A system can protect its private keys while still facing risk from a software vulnerability that creates invalid assets or bypasses an important validation rule.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is especially relevant for sidechains, bridges, wrapped tokens and other systems that connect blockchain assets across different environments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For users, the lesson is not that every sidechain or wrapped asset is unsafe. Instead, the incident shows why the technical assumptions behind a peg matter just as much as the custody arrangements protecting the underlying assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens to the 4,000 BTC Now?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next major development will be whether the Bitcoin is actually returned.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The party holding the funds has said it intends to return most of them after the vulnerability is fixed. Blockstream has reportedly confirmed that its bridge nodes have been patched.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But until the Bitcoin is transferred back to the appropriate federation-controlled wallet and the network establishes how the incident will be reconciled, the recovery should be considered &lt;strong&gt;promised rather than completed&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The investigation also needs to establish exactly how the vulnerability worked, why the invalid L-BTC was accepted and what changes are required to prevent a similar incident from happening again.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Users Should Watch Now&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Network status:&lt;/strong&gt; When Liquid resumes normal operations.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;BTC recovery:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether most or all of the withdrawn Bitcoin returns.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Elements patch:&lt;/strong&gt; Details of the vulnerability and the permanent fix.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;L-BTC deposits:&lt;/strong&gt; When exchanges restore deposits and withdrawals.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Post-mortem:&lt;/strong&gt; Blockstream and Liquid's final technical explanation.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Peg security:&lt;/strong&gt; Whether additional safeguards are introduced around L-BTC issuance and redemption.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How much Bitcoin was withdrawn from Liquid Network?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Approximately 3,996 to 4,000 BTC was withdrawn from the Liquid Federation wallet, with the value reported at roughly $320 million at the time of the incident. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What percentage of Liquid's Bitcoin was affected?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The withdrawal represented approximately 95% of the roughly 4,200 BTC held in the federation wallet before the incident. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Was Liquid's private key stolen?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is currently no indication that the federation's cryptographic key was compromised. The withdrawal was reportedly processed using a valid peg-out authorization, while the underlying problem was linked to an Elements software vulnerability. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What caused the Liquid Network incident?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Current reporting points to a vulnerability in Elements software that allowed approximately 4,000 L-BTC to be created and subsequently redeemed through Liquid's peg-out infrastructure. The precise technical root cause remains under investigation. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Are the hackers going to return the Bitcoin?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The party controlling the funds has said it intends to return most of the Bitcoin after the vulnerability is fixed. Blockstream has reportedly said its bridge nodes were patched, but the recovery is not complete until the funds are actually returned. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Was Bitcoin itself hacked?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. The incident affected Liquid's sidechain infrastructure and its L-BTC peg mechanism. There is no indication that Bitcoin's underlying blockchain consensus was compromised.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is Liquid Network still paused?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Liquid has paused network activity while the security incident is addressed. The status of deposits, withdrawals and normal sidechain operations remains an important development to monitor as the response continues. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Liquid Network's roughly 4,000 BTC incident is significant not simply because of the dollar value involved, but because it exposes a different class of blockchain security risk.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The latest information points away from a straightforward private-key theft. Instead, approximately 4,000 L-BTC appears to have been created through an Elements software vulnerability and then redeemed for roughly 3,996 BTC through the Liquid peg-out system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The actors call themselves white hats and have offered to return most of the funds after the bug is fixed. Blockstream has reportedly patched the relevant bridge nodes, but the Bitcoin recovery still needs to be verified on-chain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Bitcoin users, the key takeaway is straightforward: &lt;strong&gt;Liquid was affected; Bitcoin itself was not hacked.&lt;/strong&gt; The final technical post-mortem, the return of the withdrawn BTC and the safeguards introduced afterward will determine how the crypto industry ultimately assesses this incident.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Trump Says Bitcoin Adoption 'Takes a Lot of Pressure Off Our Dollar,' Calls Crypto a 'Big Deal'</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj8LR_eiXbfjgDn_nLt_XEj9sYLqzoYypplhyphenhyphenxKgPwyBObq6BnScVqQvjNV2Y7iYrplMyEzIcoazemeGzEwMhLaXaQn6jh7vev3s9dFM2leXfhbABR0xvU-UfcrnApufthdvaClP3Y8TI8_8E9cvt_xhTG_bl41Yf0Y6y47CjTjaBCV8gWF4Fp7wdGAFrBc/s1536/trump.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Trump says Bitcoin adoption takes pressure off dollar crypto big deal BTC rally 65000" border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="213" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj8LR_eiXbfjgDn_nLt_XEj9sYLqzoYypplhyphenhyphenxKgPwyBObq6BnScVqQvjNV2Y7iYrplMyEzIcoazemeGzEwMhLaXaQn6jh7vev3s9dFM2leXfhbABR0xvU-UfcrnApufthdvaClP3Y8TI8_8E9cvt_xhTG_bl41Yf0Y6y47CjTjaBCV8gWF4Fp7wdGAFrBc/w320-h213/trump.png" title="President Trump supports Bitcoin adoption cryptocurrency national security strategic reserve" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aug 8, 2026&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;– President Donald Trump has voiced
strong support for Bitcoin and the broader cryptocurrency industry, stating
that growing adoption of the digital asset is easing pressure on the U.S.
dollar and is "a good thing for our country"&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In an interview with Punchbowl News, Trump described
cryptocurrency as a "big deal" and highlighted the increasing use of
Bitcoin for everyday payments&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"Crypto is a big deal," Trump said. "I see it
more and more where people are paying with Bitcoin and they don't even know
about cash anymore. That takes a lot of pressure off our dollar. It's a good
thing for our country"&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;National Security Framing&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The president framed his support for crypto as a national
security imperative, warning that the United States cannot afford to let China
dominate the digital asset space&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"If we don't have it, China's going to have it,"
Trump said, adding that former President Joe Biden only embraced crypto late
because he saw Trump winning the crypto community's support&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Trump placed cryptocurrency alongside artificial
intelligence as technologies that could shape global competition, emphasizing
that the U.S. should stay ahead as governments compete for influence over
digital assets&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Market Reaction: Bitcoin Pushes Past $65,000&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The president's comments helped push Bitcoin above $65,000
on Friday, with the asset trading near $65,250 during the session after surging
over 4% in the past month&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The move was supported by:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Whale
     accumulation:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Wallets holding between 10 and 10,000 BTC increased
     their balances by 0.34% from July 29&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;ETF
     inflows:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $754.69
     million in net inflows so far in August&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Weak
     jobs data:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000 in July, far below
     expectations, boosting risk assets&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;CLARITY Act Stalls in Senate&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Trump's remarks came as lawmakers struggled to advance the
CLARITY Act, a bipartisan bill that would establish federal rules for digital
asset trading and define oversight roles for regulators&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Senators failed to reach an agreement before the August
recess, pushing the next window for action into September&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Trump also addressed proposed ethics rules tied to crypto
ownership by federal officials. Some Democrats want tighter restrictions on the
president's crypto interests before they support the bill. Trump said he could
place assets in a blind trust while arguing against rules that could limit U.S.
crypto activity&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Easing Dollar Pressure: A New Narrative&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The president's framing of Bitcoin adoption as easing
pressure on the dollar represents a shift in the political discourse around
digital assets. Rather than viewing crypto as a threat to dollar dominance,
Trump positioned organic consumer adoption as a relief valve for the U.S.
currency&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;This aligns with his broader push to make America "the
undisputed Bitcoin superpower and the crypto capital of the world"&amp;nbsp;.
His administration has already established a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a
U.S. digital assets stockpile, reversing the previous administration's approach
of selling seized crypto assets&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;What This Means for Markets&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The president's comments reinforce the growing political
consensus around crypto in Washington, even as regulatory details remain
unresolved. With the CLARITY Act stalled until September, the industry faces
continued uncertainty around federal oversight&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Bitcoin's technical positioning near the $66,896 resistance
level has traders watching for a potential breakout toward $70,000&amp;nbsp;.
Combined with sustained ETF inflows and whale accumulation, market sentiment
remains cautiously optimistic.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Crypto Market Remains Resilient Amid Bear Sentiment, Says Binance CEO CZ</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp; These macroeconomic influences not only impact cryptocurrencies but also provoke broader concerns about investor sentiment across all risk assets.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;Market Participants React&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;Zhao’s comments come amidst active discussions among major players about how best to navigate these challenging waters.     <title>I Found an Old Bitcoin TXID — Can I Recover My BTC Without My Email or Phone?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

  &lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjaL7B-d9yR09iWswFggOmCtWCsatP_UvHrdIx243cBffb_p8oWNWYlh8r0ZayUU27wQIl_5LHfVvnlxtzmKfTQIPFTswpNOVqbGWuq59mVdOVbIw38kFp40xFX9XKyVBfKLEQ2dkFI73mZrQwrNga5A4eA0mqAKTtHs1IwX48dFfB85MEnluzm4KY5thdc/s1672/old-bitcoin-txid-recover-btc-without-email-phone.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Old Bitcoin TXID used to trace a transaction and recover BTC without email or phone" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjaL7B-d9yR09iWswFggOmCtWCsatP_UvHrdIx243cBffb_p8oWNWYlh8r0ZayUU27wQIl_5LHfVvnlxtzmKfTQIPFTswpNOVqbGWuq59mVdOVbIw38kFp40xFX9XKyVBfKLEQ2dkFI73mZrQwrNga5A4eA0mqAKTtHs1IwX48dFfB85MEnluzm4KY5thdc/w400-h225/old-bitcoin-txid-recover-btc-without-email-phone.jpg.png" title="Can an Old Bitcoin TXID Help Recover BTC Without Email or Phone?" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Finding an old Bitcoin transaction can create a surprisingly confusing situation.
    You may have a &lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin transaction ID (TXID)&lt;/strong&gt; showing that BTC was sent
    or received, but the email address, phone number, exchange account, or wallet details
    connected with the transaction are no longer available.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    So what can you actually do with the transaction ID?
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The short answer is: &lt;strong&gt;a Bitcoin TXID can help you trace and verify what happened
    on the blockchain, but it cannot by itself recover a lost wallet, private key, email
    account, phone number, or exchange login.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That distinction is extremely important because Bitcoin works differently from a
    traditional bank account.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Is a Bitcoin Transaction ID?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A Bitcoin transaction ID, commonly called a &lt;strong&gt;TXID&lt;/strong&gt;, is a unique identifier
    associated with a Bitcoin transaction recorded on the network.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    You may also see the same concept described as a &lt;strong&gt;transaction hash&lt;/strong&gt; or
    &lt;strong&gt;transaction ID&lt;/strong&gt;. Different wallets, exchanges and blockchain explorers
    may use slightly different terminology, but in normal Bitcoin discussions these terms
    are often used interchangeably when referring to the transaction's identifying hash.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A Bitcoin TXID is typically a long hexadecimal string. By entering it into a Bitcoin
    blockchain explorer, you can inspect publicly available information associated with
    that transaction.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Depending on the transaction, an explorer can show information such as:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Transaction status&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Confirmation count&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Bitcoin amount&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Transaction inputs&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Transaction outputs&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Sending and receiving addresses&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Transaction fee&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Block information&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Whether an output remains unspent&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In simple terms, think of a TXID as a &lt;strong&gt;reference number for a blockchain
    transaction&lt;/strong&gt; rather than a password or account-recovery code.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;TXID vs Transaction Hash: Are They the Same Thing?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This is one of the first things to understand when researching an old Bitcoin
    transaction.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    You might see a wallet or explorer call the value a &lt;strong&gt;TXID&lt;/strong&gt;, while another
    service calls it a &lt;strong&gt;transaction hash&lt;/strong&gt;. In the Bitcoin context, both
    commonly refer to the identifier used to locate a particular transaction.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); min-width: 650px; width: 100%;"&gt;
    &lt;thead&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; text-align: left;"&gt;Term&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; text-align: left;"&gt;Meaning&lt;/th&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
    &lt;/thead&gt;
    &lt;tbody&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;TXID&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Transaction identifier used to locate a &lt;br /&gt;Bitcoin transaction.&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Transaction ID&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Another common name for a &lt;br /&gt;transaction identifier.&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Transaction hash&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;A commonly used term for the &lt;br /&gt;transaction's hash-based identifier.&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
    &lt;/tbody&gt;
  &lt;/table&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Therefore, if an old exchange email says "transaction hash" while your current
    &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/how-does-blockchain-really-work.html"&gt;blockchain&lt;/a&gt; explorer asks for a "TXID," you generally do not need a different number.
    The same transaction identifier may be described using different terminology.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Can a Bitcoin TXID Tell You Who Sent the Bitcoin?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Not by itself.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This is one of the biggest misconceptions about Bitcoin.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A blockchain explorer can normally show the addresses involved in a transaction,
    but a standard Bitcoin transaction does not simply contain the sender's real-world
    name, email address or telephone number.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A Bitcoin address is therefore not the same thing as a person's identity.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The blockchain can show what happened to the transaction. Connecting an address to
    a real person generally requires information outside the basic blockchain record.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Information Can You See From a Bitcoin TXID?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;div style="overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
    &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); min-width: 700px; width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;thead&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; text-align: left;"&gt;Information&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px; text-align: left;"&gt;What It Tells You&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/thead&gt;
      &lt;tbody&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;TXID&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Identifies the transaction.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Inputs&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Shows previous outputs being spent by &lt;br /&gt;the transaction.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Outputs&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Shows where the transaction assigns &lt;br /&gt;Bitcoin.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Amount&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Shows the BTC assigned to outputs.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Fee&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Shows the transaction fee paid to the &lt;br /&gt;network.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Confirmations&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Shows how deeply the transaction is &lt;br /&gt;embedded in the blockchain.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Block&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Identifies the block containing the &lt;br /&gt;confirmed transaction.&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/tbody&gt;
    &lt;/table&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    What the TXID normally does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; provide directly includes:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Sender's name&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Sender's email address&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Sender's phone number&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Exchange username&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Wallet password&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Private key&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Recovery phrase&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;How Do You Check a Bitcoin Transaction Using a TXID?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If you already have the transaction ID, checking the blockchain record is usually
    the logical first step.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Step 1: Open a Reputable Bitcoin Blockchain Explorer&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    You can use services such as
    &lt;a href="https://blockstream.info/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Blockstream Explorer&lt;/a&gt;,
    &lt;a href="https://www.bitcoin.com/explorer/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Bitcoin.com Explorer&lt;/a&gt;,
    or
    &lt;a href="https://blockchair.com/bitcoin" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Blockchair&lt;/a&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Blockchair is particularly useful when you want a broader blockchain-search interface,
    as its platform supports Bitcoin along with multiple other blockchain networks.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Step 2: Paste the TXID&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Copy the complete transaction ID and paste it into the explorer's search field.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If the transaction is available, the explorer should return the associated transaction
    information.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Step 3: Check Whether the Transaction Is in the Mempool or Confirmed&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This part is important because a Bitcoin transaction does not have to be confirmed
    before its TXID can become visible.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    After a transaction is broadcast to the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-is-bitcoin-price-rising-so-fast.html"&gt;Bitcoin network&lt;/a&gt;, it can enter the
    &lt;strong&gt;mempool&lt;/strong&gt;. The mempool is where valid but not-yet-confirmed transactions
    are kept by participating Bitcoin nodes.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Therefore, an explorer may show a TXID with a status such as
    &lt;strong&gt;"unconfirmed," "in mempool," or "waiting for confirmation."&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Once miners include the transaction in a block, it becomes confirmed. Additional
    blocks then build on top of that block.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Step 4: Examine the Transaction Outputs&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If your question is &lt;strong&gt;"Was Bitcoin actually sent to me?"&lt;/strong&gt;, carefully
    examine the outputs.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin transactions can contain multiple inputs and multiple outputs. That means
    you should not automatically assume that the first address shown by an explorer
    belongs to you.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Is the Bitcoin Mempool?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The &lt;strong&gt;mempool&lt;/strong&gt; is essentially a waiting area for transactions that have
    been received by a node but have not yet been included in a confirmed block.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This explains an important situation that sometimes confuses people:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;You can have a TXID even though the transaction does not yet have a block
    confirmation.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A transaction may therefore appear in an explorer as unconfirmed. This does not mean
    that the transaction has been permanently recorded in a block yet.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If a transaction remains unconfirmed for a long period, its status can depend on
    network conditions, transaction fees, node policies and other factors.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;I Can See the BTC Transaction, but I Don't Have the Wallet — What Now?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This is where the difference between &lt;strong&gt;finding Bitcoin&lt;/strong&gt; and
    &lt;strong&gt;controlling Bitcoin&lt;/strong&gt; becomes critical.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Seeing BTC on a blockchain explorer does not mean you can spend it.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin funds are controlled through cryptographic keys. If the transaction sent BTC
    to an address you control, the relevant wallet credentials are what allow you to
    spend those funds.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The key question is:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Do you still have the private key, recovery phrase, wallet backup, hardware
    wallet, or access to the custodial account that controls the BTC?&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If yes, there may be a legitimate recovery path.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If no, the TXID alone is not enough.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Doesn't the TXID Give Me Access to the Bitcoin?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A TXID is designed to identify a transaction. It is not designed to prove that you
    own the Bitcoin involved in that transaction.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The blockchain can publicly show that &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/tether-brings-offline-ai-translation-to.html"&gt;BTC&lt;/a&gt; was assigned to a particular output.
    Spending that output requires the correct cryptographic authorization.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This is why someone can know the TXID of a transaction without having the ability to
    spend the Bitcoin associated with it.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What If I Lost My Old Email or Phone Number?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The answer depends on how you originally held the Bitcoin.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;If the Bitcoin Was in a Self-Custody Wallet&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If you controlled the Bitcoin yourself, the old email address or phone number may
    not have been the critical recovery mechanism.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;You may instead need:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Recovery phrase&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Private key&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Wallet backup&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Original wallet file&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Hardware wallet&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The correct wallet software and account setup&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If you still have the correct recovery phrase, you may be able to restore the wallet
    even if the original phone or computer is no longer available.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Is Address Derivation in a Bitcoin Wallet?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Address derivation is another important concept when trying to recover an old Bitcoin
    wallet.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Modern wallets commonly use &lt;strong&gt;hierarchical deterministic (HD) wallet&lt;/strong&gt;
    structures. Instead of storing every Bitcoin address as a completely independent
    secret, an HD wallet can derive many addresses from a common seed or recovery phrase.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This means one recovery phrase can be associated with a large number of derived
    addresses.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    As a result, restoring a wallet does not always mean that the first address displayed
    by the wallet will be the old address you remember.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The wallet may need to derive the correct accounts, branches and address indexes
    associated with the original wallet setup.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This is one reason why someone might restore a wallet and initially see a zero
    balance even though an old blockchain transaction shows BTC going to an address
    they believe was theirs.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In such cases, the problem may be related to the wallet's derivation path, account
    type, address discovery or synchronization rather than the Bitcoin blockchain itself.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Can the Same Seed Phrase Generate Multiple Bitcoin Addresses?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin wallets can derive multiple addresses from the same underlying wallet seed.
    This improves usability and privacy because users do not have to reuse the same
    receiving address for every payment.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    For example, you might have received Bitcoin years ago at one address and later
    received Bitcoin at several different addresses, all ultimately derived from the
    same wallet seed.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Therefore, when recovering an old wallet, finding the original address can require
    more than simply opening the wallet and looking at its current receiving address.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What If the BTC Was Held by an Exchange?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The situation is different if the Bitcoin was held by a centralized exchange or
    custodial service.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In a custodial setup, the company may control the underlying private keys while
    customers access their balances through an account.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If you have lost the old email address or phone number, use the exchange's
    &lt;strong&gt;official account-recovery process&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The exchange may ask for information to verify that you are the legitimate account
    holder.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Your TXID can be useful evidence when communicating with an exchange because it can
    help identify a specific blockchain deposit or withdrawal.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Can a Transaction ID Recover a Lost Bitcoin Wallet?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;No, not by itself.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A TXID identifies a transaction. It is not a wallet backup.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A transaction ID can help you locate the blockchain record, but it does not contain
    your wallet's private key, seed phrase or exchange password.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Can Someone Get a Bitcoin Private Key From a TXID?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;No legitimate recovery service can simply calculate your Bitcoin private key
    from a transaction ID.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A TXID exposes public transaction information. It does not provide the secret
    cryptographic information required to spend the Bitcoin.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Anyone claiming that they can recover a private key simply from a TXID should be
    treated with extreme suspicion.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What If the Bitcoin Was Actually Credited to My Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If a blockchain explorer shows that BTC was sent to an address you genuinely control,
    the next step is to determine why your wallet is not showing the funds.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Check the following:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ol&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The exact receiving address.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The transaction output containing the BTC.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The amount received.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The transaction confirmation status.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Whether the output is still unspent.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Whether the address belongs to your wallet.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Whether the wallet was restored from the correct recovery phrase.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Whether the correct account or derivation path is being used.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Whether the wallet has fully synchronized.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ol&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Is a UTXO and Why Does It Matter?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin does not work like a conventional bank balance where a single account simply
    contains a number such as "$500."
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin uses &lt;strong&gt;unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs)&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A transaction creates outputs that can later be spent by another transaction. An
    output that has not yet been spent is called a UTXO.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    When investigating an old Bitcoin transaction, checking whether the relevant output
    remains unspent can help you understand whether the BTC has already been moved.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What If I Don't Recognize the Receiving Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Be careful.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Finding an unfamiliar Bitcoin address in a transaction does not prove that you own
    it.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin transactions can contain multiple outputs, including change outputs.
    Therefore, an address appearing in a transaction should not automatically be treated
    as your personal wallet address.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If you have an old recovery phrase or wallet backup, restoring the wallet through
    legitimate wallet software can help determine whether the address belongs to that
    wallet.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Can a Blockchain Explorer Reveal the Owner's Name?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Generally, no.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A blockchain explorer displays blockchain data rather than a government-style
    identity database.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    An address may sometimes become associated with an exchange, company, public figure
    or other organization through information outside the blockchain itself.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    But the basic Bitcoin transaction record does not automatically display a person's
    legal name, email address or phone number.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Which Bitcoin Blockchain Explorer Should You Use?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    There is no requirement to use only one explorer. If a transaction does not appear
    correctly on one service, checking another reputable explorer can be useful.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Information Should You Collect Before Trying to Recover the BTC?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If you are investigating an old Bitcoin transaction, create a recovery checklist
    containing only information that is safe to handle.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Useful information can include:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;TXID&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Receiving address&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Approximate transaction date&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;BTC amount&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Block number&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Exchange name, if known&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Old wallet name, if known&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Old transaction records&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Wallet backup files that you legitimately own&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Never place your private key or recovery phrase in a public document or send
    it to a stranger.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What You Should Never Do When Trying to Recover Bitcoin&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Lost-Bitcoin situations attract scammers because people may be desperate to recover
    potentially valuable funds.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Never:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Pay someone who promises guaranteed Bitcoin recovery.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Give a stranger your recovery phrase.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Send your private key to "support."&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Install unknown wallet-recovery software.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Give someone remote access to your computer.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Share exchange passwords.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Enter your seed phrase into an unknown website.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Believe that a TXID can be used to calculate your private key.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Most Important Difference: Tracking vs Controlling Bitcoin&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The easiest way to understand the entire problem is to separate two completely
    different concepts: &lt;strong&gt;tracking a blockchain transaction&lt;/strong&gt; and
    &lt;strong&gt;controlling the Bitcoin associated with it&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;

          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Recovery phrase, &lt;br /&gt;private key or backup&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Recover an exchange &lt;br /&gt;account&lt;/td&gt;

          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Official exchange &lt;br /&gt;recovery process&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Recover an old email &lt;br /&gt;account&lt;/td&gt;

          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;Email provider &lt;br /&gt;recovery process&lt;/td&gt;

        &lt;tr&gt;
