          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 14px;"&gt;There is no legitimate &lt;br /&gt;TXID-to-private-key &lt;br /&gt;recovery method&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/tbody&gt;
    &lt;/table&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Can You Recover the Bitcoin With Only a TXID?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Usually, no.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A TXID can help you investigate the blockchain history, but it does not prove that
    you control the Bitcoin.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If you have the &lt;strong&gt;TXID plus the correct recovery phrase or private key&lt;/strong&gt;,
    you may have a legitimate path to accessing the funds.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If the Bitcoin was held by an exchange, the TXID can help document the transaction
    while the exchange's official account-recovery process handles access.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    But if all you have is a TXID and you have no wallet credentials, no recovery phrase,
    no private key and no accessible custodial account, the TXID alone is generally not
    enough to take control of the Bitcoin.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;A Simple Example of Bitcoin Recovery Using a TXID&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Imagine someone discovers an old document containing a Bitcoin transaction ID.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    They enter the TXID into a blockchain explorer and discover:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Transaction:&lt;/strong&gt; Found&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Status:&lt;/strong&gt; Confirmed&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Amount:&lt;/strong&gt; 0.50 BTC&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Receiving address:&lt;/strong&gt; A Bitcoin address shown by the explorer&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    At this point, the person has established that a transaction involving 0.50 BTC
    exists on the blockchain.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    But they still need to answer a different question:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;"Do I control the receiving address?"&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If they have the correct wallet recovery phrase and can restore the wallet containing
    that address, they may be able to regain access.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If they have no credentials and cannot establish control of the address, the
    blockchain record alone does not give them ownership.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What If the Transaction Is Still Unconfirmed?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If the explorer shows the transaction in the &lt;strong&gt;mempool&lt;/strong&gt;, it means the
    transaction has been seen by the network but has not yet been included in a confirmed
    block.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This is different from a transaction that has already been confirmed.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Therefore, when investigating a TXID, always check whether the status is:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Unconfirmed / In Mempool&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Confirmed in a Block&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The distinction matters because confirmation is what places the transaction into the
    permanent blockchain history.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why a Missing Balance Does Not Always Mean the Bitcoin Is Gone&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Suppose you restore an old wallet and see a zero balance, while a blockchain explorer
    shows that BTC was once sent to an address you remember using.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    There are several possible explanations.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The wallet has not synchronized completely.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The wrong account was restored.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The wallet uses a different address type or derivation path.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The relevant address has not been discovered by the wallet.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The BTC was later spent.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The address was never actually controlled by that wallet.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This is why the TXID should be treated as an investigation starting point rather than
    as a recovery credential.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Final Answer: A TXID Is a Starting Point, Not a Recovery Key&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Having a Bitcoin transaction ID is valuable. It allows you to independently inspect
    a transaction recorded or broadcast on the Bitcoin network.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    But a TXID is &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; a password, wallet backup, private key, recovery
    phrase, email address or phone number.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If you are trying to recover Bitcoin from an old transaction, start by identifying
    the transaction's outputs and determining whether one of the addresses belongs to a
    wallet you still control.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Then look for legitimate wallet backups, recovery phrases, private keys or the
    official account-recovery process of the exchange involved.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If you restored a wallet but cannot see the old funds, investigate address derivation,
    wallet account type, synchronization and whether the relevant output remains unspent.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Most importantly, &lt;strong&gt;never give your seed phrase or private key to anyone who
    claims they can recover your Bitcoin.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;The blockchain can tell you what happened to the transaction. Your wallet
    credentials determine whether you can actually control the funds.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions About Bitcoin TXIDs&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is a Bitcoin TXID the same as a transaction hash?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In normal Bitcoin usage, TXID, transaction ID and transaction hash are commonly used
    to refer to the identifier used to locate a transaction.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can I find my Bitcoin wallet using only a TXID?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Not necessarily. A TXID identifies a transaction, not a wallet account. It can help
    you identify addresses involved in the transaction, but it does not contain your
    wallet's private key or recovery phrase.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can I recover Bitcoin with a transaction ID?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A TXID alone generally cannot recover or unlock Bitcoin. It can help you locate the
    transaction and determine where BTC was assigned. Actual control requires the
    appropriate wallet credentials or custodial account access.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can a Bitcoin transaction reveal an email address?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A standard Bitcoin transaction does not normally contain the sender's or recipient's
    email address. Real-world identity associations generally come from information
    outside the basic blockchain transaction.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can a TXID be found before Bitcoin confirmation?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Yes. A transaction can be visible through a node or blockchain explorer while it is
    still unconfirmed and waiting in the mempool.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What is the Bitcoin mempool?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The mempool is where valid, unconfirmed Bitcoin transactions can wait before being
    included in a block.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Why do Bitcoin wallets have multiple addresses?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Modern hierarchical deterministic wallets can derive multiple addresses from a
    common seed or recovery phrase. This allows wallets to generate new receiving
    addresses without requiring a completely separate seed for each address.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Why can't I see an old Bitcoin address after restoring my wallet?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The wallet may need to discover additional derived addresses, or you may be using a
    different account type or derivation path from the original wallet. Synchronization
    can also affect what the wallet displays.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is it safe to share a Bitcoin TXID?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A TXID is generally public blockchain information and can be used by others to inspect
    the transaction. However, you should never share your private key, seed phrase,
    wallet password or other secret credentials.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What if my Bitcoin is visible on the blockchain but missing from my wallet?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    First check that the receiving address actually belongs to your wallet. If it does,
    investigate wallet restoration, synchronization, address derivation, account type
    and whether the output has already been spent.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can someone reverse an old Bitcoin transaction?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Bitcoin transactions are not ordinary bank transfers that can simply be reversed by
    customer support. Once confirmed, recovering funds generally requires a new
    transaction from whoever controls the relevant Bitcoin.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What is the difference between a TXID and a private key?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A TXID identifies a blockchain transaction. A private key is secret cryptographic
    information used to authorize spending from Bitcoin controlled by that key. They
    serve completely different purposes.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If you have an old &lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin transaction ID but no email or phone number&lt;/strong&gt;,
    don't panic and don't immediately pay someone who promises instant recovery.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    First inspect the TXID using a reputable blockchain explorer. Determine whether the
    transaction is confirmed or still in the mempool, examine its inputs and outputs,
    identify the relevant receiving address and check whether the output remains unspent.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If you believe the address belonged to an old wallet, search for your legitimate
    recovery phrase, private key or wallet backup. Remember that an HD wallet can derive
    many addresses from one seed, so recovering the correct address may require the right
    wallet configuration and derivation path.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If the Bitcoin was held on an exchange, use the exchange's official account-recovery
    process rather than relying on a third-party "recovery expert."
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;The TXID can show you where a Bitcoin transaction went. It cannot, by itself,
    give you the keys needed to spend the Bitcoin.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Sources and Further Reading&lt;/h2&gt;

    <title>Will the U.S. Actually Buy Bitcoin for Its Strategic Reserve? Bitget CEO Says Don't Hold Your Breath</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhyVXFjwbEtN9jBlsCqB-L0dBavJdRY1vaS8m8inqElWxqO-a9sQ6lvjYG3u2LGrJzDhKbBwDSoApG-1SqVLLtDMxkvn4_x02O1c0BwlUyaBu57P0BDWyaGla7i-CAg_AeFswagmr2CxaNgEQzWn1WNVuETwnpGCi7gGibh64nnkRsR4srddQhWgdZgMdkv/s1672/us-strategic-bitcoin-reserve-trump-bitcoin-purchases.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Donald Trump and Bitcoin representing the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and potential government purchases" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhyVXFjwbEtN9jBlsCqB-L0dBavJdRY1vaS8m8inqElWxqO-a9sQ6lvjYG3u2LGrJzDhKbBwDSoApG-1SqVLLtDMxkvn4_x02O1c0BwlUyaBu57P0BDWyaGla7i-CAg_AeFswagmr2CxaNgEQzWn1WNVuETwnpGCi7gGibh64nnkRsR4srddQhWgdZgMdkv/w400-h225/us-strategic-bitcoin-reserve-trump-bitcoin-purchases.jpg.png" title="U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and Potential Bitcoin Purchases" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/i&gt;&amp;nbsp;|&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;When President Trump said the U.S. government was
considering buying "sizable" amounts of Bitcoin, the comments came as
Bitcoin reclaimed $70,000 for the first time since June.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But according to Bitget CEO Gracy Chen, the market might be
reading the tea leaves wrong.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In a recent interview, Chen said she does not expect any
open-market Bitcoin purchases before the end of Trump's current term. Her
reasoning is grounded in how the reserve was actually built—and what it's
legally allowed to do.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What the Executive Order Actually Says&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Strategic Bitcoin Reserve was established on March 6,
2025, through Executive Order 14233. The reserve is initially capitalized with
Bitcoin held by the U.S. government, primarily from criminal and civil asset
forfeiture proceedings.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The reserve is not funded with new taxpayer appropriations,
and no confirmed open-market purchase has been reported.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The order also directed the Treasury and Commerce
departments to explore "budget-neutral" methods of potentially
expanding holdings—but no mechanism has been formally activated to date. The
executive order does not authorize unrestricted taxpayer-funded open-market
purchases. Any acquisition strategy would have to remain budget-neutral and
comply with existing law, while broader purchases could require additional
legislative authority.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;As of mid-2026, questions remained around the practical
implementation and management of the reserve, including how the government
would pursue any future budget-neutral acquisitions. As of mid-2026, the U.S.
government is estimated to hold more than 300,000 BTC in government-controlled
holdings, worth over $20 billion. Those holdings largely stem from government
seizures and forfeitures rather than from a sovereign wealth fund or
open-market purchases.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"I didn't expect Bitcoin's inclusion in the strategic
reserve to become concrete in the first half of 2025—or even throughout the
year." — Gracy Chen, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/the-truth-about-ai-agents-why-theyre.html"&gt;Bitget CEO&lt;/a&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Trump Signal vs. The Structural Reality&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;On August 19, at the White House Crypto Summit, Trump was
asked whether the administration planned to buy Bitcoin. His response was
careful but attention-grabbing: "Well, it's been talked about. It's taken
a lot of pressure off the dollar; it's been very, very good for the dollar. And
I think if you came in with recommendations, I would certainly listen."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Chen's assessment, however, is that this is more
"promise than action."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Her argument has two parts:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;First, there's the legal constraint.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Treasury
Secretary &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/you-can-now-trade-spacex-and-gold.html"&gt;Scott Bessent&lt;/a&gt; made this explicit during a February 4, 2026, House
Financial Services Committee hearing: "I do not have the authority to do
that," he said, when asked whether he could direct private banks to buy
Bitcoin or use taxpayer funds to stabilize its price. The executive order does
not authorize unrestricted purchases. Unrestricted taxpayer-funded open-market
purchases would likely require additional legislative authority, while any
acquisition strategy under the executive order would have to remain
budget-neutral and comply with existing law. None of those conversations have
gained serious traction. A bill to codify the reserve and authorize purchases
has made little progress in Congress.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Second, there's the operational reality.&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;According
to reports, the administration continues to work through implementation details
surrounding the reserve. Treasury is responsible for administering and
maintaining control of the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve under the executive order,
while Treasury and Commerce were directed to develop budget-neutral strategies
for acquiring additional Bitcoin. The administration's focus has largely been
on custody, legal frameworks, and operational infrastructure rather than
establishing an unrestricted open-market accumulation program.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bo Hines episode is instructive here. Hines, who was the
executive director of the President's Council of Advisors for Digital Assets
through mid-2025, characterized the U.S. as needing to become "the Bitcoin
superpower of the world." But his framing clashed with the executive
order's actual provisions. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent eventually
clarified the administration's position: "We're not going to be buying
that, but are going to use confiscated assets."&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Hines stepped down from his White House role within days,
returning to the private sector where he became CEO of Tether USA. Patrick Witt
took over, and the framing shifted from "Bitcoin superpower" to
"getting our house in order" through custody centralization and legal
framework development.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Gracy Chen Is Actually Saying&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Chen's view—that purchases are unlikely before Trump's term
ends in January 2029—isn't a bet against Bitcoin. It's a read on the structural
constraints of U.S. governance.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;She has consistently argued that&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;macroeconomic
conditions, not government buying, will play the biggest role in Bitcoin's
future&lt;/b&gt;—things like U.S. interest rate cuts and broader fiscal policy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;"Even if the U.S. government, some individual states
like Florida and Texas, and other countries like the Czech Republic have
mentioned a Bitcoin reserve, there isn't solid action yet." — Gracy Chen,
Bitget CEO&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What This Means for the Market&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The restriction on selling most Bitcoin held in the reserve
does remove some supply-side uncertainty. Bitcoin held in the reserve stays
there, reducing the risk that a future administration could liquidate holdings
and depress prices.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But the accumulation narrative—the idea that the U.S.
government is about to become a major buyer—is not supported by the current
framework. Several proposals have circulated on Capitol Hill that would
authorize direct purchases, funded through mechanisms that avoid direct
taxpayer exposure, but none have cleared committee as of mid-2026. The
legislative path, if it exists at all, is a long one.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Trump's comments were real. The market's reaction was real.
But the reserve, as currently structured, does not establish an unrestricted
taxpayer-funded Bitcoin buying program.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Chen's skepticism about near-term purchases is grounded in
how the executive order was actually written, the legislative constraints that
still apply, the unresolved inter-agency discussions, and the administration's
own operational choices. The Strategic Bitcoin Reserve exists. It holds over
$20 billion in BTC. It's a structural shift in the U.S. government's
relationship with Bitcoin.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But it is not a buying program.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

not constitute investment advice.&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Forgot Your BTC Password? Here's the Honest Truth About Recovery</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;
  &lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgq7wA-VU7r-29W5vmUOh0IK7gtQ8Op8WgnMRO8XPDXYBWa-Au_WltQk9bBrRvfYNzFY3mgstOrNDwk2OWxvs92EkljOu_r3prdSsX7sTgkz2ZRxBlSyj6QSmfT7UO3meh9TJsXU3qVjQHQI8t3APxBUYaWC-IzI1ZYu9_IKAAvcuuBpmsqg5s_1oDT1PlY/s1733/forgot-bitcoin-wallet-password-recovery-2026.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Forgot Bitcoin wallet password and secure recovery phrase backup" border="0" data-original-height="907" data-original-width="1733" height="334" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgq7wA-VU7r-29W5vmUOh0IK7gtQ8Op8WgnMRO8XPDXYBWa-Au_WltQk9bBrRvfYNzFY3mgstOrNDwk2OWxvs92EkljOu_r3prdSsX7sTgkz2ZRxBlSyj6QSmfT7UO3meh9TJsXU3qVjQHQI8t3APxBUYaWC-IzI1ZYu9_IKAAvcuuBpmsqg5s_1oDT1PlY/w640-h334/forgot-bitcoin-wallet-password-recovery-2026.webp.png" title="Forgot Your Bitcoin Wallet Password? Bitcoin Recovery Explained" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Editorial Team&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;Forgetting a Bitcoin wallet password can be a frightening experience, especially when the wallet contains funds that may have been untouched for years. But there is an important distinction that often gets lost in online discussions: a wallet password, a hardware-wallet PIN, a recovery phrase and a Bitcoin private key are not necessarily the same thing.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;So, can a hacker recover a forgotten Bitcoin wallet password?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Sometimes access can be restored using a separate backup. In other situations, there may be no practical recovery path at all.&lt;/strong&gt; The answer depends on what exactly was forgotten and what backup information is still available.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin itself does not have a central password-reset system for self-custodied wallets. There is no Bitcoin administrator who can verify your identity and simply reset access to a wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;First: What Exactly Did You Forget?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is the most important question.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;People often use the word “password” to describe several different things. A Bitcoin wallet might involve a device PIN, an app password, an encrypted wallet password, a recovery phrase or an optional passphrase.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;These credentials serve different purposes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Wallet password:&lt;/strong&gt; may encrypt or protect access to a wallet file or application.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Hardware-wallet PIN:&lt;/strong&gt; protects the physical signing device.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Recovery phrase:&lt;/strong&gt; a backup that can be used to restore a wallet in supported wallet software.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Optional passphrase:&lt;/strong&gt; an additional secret that can create a separate wallet on some hardware-wallet systems.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Private key:&lt;/strong&gt; the cryptographic secret that ultimately controls the ability to spend funds from a Bitcoin address.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Confusing these terms can lead people to take the wrong recovery steps.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Can a Hacker Recover a Forgotten Bitcoin Password?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There is no universal answer because Bitcoin wallets use different security models.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For a self-custodied wallet, there is normally no central company holding a master copy of your password. Bitcoin.org explains that protecting wallet credentials and backups is the user's responsibility, and warns that forgetting a password can result in permanent loss of access. &lt;a href="https://bitcoin.org/en/secure-your-wallet" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Bitcoin.org's wallet security guidance&lt;/a&gt; explains why backups and secure credential storage are so important. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That does not mean every forgotten password is automatically unrecoverable. Someone may have forgotten an application password while still possessing a valid wallet backup. In that situation, restoring the wallet from the backup may provide a legitimate route back to the funds, depending on how that particular &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/openai-calls-for-global-ai-standards-as.html"&gt;wallet &lt;/a&gt;was designed.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The key point is simple: &lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin does not have a universal “forgot password” button.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What If You Still Have Your Recovery Phrase?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is one of the most important situations to understand.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A recovery phrase is designed to restore a wallet. Bitcoin.org explains that wallet backups can protect users against device failure and can allow a wallet to be recovered after a computer or mobile device is lost or stolen, depending on the wallet's backup system. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If you still have the correct recovery phrase, losing access to a particular phone, computer or hardware wallet does not necessarily mean that the Bitcoin itself is lost.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For example, a hardware wallet can be lost or damaged while the wallet backup remains available. A compatible wallet can potentially restore access using that backup, provided the correct wallet configuration is also used.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;However, users should never enter a recovery phrase into an unfamiliar website or send it to someone claiming to be a recovery expert.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What If You Forgot the Hardware Wallet PIN?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is different from losing the recovery phrase.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Hardware-wallet manufacturers design their devices so that a forgotten PIN can, depending on the product, be handled through a reset-and-recovery process when the legitimate wallet backup is still available.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For example, Ledger says that after three incorrect PIN attempts, a Ledger signer factory-resets. If the user still has the Secret Recovery Phrase, the accounts can then be recovered and a new PIN can be set. &lt;a href="https://www.ledger.com/academy/topics/ledgersolutions/ledger-pin-code-what-you-need-to-know" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Ledger's official PIN guidance&lt;/a&gt; explains this process. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Trezor similarly documents a factory-reset process and says users should make sure they have their wallet backup and any passphrase before resetting a device. &lt;a href="https://trezor.io/support/troubleshooting/device-issues/how-to-reset-your-trezor-pin-using-factory-reset" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Trezor's official PIN-reset guidance&lt;/a&gt; explains the recovery requirements. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;But never reset a device simply because somebody online tells you to.&lt;/strong&gt; First make sure you understand what backup you have and what the reset will erase.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Hardest Case: You Lost the Recovery Phrase Too&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is where the situation becomes much more serious.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If you have lost the recovery phrase, forgotten the required credentials and have no other valid backup or access path, there may be no legitimate way to recover the Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Self-custody is built around control of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bernstein-sees-prediction-markets.html"&gt;cryptographic &lt;/a&gt;credentials. There is no central Bitcoin authority that can simply recreate a lost private key or override the security of a self-custodied wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is one of the fundamental trade-offs of self-custody: users have direct control over their funds, but they also carry responsibility for protecting their credentials and backups.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What About Guessing the Forgotten Password?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There is a difference between recovering a credential from information you legitimately possess and asking a stranger to “hack” a wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If you created the wallet yourself and remember parts of a password, you may be able to reconstruct the correct credential using your own records or memory. Some wallet-recovery situations may involve trying known variations of a password, but this should only be performed on a wallet you legitimately own.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A strong password that is completely unknown and has no usable backup may be practically impossible to recover. Modern cryptography is specifically designed to prevent outsiders from simply calculating secret credentials from a public Bitcoin address.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What About a Trezor Passphrase?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is another situation where the word “password” can cause confusion.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Trezor's documentation explains that adding a passphrase to a wallet backup creates a separate wallet with its own addresses and balance. The exact passphrase is required to access that particular wallet. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Trezor is explicit about what happens if the passphrase is forgotten: &lt;strong&gt;there is no recovery or reset, including through Trezor Support.&lt;/strong&gt; The passphrase is not stored on the Trezor device or in Trezor Suite. &lt;a href="https://trezor.io/support/troubleshooting/trezor-suite-issues/fix-passphrase-wallet-problems-in-trezor-suite" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Trezor's official support documentation&lt;/a&gt; confirms this. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is why a person can have the correct wallet backup and still be unable to access a particular passphrase-protected wallet if the additional passphrase has been permanently forgotten.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Can Bitcoin Developers or Exchanges Recover the Coins?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Not in the same way a bank can reset an online-banking password.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For a self-custodied Bitcoin wallet, control depends on the cryptographic credentials. A wallet provider can explain its own recovery process, but it cannot generally recreate a secret that the user has permanently lost.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;An exchange is different because the exchange controls the custody infrastructure. If the Bitcoin was held on an exchange account, the user may have an account-recovery process governed by that company's policies.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That distinction is critical: &lt;strong&gt;forgetting the login password for an exchange account is not the same problem as losing the credentials for a self-custodied Bitcoin wallet.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Be Extremely Careful With “Bitcoin Recovery Experts”&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A forgotten wallet is exactly the type of situation scammers look for.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org specifically warns about fake support and recovery services that ask users for seed phrases, private keys, remote access or upfront payments. Its current scam guidance states that legitimate support representatives will not ask for a seed phrase or private key and that there is no legitimate firm offering guaranteed cryptocurrency recovery. &lt;a href="https://bitcoin.org/en/scams" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Bitcoin.org's scam guidance&lt;/a&gt; covers these recovery scams. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If somebody contacts you after you publicly mention that you have lost access to Bitcoin and claims they can recover the funds for a fee, treat the offer with extreme caution.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Never send your recovery phrase or private key to anyone.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Should You Do If You Forgot Your Bitcoin Wallet Password?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The safest approach is to slow down instead of immediately trying random recovery services.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ol&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Identify the wallet.&lt;/strong&gt; Determine which wallet software, hardware device or exchange you used.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Determine what you actually forgot.&lt;/strong&gt; Was it an app password, device PIN, wallet encryption password or optional passphrase?&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Look for your legitimate backup.&lt;/strong&gt; Check whether you have a recovery phrase, wallet backup file or another documented recovery method.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Use only official documentation.&lt;/strong&gt; Follow the recovery procedure published by the wallet manufacturer or software developer.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Do not give anyone your recovery phrase.&lt;/strong&gt; Genuine support should not require your secret recovery information.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Do not rush into a reset.&lt;/strong&gt; Make sure you understand what a reset will erase and what backup will be needed afterward.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ol&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;How to Prevent This From Happening Again&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The easiest wallet recovery problem to solve is the one you prepare for before it happens.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org recommends maintaining secure backups and protecting wallet credentials. It also warns that online backups can be vulnerable to theft and recommends considering multiple secure locations for backups. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For long-term holdings, users should consider how their backup would survive device failure, theft, accidental deletion and loss of access to a particular location.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It is also worth periodically checking that a backup actually works rather than discovering years later that a word was written incorrectly or an important credential was forgotten.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Honest Answer&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;So, can a hacker recover your forgotten Bitcoin wallet password?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;There is no universal recovery method, and a hacker cannot simply bypass Bitcoin's cryptography because you forgot a password.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If you still have the correct recovery phrase or another valid backup, you may have a legitimate route to restore the wallet, depending on the wallet design. If you forgot only a hardware-wallet PIN, recovery may also be possible through the wallet's backup. But if you have permanently lost the credentials and backup information needed to control a self-custodied wallet, the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/arthur-hayes-ai-safety-anthropic-ipo-2026.html"&gt;Bitcoin &lt;/a&gt;may be inaccessible permanently.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;And if someone promises to recover those coins for a fee and asks for your recovery phrase or private key, that is not a shortcut. It is a major security warning. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can a forgotten Bitcoin password be reset?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;It depends on the wallet. Some wallet or device credentials can be replaced after a legitimate recovery process, while some self-custody credentials, such as certain optional passphrases, cannot be reset.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can I recover Bitcoin with my recovery phrase?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;A correct recovery phrase can restore a wallet in supported wallet software, but the exact wallet configuration and any additional passphrase may also matter.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can Bitcoin Support recover my lost password?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;There is no central Bitcoin support authority that can reset the credentials of a self-custodied wallet. Wallet providers can explain their own recovery procedures, but they cannot generally recreate a secret that you have permanently lost.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What happens if I lose my hardware wallet?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;If you still have the correct wallet backup, the physical device itself may be replaceable. Hardware-wallet recovery is designed around the backup rather than relying solely on the device. Trezor and Ledger both document recovery processes that rely on the wallet backup when a device is reset or replaced. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Should I give my recovery phrase to a wallet recovery company?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;No. Treat your recovery phrase and private keys as secret credentials. Bitcoin.org specifically warns about fake recovery services that request this information. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can I recover Bitcoin if I forgot my exchange password?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;Usually, an exchange account is a different situation from a self-custody wallet. The exchange may provide its own account-recovery or password-reset process. Follow the exchange's official recovery procedure and avoid links or messages sent by strangers claiming to be support.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin gives users control over their own funds, but that control comes with responsibility. A forgotten password is not always the end of the road—but a permanently lost recovery secret can be.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The safest approach is to identify exactly which credential was forgotten, locate the legitimate backup, and follow only the official recovery procedure for the wallet or exchange involved.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Never share a recovery phrase or private key with a supposed recovery expert, support agent or stranger.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Sources:&lt;/strong&gt; Bitcoin.org, Trezor Support and Ledger Academy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Editorial note:&lt;/strong&gt; This article is for informational purposes and does not provide individualized wallet-recovery instructions. Never share a recovery phrase, private key or hardware-wallet security credentials with another person.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/article&gt;

    <title>BNB Chain Introduces Standards to Foster Agent Economy</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjgTR8kiV1OJF1tVi4S2OOn9rNt4vH4Fh3MgUyLOHwThEPJ8eRWHrEfZeajOw-cNokCNct5B0DIpcONxayyhwy78HrXDC2-7L9m3nqrE2KefBRSaEICmuBNfczYhRStdYw3gy16M88mu9uLsYcg5Ya4pBoc85NuoyLOLmTBchXxK1kAvQ03IKlhNlu77mQM/s1536/bnb.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="213" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjgTR8kiV1OJF1tVi4S2OOn9rNt4vH4Fh3MgUyLOHwThEPJ8eRWHrEfZeajOw-cNokCNct5B0DIpcONxayyhwy78HrXDC2-7L9m3nqrE2KefBRSaEICmuBNfczYhRStdYw3gy16M88mu9uLsYcg5Ya4pBoc85NuoyLOLmTBchXxK1kAvQ03IKlhNlu77mQM/s320/bnb.png" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;In a recent announcement, &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=BNB+Chain&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=7464790706002645129" target="_blank"&gt;BNB Chain&lt;/a&gt; emphasized the importance of four essential components for developing an effective &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=define+agent+economy&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=7464790706002645129" target="_blank"&gt;agent economy&lt;/a&gt;: identity, capability, payments, and accountability. This initiative aims to integrate these elements through various proposed standards including &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=ERC-8004&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=7464790706002645129" target="_blank"&gt;ERC-8004&lt;/a&gt;, BAP-578, x402 and &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=ERC-8183&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=7464790706002645129" target="_blank"&gt;ERC-8183&lt;/a&gt;. The effort is further supported by a robust ecosystem of &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=what+are+stablecoins&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=7464790706002645129" target="_blank"&gt;stablecoins&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The tweet from BNB Chain’s official account highlighted that constructing an agent economy hinges on establishing clear frameworks that manage how agents—representatives or automated systems acting on behalf of users—interact within decentralized environments.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The introduction of standards like ERC-8004 represents a significant step in enhancing &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=blockchain+interoperability&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=7464790706002645129" target="_blank"&gt;interoperability&lt;/a&gt; among blockchain platforms. According to industry experts, such advancements could streamline operations across decentralized applications (dApps) by ensuring that different systems can work together effectively without compromising security or performance.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Understanding the Four Components&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Breadth in capabilities requires that participants within this new structure have verified identities. Identity management is crucial for both user trust and regulatory compliance. It allows individuals to maintain control over their data while enabling seamless interactions with multiple platforms within the ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Capability refers to the skills or functions enabled by these identities; it encompasses everything from transaction execution to smart contract deployment. Payments refer specifically to how value transfers occur between agents in this framework; integrating stablecoins serves as a stabilizing influence amid volatile crypto markets.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Finally, accountability ensures that actions taken within this ecosystem are traceable and verifiable—which is paramount for maintaining integrity and trust among users participating in cryptocurrency transactions.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The Role of Stablecoins&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;A massive &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=stablecoin+ecosystem+BNB+Chain&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=7464790706002645129" target="_blank"&gt;stablecoin ecosystem&lt;/a&gt; backs these developments announced by BNB Chain. Stablecoins serve as crucial tools within &lt;a data-preview="" href="https://www.google.com/search?ved=1t:260882&amp;amp;q=define+crypto+economies&amp;amp;bbid=1063445581464181190&amp;amp;bpid=7464790706002645129" target="_blank"&gt;crypto economies&lt;/a&gt; due mainly to their price stability compared with more volatile cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin or Ethereum.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;This stability encourages broader adoption as businesses are often hesitant about accepting payment in currencies subjected frequently into severe fluctuations which could lead losses during processing times related delays associated with traditional bank transfers . As such having established mechanisms behind payment processes should contribute positively towards fostering larger merchant participation overall&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Industry Impact&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;This strategic move positions BNB Chain at the forefront of discussions surrounding decentralized finance (DeFi) architecture development efforts taking place globally today . With regulations evolving quickly while technological capabilities expand , projects willing lead charge towards unifying experiences will likely find favor amongst developers looking build innovative solutions available various sectors ranging entertainment gaming financial services etc..&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Expert Analysis&lt;/p&gt;</content>

    <title>Strategy Pauses Bitcoin Buying as $6.69B Cash Reserve Builds</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjslfdc_K-eybXkLsNfHckJMaTzPfXQzXOAmi6JAcuCkyG81D-uFbtFJqcaA3m-Bx4HzZW4-40Z2P96YX3x39YpjYngkGJTmMbslWIOxrzhFdku6JrVBfaAqMVjzaKlyiqsQvRE1J_-MoDE6CGLZ0Tr8DzsFVmzF_ID1eQ9r9_UIaj2nuoFrorEb8HOYX_0/s1672/strategy-bitcoin-buying-pause-669b-cash-reserve.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Strategy Bitcoin holdings and $6.69 billion cash reserve illustration" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjslfdc_K-eybXkLsNfHckJMaTzPfXQzXOAmi6JAcuCkyG81D-uFbtFJqcaA3m-Bx4HzZW4-40Z2P96YX3x39YpjYngkGJTmMbslWIOxrzhFdku6JrVBfaAqMVjzaKlyiqsQvRE1J_-MoDE6CGLZ0Tr8DzsFVmzF_ID1eQ9r9_UIaj2nuoFrorEb8HOYX_0/w400-h225/strategy-bitcoin-buying-pause-669b-cash-reserve.jpg.png" title="Strategy Pauses Bitcoin Buying as Cash Reserve Reaches $6.69B" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;By CoinAINews Staff | &lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Strategy has paused its latest Bitcoin purchase, leaving its
massive BTC position unchanged while building a &lt;b&gt;$6.69 billion cash and USD
reserve&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The company bought &lt;b&gt;zero Bitcoin between August 17 and
August 23&lt;/b&gt;, according to its latest update. Strategy's Bitcoin holdings
therefore remained at &lt;b&gt;840,447 BTC&lt;/b&gt;, acquired for approximately &lt;b&gt;$63.36
billion&lt;/b&gt;, including fees and expenses.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The pause is notable because Bitcoin accumulation has become
the defining feature of Strategy's corporate strategy. But the latest numbers
suggest the company is not simply stepping away from Bitcoin. Instead, it is
keeping a substantial amount of capital available for different uses.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Strategy Holds 840,447 BTC&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Strategy's Bitcoin holdings remained unchanged during the
latest reporting period.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The company's average acquisition price was approximately &lt;b&gt;$75,385
per Bitcoin&lt;/b&gt;, based on its reported total acquisition cost.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That puts Strategy among the largest &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/us-treasury-may-tap-nearly-1t-cash-pile.html"&gt;corporate holders&lt;/a&gt; of
BTC, making its buying activity closely watched by investors across the
cryptocurrency market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For years, a new Bitcoin purchase from Strategy has been
treated as a significant signal of corporate demand.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;This week's decision to buy nothing therefore stands out.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;But the company's cash position may be even more important.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Cash Reserve Reaches $6.69 Billion&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Strategy reported approximately &lt;b&gt;$6.69 billion across its
USD Reserve and USD Cash&lt;/b&gt; as of August 23.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The amount included roughly &lt;b&gt;$5.10 billion in USD Reserve&lt;/b&gt;
and &lt;b&gt;$1.59 billion in USD Cash&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That distinction gives investors a better idea of how
Strategy is managing its liquidity.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The reserve can support financial obligations, while the
separate cash balance provides management with greater flexibility.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That cash could potentially be used for future Bitcoin
purchases, securities repurchases, preferred-stock obligations, debt-related
payments or other corporate purposes.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;In other words, Strategy now has a significant pool of
capital available without immediately having to deploy it into Bitcoin.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;$2.01 Billion Raised Without Buying Bitcoin&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Strategy continued to access the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/germany-extends-eu-lead-with-79-mica.html"&gt;capital markets&lt;/a&gt; during the
same period.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The company sold approximately &lt;b&gt;18.26 million MSTR shares&lt;/b&gt;
through its at-the-market program, generating about &lt;b&gt;$2.01 billion in net
proceeds&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Yet none of that activity resulted in a new Bitcoin purchase
during the reporting week.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That is an important change in the usual pattern.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Strategy has frequently used capital-market transactions to
help finance its Bitcoin accumulation. This time, the company appears to have
prioritized liquidity and other financial uses.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Strategy Also Bought Back Preferred Stock&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Part of the company's capital was directed toward its
preferred securities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Strategy repurchased approximately &lt;b&gt;1.43 million STRC
preferred shares for $136.4 million&lt;/b&gt; during the period.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The move highlights the balancing act behind the company's
Bitcoin strategy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Strategy is managing a large Bitcoin position while also
dealing with preferred-stock obligations, financing costs and shareholder
interests.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That means every dollar raised does not necessarily have to
go toward buying BTC.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Does the Pause Signal a Change in Strategy?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Not necessarily.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;One week without a Bitcoin purchase is not enough to
establish that Strategy has changed its long-term view of Bitcoin.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The company still holds &lt;b&gt;840,447 BTC&lt;/b&gt;, and Bitcoin
remains central to its corporate strategy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;What has changed is the amount of flexibility sitting on the
balance sheet.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The &lt;b&gt;$1.59 billion USD Cash&lt;/b&gt; gives Strategy room to
respond if market conditions change.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;If Bitcoin falls substantially, the company could
potentially use some of that money for additional purchases. If markets remain
uncertain, it can keep the cash available for other financial needs.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That flexibility may be particularly valuable during periods
of high market volatility.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why the Market Is Watching&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Strategy's Bitcoin activity has become an important part of
the broader crypto narrative.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;When the company buys BTC, it reinforces the idea that
corporate investors continue to see Bitcoin as a long-term treasury asset.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;When purchases stop, investors naturally begin asking why.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The latest numbers don't provide evidence that Strategy has
abandoned its Bitcoin thesis. Instead, they show a company with an enormous BTC
position and billions of dollars in liquidity deciding not to immediately
increase that exposure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For investors, the next purchase could therefore be just as
interesting as the latest pause.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;A New Question for Strategy Investors&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Strategy's evolution has made its capital allocation
increasingly important.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The company is no longer simply deciding whether to buy
Bitcoin. It is deciding &lt;b&gt;how much capital should remain liquid, how much
should support its securities, and how much should ultimately be converted into
BTC&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That makes the company's cash balance worth watching
alongside its Bitcoin holdings.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The next major move could reveal whether the current pause
is temporary or part of a broader shift toward a more flexible approach to
Bitcoin accumulation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Strategy bought &lt;b&gt;zero Bitcoin during the latest reporting
week&lt;/b&gt;, leaving its holdings at &lt;b&gt;840,447 BTC&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;At the same time, its combined USD Reserve and USD Cash
reached approximately &lt;b&gt;$6.69 billion&lt;/b&gt;, while the company raised roughly &lt;b&gt;$2.01
billion&lt;/b&gt; through MSTR share sales.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The numbers point to a company that is still heavily
committed to Bitcoin but is keeping a larger amount of capital available for
other purposes.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;For now, the story isn't that Strategy has stopped believing
in Bitcoin.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;It's that &lt;b&gt;Strategy has stopped buying—for the moment—and
built itself a much larger financial cushion while it waits.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The next time the company moves that cash into Bitcoin could
tell investors considerably more about where its strategy is heading.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;Source: Strategy's latest corporate update, as reported
by Bitcoin.com News.&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
