    <title>What Will Change in Crypto by the End of 2026?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjMFHGDHZDyAW_romGimr5Fz232G-7L-r-yr4nh06S2Cr2ZpxLDamQHWcg-BbSaekO101CT5NeNGj7DgoyXua98rfqq63hG1UMcaSa3C4peKBuUbOTCPJlIG7VFzCyzuUcgLYdy3NU_tc9llwuPzQ64AVDT7tvRFr4b4flMgKj6LgsnK21NtMP6rGlLprqu/s1536/22.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Crypto market outlook for the end of 2026 showing Bitcoin recovery, institutional adoption, SEC regulation, stablecoins, tokenization and prediction markets" border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="213" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjMFHGDHZDyAW_romGimr5Fz232G-7L-r-yr4nh06S2Cr2ZpxLDamQHWcg-BbSaekO101CT5NeNGj7DgoyXua98rfqq63hG1UMcaSa3C4peKBuUbOTCPJlIG7VFzCyzuUcgLYdy3NU_tc9llwuPzQ64AVDT7tvRFr4b4flMgKj6LgsnK21NtMP6rGlLprqu/w320-h213/22.png" title="What Will Change in Crypto by the End of 2026?" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;Aug 9,
2026&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt; – The
crypto market has been through a rough first half of 2026. Bitcoin is down
nearly 28% year-to-date, ETF outflows have rattled sentiment, and the AI
narrative has siphoned attention and capital away from digital assets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;But if
history is any guide, the second half of the year could tell a very different
story.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;The question
on everyone's mind: &lt;b&gt;What will change by December 31?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;





&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;Here's what
industry analysts, institutional investors, and the data itself are signaling
for the remainder of 2026.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;1.
Bitcoin's Recovery: The Four-Year Cycle Isn't Dead&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;Despite
growing institutional participation, Bitcoin continues to follow its historical
four-year cycle, according to 21Shares' mid-year crypto report. The current
drawdown, while painful, is far milder than the 80%+ corrections of previous
cycles. Bitcoin has consistently stayed above its aggregate investor cost basis
of $54,000 — a level it has not traded below in this cycle.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;The
structural picture has shifted. Both Ethereum and Solana have seen their
fundamentals strengthen through the drawdown that began in October 2025, with
Bitcoin leading relative performance among major assets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;What
analysts are saying:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;"Following
the peak at $126,000 in October 2025, Bitcoin corrected sharply, tracking
closely with historical post-halving rhythms. Fundamental metrics point to a
base-case recovery toward $100,000 by year-end."&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;— &lt;b&gt;21Shares
mid-year crypto market report&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;"These
are signs of a more mature market with stickier capital flows."&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;













&lt;span style="font-family: &amp;quot;Calibri&amp;quot;,sans-serif; font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family: &amp;quot;Times New Roman&amp;quot;; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-bidi; mso-fareast-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"&gt;— &lt;b&gt;21Shares report&lt;/b&gt;, noting Bitcoin
has avoided outright capitulation&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: &amp;quot;Calibri&amp;quot;,sans-serif; font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family: &amp;quot;Times New Roman&amp;quot;; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-bidi; mso-fareast-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;2.
Institutional Capital: The Tide Is Turning&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;Institutional
investors remain broadly positive on digital assets despite recent volatility.
A Coinbase and EY-Parthenon survey of 351 institutional decision-makers found
that &lt;b&gt;73% plan to increase their digital asset allocations in 2026&lt;/b&gt;,
and 74% expect crypto prices to rise over the next 12 months.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;Key
institutional trends:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;66% already hold spot crypto
     ETFs/ETPs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;,
     while &lt;b&gt;81% prefer accessing spot crypto through a registered
     vehicle&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;86% already use stablecoins or
     are interested in using them&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;, with T+0 settlement and cash management as top use
     cases&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;63% are very interested in
     investing in tokenized assets&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;, and more than 60% expect tokenization to significantly
     affect trading, clearing, and settlement within 3-5 years&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;65% cite improved regulatory
     clarity&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt; as
     the number one factor behind their decision to boost crypto exposure&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: &amp;quot;Calibri&amp;quot;,sans-serif; font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family: &amp;quot;Times New Roman&amp;quot;; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-bidi; mso-fareast-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"&gt;







&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;David Duong,
Coinbase's head of institutional research, summarized the sentiment: &lt;i&gt;"People
are still interested in crypto. They want to see tighter risk controls, but
they want to stay allocated."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span&gt;&amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;3. SEC
Rules Could Bring Greater Regulatory Clarity&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;One of the
biggest catalysts for the second half could come from Washington. The SEC's
2026 Regulatory Agenda includes proposed rules for crypto asset offerings,
broker-dealer requirements, and market structure — all marked for proposed
rulemaking as early as July 2026.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;What the
SEC says:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;"The
proposed rules may provide greater certainty to the market, facilitate capital
formation, and accommodate innovation within the crypto asset markets while
ensuring that investors are adequately protected."&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;— &lt;b&gt;SEC
2026 Regulatory Agenda&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;The shift
represents a significant departure from the enforcement-heavy approach of
former Chair Gary Gensler. The SEC is also exploring "safe harbors"
and regulatory exemptions related to crypto issuance, custody, and trading. In
March 2026, the SEC issued an interpretation of federal securities laws
applicable to crypto assets, further signaling a move toward clarity.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;

&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: &amp;quot;Calibri&amp;quot;,sans-serif; font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family: &amp;quot;Times New Roman&amp;quot;; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-bidi; mso-fareast-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"&gt;The CLARITY Act&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: &amp;quot;Calibri&amp;quot;,sans-serif; font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family: &amp;quot;Times New Roman&amp;quot;; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-bidi; mso-fareast-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"&gt; could still become law this year, though
it will require significant negotiation. For institutions, clearer rules could
unlock broader participation, while continued uncertainty remains a key
constraint on capital entering the space.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: &amp;quot;Calibri&amp;quot;,sans-serif; font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family: &amp;quot;Times New Roman&amp;quot;; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-bidi; mso-fareast-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;4.
Stablecoins: From $320B Peak to Recovery&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;Stablecoin
adoption has been slower than expected. Total supply peaked at $320.8 billion
in May 2026 but has since declined to approximately $304 billion as of early
August, a $17 billion drop.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: &amp;quot;Calibri&amp;quot;,sans-serif; font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family: &amp;quot;Times New Roman&amp;quot;; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-bidi; mso-fareast-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"&gt;



&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;However, the
market could still end the year between $400 billion and $600 billion,
depending on whether adoption accelerates in the second half. Usage velocity
has actually increased — monthly adjusted volume jumped from $1.1 trillion to
$1.79 trillion between May and June 2026, suggesting that while supply is down,
transaction activity is heating up.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;5.
Tokenization: The Institutional Bridge Is Here&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;Tokenization
is where institutional interest is most tangible. Public blockchain
distribution of tokenized assets stands at $31 billion, anchored by $15 billion
in tokenized US Treasuries. However, when including assets on permissioned
institutional networks like Canton, the figure surges to approximately $350
billion.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;



&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;The DTCC
milestone:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt; The
Depository Trust &amp;amp; Clearing Corporation began limited production trades of
tokenized real-world assets in &lt;b&gt;July 2026&lt;/b&gt;, bringing Russell 1000
equities, major ETFs, and US Treasuries onto blockchain infrastructure. A full
rollout is scheduled for &lt;b&gt;October 2026&lt;/b&gt;, backed by more than 50 firms
including BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;"Wall
Street's core clearinghouse just moved tokenization out of the lab and into
live trading."&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;— &lt;b&gt;DTCC
announcement&lt;/b&gt;, July 14, 2026&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;



&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;Source:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt; DTCC official press release,
July 15, 2026&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;6.
Prediction Markets: The Dark Horse&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;Prediction
markets have exceeded expectations. 21Shares reports that prediction markets
recorded $57.5 billion in trading volume through the end of May — more than
half of the firm's full-year projection. Annual volumes are tracking toward
$100 billion and could potentially challenge $200 billion depending on
second-half activity tied to the FIFA World Cup and U.S. midterm congressional
elections.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;However,
industry analysts caution that &lt;b&gt;90% of prediction market products may go
completely unnoticed and disappear&lt;/b&gt; by year-end, reflecting the high
failure rate of projects in this sector.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;





&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: &amp;quot;Calibri&amp;quot;,sans-serif; font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family: &amp;quot;Times New Roman&amp;quot;; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-bidi; mso-fareast-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"&gt;Source:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: &amp;quot;Calibri&amp;quot;,sans-serif; font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family: &amp;quot;Times New Roman&amp;quot;; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-bidi; mso-fareast-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"&gt; Dragonfly
partner Haseeb Qureshi's forecast, reported in Coinlive&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: &amp;quot;Calibri&amp;quot;,sans-serif; font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family: &amp;quot;Times New Roman&amp;quot;; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-bidi; mso-fareast-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;7. What's
Not Changing&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;Despite the
positive outlook, some caution is warranted:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: &amp;quot;Calibri&amp;quot;,sans-serif; font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%; mso-ansi-language: EN-IN; mso-ascii-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-bidi-font-family: &amp;quot;Times New Roman&amp;quot;; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA; mso-bidi-theme-font: minor-bidi; mso-fareast-font-family: Calibri; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-theme-font: minor-latin; mso-hansi-theme-font: minor-latin;"&gt;



&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;Only 7% of organizations report
     established ROI from AI agents&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt; — the AI "bubble" may still burst before
     year-end&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;Layer-2 consolidation&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt; is accelerating, with
     Base, Arbitrum, and Optimism capturing 83% of L2 DeFi TVL&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: 14.0pt; line-height: 115%;"&gt;**DeFi TVL remains around $140

    <title>RAIN accounts for the largest share of this week's estimated $703.73 million in major token unlocks.</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

  &lt;header&gt;
    &lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj2RNzQKfs3eNtjexWw0nB0MEMcosm7XLtRxZqoMMSYaBmHU2FjjmvtRgEVN4Ehfe2_RqTi_pF71nr-eeq5RAhJyfNwnbR9iLLvGtGpCNsDbpE-HH4yNniNwoxqizACPjnUOmN4m5_wzIxiMBYU06wvDkcu1RTE1bOXMlB9F5fw0eGgmWlbFyPKeNWFHAh3/s1672/rain-token-703-73-million-weekly-token-unlocks.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="RAIN token leads $703.73 million weekly crypto token unlocks" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj2RNzQKfs3eNtjexWw0nB0MEMcosm7XLtRxZqoMMSYaBmHU2FjjmvtRgEVN4Ehfe2_RqTi_pF71nr-eeq5RAhJyfNwnbR9iLLvGtGpCNsDbpE-HH4yNniNwoxqizACPjnUOmN4m5_wzIxiMBYU06wvDkcu1RTE1bOXMlB9F5fw0eGgmWlbFyPKeNWFHAh3/w640-h360/rain-token-703-73-million-weekly-token-unlocks.jpg.png" title="RAIN Leads $703.73M Weekly Crypto Token Unlocks" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Crypto token unlocks worth approximately $703.73 million are scheduled across seven major tokens this week, with RAIN accounting for the vast majority of the total at an estimated $586.44 million.&lt;/strong&gt; The size of the release has put RAIN at the center of attention as traders assess whether the additional supply could create selling pressure or be absorbed by market demand.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;/header&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;According to the latest token-unlock data highlighted by CryptoRank, the seven largest releases this week are RAIN, ADI, STABLE, HOLO, UP, APT and JTO. Together, the scheduled unlocks represent about $703.73 million in token value. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;However, the headline dollar value alone does not determine how a token will perform. The structure of each unlock, the percentage of circulating supply being released, the recipients of the tokens and prevailing market liquidity can all influence the eventual price reaction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;RAIN Dominates This Week's Token Unlock Calendar&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;RAIN is by far the largest unlock in dollar terms this week, with an estimated &lt;strong&gt;$586.44 million&lt;/strong&gt; worth of tokens scheduled for release.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;One important distinction is that the RAIN release should not be described as a single-day cliff unlock. Current reporting characterizes the RAIN schedule as a &lt;strong&gt;linear release&lt;/strong&gt;, meaning tokens are released gradually under the vesting schedule rather than being unlocked through one concentrated cliff event. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That difference matters. A large linear unlock can still create significant potential supply pressure, but the market may have more time to absorb the additional tokens than it would during a one-time cliff release.&lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;/tbody&gt;
  &lt;/table&gt;The figures are based on the latest weekly unlock data and can change in dollar terms as token prices move. The underlying number of tokens scheduled for release may remain unchanged while the estimated USD value fluctuates with the market.&lt;h2&gt;Why the RAIN Unlock Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The biggest concern surrounding a major token unlock is the potential increase in tradable supply.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;When previously locked &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-someone-steal-bitcoin-with-wallet-address.html"&gt;tokens&lt;/a&gt; become available, recipients may hold them, use them within an ecosystem, stake them, transfer them or sell them. Therefore, an unlock itself does not mean that an equivalent amount of tokens will immediately hit exchanges.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For RAIN, the scale of the scheduled release makes the token particularly important to watch this week. The market will likely focus on trading volume, liquidity, exchange flows and price behavior as the release progresses.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Another important point is that &lt;strong&gt;unlock value is not the same thing as guaranteed selling pressure&lt;/strong&gt;. The actual impact depends on what token holders do with the newly available supply.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;RAIN Price Context: Why the Ticker Needs Careful Identification&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Investors should also be careful when looking up RAIN market data because the ticker is used by more than one crypto project. Different market-data platforms can therefore display different assets under the RAIN symbol.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For that reason, CoinAINews is not using an unverified price or market-cap figure for RAIN in this report. The &lt;strong&gt;$586.44 million&lt;/strong&gt; figure refers specifically to the RAIN asset included in the weekly unlock dataset being discussed here.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This distinction is important because publishing a price belonging to a different &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-someone-find-your-name-from-bitcoin-wallet.html"&gt;RAIN token&lt;/a&gt; could materially mislead readers.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;HOLO Has One of the Largest Unlocks Relative to Its Market Size&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;While RAIN dominates the list in absolute dollar value, &lt;strong&gt;HOLO&lt;/strong&gt; stands out when the size of the unlock is compared with the token's market capitalization.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Current reporting based on CryptoRank data puts the HOLO unlock at approximately &lt;strong&gt;$12.01 million&lt;/strong&gt;, equivalent to roughly &lt;strong&gt;51.9% of its market capitalization&lt;/strong&gt;. The release is associated with allocations for investors, core contributors and advisors becoming available after the project's cliff period. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That makes HOLO a different type of supply event from RAIN. RAIN has the largest dollar-value release, while HOLO's unlock is much more significant relative to the size of its existing market.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For traders, that distinction can be crucial. A smaller unlock can potentially have a larger percentage impact when the newly released supply represents a substantial share of the token's market capitalization.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;ADI, STABLE, UP, APT and JTO Also Face New Supply&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;After RAIN, the next-largest release is &lt;strong&gt;ADI&lt;/strong&gt;, with an estimated unlock value of $56.81 million.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;STABLE&lt;/strong&gt; follows with approximately $25.66 million, while &lt;strong&gt;HOLO&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;UP&lt;/strong&gt; represent about $12.01 million and $11.36 million, respectively.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The list is completed by &lt;strong&gt;Aptos (APT)&lt;/strong&gt; at approximately $6.43 million and &lt;strong&gt;Jito (JTO)&lt;/strong&gt; at about $5.02 million. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;These events should not be interpreted in exactly the same way. Each project has its own tokenomics, vesting schedule, holder base and market liquidity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Is a Token Unlock?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A token unlock is the scheduled release of &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-says-agi-has.html"&gt;cryptocurrency&lt;/a&gt; that was previously restricted by a vesting or distribution schedule.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Crypto projects commonly lock tokens allocated to early investors, team members, advisors, foundations, communities and ecosystem programs. Those tokens can then become available according to a predetermined schedule.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Unlocks can take several forms, including:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Cliff unlocks:&lt;/strong&gt; A larger allocation becomes available after a specified period.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Linear unlocks:&lt;/strong&gt; Tokens are released gradually over a defined period.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Periodic unlocks:&lt;/strong&gt; Tokens are released at regular intervals, such as monthly or quarterly.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Hybrid schedules:&lt;/strong&gt; A project combines a cliff period with subsequent linear vesting.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Understanding the structure is important because a one-time release and a gradual release can create very different short-term supply dynamics.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Can a $703.73 Million Unlock Trigger a Crypto Sell-Off?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It can, but there is no automatic relationship between token unlocks and price declines.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If recipients sell a significant amount of newly unlocked tokens while demand remains unchanged, the additional supply can put downward pressure on price.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;On the other hand, an unlock may have limited impact if recipients continue holding their tokens, use them within the ecosystem or sell them gradually into deep liquidity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Market conditions also play a major role. During a strong risk-on environment, buyers may absorb additional supply relatively easily. During a weak market, even a moderate increase in available supply can have a more noticeable effect.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Traders Should Watch&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Rather than focusing only on the headline $703.73 million figure, traders should monitor several indicators around major unlocks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;1. Exchange Inflows&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Large transfers of unlocked tokens to centralized exchanges can sometimes indicate that holders are preparing to sell. However, an exchange deposit by itself does not prove that a sale will occur.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;2. Trading Volume&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Higher trading volume can help the market absorb additional supply. Low liquidity can make large transactions more disruptive.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;3. Unlock-to-Market-Cap Ratio&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This can be more informative than the absolute dollar value. HOLO is a good example of why traders should compare an unlock with the size of the existing market.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;4. Recipient Allocation&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Investors, insiders, team members, foundations and community programs may have different incentives and holding periods. The recipient breakdown can therefore provide useful context.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;5. Price Reaction&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If a token absorbs a major unlock without significant downside, it can indicate that demand and liquidity are strong enough to handle the additional supply. The opposite can also be true.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Comes After This Week?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The token-unlock calendar remains active beyond this week's headline events. Several projects have additional scheduled releases later in September.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Current unlock calendars show multiple releases around &lt;strong&gt;September 15–17&lt;/strong&gt;, including scheduled events for assets such as SEI, ARB, ZK, IOTA and others. The exact dollar value of these events can change with market prices and individual vesting updates. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;One notable example is &lt;strong&gt;ZK&lt;/strong&gt;, with a scheduled September 17 release of more than 173 million tokens according to current vesting data. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Traders should therefore avoid treating the current week's $703.73 million figure as the end of the September supply story. More releases are scheduled throughout the month.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Picture for Crypto Markets&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Token unlocks are becoming an increasingly important part of crypto market analysis because they connect project tokenomics with real circulating supply.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;However, the headline dollar value can sometimes be misleading. A $500 million unlock for a large, liquid asset may have less immediate impact than a $20 million release for a small-cap token if the latter represents a much larger percentage of its circulating market.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is why professional market analysis typically considers several variables together: circulating supply, fully diluted valuation, unlock percentage, recipient allocation, liquidity, trading volume and the project's broader fundamentals.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The seven largest token unlocks this week represent approximately &lt;strong&gt;$703.73 million&lt;/strong&gt;, according to the latest weekly data, with &lt;strong&gt;RAIN leading at $586.44 million&lt;/strong&gt;. ADI, STABLE, HOLO, UP, APT and JTO make up the remainder of the top-seven list. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;RAIN's release is the week's biggest event by dollar value, but it is important to understand that the scheduled release follows a &lt;strong&gt;linear vesting structure&lt;/strong&gt; rather than being characterized as a single cliff unlock. &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;HOLO, meanwhile, stands out for the size of its release relative to market capitalization, illustrating why percentage-based supply metrics can sometimes matter more than headline dollar values.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For crypto investors, the key takeaway is straightforward: &lt;strong&gt;a token unlock creates potential additional supply, but it does not guarantee a price decline.&lt;/strong&gt; The ultimate market reaction will depend on holder behavior, liquidity, demand and broader market conditions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;aside&gt;
    &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Risk Disclaimer:&lt;/strong&gt; This article is provided for informational and educational purposes only and does not constitute investment, financial or trading advice. Cryptocurrency markets are highly volatile. Token-unlock estimates can change as token prices, vesting schedules and project disclosures change. Readers should conduct their own research before making investment decisions.&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/aside&gt;

```

&lt;p&gt;The seven largest scheduled unlocks are estimated at approximately $703.73 million in total.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is the RAIN unlock a cliff unlock?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. Current reporting describes the RAIN release as a linear vesting release rather than a single concentrated cliff unlock.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why is HOLO important this week?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;HOLO's estimated $12.01 million unlock is particularly notable because it represents roughly 51.9% of its market capitalization, according to the cited weekly unlock data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What should traders monitor during a token unlock?&lt;/h3&gt;

    <title>Brazil’s Securities Regulator Launches 120-Day Tokenization Working Group</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;header&gt;
&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjT_WW7joQZeJ10Ec49uX88Kag6GEStHiDw2KurC3UnbG401xet7Pl6dDOFq3z5EMjup1Ur8lb8LlqauSiGZ0QtyMlqzpkbaXSOIhimun_Eba5povT6dsrrbZtPkyLdY3tl1GYwupHs9FZzs1N6r0MVf7FHED41zHKaiLYIJEzTcxD6bNB8o27XJQjHaAxo/s1734/brazil-cvm-tokenization-working-group.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Brazil securities regulator CVM tokenization working group and digital securities" border="0" data-original-height="907" data-original-width="1734" height="334" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjT_WW7joQZeJ10Ec49uX88Kag6GEStHiDw2KurC3UnbG401xet7Pl6dDOFq3z5EMjup1Ur8lb8LlqauSiGZ0QtyMlqzpkbaXSOIhimun_Eba5povT6dsrrbZtPkyLdY3tl1GYwupHs9FZzs1N6r0MVf7FHED41zHKaiLYIJEzTcxD6bNB8o27XJQjHaAxo/w640-h334/brazil-cvm-tokenization-working-group.jpg.png" title="Brazil CVM Tokenization Working Group" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;Brazil’s securities regulator is moving ahead with plans to examine how blockchain-based infrastructure could be used across the country’s capital markets.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt; The Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (CVM), Brazil’s securities and exchange commission, has established a 120-day working group dedicated to studying tokenization and developing the foundations for a future regulatory framework for tokenized securities.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;/header&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The initiative was formally created through Portaria CVM/PTE 177, published on July 17, 2026. The working group has an initial mandate of 120 days, with the possibility of a 30-day extension. Its work covers areas including the registration, deposit, custody, trading and settlement of securities using distributed ledger technology (DLT).&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Brazil Begins Formal Study of Securities Tokenization&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CVM’s initiative goes beyond &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/clarity-act-stalls-in-senate-as_01396500536.html"&gt;cryptocurrencies&lt;/a&gt;. The regulator is examining how DLT could be integrated into the regulated securities market and whether existing rules are sufficient for financial assets represented or processed through distributed ledgers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The working group brings together representatives from 14 organizational units within the CVM. It can also work with government agencies, self-regulatory organizations, industry associations and invited specialists.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Its responsibilities include studying tokenization experiments in Brazil and other countries, reviewing regulatory sandbox experiences, consulting with market participants and evaluating how DLT could affect the structure and operation of Brazil’s capital markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does the 120-Day Working Group Do?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The group has been tasked with examining both the potential benefits and risks associated with tokenized securities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Among its responsibilities are evaluating cybersecurity issues, identifying possible gaps in the current regulatory framework, coordinating experimental prototypes and developing technical recommendations that could eventually support new regulatory measures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CVM has also said the working group will establish the foundations for future regulation covering the tokenization of securities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means the 120-day period is not itself a final &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/openai-makes-progress-on-another.html"&gt;tokenization rule.&lt;/a&gt; Instead, it is part of a regulatory process designed to gather evidence before Brazil determines how tokenized securities should operate under its capital-market framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;CVM Has Already Submitted a DLT Pilot Proposal&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The process has moved quickly since the working group was created.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On September 15, 2026, the Tokenization Working Group submitted a draft resolution to the CVM’s Collegiate proposing the creation of the &lt;strong&gt;CVM DLT Pilot Program&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proposed program would allow experimental operations involving the issuance, offering, distribution, trading, registration, custody, centralized deposit and settlement of securities through distributed ledger technology networks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The pilot is intended to help the regulator determine whether DLT is technically, operationally and legally viable for Brazil’s securities market. It would also allow the CVM to study interoperability between different networks and identify potential risks, vulnerabilities and regulatory gaps.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Which Securities Could Be Tested?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proposed pilot is designed to cover more than one type of financial asset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to the CVM, experimental operations could include &lt;strong&gt;shares, debentures, receivables certificates, investment-fund units and other securities or collective investment contracts&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is significant because it places tokenization within the broader financial-market infrastructure rather than treating it solely as a cryptocurrency issue.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The experiments would allow regulators and participating institutions to examine how tokenized securities could function throughout different stages of the market, from issuance and distribution to trading, custody and settlement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Long Would the DLT Pilot Last?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Under the proposal submitted by the working group, the experimental tests would run for &lt;strong&gt;60 days&lt;/strong&gt;, with the possibility of an extension of up to 30 additional days.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CVM would directly monitor the tests through mechanisms that could provide access to the selected networks and allow real-time reading of transaction records.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;After the experiments, participating entities would submit reports describing their results. A management committee made up of CVM members participating in the working group would then consolidate the findings and submit a final evaluation to the regulator’s Collegiate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Brazil Is Studying Tokenization&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tokenization refers to representing an asset or financial right digitally on a blockchain or another distributed ledger. In capital markets, the technology could potentially change how securities are issued, recorded, transferred, traded and settled.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional securities transactions can involve multiple systems and intermediaries. DLT-based infrastructure may allow some records and processes to be shared or automated across a network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, introducing blockchain technology into regulated financial markets also creates questions around cybersecurity, legal ownership, custody, operational resilience, investor protection and market supervision.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CVM’s working group is therefore examining both the technological possibilities and the regulatory consequences before establishing a permanent framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Brazil Wants Innovation Without Removing Market Safeguards&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CVM has positioned the initiative as part of its effort to modernize financial-market regulation while maintaining investor protection, market integrity and legal certainty.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When the working group was announced, the regulator said its purpose was to follow technological developments and develop regulatory solutions capable of supporting innovation while preserving those safeguards.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The approach also involves consultation with market participants. In July, more than 50 people from the CVM and organizations including Anbima, Abrasca, Ancord, ABCripto, ABToken, BEE4 and CSD BR participated in discussions about possible experimental tokenization frameworks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Brazil’s Tokenization Rules Are Not Final Yet&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Despite the creation of the working group and the proposed DLT pilot, Brazil has not yet finalized a comprehensive set of rules governing securities tokenization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The current process is experimental and investigative. The CVM is using the working group and proposed pilot to collect information that could help determine whether existing regulations need to be changed or supplemented.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The eventual regulatory framework could therefore depend on what the experiments reveal about technology, market infrastructure, investor protection and legal requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next stage is for the CVM to consider the proposed DLT pilot and, if approved, oversee the experimental operations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The results could provide the regulator with practical information about how tokenized securities perform in real market environments. The findings may also identify areas where existing legislation or regulations need clarification.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The working group’s broader mandate will continue beyond the initial pilot proposal, with a final report expected at the conclusion of its 120-day period, subject to the possible 30-day extension provided in its mandate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Brazil’s Move Means for the Digital Asset Industry&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Brazil’s initiative shows that the regulatory conversation around blockchain is expanding beyond cryptocurrencies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For financial institutions, tokenization could eventually provide another infrastructure option for issuing and managing traditional securities. For &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/revolut-data-breach-hacker-launches.html"&gt;blockchain companies,&lt;/a&gt; a regulated testing environment could offer an opportunity to demonstrate how distributed ledger technology can operate within established capital-market requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the CVM’s approach also makes clear that technological adoption will be evaluated alongside regulatory safeguards. The outcome of the pilot and subsequent regulatory discussions will help determine the role tokenized securities can play in Brazil’s financial system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is Brazil’s tokenization working group?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is a CVM working group created to study distributed ledger technology, conduct tests, develop technical recommendations and help establish the foundations for future regulation of tokenized securities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How long will the CVM working group operate?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The working group has an initial duration of 120 days and can be extended by another 30 days.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Has Brazil finalized its tokenization rules?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. The CVM is still developing its regulatory approach. The working group and proposed DLT pilot are intended to provide evidence for future regulatory decisions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is the CVM DLT Pilot Program?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is a proposed experimental program for testing securities-market operations using distributed ledger technology. The proposal was submitted to the CVM’s Collegiate on September 15, 2026.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Which securities could be tested?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proposed pilot could include shares, debentures, receivables certificates, investment-fund units and other securities or collective investment contracts.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How long would the proposed DLT tests last?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proposed experimental operations would last 60 days, with a possible extension of up to 30 additional days.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>What Happens If a Bitcoin Transaction Disappears From the Mempool?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhoibXQ4fQ-4gY5J7Ljpg7OPVbMnsOyaPrz-jEeZzJe-9zO0FGWxBwrHGpLJ9ONiv5ExBRB94IwaV-f5LjasJuIsKSVsfdvfpMy3zgy8sS_ps7t6ngMfJoGSNhRcJ3zasBJ6M8xoSkuU8fo_UQxPflSsV-yA0XZ946WPd0C24JBT5S_LMSKsqaDfytOadNF/s1670/bitcoin-transaction-disappears-from-mempool.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin transaction disappears from the mempool while waiting for confirmation" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1670" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhoibXQ4fQ-4gY5J7Ljpg7OPVbMnsOyaPrz-jEeZzJe-9zO0FGWxBwrHGpLJ9ONiv5ExBRB94IwaV-f5LjasJuIsKSVsfdvfpMy3zgy8sS_ps7t6ngMfJoGSNhRcJ3zasBJ6M8xoSkuU8fo_UQxPflSsV-yA0XZ946WPd0C24JBT5S_LMSKsqaDfytOadNF/w640-h360/bitcoin-transaction-disappears-from-mempool.jpg.png" title="What Happens If a Bitcoin Transaction Disappears From the Mempool?" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span&gt;&amp;nbsp;&amp;nbsp; &amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;You send Bitcoin, receive a transaction ID, and watch the payment sit in the mempool. Then, unexpectedly, it disappears.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That can be alarming. The first thought is usually: &lt;em&gt;Did my Bitcoin disappear? Was the transaction cancelled? Did something go wrong?&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Usually, the answer is no.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When an unconfirmed Bitcoin transaction disappears from the mempool, it generally means that a particular node or group of nodes is no longer keeping or relaying that transaction. The transaction may have been &lt;strong&gt;confirmed, replaced, evicted because of mempool pressure, or removed after remaining unconfirmed for too long&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important distinction is this: &lt;strong&gt;disappearing from the mempool is not the same thing as being confirmed or permanently cancelled.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Quick Answer: What Does It Mean When a Bitcoin Transaction Disappears?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 720px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;What happened?&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;What it usually means&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;What to do&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Transaction confirmed&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;It was included in a Bitcoin block.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Check the transaction's confirmations.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Transaction replaced&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;A conflicting transaction replaced it, commonly through RBF.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Look for the replacement transaction.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Low-fee transaction dropped&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;The transaction was no longer attractive for relay or was evicted from a full mempool.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Check the transaction status and rebroadcast or fee-bump when appropriate.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Long-unconfirmed transaction expires&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Nodes can remove old unconfirmed transactions from their mempools.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Verify whether it confirmed elsewhere before taking action.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;First, What Is the Bitcoin Mempool?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The mempool is essentially a waiting area for Bitcoin transactions that have been broadcast to nodes but have not yet been included in a block.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When you send BTC, your wallet creates and signs a transaction. The transaction is then broadcast to the Bitcoin network. Nodes validate it according to their rules and may keep it in their local mempool while miners consider it for inclusion in a future block.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is important to understand that Bitcoin does not have one single global mempool.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Different nodes can have slightly different sets of unconfirmed transactions. A transaction may disappear from one node's mempool while still being visible elsewhere.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's developer documentation also notes that nodes do not necessarily retain arbitrary historic transactions that are no longer in their memory pool or relay set. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Would a Bitcoin Transaction Disappear From the Mempool?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are several possible explanations. The most important ones are confirmation, replacement and eviction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;1. The Transaction Was Confirmed&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The simplest explanation is that the transaction was mined into a block.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once a transaction is included in the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-bitcoin-transaction-get-stuck.html"&gt;Bitcoin blockchain&lt;/a&gt;, it is no longer an unconfirmed mempool transaction. It disappears from the mempool because it has moved into the permanent blockchain history.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why a transaction disappearing from a mempool explorer is not automatically bad news.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Before assuming the payment failed, search the transaction ID on a reliable Bitcoin block explorer and check whether it has a block height and confirmations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;2. The Transaction Was Replaced by Another Transaction&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin supports transaction replacement mechanisms such as &lt;strong&gt;Replace-by-Fee, or RBF&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With RBF, an unconfirmed transaction can be replaced by another transaction that spends the same inputs under the applicable replacement rules, generally offering a higher fee rate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This can happen when a sender realizes that the original fee is too low and uses a wallet's fee-bumping feature.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The original transaction may then disappear from the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-someone-steal-bitcoin-with-wallet-address.html"&gt;mempool &lt;/a&gt;while the replacement transaction becomes the one waiting for confirmation. Bitcoin's BIP 125 describes the opt-in RBF mechanism for replacing transactions in node mempools. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So if your original transaction suddenly disappears, check whether a replacement transaction exists before assuming the BTC has been lost.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;3. The Transaction Was Dropped Because of Low Fee Pressure&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin block space is limited. When many transactions compete for that space, fee rates can rise.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Transactions paying relatively low fees can remain unconfirmed while higher-fee transactions move ahead of them.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org explains that transaction fees are based on transaction size and the price of block space rather than simply the amount of BTC being sent. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If a transaction remains unconfirmed and becomes unattractive compared with the transactions competing for block space, a node can eventually remove it from its mempool.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;4. The Mempool Became Too Full&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Mempools have resource limits. Bitcoin Core currently has a default maximum mempool size of 300 MB, and its policy allows transactions to be removed when the mempool needs to make room.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This means a transaction does not necessarily have to wait for the full expiration period before disappearing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In a crowded fee market, lower-fee transactions can be pushed out as nodes prioritize their available mempool space.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;5. The Transaction Reached Its Mempool Expiry&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin Core's current source code sets the default &lt;code&gt;-mempoolexpiry&lt;/code&gt; value to &lt;strong&gt;336 hours&lt;/strong&gt;, which equals approximately &lt;strong&gt;14 days&lt;/strong&gt;. This is a node policy setting, not a Bitcoin consensus rule. Operators can configure it differently. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no Bitcoin blockchain rule saying that every unconfirmed transaction must disappear exactly after 14 days. Instead, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-can-sending-10-bitcoin-cost-more.html"&gt;Bitcoin Core's&lt;/a&gt; default policy tells a node not to keep a transaction in its mempool longer than that configured period.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Other nodes may have different policies, and a transaction can be removed earlier for other reasons.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does a Disappeared Transaction Mean My Bitcoin Is Gone?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No, not by itself.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A transaction disappearing from the mempool does not mean that the Bitcoin itself has vanished from the blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important question is whether the transaction was actually confirmed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If it was not confirmed and was simply dropped from the mempool, the original transaction did not become part of the blockchain. In a normal self-custody situation, the inputs have not been permanently spent by that transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, you should not immediately create another transaction without checking the original transaction's status. A transaction can still exist in another node's mempool or may have been confirmed even if one particular explorer no longer shows it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can a Dropped Bitcoin Transaction Come Back?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A transaction that disappeared from one or more mempools can potentially be broadcast again if it is still valid and its inputs have not been spent by a conflicting confirmed transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one reason wallets can sometimes show an old transaction as pending again after rebroadcasting.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's network is decentralized, so there is no single central server that permanently decides whether an unconfirmed transaction exists.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, if the transaction has been replaced or its inputs have already been spent by another confirmed transaction, simply rebroadcasting the old transaction will not make it valid again.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If the Transaction Disappears but the Recipient Has Not Received Bitcoin?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the most confusing situations for users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Suppose you send BTC, the recipient sees nothing, and later the transaction disappears from the mempool.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Do not immediately send the Bitcoin again.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;First check these things:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Look up the original transaction ID.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Check whether the transaction has any confirmations.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Check whether a replacement transaction exists.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Confirm that the receiving address was correct.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Check whether your wallet still considers the inputs spent or pending.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Check whether the transaction was dropped because of its fee rate.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the original transaction was never confirmed and was genuinely dropped, your wallet may be able to create or rebroadcast a valid transaction using the available funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens to the Bitcoin After a Transaction Is Dropped?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This depends on the wallet's state and whether another transaction has spent the same inputs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A useful way to think about it is that an unconfirmed transaction is a proposed spend, not yet a confirmed change to Bitcoin's blockchain state.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If that transaction disappears without being confirmed or replaced by a conflicting confirmed transaction, the underlying unspent outputs can remain available to the owner.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But wallet software may continue displaying the funds as unavailable until it rescans the network, rebroadcasts transactions, or updates its internal transaction state.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why the balance shown by a wallet and the actual blockchain state can temporarily look confusing after a transaction disappears.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can You Cancel a Bitcoin Transaction After It Disappears?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no universal Bitcoin "cancel" button.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If an unconfirmed transaction is still in the network and supports an appropriate replacement mechanism, the sender may be able to replace it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If it has already disappeared from many mempools, the situation can be different. It may simply need to be rebroadcast, replaced, or recreated depending on what happened to the original inputs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once a transaction is confirmed in a Bitcoin block, it cannot be reversed through a normal cancellation request.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;RBF Can Explain a Disappearing Transaction&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Replace-by-Fee is particularly important when investigating a missing mempool transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Imagine you send 0.01 BTC with a fee that later turns out to be too low.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Your wallet may create a replacement transaction using the same input but a higher fee. If the replacement satisfies the applicable relay rules, nodes can remove the old transaction and accept the replacement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The result can look like this:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 650px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Stage&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Transaction&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Status&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;1&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Unconfirmed&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;2&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Higher-fee replacement&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Removed/replaced&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Waiting for confirmation&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What About CPFP?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Child Pays for Parent, or CPFP&lt;/strong&gt;, is another mechanism used to help accelerate an unconfirmed transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of replacing the original transaction, a new transaction spends an output from the unconfirmed transaction and attaches a higher fee. Miners can consider the combined fee economics of the parent and child transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;CPFP is particularly useful when the recipient controls an output from the pending transaction and wants to help get the package confirmed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Importantly, CPFP does not mean the original transaction has been cancelled. It is a way of encouraging confirmation of the transaction package.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Does a Bitcoin Transaction Disappear From One Explorer but Not Another?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This can happen because different services observe different nodes and relay paths.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin does not maintain one global mempool database. Each node maintains its own local mempool, subject to its own policies and configuration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Therefore, seeing a transaction disappear from one mempool explorer does not automatically prove that every Bitcoin node has forgotten it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For that reason, a transaction ID should be checked against more than one reliable source when the status is unclear.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Should You Do If Your Bitcoin Transaction Disappears?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Stay calm and follow a simple checklist.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Step 1: Check the Transaction ID&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Search the transaction ID in a reputable Bitcoin block explorer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Step 2: Check Confirmations&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction has a block height and confirmations, it was confirmed. The fact that it no longer appears in the mempool is normal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Step 3: Look for a Replacement&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your wallet supports RBF, check whether it created a replacement transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Step 4: Check the Fee&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Compare the transaction's fee rate with the fee environment around the time it was broadcast. Bitcoin fees are based on transaction size and competition for block space, not simply on how much BTC is being transferred. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Step 5: Check Your Wallet&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Your wallet may need to rescan or rebroadcast the transaction. The exact process depends on the wallet you use.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Step 6: Do Not Double-Spend Manually Without Understanding the State&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sending another transaction immediately can create unnecessary confusion if the original transaction is still alive somewhere on the network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Always determine what happened to the original inputs first.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Is a Bitcoin Transaction Permanently Lost If It Leaves the Mempool?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not necessarily.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The word "disappeared" can sound much more serious than it actually is.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A transaction can disappear because it was confirmed. It can disappear because it was replaced. It can disappear because a node evicted it. Or it can disappear because it reached that node's configured mempool expiry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;None of those situations automatically means that Bitcoin itself has been destroyed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The blockchain is what ultimately matters for confirmed ownership and spending history.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Pending vs Dropped vs Confirmed Bitcoin Transactions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 720px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Status&lt;/th&gt;

&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Can it change?&lt;/th&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Transaction is unconfirmed and may be in one or more mempools.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Yes.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;It may be rebroadcast if still valid.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Another transaction superseded the original under replacement rules.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;The replacement may confirm.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Confirmed&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Transaction is included in a block.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;It becomes part of blockchain history.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What happens if a Bitcoin transaction disappears from the mempool?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It usually means the transaction was confirmed, replaced, or removed from a node's mempool. It does not automatically mean the Bitcoin was lost.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can a Bitcoin transaction disappear after 14 days?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. Bitcoin Core's default mempool expiry is currently 336 hours, or about 14 days. However, this is a node policy setting and transactions can be removed earlier for other reasons. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does a dropped Bitcoin transaction mean it was cancelled?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not exactly. A dropped transaction was removed from a node's mempool, but it was not necessarily "cancelled" by the Bitcoin network. You should first verify whether it was confirmed or replaced elsewhere.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can a dropped Bitcoin transaction be rebroadcast?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Potentially, yes. If the transaction remains valid and its inputs have not been spent by another confirmed transaction, it may be possible to broadcast it again.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can an RBF transaction make the original transaction disappear?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes. A valid replacement can cause the original transaction to be removed from a node's mempool. BIP 125 defines the opt-in RBF mechanism. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Will my Bitcoin come back if the transaction is dropped?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction never confirmed and the relevant inputs remain unspent, the funds can generally become spendable again. Your wallet may need to update or rescan before displaying the correct available balance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is a Bitcoin transaction that disappeared from the mempool gone forever?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. A transaction leaving a mempool does not by itself determine its final status. Check the blockchain and look for confirmation or a replacement transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Should I send the Bitcoin again if the transaction disappeared?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not immediately. First determine whether the original transaction confirmed, was replaced, or was genuinely dropped. Sending again without checking can create unnecessary complications.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;A Bitcoin transaction disappearing from the mempool does not automatically mean your Bitcoin is gone.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The transaction may have been confirmed, replaced through RBF, removed because of mempool pressure, or aged out of a node's mempool. Bitcoin Core currently uses a default mempool expiry of 336 hours, or 14 days, although operators can configure this policy and transactions can leave the mempool for other reasons. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The safest approach is simple: &lt;strong&gt;check the transaction ID, verify confirmations, look for a replacement, and only then decide what to do next.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The mempool is temporary. The Bitcoin blockchain is what ultimately records confirmed transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

As co-founder and executive chairman of MicroStrategy Inc., he led his company in adopting a strategy that emphasizes substantial investments in bitcoin as part of its balance sheet. Since initiating this approach in August 2020, MicroStrategy has accumulated thousands of bitcoins.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: Georgia, serif; font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: Georgia, serif; font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Sale Details and Market Reaction&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;span style="font-family: Georgia, serif;"&gt;&lt;div style="font-weight: bold;"&gt;The recent sale raises questions regarding market timing and motivations behind divesting such a significant amount. Given that price fluctuations are common in cryptocurrencies — with Bitcoin recently hovering around critical support levels — many analysts will scrutinize this move closely.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="font-weight: bold;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="font-weight: bold;"&gt;If confirmed that MicroStrategy executed this transaction through typical trading mechanisms, it could imply strategic reallocation or risk management decisions intended to bolster liquidity or capitalize on favorable market conditions. Conversely, it may also signify concerns over longer-term price trajectories amid ongoing regulatory scrutiny affecting digital assets globally.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="font-weight: bold;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Potential Industry Context and Broader Implications&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;b&gt;This sale occurs during a period characterized by heightened volatility across crypto markets due to regulatory developments ranging from proposed legislation in various countries aiming to regulate digital asset transactions more stringently. Furthermore, macroeconomic factors like inflation rates and monetary policy adjustments continue influencing investor sentiment towards riskier assets like cryptocurrencies.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Previous Related Events&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;b&gt;A Round-Up on Cryptocurrency Pricing Trends: Over the past year alone, we have seen massive fluctuations with bitcoin peaking near its all-time high before retreating significantly amid profit-taking behaviors by investors.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Securities Implications for Other Investors&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;h3 style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Potential Ripple Effect:&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;b&gt;The unloading of such large quantities can lead other holders—especially institutional players—to reevaluate their positions considering how crucial confidence plays into sustaining bullish runs amid bearish sentiments dominating parts of investor psychology right now.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div&gt;&lt;h2 style="background: 0px 0px rgb(15, 22, 34);
