    <title>Bill Gates Warns AI Is Advancing Faster Than Expected — and the Bioweapon Risk Is Part of the Concern</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEg5j6KScXncdEFXb-YrnxsNRQKHO4mg5CWw8mHgB7IRjvP5wIXwNCPmh768pTpQQ-odOixQgRapcpBvVyFx-LcKH4LXbPGqreHnSwh7yx59dSy9-fjDQR0aBddEtdS4apoR-u0j9TvfbRBSFowwSx_xb_e0lXX9EEkLtnFD5ouFNwuolnkmjT5hz_H0nC1R/s1672/bill-gates-ai-biosecurity-risk.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="AI neural network and molecular graphics representing artificial intelligence biosecurity risks" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEg5j6KScXncdEFXb-YrnxsNRQKHO4mg5CWw8mHgB7IRjvP5wIXwNCPmh768pTpQQ-odOixQgRapcpBvVyFx-LcKH4LXbPGqreHnSwh7yx59dSy9-fjDQR0aBddEtdS4apoR-u0j9TvfbRBSFowwSx_xb_e0lXX9EEkLtnFD5ouFNwuolnkmjT5hz_H0nC1R/w400-h225/bill-gates-ai-biosecurity-risk.jpg.png" title="Bill Gates Warns About AI and Biosecurity Risks" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: small;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Artificial intelligence is moving faster than Bill Gates expected — and the Microsoft co-founder says one of the biggest concerns isn't what AI can build for legitimate users, but what happens when the technology reaches people who want to cause harm.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gates has become increasingly vocal about the risks surrounding increasingly capable AI systems. In a recent interview with Reuters, he warned that governments should pay closer attention to the possibility of AI being misused for biological attacks and said countries should consider monitoring AI's ability to create molecules and potentially assist with biological attacks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;That does not mean AI has created a biological weapon, or that an AI-driven biological attack is currently underway.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The concern is more straightforward — and potentially more difficult to solve. If AI continues becoming more capable, could it lower some of the expertise barriers that have historically made dangerous biological work difficult?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is the question Gates wants policymakers to start addressing before the technology advances even further.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI's Rapid Progress Is Changing the Risk Conversation&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For years, discussions around artificial intelligence focused mainly on productivity, automation and the possibility of machines eventually outperforming humans at specific tasks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That conversation has changed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Modern AI systems can already write software, analyze large amounts of information, interact with digital tools and perform increasingly complicated multi-step tasks. Gates has pointed to recent AI security incidents involving models interacting with real-world websites during &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/justin-sun-says-tron-targets-quantum.html"&gt;cybersecurity&lt;/a&gt; evaluations as evidence that the technology is moving into territory that deserves much closer attention.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The concern isn't that AI suddenly becomes malicious.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It's that increasingly capable systems can make powerful capabilities easier to access.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important when discussing biological risks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Gates Is Worried About Bioweapons&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Biological research is an enormous field, ranging from medicine and vaccine development to agriculture and disease research.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The same scientific knowledge can also be misused.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gates told Reuters that countries should monitor AI's ability to create molecules and carry out biological attacks. He has argued that such monitoring could focus on particularly dangerous capabilities without necessarily restricting the wider technology industry.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The underlying concern is about &lt;strong&gt;access to expertise&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A highly trained scientist can spend years developing specialized knowledge. An increasingly capable AI system can potentially explain complicated scientific concepts, organize information and assist with technical problem-solving much faster.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not eliminate the physical or experimental barriers involved in biological research.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But it could potentially reduce some informational barriers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And that is enough to make the issue worth taking seriously.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI Does Not Automatically Create a Bioweapon&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This point needs to be clear.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no evidence that an AI system has independently developed a biological weapon.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gates' warning is about potential misuse.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Creating a biological weapon involves far more than obtaining information. Real-world biological work can require specialized facilities, equipment, materials, expertise and experimentation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI does not magically remove those requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;What AI could potentially change is how quickly someone can learn, plan or navigate complicated technical information.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why the debate is increasingly moving away from asking only what an &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/kalshi-sells-112b-of-equity-to-71.html"&gt;AI model&lt;/a&gt; can say and toward asking what a sufficiently capable AI system could help someone actually accomplish.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Speed Mismatch Could Become the Biggest Problem&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where Gates' warning becomes broader than biology.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Technology can improve in months.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Government policy can take years.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;International agreements can take even longer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That mismatch creates a difficult window in which technology can advance faster than the systems responsible for managing its risks — &lt;strong&gt;and that gap could be the most dangerous part of the story.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gates has called for international cooperation on AI governance and is seeking discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping about global approaches to managing advanced AI risks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An AI model developed in one country can be used somewhere else.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A cyberattack can cross several jurisdictions in seconds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Information generated by an AI system can spread around the world almost immediately.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Regulation doesn't move that quickly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Cybersecurity Warning Is Already More Concrete&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Biological misuse is a forward-looking concern, but AI-assisted cyberattacks provide a more immediate example of why Gates is worried.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Reuters reported that Gates pointed to recent incidents in which AI systems from major companies were able to interact with and attack real-world websites during controlled cybersecurity evaluations. Gates described these incidents as deeply concerning.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That matters because it demonstrates an important transition.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI isn't simply generating text about a task.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It can increasingly interact with digital environments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The more autonomy these systems receive, the more important permission controls, monitoring and human oversight become.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A system that can write code is one thing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A system that can write code, execute it, access tools and make decisions independently is something else.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Same Technology Can Help and Hurt&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is an uncomfortable paradox at the center of the AI-and-biology debate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI could become extremely useful for medicine.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Researchers can use machine learning to study diseases, analyze biological structures, discover potential drug candidates and accelerate scientific research.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those are precisely the kinds of applications society wants to encourage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The challenge is preventing useful capabilities from becoming dangerous capabilities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blanket ban could sacrifice enormous benefits.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Doing nothing could leave governments unprepared for misuse.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The likely answer will involve more targeted safeguards around high-risk capabilities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Could Those Safeguards Look Like?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Governments and AI developers could focus on several layers of protection.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Stronger evaluations for models with advanced biological capabilities&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Controlled access to particularly sensitive functionality&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Monitoring for suspicious or high-risk patterns&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Closer cooperation between AI companies and scientific institutions&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;International coordination on advanced AI safety standards&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The exact structure remains an open question.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the direction of the debate is becoming clearer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Expertise Barrier Is What Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the most important questions isn't whether AI can perform a task entirely on its own.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It's whether AI can make that task substantially easier for someone who previously couldn't perform it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That's a very different threshold.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If an AI system can explain complicated scientific concepts, identify relevant research, organize information and help a user work through difficult problems, the technology could potentially shrink the gap between experts and non-experts.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For normal scientific research, that could be transformative.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For malicious applications, it could be dangerous.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why AI safety increasingly focuses on capability thresholds rather than simply judging models by whether they produce harmful text.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Gates Wants Governments to Move Earlier&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Gates' message is essentially about preparation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;He believes governments should not wait for a major incident before deciding how &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/japan-eyes-blockchain-for-real-time.html"&gt;advanced AI&lt;/a&gt; should be monitored.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Reuters reported that Gates is seeking discussions with Xi and wants stronger international cooperation on AI governance. He has also argued for new institutions capable of dealing with AI risks in ways comparable to international frameworks used in other high-risk areas.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The challenge will be finding rules that are strong enough to reduce serious risks without slowing legitimate AI research and innovation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That balance won't be easy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And it becomes harder as models become more capable.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What This Means for the AI Industry&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For AI companies, the debate could lead to greater scrutiny around models capable of advanced scientific reasoning.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Developers may face pressure to demonstrate that powerful systems have been tested against high-risk biological and cybersecurity scenarios before being widely deployed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For governments, the challenge is different.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They need enough technical understanding to identify genuinely dangerous capabilities without creating regulations that quickly become obsolete.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For researchers, the issue is even more complicated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The same AI system that could help discover a new treatment could potentially be misused for a completely different purpose.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means AI safety cannot be separated entirely from scientific safety.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bill Gates isn't saying that AI has become a bioweapon machine.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;His warning is about what could happen if AI capabilities continue advancing rapidly while governments and security systems struggle to keep pace.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The biological threat is only one part of a much larger conversation that includes cyberattacks, misinformation, job disruption and the increasing autonomy of AI systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The key issue is speed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI capabilities can improve extraordinarily quickly, while laws, institutions and international agreements move much more slowly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a dangerous gap.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The question policymakers now face is not simply &lt;strong&gt;how powerful AI can become&lt;/strong&gt;, but &lt;strong&gt;how much power society is willing to give it before the safeguards are ready.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The goal isn't to stop useful AI.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It's to make sure the technology's most powerful capabilities don't become easier to misuse faster than society can respond — &lt;strong&gt;before the technology moves another step faster than the rules designed to control it, because waiting for the first incident may mean waiting too long.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;This article discusses potential AI-related risks based on public comments by Bill Gates and reporting from Reuters. It does not claim that AI has created a biological weapon or that a specific biological attack is underway. This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute financial, investment, medical or legal advice.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Why Is Bitcoin Price Rising So Fast Right Now? The Real Reasons Behind BTC’s Rally</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

  &lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhv9cHRqJ-fUBRGFpHaH-eoBMkC_frzljKU-ALoCI9q2mJwh4ux4RxY_mPfY8yiEpqz3qu5XKmOlx7BwOQSBxd0nd_LB8U274obA0cHC3NoLli7OPWgIh09OZlMbpBFiTbcrksBd-Awq6cd44LX8ttABJcTbtFjD3QCS8fFTawhbm7UVAeE3kSpU_qY3Y_e/s1672/bitcoin-price-rising-fast-btc-rally-2026.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin price rising as institutional demand and ETF inflows support BTC rally" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhv9cHRqJ-fUBRGFpHaH-eoBMkC_frzljKU-ALoCI9q2mJwh4ux4RxY_mPfY8yiEpqz3qu5XKmOlx7BwOQSBxd0nd_LB8U274obA0cHC3NoLli7OPWgIh09OZlMbpBFiTbcrksBd-Awq6cd44LX8ttABJcTbtFjD3QCS8fFTawhbm7UVAeE3kSpU_qY3Y_e/w400-h225/bitcoin-price-rising-fast-btc-rally-2026.jpg.png" title="Why Is Bitcoin Price Rising So Fast Right Now?" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;Bitcoin has once again become one of the most watched assets in global financial markets. After a sharp recovery during August, investors are asking a familiar question: &lt;/span&gt;&lt;strong style="font-size: large;"&gt;Why is Bitcoin price rising so fast right now?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The answer is more complicated than simply saying that investors are buying Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;BTC gained roughly 25% during August, making it one of Bitcoin’s strongest monthly performances in recent years. The cryptocurrency moved toward the $80,000 area before pulling back and trading around the $77,000–$78,000 zone in early September.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Several forces have been working together: renewed institutional demand, Bitcoin ETF flows, changing expectations around U.S. monetary policy, short-covering, improving market sentiment and a broader shift in how investors view Bitcoin as a financial asset.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But there is an important catch. The same macroeconomic environment that helped Bitcoin recover could also limit its next move.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin’s Recent Rally in Simple Terms&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin entered August under significant pressure. VanEck reported that BTC was trading around $63,500 in mid-August, while long-term holders had reduced their holdings by hundreds of thousands of BTC over the preceding 30 days.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The market then changed direction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;As Bitcoin moved higher, momentum traders returned, short positions were forced to close and spot buying became increasingly important. Bitfinex reported that &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/tether-brings-offline-ai-translation-to.html"&gt;Bitcoin’s &lt;/a&gt;August advance was increasingly supported by spot buying rather than excessive leverage, while U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded almost $1 billion of net inflows during the week covered in its analysis.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That combination matters.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A rally supported by actual spot demand can be more durable than one driven almost entirely by leveraged futures positions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;1. Institutional Demand Is One of the Biggest Drivers&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The biggest structural change in the Bitcoin market is the growing role of institutional investors.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin is no longer traded only by individual crypto enthusiasts. Asset managers, hedge funds, family offices and other professional investors can gain exposure through regulated investment products, including U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That creates a different type of demand.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;When investors buy shares of a spot Bitcoin ETF, the underlying fund structure can require exposure to actual Bitcoin. Large and sustained inflows can therefore contribute to buying pressure in the underlying market.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin ETF activity has consequently become one of the most important indicators traders watch when trying to understand BTC’s price.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Recent market data showed that ETF demand remained significant even as Bitcoin moved toward the $80,000 area. Bitfinex said U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded almost $1 billion in net inflows in the week discussed in its latest Bitcoin analysis.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;2. August’s Rally Created a Momentum Effect&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Markets rarely move in a straight line.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;When an asset breaks higher after a prolonged period of weakness, traders who were positioned for further declines may be forced to exit their positions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This can create a &lt;strong&gt;short squeeze&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin’s August recovery appears to have benefited partly from this dynamic. As BTC moved through important technical levels, bearish traders faced increasing pressure.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The result can become self-reinforcing:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Price rises → shorts lose money → shorts close positions → buying increases → price rises further.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;However, short squeezes are normally temporary. Once forced buying disappears, the market needs genuine demand to continue moving higher.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is why the quality of Bitcoin’s spot demand is more important than the size of a single day’s price move.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;3. Investors Are Watching the Federal Reserve Closely&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin is increasingly sensitive to expectations around U.S. interest rates.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;When investors expect easier monetary policy, risk assets can become more attractive because lower rates reduce the relative appeal of cash and some fixed-income investments.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin does not pay a traditional yield, so liquidity and interest-rate expectations can have a major influence on its valuation.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The current environment, however, is unusual.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Markets are simultaneously dealing with inflation concerns, higher energy prices and uncertainty over the Federal Reserve’s next move. Reuters reported on September 3 that markets were assigning roughly a 60% probability to a September Fed rate hike, up from about 40% a week earlier. U.S. and German bond yields had also recently moved lower before the latest positioning changes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That means Bitcoin’s rally cannot simply be described as a “Fed-cut trade.”&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Instead, traders are constantly adjusting positions based on incoming inflation, employment, bond-yield and central-bank signals.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;4. Bitcoin Is Benefiting From a Broader Risk-Asset Repricing&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin does not trade in isolation.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Institutional investors increasingly consider BTC alongside equities, commodities, bonds, currencies and other alternative assets.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;When global investors become more willing to take risk, money can flow into higher-volatility assets.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The opposite is also true.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is why Bitcoin can sometimes rally alongside stocks and other risk assets, while at other times it behaves more defensively.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Recent global markets have been highly sensitive to economic data, bond yields, the dollar and geopolitical developments. Investors have also been watching U.S. payrolls data and Federal Reserve officials for clues about future interest-rate policy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For Bitcoin traders, these events can matter almost as much as crypto-specific news.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;5. Limited Bitcoin Supply Makes Demand Shocks More Powerful&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin has a maximum supply of 21 million coins.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That does not mean Bitcoin automatically goes up whenever demand increases. Price still depends on how many existing holders are willing to sell.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But when demand suddenly increases while available selling supply is relatively limited, the market can move quickly.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is one reason Bitcoin rallies can appear much faster than moves in traditional currencies or large-cap stocks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A relatively small change in marginal demand can produce a disproportionately large price movement when liquidity is thin.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That effect becomes particularly noticeable during periods of strong institutional buying.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;6. The Market Has Become More Sensitive to ETF Flows&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;One of the clearest differences between today’s &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitcoins-4-year-cycle-may-be-changing.html"&gt;Bitcoin market&lt;/a&gt; and earlier cycles is the importance of daily fund flows.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Traders now monitor whether money is entering or leaving spot Bitcoin ETFs almost every trading day.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;When inflows remain strong, investors may interpret that as evidence of sustained demand.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;When outflows accelerate, the interpretation changes quickly.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Recent data already shows why investors should avoid assuming that every rally will continue indefinitely. Reports from early September indicated that ETF demand had begun to cool after August’s powerful advance.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In other words, the Bitcoin story is no longer simply “institutions are buying.”&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The more useful question is:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Are institutions still buying at a rate strong enough to support the current price?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;7. Bitcoin’s Rally Is Also Attracting Momentum Traders&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Once Bitcoin starts moving higher, attention returns to the market.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Search interest increases. Financial media coverage expands. Traders who missed the initial move begin looking for entry points.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This creates another feedback loop:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Higher prices → more attention → more trading activity → more momentum buying.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That does not necessarily mean the rally is irrational.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Momentum is a normal part of financial markets.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But it can make the market more fragile. If sentiment changes suddenly, the same traders who chased the rally can become sellers.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is why Bitcoin can rise thousands of dollars in a short period and then give back part of that move just as quickly.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Is Bitcoin Rising Because of the Halving?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The Bitcoin halving remains part of the long-term supply story, but it should not be used as the sole explanation for every 2026 price movement.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin’s block subsidy has already been reduced by previous halvings, meaning the rate at which new BTC enters circulation is much lower than it was in Bitcoin’s early years.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;However, market cycles have become more complicated.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Institutional flows, ETFs, derivatives, global liquidity, interest rates, regulation and macroeconomic conditions now play a much larger role in price discovery.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is why investors should be cautious about using an old four-year-cycle model as a perfect timing tool.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Bitcoin Could Keep Rising&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;There are several factors that could support Bitcoin if the current recovery continues.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Continued ETF Inflows&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs continue attracting substantial capital, that could provide a persistent source of demand.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Strong Institutional Adoption&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;More traditional financial institutions treating Bitcoin as a legitimate portfolio asset could expand the investor base.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Falling Real Yields&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If inflation cools and interest-rate expectations become more supportive, Bitcoin could benefit from improving liquidity conditions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Strong Spot Demand&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A rally supported by spot buying rather than excessive leverage is generally healthier because it reduces the risk of a sudden liquidation cascade.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Improving Crypto Regulation&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Greater regulatory clarity could encourage additional institutional participation, although regulatory developments can also create short-term volatility.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;But There Are Serious Risks Too&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin’s recent rally does not eliminate the possibility of another correction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In fact, several warning signs are already visible.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;1. Federal Reserve Uncertainty&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If inflation remains stubborn or energy prices push inflation expectations higher, the Federal Reserve could maintain a tighter policy stance for longer than investors expect.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;2. ETF Outflows&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If institutional ETF demand reverses, one of the strongest sources of recent market support could weaken.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;3. Bond Yields and the Dollar&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Higher real yields and a stronger U.S. dollar can make speculative assets less attractive.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitfinex has highlighted the 10-year real yield as an important macro variable for the Bitcoin market.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;4. Overheated Sentiment&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;When investors become convinced that prices can only go higher, leverage can build quickly.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is often when corrections become more violent.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;5. Technical Resistance&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin’s move toward $80,000 has already shown that psychological price levels can attract significant selling.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Recent market reports described BTC as struggling to establish sustained support above the $80,000 area.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;So, Why Is Bitcoin Price Rising So Fast Right Now?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The simplest answer is that &lt;strong&gt;several sources of demand are arriving at the same time.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin’s August recovery was supported by a combination of institutional participation, ETF inflows, spot buying, momentum and short covering. At the same time, traders have been reassessing the outlook for interest rates, liquidity and global risk assets.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But calling the move a guaranteed new bull market would be premature.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;As of early September 2026, Bitcoin is still dealing with a complicated macroeconomic backdrop. BTC recently approached $80,000 but was trading back around the upper-$70,000 range, while investors continued watching &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/trump-1-coin-is-here-us-mints-new.html"&gt;ETF&lt;/a&gt; flows, employment data, Treasury yields and Federal Reserve policy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The next major move may therefore depend less on whether Bitcoin can produce another one-day surge and more on whether &lt;strong&gt;real demand continues after the initial momentum fades.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Bitcoin Investors Should Watch Next&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Anyone trying to understand where BTC goes next should watch five things closely:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ol&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF net flows&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Federal Reserve interest-rate expectations&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;U.S. Treasury yields and the dollar&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Bitcoin spot volume versus futures leverage&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;BTC’s ability to hold important support levels after rallies&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ol&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;These indicators provide a more useful picture than looking at the Bitcoin price alone.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin is rising rapidly because the market is experiencing a powerful combination of institutional demand, renewed spot buying, momentum and changing macro expectations.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The introduction of large regulated investment vehicles has also made Bitcoin’s market structure very different from previous cycles.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But the rally is not risk-free.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;ETF flows can reverse, interest-rate expectations can change and geopolitical or economic shocks can quickly push investors away from risk assets.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For that reason, the better question is not simply &lt;strong&gt;“How high can Bitcoin go?”&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It is:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;“Is the demand behind the Bitcoin rally strong enough to survive the next macroeconomic shock?”&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If institutional and spot demand remain strong, Bitcoin could continue testing higher levels. If those flows weaken while yields and monetary-policy expectations move against risk assets, the cryptocurrency could face another sharp correction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin remains one of the most volatile major financial assets in the world—and that is unlikely to change anytime soon.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Why is Bitcoin price rising so fast?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin’s recent strength has been driven by a combination of institutional demand, spot Bitcoin ETF activity, spot buying, momentum trading and short covering. Macro expectations around interest rates and liquidity are also influencing the market.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is Bitcoin still bullish in September 2026?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The market remains constructive after August’s strong rally, but the outlook is not certain. Bitcoin has pulled back from the $80,000 area, while ETF flows and Federal Reserve policy remain important risks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Are Bitcoin ETFs causing the price to rise?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;ETF flows are an important source of Bitcoin demand, but they are not the only factor. Spot market demand, derivatives positioning, macroeconomic conditions and investor sentiment also influence BTC.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can Bitcoin fall even after a strong rally?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Yes. Bitcoin can experience large corrections even during broader uptrends. A strong rally can also increase leverage and speculative positioning, making sudden pullbacks more severe.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What should investors watch to understand Bitcoin’s next move?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;ETF flows, Federal Reserve expectations, Treasury yields, the U.S. dollar, spot trading volume and futures leverage are among the most useful indicators to monitor.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is Bitcoin’s four-year cycle still reliable?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Bitcoin’s historical four-year pattern remains useful as a reference, but it should not be treated as a precise forecasting mechanism. Institutional adoption, ETFs, macroeconomic conditions and changing market structure have made Bitcoin cycles more complex.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>How Supporters Turned the Marmot Project Into a Crypto Fundraising Story</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi-tqwM502cyN2liIrPhOYMMh7aILKJtV1mEYI3sEUPBbII46FcuHFAZzVxmuKHJIRCgnqYsj83FzZbmUCG21M7X3snzg0Wt8HC98ePsEy_jC2ln8Dz_tc_2LjnAy7S5ck3rZWKwLSHnQNfcBXdjZH-Tvw9uYKgqFBOtYKyYsgyq7K8bTHqNzkGLLYvrA9s/s1672/marmot-crypto-fundraising-onlymarms-solana.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Yellow-bellied marmot representing the ONLYMARMS crypto fundraising campaign for long-term scientific research" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi-tqwM502cyN2liIrPhOYMMh7aILKJtV1mEYI3sEUPBbII46FcuHFAZzVxmuKHJIRCgnqYsj83FzZbmUCG21M7X3snzg0Wt8HC98ePsEy_jC2ln8Dz_tc_2LjnAy7S5ck3rZWKwLSHnQNfcBXdjZH-Tvw9uYKgqFBOtYKyYsgyq7K8bTHqNzkGLLYvrA9s/w400-h225/marmot-crypto-fundraising-onlymarms-solana.jpg.png" title="ONLYMARMS Crypto Helps Support Marmot Research" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A scientific project studying marmots for more than six decades probably wasn't expected to become a cryptocurrency story. Yet that is exactly what happened in 2026, when an unusual fundraising campaign around Colorado's yellow-bellied marmots caught the attention of an online crypto community.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Supporters independently created a Solana-based meme coin called &lt;strong&gt;$ONLYMARMS&lt;/strong&gt;. The token was not originally launched by the scientists themselves, but its creator fees were directed toward the marmot research effort. Combined with other donations and fundraising, the broader campaign has now raised &lt;strong&gt;more than $100,000&lt;/strong&gt;, according to recent reporting. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The story is unusual, but it also highlights something more serious: the researchers are trying to keep a long-running scientific record alive at a time when reliable research funding has become harder to secure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is the Marmot Research Project?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Marmot Research Project is a long-term scientific study of yellow-bellied marmots in Colorado. Researchers have been following the animals since &lt;strong&gt;1962&lt;/strong&gt;, building one of the longest-running datasets on a wild mammal population.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The researchers study subjects including animal behavior, reproduction, survival, body condition and how marmots respond to environmental changes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Long-term studies like this are valuable because individual years can tell scientists only so much. Decades of continuous observations can reveal changes that are difficult to see in a short research project.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That continuity was put under pressure by funding problems, forcing the team to experiment with unconventional ways of reaching potential supporters.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Did OnlyMarms Start?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the most unusual fundraising ideas was &lt;strong&gt;OnlyMarms&lt;/strong&gt;, a social-media campaign built around the OnlyFans platform.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Despite the name of the platform, the content was not sexual. Instead, the researchers posted photographs and videos of marmots living in their natural environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The idea was partly humorous, but the underlying objective was straightforward: attract attention to the research and raise money to keep the project operating.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The campaign initially generated only a relatively small amount compared with the project's longer-term needs. Then &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-crypto-scam-transactions-be-traced.html"&gt;crypto&lt;/a&gt; supporters discovered the story.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Where Did $ONLYMARMS Come From?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The cryptocurrency was &lt;strong&gt;not created by the Marmot Research Project itself&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Outside supporters of the research created a marmot-themed meme coin on the &lt;strong&gt;Solana blockchain&lt;/strong&gt;. The token became known as &lt;strong&gt;$ONLYMARMS&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important. A cryptocurrency using the name or imagery of a real-world project does not automatically mean that the organization behind that project issued or endorsed it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In this case, however, the relationship developed further when project co-lead &lt;strong&gt;Julien Martin&lt;/strong&gt; became involved with the creator-fee arrangement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Can a Meme Coin Fund Scientific Research?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The basic mechanism is different from a traditional donation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When people trade a token using a platform that distributes creator fees, those fees can generate revenue. In the $ONLYMARMS arrangement, creator-related fees were directed toward the marmot research effort.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means the research team does not need the token itself to remain permanently valuable in order for the arrangement to have generated funding. What matters for the fundraising mechanism is the activity that produces the relevant fees.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Much Money Has the Campaign Raised?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The figures have changed as the campaign developed, which is why it is important to distinguish between different sources of funding.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Earlier reporting in August said the marmot-themed &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/binance-launches-physically-settled.html"&gt;cryptocurrency&lt;/a&gt; had generated more than &lt;strong&gt;$88,000&lt;/strong&gt; in two weeks. Combined with outside donations and other fundraising, the project had already crossed the $100,000 mark. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;More recent reporting continues to describe the overall fundraising effort as having brought in &lt;strong&gt;more than $100,000&lt;/strong&gt;, including cryptocurrency, donations and the OnlyMarms campaign. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is the safer figure to use for the broader campaign because the token's trading activity and fee generation can change over time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Researchers Are Still Aiming Much Higher&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Even a six-figure fundraising result does not solve the project's long-term funding problem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Project co-lead Julien Martin has said that reaching approximately &lt;strong&gt;$300,000&lt;/strong&gt; would be enough to fund a PhD student working on the project for four years.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That target puts the crypto fundraising story into perspective.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;More than $100,000 is meaningful money for a scientific project, but it is not the same as having a stable, multi-year funding source.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The researchers therefore continue to face the broader challenge of keeping a decades-long scientific dataset alive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Fat Marmot Week Took the Story Beyond Crypto&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The cryptocurrency was not the only unusual idea to emerge from the marmot project's fundraising push.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In August 2026, the researchers launched the first-ever &lt;strong&gt;Fat Marmot Week&lt;/strong&gt;, a public competition inspired by Alaska's better-known Fat Bear Week.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Eight yellow-bellied marmots competed as they built up body fat before their winter hibernation. Members of the public could vote for their favorite animal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The event ran from &lt;strong&gt;August 24 through August 29&lt;/strong&gt; and attracted more than &lt;strong&gt;23,000 votes&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A six-year-old marmot named &lt;strong&gt;Dawn&lt;/strong&gt; won both the mass-gain and popular-vote categories. Dawn reached roughly &lt;strong&gt;6 kilograms (13.2 pounds)&lt;/strong&gt;, which researchers described as exceptionally large for the species. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The contest was entertaining, but the science behind it is serious. Marmots spend the summer building up fat reserves before spending months underground during hibernation. Having enough stored energy can be critical to surviving the winter. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Fat Marmot Week also gave the researchers another way to bring public attention to a scientific project that might otherwise be known mainly inside academic circles.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Does Long-Term Marmot Research Matter?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It may be easy to dismiss marmot research as a niche scientific subject. But long-term ecological datasets can provide information about how wildlife responds to environmental changes over time.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Researchers can compare conditions from one decade with observations from another. That can help scientists examine changes in reproduction, survival, body weight, seasonal behavior and population dynamics.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is particularly relevant as weather patterns and snow conditions change in mountain environments.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A single year of observations cannot provide the same historical context as a dataset stretching back more than 60 years.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Is $ONLYMARMS an Investment?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where readers should separate the &lt;strong&gt;fundraising story&lt;/strong&gt; from the &lt;strong&gt;investment question&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;$ONLYMARMS is a community-created meme coin. Its association with scientific research does not make it a safe investment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Meme coins can experience extreme price swings, limited liquidity and rapidly changing market interest. A token can fall sharply even while its underlying charitable or community purpose remains unchanged.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In other words, supporting the research and buying the token are not necessarily the same decision.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Someone who wants to support the Marmot Research Project should understand exactly where their money is going rather than assuming that buying a speculative token is equivalent to making a direct donation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Solana Memecoins Can Move Extremely Fast&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader Solana memecoin market also helps explain why caution is necessary.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Galaxy Research reported in 2025 that the median token holding time on Solana was roughly &lt;strong&gt;100 seconds&lt;/strong&gt;, down from about 300 seconds a year earlier. The research described an increasingly fast, speculative trading environment. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That figure is a &lt;strong&gt;broader Solana market statistic&lt;/strong&gt;. It does not mean $ONLYMARMS holders specifically keep their tokens for 100 seconds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The more useful takeaway is that Solana's memecoin market can be highly short-term and speculative. That makes it especially important to distinguish token trading from the research project's actual fundraising.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the $100,000 Figure Does Not Equal Market Capitalization&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Another common mistake would be to treat the amount raised for the research as the same thing as the market value of $ONLYMARMS.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They are different measurements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;/table&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction matters because a token's market capitalization can change dramatically without changing the amount of money already transferred to a research project.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Did the Scientists Create the Crypto Token?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The token was created independently by supporters of the project.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is one of the most important facts in the entire story because it prevents readers from assuming that the Marmot Research Project launched a cryptocurrency as an official financial product.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The later connection between the token's creator-fee mechanism and the research project is what turned an independently created meme coin into an unexpected fundraising channel.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Story Matters for Crypto&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto has a long history of tokens built around internet jokes, animals and viral communities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;What makes $ONLYMARMS different is the real-world project sitting behind the meme.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of an animal simply being used as a symbol for speculation, the attention surrounding the marmots was connected to an existing scientific effort.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not eliminate the risks associated with the token. But it demonstrates how online communities can sometimes mobilize around causes and turn attention into real-world funding.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why It Matters for Science&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The more important lesson may actually have little to do with cryptocurrency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Scientific projects that depend on long-term observations need stable funding. A viral campaign can produce a burst of attention, but maintaining research for years requires predictable resources.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The marmot project has shown that researchers can reach audiences far outside traditional scientific institutions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;OnlyMarms, $ONLYMARMS and Fat Marmot Week all attracted people who may never have encountered the project through an academic paper or university website.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That exposure could prove valuable even beyond the money raised.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The research team still needs long-term &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/hyperliquid-in-advanced-talks-with.html"&gt;financial support&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The $300,000 target for a four-year PhD position shows that the project requires considerably more than a one-time fundraising boost.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Meanwhile, the researchers have already indicated that &lt;strong&gt;Fat Marmot Week will return in 2027&lt;/strong&gt;, giving the public another opportunity to engage with the animals and the science behind the project. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Whether $ONLYMARMS remains popular in the crypto market is much harder to predict.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Memecoin attention can disappear quickly, and trading activity can change just as fast.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the scientists, the more durable achievement may be the audience they have built around the research.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is $ONLYMARMS?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;$ONLYMARMS is a community-created meme cryptocurrency built on Solana and inspired by the Marmot Research Project.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Did the Marmot Research Project launch $ONLYMARMS?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. Outside supporters independently created the token. The project later became connected to its creator-fee mechanism.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How much money has the marmot fundraising campaign raised?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent reporting says the broader fundraising effort has raised more than $100,000 through a combination of cryptocurrency, donations and the OnlyMarms campaign. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why was $300,000 important?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Project co-lead Julien Martin said reaching around $300,000 could fund a PhD student on the project for four years. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What was Fat Marmot Week?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Fat Marmot Week was a public competition featuring eight yellow-bellied marmots. It ran from August 24 to August 29, 2026, and attracted more than 23,000 votes. Dawn won both the mass-gain and popular-vote categories. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is $ONLYMARMS a safe investment?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No cryptocurrency should be assumed to be safe simply because it supports a real-world cause. $ONLYMARMS is a speculative meme coin and can be highly volatile.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does the token's market value equal the money raised for science?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. Token market capitalization, token price, trading volume and actual funds directed to the research project are separate measurements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The $ONLYMARMS story began with a group of scientists looking for unconventional ways to keep a decades-long marmot study alive. It then took an unexpected turn when online supporters created a Solana meme coin around the project.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader fundraising campaign has now raised more than &lt;strong&gt;$100,000&lt;/strong&gt;, while the researchers continue to pursue much larger and more sustainable funding goals. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Fat Marmot Week added another layer to the story, bringing more than 23,000 public votes into a scientific project that began in 1962. Dawn's victory may have been fun, but the attention it generated helped highlight why long-term ecological research matters. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For crypto, the episode is a reminder that meme coins can occasionally support real-world causes, but their speculative nature should never be ignored.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For science, it offers a different lesson: sometimes an unconventional idea can bring an old research project to an entirely new audience.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The marmot may be the meme, but keeping the science alive is the real story.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Editorial note: This article is for informational purposes only. $ONLYMARMS is a speculative digital asset. Nothing in this article should be interpreted as financial, investment or trading advice.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Hong Kong SFC Flags Star Bridge Capital and SBCFX as Unlicensed — Here’s What Investors Should Know</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

  &lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEinAlhwYX6ywudR71LmtZFsS7mH1iRxHamHb7s-Q_d1EV4BrcDLUwnvIr-XRbqa7Mnb2QXAs5o-burI2HoJ8T7lgrnJFVD-YT9NxhO6BWXtX3JUvdkHQMOoVUkhuUb9Bn6Y5O1i5X3ug8BzJ0tp_8U02nwR6qfLWOYjUUmQJ3eOEL-G4mLG-zssVYT0hPf3/s1672/hong-kong-sfc-star-bridge-capital-sbcfx-warning.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Hong Kong SFC warning about Star Bridge Capital Group and SBCFX" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEinAlhwYX6ywudR71LmtZFsS7mH1iRxHamHb7s-Q_d1EV4BrcDLUwnvIr-XRbqa7Mnb2QXAs5o-burI2HoJ8T7lgrnJFVD-YT9NxhO6BWXtX3JUvdkHQMOoVUkhuUb9Bn6Y5O1i5X3ug8BzJ0tp_8U02nwR6qfLWOYjUUmQJ3eOEL-G4mLG-zssVYT0hPf3/w400-h225/hong-kong-sfc-star-bridge-capital-sbcfx-warning.webp.png" title="Hong Kong SFC Flags Star Bridge Capital and SBCFX" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&amp;nbsp;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Hong Kong’s securities regulator has warned investors about Star Bridge Capital Group and related entities — but being unlicensed in Hong Kong is not the same as being accused of fraud.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has added &lt;strong&gt;SBCFX, Star Bridge Capital Group and related entities&lt;/strong&gt; to its Alert List, warning that the named entities are not licensed or registered by the regulator to conduct regulated activities in Hong Kong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The warning was highlighted by Cointelegraph on August 29 after the regulator identified entities operating under names including &lt;strong&gt;“Star Bridge Capital,” “Star Bridge Capital Group” and “SBCFX.”&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;According to the SFC, the entities named in the alert include &lt;strong&gt;SBCFX, Star Bridge Capital Group, Star Bridge Capital Pty Limited and Topical Wealth International Ltd&lt;/strong&gt;. The regulator also listed the Chinese names &lt;strong&gt;星橋資本&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;星橋資本集團&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The SFC said the entities have never been licensed or registered by the commission to carry out regulated activities in Hong Kong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The regulator’s warning puts the focus on an important issue for online investors: a company may claim regulatory authorization in another jurisdiction while still not being authorized to provide regulated services in Hong Kong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Which Entities Did the SFC Flag?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The SFC’s Alert List identifies several entities connected with the Star Bridge Capital and SBCFX names.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;SBCFX&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Star Bridge Capital Group&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Star Bridge Capital Pty Limited&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Topical Wealth International Ltd&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;星橋資本&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;星橋資本集團&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The SFC also identifies &lt;strong&gt;sbcfx.com&lt;/strong&gt; in its warning.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The regulator maintains an Alert List to warn the public about entities that appear to be operating without the required authorization in Hong Kong and may be targeting &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/trump-announces-biggest-oil-deal-in.html"&gt;investors&lt;/a&gt; there.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What the SFC Is Warning Investors About&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The central issue raised by the regulator is licensing.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The SFC says the named entities are &lt;strong&gt;not licensed or registered to conduct regulated activities in Hong Kong&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That distinction matters because financial regulation is generally jurisdiction-specific. A company may hold authorization in another country, but that does not automatically give it permission to provide regulated financial services in Hong Kong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The SFC has also warned investors about claims that the entities were licensed by the commission. Investors are encouraged to verify a firm's regulatory status through the regulator’s official records rather than relying solely on information published by a trading platform.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For anyone considering an online broker or trading platform, the important question is not simply whether the company mentions a regulator on its website. Investors should determine &lt;strong&gt;which legal entity they are dealing with, which regulator supervises that entity and what activities its licence actually covers.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;SBCFX Lists Regulatory Authorizations in Other Jurisdictions&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The Hong Kong warning should not be interpreted as a finding that every regulatory authorization claimed by entities associated with SBCFX is invalid.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;On its own website, SBCFX says that entities connected with its brand hold regulatory authorizations in other jurisdictions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The company states that &lt;strong&gt;Star Bridge Capital Group Pty Ltd&lt;/strong&gt; is regulated by South Africa’s Financial Sector Conduct Authority under FSP licence &lt;strong&gt;54813&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;SBCFX also identifies &lt;strong&gt;Topical Wealth International Ltd&lt;/strong&gt; as holding a Seychelles Securities Dealer licence, &lt;strong&gt;SD077&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The company’s website additionally references an Australian &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/if-ai-writes-smart-contract-that.html"&gt;Financial Services&lt;/a&gt; Licence, &lt;strong&gt;AFSL 503908&lt;/strong&gt;, in connection with an Australian entity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;These regulatory disclosures are separate from the question of authorization in Hong Kong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The SFC’s position is specifically that the entities identified in its alert are &lt;strong&gt;not licensed or registered by the Hong Kong regulator to conduct regulated activities in the city.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why the Warning Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Regulatory warnings can be particularly important for online trading platforms because investors may have difficulty determining which legal entity actually provides a service.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A brokerage brand can operate through different companies depending on a customer's location, while the website, trading interface and marketing materials may appear almost identical.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That can make it difficult for an investor to determine which company is actually accepting their money, which regulator oversees that company and what protections may be available if something goes wrong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The situation can become even more confusing when a platform references licences from several different countries.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A licence may be genuine and still not authorize a company to provide a particular financial service in every jurisdiction where its website can be accessed.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is why investors should look beyond the brand name and check the &lt;strong&gt;exact legal entity, licence number, regulator, jurisdiction and permitted activities&lt;/strong&gt; before opening an account or depositing funds.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The SFC warns that investors dealing with unlicensed entities may have limited or no protection under Hong Kong’s regulatory framework and could lose their investment.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Being Unlicensed Is Not the Same as Being Accused of Fraud&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The SFC’s warning should also be read carefully.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The regulator has identified the entities as &lt;strong&gt;unlicensed in Hong Kong&lt;/strong&gt;. That is not the same as an official finding that the businesses committed fraud.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The warning concerns authorization to conduct regulated activities in Hong Kong. Any separate allegation involving fraud, criminal conduct, misconduct or investor losses would require independent evidence and confirmation from the appropriate authorities.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For investors, however, the licensing issue alone is significant.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If a platform is not authorized to provide a regulated service in a particular jurisdiction, customers may not have the same protections available when dealing with a properly licensed firm.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Investors Should Check&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The SFC’s warning provides a useful reminder for anyone using online trading platforms.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Before opening an account or sending money, investors should verify several basic details.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The exact legal entity:&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
  Do not rely only on the trading brand. Check which &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bitcoin-knocks-on-50-week-moving.html"&gt;company&lt;/a&gt; will actually provide the service and handle the customer relationship.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The regulator:&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
  Confirm the licence directly through the regulator’s official website rather than relying only on claims made by a broker.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The licence number:&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
  A company name alone is not enough. Check whether the licence number belongs to the same legal entity listed in the platform’s terms and regulatory disclosures.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The permitted activities:&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
  A company may be authorized for certain financial services but not necessarily for every product or service it advertises.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The jurisdiction:&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
  Authorization in one country does not automatically mean a firm is licensed in another.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;These checks are particularly important when dealing with leveraged trading products, where losses can accumulate quickly.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Hong Kong’s Regulatory Status Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Hong Kong has developed a detailed regulatory framework for financial services and virtual-asset activities as it continues to position itself as a major international financial center.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That makes investor protection and action against unauthorized financial businesses an important part of the city’s regulatory system.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The SFC’s Alert List is one of the tools used to warn the public about entities that appear to be operating without the required authorization.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The regulator also encourages investors to verify the status of financial firms through its official records before committing funds.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For online brokers and trading platforms, the message is straightforward: an international website or a reference to an overseas licence is not, by itself, proof that a firm is authorized to provide regulated services in Hong Kong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The SFC’s alert does not, by itself, provide a timetable for what happens next with the named entities.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Instead, it serves as a public notice that the entities identified by the regulator are not authorized to conduct regulated activities in Hong Kong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The companies could respond to the warning, clarify their corporate structure or provide additional information about which legal entities serve customers in different jurisdictions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For investors, the key issue is whether the regulatory status of the relevant entities changes and whether the SFC announces any further action.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Until then, the regulator’s warning gives Hong Kong investors a clear reason to exercise caution and verify the status of any firm before transferring funds.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Lesson for Crypto and Online Trading Users&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Although the SFC warning concerns a financial trading group rather than a cryptocurrency token itself, it highlights a broader issue across the digital-asset and online trading industry.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Platforms can operate internationally, advertise through social media and offer products to customers across multiple jurisdictions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But financial regulation remains largely jurisdiction-specific.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A company that is authorized somewhere else may still require separate approval to offer regulated services in Hong Kong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is why investors should verify the &lt;strong&gt;actual legal entity and local regulatory status&lt;/strong&gt; rather than relying on marketing claims or a platform’s general international presence.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission has placed &lt;strong&gt;SBCFX, Star Bridge Capital Group and related entities&lt;/strong&gt; on its Alert List, saying the named entities are not licensed or registered to conduct regulated activities in Hong Kong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The warning does not by itself establish that the businesses are fraudulent, but it does raise an important regulatory issue for investors considering their services in Hong Kong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;SBCFX says entities associated with its brand have regulatory authorizations in other jurisdictions, including South Africa, Seychelles and Australia. Those disclosures are separate from the SFC’s position regarding authorization in Hong Kong.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For investors, the safest takeaway is simple: &lt;strong&gt;check the exact legal entity, verify the licence directly with the relevant regulator and understand what protections apply before depositing funds.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;As online trading continues to expand across borders, &lt;strong&gt;regulatory status may be just as important as the platform’s trading features — because the wrong assumption could cost you more than just a trade.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Disclaimer:&lt;/strong&gt; This article reports on a regulatory warning issued by Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission. Being identified as unlicensed in Hong Kong does not, by itself, establish that an entity has committed fraud or other criminal wrongdoing. Regulatory information and company disclosures can change, so readers should verify the latest information directly with the relevant authorities before making financial decisions. This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment or financial advice.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Tether Brings Offline AI Translation to 19 African and 9 European Languages</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

  &lt;header&gt;
    &lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjcVERUJG8fnG1OrKwQwpTlMhgSr7_VwYQO3Ha-_9EjcOYBLTGEsioGlvTJBzNySug66KGmIhHlr81EMJtCtPmt1vKW1RLxjXS3VLiQKEaJeBSUXrcDrs9PKQ-SkaGdMkTYiZuZ1MZcv8wlwfApH-SzOaBHt3IFqcWDpES9-Riz7jlEQGxL4V9h01i_ZU-C/s1672/tether-offline-ai-translation-african-european-languages.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Tether offline AI translation models for African and European languages" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjcVERUJG8fnG1OrKwQwpTlMhgSr7_VwYQO3Ha-_9EjcOYBLTGEsioGlvTJBzNySug66KGmIhHlr81EMJtCtPmt1vKW1RLxjXS3VLiQKEaJeBSUXrcDrs9PKQ-SkaGdMkTYiZuZ1MZcv8wlwfApH-SzOaBHt3IFqcWDpES9-Riz7jlEQGxL4V9h01i_ZU-C/w320-h180/tether-offline-ai-translation-african-european-languages.jpg.png" title="Tether Launches Offline AI Translation Models" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: large;"&gt;Artificial intelligence is usually associated with massive data centers, cloud computing and increasingly large models. Tether is taking a different approach: making specialized AI small enough to run directly on everyday devices.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;
      Tether AI Research has released a new family of open-source translation models designed to run locally on smartphones, laptops and other edge devices. The project places particular emphasis on African languages that have historically received limited support from mainstream AI systems, while a separate compact model family targets nine European languages.
    &lt;/p&gt;

    &lt;p&gt;
      The most important part of the announcement, however, may not be the number of languages. It is the fact that the models are designed to work &lt;strong&gt;offline&lt;/strong&gt;, without requiring every translation request to be sent to a cloud server.
    &lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/header&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Tether's New TranslatePsy Models Explained&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The new translation technology is part of Tether's broader &lt;strong&gt;QVAC&lt;/strong&gt; artificial intelligence initiative. The September 2, 2026 release includes several TranslatePsy model families with different priorities around language coverage, model size and device requirements.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 15px; margin: 20px 0px; width: 100%;"&gt;
    &lt;thead&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Model&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Coverage&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Main Focus&lt;/th&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
    &lt;/thead&gt;
    &lt;tbody&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;TranslatePsy-AfriSLM&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;19 African languages&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Higher-quality translation on &lt;br /&gt;local devices&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;TranslatePsy-AfriNano&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;8 African languages&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Compact, browser-scale &lt;br /&gt;deployment&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;TranslatePsy-EuroNano&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;9 European languages&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Very small footprint for &lt;br /&gt;local translation&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
    &lt;/tbody&gt;
  &lt;/table&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Tether says TranslatePsy-AfriSLM is available in 0.8B, 2B and 4B parameter versions, with full-precision and quantized builds. The company says the models can run through llama.cpp on smartphones and laptops without an expensive GPU, internet connection or account.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The 19 languages supported by AfriSLM are Afrikaans, Amharic, Hausa, Igbo, Kinyarwanda, Lingala, Luganda, Malagasy, Nyanja, Oromo, Shona, Somali, Southern Sotho, Swahili, Tswana, Wolof, Xhosa, Yoruba and Zulu.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Tether says these languages span West, East, Central and Southern Africa and collectively represent roughly half of the continent's population.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Offline AI Translation Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Most popular AI applications depend on cloud infrastructure. A user's request is transmitted to a remote server, processed by a large model and then returned over the internet.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That model works well when connectivity is fast and affordable. It becomes much less practical when internet access is unreliable, expensive or unavailable.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Tether's TranslatePsy approach is different. Translation can take place directly on the user's device, meaning the system can continue operating without a live internet connection. Tether also says processing locally keeps users' data on their devices rather than sending it to third-party cloud servers.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That creates two potentially important advantages: &lt;strong&gt;availability and privacy&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A student, healthcare worker, researcher or field worker may not need a permanent connection to use the translation technology. At the same time, local processing can reduce the amount of sensitive text that has to leave the device.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Of course, offline AI is not automatically better in every situation. Device hardware, storage, model quality, language coverage and battery consumption remain important considerations.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Africa Has a Major AI Language Gap&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The language problem is particularly significant in Africa because the continent has extraordinary linguistic diversity. UNESCO estimates that Africa is home to around &lt;strong&gt;2,000 languages&lt;/strong&gt;, yet only a small fraction have a meaningful presence in digital services such as localized software, translation and speech technologies.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    UNESCO has also highlighted the difficulties that African-language users can face with AI systems trained primarily on dominant languages. In other words, simply making an AI model available globally does not necessarily mean that it works equally well for every language community.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That is the gap &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitcoins-4-year-cycle-may-be-changing.html"&gt;Tether &lt;/a&gt;is attempting to address with TranslatePsy-AfriSLM.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Instead of trying to build one enormous general-purpose model, the project focuses on specialized translation models for languages that have historically had less AI training data and fewer digital resources.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The 800 Million Parameter Model Is the Interesting Part&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    One of the most notable claims from Tether concerns the smallest AfriSLM model.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;TranslatePsy-AfriSLM-0.8B contains 800 million parameters.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Tether says that despite its relatively small size, the model outperformed much larger systems including Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, TranslateGemma-27B and NLLB-3.3B across the FLORES-200, BOUQuET and SMOL translation benchmarks.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Tether's own research says the smallest model can outperform systems up to 152 times its parameter count on the evaluated benchmarks.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    These are &lt;strong&gt;Tether-reported benchmark results&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than independent verification. That distinction matters, particularly when comparing &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/trump-1-coin-is-here-us-mints-new.html"&gt;models&lt;/a&gt; with very different architectures, training methods and evaluation setups.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Still, the underlying idea is important: specialized AI does not necessarily need to be enormous to be useful.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Data Quality May Matter More Than Model Size&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Tether says one of the biggest challenges in developing African-language translation models was not simply computing power. It was the quality of available training data.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    According to Tether, its quality-estimation pipeline evaluates candidate sentence pairs using multiple quality-estimation models and keeps the strongest training signals.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The company reports that the filtering process reduced its open-source training data from approximately &lt;strong&gt;44.93 billion tokens to 1.76 billion tokens&lt;/strong&gt;—a reduction of about &lt;strong&gt;96%&lt;/strong&gt;—without a meaningful loss in translation quality.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Tether argues that adding enormous amounts of low-quality data can eventually dilute the useful training signal rather than improve the model.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That is an important lesson for low-resource languages. When high-quality human-translated datasets are limited, better filtering and carefully generated synthetic data can potentially compensate for the lack of massive datasets.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Translation Speed: About 46 Milliseconds per Sentence&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Model size is only useful if the model can actually respond quickly enough on the hardware people own.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Tether's QVAC research reports that a Bergamot-based translation setup can process a sentence in approximately &lt;strong&gt;46 milliseconds&lt;/strong&gt; on a Linux laptop in its benchmark.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The same research tested a compact translation model on a Pixel 10 Pro XL. In batch mode, Tether reported approximately &lt;strong&gt;26.1 milliseconds per sentence&lt;/strong&gt; and around &lt;strong&gt;870 tokens per second&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Tether says that at that speed, a full page of text can be translated in under three seconds in batch mode, entirely on-device and without network calls.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    These numbers are benchmark measurements, not guarantees for every smartphone or laptop. Real-world performance will vary according to hardware, language pair, model configuration and workload.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 15px; margin: 20px 0px; width: 100%;"&gt;
    &lt;thead&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Test&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Reported Result&lt;/th&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
    &lt;/thead&gt;
    &lt;tbody&gt;

      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
