    <title>Can I Generate the Same Bitcoin Address Again in a Deterministic Wallet?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjtCxyJfUvMzLFU2rDiutMsGDXs5s2Zo9mRI8MF0zLIJAfvMDdVBj2WzIcSjiYrelmZgdvLB35k6MnvdXkx6hxuJ3Nsg_7mQrTouqQ_cno0z5PyT6-WwWra8PtTuYcRnrhCZYaEa-J6G41Z29WAc1I4U1N22ItY9qyxrnULugHRZNkzkOmW3hMf1Bb_3IO0/s1671/same-bitcoin-address-deterministic-wallet-bip32-bip39.jpg.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Deterministic Bitcoin wallet regenerating the same address from a seed" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1671" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjtCxyJfUvMzLFU2rDiutMsGDXs5s2Zo9mRI8MF0zLIJAfvMDdVBj2WzIcSjiYrelmZgdvLB35k6MnvdXkx6hxuJ3Nsg_7mQrTouqQ_cno0z5PyT6-WwWra8PtTuYcRnrhCZYaEa-J6G41Z29WAc1I4U1N22ItY9qyxrnULugHRZNkzkOmW3hMf1Bb_3IO0/w640-h360/same-bitcoin-address-deterministic-wallet-bip32-bip39.jpg.png" title="Can I Generate the Same Bitcoin Address Again?" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Yes. In a deterministic or hierarchical deterministic (HD) Bitcoin wallet, the same receiving address can usually be generated again as long as the wallet is restored from the same seed and uses the same derivation method, account, chain and address index.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is one of the most useful properties of HD wallets. Instead of storing every Bitcoin private key separately, the wallet can derive a large tree of keys from a common seed. BIP-32 defines this hierarchical deterministic key structure, while BIP-39 describes how a mnemonic phrase can be converted into the seed used to create a deterministic wallet. BIP-44 then provides a standardized hierarchy for accounts, change chains and address indexes. &lt;a href="https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0032.mediawiki" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;BIP-32&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href="https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0039.mediawiki" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;BIP-39&lt;/a&gt; and &lt;a href="https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0044.mediawiki" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;BIP-44&lt;/a&gt; are the key standards behind this model.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 650px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Question&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Short Answer&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Can the same address be &lt;br /&gt;generated again?&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Yes, if the same wallet seed and &lt;br /&gt;derivation parameters are used.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Does every new wallet &lt;br /&gt;address come from a &lt;br /&gt;new random seed?&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;No. HD wallets derive many &lt;br /&gt;addresses from the same &lt;br /&gt;underlying seed.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Why does my wallet &lt;br /&gt;show a different address?&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;The wallet may have moved to &lt;br /&gt;the next address index for privacy &lt;br /&gt;and address management.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Can a different derivation &lt;br /&gt;path produce a different &lt;br /&gt;address?&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Yes. The seed can be the same &lt;br /&gt;while a different path produces &lt;br /&gt;different keys and addresses.&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is a Deterministic Bitcoin Wallet?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A deterministic wallet is a wallet in which keys are derived in a predictable way from a common starting point, rather than being generated as unrelated random keys.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Modern Bitcoin wallets commonly use hierarchical deterministic architecture. BIP-32 describes a tree of parent and child keys. Starting from a master key, the wallet can derive child keys through different branches and indexes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This makes backups much simpler. Instead of backing up every receiving address individually, a user can back up the wallet's underlying seed and use compatible wallet software to recreate the key hierarchy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Bitcoin developer documentation describes HD wallets as a way to simplify backups while allowing large numbers of child keys and addresses to be generated from a common source. &lt;a href="https://developer.bitcoin.org/devguide/wallets.html" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Bitcoin Developer Guide&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How BIP-39 and BIP-32 Work Together&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where many Bitcoin users become confused.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;BIP-39 does not directly define Bitcoin addresses.&lt;/strong&gt; It defines a mnemonic system that represents entropy in a human-readable sequence of words and explains how that mnemonic can be converted into a binary seed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BIP-39 specifies that the mnemonic and an optional passphrase are processed using PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 to produce a 512-bit seed. That seed can then be used to create a deterministic wallet using BIP-32 or a similar method. &lt;a href="https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0039.mediawiki" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;BIP-39 specification&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BIP-32 takes the resulting seed and establishes the hierarchical key structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A simplified version of the process looks like this:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Mnemonic words → BIP-39 seed → BIP-32 master key → child keys → public keys → Bitcoin addresses&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because this process is deterministic, the same inputs can reproduce the same resulting keys and addresses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;So, Can You Generate the Exact Same Address Again?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Yes.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you restore the same wallet using the same seed and follow the same derivation scheme, the same address at the same derivation index can be generated again.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, imagine a wallet derives its first external receiving address at a particular path. If that wallet is later restored from the same seed and the software derives that exact same path, it will arrive at the same key and therefore the same &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-is-my-bitcoin-transaction-still_0394756778.html"&gt;Bitcoin address&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important part is that the &lt;strong&gt;derivation path and index matter&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is not enough to say, "I used the same seed." Two wallets can use different derivation standards or paths and therefore show different addresses even though the underlying recovery phrase is identical.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is an Address Index?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;HD wallets can generate addresses sequentially.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Think of the address index like a counter:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Index 0 → first receiving address&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Index 1 → second receiving address&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Index 2 → third receiving address&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Index 3 → fourth receiving address&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And the process can continue for a very large number of addresses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BIP-44 describes a hierarchy that includes an address index and separates external receiving addresses from internal change addresses. Its general path structure is:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;m / purpose' / coin_type' / account' / change / address_index&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The address index is therefore one of the pieces of information that determines which particular address is being derived. &lt;a href="https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0044.mediawiki" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;BIP-44 specification&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Does My Wallet Keep Giving Me a New Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where deterministic wallets can appear confusing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You may receive Bitcoin at one address today and then press "Receive" tomorrow and see a completely different address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not mean your old address disappeared.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The wallet may simply have moved to another unused address in its deterministic sequence. The old address and its private key remain part of the wallet's derived key structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One important reason for generating fresh receiving addresses is &lt;strong&gt;privacy&lt;/strong&gt;. Reusing the same Bitcoin address can make it easier for observers to connect multiple payments and transactions to the same address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Therefore, the ability to reproduce an old address does not mean that repeatedly using that address is necessarily a good privacy practice.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can I Restore an Old Bitcoin Address From My Seed Phrase?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Usually, yes, provided the address was derived from that seed and you know or can identify the relevant wallet configuration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the fundamental benefits of deterministic wallets. The seed acts as the root from which the wallet can recreate its key hierarchy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, restoration is not always as simple as entering the words into any wallet and immediately seeing every historical address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The wallet may need to use the correct:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Mnemonic phrase&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Optional BIP-39 passphrase, if one was used&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Bitcoin address format&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Derivation standard&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Derivation path&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Account number&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Address/change chain&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Address index&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If one of these differs, the wallet may derive a different branch of the key tree.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If the Same Seed Produces Different Addresses?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Seeing different addresses after restoring a wallet does not automatically mean that the seed is wrong.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The first thing to investigate is the wallet's derivation scheme.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Different Bitcoin address types and wallet standards can use different derivation paths. BIP-44, for example, defines a multi-account hierarchy based on BIP-32, while other standards define different paths for other Bitcoin script types.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This means two compatible wallets can potentially accept the same recovery phrase while presenting different addresses if they are looking at different derivation paths.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For recovery work, it is therefore important to identify the original wallet and address type rather than simply importing the seed into random &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-someone-find-your-name-from-bitcoin-wallet.html"&gt;wallet software&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does Reusing the Same Address Create a New Bitcoin Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A Bitcoin address is not regenerated into something different every time someone sends coins to it. If you give someone the same receiving address twice, it remains the same address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;What changes is the blockchain history associated with that address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, if an address receives 0.01 BTC today and another 0.02 BTC later, both payments can be associated with that same address on the public Bitcoin blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one reason wallets often generate fresh receiving addresses even though they retain the ability to derive previously used addresses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can an Address Be Recreated Without the Seed?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not generally from the address alone.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A Bitcoin address is designed to be shared publicly for receiving funds. It does not contain enough information to reconstruct the wallet's private key.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the wallet is self-custodied, access to the relevant private key or a valid wallet backup is needed to spend the Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is also why an address should not be confused with a recovery phrase. The address identifies where Bitcoin can be received, while the private key provides the cryptographic authority required to spend it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For more information about recovery when a seed phrase is unavailable, see our related guide: &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-i-generate-same-bitcoin-address.html" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Can Bitcoin Be Recovered Without a Seed Phrase?&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Role Does BIP-44 Play?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BIP-44 provides a logical structure for deterministic wallets built on BIP-32. It separates different levels of the wallet hierarchy, including purpose, coin type, account, change and address index.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Bitcoin, this allows one underlying wallet to manage multiple accounts and large numbers of addresses without requiring a completely separate random seed for every address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The concept can be simplified as:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 650px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Level&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Purpose&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Purpose&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Identifies the wallet &lt;br /&gt;structure being used&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Coin type&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Identifies the cryptocurrency/&lt;br /&gt;network&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Account&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Separates wallet accounts&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Change&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Separates external receiving &lt;br /&gt;addresses from internal change &lt;br /&gt;addresses&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Address index&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Selects a particular address in &lt;br /&gt;that branch&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Is Address Reuse Safe?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;From a basic spending perspective, receiving Bitcoin at a previously used address does not make the Bitcoin invalid. The address remains usable as long as the corresponding private key is controlled by the wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bigger issue is privacy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin transactions are publicly visible. Repeatedly using one address can make it easier to connect payments and activity associated with that address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For that reason, users should generally allow their wallet to generate fresh receiving addresses when the wallet supports this feature rather than manually reusing an old address for every payment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If I Restore the Same Wallet on Another Device?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the second wallet correctly supports the same seed format, derivation method and relevant wallet configuration, it can reproduce the same deterministic key hierarchy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is the main reason HD wallets make recovery and device migration possible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, users should not assume that every wallet application will automatically scan every possible derivation path. If an expected balance or old address is missing after restoration, checking the original wallet's address type and derivation path can be an important troubleshooting step.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Seed Phrase vs Address: What Can Be Recreated?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 700px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Item&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Can It Recreate the Wallet?&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Purpose&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Bitcoin address&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;No&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Used to receive Bitcoin&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Public key&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;No, by itself&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Public cryptographic information&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Private key&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Can control the corresponding funds&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Authorizes spending&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;BIP-39 seed phrase&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Yes, when used with the correct wallet configuration&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(119, 119, 119); padding: 10px;"&gt;Backup/recovery of the deterministic wallet&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Important Security Warning&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Never enter your real Bitcoin recovery phrase into an unknown website just to check whether an address can be regenerated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A BIP-39 mnemonic is highly sensitive wallet-recovery information. Anyone who obtains the required recovery information and wallet configuration may be able to recreate the corresponding keys and access funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you are troubleshooting an old wallet, use trusted wallet software and preferably perform recovery in a controlled environment. Never send your seed phrase to someone claiming to be "wallet support."&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can I generate the same Bitcoin address twice?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes. In an HD wallet, the same seed combined with the same derivation path and address index can reproduce the same address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does a new Bitcoin address mean I have a new seed phrase?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. HD wallets can generate many addresses from the same underlying deterministic wallet seed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why does my Bitcoin wallet keep changing my receiving address?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Many wallets automatically move to a new unused address to improve privacy and organize incoming payments. The previous address remains part of the wallet's derived key structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can I recover an old Bitcoin address with my seed phrase?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Usually, yes, if the address was derived from that seed and you use the correct derivation scheme, account and address index.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can someone recover my Bitcoin wallet from only my address?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. A public Bitcoin address does not provide the private key needed to spend the funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does BIP-39 generate Bitcoin addresses?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Not directly. BIP-39 defines the mnemonic and its conversion into a binary seed. That seed can then be used by BIP-32 or compatible deterministic wallet systems to derive keys.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What if the same seed gives me a different address?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Check the wallet's address type, derivation path, account and other configuration settings. A different derivation path can produce a different branch of addresses from the same underlying seed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Yes, a deterministic Bitcoin wallet can generate the same address again.&lt;/strong&gt; The key is that deterministic wallets do not randomly create an unrelated private key every time an address is displayed. They derive addresses from an underlying wallet seed through a defined hierarchy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;BIP-39 provides the mnemonic-to-seed process, BIP-32 defines hierarchical deterministic key derivation, and BIP-44 provides a commonly used structure for accounts, change and address indexes. With the same recovery information and the same derivation parameters, an old address can therefore be reproduced.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, address reuse is not ideal for privacy. Modern wallets can generate fresh receiving addresses while retaining the ability to derive earlier addresses when the correct wallet configuration is restored.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Zcash Just Got a Major Speed Boost: Zakura Says Private Transactions Can Drop Below 200ms</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;br /&gt;&lt;article&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj7TaBrpaUKCiiducqRvces8MtRKgxSqpSkqe_3pshjBAyvtcyqpMWCk-WDSQPSTkX6MYdduSxHgLIoS3M9u7GvWVatAW0mOIxQnm4IMuipg2y3R0LiSwQTXjn0I1PIVNenSeb_LZ1vEyWZHdCoKdkGFU-PI0WvmEXeKldqP332c2f_Mt022P310-7Ttn71/s1672/zakura-zcash-common-14x-faster-private-transactions.jpg.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Zakura Common Boosts Zcash Private Transaction Speed" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj7TaBrpaUKCiiducqRvces8MtRKgxSqpSkqe_3pshjBAyvtcyqpMWCk-WDSQPSTkX6MYdduSxHgLIoS3M9u7GvWVatAW0mOIxQnm4IMuipg2y3R0LiSwQTXjn0I1PIVNenSeb_LZ1vEyWZHdCoKdkGFU-PI0WvmEXeKldqP332c2f_Mt022P310-7Ttn71/w400-h225/zakura-zcash-common-14x-faster-private-transactions.jpg.png" title="Zakura Common improves Zcash private transaction performance with faster mobile proof generation" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zcash has spent years trying to solve one of the hardest problems in cryptocurrency: how do you make private payments fast enough for ordinary people to use every day?&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Now, a new release from the team behind the Zakura Zcash node is taking aim at one of the most noticeable bottlenecks — the time a user's device spends creating a private transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;On August 29, Zakura announced &lt;strong&gt;Zakura Common&lt;/strong&gt;, an open-source collection of cryptography and protocol libraries designed to accelerate Zcash wallets and full nodes. According to Zakura's published benchmarks, mobile proof generation is now &lt;strong&gt;more than 14 times faster&lt;/strong&gt;, while desktop performance is more than five times faster.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In some cases, Zakura says the time a wallet spends creating a private transaction can fall from &lt;strong&gt;more than three seconds to under 200 milliseconds&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is a significant change for a privacy-focused cryptocurrency where the transaction can feel slow before it even reaches the blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://zakura.com/announcements/zakura-common/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;
      Read Zakura's official announcement
    &lt;/a&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Problem Zakura Is Trying to Fix&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zcash is designed around privacy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Shielded transactions can hide important transaction details, including the sender, receiver and amount. But that privacy comes with a computational cost.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Before a private &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/how-can-you-tell-if-crypto-investment.html"&gt;Zcash payment&lt;/a&gt; can be broadcast, a wallet has to perform cryptographic calculations to construct the necessary proof. On mobile devices, that work can become a noticeable part of the user experience.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A three-second wait may not sound enormous in isolation. But if someone has to stare at a loading screen every time they make a private payment, the delay can become a serious usability problem.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zakura's latest software attacks that bottleneck at the cryptographic-library level.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;And importantly, &lt;strong&gt;this is not a Zcash consensus upgrade&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Existing Zcash network rules do not need to change for compatible wallets and software to benefit. Developers can integrate the new libraries into their own releases.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That distinction matters: Zakura Common is primarily a &lt;strong&gt;software-performance improvement&lt;/strong&gt;, not a new blockchain consensus mechanism.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://zakura.com/announcements/zakura-common/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;
      Zakura Common — Official Announcement
    &lt;/a&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;More Than a 14x Improvement&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The headline number is the mobile proof-generation improvement, but Zakura says several components of its cryptographic stack have become substantially faster.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
    &lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 16px; min-width: 650px; width: 100%;"&gt;
      &lt;thead&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Component&lt;/th&gt;
          &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Reported Improvement&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/thead&gt;
      &lt;tbody&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Mobile proof generation&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;More than 14x faster&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Desktop proof generation&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;More than 5x faster&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Sinsemilla hashing&lt;/td&gt;

        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Trial decryption&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;More than 1.5x faster&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;zk-SNARK verification&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;4x–8x faster&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
        &lt;tr&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Wallet transaction creation&lt;/td&gt;
          &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Under 200ms in many cases&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;/tbody&gt;
    &lt;/table&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;These are Zakura's benchmark results rather than a guarantee that every device or wallet will achieve identical performance. Actual results will depend on hardware, software implementation and how quickly individual wallets adopt the new libraries.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Mobile Performance Matters So Much&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Desktop computers have considerably more processing power than smartphones.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That makes mobile devices one of the more difficult environments for privacy-preserving cryptography.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zakura says its optimization work specifically targets this problem. The team's published benchmarks show the largest improvement in proof generation on mobile hardware, where the process is now more than 14 times faster.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The result could be particularly important for &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/can-cryptocurrencies-survive-quantum-era.html"&gt;wallets&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Instead of treating privacy as something that necessarily requires a long computational wait, wallet developers can potentially use a more optimized cryptographic stack to make shielded transactions feel almost instantaneous.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Zakura Common Does Not Require a Network Upgrade&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;One of the more interesting aspects of the release is what it &lt;strong&gt;doesn't&lt;/strong&gt; require.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zakura says the improvements are publicly available under the MIT/Apache 2.0 dual license and do not require a Zcash network upgrade.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The upcoming Zakura 1.3.0 release is moving to the new stack, while other projects can independently integrate the libraries.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://zakura.com/announcements/zakura-common/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;
      View the official Zakura Common release
    &lt;/a&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Ambition: 50,000+ Private Transactions Per Second&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zakura Common should not be viewed as an isolated optimization.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It fits into a much larger effort to scale Zcash.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The Zakura team has described a long-term ambition of supporting payment volumes in the range of major global payment networks, with &lt;strong&gt;more than 50,000 transactions per second&lt;/strong&gt; serving as a benchmark for the project's scalability goals.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is dramatically beyond the performance requirements of today's Zcash software.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Reaching that level would require much more than faster proof generation.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It would require improvements across the entire stack — including transaction verification, networking, wallet synchronization, data availability and the amount of information validators need to process and retain.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is where &lt;strong&gt;Project Tachyon&lt;/strong&gt; enters the picture.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Project Tachyon: The Larger Zcash Scaling Effort&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Project Tachyon is a proposed Zcash scalability initiative being developed by community members.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Its goal is much broader than simply making transactions faster on a smartphone.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Tachyon explores advanced cryptographic techniques, including proof-carrying data and recursive proofs, to reduce the amount of work required to process large numbers of shielded transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The project explores a future in which private payments can scale while preserving Zcash's core privacy properties.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://tachyon.z.cash/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;
      Explore Project Tachyon
    &lt;/a&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The relationship between the projects is important.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Zakura Common improves the cryptographic machinery. Tachyon tackles deeper protocol-level scaling problems.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Together, they form part of a broader attempt to move Zcash toward much higher transaction capacity without abandoning privacy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;NU7 Is Another Piece of the Story&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The timing also matters because Zcash is preparing for its next major network-development phase.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zakura says its optimized software can handle the &lt;strong&gt;25-second block times proposed for NU7&lt;/strong&gt;. The project's announcement describes the new cryptographic stack as something that can push performance further while the broader Zcash ecosystem continues working toward future upgrades.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;NU7 itself remains a community-governance process rather than a completed upgrade.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The Zcash Foundation opened a ZCAP poll in late August to resolve outstanding questions about the scope of NU7, illustrating that parts of the upgrade remain subject to community discussion and approval.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://zfnd.org/zcap-poll-now-open-nu7/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;
      Read the Zcash Foundation's NU7 update
    &lt;/a&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Zcash Is Trying to Solve More Than One Bottleneck&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A blockchain cannot reach payment-network scale by optimizing only one piece of code.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Imagine a highway where cars can suddenly accelerate five times faster, but the road still has the same number of lanes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Traffic will eventually hit another bottleneck.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zcash faces a similar problem.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Faster proof generation helps users create transactions more quickly. Faster verification helps nodes process transactions. Faster hashing improves another computational component. But network bandwidth, state growth, transaction size and synchronization can still constrain overall performance.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is why the broader Zcash scaling strategy involves multiple projects attacking different bottlenecks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zakura is focused heavily on node and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/can-coinbase-pull-back-crypto.html"&gt;cryptographic&lt;/a&gt; performance.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Tachyon is exploring deeper protocol and proof-system improvements.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The objective is not simply to make one benchmark look better.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The objective is to make &lt;strong&gt;private digital payments practical at global scale&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Helius CEO Reaction&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The release also attracted attention outside the immediate Zcash developer community.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Helius CEO Mert highlighted the result, describing it as an &lt;strong&gt;"insane engineering feat."&lt;/strong&gt; The reaction reflects why the release has generated interest beyond Zcash itself: achieving a double-digit improvement in a highly optimized cryptographic workload is technically difficult.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;However, the reaction should not be confused with independent verification of the benchmark. Zakura's published measurements remain the primary source for the performance claims.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What About ZEC's Price?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The release also arrived alongside renewed market interest in Zcash.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Reporting following the announcement placed &lt;strong&gt;ZEC around the $839 area&lt;/strong&gt;, with the token gaining roughly 5% around the time of the news.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;a href="https://www.tradingview.com/news/coinpedia%3Ae5f8a6623094b%3A0-zcash-developer-zakura-launches-common-as-zec-price-jumps-5/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;
      Read the market report
    &lt;/a&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But investors should separate the technology story from the price story.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A faster cryptographic library does not automatically mean that ZEC must rise.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Crypto markets react to multiple factors, including liquidity, broader market conditions, speculation and expectations about future adoption.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The most defensible conclusion is simply that the Zakura announcement coincided with a period of stronger ZEC price activity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;It would be misleading to claim that Zakura Common alone caused the price move.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why This Could Matter for Zcash Adoption&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Privacy is only useful if people are willing to use it.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If sending a private transaction requires several seconds of computation on a modern smartphone, some users may choose convenience over privacy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Reducing that delay to hundreds of milliseconds changes the equation.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A wallet that can construct a shielded transaction almost instantly feels fundamentally different from one that makes users wait through a visible processing step.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That could matter for:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Mobile Zcash wallets&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Everyday private payments&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Wallet onboarding&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Merchant applications&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;High-frequency private transactions&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Future payment infrastructure&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But software adoption is crucial.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The performance improvement exists in Zakura Common. It does not automatically propagate to every Zcash wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;A Faster Wallet Is Not the Same as a Faster Blockchain&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;This is perhaps the most important distinction for readers.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If a wallet creates a transaction in 200 milliseconds instead of three seconds, that does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean the Zcash blockchain has suddenly reached 50,000 transactions per second.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Those are two different measurements.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Transaction creation latency&lt;/strong&gt; measures how long the user's device takes to construct the cryptographic transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Blockchain throughput&lt;/strong&gt; measures how many transactions the network can process.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zakura Common primarily addresses the first problem while also improving several node-side operations.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The 50,000+ TPS ambition requires additional protocol, networking and infrastructure improvements. Project Tachyon is part of that broader effort.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The next stage is adoption.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zakura has said it is inviting wallet developers to integrate the new libraries. Its upcoming 1.3.0 release is expected to use Zakura Common, and the project says Tachyon has also moved to the new stack.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If more wallets adopt the libraries, users could gradually begin seeing faster shielded transaction creation without needing to wait for a network-wide upgrade.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That could make the improvement more meaningful than a benchmark alone.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A cryptographic optimization becomes valuable when it disappears into the user experience.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;If someone taps &lt;strong&gt;Send&lt;/strong&gt;, waits a fraction of a second and sees the transaction broadcast, they do not need to understand the mathematics underneath.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;They simply experience a faster wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Picture&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zakura Common is not the final answer to Zcash's scaling challenge.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It is better understood as one important layer of a much larger engineering effort.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The release addresses a real user-facing problem: the computational delay involved in creating private transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The numbers are striking — more than 14x faster mobile proof generation, more than 21x faster Sinsemilla hashing, faster verification and transaction creation that can fall below 200 milliseconds in many cases.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;But the more interesting story may be what comes next.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zcash developers are trying to combine faster cryptography, more efficient node software, recursive-proof research, privacy-preserving synchronization and future protocol changes into a system capable of supporting private payments at global scale.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That is a much bigger ambition than simply making a wallet load faster.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For now, Zakura Common gives the Zcash ecosystem a tangible performance improvement that developers can use on the existing network.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;And if the project's broader roadmap succeeds, today's 200-millisecond benchmark could eventually look like just one early step toward making private cryptocurrency payments fast enough for everyday global use.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;hr /&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What is Zakura Common?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zakura Common is an open-source collection of cryptography and protocol libraries developed for the Zcash ecosystem. It is designed to improve the performance of wallets and full nodes.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;How much faster is Zakura Common?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zakura reports that mobile proof generation is more than 14 times faster, desktop proof generation is more than five times faster, Sinsemilla hashing is more than 21 times faster, and zk-SNARK verification is between four and eight times faster.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Can Zcash transactions really be created in under 200 milliseconds?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Zakura says wallet transaction creation can take less than 200 milliseconds in many cases with its optimized cryptographic stack. That is a benchmark claim, not a guarantee for every device or wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Does Zakura Common require a Zcash hard fork?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;No. Zakura says the improvements do not require a network upgrade. Wallets and node implementations can adopt the libraries through their own software releases.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What is Project Tachyon?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Project Tachyon is a proposed Zcash scalability initiative exploring advanced cryptographic techniques to make private payments more scalable while maintaining privacy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is Zcash targeting 50,000 transactions per second?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The Zakura team has described more than 50,000 transactions per second as a long-term benchmark for supporting payment volumes comparable to major global payment networks. Reaching that level would require improvements across multiple layers of the Zcash stack.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Does the Zakura release guarantee that ZEC will rise?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;No. Faster technology may improve the long-term usability and scalability outlook, but it does not guarantee a particular ZEC price. Market prices are influenced by many factors.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Bitcoin Shrugs Off Inflation Data as Market's Macro Sensitivity Fades</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiFJjmNhRJsoaYRicE3Synidc51dOVvSX3iZWZQwnYaOZ0Y1Afv4iHSoA9Bidp_Ki-U34JlJsAmBvtHVcgMBcZfJZo8lxgcXkzbXxzEurPFlQu313-aEml8huaHsj0459gpWXYxVMgN9bDIT6oA4q6SLxcq4VEccenVw0zAC-xqdYqOfQO0_VY3tsAe2NMD/s1672/Bitcoin%20Market%20Amid%20Inflation%20Data.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin price holding near $65,000 after U.S. inflation data as crypto market macro sensitivity fades" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiFJjmNhRJsoaYRicE3Synidc51dOVvSX3iZWZQwnYaOZ0Y1Afv4iHSoA9Bidp_Ki-U34JlJsAmBvtHVcgMBcZfJZo8lxgcXkzbXxzEurPFlQu313-aEml8huaHsj0459gpWXYxVMgN9bDIT6oA4q6SLxcq4VEccenVw0zAC-xqdYqOfQO0_VY3tsAe2NMD/w320-h180/Bitcoin%20Market%20Amid%20Inflation%20Data.png" title="Bitcoin price holding near $65,000 after U.S. inflation data as crypto market macro sensitivity fades" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Aug 13, 2026&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;– Bitcoin barely moved after July's
U.S. inflation report landed exactly in line with expectations. Traders had
hoped the print would spark a rally. Instead, BTC stayed pinned near
$65,000&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;July headline inflation rose 0.1% on the month and 3.4% on
the year, with core CPI easing to 2.5%. The numbers matched forecasts closely
enough that futures markets cut the implied odds of a September rate hike to
roughly 34% from over 50% before the release&amp;nbsp;. Yet Bitcoin moved from
$63,890 to just $64,100 — a $210 gain of 0.33%&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;That's a fraction of the reaction CPI used to generate. In
December 2024, Bitcoin moved 7% in four hours on a CPI print. In June 2025, a
4.2% inflation spike sent it down 9% in a single day. Now the market has gone
quiet for three straight months&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Why CPI No Longer Moves Bitcoin&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The muted reaction reflects a structural shift in who buys
Bitcoin. Before the spot &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/cypherpunk-technologies-boosts-zcash.html"&gt;ETFs &lt;/a&gt;launched, the marginal buyer was a crypto-native
trader watching CPI obsessively because the Fed funds rate directly affected
funding rates on leveraged positions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;After the ETFs, the marginal buyer is increasingly a wealth
management client whose advisor allocated 1% to 3% of a diversified portfolio
to IBIT on a quarterly rebalancing schedule. That buyer does not watch CPI at
all&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Meanwhile, perpetual trading volumes on Binance and Bybit
have dropped to their lowest level since 2023. Open interest remains relatively
high, leaving the market exposed to liquidation-driven moves in either
direction&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Two Catalysts Could Break the Range&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;With Bitcoin trapped between $62,000 and $66,000 for five
consecutive weeks, analysts point to two catalysts that could finally break the
stalemate&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;1. The Political Tailwind&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The White House remains "fully committed" to
passing the CLARITY Act in September. The bill would establish a comprehensive
federal framework for digital assets, ending the "regulation by
enforcement" approach that has dominated U.S. crypto policy. The Senate
returns from recess on September 8, with a cloture vote scheduled for September
15.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Derivatives positioning shows investors remain well hedged
rather than betting on an imminent breakout, suggesting traders are waiting for
clarity from Washington&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;2. Thin Liquidity Risk&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Summer liquidity has thinned to multiyear lows, with trading
volumes falling to their lowest levels since early 2019&amp;nbsp;. Glassnode noted
that spot exchange volume has dropped to levels last seen during the 2023 bear
market, warning that such a thin market could amplify the next major move&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;"There is this classic setup for volatility expansion
once participation returns," the firm wrote in a report Wednesday&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Opposing Views&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bullish case:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;BlackRock's Robert Mitchnick noted
on &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/saylors-digital-asset-spectrum-bitcoin.html"&gt;Bloomberg &lt;/a&gt;ETF IQ that Bitcoin's decoupling from equities is positive for the
diversification thesis. "It reinforces the thesis of Bitcoin as a
diversification tool and a hedge against sharp drawdowns in other parts of the
portfolio," he said&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;Large addresses holding 10,000+ BTC have grown to 90 — a
six-month high, adding six wallets in the past eight weeks&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Bearish case:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Peter Schiff claims Bitcoin is now
"anti-gold," arguing the asset's slide will continue as war-driven
inflation fears send gold and silver higher&amp;nbsp;. Meanwhile, Glassnode warned
that sellers are tiring but the market has yet to experience the deeper
capitulation that marked previous cycle bottoms&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;The next tests are the Jackson Hole gathering of central
bankers later this month, the Sept. 4 jobs report, and the Sept. 11 inflation
release&amp;nbsp;. The Federal Reserve's Sept. 16 meeting is the biggest catalyst:
Polymarket data shows traders assigning 34% probability to a 25-basis-point
hike&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;A hike would be the first since spot Bitcoin ETFs launched.
No existing model can predict how $55 billion in ETF assets would respond to a
hiking cycle. Until one of those catalysts arrives, Bitcoin's response to macro
data remains muted&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

    <title>Japan FSA Seeks Tax-Filing Exemption for Trust-Based Stablecoins</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi3wKr186ybUywbvNaGLkpszOH-Er_lFLuH9vIDdMxcUcDX0LZTma9i2f60i-c15fACyevPseVeyaJGOhZlVda7pnQpze0mCifDRV2_ZZm53TJw6776BEPZnY-gdrTrxYsh773qHMNCFct4Gq-felHcSuAOmzVBXqXHYxTPdFL33Jq1jBwOxkj4n4Z0iduX/s1672/japan-fsa-trust-based-stablecoins-2027-tax-reform.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Japan Financial Services Agency proposal for tax filing exemption on trust-based stablecoins" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEi3wKr186ybUywbvNaGLkpszOH-Er_lFLuH9vIDdMxcUcDX0LZTma9i2f60i-c15fACyevPseVeyaJGOhZlVda7pnQpze0mCifDRV2_ZZm53TJw6776BEPZnY-gdrTrxYsh773qHMNCFct4Gq-felHcSuAOmzVBXqXHYxTPdFL33Jq1jBwOxkj4n4Z0iduX/w400-h225/japan-fsa-trust-based-stablecoins-2027-tax-reform.jpg.png" title="Japan FSA Seeks Tax Filing Exemption for Trust-Based Stablecoins" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Japan is taking another step toward making stablecoins easier to use as digital payment instruments.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The country's Financial Services Agency (FSA) is seeking a tax-filing exemption for certain trust-based stablecoins as part of its fiscal 2027 tax-reform proposal. The request is aimed at removing a reporting requirement that can become difficult to apply when the holder of a trust-based stablecoin changes repeatedly as the token moves between users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proposal does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean Japan has made stablecoins tax-free. It is a request for targeted administrative relief, and the final decision will come through Japan's broader tax-reform process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.fsa.go.jp/en/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Japan Financial Services Agency (FSA) — Official Website&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Japan Wants to Change the Rule&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The problem comes from the way trust-based stablecoins are structured.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In a conventional trust, the number of beneficiaries may be relatively small and changes may happen infrequently. A trustee can therefore identify beneficiaries and handle the required documentation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A stablecoin works differently.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A token can move from one wallet to another many times during a single day. If every transfer effectively changes the beneficiary of the underlying trust, applying traditional trust-reporting procedures to every transaction could create a significant administrative burden.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent reporting on the FSA's fiscal 2027 request says the agency wants trust-based stablecoins to be exempt from certain tax-document filing requirements that can arise when beneficiaries change. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;This Is a Tax-Filing Relief Proposal, Not a Tax-Free Stablecoin Policy&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Japan is not proposing to eliminate taxes on trust-based &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/imf-warns-stablecoins-could-cut-payment.html"&gt;stablecoins&lt;/a&gt; altogether. Instead, the FSA is asking policymakers to remove a specific filing obligation that may not work efficiently for a digital payment instrument designed to circulate continuously.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So the accurate description is that Japan's FSA is &lt;strong&gt;seeking an exemption from certain tax-document filing requirements&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It would be misleading to say that Japan has already approved a blanket stablecoin tax exemption.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Trust-Based Stablecoins Work&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trust-based stablecoins are designed around a trust structure in which assets backing the tokens are held and managed through a regulated trust arrangement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The token represents rights connected to those underlying assets, while blockchain technology allows the digital instrument to be transferred between users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Japan's stablecoin framework recognizes different structures for electronic &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/how-do-companies-use-ai-today.html"&gt;payment &lt;/a&gt;instruments. Trust-based stablecoins fall within the trust-company model, which is different from stablecoins issued under a funds-transfer-service structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One example is &lt;strong&gt;JPYSC&lt;/strong&gt;, a yen-denominated stablecoin associated with SBI Shinsei Trust Bank.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters because the FSA's latest proposal is specifically focused on the administrative problems created by trust-based stablecoins and their constantly changing holders. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Reporting Problem in Simple Terms&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 650px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Traditional Trust&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px; text-align: left;"&gt;Trust-Based Stablecoin&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Beneficiaries may change &lt;br /&gt;relatively infrequently&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Holders can change with &lt;br /&gt;each transfer&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Beneficiary records can be &lt;br /&gt;maintained conventionally&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Large numbers of blockchain&lt;br /&gt;&amp;nbsp;users may hold tokens&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Transfers are generally limited&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Tokens can circulate &lt;br /&gt;continuously&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Reporting burden is relatively &lt;br /&gt;predictable&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 12px;"&gt;Reporting could grow with &lt;br /&gt;transaction activity&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That difference is at the heart of the FSA's request.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Proposal Matters for Japan's Stablecoin Industry&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Japan has spent several years building a regulatory framework for stablecoins. The country wants digital assets to operate within a regulated financial environment rather than outside the traditional financial system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But regulation also has to work in practice.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If a payment token can move thousands or millions of times between users, applying a reporting system designed for conventional trust arrangements can become inefficient.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The FSA's proposal attempts to address that mismatch without removing the underlying regulatory framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If adopted, the change could reduce administrative work for trustees and make it easier for regulated financial institutions to operate trust-based stablecoin products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Japan Is Treating Stablecoins More Like Payment Infrastructure&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The proposal also reflects a broader shift in how policymakers view stablecoins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Stablecoins are no longer being discussed only as tools for cryptocurrency trading. They are increasingly being considered for:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Digital payments&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Cross-border transfers&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Corporate settlement&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Remittances&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Tokenized assets&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;On-chain financial settlement&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For these applications to grow, the underlying regulatory and tax systems need to accommodate frequent digital transfers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is where Japan's latest proposal becomes particularly interesting.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Foreign-Issued Trust-Based Stablecoins Are Also on the Agenda&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The FSA's fiscal 2027 tax-reform requests also include a separate issue involving trust-based stablecoins issued outside Japan.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The agency is seeking changes that would provide a clearer framework for these products as Japan's stablecoin market becomes increasingly connected to international digital-asset markets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the details and final treatment will depend on the government's subsequent tax-reform discussions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Reports say the Japanese government and ruling party will consider the proposals as they work toward the year-end tax-reform package. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The FSA's request is not the final step.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Japan's government and ruling coalition will review the requested tax measures before determining what is included in the final fiscal 2027 tax-reform outline.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means the proposed exemption could still be modified or rejected.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, the most accurate description is simple: &lt;strong&gt;Japan's FSA is asking for the exemption.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It has not yet become a blanket change in Japanese tax law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Move Could Matter Beyond Japan&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Japan's approach could become relevant to other countries facing the same problem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traditional financial regulations were largely designed around identifiable accounts, institutions and relatively predictable transaction flows.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchain-based payment instruments operate differently. A stablecoin can move between &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/zcash-just-got-major-speed-boost-zakura.html"&gt;wallets &lt;/a&gt;around the clock, potentially crossing borders within seconds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a challenge for regulators: how do you maintain transparency and compliance without applying administrative procedures that were designed for a completely different financial system?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Japan's proposed exemption is one example of regulators trying to answer that question.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bigger Stablecoin Picture&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The timing is also notable because Japan has continued developing its digital-asset framework while financial institutions explore yen-based stablecoins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A more practical tax and compliance environment could make it easier for regulated institutions to experiment with blockchain-based payment products.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the success of any reform will ultimately depend on how policymakers balance innovation with consumer protection, tax transparency and financial oversight.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Japan's Financial Services Agency is seeking a &lt;strong&gt;tax-filing exemption for certain trust-based stablecoins&lt;/strong&gt; as part of its fiscal 2027 tax-reform proposal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The central issue is straightforward: trust-based stablecoins can change hands repeatedly, while traditional trust-reporting rules can require documentation when beneficiaries change.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The FSA wants that mismatch addressed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the proposal is adopted, it could reduce administrative friction for trustees and regulated financial institutions working with trust-based stablecoins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But it is important not to overstate the development. &lt;strong&gt;This is a proposal, not a final tax-law change.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For Japan's stablecoin industry, however, the direction is clear: policymakers are trying to build rules that fit the way digital money actually moves.&lt;/p&gt;
