    <title>CLARITY Act Gains Momentum as Sheriffs Drop Opposition Ahead of Senate Vote</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjrtEMfbdTfhbUfLW2FoXqICuxIC1go10kNSPpKNr6IXn7fauiGIf8oK8bW8xwH-GMU6M_RYD92QQVDE6i2PmGcnRuhcjRyXFWOHmyDXrKvZEf0ZnS550AJPBc5XQ6jO6921HikqSZQYOW5u1DHkvbXlwe_9yfENIcqtoI4Al1eShQc4qZ72T6NZwkLo58A/s1672/clarity-act-senate-vote-sheriffs-french-hill.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="CLARITY Act gains momentum as National Sheriffs’ Association shifts to neutral ahead of Senate vote" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjrtEMfbdTfhbUfLW2FoXqICuxIC1go10kNSPpKNr6IXn7fauiGIf8oK8bW8xwH-GMU6M_RYD92QQVDE6i2PmGcnRuhcjRyXFWOHmyDXrKvZEf0ZnS550AJPBc5XQ6jO6921HikqSZQYOW5u1DHkvbXlwe_9yfENIcqtoI4Al1eShQc4qZ72T6NZwkLo58A/w640-h360/clarity-act-senate-vote-sheriffs-french-hill.jpg.png" title="CLARITY Act Gains Momentum Ahead of Senate Vote" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;
&lt;strong&gt;September 4, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. crypto market structure bill known as the &lt;strong&gt;CLARITY Act&lt;/strong&gt; has picked up fresh momentum ahead of a crucial Senate vote, after two developments put the legislation back in focus in Washington.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;House Financial Services Committee Chair &lt;strong&gt;French Hill&lt;/strong&gt; said Senate Majority Leader &lt;strong&gt;John Thune could have the votes&lt;/strong&gt; needed to move the legislation forward. At the same time, the &lt;strong&gt;National Sheriffs’ Association (NSA)&lt;/strong&gt; is dropping its opposition to the bill and moving to a &lt;strong&gt;neutral position&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The developments come less than two weeks before the Senate is scheduled to hold a procedural vote on September 15. That vote will be an important test for the bill, but it will &lt;strong&gt;not be the final vote to pass the CLARITY Act into law&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;French Hill Says John Thune Could Have the Votes&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In an interview with Fox Business, French Hill, who chairs the House Financial Services Committee, expressed optimism about the Senate's ability to advance the CLARITY Act.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hill said Thune could have enough support to move the legislation forward, pointing to the September 15 Senate vote as a key moment for the bill.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The comments were highlighted by CoinMarketCap after Hill discussed the legislation and the Senate's upcoming procedural step. Hill has been one of the prominent congressional supporters of establishing a federal framework for digital assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;His comments are significant because the biggest question facing the CLARITY Act is no longer whether the bill has enough support to remain alive, but whether Senate negotiators can assemble the bipartisan coalition needed to clear the chamber's procedural threshold.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;National Sheriffs’ Association Moves From Opposition to Neutral&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The second major development came from the law-enforcement community.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The National Sheriffs’ Association is dropping its opposition to the CLARITY Act and changing its position to &lt;strong&gt;neutral&lt;/strong&gt;, according to a September 4 report by Semafor.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The organization had previously raised concerns about the bill's potential impact on law enforcement, particularly provisions dealing with decentralized finance and the treatment of certain blockchain developers and infrastructure providers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to Semafor, the NSA's planned letter to lawmakers says the group is stepping back because of the complexity of the legislation and the number of important details that remain under consideration. The organization said it believes the appropriate course is to allow the legislative process to continue.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The distinction is important: &lt;strong&gt;neutral does not mean the National Sheriffs’ Association is endorsing the CLARITY Act.&lt;/strong&gt; Instead, the group is withdrawing its opposition while lawmakers continue negotiating the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the Sheriffs’ Position Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Law-enforcement concerns have been one of the issues surrounding the CLARITY Act's path through Congress.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The National Sheriffs’ Association had argued that parts of the bill could create difficulties for authorities investigating illicit finance involving digital assets. The debate has focused heavily on provisions dealing with decentralized finance and non-custodial software developers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Blockchain Association previously pushed back against those concerns, arguing that the CLARITY Act does not create a broad exemption from anti-money-laundering and sanctions requirements for regulated intermediaries.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The dispute illustrates one of the central challenges facing the legislation: lawmakers are trying to create clearer rules for the digital asset industry without weakening the government's ability to investigate fraud, money laundering and other financial crimes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The NSA's decision to move from opposition to neutrality therefore removes one source of organized resistance, although it does not resolve all of the remaining disagreements surrounding the bill.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;September 15 Vote Is a Procedural Test, Not Final Passage&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One point is especially important for readers following the latest headlines: the Senate's September 15 vote should &lt;strong&gt;not be described as the final CLARITY Act passage vote&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Senate Majority Leader John Thune filed a cloture motion on the motion to proceed to the legislation before the August recess. The Senate is scheduled to consider that procedural step on September 15.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The motion requires &lt;strong&gt;60 votes&lt;/strong&gt; to overcome the procedural hurdle and allow the Senate to formally move forward with consideration of the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the motion succeeds, senators would still need to debate the bill, consider amendments and eventually hold a separate vote on final passage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the procedural vote fails to reach the required threshold, the bill's prospects for advancing during the current congressional session could become significantly more difficult.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;CLARITY Act Has Already Cleared Major Hurdles&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The legislation is formally known as the &lt;strong&gt;Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, H.R. 3633&lt;/strong&gt;. It is designed to establish a broader federal regulatory framework for digital assets and clarify the respective roles of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/standard-chartered-launches-bitcoin-and.html"&gt;Trading Commission&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The House of Representatives passed its version of the CLARITY Act in July 2025 by a bipartisan vote of &lt;strong&gt;294-134&lt;/strong&gt;. The measure received support from 78 Democrats at that stage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bill later cleared another important hurdle in the Senate. The Senate Banking Committee advanced the legislation on May 14, 2026, by a &lt;strong&gt;15-9 vote&lt;/strong&gt;, with two Democrats joining Republicans in supporting the measure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, those committee-level developments did not guarantee support for the bill on the Senate floor. Negotiations have continued over several issues, including ethics provisions, stablecoin rewards and the treatment of decentralized finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;DeFi and Law Enforcement Remain Important Issues&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the more closely watched parts of the legislation concerns decentralized finance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bill attempts to distinguish between financial intermediaries that exercise control over customer assets and developers or infrastructure providers that create non-custodial software without controlling users' funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction has generated debate between the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/kraken-parent-payward-delays-ipo-to-q2.html"&gt;crypto industry&lt;/a&gt; and law-enforcement organizations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Crypto industry representatives argue that software developers who do not control customer assets should not automatically be treated like financial intermediaries. Law-enforcement groups have been more concerned about whether bad actors could exploit those distinctions to avoid regulatory or investigative requirements.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Blockchain Association previously argued that regulated exchanges, brokers and dealers would still face anti-money-laundering, customer-identification and sanctions obligations under the proposed framework.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The disagreement has made the final wording of the legislation particularly important as senators work toward a floor vote.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Ethics Debate Could Still Complicate the Bill&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Even with the NSA stepping back from its opposition, other political disagreements remain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One of the most difficult issues involves restrictions related to government officials and digital assets. Democratic senators have pushed for stronger ethics provisions, including restrictions designed to address concerns about government officials benefiting financially from &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/i-found-old-bitcoin-txid-can-i-recover.html"&gt;crypto ventures&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These negotiations have contributed to delays in bringing the CLARITY Act to the Senate floor.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;As a result, Hill's assessment that Thune could have the votes should be viewed as an indication of optimism rather than confirmation that the legislation has secured the 60 votes it needs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If the September 15 Vote Succeeds?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the Senate reaches the 60-vote threshold on September 15, the CLARITY Act would move into a more formal phase of Senate consideration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That would allow senators to debate the legislation and potentially negotiate or vote on amendments before a final Senate vote.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Even a successful Senate passage would not immediately turn the CLARITY Act into law. If the Senate version differs from the legislation previously approved by the House, lawmakers would need to resolve those differences before the final legislation could reach the president.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In other words, September 15 is potentially a major turning point, but it is only one step in a longer legislative process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What the Latest Developments Mean for Crypto&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The combination of Hill's comments and the NSA's policy shift gives supporters of the CLARITY Act a more favorable backdrop heading into the September vote.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Hill's remarks suggest that Senate leadership believes a path toward the necessary votes may exist. Meanwhile, the NSA's move from opposition to neutrality removes one law-enforcement objection that had complicated the political debate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But neither development guarantees passage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The legislation still needs to overcome the Senate's 60-vote procedural threshold, survive debate and amendments, and ultimately secure enough votes for final passage. Differences between the House and Senate versions could also create another hurdle later in the process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the crypto industry, the importance of the bill is tied to the possibility of replacing years of regulatory uncertainty with clearer federal rules governing digital assets and the responsibilities of the SEC and CFTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For lawmakers, however, the remaining negotiations will determine how much regulatory clarity can be provided without weakening investor protections, financial-crime enforcement or other policy safeguards.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CLARITY Act enters September with a fresh political boost.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;French Hill says Senate Majority Leader John Thune could have the votes needed to move the legislation forward, while the National Sheriffs’ Association is stepping away from its previous opposition and adopting a neutral position.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those developments are meaningful ahead of the September 15 Senate procedural vote, but they should not be interpreted as confirmation that the bill will pass.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next major test is whether supporters can secure the required &lt;strong&gt;60 votes to advance the legislation&lt;/strong&gt;. If they do, the CLARITY Act would still face debate, amendments and a separate final passage vote before it could move any closer to becoming U.S. law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is the CLARITY Act?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The CLARITY Act, formally H.R. 3633, is proposed U.S. legislation designed to establish a federal regulatory framework for digital assets and clarify the roles of the SEC and CFTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What did French Hill say about the CLARITY Act?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;House Financial Services Committee Chair French Hill said Senate Majority Leader John Thune could have the votes needed to move the CLARITY Act forward.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What changed with the National Sheriffs’ Association?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The National Sheriffs’ Association is dropping its opposition to the CLARITY Act and moving to a neutral position, according to a September 4 Semafor report.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does neutral mean the sheriffs support the CLARITY Act?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. A neutral position is not an endorsement. The NSA is stepping back from its opposition while lawmakers continue considering the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;When is the next major Senate vote on the CLARITY Act?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The Senate is scheduled to hold a procedural vote related to advancing the CLARITY Act on September 15, 2026.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does the September 15 vote mean the CLARITY Act will become law?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. The September 15 vote is a procedural cloture vote on the motion to proceed. It is not the final vote on whether the bill becomes law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How many Senate votes are needed for the procedural hurdle?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The cloture vote requires 60 votes to advance the legislation past the procedural hurdle.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Has the CLARITY Act already passed the House?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes. The House passed its version of the legislation in July 2025 by a bipartisan 294-134 vote.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Has the Senate Banking Committee approved the bill?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes. The Senate Banking Committee advanced the legislation by a 15-9 vote on May 14, 2026.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What happens if the Senate advances the CLARITY Act?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The Senate would proceed to debate and consideration of amendments before a separate final passage vote. If the Senate passes a version that differs from the House version, lawmakers would also need to resolve those differences before the bill could reach the president.&lt;/p&gt;

    <content type='html'>Justin Sun's HTX Adapts with On-Chain Wallet Rotation Amid Sanctions
Mon Aug 03 2026 · 6 min read · 1063 words
Justin Sun's HTX Adapts with On-Chain Wallet Rotation Amid Sanctions
In a strategic move to navigate the complexities of international regulations, Justin Sun's cryptocurrency exchange, HTX, has implemented a rotation of its on-chain wallets across various blockchains. This decision comes in light of recent sanctions imposed by the UK government on the platform. According to TRM Labs, this wallet rotation is part of HTX's efforts to maintain operational integrity and continue serving its users despite regulatory challenges.

Overview of HTX and Its Significance in Crypto Market
HTX, formerly known as Huobi Global, is a prominent player in the cryptocurrency exchange landscape. Founded by Justin Sun, a well-known figure in the crypto world for his role as the founder of Tron and his extensive involvement with blockchain technology, HTX has become synonymous with innovative trading solutions and user engagement strategies. As one of the largest exchanges by trading volume globally, it offers various services such as spot trading, futures contracts, and staking options that appeal to both retail and institutional investors.

The significance of HTX extends beyond mere numbers; it represents a pivotal point for many traders who rely on its liquidity and diverse asset offerings. However, like many crypto exchanges operating at scale, it faces increasing scrutiny from regulators worldwide.

'Rotating' Mechanism: How Hot Wallets Work Across Blockchains
Hot wallets are digital wallets connected to the internet that facilitate quick transactions but are more susceptible to security breaches than cold storage alternatives. The rotating mechanism involves periodically changing these hot wallets across different blockchains to mitigate risks associated with potential hacks or regulatory actions.

By implementing this strategy during turbulent times marked by sanctions from authorities like those in the UK, HTX seeks not only to protect user funds but also ensure compliance with evolving legal frameworks governing cryptocurrencies. This proactive approach allows them flexibility while maintaining operational continuity.

(TRM Labs) Analysis of the Impact of UK Sanctions on Crypto Exchanges
TRM Labs has conducted an analysis detailing how sanctions affect cryptocurrency exchanges like HTX. The report emphasizes that such measures can significantly hinder an exchange’s ability to process transactions smoothly due to increased scrutiny over financial flows.

For instance,
when an exchange is sanctioned by major economies like the UK,
it may face restrictions on accessing traditional financial networks or banking services necessary for smooth operations.
This could lead not just to liquidity issues but also affect user trust if they perceive their assets are at risk due directly or indirectly from regulatory pressures.

The implications extend beyond immediate operational concerns; they reflect broader trends within global finance where cryptocurrencies must increasingly adapt themselves toward compliance rather than existing solely outside conventional monetary systems.

Frequently Asked Questions
What are on-chain wallets?
On-chain wallets are digital wallets that store cryptocurrencies directly on the blockchain, allowing users to send and receive funds securely and transparently.

How does wallet rotation work?
Wallet rotation involves periodically changing the addresses of hot wallets across different blockchains to enhance security and mitigate risks associated with hacks or regulatory actions.

Why was HTX sanctioned by the UK?
HTX was sanctioned by the UK government due to regulatory concerns regarding compliance with international laws governing cryptocurrency exchanges.

What impact do sanctions have on crypto exchanges?
'Sanctions can restrict an exchange's ability to process transactions, access banking services, and maintain user trust, potentially leading to liquidity issues.'

'Who is Justin Sun?'
'Justin Sun is a prominent figure in the cryptocurrency industry, known as the founder of Tron and for his innovative contributions to blockchain technology.'

'What are the potential risks for investors due to these sanctions?'
'Investors may face increased volatility, liquidity issues, and potential loss of access to their assets if exchanges struggle under regulatory pressures.'

'How can other exchanges respond to similar regulatory pressures?'
'Other exchanges can adopt proactive compliance strategies, enhance security measures like wallet rotation, and improve communication with regulators.'

'What does this mean for the future of crypto regulation?'
'The ongoing scrutiny suggests that future regulations will likely become stricter as governments seek greater oversight over cryptocurrency activities.'

    <title>Grayscale Zcash ETF Files for 3-for-1 Share Split: What ZCSH Investors Need to Know</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEg4sMpQ3OqdzDBxvZirk4rCaq0MxnYe3a2eE7T0qGPsY35OEDKqX4s87uxQMUs4Xw9gVJ5C3fa3fpgH_iBv76wSXw_6OPQ88SSIpMupdOgKbET21ZBc_KQgW9gEUdiXQz-_Jig-btIYliZ78MXbxCdmf4dSVrU3YPzKSfDDC2DYfvHtrBq7s168KCGZeNZL/s1672/grayscale-zcash-etf-zcsh-3-for-1-share-split.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Grayscale Zcash ETF ZCSH 3-for-1 share split explained for investors" border="0" data-original-height="940" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEg4sMpQ3OqdzDBxvZirk4rCaq0MxnYe3a2eE7T0qGPsY35OEDKqX4s87uxQMUs4Xw9gVJ5C3fa3fpgH_iBv76wSXw_6OPQ88SSIpMupdOgKbET21ZBc_KQgW9gEUdiXQz-_Jig-btIYliZ78MXbxCdmf4dSVrU3YPzKSfDDC2DYfvHtrBq7s168KCGZeNZL/w640-h360/grayscale-zcash-etf-zcsh-3-for-1-share-split.webp.png" title="Grayscale Zcash ETF 3-for-1 Share Split" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;Grayscale’s Zcash ETF is preparing for a 3-for-1 forward share split that will give eligible investors two additional ZCSH shares for every share they already own.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important part is that the split does not automatically increase the value of an investor’s position. Instead, the number of shares will rise while the value represented by each individual share is expected to fall proportionally.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to a September 18 filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, shareholders of record at the close of trading on &lt;strong&gt;September 28, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, will receive two additional shares for every ZCSH share they hold. The additional shares are scheduled to be distributed after the market closes on &lt;strong&gt;September 29&lt;/strong&gt;, with split-adjusted trading expected to begin before the market opens on &lt;strong&gt;September 30&lt;/strong&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is the Grayscale Zcash ETF Share Split?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The product, known by the ticker &lt;strong&gt;ZCSH&lt;/strong&gt;, trades on NYSE Arca and provides investors with exchange-traded exposure to Zcash.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Under the planned 3-for-1 forward split, one existing ZCSH share will become three shares after the adjustment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, an investor holding &lt;strong&gt;10 ZCSH shares&lt;/strong&gt; before the split would receive 20 additional shares and hold &lt;strong&gt;30 shares&lt;/strong&gt; after the split.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But those 30 shares would not represent three times the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/sent-btc-to-wrong-address-what-happens.html"&gt;original investment.&lt;/a&gt; Each post-split share is expected to represent approximately one-third of the NAV per share that existed before the split. Grayscale's filing provides a hypothetical example of 10 shares at $300 each becoming 30 shares at $100 each, leaving the total hypothetical value at $3,000. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;The figures above are Grayscale's hypothetical illustration and are not a prediction of ZCSH's future market price.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;When Is the ZCSH 3-for-1 Split Happening?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are three dates investors should know:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;September 28, 2026:&lt;/strong&gt; Record date. Shareholders of record at market close are eligible for the split.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;September 29, 2026:&lt;/strong&gt; Payment date. The two additional shares per existing share are scheduled to be distributed after market close.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;September 30, 2026:&lt;/strong&gt; Split-adjusted trading is expected to begin before the market opens.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The SEC filing states that the fund will continue trading on &lt;strong&gt;NYSE Arca under the ticker ZCSH&lt;/strong&gt;. Its CUSIP number will also remain unchanged. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does the Zcash ETF Split Give Investors 3 Times More Money?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A 3-for-1 share split increases the number of shares but does not, by itself, increase the total value of an investor's position.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Consider a simple example. If someone owns one ZCSH share worth $300 before the split, that position would become three shares worth approximately $100 each based on the split mechanics. The investor has three shares instead of one, but the combined value remains approximately $300, assuming no other market movement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why investors should not interpret the headline “3-for-1 split” as a three-times return.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Is Grayscale Splitting ZCSH Shares?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Grayscale says the forward split is expected to decrease the price per share while proportionally increasing the number of shares outstanding. The underlying economic value of the shareholder's position is not changed by the split itself. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A lower nominal share price can make individual shares easier for some investors to buy in smaller dollar amounts. It is important, however, to distinguish accessibility from &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/rex-launches-assx-2x-leveraged-etf.html"&gt;investment &lt;/a&gt;value: reducing the price of one share does not change the value of the assets represented by the entire position.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;ZCSH Will Keep the Same Ticker&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Investors do not need to search for a new ticker after the split.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Grayscale's filing confirms that the fund will continue trading under &lt;strong&gt;ZCSH&lt;/strong&gt; on NYSE Arca. The CUSIP number will also remain unchanged. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The changes are primarily the number of shares outstanding and the split-adjusted value represented by each share.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Is the ZCSH Split Getting Attention?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The timing is notable because ZCSH has attracted significant investor interest since beginning to trade.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent market reports said the fund had attracted more than &lt;strong&gt;$233 million in cumulative inflows&lt;/strong&gt; since its August 25 launch, while net assets approached &lt;strong&gt;$890 million&lt;/strong&gt; by September 17. Those figures were reported by The Block based on market data. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Decrypt also reported more than $233 million in inflows and approximately $890 million in net assets as of September 17. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those figures help explain why the Zcash ETF has become a closely watched crypto investment product, but the share split itself should not be treated as proof of future price performance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is Zcash and Why Does ZCSH Track It?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Zcash, or ZEC&lt;/strong&gt;, is a cryptocurrency known for its focus on transaction privacy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ZCSH gives investors access to Zcash exposure through an exchange-traded security rather than requiring them to directly hold ZEC in a personal crypto wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction can matter for investors who already use traditional brokerage accounts and prefer an exchange-traded structure for digital-asset exposure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens to ZCSH's NAV After the Split?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The SEC filing provides a clear answer: immediately following the forward split, the NAV per share is expected to be approximately &lt;strong&gt;one-third of the NAV per share immediately before the split&lt;/strong&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, the number of shares outstanding will increase proportionally.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is simply the mathematical effect of dividing each existing share into three pieces. The fund does not suddenly own three times as much Zcash because the share count has increased.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If You Own 100 ZCSH Shares?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Suppose an investor is eligible for the split and owns &lt;strong&gt;100 ZCSH shares&lt;/strong&gt; at the relevant record date.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The investor would receive &lt;strong&gt;200 additional shares&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;After the distribution, the investor would therefore have &lt;strong&gt;300 ZCSH shares&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, each post-split share would represent approximately one-third of the pre-split NAV per share. The investor's total position does not automatically become three times larger simply because the share count has tripled.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Will the Split Change the Price of Zcash?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. The share split applies to &lt;strong&gt;ZCSH shares&lt;/strong&gt;, not to the Zcash &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/rex-launches-assx-2x-leveraged-etf.html"&gt;cryptocurrency &lt;/a&gt;itself.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The split does not create additional ZEC coins or change Zcash's blockchain supply. It changes the share structure of the exchange-traded fund.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ZEC and ZCSH can still move in price after the split because of normal market conditions, including changes in the value of Zcash and supply and demand for the ETF shares.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Is the ZCSH Share Split Bullish?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The split itself should not automatically be described as bullish or bearish.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Mechanically, it increases the number of shares and reduces the value represented by each individual share. Whether ZCSH rises or falls after split-adjusted trading begins will depend on market conditions rather than the mathematical split alone.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction is particularly important in crypto markets, where the underlying assets can experience substantial price volatility.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Should ZCSH Investors Watch?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For existing shareholders, the main dates and mechanics are straightforward:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Record date:&lt;/strong&gt; September 28, 2026.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Additional shares distributed:&lt;/strong&gt; After market close on September 29.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Split-adjusted trading:&lt;/strong&gt; Expected before market open on September 30.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Split ratio:&lt;/strong&gt; 3-for-1.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Additional shares received:&lt;/strong&gt; Two for every one share held.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Ticker:&lt;/strong&gt; ZCSH remains unchanged.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;CUSIP:&lt;/strong&gt; Remains unchanged.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Expected NAV per share:&lt;/strong&gt; Approximately one-third of the pre-split level immediately after the split.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Investors can also check their brokerage account after the distribution to confirm that the additional shares have been reflected correctly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions About the Grayscale Zcash ETF Split&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is the Grayscale Zcash ETF ticker?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The Grayscale Zcash ETF trades under the ticker &lt;strong&gt;ZCSH&lt;/strong&gt; on NYSE Arca. The ticker is expected to remain unchanged after the split. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;When is the ZCSH 3-for-1 share split?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The record date is September 28, 2026. Two additional shares for every existing share are scheduled to be distributed after market close on September 29, with split-adjusted trading expected to begin before market open on September 30. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How many ZCSH shares will I receive?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Eligible shareholders will receive two additional shares for every one ZCSH share they own. Therefore, one pre-split share becomes three post-split shares in total.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does the ZCSH split increase my investment value?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. The split itself does not automatically increase the total value of an investor's position. The number of shares increases while the value represented by each share decreases proportionally. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Will ZCSH keep the same ticker after the split?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes. Grayscale's SEC filing says the fund will continue trading under the &lt;strong&gt;ZCSH&lt;/strong&gt; ticker on NYSE Arca, and its CUSIP number will remain unchanged. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is the ZCSH split the same thing as a Zcash token split?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. The event applies to shares of Grayscale's Zcash ETF. It does not split ZEC tokens or change the Zcash blockchain's supply.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why is Grayscale doing a 3-for-1 split?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;The filing says the split is expected to reduce the price per share while increasing the number of shares outstanding proportionally. A lower per-share price can make individual shares more accessible to some investors, but the split itself does not change the total value of a shareholder's position. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Grayscale's Zcash ETF is preparing for a &lt;strong&gt;3-for-1 forward share split&lt;/strong&gt;, giving eligible shareholders two additional ZCSH shares for every one share they already own.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The key dates are &lt;strong&gt;September 28 for the record date, September 29 for the additional-share distribution and September 30 for split-adjusted trading&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most important point for investors is simple: &lt;strong&gt;three shares do not mean three times the investment value.&lt;/strong&gt; The share count increases while the expected NAV per share falls proportionally. Grayscale's own example shows how 10 shares at a hypothetical $300 each become 30 shares at $100 each, leaving the total value at $3,000. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The fund will continue trading as &lt;strong&gt;ZCSH on NYSE Arca&lt;/strong&gt;, with the same CUSIP number. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For anyone following the growing market for crypto exchange-traded products, the ZCSH split is a useful example of how traditional ETF share mechanics are being applied to digital-asset exposure.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Can a Bitcoin Transaction Get Stuck Forever?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgCyqmg74uSWCy_Bx68pmZMULQv-UtdCx5gEDOB4fjaXe9Sxfnx7CYe51ySV11_qU3ADvFonx-ypoy1M8ad1oonl8yZbiefMRVRadsSXWwwG-61QpGGcye_BekAhRDupTdgsFK3TVSmTADQk0rk9CC855hKQ7j0MUXTvgDJBJJI-phDlWczDoQGultCM3JV/s1672/bitcoin-transaction-stuck-forever-pending-confirmation.jpg%20(2).png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Can a Bitcoin transaction get stuck forever while waiting for confirmation" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgCyqmg74uSWCy_Bx68pmZMULQv-UtdCx5gEDOB4fjaXe9Sxfnx7CYe51ySV11_qU3ADvFonx-ypoy1M8ad1oonl8yZbiefMRVRadsSXWwwG-61QpGGcye_BekAhRDupTdgsFK3TVSmTADQk0rk9CC855hKQ7j0MUXTvgDJBJJI-phDlWczDoQGultCM3JV/w640-h360/bitcoin-transaction-stuck-forever-pending-confirmation.jpg%20(2).png" title="Can a Bitcoin Transaction Get Stuck Forever?" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;You send Bitcoin, the wallet says &lt;strong&gt;“pending,”&lt;/strong&gt; and then nothing seems to happen. Minutes turn into hours. Maybe even a full day passes, and the transaction still has zero confirmations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That naturally raises a worrying question: &lt;strong&gt;Can a Bitcoin transaction get stuck forever?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Usually, no.&lt;/strong&gt; An unconfirmed Bitcoin transaction does not remain permanently trapped in the network simply because it has a low fee. Depending on what happens to the transaction, it can eventually confirm, be replaced by another transaction, or disappear from individual nodes' mempools after being dropped. If the transaction is still unconfirmed, the Bitcoin itself has not necessarily been lost.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important distinction is between a transaction being &lt;strong&gt;delayed&lt;/strong&gt; and Bitcoin being &lt;strong&gt;permanently lost&lt;/strong&gt;. They are not the same thing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Miners may prefer higher-fee transactions&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;May confirm later or be dropped&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;RBF-enabled&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Parent and child can be confirmed together&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Nodes no longer keep the unconfirmed transaction&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Funds can generally be spent again by the sender&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Already confirmed&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Transaction is part of the blockchain&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;It cannot simply be cancelled&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can a Bitcoin Transaction Really Get Stuck Forever?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In practical terms, an ordinary valid Bitcoin transaction does not sit forever in one universal waiting line.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin does not have one centralized mempool that every transaction must remain in until a miner picks it. Individual nodes maintain their own mempools, and those &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-can-sending-10-bitcoin-cost-more.html"&gt;mempools&lt;/a&gt; can differ.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A transaction that has not yet been confirmed is therefore in a temporary state. It may continue to be relayed, eventually get included in a block, be replaced through a fee-bumping mechanism such as RBF, or be removed from nodes' mempools.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why the word &lt;strong&gt;“forever”&lt;/strong&gt; can be misleading when talking about pending Bitcoin transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bigger question is not whether the transaction will remain visible forever. The question is &lt;strong&gt;what happens to the coins if the transaction never confirms?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Do Bitcoin Transactions Get Stuck?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most common reason is a fee rate that is too low compared with the transactions competing for block space.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin blocks have limited capacity. Miners generally have an economic incentive to prioritize transactions that offer attractive fees relative to the amount of block space they consume.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin fees are therefore not simply based on how much BTC you are sending. A small transaction can require a similar amount of block space to a much larger transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why sending $10 worth of Bitcoin can sometimes cost more than sending $1,000 worth of Bitcoin if the smaller payment happens to require a larger transaction structure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When network demand rises, transactions offering low fee rates can wait longer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is the Bitcoin Mempool?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The &lt;strong&gt;mempool&lt;/strong&gt; is essentially temporary storage for transactions that have been broadcast but have not yet been confirmed in a block.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is important to understand that there is no single global mempool. Different Bitcoin nodes maintain their own collections of unconfirmed transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This explains why one block explorer may show a transaction as pending while another node may no longer have it in its local mempool.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Mempool data can also change as transactions are confirmed, replaced or removed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The mempool is therefore better thought of as a temporary holding area rather than a permanent queue.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Long Can a Bitcoin Transaction Stay Pending?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no universal guaranteed maximum confirmation time for every Bitcoin transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A transaction with an attractive fee rate may confirm relatively quickly. A transaction with a very low fee rate can remain unconfirmed much longer, especially when the network is busy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org notes that transactions paying too low a fee can take much longer to receive their first confirmation. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the node-policy level, unconfirmed transactions can also eventually be removed from mempools. Current Bitcoin Core policy uses a default mempool expiry of about &lt;strong&gt;14 days&lt;/strong&gt;, although individual nodes and network conditions can differ.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does &lt;strong&gt;not&lt;/strong&gt; mean every transaction automatically disappears after exactly 14 days. It means nodes are not required to keep an unconfirmed transaction in memory indefinitely.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If Your Transaction Is Dropped?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the most misunderstood parts of Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If an unconfirmed transaction disappears from a node's mempool, that does not mean the Bitcoin was burned.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction never became part of a confirmed block, the original coins have not been permanently transferred by that transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Depending on the wallet and the network state, the wallet may eventually be able to treat the inputs as available again and create a new transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, wallets can behave differently while they are still tracking the old transaction. Sometimes the old transaction may also be rebroadcast and appear again on the network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why it is better to check the transaction ID and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-bitcoin-be-recovered-without-seed.html"&gt;wallet&lt;/a&gt; status rather than immediately assuming the BTC has disappeared.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can You Speed Up a Stuck Bitcoin Transaction?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Often, yes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are two important mechanisms to understand: &lt;strong&gt;Replace-By-Fee (RBF)&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;Child-Pays-For-Parent (CPFP)&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;1. Replace-By-Fee (RBF)&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;RBF allows an unconfirmed Bitcoin transaction to be replaced with another transaction that spends the same coins while offering a higher fee under the applicable replacement rules.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The idea is simple: if the original transaction is not attractive enough for miners, a higher-fee replacement gives miners a stronger economic incentive to include the replacement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;RBF is an &lt;strong&gt;unconfirmed-transaction mechanism&lt;/strong&gt;. Once a transaction has been confirmed, you cannot use RBF to simply undo it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's RBF rules are described in BIP 125, while modern Bitcoin software also supports broader full-RBF relay policies. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;2. Child-Pays-For-Parent (CPFP)&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;CPFP works differently.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of replacing the original transaction, a new transaction is created that spends an output from the unconfirmed transaction and pays a sufficiently high fee.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because the child transaction depends on the parent, miners can consider the combined economics of the package when deciding whether to include the transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This can be especially useful when the &lt;strong&gt;recipient&lt;/strong&gt; controls an output from the stuck transaction and the original sender cannot increase the fee.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Mempool's documentation lists both RBF and CPFP as established ways to increase the effective fee rate of a stuck transaction. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can You Cancel a Stuck Bitcoin Transaction?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Not in the normal sense of pressing a universal “cancel” button.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin transactions are designed to become final once confirmed. Before confirmation, however, an eligible transaction may be replaced.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you accidentally sent BTC to the wrong address and the transaction has already confirmed, RBF cannot rescue you. Bitcoin does not have a central authority that can reverse the blockchain transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction is still unconfirmed and your wallet supports an appropriate replacement mechanism, you may be able to replace it with a transaction that sends the funds somewhere else.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is better described as &lt;strong&gt;replacement&lt;/strong&gt;, not cancellation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If You Sent Bitcoin to the Wrong Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This situation requires extra caution.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction is still unconfirmed and your wallet supports RBF, there may be a possibility of replacing the transaction, depending on the transaction's structure and the wallet's capabilities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But if the transaction has already been confirmed, the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-someone-find-your-name-from-bitcoin-wallet.html"&gt;Bitcoin network&lt;/a&gt; does not provide a normal reversal mechanism.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The only practical recovery route may then involve the owner of the receiving address voluntarily sending the Bitcoin back.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the address belongs to an exchange or another identifiable service, contacting that service may be worth trying. Recovery is not guaranteed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does a Stuck Transaction Mean My Bitcoin Is Lost?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No—not automatically.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A pending transaction is different from a confirmed transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When you create a Bitcoin transaction, the transaction attempts to spend specific unspent transaction outputs, commonly called &lt;strong&gt;UTXOs&lt;/strong&gt;. Until the transaction is confirmed, the blockchain has not permanently recorded that spend.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The wallet may still show the BTC as pending or unavailable because it is tracking the transaction, but that is different from the Bitcoin being destroyed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction eventually gets dropped without confirmation, the wallet can generally return to a state where those coins can be spent again, although wallet software may need to rescan, refresh or otherwise reconcile its transaction history.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If My Transaction Has Been Pending for Days?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Do not immediately send another transaction without understanding what happened to the first one.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Start with the &lt;strong&gt;transaction ID (TXID)&lt;/strong&gt; and check it on a reputable Bitcoin block explorer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Then determine:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether the transaction is still unconfirmed.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;What fee rate it paid.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether it signals or otherwise qualifies for RBF in the relevant wallet/network policy.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether the transaction has descendants that affect replacement.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether the transaction has disappeared from the mempools being monitored.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Whether your wallet has a “speed up,” “bump fee,” or RBF option.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction was created through an exchange, the situation can be different because the exchange controls the transaction construction and may not expose RBF or CPFP controls to customers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can a Bitcoin Transaction Disappear and Then Come Back?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes, this can happen.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Remember that Bitcoin does not have one permanent global mempool. A transaction can disappear from one node's mempool while still being held by another node or wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A wallet may also rebroadcast a transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So seeing a transaction disappear from one explorer does not necessarily mean the transaction has been permanently abandoned.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is another reason why the &lt;strong&gt;TXID&lt;/strong&gt; is important when troubleshooting a pending payment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Once a Bitcoin Transaction Is Confirmed?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once a transaction is included in a valid Bitcoin block, it has received its first confirmation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Additional blocks add additional confirmations and make the transaction increasingly difficult to reverse through a blockchain reorganization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org explains that each additional confirmation increases the consensus that the received bitcoins have not been spent elsewhere. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For everyday transactions, the number of confirmations considered sufficient can depend on the recipient, transaction size and risk tolerance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important point for this article is simple: &lt;strong&gt;RBF and ordinary mempool troubleshooting apply to unconfirmed transactions.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Low Fees Can Cause Long Delays&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin block space is scarce.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When many users want their transactions confirmed at the same time, fee competition can increase. A transaction that looked perfectly reasonable when it was created can become less attractive if the market suddenly becomes more competitive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This can happen during major market moves, periods of unusually high Bitcoin activity or other events that increase demand for block space.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The result is a fee market in which transactions offering higher fee rates can generally become more attractive to miners.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org explains that transaction fees are related to the size of the transaction rather than simply the amount of Bitcoin being transferred. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Is There a Difference Between “Pending” and “Dropped”?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes, and the difference is important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Pending:&lt;/strong&gt; The transaction is still being tracked as unconfirmed and may be present in one or more mempools.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Dropped:&lt;/strong&gt; A node has removed the transaction from its mempool. This does not mean the transaction was confirmed or that the Bitcoin was destroyed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Confirmed:&lt;/strong&gt; The transaction has been included in the blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These three states should not be treated as interchangeable.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 650px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Status&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Blockchain?&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Can RBF Apply?&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Unconfirmed&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Potentially&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Dropped from mempool&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;No&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;A new transaction may be created if funds are available again&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Yes&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;No&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How to Avoid Getting a Bitcoin Transaction Stuck&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You cannot guarantee an exact confirmation time, but you can reduce the risk of unnecessary delays.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Check the fee estimate:&lt;/strong&gt; Use your wallet's current fee recommendations before broadcasting.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Understand fee rates:&lt;/strong&gt; Bitcoin fees are commonly discussed in satoshis per virtual byte, or sat/vB.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Use RBF when appropriate:&lt;/strong&gt; If your wallet supports it, RBF can provide a useful fee-bumping option.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Do not panic after a short delay:&lt;/strong&gt; A pending transaction does not automatically mean something has gone wrong.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Keep your wallet software updated:&lt;/strong&gt; Wallet features and fee-management options can change.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Keep your recovery information secure:&lt;/strong&gt; Never share a seed phrase or private key with someone claiming they can “unstick” your transaction.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What You Should Do If Your Bitcoin Transaction Is Stuck&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your BTC transaction has been pending for longer than expected, follow this basic checklist:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Find the transaction ID.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Check the transaction on a reputable Bitcoin block explorer.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Confirm that it is genuinely unconfirmed.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Look at the transaction's fee rate.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Check whether your wallet supports RBF or fee bumping.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;If you are the recipient and control an unconfirmed output, check whether CPFP is supported.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;If the transaction has disappeared, refresh or rescan the wallet before creating another transaction.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;If the payment originated from an exchange, contact the exchange rather than attempting random replacement transactions.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Mempool's own guidance recommends using the service or wallet that created the transaction when you are unsure how to apply RBF or CPFP. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can Bitcoin Transactions Get Stuck Forever? The Real Answer&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin transactions can certainly become &lt;strong&gt;very delayed&lt;/strong&gt;, especially when the fee rate is too low relative to current demand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But an ordinary unconfirmed transaction does not simply become a permanent blockchain transaction that sits in limbo forever.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It can be confirmed. It can potentially be replaced. Or it can eventually disappear from node mempools if it remains unconfirmed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most important thing to remember is that &lt;strong&gt;an unconfirmed Bitcoin transaction is not the same thing as a confirmed loss of Bitcoin.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And if you are dealing with a stuck transaction right now, the first step is not to panic or send another payment blindly. Find the TXID, check its status and fee rate, and determine whether RBF, CPFP or simply waiting is the appropriate option.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can a Bitcoin transaction remain pending forever?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It can remain unresolved for a long time, but an unconfirmed transaction is not permanently stored by every Bitcoin node. Nodes can eventually remove old or low-priority transactions from their mempools.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What happens to Bitcoin if a transaction never confirms?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction never becomes part of the blockchain, the original spend has not been confirmed. Once the transaction is dropped and the wallet recognizes the inputs as available again, the funds can generally be spent in a new transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can I speed up a stuck Bitcoin transaction?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Potentially. RBF can replace an eligible unconfirmed transaction with a higher-fee transaction. CPFP can increase the effective fee of a parent transaction by attaching a higher-fee child transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can I cancel a Bitcoin transaction after it is confirmed?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. Bitcoin does not provide a normal cancellation button for confirmed blockchain transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Does a low Bitcoin fee mean my BTC is lost?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;No. A low fee can make confirmation slower, but it does not by itself mean the Bitcoin has been lost.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;How long should I wait for a Bitcoin transaction?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is no single answer. Confirmation time depends on the transaction's fee rate, network demand and other factors. A low-fee transaction can take substantially longer than one paying a competitive fee.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is RBF in Bitcoin?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;RBF, or Replace-By-Fee, is a mechanism that can allow an unconfirmed transaction to be replaced with a higher-fee version under applicable relay and wallet rules.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What is CPFP in Bitcoin?&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;CPFP means Child-Pays-For-Parent. It uses a new transaction with a higher fee to encourage miners to include an earlier unconfirmed parent transaction as well.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Can a Bitcoin transaction get stuck forever?&lt;/strong&gt; Not in the simple sense that a pending transaction will remain permanently trapped in the blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A low-fee transaction can remain unconfirmed for a surprisingly long time, but Bitcoin's transaction and mempool system provides several possible outcomes: confirmation, replacement or eventual removal from mempools.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your transaction is stuck, check the TXID first. Then look at the fee rate and determine whether your wallet supports RBF or whether CPFP is possible. Most importantly, remember that &lt;strong&gt;pending does not automatically mean lost.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEg7qDV3HdnWO2njYMKi-IwH7NmoRqsye_7CoyPY4x9EqaRl2dn2JOTpG76i_MkMf8yMyz9wtkQLI28gubb8ubaEa_tar3WCd1Zcr_RwT2sLf6AITvwbBbrSHIPvNsc4gGs2vTQgVooeUZPl865qthIVLE6GsuzbLbGkFP5ZGluTYLxjxiA-7kLGks9PM91x/s1536/rex-tuttle-assx-2x-etf-strive-bitcoin-treasury.webp.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="REX and Tuttle launch ASSX 2X ETF tied to Bitcoin treasury firm Strive" border="0" data-original-height="1024" data-original-width="1536" height="426" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEg7qDV3HdnWO2njYMKi-IwH7NmoRqsye_7CoyPY4x9EqaRl2dn2JOTpG76i_MkMf8yMyz9wtkQLI28gubb8ubaEa_tar3WCd1Zcr_RwT2sLf6AITvwbBbrSHIPvNsc4gGs2vTQgVooeUZPl865qthIVLE6GsuzbLbGkFP5ZGluTYLxjxiA-7kLGks9PM91x/w640-h426/rex-tuttle-assx-2x-etf-strive-bitcoin-treasury.webp.png" title="ASSX 2X ETF and Strive Bitcoin Treasury" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;REX Shares and Tuttle Capital Management have launched ASSX, a new 2X leveraged ETF designed to provide amplified daily exposure to Strive, the Bitcoin-focused public company trading under the ticker ASST.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The &lt;strong&gt;T-REX 2X Long ASST Daily Target ETF&lt;/strong&gt; trades on Cboe under the ticker &lt;strong&gt;ASSX&lt;/strong&gt; and seeks to deliver 200% of the daily performance of Strive shares before fees and expenses. The fund began trading on September 18, giving traders a new leveraged product tied to one of the publicly traded companies building a large Bitcoin treasury. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is the ASSX ETF?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ASSX is a leveraged single-stock ETF. Its underlying asset is &lt;strong&gt;Strive, Inc. (NASDAQ: ASST)&lt;/strong&gt;, not Bitcoin itself.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The fund's objective is to provide &lt;strong&gt;200% of ASST's daily performance&lt;/strong&gt;, before fees and expenses. In simple terms, if ASST gains 1% during a trading session, ASSX is designed to target approximately a 2% gain for that day. Likewise, a 1% decline in ASST would generally translate into an approximately 2% decline in ASSX before fees, expenses and other tracking effects. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important because ASSX is &lt;strong&gt;not a 2X Bitcoin ETF&lt;/strong&gt;. The fund does not seek to deliver twice Bitcoin's daily return and does not simply hold Bitcoin to generate its exposure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;ASSX Began Trading on Cboe&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;REX Shares and Tuttle Capital Management announced the launch on September 18, 2026. The ETF is listed on the &lt;strong&gt;Cboe BZX Exchange&lt;/strong&gt; under the ticker ASSX.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;REX describes the product as the first U.S. ETF offering 2X daily long exposure specifically to Strive's ASST shares. The fund is designed around a one-trading-day objective, with its leverage reset each day. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The launch expands the T-REX lineup of leveraged and inverse products connected to companies and assets that have become closely associated with the digital-asset market.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Strive Matters to the Bitcoin Market&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Strive has transformed its balance sheet around a &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/visa-memecoin-card-rewards-crossmint-robinhood-wallet.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt; treasury strategy. The company's latest September 14 SEC filing reported that it held &lt;strong&gt;25,000 BTC as of September 11, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company added 469 BTC between September 8 and September 11 at an average purchase price of approximately &lt;strong&gt;$77,954 per bitcoin&lt;/strong&gt;, including fees and expenses. That increased its Bitcoin holdings from 24,531 BTC on September 4 to 25,000 BTC on September 11. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because ASST represents equity in a company with substantial Bitcoin exposure, the stock can be influenced by Bitcoin prices, the market value assigned to Strive's treasury holdings, capital-raising activity and broader investor sentiment toward Bitcoin treasury companies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;ASSX Is Different From a Spot Bitcoin ETF&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The easiest way to understand ASSX is to separate the three layers involved:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="overflow-x: auto;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;

&lt;/tr&gt;

&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This means ASSX adds another layer of leverage on top of a stock that is already closely associated with Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Daily Reset Is the Key Detail&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ASSX's 2X target applies to &lt;strong&gt;one trading day&lt;/strong&gt;. It does not promise to produce twice ASST's return over a week, month or year.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because the fund resets its exposure every trading day, the effects of compounding can cause its longer-term performance to differ substantially from twice the cumulative return of ASST.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, suppose ASST rises 10% on one day and then falls 10% the next day. The stock would be below its original level after those two moves. A daily leveraged product would experience a different path because the 2X exposure is recalculated after each session.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;REX explicitly states that ASSX is designed for investors who understand daily leveraged products and are prepared to monitor their positions frequently. The issuer also warns that the fund can lose its entire principal in a single day if ASST falls by more than 50%. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;ASSX Does Not Hold Bitcoin Directly&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Another important distinction is that investors buying ASSX are not directly buying Bitcoin through the ETF.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The fund seeks leveraged exposure to &lt;strong&gt;Strive's common stock&lt;/strong&gt;. REX says the fund may use derivative instruments such as swap agreements to obtain its targeted exposure. As a result, investors are exposed not only to movements in &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/coinbase-and-robinhood-could-benefit-as.html"&gt;Bitcoin-related sentiment&lt;/a&gt; but also to risks associated with Strive's stock and the fund's leveraged structure. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That can make the product behave differently from both Bitcoin and ASST over longer periods.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Strive's Bitcoin Treasury Reached 25,000 BTC&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The ASSX launch comes as Strive continues expanding its Bitcoin treasury.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to Strive's September 14 Form 8-K, the company held 25,000 BTC as of September 11. The latest purchase added 469 BTC at an average price of approximately $77,954 per coin. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The company had previously reported purchasing 1,375 BTC between August 31 and September 4 at an average price of approximately $79,281 per Bitcoin. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those purchases demonstrate why Strive has become increasingly connected to the Bitcoin treasury-company segment, although ASST remains an equity security rather than Bitcoin itself.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;ASSX Adds Another Leveraged Bitcoin-Linked Trading Product&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;REX and Tuttle already offer leveraged products connected to other companies associated with digital assets. Their lineup includes products linked to companies such as Strategy, BitMine, Cipher Mining, Circle and &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/trump-announces-ai-force-and-ai-czar-as.html"&gt;SharpLink&lt;/a&gt;. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ASSX extends that strategy to Strive, giving active traders a vehicle specifically targeting daily moves in ASST.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The structure is particularly notable because investors can already gain exposure to Strive's Bitcoin treasury strategy through ASST itself. ASSX adds a second layer by targeting twice the stock's daily move before fees and expenses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Traders Need to Understand&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The attraction of a 2X daily ETF is straightforward: a relatively small move in the underlying stock can produce a larger percentage move in the leveraged fund.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But leverage works in both directions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If ASST falls sharply, ASSX can decline approximately twice as much on that trading day before fees and other effects. The daily reset can also produce significant differences between ASSX's longer-term return and a simple 2X calculation of ASST's cumulative performance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;REX therefore describes the fund as a product for knowledgeable investors who understand leveraged ETFs and are willing to monitor their portfolios actively. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why ASSX Is Getting Attention&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The launch arrives as Bitcoin treasury companies continue to develop new ways of raising capital and giving investors exposure to corporate Bitcoin strategies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Strive's 25,000-BTC treasury makes ASST a notable equity proxy for investors following the Bitcoin treasury sector. ASSX takes that equity exposure and packages it into a daily leveraged ETF.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, the product should not be interpreted as a straightforward 2X Bitcoin investment. Its performance depends primarily on ASST's daily share-price movement, while ASST itself can be affected by Bitcoin, corporate financing, treasury valuation and broader stock-market conditions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;REX Shares and Tuttle Capital's launch of &lt;strong&gt;ASSX&lt;/strong&gt; gives traders a new way to obtain 2X daily exposure to &lt;strong&gt;Strive's ASST stock&lt;/strong&gt;, a company that has built a substantial corporate Bitcoin treasury.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The key fact is that ASSX targets &lt;strong&gt;200% of ASST's daily performance&lt;/strong&gt;, not twice the price of Bitcoin. Its leverage resets every trading day, which means longer-term returns can differ significantly from a simple 2X calculation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With Strive reporting &lt;strong&gt;25,000 BTC held as of September 11, 2026&lt;/strong&gt;, the new ETF adds another leveraged instrument to the growing market around publicly traded Bitcoin treasury companies. &lt;/p&gt;
