    <title>Super Micro Probe Finds No Evidence Management Knew of Alleged $2.5B Nvidia Diversion</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgtgD1QgFnTrDwEMXojCaxVhGgJsyoMtrOh9EfEWGpRgIJNntuOQ_iSsCZmo6WTnVTscQyIN_Q5TUZmBsHDfjyshIg0KFG-RTUVDeI_JPHAl8s7E8ZNGh2ny21iAHkM9__-jlLMRI0MIefsrgAaiyt1aM7zmQ25zApYGwrk-XvcQ1v6cb_OAZWbcrFt16M4/s1672/super-micro-nvidia-server-diversion-investigation.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Super Micro AI server with Nvidia GPUs during export diversion investigation" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgtgD1QgFnTrDwEMXojCaxVhGgJsyoMtrOh9EfEWGpRgIJNntuOQ_iSsCZmo6WTnVTscQyIN_Q5TUZmBsHDfjyshIg0KFG-RTUVDeI_JPHAl8s7E8ZNGh2ny21iAHkM9__-jlLMRI0MIefsrgAaiyt1aM7zmQ25zApYGwrk-XvcQ1v6cb_OAZWbcrFt16M4/w400-h225/super-micro-nvidia-server-diversion-investigation.jpg.png" title="Super Micro Investigation Into Alleged Nvidia Server Diversion" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/b&gt; | &lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Super Micro Computer says an independent investigation has
found no evidence that its current senior management knew about an alleged
scheme involving the diversion of Nvidia-powered servers to China.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The investigation was launched after three people associated
with the company were indicted in March over an alleged plan to illegally
divert advanced &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/next-coin-to-pump-traders-are-watching.html"&gt;AI hardware &lt;/a&gt;worth roughly &lt;b&gt;$2.5 billion&lt;/b&gt; to Chinese
customers in violation of U.S. export controls.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For Super Micro, the latest finding removes one of the
biggest questions hanging over the company: whether its current leadership knew
about the alleged activity.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;According to Super Micro, investigators reviewed
transactions identified in the federal indictment as well as a selection of
other transactions involving restricted products. They found no evidence that
current senior management knew about the alleged diversion scheme or that Super
Micro itself directly sold export-controlled products to known restricted
parties or locations.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That does not end the broader legal case, however. The
individuals charged in the federal investigation remain subject to separate
proceedings.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Super Micro's Investigation Found&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The investigation was overseen by &lt;b&gt;Scott Angel&lt;/b&gt;, Super
Micro's lead independent director, and &lt;b&gt;Tally Liu&lt;/b&gt;, chair of the board's
audit committee.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Outside law firm Munger, Tolles &amp;amp; Olson and independent
forensic accounting consultant AlixPartners were involved in the review.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The investigation examined the customer transactions at the
center of the federal indictment and additional transactions involving
customers that purchased restricted products.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Super Micro said investigators did not find evidence that
any current member of senior management knew about the alleged diversion
scheme.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The review also found no evidence that the company directly
sold export-controlled products to known restricted parties or locations. Super
Micro said investigators likewise found no reason to conclude that previously
issued financial statements could not be relied upon because of the potential
diversion.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Those findings are significant because they separate the
alleged actions of individuals associated with the company from the conduct of
Super Micro's current leadership.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The $2.5 Billion Case Is Still a Separate Matter&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The investigation should not be confused with the criminal
case that triggered it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;U.S. prosecutors charged three individuals in March 2026
over an alleged conspiracy to divert Nvidia-powered servers to China despite
U.S. export restrictions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;One of those individuals was &lt;b&gt;Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw&lt;/b&gt;,
a Super Micro co-founder and former board member. The other defendants included
a former Super Micro sales manager and a third-party broker, according to
reports on the case. All three have pleaded not guilty.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The alleged transactions involved high-end AI servers
containing Nvidia chips.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Super Micro has emphasized that &lt;b&gt;the company itself was
not named as a defendant in the indictment and has not been accused of
wrongdoing&lt;/b&gt;. The three individuals involved no longer have a relationship
with the company.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That distinction is important when assessing the latest
development.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The company's independent review addresses whether Super
Micro or its current senior management knew about the alleged activity. It does
not determine the guilt or innocence of the individuals facing criminal
charges.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Nvidia Hardware Is So Important&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;At the center of the dispute is something that has become
increasingly valuable in the global technology industry: advanced AI computing
hardware.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Nvidia's GPUs are widely used to train and operate large
artificial-intelligence models.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But access to some advanced U.S. AI chips in China is
restricted under American export-control rules.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That creates a complicated environment for companies that
manufacture servers containing high-performance GPUs.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Super Micro is one of the major companies supplying server
infrastructure for AI and high-performance computing. As demand for AI
computing has surged, the importance of export compliance has increased along
with it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The alleged diversion case therefore highlights a much
larger issue facing the technology industry: &lt;b&gt;who gets access to the world's
most powerful AI hardware, and how companies ensure that restricted products do
not end up in prohibited destinations.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Super Micro Is Tightening Its Compliance Program&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Although the investigation did not find evidence implicating
current senior management, Super Micro is not treating the issue as a problem
that can simply be forgotten.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The company said it has adopted recommendations from the
independent directors to further strengthen its export-compliance program.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Super Micro also took personnel actions following the
investigation, including terminations involving employees in areas such as
sales, technical support and business development. The company said those
actions were related to violations of internal policies and its code of
conduct.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That detail is worth paying attention to.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A finding that senior management did not know about an
alleged scheme does &lt;b&gt;not&lt;/b&gt; necessarily mean every internal control worked
perfectly.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In fact, the decision to strengthen compliance procedures
shows that Super Micro sees room to improve how sensitive products are
monitored and sold.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What the Finding Means for Investors&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For shareholders, the investigation could remove some of the
uncertainty that has surrounded Super Micro since the March indictments.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;One concern was whether the allegations could eventually
lead to questions about the company's financial reporting.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The investigation found no evidence that the company's
previously issued financial statements could not be relied upon because of the
potential diversion of restricted products, according to &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/grant-cardone-adds-350-btc-to-fort.html"&gt;Super Micro&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That is potentially reassuring for investors.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It also reduces the risk that the alleged activity will
automatically translate into a finding of management involvement.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But there are still risks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The underlying criminal case is continuing, and future
evidence from that proceeding could generate additional questions.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The company also has to prove that its enhanced
export-control procedures are effective as its AI-server business continues to
expand.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bigger Problem Is Bigger Than Super Micro&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The controversy comes at a time when AI infrastructure has
become a strategic priority for both companies and governments.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The United States is attempting to protect its technological
advantage in advanced computing while restricting the export of certain
high-end AI hardware to China.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;China, meanwhile, is investing heavily in domestic
semiconductor and AI infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That creates a highly competitive market for advanced
computing equipment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;As demand rises, so does the value of restricted hardware.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For companies such as Super Micro, this means export
compliance is no longer just a back-office regulatory issue. It can become a
major business and reputational risk.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A single compliance failure can potentially lead to
investigations, regulatory scrutiny, shareholder concerns and damage to a
company's reputation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why the Story Matters for the AI Industry&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Super Micro investigation also shows how the AI boom is
changing the technology supply chain.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A few years ago, most investors were focused on whether
companies could build profitable AI software.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Today, the conversation increasingly includes &lt;b&gt;chips,
servers, data centers, electricity and export controls&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That shift means companies supplying AI infrastructure are
becoming strategically important.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Super Micro sits directly in that part of the market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The company builds servers that can incorporate GPUs,
processors, networking components and other hardware needed for large-scale
computing.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;As AI spending grows, demand for those systems can grow with
it.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But the regulatory environment is becoming more complicated
at the same time.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A Clearance, But Not the End of the Story&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It would be easy to summarize the latest development as
Super Micro being completely “cleared.”&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That would be too broad.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The investigation found no evidence that current senior
management knew about the alleged diversion scheme. It also found no evidence
that Super Micro directly sold export-controlled products to known restricted
parties or that its previous financial statements could not be relied upon
because of the potential diversion.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;At the same time, employees were terminated following the
investigation, the company is strengthening its compliance program and the
separate criminal case involving the three indicted individuals continues.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;So the more accurate takeaway is narrower:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;The independent investigation did not find evidence
connecting Super Micro's current senior management to the alleged diversion
scheme.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That is meaningful, but it is not the same as saying every
question surrounding the case has disappeared.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Comes Next for Super Micro&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The company now has an opportunity to put the investigation
behind it and focus on its core AI-server business.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Whether investors fully move past the controversy will
likely depend on two things.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;First, the underlying criminal case will continue to receive
attention.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Second, Super Micro will have to demonstrate that its
strengthened export-compliance procedures can handle the increasingly
complicated global market for AI hardware.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For the company, that may ultimately be more important than
the investigation itself.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The AI infrastructure market is expanding rapidly, but so
are the regulatory responsibilities that come with supplying advanced computing
technology.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Super Micro's independent investigation found &lt;b&gt;no evidence
that current senior management knew about the alleged diversion of roughly $2.5
billion worth of Nvidia-powered servers to China&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The company also said the investigation found no evidence of
direct sales of export-controlled products to known restricted parties or
locations and found no reason to question the reliability of previously issued
financial statements based on the potential diversion.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;However, the separate criminal case involving three
individuals associated with Super Micro remains ongoing, and the company has
taken personnel actions while strengthening its export-compliance program.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For investors, the latest findings remove one major concern
surrounding Super Micro's management.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But the bigger story is still unfolding.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;As the global race for AI computing power intensifies, &lt;b&gt;the
ability to build powerful servers is becoming only half the challenge. Making
sure that technology reaches the right customers and destinations may become
just as important.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>What Is #GOTOK? The Truth Behind the AI Project, Developer Tool and Crypto Confusion</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

  &lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjYdGlZKxE-794g96zqEIoPtd9yXFKmHYqVIZcfvmFLu6hyqnv0LxahfEptoNVDDApejJ_FtVi8q5-JiZZs6YtDEfBmtOTw3soa9HN_6bvCgV0LKZt6KojPXfygoROW5vthMglf7s8LWcjUTyPApaQD0d0vzz9N0EBOLn4h3xjHcrSu-aj5_iD9rvxo_N70/s1672/gotok-getok-ai-research-token-confusion.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="GETok AI research and GOTOK token name confusion" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjYdGlZKxE-794g96zqEIoPtd9yXFKmHYqVIZcfvmFLu6hyqnv0LxahfEptoNVDDApejJ_FtVi8q5-JiZZs6YtDEfBmtOTw3soa9HN_6bvCgV0LKZt6KojPXfygoROW5vthMglf7s8LWcjUTyPApaQD0d0vzz9N0EBOLn4h3xjHcrSu-aj5_iD9rvxo_N70/w400-h225/gotok-getok-ai-research-token-confusion.jpg.png" title="GETok AI Research and GOTOK Token Confusion" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If you have recently come across &lt;strong&gt;#GOTOK&lt;/strong&gt; online and wondered whether it is a new AI token, you are not alone. The name can be confusing because “GOTOK” and “GETok” are associated with several different projects, tools and products.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    After reviewing available primary and authoritative sources, one distinction is especially important:
    &lt;strong&gt;GETok is an AI research method, not a cryptocurrency token.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    At the same time, a separate &lt;code&gt;gotok&lt;/code&gt; developer utility exists for counting tokens used by language models, while an older Solana ecosystem project called &lt;strong&gt;Gotok&lt;/strong&gt; was associated with crypto payments and virtual cards.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    There is also a separate company using the Gotok name. These entities should not be treated as the same project simply because their names look similar.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid rgb(216, 216, 216); margin: 25px 0px; padding: 18px;"&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 0px;"&gt;
      &lt;strong&gt;Quick answer:&lt;/strong&gt; The recently discussed &lt;strong&gt;GETok&lt;/strong&gt; is an AI research project focused on helping multimodal large language models understand and localize objects in 2D space. The official research sources reviewed do not identify GETok as a cryptocurrency.
    &lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;First, Let's Separate the Three Main GOTOK References&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The easiest way to understand the current confusion is to separate the major references instead of treating every “GOTOK” search result as one project.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ol&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;
      &lt;strong&gt;GETok — AI research:&lt;/strong&gt; A spatial representation method for multimodal large language models.
    &lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;
      &lt;strong&gt;&lt;code&gt;gotok&lt;/code&gt; — developer tool:&lt;/strong&gt; A Go-based utility designed for counting language-model tokens.
    &lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;
      &lt;strong&gt;Gotok — historical Solana payments project:&lt;/strong&gt; A project documented in the Solana Summer Camp ecosystem and associated with crypto payments and virtual cards backed by USDC.
    &lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ol&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    These are separate references. A similarity in spelling does not establish that they share the same developers, organization, token or technology.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;1. GETok — The AI Research Project&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What Is GETok?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;GETok&lt;/strong&gt; is a spatial representation method introduced in a research paper titled
    &lt;em&gt;“Grounding Everything in Tokens for Multimodal Large Language Models.”&lt;/em&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The paper was first submitted to arXiv in December 2025 and was subsequently published in the &lt;strong&gt;IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2026&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The research explores how multimodal large language models can represent spatial information more effectively using specialized tokens.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In simple terms, GETok is designed to help AI systems become better at understanding &lt;strong&gt;where objects are located inside an image&lt;/strong&gt;, rather than simply identifying what objects appear in the image.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What Problem Is GETok Trying to Solve?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Modern multimodal &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitcoin-is-crashing-again-is-that.html"&gt;AI systems&lt;/a&gt; can process text and images, but precise visual localization remains a difficult problem.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    An AI model may correctly identify a car, pedestrian or traffic sign in a photograph. A more difficult task is determining the precise location of that object and representing that location consistently.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    GETok approaches this problem by introducing a specialized vocabulary of learnable spatial tokens into multimodal language models.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;How Does GETok Work?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    One simple way to understand the approach is to imagine placing a grid over an image.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    GETok uses &lt;strong&gt;grid tokens&lt;/strong&gt; to represent structured locations in the image and &lt;strong&gt;offset tokens&lt;/strong&gt; to refine those locations.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This creates a coarse-to-fine approach to spatial localization. The model first identifies a general area and can then refine the position through additional spatial information.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    According to the research, the framework can represent different types of spatial information, including points, bounding boxes, masks and polylines.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The important distinction is that these are &lt;strong&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/bitfinex-securities-lists-five.html"&gt;AI representation tokens&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;. They are not blockchain tokens or tradable cryptocurrency assets.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What Results Did the GETok Research Report?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The research paper reports improvements across several evaluated visual-spatial tasks.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    These figures are the results reported by the researchers for their evaluated experiments. They should not be interpreted as a guarantee that every real-world AI vision system will achieve the same performance.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is GETok an AI Cryptocurrency?&lt;/h3&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;The official GETok research sources reviewed describe it as an AI research method, not as a cryptocurrency.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This distinction matters because the word &lt;strong&gt;“token”&lt;/strong&gt; has different meanings in technology.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In artificial intelligence, a token can represent a unit of text, visual information or another learned representation. In GETok, tokens are used to represent spatial information.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In cryptocurrency, a token normally refers to a blockchain-based digital asset.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Therefore, seeing the word “token” in an AI research paper does not mean that the project has a tradable cryptocurrency.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;2. &lt;code&gt;gotok&lt;/code&gt; — The Developer Token-Counting Tool&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A completely separate open-source project named &lt;code&gt;gotok&lt;/code&gt; is a developer utility written in Go.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Its purpose is to help developers count tokens in text using tokenization standards associated with language models.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Token counting can be useful when building AI applications because developers may need to estimate prompt size, understand context usage or calculate approximate API-processing requirements.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The project documentation identifies support for multiple token encodings used by different language-model systems.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This &lt;code&gt;gotok&lt;/code&gt; project is &lt;strong&gt;developer software rather than a cryptocurrency&lt;/strong&gt;.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Most importantly, there is no basis for assuming that this developer utility is the same project as GETok simply because both names contain “tok.”
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;3. Gotok — The Historical Solana Payments Project&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    There is another important historical use of the Gotok name in the crypto ecosystem.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    In September 2022, the Solana Foundation published the results of its &lt;strong&gt;Solana Summer Camp Hackathon&lt;/strong&gt;. The event featured projects across payments, DeFi, mobile, gaming and other areas of the Solana ecosystem.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Gotok was listed among the honorable mentions in the Payments Track.&lt;/strong&gt; It was not listed as one of the five prize-winning Payments Track projects. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Contemporary information about the project described Gotok as a payments-focused product involving &lt;strong&gt;virtual cards backed by USDC&lt;/strong&gt;, with the goal of allowing users to spend crypto in online and physical environments.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This historical reference is useful because it demonstrates that the Gotok name has previously been associated with a crypto-related project.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    However, that historical Solana project should &lt;strong&gt;not automatically be connected to the GETok AI research&lt;/strong&gt;. The names are similar, but that alone does not establish a relationship between the projects.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What About Gotok Technologies?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    There is also a separate organization using the Gotok name.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Gotok Technologies Limited&lt;/strong&gt; describes itself as a software company. Its current website presents &lt;strong&gt;Peckle&lt;/strong&gt; as an AI photo studio designed for businesses to create product imagery and marketing material.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This company should be treated as another separate entity when researching the term “Gotok.”
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The existence of the company does not establish a connection to the GETok academic research or to any particular cryptocurrency.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Is #GOTOK Causing So Much Confusion?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The confusion is understandable because several unrelated technologies and projects use similar spellings.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Someone searching for &lt;strong&gt;#GOTOK&lt;/strong&gt; could encounter:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;GETok AI research&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The &lt;code&gt;gotok&lt;/code&gt; developer utility&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;The historical Solana Gotok payments project&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Gotok Technologies&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Other unrelated products or services using similar names&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The safest approach is therefore to identify the exact project being discussed instead of assuming that every result containing “Gotok” belongs to the same organization.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Is There Currently an Established GOTOK Cryptocurrency?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    This is where careful wording is important.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;We could not independently verify a currently established cryptocurrency under the exact name “GOTOK” that is officially connected to the GETok AI research from the primary sources reviewed.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That statement should not be interpreted as proof that nobody can create a token using the name GOTOK.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Permissionless blockchain networks allow new &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/does-blockchain-ever-actually-delete.html"&gt;tokens&lt;/a&gt; to be created, and similarly named assets can appear on different networks.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    What this means is that the &lt;strong&gt;name or hashtag alone is not sufficient evidence&lt;/strong&gt; that a particular cryptocurrency is officially connected to the GETok research.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;div style="border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid rgb(216, 216, 216); margin: 25px 0px; padding: 18px;"&gt;
    &lt;p style="margin: 0px;"&gt;
      &lt;strong&gt;Important:&lt;/strong&gt; If someone presents a token as “GOTOK AI,” verify the exact contract address, blockchain network and official project documentation before assuming that it is connected to the GETok research.
    &lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;How to Verify a GOTOK Token&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If a cryptocurrency using the GOTOK name appears on social media or a decentralized exchange, the ticker should not be treated as proof of authenticity.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Instead, readers should verify:
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ol&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Contract address:&lt;/strong&gt; Identify the exact blockchain contract.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Blockchain network:&lt;/strong&gt; Confirm whether it operates on Solana, Ethereum, BNB Chain or another network.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Official website:&lt;/strong&gt; Check whether the project publishes the contract address itself.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Documentation:&lt;/strong&gt; Look for technical documentation explaining the project's purpose.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Token utility:&lt;/strong&gt; Determine what the asset is actually designed to do.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Supply:&lt;/strong&gt; Review total supply, circulating supply and allocation.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Liquidity:&lt;/strong&gt; Check whether meaningful trading liquidity exists.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Holder distribution:&lt;/strong&gt; Review whether ownership is heavily concentrated.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Contract permissions:&lt;/strong&gt; Examine relevant minting, ownership or administrative controls.&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Official accounts:&lt;/strong&gt; Confirm that social-media accounts are actually associated with the project.&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ol&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why This Distinction Matters&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    Names can spread quickly across social media, particularly when AI and cryptocurrency narratives overlap.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A post mentioning “GOTOK AI token” may look convincing while actually referring to an AI research term, a historical project, a developer utility or another unrelated asset.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That is why the best way to investigate a new cryptocurrency is to start with evidence rather than the ticker.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    A genuine connection should normally be supported by an identifiable project, official documentation, a verifiable blockchain contract and a clear explanation of how the cryptocurrency relates to the claimed technology.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    If you recently searched for &lt;strong&gt;#GOTOK&lt;/strong&gt; because someone described it as an AI token, the first thing to understand is that several different projects and products use similar names.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;GETok&lt;/strong&gt; is an AI research method published at CVPR 2026 that focuses on improving spatial grounding in multimodal large language models.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;code&gt;gotok&lt;/code&gt; is a separate developer utility for counting AI-model tokens.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Gotok&lt;/strong&gt; was also the name of a historical Solana payments project that received an honorable mention in the Solana Summer Camp Payments Track and was described in contemporary materials as involving USDC-backed virtual cards.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Gotok Technologies Limited&lt;/strong&gt; is another separate software company associated with the Peckle AI photo-studio product.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    We could not independently verify a currently established cryptocurrency officially connected to the GETok AI research simply from the name “GOTOK.”
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    That does not establish that no token using the name can exist. It means that anyone presenting a particular GOTOK cryptocurrency as the official AI project should provide verifiable evidence, especially the project's official website and exact blockchain contract address.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;
    The safest lesson is simple:
    &lt;strong&gt;do not confuse an AI research token with a crypto token, and do not assume that two projects are connected just because their names look similar.&lt;/strong&gt;
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What is GETok?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;
    GETok is a spatial representation method for multimodal large language models. It is designed to improve how AI systems represent and reason about spatial information in visual content.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is GETok a cryptocurrency?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;
    The official research sources reviewed describe GETok as an AI research method, not a blockchain cryptocurrency.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;When was the GETok research published?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;
    The research was first submitted to arXiv in December 2025 and was subsequently published in the CVPR 2026 proceedings.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;What is the gotok developer tool?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;
    &lt;code&gt;gotok&lt;/code&gt; is a Go-based command-line utility designed to count tokens in text using tokenization standards associated with AI language models.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Was there a crypto project called Gotok?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;
    Yes. A historical Solana ecosystem project called Gotok was listed as an honorable mention in the Payments Track of the 2022 Solana Summer Camp Hackathon. Contemporary descriptions associated it with virtual cards backed by USDC.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is the historical Gotok project the same as GETok?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;
    The available sources reviewed do not establish that connection. The historical Gotok payments project and the GETok academic research should therefore be treated as separate entities.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Is there an official GOTOK AI cryptocurrency?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;
    We could not independently verify a currently established cryptocurrency officially connected to the GETok research from the sources reviewed. A specific token should be verified using its official contract address and project documentation.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h3&gt;Should I buy a token called GOTOK?&lt;/h3&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;
    Do not make an investment decision based only on the name, ticker or hashtag. Verify the contract address, blockchain, official website, tokenomics, liquidity and project documentation first.
  &lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Could a State Actor Use AI to 51% Attack a Blockchain Without Anyone Noticing? The Economics Say No — For Now.</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;br /&gt;&lt;article&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjnCKXafGOC6M3X1HDCWfASh-4dRoZe6TikP-Bau35-sjcg1YzWfutK-ypunMQ37drKfx2aRDOS5oINHsRt0f5MkC9GqrJE_7PLkpknbdW6aYFKBPbn6gjt_fn5Mqid58rxVLP3o23FaFvRSloRUYQzi0bP1FO0I2RBMEiP5fiYhd98tc_-F3gVg7TbmK3u/s1672/ai-state-actor-51-percent-blockchain-attack.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="AI monitoring a blockchain network in a hypothetical 51% attack scenario" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjnCKXafGOC6M3X1HDCWfASh-4dRoZe6TikP-Bau35-sjcg1YzWfutK-ypunMQ37drKfx2aRDOS5oINHsRt0f5MkC9GqrJE_7PLkpknbdW6aYFKBPbn6gjt_fn5Mqid58rxVLP3o23FaFvRSloRUYQzi0bP1FO0I2RBMEiP5fiYhd98tc_-F3gVg7TbmK3u/w400-h225/ai-state-actor-51-percent-blockchain-attack.jpg.png" title="Could AI Help a State Actor Attack a Blockchain?" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&amp;nbsp;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;What if a government-backed group decided that breaking a blockchain didn't require stealing private keys, taking down servers, or hacking individual users — just controlling enough of the network's consensus power?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is the basic idea behind a 51% attack.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Now add artificial intelligence to the picture.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI is increasingly being used across different parts of cybersecurity, including reconnaissance, vulnerability research and automated analysis. Security researchers have also reported increasingly sophisticated use of AI by state-aligned threat actors.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is an important distinction between &lt;strong&gt;AI making cyber operations faster&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;AI making a 51% blockchain attack technically or economically practical&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The second remains a much bigger challenge.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There is currently &lt;strong&gt;no verified evidence that a state actor has secretly used AI to carry out a successful 51% attack against Bitcoin or another major, highly secured blockchain.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This article therefore examines a hypothetical cybersecurity scenario rather than reporting a confirmed incident.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;First, What Actually Is a 51% Attack?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The phrase sounds simple, but it is often misunderstood.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;On a proof-of-work &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bitcoin-reclaimed-four-major-moving.html"&gt;blockchain&lt;/a&gt;, an attacker generally needs control of more than half of the network's mining power to reliably dominate the chain's block-production process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That doesn't mean the attacker suddenly owns everybody's coins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It doesn't mean private keys are magically exposed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And it doesn't mean the attacker can simply rewrite anything they want.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, majority control can give an attacker significant influence over transaction ordering and chain history and, depending on the circumstances, enable chain reorganizations or double-spending attacks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's developer documentation explains how majority hash-power control can allow an attacker to reorganize recent transaction history and perform certain forms of double spending.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://developer.bitcoin.org/devguide/block_chain.html?highlight=consensus" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Bitcoin Developer Guide — Blockchain and Consensus&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction matters because a 51% attack is fundamentally a &lt;strong&gt;consensus attack&lt;/strong&gt;, not simply a conventional cybersecurity breach.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Where Could AI Actually Help?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI doesn't create hashing power out of thin air. A powerful model cannot simply tell Bitcoin's network to accept an attacker's blocks.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The attacker would still need the underlying resources required by the blockchain's consensus mechanism.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For a proof-of-work network, that means enormous computational resources, infrastructure and energy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI could potentially help with the surrounding intelligence and coordination.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, an adversary could theoretically use &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/taiwan-lawmaker-pushes-bitcoin-reserve.html"&gt;AI&lt;/a&gt; to process large amounts of public information, identify weaknesses in infrastructure, automate monitoring or improve operational decision-making.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those capabilities are increasingly relevant in cybersecurity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Trend Micro's 2026 reporting described state-aligned threat actors using generative AI across multiple stages of intrusion operations, including reconnaissance, exploit development and lateral movement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://newsroom.trendmicro.com/2026-07-29-TrendAI-TM-Reports-Nation-State-Activity-in-H1-2026-APT-Activity-Roundup" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Trend Micro — H1 2026 APT Activity Roundup&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Google Threat Intelligence has also reported growing use of AI in vulnerability research and exploitation workflows.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/ai-vulnerability-exploitation-initial-access/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Google Threat Intelligence — AI and Vulnerability Exploitation&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But there is a major gap between &lt;strong&gt;using AI around an attack&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;using AI to obtain majority blockchain consensus power&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI can potentially improve efficiency.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It does not remove the underlying economic and computational requirements of consensus control.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bitcoin Would Be a Very Different Target&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the target were Bitcoin, the scale of the challenge would be enormous.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's proof-of-work network is supported by substantial specialized mining infrastructure and electricity consumption.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An attacker attempting majority control would therefore face a major economic problem before even reaching the technical one.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They would need sufficient mining capacity, access to infrastructure and the ability to sustain that operation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Research examining 51% attacks has found that mature networks such as Bitcoin can be dramatically more expensive to attack than young or lightly secured blockchains.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40747-026-02256-w" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Springer Nature — 51% Attack Vulnerability of Nascent Blockchains&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That leads to an important point:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The biggest blockchain may not be the easiest target simply because it is the biggest prize.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Its scale and mining participation can also be part of its defense.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Smaller Blockchains Are a Different Story&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The risk changes considerably when a blockchain has a small mining network or limited economic security.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Research into historical 51% attacks has found that smaller and younger networks can be significantly more exposed because obtaining majority control may require fewer resources.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40747-026-02256-w" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Research on 51% Attack Economics Across Blockchain Networks&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a more plausible hypothetical scenario for an AI-assisted state operation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of trying to overpower Bitcoin, an attacker could theoretically look for a smaller network where the cost of obtaining majority consensus power is substantially lower.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not mean such an attack is happening.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It means the economics can be fundamentally different.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For a small blockchain, the question could be less about whether an attacker has access to futuristic AI and more about whether the network has enough economic security to resist a well-funded adversary.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Proof-of-Stake Changes the Equation&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Not every blockchain uses mining.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ethereum, for example, uses proof-of-stake.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In that environment, the relevant resource isn't mining hash power.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An attacker would instead need control of a very large amount of the network's staked asset.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Ethereum's documentation explains how control of a majority of staked ETH could give an attacker significant influence over consensus.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/consensus-mechanisms/pos/faqs" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Ethereum.org — Proof-of-Stake FAQs&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That doesn't make proof-of-stake automatically immune.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It changes the economics and the mechanisms involved.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important lesson is that an AI-driven threat model would have to consider the blockchain's actual consensus design rather than treating every network as if it were Bitcoin.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Could It Happen Without Anyone Noticing?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is probably the most intriguing part of the question.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A truly large-scale attack would be difficult to hide indefinitely.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A sudden change in mining participation, unusual block production, abnormal reorganizations or suspicious transaction behavior could create signals for exchanges, developers, miners and security researchers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But detection is not necessarily the same thing as prevention.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An attacker might theoretically attempt to operate quietly before revealing its objective.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is where AI could potentially make monitoring more complicated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If an adversary can automate analysis and adapt its behavior faster than human defenders can investigate it, the window between an unusual event and a coordinated response could become smaller.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But that still does not establish that AI can secretly overpower a major blockchain's consensus mechanism.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The two questions should not be confused.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;A 51% Attack Doesn't Give Unlimited Power&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Another misconception is that majority control means total control.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It doesn't.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A 51% attacker generally cannot use consensus control to create valid signatures for somebody else's wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It cannot simply steal coins from arbitrary addresses whose private keys it does not possess.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And it cannot change the underlying rules of the blockchain merely by controlling consensus power.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The attacker is primarily influencing consensus.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That could still be extremely damaging.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, a successful attack could potentially enable transaction censorship, reorganizations or double-spending under appropriate conditions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But the scope of the damage is still determined by the blockchain's design and the attacker's actual capabilities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The State-Actor Question Makes It More Complicated&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A state actor would potentially have access to resources that ordinary criminals may not have, including specialist personnel, infrastructure, intelligence capabilities and long-term funding.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Recent threat-intelligence reporting has documented state-aligned groups using AI to enhance different stages of cyber operations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://newsroom.trendmicro.com/2026-07-29-TrendAI-TM-Reports-Nation-State-Activity-in-H1-2026-APT-Activity-Roundup" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Trend Micro — State-Aligned AI Cyber Activity&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That doesn't mean governments can simply "ask AI to attack &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bill-gates-warns-ai-is-advancing-faster.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt;."&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It means the broader threat environment is changing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI may increasingly become part of the toolkit used by sophisticated actors.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For blockchain defenders, that could mean preparing for attackers who can analyze information and react at machine speed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Would Defenders Watch?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The most important defense may not be trying to identify "AI" directly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockchains already produce large amounts of observable data.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Developers, miners, validators, exchanges and security firms can monitor changes in network behavior, consensus participation and transaction patterns.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For proof-of-work networks, unusual changes in mining distribution could be important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For proof-of-stake networks, changes in validator participation, stake concentration and consensus behavior could matter.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The exact indicators depend on the blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The broader lesson is that &lt;strong&gt;consensus security needs to be monitored continuously rather than assumed permanently.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Real Weak Point May Be Smaller Than the Blockchain&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blockchain doesn't exist in isolation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It connects to exchanges, bridges, wallets, mining pools, validator infrastructure, cloud services and other systems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An attacker may not need to defeat the blockchain's consensus mechanism if it can compromise something around it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important for security planning.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A blockchain with strong consensus security can still be exposed through weak surrounding infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;AI could potentially make those broader cyber operations faster.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Google Threat Intelligence has documented the growing role of AI in vulnerability research and exploitation workflows.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/ai-vulnerability-exploitation-initial-access/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"&gt;Google Threat Intelligence — AI and Cybersecurity&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So the bigger concern may not be a magical AI capable of instantly launching a 51% attack.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It may be an AI-assisted operation that patiently searches for the weakest part of an entire blockchain ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Could a state actor use AI as part of an attempt to attack a blockchain?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Yes, that is a credible hypothetical cybersecurity scenario.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Could AI by itself give a state actor enough power to secretly 51% attack Bitcoin?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;There is no evidence that it can, and AI does not eliminate the enormous resource requirements of Bitcoin's proof-of-work consensus.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The risk looks different for smaller or less mature blockchains, where the economic cost of majority control can be dramatically lower.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That may be the real lesson.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The future blockchain threat may not arrive as a dramatic moment when an &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/bill-gates-warns-ai-is-advancing-faster.html"&gt;AI suddenly&lt;/a&gt; "takes over" a network.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It could look much more ordinary: an automated system helping a sophisticated adversary find weaknesses, evaluate opportunities and coordinate activity faster than defenders expect.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The question isn't whether AI can magically create a 51% attack. It's whether AI can help an attacker reach the point where the cost, timing and opportunity finally make one worth attempting.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And for smaller blockchains, that question may become important sooner than many people expect — and the answer may depend on how well smaller chains prepare.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div class="article-disclaimer"&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Editorial and factual note:&lt;/strong&gt; This article examines a hypothetical cybersecurity scenario. It does not claim that any state actor has secretly used AI to conduct a 51% attack. No verified incident involving Bitcoin or another major blockchain was identified in the sources reviewed for this article.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute legal, financial or cybersecurity advice.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Can Someone Steal Bitcoin With Only Your Wallet Address?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj6Xj4l3hoGgKSKrNeKSbe0pyfFaSWMjVCZ2TOhYfrumzXqY4MejBBEI6h9y6DJJQPZ9OrWUG2IM05mlfOjYhWGmx9G-PGGZrtCOZ2Qm5-VPUVdL4l-KIJNVm_GMrKj5g8bYHYgzX8RX88mgof9aVGxbIIPcq1-WA1_345ptp-kh2iLNBW87eU7VS4BKbbb/s1671/bitcoin-wallet-address-security-theft.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin wallet address protected from unauthorized access and theft" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1671" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEj6Xj4l3hoGgKSKrNeKSbe0pyfFaSWMjVCZ2TOhYfrumzXqY4MejBBEI6h9y6DJJQPZ9OrWUG2IM05mlfOjYhWGmx9G-PGGZrtCOZ2Qm5-VPUVdL4l-KIJNVm_GMrKj5g8bYHYgzX8RX88mgof9aVGxbIIPcq1-WA1_345ptp-kh2iLNBW87eU7VS4BKbbb/w640-h360/bitcoin-wallet-address-security-theft.jpg.png" title="Can Someone Steal Bitcoin With Only Your Wallet Address?" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/strong&gt; |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If someone knows your Bitcoin wallet address, should you be worried that they can take your BTC?&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No—not from the wallet address alone.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A Bitcoin address is public information. It is designed to be shared when you want someone to send you Bitcoin. Knowing that address does not give another person the private key required to authorize a Bitcoin transaction from the wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Coinbase explicitly says that it is not possible to steal digital currency using a public crypto address alone. Bitcoin.org similarly explains that private keys are the secret information used to spend Bitcoin. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not mean your Bitcoin is automatically safe from every type of attack. The real danger usually comes when someone gets access to your &lt;strong&gt;private key, recovery phrase, wallet device, exchange account or transaction-signing process&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 700px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;

&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Can Someone Use It to Spend Your BTC?&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Main Risk&lt;/th&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Can reveal public &lt;br /&gt;transaction information&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Potentially&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Unauthorized account access&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Does a Bitcoin Wallet Address Actually Do?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A Bitcoin wallet address is essentially a destination for receiving BTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You can give your address to another person, display it on a website or use it to receive a payment. Coinbase describes a wallet address as a string of letters and numbers from which cryptocurrency can be sent and received. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The address does not function like a password.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Someone who knows your address can send &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-coinbase-reverse-bitcoin-sent-to-another-coinbase-user.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt; to it, but that knowledge alone does not authorize them to spend the Bitcoin already associated with it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Think of it roughly like giving someone your bank account number so they can send you money. The information identifies where funds can be sent, but it is not itself the secret needed to authorize a withdrawal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Can't Someone Spend Bitcoin With Your Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin uses public and private keys to control funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The public side can be shared. The private key is secret and is used to authorize transactions. Bitcoin.org describes the private key as secret data that proves the right to spend Bitcoin from the corresponding wallet. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin's developer documentation describes the same basic structure: wallets create public keys for receiving satoshis and use the corresponding private keys to spend them. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So simply knowing the destination address does not give an attacker the cryptographic authorization needed to move the coins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If Someone Knows Your Bitcoin Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;They may be able to observe information associated with that address on the public blockchain.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Depending on the address, an observer may be able to see incoming and outgoing transactions and the amount of Bitcoin associated with the address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That creates a &lt;strong&gt;privacy risk&lt;/strong&gt;, but it is different from a direct theft risk.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Someone could know that an address belongs to you and monitor its activity without having the ability to spend the BTC.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org recommends using a new Bitcoin address when receiving a new payment and using multiple wallets for different purposes to reduce the ability to associate transactions with one another. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can Someone Steal Bitcoin With Your Public Key?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Not simply because they know your public key.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Public keys are designed to be exposed as part of Bitcoin's &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-you-recover-crypto-sent-to-the-wrong-network.html"&gt;cryptographic system&lt;/a&gt;. Coinbase explains that public information can be shared to allow others to send funds, while the private key is what provides control over the funds. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The important distinction is between &lt;strong&gt;public information&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;secret authorization information&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Your public address can be shared. Your private key should never be shared.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Information Can Actually Put Your Bitcoin at Risk?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bigger security problem starts when an attacker obtains something that allows them to control the wallet or authorize transactions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;1. Private Key&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A private key is one of the most sensitive pieces of information associated with a self-custody Bitcoin wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org states that private keys must never be revealed because they allow the holder to spend the Bitcoin associated with the wallet. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If somebody obtains the private key controlling a wallet, the situation is completely different from simply knowing the public address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;2. Recovery or Seed Phrase&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Many modern wallets use a recovery phrase to restore access to a wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Coinbase explains that a seed phrase contains the information needed to access or recover cryptocurrency associated with a wallet and should be kept private. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why scammers frequently target recovery phrases rather than public wallet addresses.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;3. Exchange Account Access&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your Bitcoin is held with a cryptocurrency exchange, the security model is different from a self-custody wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In that situation, unauthorized access to your exchange account can potentially put your assets at risk, depending on the account's security controls and withdrawal protections.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org notes that users who leave coins with an exchange or another custodian rely on that third party to safeguard the funds and process withdrawals. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;4. Compromised Device or Wallet&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A stolen or compromised computer or phone can create a much more serious security problem than someone merely knowing your address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org warns that malware can undermine wallet security and that protecting wallet backups is also essential. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one reason keeping your recovery information away from compromised devices is so important.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can Someone Hack Your Bitcoin Just by Knowing the Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Knowing a Bitcoin address does not provide the private key associated with it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An attacker cannot normally derive the private key simply by looking at the public address and then use it to spend the funds. Bitcoin's cryptographic system is specifically designed to prevent that.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The real-world attacks people often describe as “someone stole my Bitcoin after seeing my address” usually involve something else—such as a leaked recovery phrase, phishing, malware, compromised credentials or unauthorized access to a wallet or exchange.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;How Scammers Use a Public Bitcoin Address&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Although a public address itself cannot authorize a withdrawal, scammers can still use information about your wallet as part of a social-engineering attack.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For example, a scammer may see a public Bitcoin address and then pretend to be wallet support. They may claim that your account has a security problem and ask you to provide your recovery phrase or private key.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org specifically warns about fake support and recovery scams in which attackers impersonate wallet or exchange support staff and request seed phrases, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-you-recover-crypto-sent-to-the-wrong-network.html"&gt;private keys&lt;/a&gt; or remote access. Legitimate support should not require your seed phrase or private key. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is why sharing your address can be safe while sharing your recovery phrase can be disastrous.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If Someone Sends You a Message Saying Your Wallet Is “Compromised”?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Be extremely careful.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If somebody contacts you unexpectedly and claims they can protect, recover or unlock your Bitcoin, do not give them your seed phrase or private key.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Do not install remote-access software at their request either.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org specifically identifies fake support and fake recovery services as common scam patterns. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A genuine wallet address does not need to be “verified” by giving a stranger your private key.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Is It Safe to Post a Bitcoin Wallet Address Online?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;From a direct spending perspective, a public Bitcoin address can be shared. Coinbase says crypto addresses are safe to display publicly for receiving tips, payments or donations and that a public address alone cannot be used to steal digital currency. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, there is a separate &lt;strong&gt;privacy&lt;/strong&gt; consideration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin transactions are publicly visible. If you repeatedly use the same address and publicly connect it to your identity, other people may be able to monitor activity associated with that address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Bitcoin.org therefore recommends generating a new address for each new payment when possible. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So the answer is:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Safe from direct theft by address alone? Yes.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
&lt;strong&gt;Completely private? No.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Should You Never Share?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you use a self-custody Bitcoin wallet, treat the following information as highly sensitive:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Private key&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Seed phrase or recovery phrase&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Wallet backup containing private keys&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Wallet password or PIN where it protects access&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Exchange login credentials&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Authentication codes or recovery credentials&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Coinbase advises users to keep private keys and recovery phrases confidential, while Bitcoin.org recommends securing wallet backups and private keys. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Should You Do If You Already Shared Your Wallet Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you only shared your public Bitcoin address, there is normally no reason to panic.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You do not need to move your Bitcoin simply because somebody knows the address.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead, consider the privacy implications and avoid sharing sensitive wallet information.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you accidentally shared your &lt;strong&gt;private key or recovery phrase&lt;/strong&gt;, however, that is a completely different situation. The wallet should be treated as potentially compromised, and you should move funds to a new secure wallet using a trusted process.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Do not wait for someone to prove they can access the wallet before taking action.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Public Address vs. Private Key: The Difference&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 650px; width: 100%;"&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can someone steal Bitcoin with only my wallet address?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. A public Bitcoin address alone does not provide the private key or authorization required to spend the BTC. Coinbase explicitly states that digital currency cannot be stolen using a public address alone. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Is it safe to give someone my Bitcoin address?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes, if you are giving them the address so they can send you Bitcoin. A public address is designed to be shared. However, remember that transactions associated with a Bitcoin address can be publicly visible. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can someone hack my wallet from my Bitcoin address?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Knowing the address does not give someone the private key needed to authorize a Bitcoin transaction. The more realistic risks involve compromised private keys, recovery phrases, devices or account credentials.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What happens if someone has my Bitcoin private key?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;A private key is used to authorize spending from the corresponding wallet. Bitcoin.org says private keys must never be revealed because they allow Bitcoin to be spent. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can someone steal Bitcoin with my seed phrase?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Yes. A recovery or seed phrase can provide access to the wallet it protects. Coinbase advises keeping seed phrases private and secure. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can someone see my Bitcoin balance if they know my address?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;They may be able to inspect the balance and transaction history associated with that public address through the Bitcoin blockchain. That is a privacy issue, not the same as having permission to spend the funds.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Should I create a new Bitcoin address if someone knows my old one?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;You do not normally need to create a new address simply because somebody knows an existing public address. However, if privacy is important, Bitcoin.org recommends using a new address for each new payment and using multiple wallets for different purposes. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Someone cannot steal your Bitcoin simply by knowing your wallet address.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Your Bitcoin address is public information designed to let people send you BTC. The secret that matters is the private key or recovery information that authorizes control of the funds. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The bigger danger is not someone seeing your address. It is someone tricking you into revealing your private key or seed phrase, compromising your device, taking over your exchange account or gaining another form of authorization.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So if you posted your Bitcoin address online, &lt;strong&gt;don't panic&lt;/strong&gt;. Just remember the golden rule of self-custody: &lt;strong&gt;your address can be public; your private key and recovery phrase must stay private.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
