        &lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Possible Cost&lt;/th&gt;

      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Explorer API&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Developers&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Free tiers and/or paid plans&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Premium explorer features&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Advanced users&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;May require payment&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Private enterprise explorer&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;Businesses and organizations&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(204, 204, 204); padding: 10px;"&gt;May involve commercial licensing&lt;br /&gt;or infrastructure costs&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
    &lt;/tbody&gt;
  &lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;
```

  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;Can You Check Someone's Wallet Without Paying?&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;
  In most cases, yes.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
  If the blockchain is public, you can generally enter a public wallet address into the appropriate explorer and inspect information that the network makes publicly available.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
  You do not need to own the wallet, and you do not need its private key simply to inspect public blockchain data.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
  However, public visibility also creates a privacy consideration. If a wallet address becomes linked to a real-world identity, its on-chain history may be easier for other people to investigate.
&lt;/p&gt;
```

  &lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;Can an Explorer Move Your Crypto?&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;
  Simply viewing an address or transaction on a normal public explorer does not move the cryptocurrency stored in that address.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
  A legitimate explorer should not need your seed phrase or &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/can-cryptocurrencies-survive-quantum-era.html"&gt;private key&lt;/a&gt; merely to show public blockchain information.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
  &lt;strong&gt;Never enter your seed phrase or private key into a website claiming that it is required to "verify" your wallet through a blockchain explorer.&lt;/strong&gt;
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
  If a website asks for sensitive wallet credentials just to display a transaction, treat that as a major warning sign.
&lt;/p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;How to Use a Blockchain Explorer Safely&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;ol&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Check the domain.&lt;/strong&gt; Make sure you are using the legitimate explorer before interacting with any links or wallet-related features.
  &lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Never enter your seed phrase.&lt;/strong&gt; A normal block explorer does not need your recovery phrase to show public blockchain data.
  &lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Verify the network.&lt;/strong&gt; Make sure the explorer corresponds to the blockchain you are checking.
  &lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Verify the transaction hash.&lt;/strong&gt; Compare the hash shown by your wallet or exchange with the explorer result.
  &lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;li&gt;
    &lt;strong&gt;Understand the fee shown.&lt;/strong&gt; A fee displayed on a transaction page normally relates to the blockchain transaction, not the act of viewing the page.
  &lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Is a public blockchain explorer free?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;
  Public explorers are generally free for ordinary browsing. However, some providers may offer premium features, paid APIs, advertisements or other commercial services.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Do I pay gas to check an Ethereum wallet?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;
  No. Simply viewing an Ethereum address on an explorer does not require an on-chain transaction and therefore does not require you to pay gas.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Do I pay Bitcoin fees to search for a transaction?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;
  No. Searching for an existing Bitcoin transaction does not create another Bitcoin transaction. Any fee displayed belongs to the original transaction.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Why does Etherscan show a transaction fee?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;
  Etherscan displays information recorded on the Ethereum blockchain. The transaction fee shown on a transaction page relates to the gas required for that transaction.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Can blockchain explorers have paid plans?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;
  Yes. Explorer providers may offer premium features or API services with paid plans. These charges are separate from blockchain network transaction fees.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Do explorers accept donations?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;
  Some projects may accept voluntary donations. A donation is not the same as a mandatory explorer usage fee. Sending the donation itself may still require a blockchain transaction fee.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Are private blockchain explorers different?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;
  Yes. Enterprise blockchain explorer services can provide private dashboards, analytics, compliance tools or controlled access and may involve commercial fees. They are different from publicly accessible explorers.
&lt;/p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;section&gt;
    &lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;
  &lt;strong&gt;You generally do not need to pay a fee just to use a public blockchain explorer.&lt;/strong&gt;
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
  Searching for a transaction, checking a wallet address, viewing a token transfer or inspecting a block is normally a read-only activity. You are looking at information that has already been recorded on the blockchain.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
  Sending cryptocurrency or interacting with a smart contract is different. Those actions can require a network transaction fee.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
  At the same time, "free explorer" does not necessarily mean that every service provided by the explorer company is free. Premium features, developer APIs, advertisements, donations and private enterprise services can all exist alongside a free public explorer.
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
  The simplest rule to remember is this:
&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;
  &lt;strong&gt;The explorer lets you look at the blockchain. The network fee pays for having the blockchain process your transaction.&lt;/strong&gt;
&lt;/p&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/section&gt;

  &lt;footer&gt;
    &lt;hr /&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;p&gt;
  &lt;strong&gt;Editorial note:&lt;/strong&gt; Explorer features, API pricing and blockchain fee structures can change over time. Readers should verify current service terms and network fees directly with the relevant provider or blockchain network.
&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;em&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute financial, legal or investment advice.&lt;/em&gt;

Together, those seven figures add up to approximately &lt;strong&gt;$69.3 million&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Token-unlock data can vary between tracking platforms. Differences may result from token prices used at the time of calculation, circulating-supply snapshots, whether the figure represents a specific day's release or a weekly event, and how each provider defines the percentage of supply affected.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;1. LayerZero (ZRO): The Largest Unlock of the Week&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;LayerZero's ZRO&lt;/strong&gt; ranks first in the weekly list with an estimated &lt;strong&gt;$26.8 million&lt;/strong&gt; of tokens scheduled for release and a reported impact of &lt;strong&gt;6.87% of circulating supply&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;ZRO is therefore the largest unlock in the September 14–20 ranking by estimated dollar value. A release of this size can increase the amount of tradable supply available to the market, although an unlock does not automatically mean that all released tokens will immediately be sold.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Other tokenomics trackers have published somewhat different ZRO estimates. Some reports place the relevant event at roughly &lt;strong&gt;$25.8 million to $26.4 million&lt;/strong&gt;, with a percentage around &lt;strong&gt;4.22%&lt;/strong&gt; under their own supply methodology. That percentage should not be treated as directly equivalent to KuCoin's 6.87% figure because the underlying denominator can differ.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;For clarity, the $26.8 million figure is the weekly-ranking estimate used in this article; other reports may show slightly different values depending on the token price and supply methodology used.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;2. Bedrock (BR): Large Supply Impact Despite a Lower Dollar Value&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Bedrock's BR&lt;/strong&gt; is second with an estimated &lt;strong&gt;$16.9 million&lt;/strong&gt; unlock and a reported &lt;strong&gt;13.47% of circulating supply&lt;/strong&gt; in KuCoin's weekly ranking.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The percentage is particularly important because BR's reported supply impact is considerably larger than its dollar ranking alone suggests. A token release can create additional selling pressure when newly unlocked holdings become transferable, but the actual market impact depends on whether recipients sell, hold, stake or otherwise use their &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/nvidia-in-talks-to-invest-up-to-10.html"&gt;tokens&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Alternative reports have used different supply calculations for the BR event. Some datasets report a figure around &lt;strong&gt;$10.4 million&lt;/strong&gt; and approximately &lt;strong&gt;18.68%&lt;/strong&gt; under their own methodology. The difference highlights why the percentage should always be read together with the provider's definition of the relevant supply base.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;3. YZY MONEY (YZY): A Significant Percentage of Supply&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;YZY MONEY's YZY&lt;/strong&gt; ranks third at approximately &lt;strong&gt;$8.4 million&lt;/strong&gt;, with KuCoin reporting an unlock equivalent to &lt;strong&gt;9.63% of circulating supply&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For traders, the percentage figure can be more important than the raw dollar amount. A smaller token can experience a meaningful supply change even when its unlock is much smaller than those of larger crypto assets.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Other token-unlock datasets have reported a lower percentage, around &lt;strong&gt;4.4%–4.49%&lt;/strong&gt;, depending on the supply calculation used. The dollar estimate remains broadly centered around the same event, but the percentage discrepancy shows why different supply denominators should not be mixed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;4. Sei (SEI): Weekly Figure Versus Individual-Day Data&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Sei (SEI)&lt;/strong&gt; appears fourth in KuCoin's weekly ranking at approximately &lt;strong&gt;$5.4 million&lt;/strong&gt;, equal to a reported &lt;strong&gt;1.61% of circulating supply&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Other tracking reports have placed a specific September 15 SEI release at approximately &lt;strong&gt;$2.46 million to $2.50 million&lt;/strong&gt;, or around &lt;strong&gt;0.86%&lt;/strong&gt; under their respective methodology.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The difference does not necessarily mean that one figure is incorrect. A weekly ranking can aggregate or classify scheduled releases differently from a tracker that highlights a particular day's unlock. Traders should therefore confirm the release date and event scope before interpreting the number as a single-day supply increase.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;5. KAITO (KAITO): Around $5.3M in the Weekly Ranking&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;KAITO&lt;/strong&gt; ranks fifth in KuCoin's September 14–20 list with an estimated &lt;strong&gt;$5.3 million&lt;/strong&gt; unlock and a reported &lt;strong&gt;7.29% of circulating supply&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An alternative report from &lt;strong&gt;Bitcoinsistemi&lt;/strong&gt; places the September 20 KAITO unlock at approximately &lt;strong&gt;$5.36 million and 7.29%&lt;/strong&gt;. The dollar-value difference is small, while the reported percentage is the same.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Because the two estimates are very close, KAITO does not show the same major data discrepancy seen with some of the other tokens in the weekly ranking.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;6. Starknet (STRK): Another Smaller-Dollar Unlock to Watch&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Starknet's STRK&lt;/strong&gt; is sixth with an estimated &lt;strong&gt;$4.7 million&lt;/strong&gt; unlock and a reported &lt;strong&gt;2.27% of circulating supply&lt;/strong&gt; in KuCoin's weekly ranking.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Alternative reports have placed the relevant release closer to approximately &lt;strong&gt;$3.53 million–$3.63 million&lt;/strong&gt;, with percentages reported in the roughly &lt;strong&gt;1.79%–3.48%&lt;/strong&gt; range depending on the dataset and calculation method.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The difference can reflect variations in token prices, supply snapshots and event definitions. For STRK, the safest approach is to treat the &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/singapore-exchange-targets-us.html"&gt;KuCoin figure&lt;/a&gt; as the weekly-ranking estimate while recognizing that other trackers may show a different value for the scheduled release.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;7. OFFICIAL TRUMP (TRUMP): $1.8M for This Week, Not the Entire September Unlock&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;OFFICIAL TRUMP (TRUMP)&lt;/strong&gt; ranks seventh in KuCoin's September 14–20 weekly list at approximately &lt;strong&gt;$1.8 million&lt;/strong&gt;, representing &lt;strong&gt;0.33% of circulating supply&lt;/strong&gt; according to that ranking.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This number needs an important qualification: &lt;strong&gt;$1.8 million refers to the amount included in the September 14–20 weekly ranking, not the entire September unlock schedule.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Broader September reporting has cited a much larger TRUMP unlock of approximately &lt;strong&gt;$60.25 million&lt;/strong&gt;, or around &lt;strong&gt;10.35%&lt;/strong&gt; under that dataset's methodology. The two numbers therefore describe different event scopes and should not be presented as direct contradictions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Token Unlock Figures Differ Across Platforms&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Investors often see different numbers for the same token unlock. That does not automatically mean that one source is incorrect. The most common reasons include token-price timing, circulating-supply snapshots, different denominators and whether a platform is reporting a single-day event, a weekly total or a broader monthly schedule.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Token Unlocks Matter for Crypto Traders&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Token unlocks matter because they can change the amount of supply that becomes transferable or potentially available to the market. When a large allocation becomes unlocked, investors may reassess the balance between available supply and demand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, an unlock itself is &lt;strong&gt;not a guaranteed sell signal&lt;/strong&gt;. Tokens may remain with investors, project contributors, foundations, ecosystem participants or other recipients. Some may be staked, transferred, held or used within the project's ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The potential market effect depends on several factors:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Unlock size:&lt;/strong&gt; Larger dollar-value releases can attract more market attention.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Percentage of supply:&lt;/strong&gt; A smaller dollar unlock can still be significant if it represents a large share of the relevant supply.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Recipient type:&lt;/strong&gt; Investor, team, foundation and ecosystem allocations can have different selling behavior.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Liquidity:&lt;/strong&gt; A highly liquid token may absorb additional supply more easily than a thinly traded asset.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Market conditions:&lt;/strong&gt; Risk appetite, Bitcoin's direction and broader crypto liquidity can amplify or reduce the effect.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;PUMP and STBL Are Not Part of This Top 7&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Two tokens frequently mentioned in broader &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/ai-crashed-market-whos-liable.html"&gt;token-unlock&lt;/a&gt; discussions this month are &lt;strong&gt;PUMP&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;STBL&lt;/strong&gt;. They should not, however, be inserted into this specific September 14–20 top-seven ranking simply because they have notable upcoming supply events.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Broader September schedules can include releases outside the September 14–20 window. In particular, an STBL event scheduled later in September belongs to a different reporting period. Likewise, broader PUMP unlock figures should not be substituted for the seven-token weekly ranking above.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This distinction is important for avoiding misleading headlines that combine events from different dates into a single weekly list.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Traders Should Watch This Week&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;ZRO is the headline event by dollar value&lt;/strong&gt;, while BR and YZY stand out because their reported supply percentages are comparatively large. SEI, KAITO and STRK have smaller dollar values but can still become relevant if liquidity is weak or market sentiment deteriorates.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;TRUMP requires the most careful interpretation because its $1.8 million figure in the weekly ranking represents only the portion assigned to the September 14–20 period. Broader monthly figures can look dramatically larger because they cover additional scheduled releases.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Traders should therefore avoid treating the ranking as a simple “sell list.” The more useful approach is to monitor the unlock date, recipient allocation, exchange liquidity, spot volume, derivatives positioning and price action around the release.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The September 14–20 token-unlock schedule is led by &lt;strong&gt;LayerZero (ZRO) at $26.8 million&lt;/strong&gt;, followed by &lt;strong&gt;Bedrock (BR) at $16.9 million&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;YZY MONEY (YZY) at $8.4 million&lt;/strong&gt; in KuCoin's published weekly ranking.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The seven highlighted releases total approximately &lt;strong&gt;$69.3 million&lt;/strong&gt; using those weekly-ranking figures. But the comparison also shows why token-unlock data should be handled carefully: alternative platforms can report different dollar values or supply percentages because they may use different prices, supply snapshots, denominators or event scopes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For readers and traders, the key takeaway is simple: &lt;strong&gt;the size of an unlock matters, but the percentage of supply, recipient allocation, liquidity and exact event period matter just as much.&lt;/strong&gt; ZRO is the largest dollar-value event in this week's ranking, while BR and YZY deserve additional attention because of their reported supply impact.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Data note: This article uses KuCoin's September 14–20 weekly ranking as the primary ranking framework. Alternative figures are included to show how token-unlock providers can differ in methodology and should not be interpreted as identical calculations.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Mistral Partners With Saudi-Backed HUMAIN to Build Sovereign AI Infrastructure in the Middle East</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;
  &lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiYQXrGQbRdmMYThaL4GXuZdWWP56G-vwPSc_p1_41Yb_LXxyIDZBgwvOb_HN42WRAXV5S8jWKAd9M5bWcpL2A9psh_N4pLVqZv52P8f5mAz-0Ql5hLrklqHJ__c1nEwngAZ5IfMS7iHOUxdbpo-o0gQR95UO30xA3smGEKl-RWK9xA13z52VvLPNOXGGGP/s1672/mistral-humain-saudi-arabia-sovereign-ai-infrastructure.jpg%20(2).png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Mistral and HUMAIN sovereign AI infrastructure partnership in Saudi Arabia" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiYQXrGQbRdmMYThaL4GXuZdWWP56G-vwPSc_p1_41Yb_LXxyIDZBgwvOb_HN42WRAXV5S8jWKAd9M5bWcpL2A9psh_N4pLVqZv52P8f5mAz-0Ql5hLrklqHJ__c1nEwngAZ5IfMS7iHOUxdbpo-o0gQR95UO30xA3smGEKl-RWK9xA13z52VvLPNOXGGGP/w400-h225/mistral-humain-saudi-arabia-sovereign-ai-infrastructure.jpg%20(2).png" title="Mistral and HUMAIN Build Sovereign AI Infrastructure" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: small;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: left;"&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: small;"&gt;By CoinAINews Staff |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;French AI company &lt;strong&gt;Mistral AI&lt;/strong&gt; is expanding its presence in the Middle East through a major strategic collaboration with &lt;strong&gt;HUMAIN&lt;/strong&gt;, the Saudi Arabian artificial intelligence company backed by the country's Public Investment Fund.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The partnership, which the companies said is valued in the &lt;strong&gt;hundreds of millions of euros&lt;/strong&gt;, will focus on AI infrastructure, advanced model development and localized artificial intelligence capabilities for Saudi Arabia and the wider region.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The announcement comes as Saudi Arabia continues to position itself as a major global destination for artificial intelligence investment and computing infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For Mistral, the agreement offers access to a rapidly developing market and Saudi-based computing capacity. For Saudi Arabia, it is another step toward building AI infrastructure that can operate with greater local control over data, computing resources and AI systems.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Is Sovereign AI?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The phrase &lt;strong&gt;“sovereign AI”&lt;/strong&gt; is at the center of the partnership.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;In simple terms, sovereign AI refers to artificial intelligence infrastructure and systems that can be operated under the control of a particular country, organization or customer rather than depending entirely on foreign platforms and infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That can involve several layers of the AI stack, including:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Data storage and governance&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Computing infrastructure&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;AI models&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Model deployment&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Operational control&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The idea has become increasingly important as governments and large organizations look at where sensitive data is processed and which companies control the infrastructure powering their AI systems.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For Saudi Arabia, local AI infrastructure could be particularly relevant in areas such as government services, financial services, telecommunications, manufacturing and cybersecurity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Mistral and HUMAIN Are Planning&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The collaboration covers several areas rather than focusing on a single AI product.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;table&gt;
    &lt;thead&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;th&gt;Focus Area&lt;/th&gt;
        &lt;th&gt;What the Partnership Covers&lt;/th&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
    &lt;/thead&gt;
    &lt;tbody&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI Infrastructure&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td&gt;Mistral will explore using HUMAIN's Saudi-based data center infrastructure for local AI computing requirements.&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI Models&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td&gt;The companies plan to work together on advanced models and localized AI capabilities.&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Arabic AI&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td&gt;The partnership includes work toward AI models with strong Arabic-language capabilities.&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Cybersecurity&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td&gt;Cybersecurity is among the initial areas identified for model and application development.&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Voice Technology&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td&gt;Voice-based AI is another early focus of the collaboration.&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
      &lt;tr&gt;
        &lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Commercial Deployment&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;
        &lt;td&gt;The companies intend to develop AI solutions for industries where data control and regulatory requirements are particularly important.&lt;/td&gt;
      &lt;/tr&gt;
    &lt;/tbody&gt;
  &lt;/table&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Saudi Arabia Is Betting Big on AI&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Saudi Arabia has been investing heavily in &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/thorchain-320-brings-monero-and-zcash.html"&gt;artificial intelligence&lt;/a&gt; as part of its broader economic transformation strategy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The country's &lt;strong&gt;Vision 2030&lt;/strong&gt; program aims to diversify the economy beyond oil and develop new technology-driven industries.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;AI has become one of the most important parts of that strategy.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Rather than simply becoming a major consumer of AI services, Saudi Arabia is attempting to build the infrastructure required to host and operate large-scale AI systems inside the country.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That includes data centers, computing capacity, semiconductor access, cloud infrastructure and partnerships with international AI companies.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;HUMAIN was established as one of the vehicles for that effort.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;HUMAIN's Role in the AI Buildout&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;HUMAIN is backed by Saudi Arabia's &lt;strong&gt;Public Investment Fund (PIF)&lt;/strong&gt; and has been working to build an AI ecosystem around data centers, computing infrastructure, models and applications.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The company has announced partnerships across different parts of the AI technology stack, reflecting Saudi Arabia's effort to secure access to both hardware and software.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That strategy matters because building competitive &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/monad-developers-propose-upgradeable.html"&gt;AI infrastructure&lt;/a&gt; requires much more than simply training a model.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Large AI systems need enormous amounts of computing power, reliable electricity, specialized chips, high-speed networking and large-scale data center capacity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Saudi Arabia has the capital and energy resources to invest heavily in that infrastructure, while partnerships with international technology companies can provide access to expertise and technology.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Why Mistral Is Interested&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For Mistral, the Middle East represents an increasingly important opportunity.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The French company has positioned itself as one of Europe's leading independent AI developers and has sought to expand beyond its home market.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;A Saudi partnership gives Mistral access to local infrastructure and customers while allowing its technology to become part of a broader regional AI ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The arrangement also fits into a larger trend among AI companies.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Instead of every customer sending sensitive information to a centralized cloud platform operated elsewhere, organizations are increasingly interested in deploying AI closer to where their data is generated.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That can be particularly attractive for governments and heavily regulated businesses.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Arabic AI Could Become a Major Focus&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;One of the more interesting elements of the partnership is the focus on &lt;strong&gt;Arabic-language AI&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Arabic is spoken by hundreds of millions of people, but developing highly capable AI systems for Arabic presents its own technical challenges.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Arabic includes multiple dialects, regional variations and different writing conventions. An AI model that performs well in English does not automatically provide the same quality across Arabic-language applications.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Better Arabic models could have applications across:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;ul&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Government services&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Customer support&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Education&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Healthcare&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Banking&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Media&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Enterprise software&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For Saudi Arabia, developing strong Arabic AI capabilities could therefore have strategic value beyond simply improving chatbot performance.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Cybersecurity and Voice Are Early Priorities&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The companies have also identified &lt;strong&gt;cybersecurity and voice technology&lt;/strong&gt; as early areas of interest.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Cybersecurity is becoming an increasingly important &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/monad-developers-propose-upgradeable.html"&gt;AI application&lt;/a&gt; as organizations use machine learning to detect threats, analyze large volumes of security information and respond to attacks.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Voice AI, meanwhile, could become especially important for Arabic-language applications where natural speech interaction is a major part of the user experience.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Combining those technologies with locally controlled infrastructure could allow Saudi organizations to deploy AI systems while keeping sensitive workloads closer to home.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Deal's Financial Scale&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The partnership is valued in the &lt;strong&gt;hundreds of millions of euros&lt;/strong&gt;, according to the companies.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That puts the agreement among the more significant commercial AI collaborations associated with Mistral as the company continues expanding internationally.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The exact economics and implementation schedule, however, are different from simply announcing a single software product.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The collaboration involves infrastructure, model development and commercial deployment, meaning its impact is likely to unfold over time rather than through one immediate product launch.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;A Bigger Shift in Global AI&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The Mistral-HUMAIN agreement reflects a trend that is becoming increasingly visible around the world.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Governments are beginning to view AI infrastructure as strategic infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The question is no longer only which AI model is the smartest.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Countries are also asking:&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Where is the model running?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Who controls the computing infrastructure?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Where is sensitive data stored?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Who controls access to the technology?&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Those questions are pushing governments in Europe, the Middle East and Asia to explore their own AI infrastructure and partnerships.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The result could be a more geographically distributed AI industry instead of one dominated entirely by a handful of technology companies operating primarily from the United States and China.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What This Means for the Middle East&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For the Middle East, the partnership could help accelerate the development of a regional AI ecosystem.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Saudi Arabia already has access to significant financial resources through its sovereign wealth fund. What it needs is the technology, infrastructure and talent required to turn those investments into commercially useful AI capabilities.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Partnerships with companies such as Mistral can help bridge that gap.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;At the same time, international AI companies gain access to a market that is willing to spend heavily on computing infrastructure and large-scale technology projects.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That creates a potentially attractive relationship for both sides.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;Mistral's Broader Gulf Connections&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The HUMAIN agreement is not Mistral's first connection to Gulf capital.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Saudi Arabia's &lt;strong&gt;Sanabil Investments&lt;/strong&gt;, a PIF subsidiary, has previously invested in Mistral.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Mistral has also developed relationships with investors and technology organizations in the United Arab Emirates.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Those connections show that Gulf sovereign wealth and technology investment are becoming increasingly intertwined with the global AI industry.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For Mistral, that could provide an important source of capital and infrastructure as it competes with much larger American AI companies.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next?&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The immediate focus will be on turning the strategic agreement into actual infrastructure and products.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;That means deploying computing capacity, developing localized models, improving Arabic-language performance and identifying commercial applications where sovereign AI provides a clear advantage.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The biggest test will be whether those investments translate into AI systems that businesses and government organizations actually use at scale.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Building data centers is only the beginning.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The harder challenge is creating an ecosystem of models, developers, applications and customers around that infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h2&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Mistral's partnership with HUMAIN is more than another AI collaboration.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;It reflects the growing push by governments and major organizations to gain greater control over the technology powering their artificial intelligence systems.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For Saudi Arabia, the agreement supports its ambition to become a major global AI hub while developing computing infrastructure and Arabic-language AI capabilities closer to home.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;For Mistral, it creates a significant foothold in one of the world's fastest-growing AI investment markets and gives the French company another route to expand beyond Europe.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;The bigger story, however, is the shift toward &lt;strong&gt;sovereign AI&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly important to governments, businesses and national economies, control over data, computing power and AI models could become just as important as the models themselves.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Saudi Arabia is betting that it can build that infrastructure at scale. Mistral is now becoming part of that bet.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment or financial advice. AI technology, partnerships and commercial arrangements can change as projects develop.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Can a Pending Bitcoin Transaction Be Cancelled?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiI0pxR_k-xcnV0p2PaMr8n6mXaw6dlavMgzOKgMMzaWaY6sw_i_wNDsO-_q2JvdMmU__XjCwGHmIinDzMZ97iLgrERLcdfrs7vC16EAK0kA3i62m855HChAjstkTtGqqeV0rcu6BKESM8IMTaX-_o5o33dAbg0WsYnEzJCey6Vb3mhiiOv9056XfKemicl/s1672/pending-bitcoin-transaction-cancel-rbf.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Pending Bitcoin transaction waiting for confirmation and RBF replacement" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="360" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEiI0pxR_k-xcnV0p2PaMr8n6mXaw6dlavMgzOKgMMzaWaY6sw_i_wNDsO-_q2JvdMmU__XjCwGHmIinDzMZ97iLgrERLcdfrs7vC16EAK0kA3i62m855HChAjstkTtGqqeV0rcu6BKESM8IMTaX-_o5o33dAbg0WsYnEzJCey6Vb3mhiiOv9056XfKemicl/w640-h360/pending-bitcoin-transaction-cancel-rbf.jpg.png" title="Can a Pending Bitcoin Transaction Be Cancelled?" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&lt;p&gt;
September 7, 2026&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes, a &lt;strong&gt;pending Bitcoin transaction may sometimes be replaced before it is confirmed&lt;/strong&gt;, but calling it a simple “cancellation” can be misleading. Bitcoin does not have a central authority or cancel button that can simply pull a transaction back after it has been broadcast.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If a transaction is still unconfirmed in the Bitcoin mempool, the sender may be able to use &lt;strong&gt;Replace-by-Fee (RBF)&lt;/strong&gt; to replace it with another transaction that spends the same inputs and pays a higher fee. Another technique, &lt;strong&gt;Child-Pays-for-Parent (CPFP)&lt;/strong&gt;, can help accelerate a stuck transaction, but it does not cancel the original payment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once a Bitcoin transaction has been confirmed in a block, the situation is different. A normal confirmed Bitcoin transaction cannot simply be cancelled or reversed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Quick Answer: Can You Cancel a Pending Bitcoin Transaction?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 700px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Transaction Status&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Can It Be Cancelled?&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;What You Can Do&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Unconfirmed / Pending&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Sometimes, indirectly&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Use RBF to replace it, if supported; &lt;br /&gt;CPFP may accelerate confirmation&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Stuck in the mempool&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Not with a normal &lt;br /&gt;cancel button&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Consider RBF or CPFP depending &lt;br /&gt;on the transaction&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Confirmed in a block&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;No&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;A normal Bitcoin transaction cannot &lt;br /&gt;be reversed&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The key distinction is between &lt;strong&gt;cancelling a transaction&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;replacing an unconfirmed transaction&lt;/strong&gt;. Bitcoin's network does not process cancellations in the way a bank or payment app might.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why Is a Bitcoin Transaction Pending?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When you send &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/why-is-my-bitcoin-transaction-still.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt;, the signed transaction is broadcast to the network. Before it is included in a block, it can remain in the &lt;strong&gt;mempool&lt;/strong&gt;, where unconfirmed transactions wait for miners to select them for inclusion in a block.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A common reason for a transaction remaining pending is that its fee rate is too low compared with the fees being offered by other transactions competing for limited block space.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Network congestion can make the problem more noticeable. If demand for block space rises after you broadcast the transaction, a transaction with a relatively low fee rate may take longer to confirm.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Coinbase also lists insufficient fees, high network activity, network synchronization issues and insufficient confirmations among reasons a transaction can remain pending on its platform. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is Replace-by-Fee (RBF)?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Replace-by-Fee, or RBF,&lt;/strong&gt; is the main mechanism people refer to when they ask whether a pending Bitcoin transaction can be cancelled.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Instead of literally cancelling the original transaction, RBF allows an unconfirmed transaction to be replaced by another transaction that spends at least one of the same inputs and pays a higher fee under the applicable replacement rules.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new transaction can be constructed to send the Bitcoin to a different output, including an address controlled by the sender. If the replacement is accepted and later confirmed, the original conflicting transaction cannot also confirm using the same spent inputs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Blockstream's current explanation describes RBF as a way to replace an unconfirmed Bitcoin transaction with a new version carrying a higher fee. Bitcoin Optech likewise describes RBF as a node policy for replacing an unconfirmed transaction with another transaction that spends at least one of the same inputs and pays a higher fee. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can RBF Be Used to Cancel a Bitcoin Payment?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Sometimes, yes—but “replace” is the more accurate word.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Imagine you accidentally send 0.1 &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-you-recover-crypto-sent-to-the-wrong-network.html"&gt;BTC &lt;/a&gt;to the wrong address. The transaction has been broadcast but is still unconfirmed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your wallet supports fee bumping and the transaction can be replaced, you may be able to create a replacement transaction that spends the same inputs and sends the funds to an address you control, while paying a higher fee.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the replacement is accepted and confirmed, the original transaction will not subsequently confirm as a separate transaction using those same inputs.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;However, this is not a guaranteed emergency cancellation feature. The exact options depend on the wallet, transaction structure and network policies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If My Wallet Shows “Bump Fee” or “Speed Up”?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Many modern Bitcoin wallets use terms such as &lt;strong&gt;“Bump Fee,” “Increase Fee,” or “Speed Up”&lt;/strong&gt; for fee-management features.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;These options are primarily designed to make an unconfirmed transaction more competitive for block inclusion. Depending on the wallet and transaction, the feature may use RBF or another fee-bumping mechanism.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your goal is to stop an accidental payment rather than simply confirm it faster, do not assume that pressing “Speed Up” will cancel anything. Check exactly what the wallet is offering before signing a replacement transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Is CPFP and Does It Cancel a Bitcoin Transaction?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No. CPFP does not cancel a Bitcoin transaction.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;CPFP stands for &lt;strong&gt;Child-Pays-for-Parent&lt;/strong&gt;. It is primarily a way to encourage miners to confirm a stuck transaction by creating a second transaction with a higher fee.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The idea is relatively simple: a new “child” transaction spends an output from the unconfirmed “parent” transaction. Because the child depends on the parent, a miner that wants the child's fee generally needs to include the parent as well.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This can increase the effective fee rate of the package and make confirmation more attractive.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Mempool's documentation specifically identifies CPFP as an option when the sender cannot use RBF, provided the user controls an appropriate output from the stuck transaction. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So if you accidentally sent Bitcoin to the wrong address, &lt;strong&gt;CPFP is generally not the tool you want&lt;/strong&gt;. It is designed to help get a transaction confirmed, not to undo it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;RBF vs. CPFP: What's the Difference?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;div style="margin: 20px 0px; overflow-x: auto; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;table style="border-collapse: collapse; min-width: 760px; width: 100%;"&gt;
&lt;thead&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;Feature&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;RBF&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;th style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px; text-align: left;"&gt;CPFP&lt;/th&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/thead&gt;
&lt;tbody&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Main purpose&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Replace an unconfirmed &lt;br /&gt;transaction&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Accelerate confirmation&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Creates a new transaction?&lt;/td&gt;

&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Yes&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Can it undo a pending payment?&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Potentially, by replacing it &lt;br /&gt;before confirmation&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;No&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Needs access to original inputs?&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;The replacement must satisfy &lt;br /&gt;the relevant rules and &lt;br /&gt;requirescontrol of the spending keys&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Requires control of a suitable &lt;br /&gt;unconfirmed output&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;tr&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Useful for stuck transactions?&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Yes&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;td style="border: 1px solid rgb(153, 153, 153); padding: 10px;"&gt;Yes&lt;/td&gt;
&lt;/tr&gt;
&lt;/tbody&gt;
&lt;/table&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens If the Bitcoin Transaction Is Already Confirmed?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is where the answer becomes much simpler.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;A normal Bitcoin transaction that has already been confirmed in a block cannot be cancelled through RBF.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;RBF operates on unconfirmed transactions. Once the transaction has been included in a confirmed block, it is no longer sitting in the mempool waiting for inclusion.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means an accidental payment to the wrong Bitcoin address generally cannot be recovered simply because the sender made a mistake.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At that point, recovery depends on the circumstances. If the recipient is known and willing to return the funds, they may send them back in a new transaction. If the destination belongs to an exchange or another identifiable service, contacting that service may be worth trying, although recovery is not guaranteed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can a Pending Transaction Eventually Disappear?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Yes, an unconfirmed transaction can eventually disappear from a node's mempool if it is not confirmed and is removed under that node's&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/can-bitcoin-transaction-be-reversed.html"&gt; mempool policies&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That does not mean Bitcoin has processed a formal cancellation. It means the transaction is no longer being retained by that particular node or set of nodes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Mempool notes that an unconfirmed transaction can either confirm or otherwise be removed from mempool handling, and users can continue tracking the transaction using its transaction ID. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If a transaction disappears from one mempool, that does not automatically mean the transaction has been cancelled everywhere. The safest approach is to check its status using a reputable Bitcoin block explorer and understand what your wallet is reporting.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Should You Do If Your Bitcoin Transaction Is Stuck?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Before taking action, find the transaction ID, also known as the &lt;strong&gt;TXID&lt;/strong&gt;, and check it on a Bitcoin block explorer.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Then determine whether it is:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Unconfirmed:&lt;/strong&gt; It is still waiting for confirmation.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Confirmed:&lt;/strong&gt; It has already been included in a block.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Missing from the mempool:&lt;/strong&gt; It may have been dropped by the node or may require further investigation.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If it is unconfirmed, check whether your wallet provides an RBF or fee-bump option.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you are trying to accelerate an incoming transaction and control an output that can be spent before confirmation, CPFP may be an option.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction was sent through an exchange rather than directly from a self-custody wallet, the exchange's own policies matter. Coinbase, for example, advises users with pending sends to check the transaction through a block explorer and contact support if the confirmation remains stuck. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What If You Sent Bitcoin to the Wrong Address?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is one of the most important situations to understand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction is still unconfirmed, you may have an opportunity to replace it depending on the transaction and wallet.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If it has already confirmed, however, Bitcoin itself cannot identify that you made a mistake and automatically return the coins.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the address belongs to another person, the recipient would generally need to cooperate and send the Bitcoin back.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the address belongs to an exchange or identifiable service, contact its official support channel as soon as possible and provide the TXID and relevant transaction information.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Never give anyone your seed phrase or private keys while asking for help recovering a transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Does RBF Guarantee That a Transaction Can Be Cancelled?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;No.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;RBF is a transaction replacement mechanism, not a guaranteed cancellation service.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are technical rules governing replacements, and wallet interfaces vary. A replacement transaction also needs to be accepted and propagated through the network before it can compete for confirmation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Most importantly, once a conflicting transaction has already been confirmed, the opportunity to replace the original unconfirmed transaction is gone.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Can Coinbase or Another Exchange Cancel a Pending Bitcoin Transaction?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This depends on what “pending” means inside the exchange.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An exchange may have an internal status for a withdrawal that has not yet been broadcast to the Bitcoin network. In that situation, the exchange may have more control than it would after the transaction has been broadcast.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once an actual Bitcoin transaction has been broadcast to the network, however, the exchange cannot simply rewrite Bitcoin's blockchain history.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Coinbase distinguishes between pending transactions and confirmed transactions and notes that once a blockchain transaction is confirmed, it cannot be reversed. &lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Can a pending Bitcoin transaction be cancelled?&lt;/strong&gt; Not in the traditional sense.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If the transaction is still unconfirmed, &lt;strong&gt;RBF may allow you to replace it&lt;/strong&gt; with another transaction, potentially redirecting the funds while paying a higher fee. &lt;strong&gt;CPFP can help accelerate confirmation but does not cancel the original transaction.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Once a transaction has been confirmed, there is no normal Bitcoin “undo” button. Recovery then depends on the recipient, exchange or other party involved—not on reversing the confirmed Bitcoin transaction itself.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The safest habit is simple: &lt;strong&gt;check the address and amount carefully before signing and broadcasting a Bitcoin transaction.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Frequently Asked Questions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;1. Can I cancel a Bitcoin transaction while it is pending?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;Sometimes. If it is still unconfirmed, an appropriate RBF replacement may allow the original transaction to be replaced. Bitcoin does not provide a conventional cancel button.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;2. Can I cancel a Bitcoin transaction after one confirmation?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. Once a normal transaction has been confirmed in a block, RBF cannot be used to replace it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;3. What is RBF in Bitcoin?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;RBF, or Replace-by-Fee, is a mechanism that allows an unconfirmed transaction to be replaced with another transaction that satisfies the network's replacement rules and pays a higher fee.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;4. Does CPFP cancel a stuck Bitcoin transaction?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;No. CPFP, or Child-Pays-for-Parent, is designed to encourage confirmation of an unconfirmed transaction by attaching a higher-fee child transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;5. Why is my Bitcoin transaction stuck pending?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;A transaction can remain pending because of a relatively low fee rate, network congestion, node synchronization issues or other transaction-processing conditions.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;6. What happens if my Bitcoin transaction never confirms?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;An unconfirmed transaction may eventually be removed from a node's mempool under its policies. If that happens and the transaction is no longer being propagated, the underlying coins may become available to spend again, depending on the wallet and transaction state.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;7. Can an exchange reverse a Bitcoin transaction?&lt;/h3&gt;
&lt;p&gt;An exchange may be able to cancel an internal or not-yet-broadcast withdrawal under its own systems. Once a Bitcoin transaction has been broadcast and confirmed on the blockchain, however, the exchange cannot simply reverse the confirmed transaction.&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>North Korea Stole $2.8B in Crypto and Is Now Laundering It Through Crime Networks, RUSI Says</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhfQutKyfEKzJRBzkar-lbaBBwdbEAIITAh3012CUFFlugQjcKEGBauqC5dTibD3Q9ipZbCDwuJmVvCX105fStbHxelIBtqKXbrV7HJub3G0JW6hKOkeyQUtsEl-12caSzz_gm5LJSxYgbHeX55I-jpVONPbidKlrlkf5HqQdB_jD35UCxqUAsIraKACdpg/s1672/hackers.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="North Korean crypto hacking and money laundering network with Bitcoin, blockchain transactions and cybercrime imagery" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="180" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhfQutKyfEKzJRBzkar-lbaBBwdbEAIITAh3012CUFFlugQjcKEGBauqC5dTibD3Q9ipZbCDwuJmVvCX105fStbHxelIBtqKXbrV7HJub3G0JW6hKOkeyQUtsEl-12caSzz_gm5LJSxYgbHeX55I-jpVONPbidKlrlkf5HqQdB_jD35UCxqUAsIraKACdpg/w320-h180/hackers.png" title="North Korean crypto hacking and money laundering network with Bitcoin, blockchain transactions and cybercrime imagery" width="320" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Aug 12, 2026&amp;nbsp;– North Korean hackers stole at
least&amp;nbsp;$2.8 billion&amp;nbsp;in &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/white-house-fully-committed-to-passing_01754799517.html"&gt;cryptocurrency &lt;/a&gt;between January 2024 and
September 2025, and they are now laundering the proceeds through scam
syndicates and organized crime networks to make the funds harder to trace,
according to a new report from the Royal United Services Institute&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The London-based defense and security think tank said the
regime has built a complex laundering pipeline that spans multiple blockchains,
Chinese-language markets, and traditional banks, increasingly relying on
third-party criminal networks to convert stolen digital assets into fiat
currency&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"The regime has pushed at least $2.8 billion in
stolen virtual assets between January 2024 and September 2025, with researchers
focusing on the moment those assets convert into cash."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;br /&gt;
—&amp;nbsp;Royal United Services Institute report&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Scale of the Theft&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The $2.8 billion figure aligns with estimates from the
Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT), which reported in October 2025
that North Korea stole approximately **$2.84 billion** in virtual assets during
the same period&amp;nbsp;. U.S. officials have described this as a
"conservative low-end estimate," with the actual number likely
higher&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The breakdown of stolen funds:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;$1.65
     billion&amp;nbsp;stolen in 2025 alone&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;$1.46
     billion&amp;nbsp;from the Bybit exchange in February 2025 — the largest single
     crypto heist in history&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;$308
     million&amp;nbsp;from DMM Bitcoin in Japan&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;$234
     million&amp;nbsp;from WazirX in India&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l2 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;$50
     million&amp;nbsp;from Radiant Capital&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Chainalysis estimated that North Korean hackers
stole&amp;nbsp;$2.02 billion&amp;nbsp;in cryptocurrency in 2025, a 51% year-over-year
increase, with the group now holding more bitcoin than Tesla — funds it stole
rather than bought&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;How the Laundering Pipeline Works&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The RUSI report focuses on how stolen &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/white-house-fully-committed-to-passing.html"&gt;crypto &lt;/a&gt;is converted
into cash, revealing a sophisticated system that makes tracing increasingly
difficult&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Key findings on the laundering process:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;1. Third-party bulk purchases:&amp;nbsp;In some cases, third
parties buy entire batches of stolen assets at a discount before the funds are
mixed with scam proceeds or money tied to criminal groups&amp;nbsp;. Elliptic data
suggests these transfers frequently occur on the Bitcoin blockchain&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;2. Criminal network overlap:&amp;nbsp;North Korean funds are
increasingly laundered through the same networks used by scam syndicates,
including "pig butchering" investment scams. Once proceeds mix with
scam money, exchanges struggle to separate proliferation finance from ordinary
laundering&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;3. Money mules and fragmented cash-outs:&amp;nbsp;The
accounts used to cash out typically belong to mules recruited in the
Philippines, Indonesia, and China, where identities are cheap enough to buy in
bulk&amp;nbsp;. Conversion happens in small slices:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;~$7,000&amp;nbsp;in
     stablecoins sold at a time on peer-to-peer marketplaces to stay below bank
     review thresholds&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l1 level1 lfo2; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Larger
     sums broken into&amp;nbsp;$30,000&amp;nbsp;pieces so any freeze "would not be
     overly damaging"&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;4. Fiat delivery through Chinese banks:&amp;nbsp;OTC brokers
deposit proceeds into North Korean-controlled accounts using UnionPay cards
issued by Chinese banks. The MSMT last year identified&amp;nbsp;19 Chinese banks&amp;nbsp;used
by the regime and its proxies&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Lazarus Group's Role&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The thefts are attributed to North Korea's Reconnaissance
General Bureau, with sub-clusters tracked as&amp;nbsp;Lazarus Group, APT38,
TraderTraitor, and AppleJeus&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bybit hack demonstrated their sophistication:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Attackers
     compromised the SAFE front-end UI that Bybit operations personnel used to
     approve transactions&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Replaced
     transaction data with a malicious delegatecall that changed the wallet's
     implementation contract&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Signers,
     seeing what looked like a legitimate transaction on their Ledger screens,
     approved it&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo3; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Minutes
     later, the attacker drained ETH and ERC-20 tokens&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The FBI attributed the Bybit theft to TraderTraitor on
February 26, 2025&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why This Matters for Crypto&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The implications are significant:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;National
     security threat:&amp;nbsp;The stolen funds are used to finance North Korea's
     nuclear and ballistic missile programs&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Regulatory
     scrutiny:&amp;nbsp;The report could accelerate stricter KYC requirements on
     OTC desks and peer-to-peer platforms&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l3 level1 lfo4; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Detection
     challenges:&amp;nbsp;Once inside criminal ecosystems, proliferation finance
     becomes difficult to distinguish from standard money laundering&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The recovery challenge is stark:&amp;nbsp;Bybit has recovered
only&amp;nbsp;$48.4 million** and frozen **$30.5 million&amp;nbsp;more — about&amp;nbsp;5%&amp;nbsp;of
what was stolen&amp;nbsp;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;North Korea has built the highest-value sustained
cybercrime campaign in history. The RUSI report reveals that the regime is no
longer just hacking exchanges — it has integrated its theft operations into the
broader criminal economy, making it harder to track, harder to stop, and harder
to recover stolen funds.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For the crypto industry, the report is a reminder that
the same tools that enable borderless, permissionless finance also enable
state-backed criminal enterprises. The methods are evolving. The response must
as well.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;
