color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;However, because SkyAI uses a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;plurality voting standard&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;, the withheld votes did not directly remove the directors, and all five retained their seats. Bastion criticized this voting standard as "archaic and undemocratic," noting the board lacks a policy requiring directors to resign when they fail to receive majority support.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Treasury Holdings and the Broader Picture&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;SkyAI holds approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;2,009,494 SOL&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;, a position valued at roughly &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;$207 million in September reporting&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;, making it the fifth-largest publicly traded Solana treasury company by SOL holdings.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;The company, formerly Sharps Technology, pivoted to a Solana treasury strategy and has positioned itself around "Agentic Finance for the Global South." In Q2 2026, SkyAI reported a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;net loss of $23.3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;, largely reflecting losses on its SOL holdings, according to its SEC filing.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;The Acquisition Backdrop: Forward Industries' Proposals&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;One backdrop to the governance conflict was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;Forward Industries' proposals&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; to acquire SkyAI. As one of the largest publicly traded Solana treasury companies, Forward had reported &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;7,013,536 SOL&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; in September reporting. It first proposed an all-stock acquisition of SkyAI on &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;June 15&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; at &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;0.367 FWDI shares per SKYA share&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;, representing roughly a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;20% premium&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; to SkyAI's then-current price. SkyAI's board &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;unanimously rejected&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt; the proposal on &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;July 17&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;On &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;September 15&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;, Forward raised its proposal to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;$2.13 per share** in cash and/or stock, representing a **50% premium** to SkyAI's September 14 closing price of **$1.42&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;, and requested a board response by &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;September 25&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;. In a public letter, Forward said the SkyAI board "missed a compelling strategic opportunity" and pointed to serious governance concerns.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight: 600;"&gt;What Happens Next&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;Bastion Trading said in its latest statement that the board should "engage meaningfully with shareholders promptly" and "substantially reconstitute the board with new independent directors." Bastion said it is prepared to pursue all available legal remedies if the board fails to respond meaningfully.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="ds-markdown-paragraph" style="background-color: white; color: #0f1115; font-family: quote-cjk-patch, Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, &amp;quot;Segoe UI&amp;quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, &amp;quot;Open Sans&amp;quot;, &amp;quot;Helvetica Neue&amp;quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 16px 0px;"&gt;&lt;span class=""&gt;For SkyAI, the dispute centers on board composition, related-party transactions and the management of its SOL treasury. Bastion has called for meaningful shareholder engagement and new independent directors, while the existing board has retained its seats following the September 18 vote.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>

    <title>So, Are We at the Bottom or Just Seeing Another Dead Cat Bounce?</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhfc7_PEuDSH_VavsFG4UU0_os5Z_U1LSwI4HF789OK__D0moSewBP2lGdnZcifffFg-YeWQWla_liDHMBIzyKla1f13JSPbk3hIZkpBL214NhLKycZg5Fywwvo_mdC0dOvVJGrefDicztZ1gC9kWEdFbajZLViyUKAwubiVNz3CeCnI07Wuybf7V3n_xFu/s1672/bitcoin-bottom-dead-cat-bounce-crypto-market.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin price chart showing a possible market bottom, 200-day moving average breakout, and renewed crypto market momentum" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEhfc7_PEuDSH_VavsFG4UU0_os5Z_U1LSwI4HF789OK__D0moSewBP2lGdnZcifffFg-YeWQWla_liDHMBIzyKla1f13JSPbk3hIZkpBL214NhLKycZg5Fywwvo_mdC0dOvVJGrefDicztZ1gC9kWEdFbajZLViyUKAwubiVNz3CeCnI07Wuybf7V3n_xFu/w400-h225/bitcoin-bottom-dead-cat-bounce-crypto-market.jpg.png" title="Bitcoin Bottom or Dead Cat Bounce? Crypto Market Turning Point" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/i&gt;&amp;nbsp;|&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If you've been staring at Bitcoin charts this week, you know
the feeling. You check the price at breakfast, and it's cruising at $68,000.
You look again before lunch, and suddenly it's testing $72,000. By dinner, it's
settled back into the $69,000 range. It's enough to give you whiplash.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;And the sentiment is just as confusing. Just a few days ago,
the Fear and Greed Index was stuck in "Extreme Fear" territory.
Nobody wanted to touch crypto. Then, like a switch was flipped, the index
jumped 16 points in a single day, hitting a "Greed" reading of 62.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;So, which is it? Are we finally out of the bear market
woods, or is this just another headfake designed to suck in retail before a
bigger drop?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Honestly, the data is pointing in both directions. But
there's one technical signal that just flipped—and it's a big one.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Biggest Technical Signal of the Year Just Flipped&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;You've probably heard of the 200-day moving average. It's
not some magical line in the sand, but it's one of the most closely watched
indicators in the market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Here's what happened: Bitcoin had been trading&amp;nbsp;&lt;i&gt;below&lt;/i&gt;&amp;nbsp;its
200-day MA for&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;270 straight days&lt;/b&gt;. That's an eternity in crypto.
Being under the 200-day MA is basically a red flag—it tells you the market is
in a long-term downtrend. For more than nine months, that line hovered above
the price, taunting everyone who was bullish.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Well, that just changed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Earlier this month, Bitcoin finally broke above its 200-day
MA. The line was sitting near $69,000 while BTC was stuck around $64,000. The
gap between price and that MA was a constant reminder of how weak the market
had been. Breaking above it is the kind of thing that makes institutional
portfolio managers sit up and pay attention.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But here's the thing about the 200-day MA: it's a lagging
indicator. It doesn't predict the future; it just reflects the past. Breaking
above it can strengthen the case for a new bull market, but it is far from
conclusive on its own. In 2022, similar breakouts turned out to be fakeouts. We
need to see &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/anthropic-vs-spacex-2-trillion-ipo-that.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;i&gt;hold&lt;/i&gt;&amp;nbsp;above this level before we can say
the trend has truly changed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Sentiment Went from "I'm Done" to "I'm
All In" in 24 Hours&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Fear and Greed Index is another data point that tells a
story. The index is based on volatility, market volume, social media chatter,
and a few other factors. It's essentially a thermometer for market emotion.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For a while now, it's been stuck in the dumps. On August 19,
it was at a miserable 29. A week earlier, it was at 25—deep in "Extreme
Fear." The mood was pessimistic. Every rally was getting sold.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Then came August 20. The index shot up 16 points to
62—turning "Greed" for the first time since March 2026. That's the
kind of sentiment shift that only happens when the market is caught completely
off guard.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A lot of traders had been betting against Bitcoin. They had
short positions open, expecting prices to keep falling. But when BTC broke out,
they were forced to scramble. The short squeeze was massive—over&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$1.4
billion&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;in short positions were liquidated in a single day.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Now, there are two ways to look at this. On one hand, it
shows there was real momentum behind the move. The shorts got crushed, and that
added fuel to the rally. On the other hand, a squeeze is just positioning. It's
not the same as real, organic demand. When the squeeze is over, you need new
buyers to step in. If they don't, the rally can fizzle out just as fast as it
started.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bear Case: Why Some People Still Think This Is a Trap&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Look, I get why some people are skeptical. Even with this
rally, there are some clear warning signs.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin Dominance Hasn't Budged&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If this were the start of a real bull market, you'd expect
capital to start rotating from Bitcoin into altcoins. That's what usually
happens—the excitement spreads. But right now, Bitcoin dominance is still stuck
in the 58%–59% range. It hasn't moved. That tells you this rally is still a
Bitcoin-only affair. Altcoins haven't caught up yet.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The 2022 Warning Is Still Fresh in Everyone's Mind&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In March 2022, the same indicator that's now turning
positive gave a similar signal. A lot of people got excited. They thought the
bottom was in. They bought the dip. And then Bitcoin just kept falling. That
"bullish signal" ended up being a bull trap, and the market went on
to have a brutal, prolonged decline.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Macro Picture Is Still Messy&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The crypto market doesn't exist in a vacuum. There's a lot
of competition for investor attention right now. &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/ex-cftc-commissioner-quintenz-us.html"&gt;AI stocks&lt;/a&gt; have been sucking up
capital. There are geopolitical tensions everywhere. And Binance CEO CZ has
pointed out that we're still in the bear market phase of the natural four-year
cycle, suggesting that volatility could persist.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;We're Still Off the ATH by a Significant Margin&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin hit an all-time high of around&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$126,000 in
October 2025&lt;/b&gt;. At the worst point of this bear market, BTC was down more
than 50%. That's a deep correction. Even though we've recovered a bit, Bitcoin
remains significantly below its all-time high. The market hasn't fully healed
yet.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bull Case: Why This Time Might Actually Be Different&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Of course, there's another side to the story. And it's also
pretty compelling.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The 200-Day MA Breakout Is a Significant Milestone&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The move above the 200-day MA represents a significant
technical milestone. It's the first time we've seen this level reclaimed since
the bear market started.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Regulatory Clarity Is Finally on the Horizon&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;One of the biggest things that's changed in the last week is
the political landscape. President Trump hosted a crypto summit at the White
House. He called on Congress to pass the "fair version" of the
CLARITY Act—a bill that would give crypto a permanent regulatory framework.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The SEC also dropped a major proposal on August 18
called&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;"Regulation Crypto Assets."&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;It's a framework
for how crypto projects can raise capital without getting sued. It includes
small exemptions for startups and conditional safe harbors. The details might
change, but the direction is clear: the regulatory approach appears to be
moving toward clearer rules for digital-asset issuers.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Institutional Money Is Trickling Back&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This isn't just retail hype. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs
recorded&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$297.6 million in net inflows on August 17** and **$189.3
million on August 18&lt;/b&gt;. That's back-to-back days of serious institutional
buying. BlackRock's IBIT was among the funds contributing to the inflows.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Institutional inflows suggest that longer-term demand may be
returning.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The "Supercycle" Narrative Is Getting Louder&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Wall Street broker Bernstein has suggested that we're at the
beginning of a "tokenization supercycle." If they're right, this
rally is just the opening act. The idea is that everything—from real estate to
bonds—will eventually be tokenized on blockchains. That's a potentially
multi-trillion-dollar market over time, and crypto is the infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What I'm Watching Over the Next Few Weeks&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If you're trying to figure out whether this is real or not,
don't just look at the price. Watch these five things instead.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;1. Will Bitcoin Hold the 200-Day MA?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;This is the most important signal. If Bitcoin can stay above
the 200-day MA for a sustained period—say, a few weeks—it'll strengthen the
case that this breakout is real. A drop back below would be a major red flag.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;2. ETF Flows: One-Off or a Trend?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The inflows on August 17 and 18 were encouraging. But are
they a one-off reaction, or the start of a sustained trend? Watch the ETF flow
data every day. If it keeps coming, it's a bullish sign.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;3. Will Bitcoin Dominance Break 59% or 58%?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If Bitcoin dominance breaks above 59%, it means this is
still a Bitcoin-only rally—which could be bearish for altcoins. If it drops
below 58%, it suggests capital is starting to rotate into other coins, which is
usually a bullish sign for the broader market.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;4. Does Regulatory Clarity Actually Bring Capital?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The SEC proposal and the White House summit are positive
signals. But they only matter if they translate into real institutional
capital. Watch for announcements from major banks or asset managers about new
crypto products.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;5. Is This Demand-Driven or Just a Squeeze?&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A short squeeze can create a sharp rally, but it doesn't
create sustainable demand. Watch the trading volume. If it stays high and ETF
inflows continue, it's a good sign. If volume fades, the rally might have been
purely positioning-driven.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;I'll be honest with you: I don't know if the bottom is in.
Nobody does.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What I do know is that the market is at a genuine
crossroads. The 200-day MA breakout is significant. The regulatory developments
are real. The ETF inflows are real. But the market is still fragile. Sentiment
hasn't fully healed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The bear market has been brutal. Bitcoin was down 50% at its
worst. The 270-day stretch below the 200-day MA was unusually long by Bitcoin's
historical standards. The Fear and Greed Index spent two months in
"Extreme Fear." People were genuinely giving up.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The last few days have been different. Volume is picking up.
Sentiment has shifted. Shorts are getting crushed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Whether this is the start of a new bull market, I can't say
for sure. What I can tell you is that something has changed. The next few weeks
will tell us whether it's a real turning point or just another dead cat bounce.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

not constitute investment advice. Markets are volatile, and past performance
does not guarantee future results.&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Standard Chartered Analyst Sees $100K Bitcoin Path as Treasury Boosts Bond Buybacks</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div style="text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEggZgx9RJtsSQIJxlrJjqmLlvN8Y4vJWOhyphenhyphen6GxNOlLWWec3a7Q4Cw8DtZ0fngWqkf-5IWPObK7ofJs9xSr2kLtV_oDSI3f-C-obb0lJXHSZmfWnUiQz8wszWkH2uL4Ji4bp5bCTH3Wy3-wgGQ8iH51TA4Vib8_L4r4YAqqKHm3pglbPqFpdhZuKfkr0jpvq/s1672/standard-chartered-bitcoin-100k-treasury-bond-buybacks.jpg.png"&gt;&lt;img alt="Bitcoin and U.S. Treasury bonds illustrated as Standard Chartered sees a potential $100,000 Bitcoin target" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEggZgx9RJtsSQIJxlrJjqmLlvN8Y4vJWOhyphenhyphen6GxNOlLWWec3a7Q4Cw8DtZ0fngWqkf-5IWPObK7ofJs9xSr2kLtV_oDSI3f-C-obb0lJXHSZmfWnUiQz8wszWkH2uL4Ji4bp5bCTH3Wy3-wgGQ8iH51TA4Vib8_L4r4YAqqKHm3pglbPqFpdhZuKfkr0jpvq/w400-h225/standard-chartered-bitcoin-100k-treasury-bond-buybacks.jpg.png" title="Standard Chartered Bitcoin $100K Treasury Bond Buybacks" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;By CoinAINews Staff&lt;/i&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin could be poised for a run toward $100,000 by
year-end as the U.S. Treasury ramps up support for the long end of the
government bond market, according to Standard Chartered analyst Geoff Kendrick.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;In a client note shared with Cointelegraph, Kendrick said
Bitcoin's key technical level to watch is&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$65,500&lt;/b&gt;, with a sustained
break above that threshold potentially confirming that the cycle low is already
in place.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"Investors should now be positioning for a move to
$100,000 by year-end 2026."&lt;/i&gt;&amp;nbsp;— Geoff Kendrick, Standard Chartered&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Treasury Move That Has Bitcoin's Attention&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Kendrick's call is tied to a specific policy catalyst. On
Wednesday, the Treasury Department announced that it would increase the maximum
size of certain long-dated bond buyback operations from&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$2 billion to
at least $4 billion per operation&lt;/b&gt;. The expanded program is scheduled to run
from&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;Sept. 9 through Nov. 4&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The move is designed to improve liquidity and reduce stress
in longer-dated Treasuries after a steep bond selloff sent yields surging.
Following the announcement, long-term Treasury yields fell sharply, easing
pressure across financial markets.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Kendrick Sees This as Bullish for Bitcoin&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Kendrick described the Treasury's action as&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;"exactly
the type of thing Bitcoin loves."&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;His reasoning rests on two factors:&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol start="1" style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="1"&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Historical
     precedent:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/how-to-start-with-crypto-in-2026.html"&gt;Bitcoin&lt;/a&gt; has historically tended to benefit from
     government liquidity interventions, according to Kendrick.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
 &lt;li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;Fixed
     supply:&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;Bitcoin's capped supply makes it resistant to monetary
     debasement—when liquidity expands, the argument goes, fixed-supply assets
     tend to hold value better.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Kendrick also pointed to Bitcoin's four-year cycle dynamics,
which he says point to an imminent market low.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Key Level to Watch: $65,500&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Kendrick identified&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$65,500&lt;/b&gt;&amp;nbsp;as the critical
technical level for Bitcoin right now.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;"If Bitcoin breaks above and sustains that level, it
would suggest the cycle low is already in."&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;From there, Kendrick believes Bitcoin could run toward&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$100,000
by year-end 2026&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Importantly, this is a&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;conditional thesis&lt;/b&gt;, not a
guarantee. A break above $65,500 would be a validation event for Kendrick's
perspective; failing to hold that area could undermine the signal that the
cycle bottom is already in place.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Market Reaction&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Early signs appeared to support &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/trump-leaves-door-open-for-bigger-us.html"&gt;Kendrick's&lt;/a&gt; thesis, with
Bitcoin surging more than 6% in U.S. late-morning trading following the
announcement, climbing to nearly&amp;nbsp;&lt;b&gt;$69,000&lt;/b&gt;—its highest level since
early June.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Bitcoin's move toward the $69,000 area highlights the
market's immediate reaction to the Treasury announcement, although the move
does not confirm Kendrick's year-end target.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

&lt;/div&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Standard Chartered analyst Geoff Kendrick sees a potential
path for Bitcoin to reach $100,000 by year-end 2026. The catalyst? An unusual
one—the U.S. Treasury expanding liquidity-support buybacks for longer-dated
government bonds.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Kendrick's argument is that government liquidity
interventions historically benefit fixed-supply assets like Bitcoin. Whether
Bitcoin actually hits $100,000 depends on continued support from both technical
and macro conditions. But for now, the bank's top digital assets analyst says
investors should be positioning for that scenario.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;div align="center" class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: center;"&gt;

&lt;hr align="center" size="1" width="100%" /&gt;

not constitute investment advice. Cryptocurrency markets are volatile, and past

    <title>Sam Altman Warns AI's Biggest Risks: Losing Control and Concentrated Power</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;p&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&amp;nbsp;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjKk5DA50_IYNgOHnonglWE7NZPl5JgKcCR_dvpARiuh7TGLHU_PqStGDShNipIgf1Tv6L5IyFfQh3eUlUEsnlrNoIdIwTctSgCzPGkimvz6gT_OYHj0V4xLE6tQ2poBLc5t3cB7IP3x5z5srBPiypQcROm49B78WtnFCvANTYQMfKWzuxoOrCJSkJG-0lQ/s1672/sam-altman-ai-risks-control-concentrated-power.jpg.png" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Sam Altman warns about losing control of AI and excessive concentration of AI power" border="0" data-original-height="941" data-original-width="1672" height="225" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEjKk5DA50_IYNgOHnonglWE7NZPl5JgKcCR_dvpARiuh7TGLHU_PqStGDShNipIgf1Tv6L5IyFfQh3eUlUEsnlrNoIdIwTctSgCzPGkimvz6gT_OYHj0V4xLE6tQ2poBLc5t3cB7IP3x5z5srBPiypQcROm49B78WtnFCvANTYQMfKWzuxoOrCJSkJG-0lQ/w400-h225/sam-altman-ai-risks-control-concentrated-power.jpg.png" title="Sam Altman Warns About AI Control and Concentrated Power" width="400" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;b&gt;By CoinAINews Staff | &lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the two risks he worries about
most as AI becomes more capable are surprisingly broad: &lt;b&gt;humans losing
control, and too much power concentrated in too few hands&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The comments, highlighted in a recent update from
CoinMarketCap and attributed to a conversation with entrepreneur and podcast
host David Senra, come as the AI industry moves toward increasingly capable and
autonomous systems.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For Altman, the challenge is no longer simply whether AI can
become more powerful. It is also about whether humans can remain in control of
that power — and whether advanced AI becomes concentrated within a small group
of companies, models or individuals.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Losing Control Is the First Major Risk&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;One of Altman's central concerns is what happens if &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/crypto-fear-greed-index-hits-74-highest.html"&gt;AIsystems&lt;/a&gt; become capable enough that humans can no longer reliably control their
behavior.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That does not necessarily mean a science-fiction scenario in
which an AI suddenly takes over.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A more practical concern is whether increasingly capable
systems could perform actions that developers did not intend, particularly as
AI moves from generating answers to carrying out tasks with greater autonomy.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That question has become more relevant as &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/hugging-face-reportedly-explores-13b.html"&gt;AI companies&lt;/a&gt;
develop systems capable of using tools, accessing digital environments and
completing multi-step tasks with less direct human involvement.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The more autonomy an AI system receives, the more important
monitoring, testing and containment become.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Second Risk: Too Much Power in One Place&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Altman's other concern is different.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It focuses not on what AI itself might do, but on &lt;b&gt;who
controls the most powerful AI systems&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If one company, one model or one individual gains
disproportionate influence over advanced AI, the consequences could extend far
beyond the technology sector.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Powerful AI could influence how people access information,
how businesses operate and how important digital services are delivered.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That makes the distribution of AI capabilities an
increasingly important part of the broader conversation.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The question is no longer simply &lt;b&gt;who can build the best
model&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It is also &lt;b&gt;who gets to control it and who gets access to
its capabilities&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Why Centralization Matters&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Building frontier AI systems requires enormous computing
resources, specialized chips, data, infrastructure and highly skilled
researchers.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Those requirements naturally favor companies with
substantial financial and technological resources.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;There are advantages to that model. Large organizations can
spend heavily on research, safety testing and infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;But concentration also creates potential risks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;If a small number of companies control the most capable
systems, decisions made by those companies could have an outsized impact on
businesses, consumers and governments.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That is why &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/08/standard-chartered-becomes-first-bank.html"&gt;AI centralization&lt;/a&gt; has become a governance issue
as much as a technology issue.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The AI Industry Is Already Debating This — and the
Disagreements Are Becoming Sharper&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Altman's concerns are not limited to OpenAI.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Other technology leaders have also entered the debate over
how AI power should be distributed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has argued that advanced AI should
be broadly distributed rather than controlled by a small number of
institutions. In an August essay, Zuckerberg described the distribution of AI
capabilities as an important question for the future balance of power.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The disagreement highlights a fundamental divide within the
industry.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Some argue that powerful AI needs to be developed carefully
and controlled through strong safeguards.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Others emphasize wider access and competition, warning that
excessive centralization could itself become a major risk.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Both sides are ultimately wrestling with the same question: &lt;b&gt;how
much control should any single organization have over increasingly powerful AI?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Safety vs. Innovation&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The AI industry faces a difficult balancing act.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Companies want more capable systems because advanced AI
could improve software development, scientific research, productivity and a
wide range of other industries.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;At the same time, greater capability can create greater
risks if systems behave unexpectedly or gain access to sensitive tools and
environments.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That creates pressure to improve safety measures alongside
model capabilities.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;OpenAI has previously described monitoring, alignment and
security as important safeguards as AI systems become more capable.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The difficulty is that AI companies are also competing
against one another.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A company that slows development significantly could risk
falling behind competitors that continue moving faster.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That tension between &lt;b&gt;speed and safety&lt;/b&gt; is likely to
remain one of the defining issues of the AI industry.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;AI Agents Make Control More Important&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The question of control becomes even more important as AI
moves beyond traditional chatbots.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;AI agents can potentially use software, interact with
websites, access information and complete tasks across multiple steps.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;That makes them considerably more useful than systems that
simply generate text.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It also increases the potential consequences of an error.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;An AI that produces an incorrect paragraph may create a
relatively limited problem.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;An autonomous system with access to external tools could
potentially take actions that affect real systems, accounts or data.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;As a result, developers need stronger safeguards around
permissions, monitoring and containment.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;What Altman's Warning Means for AI&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Altman's comments point toward a broader challenge facing
the technology industry.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Building a more capable AI system is only one part of the
problem.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Developers also need to consider how that system behaves,
what it can access, who controls it and how its capabilities are distributed.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Those questions become more difficult as models become
increasingly autonomous.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The industry may therefore be approaching a point where &lt;b&gt;governance
and control are nearly as important as raw model performance&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;A model that is more powerful but difficult to control could
create problems that cannot be solved simply by making it smarter.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bigger Picture&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The AI debate is entering a new phase.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Early discussions focused heavily on whether AI could match
or exceed human performance on particular tasks.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Today, the conversation increasingly involves questions
about autonomy, safety, concentration of power and access.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Those issues will become even more important if AI systems
begin handling larger portions of business operations, research and digital
infrastructure.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;For policymakers, developers and users, the challenge is
finding a framework that encourages innovation without allowing powerful AI
capabilities to become either uncontrollable or excessively concentrated.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The Bottom Line&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Sam Altman's warning comes down to two fundamental risks: &lt;b&gt;losing
control over increasingly capable AI and allowing too much power to become
concentrated in too few hands&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;Neither problem has a simple solution.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;AI development is advancing rapidly, while companies and
governments are still working out how safety, competition and access should
evolve alongside the technology.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;The next stage of the AI race may therefore be about more
than building the smartest model.&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;It may be about answering a much harder question: &lt;b&gt;how do
we make sure that increasingly powerful AI remains under meaningful human
control — without letting its benefits become concentrated in the hands of too
few?&lt;/b&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p class="MsoNormal"&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;i&gt;This article is for informational purposes only and does
not constitute financial, investment or technology-policy advice.&lt;/i&gt;&lt;o:p&gt;&lt;/o:p&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

    <title>Coinbase CEO Says SEC and CFTC Rules Could Be More Permissive After CLARITY Act Setback</title>
    <content type='html'>&lt;article&gt;

&lt;h1&gt;&lt;div class="separator" style="clear: both; text-align: center;"&gt;&lt;a href="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEg6_swsJqPJT9eyaHaNelAiXpHChseNVRLZBwesWSyuZsH9XaN4mvosL6kEal-ussQpTyLONlAqqV_r4HgjUQz4wDvUWSTRTqCUYj6KL9ZlxJKlJ1s_umke24a3fd7hFk8QIzpihwu-EBcRxpFy2xGMGxBUx5HtgGpTb2oc2mv-nESHJMCeJzlzIhUkljJV/s1734/coinbase-brian-armstrong-clarity-act-sec-cftc-crypto-regulation.jpg.png" imageanchor="1" style="margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;"&gt;&lt;img alt="Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong discusses SEC and CFTC rules after CLARITY Act Senate setback" border="0" data-original-height="907" data-original-width="1734" height="334" src="https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEg6_swsJqPJT9eyaHaNelAiXpHChseNVRLZBwesWSyuZsH9XaN4mvosL6kEal-ussQpTyLONlAqqV_r4HgjUQz4wDvUWSTRTqCUYj6KL9ZlxJKlJ1s_umke24a3fd7hFk8QIzpihwu-EBcRxpFy2xGMGxBUx5HtgGpTb2oc2mv-nESHJMCeJzlzIhUkljJV/w640-h334/coinbase-brian-armstrong-clarity-act-sec-cftc-crypto-regulation.jpg.png" title="Brian Armstrong on CLARITY Act and SEC CFTC Crypto Rules" width="640" /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;h1&gt;&lt;strong&gt;&lt;span style="font-size: medium;"&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;By Coin Ai News Editorial Team |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The failure of the U.S. Senate to advance the CLARITY Act has shifted attention toward the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), with Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong saying regulatory action from the two agencies could be more permissive in some respects than the legislation that stalled in Congress.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Armstrong made the comments while speaking with Scott Melker after the Senate failed to advance the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act. Meanwhile, former Treasury digital-assets counselor Tyler Williams offered his interpretation of why some Democrats who had previously supported the legislation ultimately voted against moving it forward.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Together, the comments highlight the two different paths now facing U.S. crypto regulation: continued action by federal agencies and the possibility of renewed congressional negotiations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Brian Armstrong Says SEC and CFTC Rules Could Be More Permissive&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said that rules eventually developed by the SEC and CFTC could be “arguably” more permissive in certain areas than the CLARITY Act would have been.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Armstrong's statement was an assessment of what could happen after the legislative setback. It was not an announcement that the SEC and CFTC had already adopted a replacement framework for the bill.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;His comments came as the crypto industry began assessing what the failure of the legislation means for the regulatory environment in the United States.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Armstrong has argued that the two agencies already have significant authority under existing federal law and can continue working on clearer rules for digital assets even without Congress completing a comprehensive market-structure bill.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The distinction is important. A law passed by Congress can establish statutory definitions, responsibilities and requirements, while agency rules, guidance and other regulatory actions operate within the authority granted to federal regulators by existing statutes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Senate Failed to Advance the CLARITY Act&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The U.S. Senate failed to advance the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act on September 15, 2026.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The procedural vote ended with 49 senators voting in favor and 50 voting against. The motion required 60 votes to clear the cloture threshold and allow the Senate to proceed with consideration of the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The vote therefore was not a final up-or-down vote on the completed CLARITY Act. Instead, it was a procedural vote on whether the Senate could move forward with the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Nevertheless, the result halted the bill's immediate path through the Senate and left the cryptocurrency industry without the comprehensive federal market-structure framework that supporters had been seeking.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The failed vote came after weeks of negotiations over several contentious issues, including regulatory jurisdiction, decentralized finance, &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/brazil-securities-regulator-launches-tokenization-working-group.html"&gt;stablecoin&lt;/a&gt;-related provisions and other areas of digital-asset policy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Tyler Williams Gives His Interpretation of the Democratic Votes&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Former Treasury digital-assets counselor Tyler Williams offered another perspective on the Senate vote during a discussion with Galaxy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Williams argued that some Democrats who had previously supported the CLARITY Act voted against advancing it once it became clear that the legislation no longer had a viable path to passage.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to Williams, voting yes under those circumstances could have carried a political cost for lawmakers because the legislation was unlikely to move forward regardless of their individual vote.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Williams' explanation is his interpretation of the lawmakers' decisions and should not be treated as an independently established motive for every senator who voted against the measure.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Senate record establishes how lawmakers voted, but individual motivations can involve multiple factors. Public statements surrounding the vote also reflected disagreements over specific provisions and negotiations surrounding the legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the SEC and CFTC Are Now in Focus&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;With comprehensive market-structure legislation stalled, the SEC and CFTC remain central to the development of U.S. crypto policy.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The SEC has authority over securities markets and securities-related activity, while the CFTC oversees commodities markets and certain derivatives. Determining how that authority applies to different types of digital assets has been one of the central issues in the U.S. crypto regulatory debate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CLARITY Act was designed to provide greater statutory clarity around those responsibilities and establish a broader framework for digital-asset market participants.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Without the legislation moving forward, crypto companies and investors will continue watching agency rules, interpretations, enforcement positions and other regulatory actions to understand how existing laws will be applied.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is the environment in which Armstrong believes SEC and CFTC rules could potentially prove more permissive in certain areas than the stalled legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Agency Action Can Continue Without CLARITY&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Senate setback does not mean that crypto-related regulatory activity has stopped.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Federal agencies can continue taking actions under existing statutory authority, although the scope of those actions remains limited by the laws Congress has already enacted.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That distinction is important for &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/clarity-act-stalls-in-senate-as_01396500536.html"&gt;cryptocurrency &lt;/a&gt;businesses. Agency guidance or regulatory relief can address specific products or activities, but it does not necessarily create the same type of long-term statutory framework that Congress can establish through legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For exchanges, token issuers, brokers, custodians and blockchain companies, the practical regulatory environment will therefore continue to depend on both existing law and decisions made by federal agencies.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why the CLARITY Act Matters to Crypto Companies&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The CLARITY Act was intended to address one of the industry's biggest regulatory questions: which federal agency should oversee different types of digital assets and crypto market activity.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For cryptocurrency exchanges and other market participants, regulatory classification can determine which rules apply, whether registration may be required and which compliance obligations a business must follow.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;A comprehensive market-structure law could also provide statutory definitions and responsibilities that are more durable than individual agency interpretations or temporary regulatory measures.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is why the Senate vote represents more than a single legislative setback. It leaves many of the industry's regulatory questions unresolved while the SEC and CFTC continue operating under their existing authorities.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Armstrong's View Does Not Mean CLARITY Is Permanently Dead&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Armstrong's comments about potentially more permissive SEC and CFTC rules do not mean that Congress has permanently abandoned &lt;a href="https://www.coinainews.com/2026/09/openai-makes-progress-on-another.html"&gt;crypto market-structure &lt;/a&gt;legislation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The September 15 vote prevented the bill from advancing at that stage, but it did not legally prevent Congress from considering similar legislation in the future.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Future negotiations could produce another version of the CLARITY Act or a different market-structure proposal. The timing and substance of any future effort will depend on congressional negotiations and the broader political environment.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For now, however, the immediate focus has shifted toward what federal regulators can do under existing law.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What Happens Next for U.S. Crypto Regulation?&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The SEC and CFTC are likely to remain important sources of regulatory developments for the U.S. cryptocurrency industry while Congress considers its next steps.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Armstrong believes the agencies can make meaningful progress without waiting for Congress to complete CLARITY. His comments suggest that the industry could continue receiving regulatory guidance even after the Senate setback.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At the same time, agency action is not identical to congressional legislation. Regulatory rules can be challenged in court, modified by future administrations or affected by subsequent congressional action.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That leaves the crypto industry watching two parallel tracks: regulatory developments from federal agencies and the possibility of renewed congressional negotiations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For market participants, both could have significant implications for exchanges, token issuers, decentralized finance projects, stablecoin companies and other digital-asset businesses operating in the United States.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The failure of the CLARITY Act to advance in the U.S. Senate has changed the near-term path of crypto regulation, but it has not ended the debate over how digital assets should be regulated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong believes SEC and CFTC rules could ultimately be more permissive in certain areas than the legislation that stalled in the Senate. Former Treasury digital-assets counselor Tyler Williams, meanwhile, has argued that some Democrats who previously supported CLARITY voted against advancing it after the bill appeared to lose its path to passage, partly because supporting a measure that could not advance could carry a political cost.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Those statements represent the respective views of Armstrong and Williams. The established legislative fact is that the Senate failed to advance CLARITY in a 49–50 procedural vote and did not reach the 60-vote threshold required to proceed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The next phase of U.S. crypto regulation will therefore depend on both agency action and future congressional negotiations. For Coinbase and other cryptocurrency companies, the SEC and CFTC's next moves may become increasingly important while the legislative debate remains unresolved.&lt;/p&gt;
